Phenethyl alcohol-assisted high-pressure homogenization enhances EPA preservation and facilitates lipid release from Nannochloropsis oceanica biomass during in vitro digestion.
abstract: Microalgal biomass is a sustainable and vegan source of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), but the rigid cell wall of Nannochloropsis sp. limits lipid release and its effective utilization in food and feed applications. This study investigated the effects of high-pressure homogenization (HPH), alone and in combination with phenethyl alcohol (PEA), a food-grade membrane-permeabilizing agent, on the disruption of Nannochloropsis oceanica cells. The impact of these treatments on lipid release and eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) retention was further evaluated using a standardized in vitro digestion model. Marked cell damage in N. oceanica was observed at the fourth pass during HPH. In contrast, PEA-assisted HPH induced substantial cell disruption as early as the second pass. These observations were confirmed by microscopy and trypan blue based membrane permeability assessment. Relative EPA content decreased by 2.56% points after HPH, while PEA+HPH limited the reduction to 1.70% points by reducing the number of required processing cycles. The combined PEA+HPH approach reduced cell aggregation and increased lipid release during in vitro digestion, from 13.02 ± 3.81% in untreated biomass to a maximum of 53.06 ± 2.55% in PEA+HPH treated biomass. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of PEA-assisted HPH processing to enhance the nutritional value of N. oceanica biomass.

title: Regulatory fragmentation in the EU insect-based food sector and potential implications for the development of an emerging food chain.
abstract: Insect-based foods (IBFs) are regulated in the European Union (EU) as Novel Foods through a centralized authorization procedure. However, the absence of specific hygiene requirements for establishments operating along the IBF supply chain in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 853/2004, together with the possibility for Member States (MSs) to require their approval, may result in divergent approaches to their regulatory classification across the EU. Against this background, this study systematically examined national legal databases and the institutional websites of competent authorities (CAs) across the 27 MSs to assess how establishments producing, processing or marketing IBFs are classified and to discuss the potential implications for food business operators (FBOs) and CAs. Relevant national sources were retrieved for 16 MSs, whereas no specific information was identified for 11 MSs. Three models were identified: 1) a registration-based approach (12/16 MSs), 2) a conditional approval approach (3/16 MSs), and 3) a multi-tier hybrid approach including authorization (1/16 MSs). Further heterogeneity was observed in the delimitation between primary production and post-primary stages, as well as in the application of the identification mark in MSs requiring approval. These differences may affect legal certainty and potentially create non-uniform regulatory conditions for FBOs, while also complicating the work of CAs. These findings highlight the need for clarification at EU level regarding the regulatory classification of establishments operating along the IBF supply chain. Such clarification could enhance regulatory predictability, harmonize official controls and reduce internal market disparities.

title: Contrasting stage-associated succession and ecological assembly of bacterial and fungal communities during industrial sauce-flavor Baijiu heap fermentation.
abstract: Whether stage-associated community differentiation corresponds to inferred assembly processes and profile dissimilarities remains unclear in industrial sauce-flavor Baijiu heap fermentation. Pre-turn and post-turn samples from rounds R3-R7 of two consecutive production cycles were examined by integrating bacterial and fungal community profiles, βNTI-RCbray assembly assignments, PICRUSt2-predicted MetaCyc profiles, FUNGuild annotations, physicochemical measurements, GC-MS volatile profiles, and matched local temperatures. Exploratory pair-aligned models related each pair's assembly-process family (ProcessFamily) to annotation-profile or measured volatile-profile dissimilarity calculated from the same samples. After adjustment for Round and Position, Stage accounted for 1.85-2.01% of bacterial and 12.69-14.24% of fungal Bray-Curtis variation, while Round had the largest conditional share. Fungal Stage shares remained larger after temperature adjustment and across corresponding leave-one-round-out comparisons, without a greater prevalence of selection-related assignments. Adding round-specific time trends reduced Stage shares to 0.18-0.56% for bacteria and 0.62-1.44% for fungi, indicating substantial sensitivity to fermentation progression. In Cycle II, ProcessFamily associations with bacterial MetaCyc and fungal guild-profile dissimilarities had partial R2 values of 2.30% and 5.97%, respectively, with little change after physicochemical adjustment. Neither cross-cycle reproducibility nor a general correspondence with measured volatile-profile dissimilarity was established. These findings distinguish compositional differentiation from inferred assembly structure and ecological-annotation correspondence from measured chemical relationships. They identify fungal composition and pair-level annotation associations as candidates for further validation, without establishing an independent turning effect.

A 3D Implementation of an Elastoviscoplastic Model and Application to Creep-Driven Slow-Moving Landslides
abstract: To analyze problems involving creep-driven slow-moving landslides interacting with structures and infrastructure and gain useful information for risk management, numerical modeling is the most comprehensive tool. When resorting to numerical simulations, appropriate constitutive modeling is key to capture the time-dependent behavior of geomaterials. However, a drawback of advanced constitutive models accounting for time dependency is the high number of parameters involved, which are commonly calibrated based on site-scale monitoring data, without accounting for the characteristic creep behavior of the material. This paper describes the implementation of an existing elastoviscoplastic model in a three-dimensional (3D) finite-difference software. The model, called SHELVIP (Stress Hardening Elastic Viscous Plastic), was derived from the classical theory of elastoplasticity by adding a viscoplastic component based on Perzyna’s overstress theory. After illustrating the model and the implementation procedure, the steps to tune the constitutive parameters, especially the viscoplastic ones, are described. First, the viscoplastic parameters are determined at the laboratory scale through an analytical calibration process based on laboratory creep tests. Then, tuning of some parameters at the site scale is performed, while other parameters are kept unchanged from their laboratory-scale value being representative of the intrinsic creep behavior. The final set of parameters can be used to run predictive analyses for problems of engineering relevance. The analytical calibration is exemplified with reference to triaxial creep tests on Palombini clays. Then, the implemented SHELVIP model is validated by comparing numerical, analytical, and experimental creep strains at different deviatoric stress levels. A three-dimensional numerical model of the interaction between a deep-seated landslide and an existing motorway tunnel is developed. The capability of the constitutive framework to catch the time-dependent landslide movement is demonstrated by comparing monitoring data with the corresponding numerical results. The model is then used to run predictive analyses aimed at investigating the slow-moving landslide–infrastructure evolution.

title: Importance of Uncertainty Representation and Design Exploration Method for Robust Aerodynamic Optimization
abstract: This study examines the impact of uncertainty propagation and design exploration techniques on robust airfoil optimization processes. The RAE2822 airfoil geometry is selected as the case study and parameterized using the class/shape transformation (CST) method. The functional relationship between design inputs and outputs is modeled using a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-driven surrogate model based on Gaussian process (GP) regression. Uncertainty calculations are performed using Monte Carlo sampling (MCS) and polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). In addition, the effects of different design exploration methods are analyzed using deductive design exploration (DDEM) and inductive design exploration (IDEM). The results indicated that the DDEM method is sensitive to the choice of uncertainty propagation technique, leading to variations in the optimization results. In contrast, solutions obtained using the IDEM method are found to be independent of the uncertainty propagation approach and more robust than those from the DDEM method. Furthermore, the robustness metric provided by IDEM makes it a practical and efficient method for robust airfoil optimization processes.

title: Unsteady Aerodynamic Prediction of a Variable-Sweep Morphing Wing via Steady–Unsteady Data Fusion
abstract: Variable-sweep wing aircraft demonstrate pronounced unsteady aerodynamic characteristics throughout the wing morphing process. Accurate prediction of unsteady aerodynamics remains a critical challenge due to complex flow physics and high computational cost. Traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods are precise but time-consuming, and purely data-driven surrogates often lack robustness when applied to unseen flow conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a steady–unsteady data fusion framework for rapid and reliable prediction of unsteady pressure distributions and aerodynamic coefficients of a variable-sweep wing undergoing cosine-type sweep motions. The framework integrates a steady prediction module with an unsteady correction module, leveraging the complementary strengths of the data sets. Steady-flow data provide broad parametric coverage over Mach numbers, sweep angles, and angles of attack, whereas unsteady data offer high temporal resolution and capture dynamic response features. The fusion model generates a base pressure field from the steady module and learns unsteady corrections from time-resolved simulations, achieving both accuracy and generalizability. Performance is evaluated across three distinct validation scenarios: same-period validation, cross-period validation, and cross-Mach/angle-of-attack validation. Results showed that the fusion model reduces pressure field errors by more than 50% and decreases lift and drag coefficient errors by nearly an order of magnitude compared with a purely unsteady surrogate. This study demonstrates that combining steady and unsteady data yields a computationally efficient and robust surrogate model, offering a practical tool for rapid and accurate unsteady aerodynamic prediction of morphing wings.

title: Boundary Performance Enhancement Monitoring Based on Smart Bearing Service Performance Indicators
abstract: Boundary-condition anomalies in continuous girder bridges redistribute support reactions and internal forces, yet long-term reaction monitoring is seldom connected to field intervention and assessment. We developed a support-reaction monitoring workflow for force-measuring adjustable bearings. Here, smart refers to continuous sensing, remote transmission, and controllable in situ height adjustment rather than autonomous diagnosis or actuation. Three long-window indicators, normalized reaction time mean (NRTM), normalized reaction time variance (NRTV), and reaction time correlation coefficient (RTCC), were derived from statistically steady traffic windows to suppress individual-vehicle effects. Simulations of a 60-m + 80-m + 60-m variable-section girder showed convergence after 6 h, with NRTM, NRTV, and RTCC errors of 0.00%, 1.06%, and −1.34%, respectively. The indicators were only weakly affected by changes in traffic parameters, while NRTV and RTCC recovered stable values at signal-to-noise ratios of at least 30 dB. Up to 30°, a simplified skew influence-surface check yielded small NRTM, NRTV, and RTCC deviations of 0.18%, 0.87%, and −1.19%, respectively. This supports the use of resultant reactions within the tested skew range. Field implementation involved an in-service, skewed, variable-section, continuous steel box-girder bridge equipped with 12 force-measuring adjustable spherical bearings. Indicators were calculated using a 9-h sliding window with 10-min steps. Under open traffic conditions, the bearing height underwent four stages of adjustment (1–2 mm each), during which the monitored time series of indicators changed accordingly. The postadjustment shift toward finite-element targets provided a relative assessment of the intervention outcome. These results support the use of indicators with engineering records and finite-element analysis to assess boundary anomalies, staged adjustment, and relative postadjustment changes under routine traffic.

title: Reliability Analysis of Unsaturated Soil Slopes Using Advanced Surrogate Models: A Comparative Study of PCE-MCS, K-MCS, and Gradient-Based Methods
abstract: Probabilistic stability analysis of soil slopes is essential for reliable geotechnical design due to pronounced uncertainties in soil strength and hydraulic parameters. Although crude Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) provides a robust benchmark, its prohibitive computational cost and the limitations of gradient-based methods such as FORM and SORM in handling nonlinear and non-Gaussian performance functions restrict their practical applicability. To address these challenges, this study conducts a comparative analysis of advanced surrogate-based reliability methods, specifically polynomial chaos expansion–enhanced Monte Carlo simulation (PCE-MCS) and kriging-enhanced Monte Carlo simulation (K-MCS), against traditional gradient-based methods such as the first-order reliability method (FORM) and second-order reliability method (SORM) for evaluating the stability of unsaturated finite soil slopes. The crude MCS serves as the benchmark. The work examines the predictive accuracy and computational efficiency of these methods in estimating the probability of failure ( p f ). Parametric studies demonstrate nonlinear variations in p f with mean and coefficient of variation of stability number ( c / γ H ), internal friction angle ( ϕ ), and fitting parameters of soil-water characteristic curve (SWCC) ( a f / γ H , n f , and m f ). In terms of computational efficiency, surrogate-assisted approaches provide orders-of-magnitude reductions in wall-clock time compared to crude MCS. When normalized with respect to PCE-MCS (unity), K-MCS requires only 1.85 times the computational cost, whereas FORM/SORM requires approximately 28 times. In contrast, crude MCS incurs computational costs exceeding four orders of magnitude for large sample sizes. Statistical testing confirms that stochastic methods (K-MCS, PCE-MCS) significantly outperformed gradient-based methods (FORM, SORM). Although no statistically significant difference is observed between K-MCS and PCE-MCS ( p -value = 0.83), K-MCS exhibited slightly narrower confidence intervals and lower mean error (0.0116 versus 0.0153), indicating marginally greater robustness. Moreover, K-MCS maintains point-estimate error percentages below 8% across most scenarios, with PCE-MCS below 11%. In contrast, FORM showed maximum errors of up to 50.67%, followed by SORM with errors as high as 31.97%. The study also includes Sobol’ sensitivity analysis to identify the influence of each input parameter on the factor of safety. Comparisons of Sobol’ indices derived using post-processed PCE, PCE-MCS, and K-MCS reveal consistent results, with friction angle ( ϕ ) identified as the most influential parameter (total-order Sobol’ index = 0.66). To facilitate practical application, the study concludes with developing design charts using kriging for target reliability indices of 3.0. These charts provide an important tool for slope stability assessment, enabling precise and efficient evaluations under unsaturated soil conditions. The findings emphasize the efficacy of PCE-MCS and K-MCS as robust and computationally efficient surrogate modeling techniques for quantifying the probability of failure of unsaturated soil slopes and facilitating reliability-based design optimization of finite slopes.
journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering

title: Method for Determining Lateral Groundwater Inflow and Initial Conditions of 1D Hydrodynamic Models for Large and Medium-Sized Rivers Based on Steady Flow Calibration
abstract: To enable the direct and efficient determination of lateral groundwater inflow and initial hydrodynamic conditions in one-dimensional (1D) hydrodynamic models for large and medium-sized rivers, we propose a steady flow calibration–based method to simultaneously determine these two key parameters. Taking preflood measured discharge as the benchmark, a hydrodynamic presimulation model with lateral groundwater inflow as the sole recharge is constructed. Numerical iteration drives the flow to steady state while lateral groundwater inflow is adjusted until the simulated discharge matches the benchmark. The lateral groundwater inflow thus determined serves as the constant input for the flood process, and the corresponding spatial distributions of water level and velocity under this steady state serve as the initial hydrodynamic conditions for flood simulation. Source-term calculations and stability conditions are optimized in the presimulation to improve accuracy and stability. The method is validated using historical flood data from the Tuhai River, China. For the typical events, the mean absolute error, root mean square error, and mean absolute percentage error remain low, demonstrating satisfactory accuracy. This method enables simultaneous quantitative determination of the two key parameters, significantly reducing parameter uncertainty, subjective biases, and numerical oscillations associated with their manual calibration. It improves simulation efficiency while maintaining numerical stability and simulation accuracy, offering an effective data-lean alternative for large and medium-sized rivers with stable preflood baseflow.

title: FEM Validation of Form-Found Shell Roofs Designed in Seismic Areas
abstract: Shell structures offer high structural efficiency when their shapes allow loads to be carried mainly through compression, making them particularly suitable for materials with limited tensile strength, such as masonry, unreinforced concrete, and unreinforced 3D-printed concrete. The purpose of this work is to evaluate the structural quality and practical reliability of shells obtained through a physics-informed neural network-based optimized constrained form-finding (PINN-OCFF) methodology. This form-finding approach explicitly accounts for both vertical and horizontal loading conditions at the design stage by identifying an isoresistant volume capable of withstanding these actions through pure compression. Unlike traditional form-finding methods that focus primarily on gravity loading, the PINN-OCFF strategy generates shell shapes intended to remain in compression under combined loading conditions relevant to real design situations. The study focuses on a shell designed through this PINN-OCFF framework and assesses its performance through finite-element method (FEM) analyses carried out in Abaqus, following modeling assumptions commonly adopted in engineering practice and required by design codes such as the Eurocodes, ACI, or the Italian NTC. The FEM results are compared with the membrane equilibrium predicted by the form-finding process in terms of the stress distribution, development of tensile zones, and overall structural response. To investigate the influence of boundary conditions, three different constraint configurations are considered: fully fixed edges, fully hinged edges, and hinges located only at the base supports. For comparison, a shell of uniform thickness is considered and analyzed under the same vertical and horizontal loads used during form finding. The analyses show that the shell designed through the PINN-OCFF form-finding process better preserves compression-dominated behavior under realistic modeling assumptions, even when horizontal loading conditions and nonideal boundary conditions are introduced. Compared to shells designed considering vertical loads alone or employing a uniform thickness, the optimized shell exhibits reduced bending effects and limited tensile stresses. These findings demonstrate that incorporating horizontal actions directly into the form-finding stage leads to more robust and practically reliable shell designs, supporting the use of the PINN-OCFF methodology as an effective preliminary design tool for compression-dominated shell structures.
journal: Journal of Structural Design and Construction Practice

title: Measuring Station-Area Functional Profiles of High-Speed Rail Stations through a Node-Place Approach: Nationwide Evidence from China
abstract: High-speed rail (HSR) stations are critical interfaces between national transport networks and urban systems, shaping both regional accessibility and local development. Yet, previous studies seldom offer a nationally comparable assessment of HSR station-area functional profiles, defined here as the combined performance and balance of transportation-related node functions and surrounding urban place functions within station areas. It remains unclear how railway-level attributes and city-level contexts jointly influence these profiles. This study proposes an integrated evaluation framework grounded in the node-place approach to quantify, classify, and explain the functional characteristics of HSR station areas. The framework combines a set of multidimensional indicators capturing transportation connectivity (node) and urban development attributes (place) through a weighted multicriteria evaluation to derive overall functional performance and incorporates an interpretable machine learning model to uncover nonlinear effects and interaction mechanisms among key determinants. A case study is conducted using 90 major HSR stations in China within the 15-min walking zone. Results show that the station-area function evaluation index is low on average but highly heterogeneous across space. Stations in eastern and northeastern China more often exhibit balanced node-place profiles, whereas stations in western regions more frequently display functional deficiencies. A common structural pattern is that node-related functions exceed place-related functions, indicating that network accessibility is not consistently matched by surrounding urban development. Railway-level attributes explain more variance than city-level factors, with station built time emerging as the most influential determinant. Its interactions with distance to the city center, station building area, and urban population shape distinct station-area functional profiles within threshold ranges. These findings provide an evidence base for differentiated station-area planning and targeted investments, supporting the transformation of HSR stations into integrated, multifunctional urban nodes.
journal: Journal of Transportation Engineering, Part A: Systems

title: Interpretable Hourly Flood Forecasting Leveraging Deep Learning Recurrence and Attention Mechanisms
abstract: Timely and precise flood forecasting at subdaily intervals is crucial for mitigating the adverse impact of flood events, particularly through early warnings that enable effective emergency response. This study investigated the efficiency of the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT), a state-of-the-art sequence-to-sequence deep learning architecture, for its efficacy in forecasting flood events with lead times from 1 to 24 h across the Atlantic and Gulf coastal regions of the US, extending from Maine to Louisiana. The TFT framework integrated time-dependent meteorological and hydrological variables along with several invariant catchment attributes to effectively model the temporal variability and spatial diversity of hydrological responses across different regions. Model performance was systematically assessed utilizing the Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE), relative peak bias (RPB), and peak time bias (PTB), benchmarked across multiple forecast horizons and evaluated against both discharge observations and simulations from the physically based National Water Model (NWMv3.0). The TFT demonstrated superior predictive capability, achieving an average NSE of 0.83 for continuous hydrograph simulations across all catchments during the testing phase, significantly outperforming NWMv3.0, which had an NSE of 0.53. The proposed TFT framework incorporates antecedent observed streamflow as an autoregressive input, whereas NWMv3.0 relies primarily on meteorological forcings and physics-based process representations without directly utilizing the same observed discharge information during forecasting. Consequently, part of the superior short-term predictive performance of the TFT framework, particularly at shorter lead times, may be attributed to this additional information advantage associated with streamflow persistence and autocorrelation. An attention mechanism was utilized to perform feature importance analysis, which identified total precipitation, longwave radiation flux, and convective fraction as the dominant dynamic meteorological forcings predictors, and the catchment mean slope was the most important static attribute, underscoring the model’s interpretability for the area of interest. To enhance reliability further, a quantile regression loss function was incorporated into TFT to generate probabilistic discharge forecasts (instead of point forecasts) across seven quantiles. The associated 95% prediction uncertainty (95PPU) was evaluated rigorously using established hydrological uncertainty metrics, including the R -factor, P -factor, and the total uncertainty index (TUI). By leveraging the advanced capabilities of the TFT architecture, such as its capacity for quantifying feature importance and delivering detailed probabilistic forecasts, this study contributes substantive advancements to short-term flood forecasting methodologies. These outcomes support data-informed decision-making and resilience-building strategies in flood-prone regions, reinforcing the applicability of deep learning in operational hydrologic forecasting.

title: How social media-induced secondary traumatic stress affects depression: a moderated mediation model of self-compassion and problematic social media use in college students.
abstract: Background: Social media use has grown rapidly among college students, who constitute one of the most active user groups. However, exposure to negative and traumatic content on social media may lead to secondary traumatic stress (STS-SM), which may be linked to depression. This study examines the psychological mechanisms underlying the relationship between STS-SM and depressive symptoms among Chinese college students.Methods: A total of 1080 Chinese college students (382 females and 698 males; mean age = 19.07 years, SD = 1.08) completed web-based questionnaires including Secondary Traumatic Stress Scale for Social Media, Beck Depression Inventory-II, Self-compassion scale, and Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale. Age, gender, educational level, marital status, ethnicity, and subjective socioeconomic status were treated as covariates. Mediation and moderation analyses were performed to examine the role of self-compassion and problematic social media use (PSMU) in the relation between STS-SM and depression using the PROCESS macro in SPSS.Results: STS-SM was found to be positively associated with depression (r = 0.48, p < .001), and this correlation was mediated by self-compassion (b = 0.09, 95% CI [0.07, 0.11]). Moreover, the effect of self-compassion on depression was moderated by PSMU, with the effect being stronger for students with high PSMU (b = -0.32, p < .001) than those with low PSMU (b = -0.12, p < .001).Conclusions: STS-SM contributed to increased depressive symptoms by reducing individuals' levels of self-compassion, with the effect of self-compassion on depression moderated by PSMU. These findings underscore the importance of regulating traumatic content online and highlight self-compassion training as a promising intervention, particularly for those with PSMU.

title: Rp-Bp and the Ribotools box for translatome profiling.
abstract: We present the Ribotools "box" for the analysis of matched ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) and RNA sequencing data. Ribotools can be used in standalone mode or in combination with Rp-Bp for Ribo-seq quality control, open reading frames discovery, translation efficiency, and differential expression analyses. In this work, we use Ribotools to profile the differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into cardiomyocytes to reveal a remarkably coherent transition from plastic, signaling-driven to stable, structurally committed cardiac cells, staged through multiple layers of translational control. Together with complementary proteomics, the resulting dataset provides a rich multi-omics resource for investigating the hiPSC model of cardiac lineage commitment. Additionally, we present a reproducible and extensible pipeline for benchmarking translation efficiency analysis tools. Ribotools and Rp-Bp are available on Bioconda and help to make research accessible and reproducible. Detailed documentation, test datasets, and tutorials are available at https://ribotools.readthedocs.io and https://rp-bp.readthedocs.io.

Climate‐Driven Oceanographic Changes Shape Larval Dispersal Success in the Southern Ocean
abstract: Although climate‐driven changes in ocean circulation are increasingly recognized as key drivers of marine ecosystem structure and dynamics, their consequences for the early life stages of deep‐sea fishes remain difficult to quantify. In the Southern Ocean, variability in frontal systems such as the Polar Front (PF) may influence larval dispersal and retention, with direct implications for recruitment. We investigated how interannual variability in ocean circulation and egg production shapes larval dispersal and retention in suitable recruitment areas of a large body size deep‐sea fish species, Patagonian toothfish ( Dissostichus eleginoides ), around the Kerguelen Plateau. We developed an integrated modeling framework which combined spatially explicit models of egg production with 24 years (2000–2023) of Lagrangian dispersal simulations driven by satellite‐derived geostrophic currents to quantify successful larval retention. Ontogenetic changes in distribution and fecundity were accounted for to model egg production, allowing retention metrics to reflect spatial heterogeneity in reproductive output. Larval retention rate in suitable recruitment areas varied from 9% to 28% over the study period. PF‐associated jet intensity was significantly associated with larval retention variability: years characterized by stronger PF‐associated circulation showed lower larval retention, with more larvae advected away from the shelf toward the eastern part of the plateau. The latter part of the time series, particularly after 2010, was characterized by stronger year‐to‐year fluctuations, a higher contribution of the North‐West recruitment area, and more frequent low‐retention years. Building on new findings on toothfish spawning dynamics and long‐term altimetry data, we showed for the first time that there is the potential for self‐recruitment in the northern part of the Kerguelen Plateau (French EEZ). We also discussed the implications for fishery management since PF‐associated indices may help interpret past recruitment trends and offer useful early‐warning for future recruitment anomalies.

title: Revealing the Widespread Bias of Extinction Risk in the Antarctic and the Southern Ocean
abstract: Accelerating environmental change in the Antarctic and Southern Ocean (ASO) necessitates robust extinction risk assessments to inform conservation priorities. Nevertheless, no systematic, region‐wide baseline of extinction risk currently exists for tracking ASO biodiversity responses to ongoing change, a significant barrier to global biodiversity monitoring. Here, we conducted the first ASO‐wide synthesis of current extinction risk knowledge for plants, animals and Fungi. This included examining biases in current assessments, the distribution of Threatened species and their associated threats. Using a data‐inclusive workflow, we compiled 8908 assessments representing 4970 species, more than doubling the number of ASO species assessed compared with any single source. As expected, assessments were heavily biased towards vertebrates (58% assessed), while invertebrates, despite their ecological prevalence, were markedly underrepresented (6% assessed). Among vertebrates, mammals had the highest proportion of Threatened species (26%). Birds within the ASO were disproportionately Threatened (25%) compared to the global average (11%), with the greatest threat for ASO species being ‘Biological Resource Use’. The sub‐Antarctic Islands had the highest density of both Threatened species and assessment effort, whereas many Antarctic species remain unassessed. Additionally, Threatened species have the lowest protected area coverage of any conservation status. These pronounced assessment biases highlight the need for more balanced, representative and data‐inclusive extinction risk assessments to be able to effectively detect conservation status change. This work represents an important step in ensuring ASO representation in global biodiversity monitoring frameworks, strengthening the capacity of these frameworks to detect, attribute and respond to future biodiversity changes.

title: When Drought Is Not Drought: How Metrics Bias Estimates of Ecosystem Water Limitation
abstract: Anthropogenic warming and shifts in global precipitation regimes are increasing rainfall variability and the frequency of intense precipitation events, raising uncertainty about how conventional meteorological drought indices capture ecosystem water limitation. This uncertainty arises from two key issues: temporal aggregation, as most meteorological drought indices are based on monthly integrated summaries, and drought definition, because atmospheric water deficits do not necessarily translate into vegetation water stress. Here, we quantified ecosystem gross primary productivity (GPP) responses to drought using three approaches: (1) monthly meteorological drought identified from monthly standardized precipitation evaporation index (SPEI), (2) daily meteorological drought defined by daily SPEI, and (3) ecological drought defined using an indicator of actual vegetation water limitation. Comparing monthly and daily SPEI‐based drought isolated the effects of temporal aggregation, while comparing daily meteorological and ecological droughts quantified the influence of drought definition. Across 130 eddy‐covariance sites spanning multiple biomes and climate zones, we analyzed 6691 drought months identified using monthly SPEI. Daily SPEI data revealed that within months classified as meteorological drought, nearly 50% of days did not coincide with atmospheric water deficits owing to daily rainfall variability. As a result, monthly SPEI overestimated GPP responses (20.60% ± 5.28% increase) relative to daily SPEI (4.61% ± 1.21% increase). In contrast, daily meteorological drought metrics underestimated drought‐induced suppression of GPP by ~46% compared with ecological drought, demonstrating that atmospheric drought metrics do not fully reflect water stress experienced by vegetation. Our results show that both temporal resolution and drought definition can bias estimates of ecosystem drought responses, underscoring the need for finer‐scale temporal and ecologically relevant measures of vegetation water limitation to improve understanding of biosphere–climate interactions in an increasingly drought‐prone world.

title: From Static Choices to Navigating Clinical Trajectories: Reframing Therapeutic Reasoning in Medical Education.
abstract: PROBLEM Therapeutic reasoning is central to clinical practice and informed by established frameworks such as evidence-based medicine and shared decision-making. In educational settings, however, therapeutic decision-making is frequently taught and assessed as a discrete choice among predefined treatment options. This static framing - commonly structured through decision trees and guideline algorithms- emphasizes treatment selection under uncertainty but may insufficiently reflect the temporally evolving and regulatory nature of patient care. CONCEPTUAL SHIFT We propose that therapeutic reasoning can be more fully understood as the navigation of clinical trajectories rather than the selection of isolated choices. Drawing on complex adaptive systems theory, we conceptualize disease, resilience, and health as dynamically interacting functions evolving through feedback loops and shifting stability. Therapeutic reasoning is the anticipatory and interpretive process that guides the adaptive regulation of evolving clinical trajectories across coupled systems of organism and pathology. This perspective complements established decision-making models by making the temporal and systemic dimensions of therapeutic practice explicit. FRAMEWORK We operationalize this reframing through a phase-based model distinguishing disease-dominant decline, therapy-dominant modulation, and resilience-dominant recovery. Using severe pneumonia as an illustrative case, we demonstrate how inflection points and destabilizing events reveal the dynamic cognitive work underlying therapeutic practice and provide a conceptual scaffold for structuring therapeutic thinking. IMPLICATIONS Reframing therapeutic reasoning as trajectory navigation enriches the teaching of therapeutic decision making by providing a conceptual scaffold for curriculum design, clinical supervision, and assessment.
journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice

title: Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval via Hierarchical and Targeting Semantic Alignment
abstract: Remote sensing image-text retrieval (RSITR) can facilitate visual language mining in spatial scenarios, which holds significant importance for aviation and aerospace applications. Existing RSITR methods often lack joint coarse-grained and fine-grained alignment, or their unified learning strategies are inefficient. Additionally, there is no analysis of remote sensing characteristics in these fine-grained feature learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes Hierarchical and Targeting Semantic Alignment (HTSA) for remote sensing image-text retrieval, which simultaneously considers the construction of global and local features. In coarse-grained semantic alignment, cross-modal classification learning and inter-modal matching learning are combined. For fine-grained semantic learning, targeted semantic alignment is introduced to highlight essential objects, which are overlooked by current RSITR methods, but crucial for remote sensing scenarios. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework, while different ablation studies discuss the functions of specific components.
journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

title: Learning Video-Derived Behavioral and Physiological Representations for Automated Deception Detection
abstract: Deception detection in video conferencing is increasingly important with the rise of remote interviews, online judicial hearings, and telemedicine consultations. Existing approaches either rely on observable behavioral cues (e.g., micro-expressions and head movements) or depend on specialized equipment for physiological sensing (e.g., thermal cameras or wearable devices). The former benefits from the ubiquity and non-intrusive nature of commodity RGB cameras but often suffers from limited accuracy, while the latter provides more reliable and discriminative signals at the cost of additional hardware, hindering scalability in real-world deployment. In this work, we bridge the gap between behavioral cue-based and physiological signal-based approaches and introduce DeceptSense, a video-derived multimodal framework for contactless deception detection using only RGB video. The key insight is that complementary signals, including motion dynamics, facial temperature variations, and cardiac activity, can be jointly recovered from RGB video. DeceptSense extracts these modalities using an iDT descriptor for motion dynamics, an RGB-to-thermal pipeline for temperature variation modeling, and an rPPG module for cardiac signal extraction. It then employs a cross-modal attention mechanism to align the three temporally asynchronous modalities. Extensive experiments show that DeceptSense achieves an AUC of 89.6% on the challenging Real-Life Trial dataset and AUCs of 64.5% and 65.1% on the BOL and MU3D datasets, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed video-derived multimodal framework for automated deception detection.

title: AquaNord-SE: A Large-Scale Longitudinal Multimodal Benchmark for Swedish Inland Water Quality
abstract: Predicting inland water quality reliably requires integrating water quality observations, satellite remote sensing, meteorological reanalysis, and catchment descriptors, yet no benchmark provides these modalities jointly under reproducible evaluation protocols for optically complex, seasonally ice-affected inland waters. We introduce AquaNord-SE, a longitudinal multimodal benchmark of 883,325 samples from 18,743 Swedish lake and river monitoring stations over 2000-2025, integrating 38 water quality parameters from SLU Miljödata MVM with observations from five satellite sensor streams, ERA5-Land and MESAN meteorological reanalysis, 64 HydroATLAS catchment attributes, and 13 derived water quality indices. The dataset is structured as station-aligned multimodal feature sets and spatial-temporal archives, accompanied by a five-tier modality ablation design and three orthogonal generalization splits across spatial, temporal, and latitudinal axes. Benchmarking across tabular, spatial-temporal, and multimodal baselines under split conformal prediction and quantile regression reveals that static catchment attributes alone (R2 = 0.303 Chlorophyll-a, R2 = 0.642 Secchi) consistently outperform all non-tabular models, while total phosphorus proves intractable across all families (best R2 = 0.118). Conformal calibration error increases from 0.062 to 0.225 across the oligotrophic-hypereutrophic gradient, co-locating with the eutrophic regime where atmospheric correction (AC) failure exceeds 65% of optical retrievals. We additionally release a gridded water quality index (WQI) NetCDF at 5 km resolution over 2000-2025, supporting Water Framework Directive (WFD) compliance and long-term trend analysis. The dataset and evaluation protocols are publicly available to support reproducible research in environmental knowledge management and data-driven water quality assessment and monitoring.

title: A muzzle-based self-enhancing cow recognition method using YOLO and LLM
abstract: In the modern era, using the technology of image processing, people are beingfacilitated in many sectors. Therefore, we have decided to do research on cowrecognition using the methods of image processing. Because cows are prettyessential for human beings, and people from the entire world are being facilitatedby cows. Because of that reason, many technologies have been invented till nowfor the cow. Here we have presented an approach to identify the cow. Like thefingerprint of a human, the cow muzzle is also unique. Due to this reason, wecan recognize the cow based on the muzzle. To recognize muzzles, we have usedYolo and the Structural Similarity Index (SSI). Image processing is a sector ofArtificial Intelligence and data is quite important to train models. Moreover, totrain a model for image processing, it is needed to manage a high-configurationcomputer. But there are many regions in the world where people hardly get suchpowerful machines. To mitigate this issue, we have introduced a unique methodwhere we do not need a large amount of data for the image processing task. Toeliminate the necessity of collecting a huge amount of data, we included a self-enhancing feature, which helps the model to predict accurately and also helpsto improve performance by increasing the amount of data. However, withouta large amount of data, it will be possible to predict appropriately because ofthe presence of self-enhancing features. This certain program helps the modelto improve its capability for delivering faster responses. LLM is responsible toadd the self-enhancing feature. On the other hand, to find out the most suitableYolo model for our research, we have trained data with three different versionsof Yolo: Yolo v7, v8, and v9. We evaluated the performances of these threeversions in terms of Precision, Recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 and found Yolov9 to be the best among them. It excels with a precision of 0.391, a recall of0.916, a mAP50 of 0.559, and a mAP50-95 of 0.307.

title: CPU-optimized regularized convolutional neural network architecture for multimedia-based breast cancer metastasis detection
abstract: The histopathological diagnosis of breast cancer metastases, a subjective and lengthy process, benefits from advances in artificial intelligence for its automation. This study proposes an automatic classification method based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture with progressive regularization (Batch normalization and adaptive dropout), trained on the PatchCamelyon (PCam) dataset. Our approach integrates a data augmentation strategy specific to medical images and advanced optimization for CPU environments, allowing us to balance performance, robustness, and computational accessibility. The architecture comprises only 94,000 parameters, 223 times fewer than leading models. Multi-criteria evaluation shows competitive results: area under the curve (AUC) of 92.92%, F1-score of 82.39%, accuracy of 88.74%, and specificity of 90.61%. A bootstrap robustness analysis provides 95% confidence intervals (AUC: [89.56% 92.91%]), and an ablation study quantifies the reduction in overfitting through progressive dropout (33.6%). This research validates that a well regulated and CPU-optimized CNN architecture can achieve clinically relevant performance while remaining accessible on standard environments, thus opening up concrete prospects for the development of practical AI tools in digital pathology.

title: Advanced IoT and ML-driven personal safety technology for women
abstract: This article introduces VigilNet, a personal safety system powered by internet of things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) that identifies environmental irregularities instantaneously through intelligent wearable gadgets. In contrast to solutions dependent on extensive datasets and reactive alert systems VigilNet employs a few-shot learning (FSL) strategy utilizing siamese neural networks (SNNs) to achieve precise anomaly recognition, with limited training data. In the information and communication technology (ICT) realm, VigilNet is a smart IoT sensing and communication network with interconnected wearable sensor nodes continuously collecting physiological and environmental data for real-time processing. The SNNs based FSL module then fuses these multiple modal streams of sensor information and extracts the similarity-based threat assessment, which in turn drives an intelligent decision support system to alarm the operator to take timely action for any abnormal situations. VigilNet, thus, combines IoT connectivity, real-time data analytics, and machine-learning-driven decision support into a single personal safety system. The framework was tested on an IoT wearable dataset encompassing heart rate, body temperature, ambient noise and proximity data. Experimental results demonstrate that VigilNet achieves a threat detection rate (TDR) of 0.85, false alarm rate (FAR) of 0.10, and a response time (RT) of 3.5 seconds, outperforming conventional IoT–ML safety models. These findings validate the feasibility, efficiency, and robustness of the proposed architecture and confirm the potential of FSL-based techniques for next-generation women’s safety technologies.

title: From Governance Principles to Architectural Primitives: Designing and Evaluating a Microservices-Based Smart Governance Platform for a Wellness Tourism Ecosystem
abstract: The growing importance of Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) in tourism underscores the need for governance models that integrate strategic processes with technological infrastructures. Although digital platforms are widely credited with operationalizing governance principles such as transparency, accountability and participation, the mechanisms through which architectural decisions enact those principles remain largely unspecified. This article presents the design and evaluation of a smart governance platform for a wellness tourism ecosystem[1], developed through a hybrid methodology combining Design Science Research with the Waterfall model and Scrum. The study makes three contributions. First, it proposes an explicit mapping between six governance principles and the architectural primitives that enact them — bounded contexts with private data stores, asynchronous event propagation, role-based access control, and a consolidated analytical store — together with the observable evidence each primitive produces. Second, it documents the resulting microservices-based artifact as a reference decomposition, stating the alternatives rejected and the trade-offs accepted. Third, it reports an evaluation combining architectural analysis with functional and load testing, identifying sensitivity points and residual risks alongside confirmed strengths in scalability and reliability. The findings show that governance principles are not satisfied by digital platforms in general, but by specific and traceable architectural choices — notably the reconciliation of transparency and autonomy through the propagation mechanism rather than through access-control policy.

title: Imputation Sensitivity and Robustness of Student Clustering in Higher Education Data
abstract: This paper investigates how different approaches to handling missing data shape the outcomes of unsupervised clustering in educational datasets. Three commonly used imputation algorithms – mean substitution, Random Forest and Multiple Imputation with Chain Equations (MICE) – were applied to student records from a Croatian higher education institution. The analysis included 461 students, with 46 (9.98%) missing values for study duration. Each dataset was analyzed individually using three clustering algorithms: K-means, Ward’s hierarchical clustering and Gaussian mixture model (GMM). The three imputation methods and three clustering algorithms produced nine algorithm-dataset combinations. Solutions containing between two and ten clusters were evaluated using the silhouette coefficient. It was also examined whether the different datasets produced numerically and substantively similar student clusters. The results show that different imputation choices have a pronounced impact on Ward’s hierarchical clustering, which selected ten clusters for MICE, six for Random Forest and four for Mean Replacement. On the other hand, K-means and GMM showed a high degree of robustness, consistently identifying the same number of clusters in all completed datasets – eight clusters for K-means and two for GMM. The analysis showed that when imputation was done with the mean value, all missing study durations were replaced with the same value. In contrast, Random Forest and Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) estimated different study durations for each student, which preserved larger differences among the imputed values. Despite these methodological differences, several interpretable student profiles emerged repeatedly, including high-achieving students, long-studying older students, low-achieving early-leavers and students with moderate academic success. These results show that the effect of missing data processing on student grouping is algorithm-specific. Solutions based on centroids and mixtures were comparatively robust in this data set, while Ward’s hierarchical clustering produced different results since the imputation methods changed the calculated similarities between students. These results may benefit researchers working with unsupervised machine learning and incomplete educational data sets. Therefore, educational clustering analyses should examine whether different imputation methods produce the same number of clusters, and whether the resulting clusters represent similar groups of students.

title: Reliable Retinal Screening with Foundation Models under Distribution Shift
abstract: Reliable deployment of deep learning classifiers for retinal disease screening requires accurate in-distribution classification, effective out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, and well-calibrated predictions under distribution shift. This study investigates the open-world reliability of the EyeCLIP foundation model and evaluates whether calibration-oriented fine-tuning improves performance under external-domain shift. A three-class fundus classification task comprising diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and normal images was constructed using APTOS2019, G1020, and ORIGA, with ORIGA held out entirely for external evaluation. Standard balanced fine-tuning was compared with calibration-oriented fine-tuning and a frozen-feature linear probe. Five OOD scoring methods were evaluated alongside post-hoc temperature scaling and accept–reject analysis. Performance was assessed using classification, OOD detection, and calibration metrics. Standard balanced fine-tuning out-performed calibration-oriented fine-tuning in in-distribution accuracy (0.928 vs. 0.781), k-nearest-neighbor OOD detection (AUROC 0.938 vs. 0.878), and post-hoc OOD calibration (ECE 0.081 vs. 0.450). The calibration-oriented model misclassified 69% of normal ORIGA images as glaucoma. At 25% overall rejection, standard balanced fine-tuning rejected 50.9% of OOD samples while falsely rejecting 1.6% of in-distribution samples. Standard balanced fine-tuning combined with post-hoc calibration and feature-space k-nearest-neighbor abstention provides a simple and effective strategy for improving the reliability of open-world retinal screening.

title: Gaussian Process Modelling for Precision Olive Irrigation-Fertilization Management: Continuous Prediction and Uncertainty Quantification of Olive Oil Quality
abstract: Introduction Olive oil quality is influenced by irrigation, fertilization, and seasonal climate variability. This study aimed to predict quality at unobserved water-fertilizer combinations while quantifying predictive uncertainty for risk-informed management. Methods A two-year (2023-2024) split-plot 3×3 factorial trial at INRA Meknès, Morocco, generated 54 biological olive-oil samples of Olea europaea L. cv. Picholine Marocaine across nine water-fertilizer combinations (50-100% ETc × 50-100% NPK), yielding 324 FTIR-ATR acquisitions. Matérn-5/2 Gaussian Process models with Automatic Relevance Determination were trained on 18 treatment-year means. Performance was assessed using Spearman ρ 2 under leave-one-treatment-out and leave-one-year-out cross-validation. Uncertainty was partitioned into aleatoric, temporal, and epistemic components, and Pareto optimisation identified resource-efficient regimes. Results LOTO-CV ρ 2 ranged from 0.408 (TFC) to 0.750 (carotenoids), with DPPH at 0.633 and TPC at 0.427. LOYO ρ 2 reached 0.790 for carotenoids and 0.494 for TPC. Temporal uncertainty accounted for ~58% of total uncertainty, versus 36% aleatoric and 6% epistemic. TPC was more sensitive to irrigation than fertilization (W/F = 0.22). The Pareto-optimal regime (≈50% ETc × ≈56% NPK) achieved 91% of maximum composite quality with 28% lower fertilisation cost. Discussion Seasonal variability was the dominant uncertainty source, highlighting the importance of multi-year data. Carotenoid and TPC patterns transferred across seasons, whereas DPPH required seasonal recalibration. Conclusion FTIR-GP modelling with Pareto optimisation offers a promising framework for uncertainty-aware olive management, but broader validation across seasons, sites, and cultivars is needed.

title: TOWARD SUSTAINABLE AGRITOURISM: HOW SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY SHAPES TOURIST CITIZENSHIP BEHAVIOR
abstract: Agritourism has increasingly emerged as an important form of sustainable tourism due to its economic, social, cultural, and environmental contributions to rural communities. Despite the growing attention to sustainable tourism, limited research has examined how destination social responsibility encourages tourists to engage in voluntary behaviors that support destinations, particularly in agritourism settings. In addition, previous studies have provided limited understanding of the psychological and contextual mechanisms through which destination social responsibility influences responsible tourist behavior. To address these gaps, the study develops and tests an integrated framework based on the stimulus–organism– response framework and signaling theory to explain the psychological and social mechanisms through which destination social responsibility influences responsible tourist behavior. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling on a sample of 424 tourists at agritourism destinations in Vietnam, we find that perceived destination social responsibility stron gly and positively predicts tourist citizenship behavior. Meanwhile, tourist-destination congruence and place attachment serve as partial mediators. Furthermore, destination reputation positively moderates the relationship between perceived destination social responsibility and tourist citizenship behavior. This study contributes to the sustainable tourism literature by clarifying the cognitive, emotional, and signaling processes underlying responsible tourist behavior in agritourism settings. The findin gs also provide practical implications for destination managers seeking to develop culturally aligned and reputation-enhancing strategies to foster sustainable agritourism development.

title: Understanding socio-ecological crises through agri-food systems
abstract: This forum examines how socio-ecological crises are reshaping labor–nature relations in contemporary agri-food systems. These transformations are examined through five ethnographic cases that focus on: the cheapening of labor in the Mexican avocado industry; the migrant labor paradox in Austrian greenhouses; the novel labor surveillance dynamics in digitalized South African agriculture; the entanglement of human and non-human labor in French conservation agriculture; and the re-valuation of tortilla production in Mexico. The contributions are united by a common understanding of labor processes as mediators of the nature–society relationship and seek to broaden current debates in the study of the work-environment nexus. The forum opens up questions about sustained pressure on laborers and the combined exhaustion of soils, bodies, and climates.

title: “Forcing a standard that is unachievable”
abstract: South Africa is a major Southern Hemisphere exporter of fresh fruit, the largest share of which is destined for counter-seasonal, high-value European markets. Remote and proximal sensing technologies, such as satellites, drones, and field cameras, are among the cluster of digital agricultural technologies, also known as “agritech,” promising optimization of yields, the lowering of input costs, and compliance with standards set by overseas agri-food governance actors in the horticultural production network. Reflecting on the labor-environment nexus in the transition to the digital-industrial fruit farm, the following contribution explores data-driven technologies employed at the orchard level. I draw on ethnographic material collected between 2024 and 2025 in the Western Cape, South Africa's most economically productive and labor-intensive fruit growing region, focusing on the strategies of farm managers, agritech employees, and local fruit export actors. This article puts forward two main observations: (1) digital intervention should be examined in light of commercial pressures placed on producers in the form of a double bind of sustainability standards and quality specifications, as stipulated by supermarket retailers; and (2) well-known trends of labor restructuring in the post-deregulation period from the mid-1990s onward are being accelerated by the deployment of digital technologies and are further compounded by the labor redistribution accompanying the introduction of new categories of highly skilled technical workers.

title: The concept of adaptive management of the process of launching innovative medicines to the pharmaceutical markets of BRICS countries (review)
abstract: The article substantiates the need for the BRICS countries to transition from static to adaptive models of regulatory governance for the process of launching innovative medicines, primarily advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs), to the market. Based on a system-oriented analysis of scientific publications and official regulatory documents, trends in the development of biotechnological medicines and the transformation of regulatory systems are identified. It is demonstrated that China, India, Brazil, South Africa, Russia, and the EAEU states are implementing various configurations of adaptive regulation, including accelerated and prioritized procedures, conditional approvals, reliance approaches, Early Access Programs (EAPs), digitalization of dossiers (CTDs), and the integration of realworld evidence. A concept of adaptive management is proposed, including interrelated notions as follows: adaptive drug lifecycle management, adaptive regulation, adaptive pathways and adaptive design of clinical trials. This model is shown to allow for reducing delays in providing access to vital innovative medicines along with strengthening the scientific and methodological basis for regulatory decisions. Priority areas for the formation of a common adaptive regulatory space for BRICS countries are identified, including the development of joint scientific consulting centers, the harmonization of procedures, the expansion of mutual recognition practices, and the integration of digital technologies.

title: Residual Diagnosis-Guided Abundance Correction for Blind Hyperspectral Image Unmixing
abstract: Recent blind hyperspectral image unmixing methods have achieved effective spectral–spatial representation, yet the reliability of estimated abundances remains difficult to assess because errors in jointly estimated endmembers and abundances can compensate for each other. To address this issue, we propose Residual Diagnosis-Guided Abundance Correction (RDAC), a post-correction framework that preserves the initial abundance estimate as an anchor and characterizes its mismatch using structured reconstruction residuals. Abundance candidates are then combined with structured residual information, while only 1% reference abundances are used to learn the correction. RDAC was evaluated on the Jasper Ridge, Samson, and Urban datasets. With UNMamba as the primary blind-unmixing backbone, RDAC achieved A-RMSEs of 0.0229, 0.0175, and 0.0359, reducing the initial errors by 55.05%, 70.80%, and 59.63%, respectively. It also achieved the lowest mean A-RMSE among the compared methods on Jasper Ridge and Samson while remaining competitive on Urban. Further experiments showed that reconstruction error alone does not reliably indicate abundance accuracy. When applied to NMF, RDAC reduced A-RMSE by 80.45%, 89.25%, and 77.61% on the three datasets. The results indicate that structured residual diagnosis can support abundance correction under limited supervision, and the NMF experiment shows that the same correction framework can also be used with an alternative blind-unmixing backbone.

title: A Machine Learning Approach for XCH4 Retrieval over China Based on TROPOMI Spectral Features
abstract: Methane is a major greenhouse gas that plays a critical role in climate change. Accurate monitoring of methane at the regional scale is essential for understanding its spatiotemporal dynamics and underlying processes. Here, a machine learning-based framework is developed to retrieve column-averaged methane (XCH4) by integrating shortwave infrared spectral information from TROPOMI. Spectral channels are first analyzed through machine learning-based feature importance analysis, and normalized spectral features are subsequently constructed. These features are then combined with auxiliary variables, including meteorological conditions, observation geometry, and surface environmental factors, to develop an XCH4 retrieval model. The GOSAT L2 XCH4 product is introduced as a high-accuracy reference observation for correcting the retrieved XCH4 results, and independent validation is conducted using observations from the TCCON site. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost demonstrates the best performance, achieving an R2 of 0.91 and an RMSE of 9.28 ppb under five-fold cross-validation. The model also maintains relatively better predictive performance compared with other models under both temporal and spatial extrapolation scenarios. Compared with the TROPOMI L2 product, the retrieved XCH4 shows improved agreement with TCCON observations, with a higher correlation (R = 0.84) and reduced errors. Based on this approach, a daily, spatially continuous XCH4 dataset over China for 2021 is generated. Analysis of the retrieved dataset reveals pronounced spatiotemporal patterns, characterized by higher XCH4 concentrations in eastern China and lower values in the western regions, as well as a distinct seasonal cycle.

title: Eksplorasi Model Smart Halal Business Incubator Berbasis Artificial Intelligence untuk Mendukung Transformasi Digital UMKM Halal di Kabupaten Deli Serdang
abstract: The global halal industry has experienced rapid growth, prompting the Indonesian government to strengthen the halal MSME ecosystem through certification, mentoring, and digitalisation programmes. However, halal MSMEs in developing regions such as Deli Serdang Regency still face constraints, including limited mentor availability, restricted market access, slow halal certification processes, and the low utilisation of artificial intelligence (AI) in business incubation. This study aims to explore an AI-based Smart Halal Business Incubator model that can support the digital transformation of halal MSMEs in Deli Serdang Regency. The study employs an exploratory qualitative approach using the systematic grounded theory strategy of Strauss and Corbin, involving halal MSME actors, academics, local government, halal process assistants, business incubator managers, investors, and halal certification bodies as purposively selected informants until data saturation was reached. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, FGDs, observation, and documentation, and were analysed through open, axial, and selective coding. The findings yield a new conceptual framework, the AI-Driven Smart Halal Business Incubation Framework (ASHBI Framework).

title: Chatbot Workflow Automation Using n8n as an Innovation in Digital Academic Services in Higher Education
abstract: Improving the quality of digital academic services in higher education requires systems that are fast, responsive, structured, and accountable. While chatbots are commonly used as digital service tools, their implementation often focuses on conversation rather than effective management of service processes. This study develops workflow automation using n8n, a node automation tool, to support academic service tasks. Employing the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, the research includes problem identification, solution design, artifact development, and system evaluation. The result is a modular, reusable, node-based workflow automation model that manages academic service processes. Evaluation across four different service scenarios demonstrated that the workflows operated as intended, enhancing service accessibility, process clarity, and consistency in service delivery. This model offers a practical framework for higher education institutions to adopt and implement efficient digital academic services.
journal: Jurnal JTIK (Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Komunikasi)

title: Directional Robustness Asymmetry in Indonesian Sarcasm Detection: A Cross-Platform Evaluation of IndoRoBERTa on X and Reddit
abstract: Sarcasm can reverse sentence polarity, making it one of the hardest problems in natural language processing and a persistent obstacle to reliable sentiment analysis on social media, where models are often deployed on platforms they were not trained on. Research on Indonesian sarcasm has largely stayed within a single domain or tested transfer in only one direction, leaving the cross-domain robustness of the IndoRoBERTa family on the IdSarcasm benchmark unclear. This study measures and compares the cross-domain robustness of IndoRoBERTa-small and IndoRoBERTa-base, with IndoBERT as a baseline, across X (Twitter) and Reddit, using the F1 gap (ΔF1) after cleaning anonymization artifacts, adding a data-size control, and running Stratified 5-Fold cross-validation. The results reveal a one-sided asymmetry: X → Reddit transfer is far more fragile (ΔF1 0.345–0.400) than Reddit → X (0.135–0.240), failing by missing sarcasm (false negatives) rather than over-flagging it (false positives). Practically, training on the context-rich domain (Reddit) and choosing IndoRoBERTa-base give the most reliable cross-platform sarcasm detection, with direction-specific mitigation recommended for robust deployment.
journal: Jurnal JTIK (Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Komunikasi)

title: The Development of the SONICC Learning Model Assisted by Augmented Reality Media in Elementary Science Education
abstract: This study developed, validated, tested the practicality, and examined the effectiveness of the SONICC learning model assisted by augmented reality media in elementary science education for students in an Elementary School Teacher Education Study Program. The study used a research and development design based on the Borg and Gall model. The development process produced a SONICC learning model with six syntax stages: Setting Goals, Organization, New Idea, Innovation, Critical and Creative Thinking, and Communication. It also produced five supporting products: a learning model book, teaching material book, lecturer guidebook, student guidebook, and augmented reality media guidebook. Data were collected using validation sheets, practicality questionnaires, documentation, and learning outcome tests. The validation results reached an average score of 92.30% with a validity value of 3.69, indicating a very valid category. The practicality results reached 94.27% with a practicality value of 3.66, indicating a very practical category. The effectiveness test showed an N-Gain score of 78.78%, which was categorized as effective. These findings show that the SONICC learning model assisted by augmented reality media is valid, practical, and effective for improving elementary science learning in higher education.
journal: International Journal of Technology in Education and Science

title: Webinar-Based Capacity Building for Integrated STEM: Pre-Service Teachers' Engineering Design Process (EDP) Oriented Lessons
abstract: The Philippine Department of Education emphasizes the engineering design process (EDP) as a pedagogical approach for developing problem solvers and innovators, yet Filipino learners remain among the lowest performers in science internationally. Engineering design is widely regarded as the central integrator of integrated STEM instruction, yet its integration is hardest in the life sciences, where abstract, submicroscopic phenomena and dependence on technologies unavailable in ordinary classrooms constrain what teachers can design. This study examined a webinar-based capacity building intervention preparing pre-service science teachers to develop EDP-oriented lesson plans and activities for Cell and Molecular Biology. Delivered as a one-month, three-session synchronous webinar series with digital scaffolds such as editable lesson templates, annotated exemplars, and shared resources, the intervention was evaluated using a mixed-method design with 24 third-year pre-service science teachers. Lesson plan evaluations improved from "Moderately Evident" (M = 4.01) to "Highly Evident" (M = 4.68), a statistically significant difference (p < 0.05). EDP-oriented activities were rated "Highly Evident" (M = 4.33) and demonstration teaching "Satisfactory" (M = 87.36). Four themes emerged: Value of EDP in STEM Education, Impact of the Webinar Series, Challenges in Implementing EDP, and Novel Experiences and Insights. Notably, participants' most persistent constraint was technological: access to affordable, accessible materials for rendering cellular processes designable. Findings indicate that technology-mediated capacity building can prepare pre-service teachers for integrated STEM in the life sciences, but that teacher education must also equip them with low-cost tools for visualizing and modelling submicroscopic phenomena.
journal: International Journal of Technology in Education and Science

title: Human Pose Recognition for Real-Time Applications in Surveillance Systems
abstract: Human pose recognition is a basic issue in computer vision that is used in analyzing activities, human-computer interaction as well as surveillance systems. Nevertheless, both training pose models and testing small classes often have been assessed on the basis of large volumes of manually labelled records, which is exasperating and shared. To overcome this shortcoming, the present paper gives a weakly monitored human pose classification model, which makes use of automatic estimation of poses and manual labeling avoiding the use of manual annotation. Initially, lightweight pose estimation model is used to extract human body key points out of an image. The set of heuristic rules that will automatically form pseudo-labels of common human poses is based on geometrical relations between joints that are landmarks. These pose features are subsequently again taken to train a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) pose recognizer. The dataset on which the proposed approach is tested is MPII Human Pose which consists of 24,984 images split into train-validation-test subsets of 70%, 20% and 10% respectively. Because of the lack of reliable samples produced by the automatic labeling process, two categories of poses were not for quantitative assessment. The last assessment is based on four well-represented classes of poses, including Standing, Sitting, Walking, and Bending. The experimental outcomes indicate high-performance on all the classes that were tested with macro-averaged classification accuracy of 94.51%. Standing, Sitting, Walking, and Bending pose provide results of class-wise F1-scores 0.9450, 0.8950, 0.9298, and 0.8120, respectively. The efficacy of the proposed method is also confirmed by the high-confidence visual predictions with the help of qualitative results. The findings point to the fact that despite lacking manual labeling, the suggested weakly-supervised framework is capable of efficiently categorizing human poses and gives a viable option that can be used in practice as an alternative to pose-based activities recognition.

title: Time‐Varying Structural Approximate Dynamic Factor Model
abstract: This study proposes a time‐varying structural approximate dynamic factor (TVS‐ADF) model by extending the approximate dynamic factor (ADF) model in state‐space form. The TVS‐ADF model considers time‐varying coefficients and a time‐varying variance–covariance matrix of its innovation terms to capture complex economic dynamics. We propose the identification scheme of the common factors in the TVS‐ADF model and derive the identification theory. We also propose an effective Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm to estimate the TVS‐ADF model. To avoid the overparameterization caused by the time‐varying characteristics of the TVS‐ADF model, we include the shrinkage and sparsification approaches in the MCMC algorithm. Extensive simulation experiments and empirical applications demonstrate the outstanding performance of the TVS‐ADF model.

title: Leveraging environmental data and dominance effects in genomic prediction may accelerate genetic gain in hybrid sunflower.
abstract: Genomic prediction improves the efficiency of plant breeding by allowing the performance of a new, untested genotype to be predicted without conducting field trials. There is a dearth of knowledge on best practices for performing genomic prediction in sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.), a hybrid crop. Our objective is to address this knowledge gap by performing genomic prediction for height, oil content, and yield using 115 hybrids derived from the Sunflower Association Mapping panel grown in ten environments in the northern Great Plains. We investigated three breeding scenarios and compared models using linear, Gaussian, and dominance genomic kernels, models incorporating an environmental relationship matrix (ERM), and five Bayesian models. The most difficult breeding scenario mimics the most common scenario in breeding programs, predicting untested genotypes in untested environments. The most complex predictive model uses an ERM to model covariance in the environment and genotype-by-environment terms and a genetic dominance kernel. The ERM was composed of the average precipitation and maximum and minimum temperature in four phenological stages defined by growing degree days. Overall, there was little to no improvement with the inclusion of an ERM in only the environment term. When the ERM was used to model genotype-by-environment (G × E) covariance, there was an improvement in prediction accuracy for yield. The inclusion of dominance further improved yield prediction accuracy. Our results demonstrate the importance of incorporating environmental variables and dominance in genomic prediction models, and illustrate areas of improvement for sunflower genomic prediction.
