title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
abstract: We present a shared framework that adapts Cosmos world foundation models for real-time interactive world simulation in Physical AI. By streaming visual observations in response to actions and scene controls, the framework enables users and embodied agents to interact with evolving virtual environments. It supports both predicting the visual consequences of actions and generating observations from physical state maintained by an external simulator. We demonstrate this approach across camera navigation and robot manipulation, controllable video transfer, and multi-view autonomous vehicle (AV) simulation. These examples provide a shared foundation for developing interactive virtual environments for Physical AI training and evaluation. Our code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/nvidia/cosmos and https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/cosmos3-examples. The project website is available at https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos-simulation.

title: LifeVal: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Personalized Agentic Consumer Tasks
abstract: We introduce LifeVal, a benchmark evaluating AI model performance on personalized agentic consumer tasks. LifeVal covers the most valuable life tasks that a personalized digital superassistant could automate, representing over 1.7 trillion US dollars in annual willingness-to-pay across 148 consumer task categories (e.g., managing finances, moving apartments, searching for a job, finding childcare). To construct our activity distribution, we conducted a new survey of willingness-to-pay for a digital superassistant across a demographically representative sample of over 3,800 consumers, cross-referencing our results against the American Time Use Survey (Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2025) and the Multinational Time Use Study (Fisher et al., 2025). For the most valuable consumer activities, we recruited task creators to create AI evaluation tasks personalized using real ChatGPT conversations and memories, reference files, and personal context. Task creators had to pass our expertise threshold (including personally completing the task multiple times and seeing the results through in their real lives for over a year) and also write a rubric, ensuring that our evaluation measured the best personalized completion for that task. All tasks had to pass at least three rounds of human quality-control before acceptance into our final evaluation sets.

title: System-Theoretic Analysis of Extended Cellular Potts Models for Tumor Invasion
abstract: The Cellular Potts Model has emerged as a standard framework for modeling multicellular systems and metastatic progression. Yet, computational extensions incorporating cell movement within spatial gradients of Extracellular Matrix (ECM), an important element of the tissue microenvironment, lack theoretical foundations. This work provides a system-theoretic formulation and analysis of Extended Cellular Potts Models (ECPMs) that explicitly couple tumor dynamics with ECM degradation. We reformulate the ECPM as an interconnected dynamical system: a stochastic process describing a network of locally interacting tumor cells coupled to a jump-linear system describing ECM evolution. By exploiting the sparse energy structure of the model, we characterize asymptotic ECM behavior, transition probabilities with uniform bounds, and global system convergence. In one-dimensional settings, we derive closed-form expressions for invasion time probabilities, revealing how mean invasion time depends on local ECM gradients, number of cells and their tendency to maintain a target volume. Numerical simulations validate theoretical predictions, establishing a principled foundation for analyzing haptotaxis-driven invasion in Potts-based models.

title: Energy-Guided Transport for Projection-Free Physics-Informed Flow Matching
abstract: Deep generative models, particularly Flow Matching frameworks, have emerged as powerful tools for synthesizing complex physical systems. However, standard architectures remain purely statistically driven and agnostic to the underlying governing equations, often violating fundamental physical constraints during inference. Existing zero-shot approaches designed to enforce these constraints typically rely on rigid algebraic projections. While effective for sparse boundary conditions, applying such discrete geometric corrections to dense, full-domain PDEs may disrupt the probability path, \rev{potentially deviating from the learned manifold and introducing substantial computational overhead}. To address these challenges, we introduce Energy-Guided Transport, a novel training-free framework that formulates non-linear physical constraints as a smooth potential energy landscape. Rather than interrupting the ODE integration, our method applies a continuous dissipative force directly to the intermediate generative states, steering them toward the physical manifold. By evaluating this force implicitly via reverse-mode automatic differentiation, our framework preserves the natural dynamics of the flow while maintaining an efficient $\mathcal{O}(N)$ algorithmic complexity. We extensively evaluate our framework across various 1D and 2D physical systems, including the chaotic Navier-Stokes equations. Our method achieves stable generation without structural divergence, significantly improves the stability-accuracy trade-off compared to state-of-the-art methods, and substantially accelerates inference with respect to exact projection strategies. Code available at: https://github.com/ispamm/Projection-free-energy-guided-flow-matching.

title: Smartphone-Aided VR Exergames for HIIT: Gamifying Fitness with Real-Time Pose Estimation
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative virtual reality (VR) exergame system designed to gamify High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT) workouts through 11 predefined combo moves, including squat-punch combinations, bilateral arm strikes, and diagonal stretch combos. Unlike conventional tracking methods that often rely on wearable motion capture suits or limited headset-based sensors, our system uses a standard smartphone camera placed on a tripod to capture full-body movement. This approach offers a cost-effective and scalable alternative, particularly well-suited to the fast, dynamic motions typical of HIIT routines. The smartphone footage is processed in real time using a pose estimation algorithm, with extracted biomechanical data analyzed by a backend server built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Anthropic's open standard for connecting AI models to structured data sources and tools, and a GPT-4o large language model. The system generates personalized assessments of form accuracy, movement efficiency, exercise intensity, and potential injury risks, tailored specifically to high-impact, time-sensitive exercises. A within-subject study involving 20 participants (ages 18-25) compared experiences in VR and Non-VR HIIT sessions. Results indicated significantly higher enjoyment (Mean = 3.5 vs 2.8, p = 0.02), improved immersion/focus (Mean = 3.2 vs 2.8, p = 0.03), and increased likelihood to recommend (Mean = 3.2 vs 2.7, p = 0.04) under the VR condition. Confidence to continue did not differ significantly between conditions (p = 0.15), while perceived intensity remained comparable. The MCP system showed strong agreement with expert evaluation (87.5%, N = 10 sessions, one certified trainer), supporting its reliability as a feedback tool.

title: Earthquake Forecast via Neutrino Tomography at the DUNE Baseline
abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of accelerator-based neutrino oscillations to localized electron-density enhancements associated with seismic fault zones along the Fermilab SURF baseline of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE). Motivated by the reactor antineutrino proposal of Wang, Chen, and Li, we model the anomaly as a uniform-density slab embedded in the surrounding crust and calculate exact three flavour oscillation probabilities using layer by layer evolution. Our results show that localized density enhancements can produce measurable variations in muon-to-electron appearance probabilities for both neutrinos and antineutrinos, with potentially significant relative effects. The predicted variations exhibit weak dependence on the leptonic CP violating phase, suggesting that time-differential measurements may help reduce uncertainties associated with the unknown CP phase. However, the event statistics required for a statistically significant detection substantially exceed those expected during a short-duration precursor interval. Consequently, detecting sufficiently persistent density anomalies may be possible under favourable conditions, whereas short-term earthquake forecasting is not feasible with the nominal DUNE configuration. Our findings establish a theoretical framework for exploring localized Earth-density perturbations through long-baseline neutrino oscillations.

title: Rethinking Access Control for AI Agents: Recent Advances and Open Challenges
abstract: Large language model agents access data, invoke tools, and act on users' behalf. Keeping these actions within authorized bounds is challenging because agents choose their own execution paths while permissions and operating conditions may change. This paper surveys recent advances in agent access control across four areas: policy specification and derivation, identity and delegation, action and resource enforcement, and information flow control. We compare their control objects, enforcement boundaries, and assumptions to examine what individual mechanisms achieve and how they can work together. Building on this analysis, we rethink four aspects of authorization: plan selection shapes permission requirements; contextual information can inform decisions without itself granting authority; restrictions must retain their meaning across system interfaces; and authorization must be reassessed as workflows evolve. These insights motivate open challenges and future directions, together with concrete research questions and evaluation criteria. In particular, evaluation should examine both observed agent behavior and the unauthorized effects that remain enabled. Our analysis connects existing mechanisms to the requirements for preserving authorization throughout an agent workflow.

title: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning for Remote Sensing in Urban Management
abstract: Fine-grained visual reasoning is essential for remote sensing in urban management, yet remains underexplored in the evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We introduce UMBench, a fine-grained urban remote sensing benchmark built from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images for multiple urban management tasks such as traffic monitoring, urban construction, environmental quality, and disaster warning. Evaluations on UMBench reveal that current MLLMs often rely on scene-level priors and overlook fine-grained visual evidence. To address this issue, we further propose a novel evidence-first chain-of-thought method that directs models to inspect fine-grained visual evidence in a training-free manner. Experiments show that our method can improve the performance of both open-source and commercial MLLMs on UMBench.

title: Energy Efficient Near-Threshold Voltage Massive MIMO Computing
abstract: Near-Threshold Computing (NTC) offers a substan- tial energy savings, i.e., up to 10x, for digital circuits. However, due to Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) variations, low voltage operating digital processors face increased susceptibility to timing errors. This work equips conventional massive MIMO algorithms with computational error detection mechanisms, en- abling reliable operation down to near-threshold voltages. While conventional hardware based Timing Error Detection (TED) systems introduce substantial overhead, this work modifies MIMO algorithms to seamlessly integrate low overhead Algorithm Based Fault Tolerance (ABFT). A co-simulation framework combining transistor level SPICE simulations and workload aware fault injection is developed to investigate reliability, Bit Error Rate (BER), energy savings, and overheads of modified algorithms operating at low voltages. The transistor-level characterization was performed in PSpice using generic Level-1 Shichman-Hodges CMOS transistor models with Monte Carlo parameter variations. No specific CMOS fabrication process node was assumed. Conse- quently, the reported energy savings are analytical estimates and are not specific to a particular CMOS fabrication technology. We evaluate Gauss Seidel (GS), ADMM based infinity norm detection (ADMIN), and Conjugate Gradient (CG) detectors using circuit derived fault models. Results demonstrate remarkable algorith- mic resilience. Although undetected computational errors in some trials near the Point of First Failure (PoFF) were observed, BER increases by only 0.7% to 1.4%, while beyond PoFF, ABFT reported nearly all erroneous cases. The proposed checksum based ABFT detects most arithmetic and memory errors, with an estimated overhead below 2% for a 64 x 16 MIMO system, decreasing further for larger configurations.

title: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization for Sign Language Generation
abstract: Sign language generation (SLG) maps written sentences into signing motion while preserving both lexical content and fine-grained articulation. This requires a model to decide what signs should be expressed and to realize them through precise handshape, trajectory, facial expression and body coordination. Existing pose-based systems and reconstruction-only motion tokenizers often entangle these two decisions, leaving the generator without an explicit text-aligned intermediate target for what to sign before refining how to sign it. To address this issue, we introduce Semantic Residual Vector Quantization (SRVQ), a framework for SLG that frames generation as a two-level process moving from semantics to kinematics. The newly introduced SRV Quantizer learns a hierarchy in which the first residual level encodes sign content and subsequent levels refine pose, handshape, trajectory, and body coordination, all within a single quantizer and without separate semantic representations or external planning stages. Through word-aware conditioning for hierarchical code generation, a masked semantic generator predicts semantic codes and a kinematic generator completes the residual codes for full SMPL-X motion synthesis. We evaluate using retrieval and FID in a shared text-motion embedding space, alongside standard geometric metrics. On CSL-Daily and Phoenix-2014T, SRVQ achieves R@1 of 82.3 and 70.3, outperforming the previous SOTA by 30 and 46 points, respectively.

title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
abstract: Few-step distillation offers efficient generation with diffusion and flow models, but preserving quality with only a few sampling steps remains challenging. Distribution-matching methods via score distillation provide a strong foundation, yet they rely on accurately tracking the student's changing distribution. At intermediate generation steps in few-step sampling, student-score estimation can be difficult, and commonly used estimators may describe a different distribution from the one used to update the student. Flow matching allows a more flexible approach to supervision through velocity fields constructed from the student's sampling process. Building on this perspective, we introduce Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD), which uses a learned critic to compare student and teacher fields and turn their disagreement into feedback for learning. VAD unifies score distillation, Fisher-based matching, and moment matching, also explaining existing heuristic MMD updates and delivering new training objectives. We further develop VA-TDM, which follows trajectory distribution matching: providing supervision for partial denoising along the student trajectory. Beyond this, VA-TDM combines transition-aware online velocity learning and dual-form VAD supervision across intermediate student transitions. Extensive results show that VA-TDM is powerful for learning few-step generators, achieving state-of-the-art four-step performance in both text-to-image and text-to-video generation across various backbones and scaling effectively to 33B MiniMax-H3. In particular, our VA-TDM-H3 notably outperforms the few-step Fast-H3 and is closer to the original many-step H3 according to human preference.

title: Context-Aware Autoregressive Image Generation for Emerging Reasoning Properties
abstract: Autoregressive image generation has recently emerged as a competitive visual generation paradigm, yet its generation order is often predefined or heuristic, such as next-patch prediction, random-order prediction, or one-step generation for specific scales. We observe that these strategies can cause models to overlook important structural dependencies in images, thereby limiting both structural robustness and reasoning capability. In this work, we propose a context-aware autoregressive generation framework, where the model dynamically determines the next token location based on global context and current local information. Rather than following a fixed or random order, our method allows the generation process to adapt to image structure and semantic dependencies. Extensive experiments show that context-aware generation significantly improves structural robustness across different image AR paradigms, including masked autoregressive and scale-wise autoregressive models. Beyond quantitative improvements, we further observe emerging reasoning properties: the model can better understand complex semantic instructions and generate images that more faithfully follow the given guidance. These findings suggest that generation order is a critical yet underexplored factor in image autoregressive modeling, and that context-aware decoding can unlock stronger reasoning-aware visual generation capabilities. Code is available at https://github.com/Hpesojyjx/Saccades-AR.

title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
abstract: Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget. We study whether coding agents can carry out this step autonomously. We formulate compression as a terminal task in which an agent receives a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget, then constructs compressed weights and executable inference code. The agent controls its algorithm and experiments; perplexity feedback guides search, and independent verification checks the final model. Across six agents and six model--size settings, 29 of 36 submissions pass verification. Selecting the lowest-perplexity agent design per task yields an average 3.4% perplexity increase over BF16 and 77.33% downstream accuracy, compared with 79.56% for BF16. Recorded experiments reveal how agents achieve these outcomes and where improvement breaks down. Agents lower PPL in 21 of 24 revisions at nearly fixed storage; complete-model feedback reverses 17 of 79 prior local rankings; and generation and inference tests expose failures that likelihood alone misses. The results identify representation design, experimental judgment, and capability validation as central to agent-driven model compression, a measurable component of efficiency-oriented self-improvement.

title: GH-AWTrace: A Large-Scale Dataset of GitHub Agentic Workflow Execution Logs
abstract: Agentic workflows enable AI agents to perform recurring repository tasks on schedules or in response to repository events. Existing studies examine workflow definitions and outputs, but provide limited evidence of what happens during execution. We present GH-AWTrace, a dataset linking 25,014 verified GitHub Agentic Workflows across 5,051 repositories to 4,112,526 run records and 562,877 nonempty execution log archives. The dataset preserves execution evidence subject to GitHub's log-retention limits and links it to repository metadata and generated workflow configurations. Illustrative cases show how the logs expose tool denials, provider failures, changes in an agent's approach, and delegation among agents. These observations enable research on execution failures, tool use, and the relationship between reported run outcomes and visible task progress. Coverage varies across workflows, and the logs provide partial observations rather than complete agent trajectories. Video: https://youtu.be/KIlfmZhHxtA

title: SpecCompact: Accelerating LLM Agent Context Compaction with Slot-Parallel Semantic Speculative Verification
abstract: LLM agents use context compaction to manage growing interaction histories, but summarizing long histories with large models can introduce substantial delays. Compaction therefore requires balancing information retention against latency. We observe that structured summary slots can retain information when generated independently. Based on this observation, we present SpecCompact, a framework that accelerates compaction through slot-parallel semantic speculation. SpecCompact fine-tunes a small drafter and generates slots in parallel. The target model verifies each proposed line and repairs rejected content, while subsequent drafting uses the updated slot prefix. System optimizations further reduce repeated context processing and model calls. Across AppWorld and $τ^3$ benchmarks with two target models, SpecCompact achieves $2.04$--$5.63\times$ compaction speedups over Hermes-style summarization. Separate downstream evaluations reveal model- and task-dependent performance trade-offs. A user study within Hermes further shows an $8.68\times$ median compaction speedup.

title: VABAR: A Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics
abstract: For robots to operate reliably in commercial and industrial applications, they must persistently perform specific tasks with known variations in object shape and pose. We call this Variational Automation (VA) to differentiate these settings from fixed automation. Inspired by recent papers on Agentic Robotics, where pretrained LLM and VLM coding agents combine interpretable robot programming with the open-world adaptability of model free policies, we propose a general set of agentic robotics benchmark design criteria that includes accessibility, repeatability, diversity, relevance to agentic robotics and practical applications, physical realizability, resistance to benchmark saturation, and computational efficiency. We instantiate these principles in six manipulation task classes spanning industrial, medical, and infrastructure applications: tool sorting, tool hanging, gear meshing, syringe packing, cable insertion, and cable routing. We introduce the Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics (VABAR), an open, easily replicable, simulation-based manipulation benchmark to systematically evaluating agentic robotics systems. Built fully on open-source tools, VABAR features detailed implementations using the Newton physics engine, standardized task variations, difficulty tiers, success metrics, and a library of 33 generalizable skills with human-authored programmatic reference solutions. We provide initial baseline evaluations using an open agentic manipulation harness, Graph-as-Policy (GaP), and Isaac Lab Arena.

title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
abstract: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics, FrontierPhysics evaluates whether agents' research is correct and publishable. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. Manual review of agent trajectories shows that frontier agents' main weaknesses are insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition, rather than gaps in physics knowledge or execution errors.

title: Optimization of zoned irrigations to balance groundwater sustainability and crop yield under future irrigation source replacement scenarios
abstract: Groundwater depletion in the North China Plain threatens both aquifer sustainability and food production. Inter-basin water diversion, especially the South-to-North Water Diversion Project, may provide an alternative irrigation source, but its ability to support groundwater recovery while maintaining winter wheat yield remains poorly quantified. Here, we develop irrigmoo, a multi-objective optimization framework that scripts a three-dimensional numerical groundwater model into the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) and couples it with a statistical winter wheat yield model to optimize zoned irrigation. Applied to Cangzhou, a groundwater-depleted agricultural region in the North China Plain, irrigmoo represents hydrolithological heterogeneity through three irrigation-management zones and evaluates the joint effects of replacement-water capacity and spatial irrigation allocation. Results show that irrigation reduction alone cannot reverse groundwater depletion without substantial yield penalties. By contrast, replacement water shifts the Pareto frontier toward simultaneous groundwater recovery and yield stabilization. Under the maximum replacement scenario, the balanced solution produces 0.40 m a⁻¹ of deep groundwater-level recovery and a 4.29 % yield increase, while the base scenario fails to meet both targets simultaneously. The largest relative benefit occurs in groundwater-scarce Zone III, indicating that uniform irrigation policies miss important spatial differences in groundwater response and crop benefits. Future groundwater-level projections further show that reliable replacement water is necessary for sustaining recovery beyond the optimization period. These findings demonstrate that coordinated water replacement and zoned irrigation can transform the groundwater-yield trade-off into a feasible pathway for integrated water-food management in depleted aquifer systems.

title: CoRTeC: A Differentially Private Release for Synthetic Tabular Data, Decodable by Any Generator
abstract: The records that could train the most useful models, such as a hospital's patient files, are often the ones an institution cannot share. We propose CoRTeC, a method that releases synthetic versions of such records under differential privacy. Differential privacy places a proven limit on what the synthetic data can reveal about any person, and in particular on membership inference. CoRTeC spends the privacy budget once, on a small file of noisy counts designed for training a classifier. For each group of records, the file gives the group's size, its balance of outcomes, a histogram of every column for each outcome and the outcome rate in each of several non-overlapping cells. A reviewer can check every number before the file leaves the institution. Anyone can then turn the counts into synthetic rows, as often as they like and at no further privacy cost. A maximum-entropy decoder can do this without any language model, and so can each of the five frozen language models we tested. None of them ever sees a real record. A selection step then matches the rows to the released counts. Decoded without a language model, the automatically configured release at $\varepsilon = 2$ trains classifiers to within 0.02 AUC of a real sample of the same size on the Adult dataset, across three data splits. On NHANES and bank marketing, without the selection step, it stays within 0.05 AUC. On Adult, with a fixed cohort rule, the release carries the outcome rates a deployment names more closely than a real sample does, at some cost in accuracy on pairs of columns. Four controls show that most of the utility comes from the release and the selection step, and that a language model adds what it knows from the column names. No private row ever reaches a model, and no row CoRTeC generates copies a real one. The strongest membership attack stays far below the bound the budget allows.

title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a benchmark of annotation, perturbation and regulatory inference against simple baselines
abstract: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network (GRN) inference. To identify where they add value, we benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), CellOracle, supervised perturbation models including STATE, and task-matched simple baselines on the same data, from K562 Perturb-seq screens and primary cells to healthy-donor and isogenic leukodystrophy brain organoids, a public organoid CRISPR screen and lung cancer biopsies. FMs were most useful when labels had to be transferred across species: from human to mouse lung, Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy and Geneformer V2 and scFoundation about 0.90, against 0.68 for the best baseline. Zero-shot in silico perturbations captured the direction of real responses in K562, with up to 75% of perturbations shifted in the expected direction (scFoundation, p < 1e-8), and Geneformer V2 networks recovered patient-level tumour differential expression better than co-expression (fold enrichment 2.9 versus 2.0). Within a species, FM embeddings annotated cells as accurately as principal components. In organoids, predicted knockout effects were largely explained by where the target is expressed, and an expression-matched control test isolated the gene-specific part, 12 to 35% of the effects. Isogenic Canavan and Krabbe organoids and 4H patient organoids, with one library per line and time point, did not yet separate methods from differences between clones and donors, which defines the replication needed for future validation. Fine-tuning changed classification accuracy but not knockout rankings. We release the benchmark, baselines, pipeline checks and the isogenic reference task as the fmaudit package, so that new models can be evaluated on the tasks where FMs already help.

title: Autonomous generalizability auditing of scientific foundation models
abstract: Determining where scientific foundation models generalize beyond their development data is essential for reliable use, but aggregate benchmarks obscure performance limits and rigorous audits are difficult to conduct routinely. Here, we introduce AutoSPECTRA, a coding-agent protocol for systematic generalizability auditing. To inform its design, we reviewed 38 studies across five biological domains and evaluated coding agents, which generated hypotheses and empirical analyses but applied inconsistent standards for judging evidence. We then structured AutoSPECTRA around measurable generalization axes, prespecified analyses, controlled comparisons and independent confirmation. Across four biological foundation models, audits linked performance to protein sequence composition and relatedness to pretraining data (ESMFold2), representation of perturbations in training (STATE), effective spatial resolution (CONCH), and residue-level genomic, evolutionary and structural context (AlphaMissense). Agents also evaluated alternative explanations and rejected unsupported hypotheses. AutoSPECTRA provides a systematic approach to discovering and testing the limits of scientific foundation models.

title: Estimating bone marrow adiposity from head MRI and identifying its genetic architecture.
abstract: Bone marrow (BM) adiposity changes radically through the lifespan, but this phenomenon is poorly characterized and understood in humans. Large datasets of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of the head have been collected to study the human brain, but also contain unexploited information about other organs. We developed an artificial neural network that localizes calvarial BM in T1-weighted MRI head scans, enabling us to study its composition in several large MRI datasets, and to model sex-dimorphic age trajectories, including the effect of menopause. We revealed high heritability in single-nucleotide polymorphism and twin data, and identified 41 genetic loci significantly associated with the trait, including six sex-specific loci. Integrating mapped genes with existing BM single-cell RNA-sequencing data revealed patterns of adipogenic lineage differentiation and lipid loading. Finally, we identified significant genetic correlations with several human traits, including cognitive ability and Parkinson's disease, which is intriguing in light of the recently discovered channels that link calvarial BM to the meninges.

Neural Stem Cell Therapies for Central Nervous System Regeneration: Advances, Challenges, and Integrative Technologies.
abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are promising candidates for central nervous system (CNS) regeneration because they self-renew and differentiate into neural lineages. Advances in genome engineering, extracellular vesicles (EVs), biomaterials, organoids, single-cell technologies, and precision medicine have expanded approaches for characterizing, engineering, delivering, and evaluating NSC-based therapies for neurological disorders. CRISPR/Cas9 and related platforms may enable more precise modification of NSC function, while NSC-derived EVs offer potential cell-free strategies. Engineered hydrogels and three-dimensional scaffolds may improve cell survival, engraftment, migration, and integration. Organoids and single-cell omics provide increasingly detailed models of cellular heterogeneity and lineage specification. However, clinical translation remains limited by immune compatibility, tumorigenic risk, manufacturing standardization, graft survival and integration, and regulatory requirements. Rigorous preclinical validation, standardized manufacturing, appropriately designed clinical trials, long-term safety monitoring, and harmonized regulatory frameworks are required before routine clinical application.

title: Conversational AIs and Mnemonic Distortion
abstract: Conversational AI agents designed to simulate interactions with deceased persons—referred to here as Interactive Personality Constructs of the Dead (IPCDs)—offer a novel and potentially highly valuable way to memorialise the deceased. But IPCDs could also undermine the goal of remembrance. This paper argues that IPCDs put users at risk of mnemonic distortion—an epistemic harm in which generated misrepresentations of the deceased become incorporated into our memory of the deceased, such that some of what subsequently shapes our conception of the deceased person originates in the IPCD rather than the deceased—reshaping or, at worst, replacing our memories of the person we hoped to remember. Such distortions are importantly distinct from imaginative engagement with the deceased or the testimony of others, which may also alter our memories of the deceased. The risk of mnemonic distortion is not inherent to IPCDs but rather contingent on design; the paper concludes by considering how this concern could inform recommendations for the design of IPCDs.

title: Assessing future climate risks to date palm production in Saudi Arabia: scenario-based projections and adaptation priorities from machine learning evidence
Quantifying snowmelt contribution to streamflow using ensemble machine learning and remote sensing
abstract: Snowmelt plays a vital role in sustaining river flows and regulating water resources in mountain ecosystems, particularly under changing climatic conditions. This study aims to quantify the contribution of snowmelt to streamflow by estimating snow cover and snow water equivalent (SWE) in the Greater Caucasus Basin of Azerbaijan. MODIS snow-cover and FLDAS land-surface products were analyzed using Random Forest, with data processed on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform to support computationally efficient and consistent snow-data processing. On the held-out product-derived test data, the RF models reproduced the dominant variability in SCA and SWE, with RMSE values of 16.3 km² and 2.3 kg m⁻², respectively; these metrics represent product-based agreement rather than an independent improvement in absolute accuracy over MODIS or FLDAS. MODIS and FLDAS products indicated peak snow cover in December 2023 (1,310 km²) and maximum SWE in February 2023 (23 kg m⁻²). During 2013–2023, mean March–June net SWE depletion was 20.48 kg m⁻², equivalent to 0.168 kg m⁻² d⁻¹. Model-attributed snowmelt runoff represented 35.70% of total discharge (SMC_total) and 45.11% of rainfall- and snowmelt-associated runoff (SMC_direct), with SMC_total reaching 71.20% in winter. These findings demonstrate pronounced seasonal and interannual variability in snow storage and its model-attributed contribution to streamflow during the common 2013–2023 analysis period. The study demonstrates the value of machine learning for snowpack monitoring and highlights the need for long-term simulations and expanded ground-based networks to improve prediction of peak flow events in mountain basins.

Hydroclimatic trends in Southeastern Türkiye from multi-source earth observation data
abstract: Southeastern Türkiye, located in the upper Tigris–Euphrates basin, is increasingly exposed to hydroclimatic stress under semi-arid conditions. This study integrates multi-source remote sensing and reanalysis datasets, including ERA5-Land, CHIRPS, MODIS NDVI, GRACE MASCON, and JRC Global Surface Water, within a Google Earth Engine–QGIS workflow to assess regional hydroclimatic trends during 2000–2020, with GRACE/GRACE-FO terrestrial water storage evaluated over 2002–2020. Spatial trend analysis was complemented by Mann–Kendall significance testing and Sen’s slope estimation to strengthen statistical interpretation. Results indicate warming, vegetation greening, and declining terrestrial water storage over the study period, based on non-parametric trend analysis of annual aggregated observations. Because hydroclimatic time series may exhibit residual temporal autocorrelation, statistical significance should be interpreted cautiously and primarily as exploratory regional trend evidence rather than definitive inferential proof. The coexistence of vegetation greening and declining terrestrial water storage indicates contrasting regional environmental trends between vegetation dynamics and integrated water storage. However, the present analysis does not directly quantify irrigation withdrawals, groundwater abstraction, or other anthropogenic drivers; therefore, the causes of these contrasting trends cannot be determined from the current datasets alone. These findings should therefore be interpreted as exploratory regional evidence rather than as attribution of specific climatic or anthropogenic drivers. Persistent warming and declining terrestrial water storage highlight the importance of continued monitoring of regional water-resource conditions. These findings provide a reproducible framework for multi-variable regional hydroclimatic trend assessment.

title: Co-application of biochar and poultry manure improves plant water availability and drought tolerance of Ananas comosus in a clayey Ferralsol
abstract: Enhancing soil water availability is critical for improving crop drought resilience in highly weathered tropical soils. This study evaluated the synergistic effects of industrial charcoal fines (a biochar byproduct) and poultry litter on the water status of pineapple (Ananas comosus (L.) Merr.). We compared a process-based, flux-based model (FBM) against the traditional FAO-56 method to provide a mechanistic assessment. A greenhouse experiment was conducted using a completely randomized factorial design with nine treatments (four replications). Treatments consisted of biochar and poultry litter applied alone or in combination at rates of 5% and 10% (v/v). Irrigation was managed via tensiometry. Plant available water and drought stress were modeled by integrating soil hydraulic properties, root distribution, and plant transpiration. Results indicated that the combined application of biochar and poultry litter significantly increased both Total Available Water (TAW) and Readily Available Water (RAW). In contrast, the sole application of biochar was detrimental to plant water availability, reducing RAW by up to 16.5%. Modeling revealed that the modification of soil hydraulic properties, rather than increased root growth, was the primary driver of these improvements. Regarding plant performance, the combined application maximized agronomic traits, yielding increases of up to 417% in aboveground biomass and 464% in water use efficiency (WUE) compared to the control. These gains occurred without significant alterations to root length density, reflecting pineapple’s specific resource allocation strategy under prolonged optimal hydration. Furthermore, RAW calculated via the FBM emerged as a highly sensitive predictor of plant performance, accurately linking the improved soil mesoporosity to extended periods of optimal relative transpiration, relationships that traditional metrics failed to capture. We conclude that co-application with an organic source is a prerequisite for effectively utilizing biochar from industrial charcoal fines, overcoming their physical limitations to mitigate crop drought stress. Ultimately, this management strategy enhances key plant parameters such as aboveground biomass, WUE, and transpiration maintenance. Future research should validate these integrated amendments in long-term field trials to assess their ultimate impacts on fruit yield and the C3-CAM metabolic transition under varying seasonal climates.

title: Multi-stress environmental drivers of archaeological deterioration in Al-Fustat, Historic Cairo: integration of hydrochemistry, remote sensing, and urban analysis
abstract: This study investigates the main environmental factors causing deterioration in Al-Fustat archaeological area in Historic Cairo. A multidisciplinary approach was applied, combining field observations, hydrochemical analysis, remote sensing, and GIS techniques. Water samples were collected and analyzed to evaluate groundwater quality, while land use/land cover (LULC) and land surface temperature (LST) changes between 1996 and 2022 were assessed using Landsat data. LULC mapping was based on historical land-use maps, Google Earth Pro imagery, and field observations, while LST was derived from Landsat data using the USGS Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Temperature product. The results show the formation of waterlogged zones affecting archaeological remains. Hydrochemical analysis in 2026 indicates very high salinity levels, dominated by sodium and chloride, with significant nitrate contamination, which may be associated with anthropogenic sources such as wastewater leakage. Total dissolved solids (TDS) ranged from 22,950 to 82,880 mg/L, while nitrate concentrations reached up to 6100 mg/L in the shallow groundwater samples. Remote sensing analysis reveals an increase of 38.5% in urban land accompanied by a reduction of approximately 80% in green areas during the period from 1996 to 2022. The mean LST (μ) values increased from 32 °C in 1996 to about 38.54 °C in 2022, with a noticeable increase in urban heat island (UHI) intensity. The study identifies groundwater salinity, elevated temperature, and urban activities as important environmental factors associated with archaeological deterioration. These conditions may promote moisture movement and salt crystallization within building materials, potentially accelerating structural damage. The findings highlight the need for improved drainage, regular monitoring of groundwater levels and quality, and the use of conservation materials compatible with saline and damp conditions to protect archaeological remains.

FGFR1-driven brachyury promotes endothelial-like differentiation of glioblastoma stem cells via SOX2/ZEB1/YAP1 signaling pathways.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by intensive vascular proliferation that is essential for tumor growth. Recent studies indicate the existence of tumor-derived endothelial-like cells can arise from the differentiation of GBM stem cells (GSCs). The transcription factor brachyury plays a critical role in promoting stem cell identity and vasculogenesis during normal embryonic development. However, its involvement in endothelial-like differentiation of GSCs remains unknown. By integrating clinical bioinformatics from GBM databases with preclinical in vitro and in vivo models, including patient-derived GSC cell lines and xenografts, we found that brachyury is highly expressed in GBM tissues and correlates with angiogenesis genes. Our study demonstrated that brachyury is activated by fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1), which subsequently promotes GSC differentiation into endothelial-like cells via SOX2/ZEB1/YAP1 signaling. GSCs with high brachyury expression display great sensitivity to selective FGFR inhibitors in vascular tube formation assays. In vivo pharmacological targeting of FGFR1 with inhibitor E7090 or brachyury gene editing using Cas9/gRNA suppresses GBM neovascularization and tumor growth. Furthermore, gene signature analysis of GBM patients further demonstrated that a lower FGFR1/brachyury/SOX2/ZEB1/YAP1 signature score significantly correlates with favorable overall survival outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of FGFR1-driven brachyury activation in GSC-derived neovascularization and suggest that targeting the FGFR1-directed brachyury/SOX2/ZEB1/YAP1 signaling represents a promising therapeutic strategy for GBM.

Whole-tumor dual-layer spectral detector CT quantification for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma: An interpretable prediction model.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To develop an interpretable dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLCT) model for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), and to compare two-dimensional region-of-interest (2D ROI) with whole-tumor three-dimensional volume-of-interest (3D VOI) parameter-extraction strategies. METHODS This retrospective study included 205 surgically treated patients with CSCC who underwent contrast-enhanced DLCT before surgery. Patients were assigned to training (n = 113), internal validation (n = 47), and temporal validation (n = 45) cohorts. Parameters were extracted using 2D ROI- and 3D VOI-based analyses. Clinical, 2D DLCT, 3D DLCT, and DLCT-clinical fusion models were developed using multivariable logistic regression and evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS 3D VOI-based analysis showed higher interobserver reproducibility than 2D ROI-based analysis (mean intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.950 vs. 0.875; P < 0.001). The 3D DLCT model included arterial-phase 70-keV virtual monoenergetic attenuation (CT70keV-AP), arterial-phase normalized effective atomic number (NZeffAP), and venous-phase normalized iodine density (NIDVP). Its areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.897, 0.895, and 0.885 in the training, internal validation, and temporal validation cohorts, respectively. The 2D DLCT and 3D DLCT models did not differ significantly in AUCs after multiple-comparison correction. The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.900, 0.916, and 0.881, respectively, outperforming the clinical model without significantly improving on the 3D DLCT model. CONCLUSIONS 3D DLCT quantification provides an interpretable and noninvasive imaging biomarker for preoperative identification of poorly differentiated CSCC and may support individualized risk stratification. External validation in larger multicenter cohorts is needed to confirm generalizability.

title: Spatial spillovers and causal configurations of the digital economy driving green manufacturing transformation in China
abstract: The digital economy has emerged as a critical engine for high-quality economic development, yet its specific mechanisms and configurational pathways in empowering green manufacturing transformation remain under-explored. Based on panel data from 31 provinces in China (2012–2023), this study constructs a dual-methodological framework integrating the Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution, transmission mechanisms, and causal recipes of this relationship. The empirical results reveal four key findings. First, green manufacturing transformation exhibits a steady upward trend but follows a distinct “East-High, West-Low” spatial gradient. Second, the digital economy exerts a significant positive impact on local green transformation and generates positive spatial spillovers to neighboring regions, though the spillover effect is weaker than the direct effect due to administrative barriers; technological innovation and environmental regulation are identified as two pivotal transmission channels. Third, a “Northeast Paradox” is observed: while the digital economy promotes green growth in most regions, it shows a significant negative interaction effect in the Northeast, attributed to the “lock-in effect” of rigid industrial structures. Fourth, fsQCA identifies four sufficient pathways leading to high green efficiency: “Digital-Talent Driven,” “Digital-Innovation Driven”, “Internal-Capability Driven”, and “Comprehensive Synergy”. Notably, a substitution effect exists between talent support and R&D intensity, offering flexible transformation strategies for resource-constrained regions. By moving beyond linear effect analysis, this study provides a multidimensional analytical roadmap to support the design of differentiated, context-sensitive green transformation policies.

title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
abstract: Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

title: A Model Coupled with Fractional-Derivative and Peridynamic Theory for Water Migration in Unsaturated Expansive Clay
abstract: Expansive clay exhibits multiple fissures and undergoes deterioration due to fluctuations in moisture levels. To guarantee the stability of earth structures built on expansive clay in semiarid regions, significant emphasis has been placed on studying the effects of water migration. This paper introduces an innovative method that utilizes a nonlocal model and peridynamic theory as substitutes for the temporal and spatial derivative terms. Based on spatial integration, the peridynamic formulation effectively captures the path dependency of water transport in unsaturated expansive clay, enabling an accurate representation of the diffusion process. Furthermore, the use of a fractional derivative accurately characterizes subdiffusion phenomena arising from the fractal nature of heterogeneous media. The accuracy of the model was further confirmed by analyzing the measured data collected from migration experiments conducted in a closed system, where different temperatures and water potential gradients were applied. The findings indicate that the proposed model effectively captures the process of water migration in unsaturated clay, offering valuable insights into understanding the patterns governing water movement in expansive clay under unsaturated conditions.

title: Transfer of tropane alkaloids from maize silage contaminated with Datura stramonium to milk of dairy cows.
abstract: Datura stramonium, a poisonous plant producing toxic tropane alkaloids (L-hyoscyamine and scopolamine), is increasingly spreading on agricultural crop land used for feed production. To examine the transfer of tropane alkaloids (TAs) from feed to milk, four high yielding dairy cows received a total mixed ration containing maize silage naturally contaminated with Datura stramonium for ten days with a daily mean TA dosage of 0.12 mg/kg body weight. TA content of individual cow composite milk was measured at each milking using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. L-hyoscyamine was detected in milk with a mean of 0.90 µg/kg, corresponding to a steady-state transfer rate of 0.039% ±0.007%. D-hyoscyamine was detected in neither silage nor in milk, indicating no evidence for natural racemisation. Scopolamine remained below the limit of detection in milk. Health parameters of the experimental cows were monitored by clinical investigation and using a digital sensor system monitoring rumination. No clinical signs of intoxication were observed. Feed naturally contaminated with Datura stramonium can lead to TA occurrence in milk, which may contribute to consumer exposure. In the contaminated maize silage, Datura seeds and remaining plant parts were analysed separately to determine their contribution to total TA content. Total TAs in maize silage originated mainly from the Datura plant parts. Therefore, maximum levels based on the total TA content of animal feed instead of Datura seed weight may be more appropriate to protect animal and human health alike.

title: Visual search as a cognitive marker to discriminate progressive supranuclear palsy from Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is a high priority for both patients and clinicians. Nearly half of individuals with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy are initially given an alternative diagnosis—most commonly Parkinson’s disease—and the correct diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy is delayed by an average of three years compared with Parkinson’s disease. Problems with cognition arise early in the progression of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, including profoundly disturbed visual search. This search deficit is likely caused by a combination of oculomotor, visuospatial, attentional and executive dysfunction, which is not observed in Parkinson’s. Since assessment of visual search is not routinely included in clinical testing for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, it may represent a promising method for differentiating these movement disorders. However, few studies have systematically compared visual search in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy and Parkinson’s disease, so the extent to which search deficits can reliably differentiate the two diseases is unknown. To address this issue, patients with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (N = 28), Parkinson’s disease (N=28) and age matched controls (N=27) completed four tests of visuospatial attention: an easy feature search task, a difficult feature search task, a conjunction search task and a paper-and-pencil cancellation task (the Bells test). We measured perceptual sensitivity (d prime), search time and detection accuracy. Search efficiency in the Bells test was also modelled using Quality of Search score. In addition, patients completed tests of oculomotor system integrity, the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and the National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire 25. As predicted, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy was associated with a profound search deficit: search was slow and highly disorganised on all tests. Furthermore, reflexive orienting along the vertical axis was impaired on the easy feature search. Critically, Receiver Operator Characteristic analyses revealed that the Quality of Search score derived from the Bells test classified Progressive Supranuclear Palsy with a sensitivity of 82%, a specificity of 96%, and Area under the Curve of .90. Given the Bells test is fast to administer (∼5 mins), free, relatively simple to score and already widely used in neuropsychology assessment, it has the potential to be a highly effective addition to the battery of tests used in the differential diagnosis of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy

title: Evolving view on phylogenetic networks
abstract: Reticulate processes such as hybridization, introgression, and horizontal gene transfer cannot be fully represented by a bifurcating tree. Enter phylogenetic networks: first as split graphs to visualize tree discordance, then as explicit probabilistic models that capture biological phenomena. Here, we describe the broad taxonomy of network representations, distinguishing the principal classes of explicit networks, their biological interpretability and our ability to accurately estimate them from empirical data. We also trace the evolution of the main network inferential methods from hybrid detection tests, distance- and subgraph-based amalgamation methods, probabilistic approaches under the multispecies network coalescent, composite-likelihood and divide-and-conquer frameworks, while highlighting the selective pressures of statistical identifiability and computational scalability that have shaped this evolution. As we move towards a network thinking paradigm, previously isolated methodological lineages from population genetics, phylogenomics, and mathematical network theory are now introgressing, uniting diverse network models into a shared framework that can integrate sequence- and species-level reticulate processes, increase robustness to systematic errors, and refine algorithms for genome-scale data, expanding the tree of life into a richer, more entangled yet clearer picture of evolution.

title: Cooperation and privacy-protection strategies for cross platform targeted advertising in competitive markets
abstract: In practice, platform partnerships may be unstable, and privacy protection strategies may vary across platforms. This study examines optimal cooperation and privacy protection strategies for third-party platforms implementing cross-platform targeted advertising in competitive markets. We develop a game-theoretic model involving two competing third-party platforms, one e-commerce platform, consumers, and advertisers. Equilibrium outcomes are derived using backward induction. The model captures platforms' decisions regarding cross-platform cooperation and privacy protection strategies. In cross-platform targeted advertising, cross-platform cooperation does not necessarily confer a competitive advantage on cooperating third-party platforms. Both symmetric and asymmetric cooperation can arise in equilibrium, depending on competition in the consumer and advertiser markets. Privacy protection does not necessarily increase platform profits, and its effects depend on the relative strength of competition along the content and privacy protection dimensions. Third-party platforms do not always choose high levels of privacy protection. Their choices depend on consumer privacy concerns and rivals' strategies, while asymmetric protection can provide a basis for differentiation. This study examines competing third-party platforms' decisions on cooperation with an e-commerce platform and privacy protection in cross-platform targeted advertising. It extends platform coopetition research by explaining how vertical data cooperation reshapes horizontal competition and advances privacy strategy research by examining the relative strength of competition along the content and privacy protection dimensions. The findings help third-party platforms assess when cooperation increases profits and which privacy protection strategy is preferable.

title: Spatial and vertical price transmission in potato markets in India
abstract: This paper has examined the dynamics of price transmission and co-movement across geographically dispersed markets and in the wholesale–retail supply chains for a perishable crop (potato) in eight major Indian cities, evaluating the interconnection among the wholesale and retail prices and market arrivals of the crop. It has applied various unit-root tests, a standard vector autoregressive model, the Granger causality test and a correlation method to monthly potato prices and market arrivals data from January 2010 to December 2022. It has offered evidence for spatial and vertical integration of potato markets. The wholesale prices were transmitted across the cities involved in potato trading. The prices were transmitted between wholesale and retail markets in most cases. While market arrivals have influenced the prices and marketing margins, these factors in turn have some effects on market arrivals in some cities. There exists evidence of significant co-movement of prices in the spatial and vertical markets. In the markets with significant cross-market price transmission, the effects and incentives of any policy are likely to be transmitted to all the markets without requiring much intervention. The policies to reduce price variability and enhance market integration should focus on facilitating trade, improving infrastructure and reducing restrictions on the movement of the commodity across markets. It has applied an alternative methodology to long-range monthly data for a set of objectively selected potato markets representing different locations and market characteristics throughout the country, and conducted market integration analysis, taking into account the effects of market arrivals on the prices.

title: Strategic integration of business intelligence tools to enhance business management efficiency
abstract: This study examines how data and business intelligence (BI) systems support procurement decisions and strategic execution. It aims to improve the efficiency of business management. A five-stage implementation framework is proposed for integrating BI into strategic business execution. The methodology includes technical validation and a case study that assesses the impact of digital transformation and BI adoption on tracking strategic execution and key performance indicators (KPIs). We frame BI adoption within the broader digital transformation (DT) agenda, aligning data, processes and governance to strategic objectives. Research shows that aligning digital transformation initiatives with an organization’s specific operational needs is the most cost-effective path to achieving efficiency. Analysis suggests that a successful digital transformation must be closely linked to the management requirements. Selecting appropriate BI tools is critical to delivering substantial business value. The proposed framework offers managers a structured approach to implementing BI systems aligned with strategic goals. The case study provides actionable insights for professionals aiming to improve operational and management performance through data-driven strategies and digital transformation. The research contributes to the literature on digital transformation by presenting a structured, stage-gated framework for integrating BI tools into strategic management. It offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to enhance performance through data-informed decision-making, differentiating itself through a detailed implementation model developed and illustrated in a procurement context.

title: Islamic corporate social responsibility as a governance-embedded system: evidence from Islamic banks in Malaysia and Indonesia
abstract: Although there has been a rapid rate of expansion observed in the domain of Islamic banking, there remains an inconsistent degree of institutionalisation of Islamic corporate social responsibility (ICSR). The reason is that a higher priority level has been placed on contractual and financial compliance by existing CSR and Shariah governance models, rather than broader socio-economic aspects. The purpose of this study was to develop an ICSR framework to assess the capacity of existing Islamic banking institutions to institutionalise ICSR through relevant governance mechanisms and Islamic social finance instruments, while examining their relationships with socio-economic outcomes. In this investigation, a qualitative multiple-case study design, which involved both Maybank Islamic (Malaysia) and Bank Syariah Indonesia (Indonesia), was employed. Specifically, semi-structured interviews were conducted with a total of 20 purposively selected senior informants, with 10 from each of the two institutions, who were directly involved in the process of ICSR governance and implementation. The interviews, which ranged between 60 and 120 min, were triangulated with corresponding institutional and sustainability documents. After collecting the data, a thematic content analysis was performed through the NVivo software, which incorporated iterative coding, intercoder verification, participant validation and cross-case comparison to identify relevant patterns of ICSR institutionalisation and socio-economic value creation. The findings revealed a clear hierarchy of ICSR institutionalisation, wherein zakat represented the most formally embedded instrument, supported by Shariah oversight, structured procedures, auditing and reporting. Meanwhile, voluntary instruments, including sadaqah and infaq, and developmental instruments, such as qard al-hasan and waqf, exhibited weaker and more fragmented degrees of organisational integration. Four differentiated socio-economic outcome clusters were associated with the above instruments, namely, immediate relief and redistribution (zakat), community trust and relational legitimacy (sadaqah or infaq), economic empowerment (qard al-hasan) and long-term or intergenerational welfare (waqf). Importantly, the interview results demonstrated an institutionalisation–impact paradox, in which instruments associated with greater long-term developmental potential were not equivalent to those most strongly embedded within existing structures of governance. A policy-relevant framework was provided for existing Islamic banking institutions, regulators and Shariah boards to strengthen the governance, coordination, measurement and reporting aspects of relevant ICSR instruments that were often under-institutionalised. The proposed framework could also inform the development of Shariah-specific social responsibility indicators that were aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which could enable more substantive and comparable assessment of ICSR beyond conventional CSR reporting processes. Islamic ethical underpinnings, Shariah governance structures, Islamic social finance tools and various socio-economic outcomes were incorporated in this study into a consolidated and empirically grounded framework. Particularly, it was demonstrated that there were varying levels of institutionalisation and socio-economic value observed in existing ICSR instruments, which highlighted the existence of an institutionalisation–impact paradox. As such, there was a deeper understanding of how Islamic obligations are converted from religious teachings into actual organisational practice and developmental value.

Abundance Redistribution Increases Predator‐Prey Interaction Potentials Among North American Birds
abstract: Species are shifting their geographical ranges, yet the consequences of these spatial redistributions for species interactions have not been examined at broad spatial and temporal scales. Here, we characterize shifts in the potential for predator‐prey interactions among North American birds over the past 50 years. We first predict potential predator‐prey interactions based on existing data, then construct a novel, abundance‐weighted metric of interaction potential for each pair of predator and prey species in local communities. We found nearly universal increases in predator‐prey interaction potentials across North America that are mostly driven by increases in predator abundances. The spatial redistributions of predators and prey lead to turnover of interactions within local communities that are less associated with changes in climate than with human‐induced land use changes. Our results highlight the importance of considering traits, abundances, and species interactions—including known and potential interactions—when studying the ecological consequences of range shifts.

title: Divergent Patterns of Interactions Between Dissolved Organic Matter and Microbial Communities in Mangroves and Salt Marshes
abstract: Mangroves and salt marshes are major blue carbon reservoirs, where dissolved organic matter (DOM) dynamics are co‐regulated by primary production, microbial transformation, and environmental conditions. Understanding whether these two coastal wetlands exhibit fundamentally different DOM–microbe interaction patterns is critical for assessing blue carbon functioning. However, such interactions and their environmental determinants remain unclear. Here, we conduct a continental‐scale comparison between mangroves and salt marshes spanning ~5000 km of China's coastline to elucidate the linkages between DOM molecules and microbial communities. DOM and bacterial β‐diversity are positively correlated in both wetlands, but their respective distance–decay relationships are significant only in salt marshes. DOM–microbe co‐occurrence networks are bacteria‐dominated in both wetlands, but are more complex and positively linked in mangroves, whereas negatively linked in salt marshes. DOM‐gene networks show that carbon fixation and methanogenesis genes are primarily associated with recalcitrant DOM in mangroves, but with labile DOM in salt marshes. Soil pH, together with mean annual temperature, dissolved organic carbon, soil organic carbon, total nitrogen, and amorphous calcium, collectively influence the divergences in DOM composition, microbial community structure, and carbon metabolic functions. These findings offer key insights into DOM–microbe interaction mechanisms and their divergent patterns across “blue carbon” ecosystems.

journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
abstract: Retail procurement decisions are made by forecasting future demand and then optimizing procurement plans under time-varying unit procurement costs and operational constraints. In this predict-then-optimize pipeline, even the same magnitude of prediction error can induce different downstream procurement costs because prices vary over time, and operational constraints can make forecasted demand infeasible when used directly as a procurement plan. As a result, minimizing standard prediction losses, even with weighting schemes, does not necessarily minimize downstream procurement cost. This motivates Decision-Focused Learning (DFL), which trains predictors with respect to downstream decision objectives. Applying DFL to large numbers of consumers requires demand aggregation to smooth noisy individual demand, stabilize forecasts, and prevent downstream optimization from yielding noise-driven decisions while preserving heterogeneity relevant to procurement decisions. We propose a DFL framework with differentiable micro-demand aggregation that jointly trains consumer clustering, aggregate demand forecasting, and downstream procurement optimization in an end-to-end pipeline. In numerical experiments on demand forecasting and electricity retail procurement optimization, the proposed method reduced procurement regret, defined as the cost gap between prediction-based decisions and the full-information optimum, by 25.6% versus a k-means-based prediction-focused baseline and by 3.3% versus its DFL counterpart. Furthermore, this approach exhibits robustness to the number of clusters.

journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
abstract: In recent cases of multivariate time series forecasting, models are facing challenges that are due to complex interactions between multiple variables, rapid regime shifts and extreme events that cause problems, especially in the domain of electricity markets like the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM). In our research, we tried to improve the existing singular value decomposition autoencoder (SVD-AE) by introducing a spectral aspect to the anomaly scoring and coming up with a regularisation framework aimed at increasing the accuracy of the time series foundation model (TSFM). We used 5-minute resolution NEM data to evaluate our framework; specifically, the anomaly detection part was done on multiple variables influencing the Regional Reference Price (RRP), such as demand, generation, interconnector, temporal and weather, but the zero-shot forecasting and fine-tuning of the forecasting part were done solely on raw and regularised RRP against the same original ground truth. The forecasting outputs from our Hybrid-Scored SVD-AE (HS-SVD-AE) are then compared to the existing baseline SVD-AE. The experiments showed that in the fine-tuned scenario of TSFM, our proposed framework outperforms the existing SVD-AE regularisation by a good margin, but in the zero-shot scenario, SVD-AE performs better by a slight difference. Our findings in this research show that explicitly scored spectral information structure can complement multivariate anomaly detection, which produces more robust foundation model forecasting.

journal: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
abstract: Environmental sensor signals, including meteorological, air-quality, and eco-hydrological measurements, are highly characterized by a slowly varying trend and a small number of low-frequency periodic components. In long-term forecasting benchmarks for these signals, the models that explicitly capture trend and seasonality have consistently achieved strong performance. However, in practical deployments, the dominant periods of environmental signals vary between regimes, which heavily forces a deployed forecaster to operate over a wide range of varying prediction horizons H. Standard point forecasting models, such as DLinear, PatchTST, and TimeMixer, tie the output projection weights directly to H. Consequently, any change in the horizon severely increases the decoder parameter count and requires complete, expensive retraining. To the best of our knowledge, no prior studies have proposed a flexible forecasting framework that eliminates this horizon-dependent structural rigidity. Therefore, we propose a novel functional forecasting framework called CoefNet (Coefficient-prediction Network), which approaches long-term time-series forecasting by predicting the coefficients of a continuous function ƒ(t) composed of polynomial and Fourier terms. The decomposition into trend and seasonality is explicitly encoded in the structure of ƒ(t) itself, allowing the same trained coefficients to be evaluated on any arbitrary target grid without additional parameters or retraining. Since a pure polynomial-Fourier basis captures global trend and periodicity but may not capture the detailed local variations of signals, we further propose a per-sub-window low-rank modulation scheme. This adaptable scheme captures localized fluctuations by perturbing the shared coefficients at a minimal 4% parameter overhead. As a result, CoefNet successfully achieves the coarse-to-fine prediction property without requiring post-hoc interpolation. Extensive experimental results on four datasets of real-world environmental sensors demonstrate that the proposed approach is robust against varying horizons, attaining state-of-the-art performance in 13 of 16 settings against nine baselines for standard point forecasting.
