title: When Actors Stop Participating: Delegated Participation and Representative-Centered Organizing
abstract: Organizational theories usually treat participation as actor-bound: the actors whose interests are at stake are expected to occupy the interactions through which outcomes are produced. Agentic artificial intelligence and other autonomous representatives weaken that correspondence. This conceptual article develops a theory of delegated participation, defined as the authorized transfer of communicative, evaluative, coordinative, or exchange-related participation from a principal to a representative. The argument moves beyond treating participation delegation as merely another agency relationship. When representatives operate on multiple sides of an exchange, they form an interaction system that can persist without direct principal participation, reshape the alternatives reaching principals, and separate participation from accountability. The model identifies activity conditions, capability–structure alignment, and authorization as antecedents; bilateral representation and interaction displacement as mechanisms; and symbolic concentration and representative-centered organizing as organizational consequences. The framework contributes by challenging the actor-bound conception of participation, identifying bilateral representation as a discontinuity in organizing, and explaining why declining principal participation may coexist with persistent principal accountability and increasingly consequential symbolic appearances. The article concludes with managerial implications and an empirical research agenda focused on recruitment, procurement, customer service, and AI-mediated negotiation.

title: Towards Fine-grained and Robust Detection of Human-AI Co-authorship
abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) is reshaping how textual content is produced, complicating text provenance, and raising concerns for misinformation, plagiarism, and intellectual property. While prior work on AI-generated text detection has progressed, one-dimensional human-AI co-authorship scores lack signals directly relevant to ``AI involvement''. It remains unclear how adversarial paraphrasing distorts detection signals. In this work, we formulate a discrete-class text provenance detection framework. This framework allows an abstraction of realistic co-authorship scenarios into distinct degrees of AI involvement, differentiating the AI polishing on the surface level from the AI updating the discourse structures. This framework reveals the mechanisms of how adversarial paraphrasing blurs the decision boundaries for co-authorship detectors. To improve robustness of the detectors, we augment training data with adversarial paraphrases generated by the state-of-the-art paraphrasing attack model, exposing detectors to challenging meaning-preserving rewrites. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and generation models demonstrate that adversarial paraphrasing substantially degrades detectors trained only on benign data, while adversarial data augmentation leads to consistent robustness gains and good cross-generator transferability. Overall, our findings highlight the value of discrete-class formulation and principled data augmentation for building reliable detectors of human-AI co-authorship.

title: PIPNet EA for Robust and Explainable Crop Weed Classification Using Enhanced Prototype Evidence Aggregation
abstract: Deep learning models can achieve high accuracy on clean crop–weed images but often lose performance when field images are affected by noise, blur, poor illumination, motion, or compression. This study presents PIPNet-EA, an enhanced prototype-based interpretable prediction framework that combines top-κ spatial evidence aggregation with confidence-weighted prototype reasoning. Five deep learning architectures—ResNet50, ResNet101, ViT-B/16, PIPNet-R50, and PIPNet-R101—were evaluated on two crop–weed image datasets under seven common image corruptions at three severity levels: mild, moderate, and severe. The evaluation generated 210 model–corruption–severity accuracy measurements, while the accuracy retention rate (ARR) was used to quantify the proportion of clean-image performance preserved under degradation. PIPNet-R50 showed the strongest overall robustness. On the challenging field dataset, its mean accuracy was 0.641, 0.568, and 0.437 under mild, moderate, and severe corruption, respectively, compared with 0.594, 0.525, and 0.391 for ResNet50. It retained 98.9%, 87.7%, and 67.5% of its clean performance across the three severity levels, exceeding the corresponding retention of ResNet50. Prototype activation maps remained focused on meaningful plant structures, including leaf tips, midribs, and petiole regions, even under moderate degradation. By combining evidence from multiple spatial locations rather than relying on a single dominant activation, PIPNet-EA reduces the effect of local image corruption while maintaining interpretable predictions. These findings support prototype-based evidence aggregation as a practical approach for developing robust and explainable crop–weed classification systems for precision agriculture.

title: The Cryptocurrency Trend Factor Revisited: Predictive Information, Portfolio Construction, and Pricing Claims
abstract: We reassess five economic claims about the cryptocurrency trend factor (CTREND): cross-sectional return predictability, high risk-adjusted performance, incremental information beyond market, size, and momentum, the ability to replace momentum in factor models, and robustness among large and liquid coins and after trading costs. Our reconstruction and code audit identify issues in information timing, technical indicators, forecast coverage, portfolio formation, and return accounting. We first correct future-information use and related settlement rules, then implement broader corrections to indicators, forecast availability, and portfolio accounting. Without additional coin exclusions, the first stage changes CTREND's mean weekly gross return from 4.07% to 4.25%, annualized Sharpe ratio from 2.08 to 1.48, and weekly alpha relative to published market, size, and momentum factors from 2.77% to 3.06%. After comprehensive correction, these become 0.05%, 0.01, and -1.38%; the alpha is no longer significant. Replacing momentum with CTREND yields an advantage in maximum squared Sharpe ratios of 0.058 in the original implementation, 0.024 after the first-stage correction, and -0.0185 after comprehensive correction, with a statistically significant overall decline. Mean weekly gross returns for the largest 100 coins change from 2.93% to 3.99% to 1.00%, while mean weekly net returns for the full long-short portfolio under the lowest assumed trading costs change from 2.93% to 3.35% to -0.87%. These findings show that reported performance and factor-substitution gains depend materially on implementation and sample composition. We distinguish predictive information, an independent return premium, and the incremental value of replacing an existing factor as separate economic claims.

title: Correlation of Test Load Results of Pile Foundation for Various Selected Models
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyse the foundation of an automated high - bay warehouse using Continuous Flight Auger (CFA) piles. Data regarding the designed structure, geotechnical conditions, pile loads, and allowable differences in pile settlement were obtained from the detailed design, which included CPT probe tests, geological drilling, and laboratory tests of samples collected during drilling. This provided relatively precise data on the geological conditions in the area under consideration. The tests indicated that the area falls into Geotechnical Category 2, and the ground conditions were considered as complex. Due to the presence of the soft soils, a foundation was designed using cast - in - situ CFA piles, which will meet the requirements for the first (ULS) and, above all, the second (SLS) limit state. The primary purpose of the designed piles is to ensure uniform settlement of the foundation slab on which the self - supporting racks of the planned warehouse are placed. This study focused on determining the load - bearing capacity of piles using various calculation methods. The obtained results were compared with the values obtained from finite element method (FEM). The Midas GTS NX program was used. The results finally were compared with the pile load tests.

title: NEUROGENESIS: MECHANISMS, REGULATION, AND IMPLICATIONS FOR BRAIN FUNCTION AND DISEASE
abstract: Adult neurogenesis, the continuous generation of functional neurons from neural stem cells in the mature mammalian brain, represents one of the most remarkable forms of structural plasticity in the central nervous system. Once considered impossible, adult neurogenesis is now recognized as a fundamental process occurring primarily in two canonical neurogenic niches: the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the hippocampal dentate gyrus and the subventricular zone (SVZ) of the lateral ventricles. This review synthesizes current knowledge on adult neurogenesis, covering the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying neural stem cell maintenance and neuronal differentiation, the stages of neurogenesis from proliferation to synaptic integration, the functional contributions of adult-born neurons to learning, memory, and mood regulation, and the modulation of neurogenesis by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. We examine the impact of aging and disease on neurogenesis, with particular emphasis on the ongoing debate regarding adult human neurogenesis. Recent conflicting reports about the extent and persistence of neurogenesis in the adult human brain have highlighted critical methodological challenges and species differences that must be addressed for successful clinical translation. We discuss evidence for and against human adult neurogenesis, the methodological factors contributing to discrepancies, and the implications for understanding human brain function and developing therapeutic strategies. This review also covers therapeutic strategies targeting neurogenic processes, including behavioral interventions, pharmacological approaches, and emerging cell-based therapies. Recent advances in molecular profiling, lineage tracing, and imaging technologies have deepened our understanding while revealing the complexity of neurogenic regulation across species and throughout the lifespan. This review aims to provide researchers, clinicians, and students with an integrative perspective on adult neurogenesis with special attention to translating findings from animal models to human applications.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Driving Business Growth through Adaptive Leadership, Open Innovation, and Market Sensing: The Role of Purple Ocean Strategy in Information Technology Solution Business
abstract: The rapid development of digital technologies and increasing competitive intensity have created significant challenges for information technology (IT) solution businesses seeking sustainable growth. Organizations must continuously adapt to technological changes, customer expectations, and competitive pressures while developing innovative and differentiated solutions. However, limited research has integrated adaptive leadership, open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth within a single research framework. This study aims to investigate the causal factors and relationships among adaptive leadership, open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth in IT solution businesses, and to develop an empirical causal model explaining these relationships. The study employs a quantitative research design supported by qualitative thematic analysis. Data are collected from 400 respondents consisting of business owners, executives, managers, and individuals involved in organizational decision-making. A structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale measures the five major constructs. Descriptive statistics and structural equation modeling (SEM) are employed to assess the measurement model and test the proposed hypotheses. The anticipated results suggest that adaptive leadership positively influences open innovation, market sensing capability, purple ocean strategy formulation, and overall business growth. Open innovation and market sensing capability are expected to positively influence purple ocean strategy formulation and overall business growth. Purple ocean strategy formulation is also expected to contribute positively to organizational growth by strengthening value innovation, customer-centric innovation, competitive differentiation, continuous improvement, and strategic integration. The study is expected to provide theoretical and practical contributions by demonstrating how leadership capabilities, external knowledge, market intelligence, and strategic formulation can be integrated to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainable growth of IT solution businesses.
journal: International Review of Management and Marketing

title: A Hybrid Multi-Objective Optimization Framework for Crop Planting Planning under Digital Economy
abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence and the digital economy in agriculture, traditional crop planting planning still suffers from slow convergence, limited optimization accuracy, and weak adaptability to ecological and market uncertainties. To address these challenges, this study proposes a multi-objective crop planting optimization model that integrates the Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimizer (MOGWO), the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II, and proximal policy optimization, enabling dynamic decision-making driven by multi-source data. Experimental results on two authoritative datasets showed that the model achieved Pareto frontier coverage above 90% and stable convergence within 500 iterations. Multi-scenario simulations indicated that peak annual net profit exceeded 1.8 million yuan, and annual carbon reduction potential generally exceeded 150 tons of CO2, while computation time was maintained at approximately 4.8s per 100 iterations. Overall, the proposed model demonstrates strong robustness, ecological effectiveness, and computational efficiency, supporting intelligent agricultural decision-making under the digital economy framework.
journal: Journal of Engineering, Project, and Production Management

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE INDEPENDENT CURRICULUM ON STUDENT CREATIVITY IN PJOK LEARNING AT ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the Merdeka Curriculum implementation on the development of students' creativity in Physical Education, Sports, and Health (PJOK) learning at elementary schools in Gelumbang District. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach with participants consisting of PJOK teachers and six fifth-grade students from SDN 6 and SDN 9 Gelumbang. Data were collected through observation, interviews, questionnaires, and documentation, and analyzed using Miles and Huberman's model through data reduction, data display, and verification. The results indicate that the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum can enhance students’ creativity in the indicators of fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration, with students from SDN 6 achieving 77–91%, higher than SDN 9, which ranged from 61–83%. Supporting factors include school support and students’ learning motivation, while obstacles involve limited facilities and teachers’ understanding of differentiated learning. This study recommends improving infrastructure, providing teacher training, and expanding further research to optimally support the development of students' creativity.

title: Government Extension, Peer Communication, and Digital Technology Adoption Among Family Farms
abstract: Using survey data from 533 grain-growing family farms in Sichuan Province, this study employs a Poisson model to compare the relationships of government extension (GE) and peer communication (PC) with the number of digital technologies adopted, jointly examines cognitive and ability pathways, and conducts bounded-model, instrumental-variable and omitted-variable sensitivity analyses. The results show that PC has a stronger positive association with the adoption count; when the frequencies of the two channels increase from their respective 25th to 75th percentiles, the average predicted adoption count increases by 0.186 and 0.595 technologies, respectively, with a difference of 0.409 technologies. Perceived usefulness (PU) is a shared cognitive pathway for both channels, with a larger coefficient product for GE along this pathway; PC has a larger coefficient product along the pathway of ability to access socialized agricultural services (SA). The study reveals different linkages of the two information channels with technology cognition and service access, providing empirical evidence for connecting systematic technical information with local user experience.

title: Photorespiratory Engineering from an Evolutionary Perspective: A Constraint-Aligned Evaluation and Validation Framework
abstract: More than two billion years of photorespiratory evolution have shaped three sets of constraints: catalytic constraints associated with Rubisco oxygenase activity; compartmental topology constraints arising from compartmental organization, transport processes, and cofactor coupling; and physiological and ecological constraints arising from integration with metabolic and signaling networks. Photorespiratory engineering has emerged as a key strategy for improving photosynthetic efficiency in C3 crops, yet existing studies have not systematically assessed the practical implications of these constraints. Evaluation metrics remain inconsistent, the scope and depth of stability and risk assessments vary, and methodological heterogeneity hinders comparisons across studies. To address these issues, we synthesize the evolutionary history of photorespiration and findings from previous research to develop an evaluation and validation framework aligned with these constraints. This framework comprises eight assessment dimensions defining what to report, a context matrix specifying the conditions under which assessments should be conducted, and a five-tier validation pipeline defining the sequence of validation steps and the criteria for classifying outcomes. Retrospective application to five published case studies demonstrates that the framework enables consistent classification of outcomes and identifies distinct priorities for further improvement across studies involving different crop species, engineering strategies, and evaluation endpoints. By providing a practical evidence structure that can be updated as new findings emerge, this framework supports the transition from empirical exploration to systematic photorespiratory engineering and facilitates cross-study comparisons and the cumulative synthesis of evidence across assessment dimensions, experimental contexts, and outcomes.

title: A Modeling-Based Predictive Regenerative Braking Strategy for a Parallel P2 Hybrid Electric Vehicle
abstract: Regenerative braking control in a hybrid electric vehicle must be evaluated at both the brake and powertrain levels, and additional recovered energy does not necessarily imply lower fuel consumption. This study examines a preview-aware C3 controller for a midsize parallel P2 hybrid electric vehicle against a causal, state-of-power-constrained C2 controller. C3 changes the desired regenerative torque share during braking and modifies the SOC target and power allocation before predicted deceleration. The controllers were evaluated on FTP-75, WLTP Class 3b and US06 using 100 matched realizations of six uncertain factors per cycle (300 C2–C3 pairs). Mean battery-recovered energy increased by 1.751%, 1.420% and 4.083%, while friction braking energy decreased by 5.100%, 4.393% and 11.842%, respectively. All 300 pairs favored C3 on the three braking metrics. Full-cycle factorial ablations attributed the nominal recovery gain primarily to the braking-torque allocation channel. SOC target preparation alone yielded negligible additional recovery at the tested initial SOC. With the stated algebraic terminal-SOC correction, mean fuel effects were −0.171%, −0.439% and +0.118%, respectively, where positive values indicate a reduction. Direct SOC-matched checks preserved the cycle-dependent sign, but the US06 advantage was only about 0.03–0.05%. Thus, the robust braking-energy benefit and the small, cycle-dependent fuel response arise from distinct control mechanisms. Improved recuperation alone does not establish a fuel-economy benefit.

title: Architectural Design and Internal Working of Health Talk: An Offline-Capable, Multilingual AI Conversational Agent for Clinical Triage and Healthcare Facility Discovery in Regional India
abstract: In developing nations such as India, primary healthcare triage faces acute structural bottlenecks, including severe doctor-to-population deficits in semi-urban and rural agglomerations, fragmented municipal health informatics, and linguistic barriers across heterogeneous regional populations. While modern conversational agents and large language models (LLMs) offer promising interactive capabilities, their direct clinical deployment is severely hampered by pharmaceutical hallucination risks, non-deterministic reasoning trajectories, prohibitive cloud API costs, and an absence of localized Indic language models. To resolve this critical dilemma, this paper presents the complete architectural design, algorithmic foundations, and empirical validation of Health Talk AI—a novel, offline-first, multilingual conversational triage agent specifically engineered for Tier-2 regional healthcare ecosystems such as the Greater Nashik Metropolitan Area in Maharashtra, India. Health Talk decouples clinical urgency categorization from generative text synthesis by introducing an inviolable, deterministic three-tier triage rule engine that executes prior to any natural language parsing. The architecture synthesizes: (1) an emergency finite-state pre-filter for instant red-flag detection; (2) a multilingual Natural Language Processing (NLP) subsystem featuring Devanagari script tokenization, Hindi versus Marathi marker-word frequency ratio disambiguation, and RapidFuzz partial-ratio entity extraction for pain intensity (1–10 scale), temporal duration, and anatomical body parts; (3) an offline-first Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) vector engine utilizing dense multilingual sentence embeddings (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2) coupled with an inviolable cosine dot-product threshold (tau = 0.45) that mathematically eliminates medical hallucinations; (4) a privacy-preserving geospatial discovery subsystem indexing 347 verified healthcare facilities across Nashik using the spherical Haversine metric with two-decimal-place differential coordinate rounding (~1.1 km); and (5) automated state healthcare entitlement checklists (Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana - MJPJAY) paired with multi-lingual emergency first-aid response cards. Evaluated across 91 rigorous automated unit tests, Health Talk achieves a 100% test pass rate, 100% Top-1 retrieval precision on clinical queries in English, Hindi, and Marathi, and an end-to-end execution latency under 28 ms on commodity quad-core CPUs without GPU hardware. This work establishes an authoritative, open-access, zero-cloud-cost framework for safe, equitable, and privacy-compliant digital clinical triage.

title: Deep Learning Based Crop Health Monitoring Using IoT Sensors
abstract: This paper proposes a smart crop-health monitoring system that combines Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with deep-learning-based image analysis. Crop health is affected by soil moisture, temperature, humidity, light and plant diseases. Periodic manual inspection may delay the identification of crop stress. The proposed approach collects field conditions through low-cost sensors and captures leaf images using a camera. Sensor readings and images are processed by a controller or computer. A trained deep learning model can analyse leaf images for visible symptoms, while sensor readings provide information about growing conditions. The system aims to display crop information and generate alerts to support timely crop-care decisions. This is an introductory project proposal; performance results will be added after implementation and testing

title: Triple bubbles in the hyperbolic plane
abstract: We prove that the standard triple bubble uniquely minimizes perimeter among clusters in the hyperbolic plane with three prescribed positive finite areas. The standard family admits global pressure coordinates, and its volume differential is the negative of a positive definite grounded weighted graph Laplacian. A normalized perimeter excess attains a comparison minimum under a perimeter bound and gives a strict comparison between actual and model pressures. Component relabeling reduces the possible topologies to an all-boundary network or a 4-daisy. Discrete comparisons exclude the 4-daisy; pressure-preserving face deletion reduces the remaining network to the standard tetrahedral configuration.

title: Mathematical modeling to study combination strategies for neural stem cell therapy in glioblastoma
abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are a promising treatment platform due to their ability to cross the restrictive blood-brain barrier and migrate toward damaged regions of the brain. These properties can be leveraged to target brain tumors, as NSCs can infiltrate tumor lesions and deliver therapeutic agents such as drugs, oncolytic viruses, and genetic materials. Despite the advantages of NSCs, translational challenges remain, including patient-specific chemotactic signaling and immune responses, variability in migration and localization at tumor sites, and optimization of delivery strategies. In this work, we focus on intranasal delivery of NSCs and combination strategies for the treatment of brain cancer. To investigate strategies for improving NSC arrival at the tumor site, we developed a hybrid mathematical model of NSC migration that couples an agent-based model with a partial differential equation, where cell motion is guided by the spatial dynamics of chemoattractants. Using data collected from a murine model and our mathematical model, we {investigate treatment-motivated downstream effects associated with three combination strategies:} (1) IL-10 pretreatment, (2) CXCL12 pretreatment, and (3) radiotherapy. We find that IL-10 pretreatment improves NSC arrival numbers at tumor only under the Gaussian chemoattractant profile, whereas CXCL12 pretreatment moderately improves arrival numbers when the tumor is located in the anterior brain. Radiotherapy significantly enhances the tumor arrival under uniform profiles. These simulation studies suggest that both treatment strategies and chemoattractant distribution influence intranasal NSC delivery, and the proposed model can be used to predict how targeted modulation of chemotactic signaling and tissue-guided migration may improve delivery outcomes.

title: A Self-Exploring and Self-Evolving Paradigm for Adaptive Edge AI Development
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit powerful code generation abilities, fostering agentic systems to automate edge AI application development. However, existing agents typically operate via fixed agentic workflows and predefined design spaces, struggling to handle rapidly evolving demands of real-world scenarios (e.g., heterogeneous data modalities, diverse task pipelines). Unlike prior systems that treat LLMs mainly as code generators following rigid workflows, we fully exploit their reasoning capabilities to allow agents to determine their own workflows on the fly. To this end, we propose SE2, a self-exploring and self-evolving paradigm for adaptive edge AI development. Inspired by human learning processes, we distill development into four atomic operations (retrieve, reason, code, test), and empower agents to explore workflows by dynamically and adaptively selecting an appropriate next operation based on the current context. Extensive evaluations show that, with adaptive workflows, the synthesized programs achieve up to 26% higher accuracy and consume 28% lower resources than state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining superior adaptability to unforeseen edge AI scenarios. This highlights the potential of reasoning-driven adaptive agentic workflow in edge AI development.

title: Toward Executable Multi-framework Front-end Code Generation with Self-Correction
abstract: Generating codes from UI screenshots has recently benefited from MLLMs, yet existing methods centered on HTML targets and transfer poorly to multi-frameworks such as React, Vue, and Angular. However, unlike HTML, which does not entail compilation issues, generating executable code in multi-framework settings is more challenging due to framework-specific differences in syntax and failure modes, as well as the need to maintain global consistency across files. To address this problem, we study executable multi-framework front-end code generation and propose MESCoder, a tree-structured self-corrective generation framework. Our method first extracts a structural scaffold from the screenshot and then constructs sub-trees and assembly relations step by step, transforming large project generation into a sequence of localized decisions. On top of this scaffold, we introduce a unified Project Agent that continuously revises its own partial project under runtime sandbox feedback and dynamically chooses between local repair and cluster level repair. For training, we adopt a two-stage strategy that first initializes the policy offline to learn basic multi-framework generation and repair priors, and then refines it with online reinforcement learning to optimize long horizon executability and final page quality. The resulting framework models multi-framework executability as a conditioned project state transition process and improves the stability and quality of complex front end generation through self correction. Experiments show that our method improves executability, while narrowing the visual-fidelity gap to HTML-based generation. Code is available at https://github.com/leo-lilinxiao/MESCoder.

title: Learning by Doing: Autonomously Compiling and Curating Agent Skills from Verified Traces
abstract: Memory systems for production LLM agents mostly store semantic memory (facts about users and domains) or episodic memory (earlier interactions). Research systems such as Trace2Skill, WikiSkill, and SkillRevise learn procedures from agent runs, package them as Skills, and evaluate them on benchmarks. We describe Zep Agent Skills, a production service that gives deployed agents this procedural memory. The service uses only verified attempts as evidence, cites the supporting events for each field of a Skill, and governs the admission and distribution of each Skill version. The service records each task attempt as a Trace with ordered events, an outcome, and a verification strength. A compiler with separate Reflector and Curator roles turns verified Traces into versioned Skills. Scans and admission gates control which candidates become active, and verified use outcomes change the search rank of each Skill. The Agent Skills format is an open standard that Anthropic originated and donated to the Agentic AI Foundation, so any host of the format can load a compiled Skill. Agents retrieve Skills through lexical search with progressive disclosure, over an API or MCP. We evaluate Zep Agent Skills on $τ^3$-bench banking, AppWorld, and EnterpriseOps-Gym. Skills compiled from the Traces of a teacher model increase the pass rate of three weaker executor models on the same tasks, at every reasoning effort, by 4.5 to 18.8 points. Most of the gain is on the tasks that the teacher solved. On ALFWorld, Skills compiled from the runs of a small model give a gain similar to or larger than the gain that prior work reports for continuous fine-tuning, with no training.

title: Log-Sobolev inequality for the sine-Gordon model in the subcritical regime
abstract: We prove a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the massive two-dimensional sine-Gordon model throughout the subcritical range $0<β<8π$. For fixed mass, volume and arbitrary real coupling, the constant has a positive lower bound independent of the lattice spacing. When the dimensionless coupling is small, the lower bound is also uniform in volume and approaches the Gaussian constant as the coupling tends to zero. This extends the known range $β<6π$ and gives a rate of entropy decay for the reversible Langevin dynamics that remains positive as the cutoff is removed. The proof follows the Polchinski flow to a positive physical scale, where the Hamiltonian is a bounded perturbation of a uniformly convex one. For interactions invariant under constant field shifts, spatial differences bound their curvature by the gradient energy. For the oscillating part, we compare Gaussian integration with an average in which the original cosine phase fluctuates independently of the remaining variables. We estimate the comparison error at an intermediate scale, then differentiate the remaining Gaussian density. This preserves both phase damping and spatial decay without assuming bounds on second derivatives of the incoming local terms. The resulting strict gain between scales closes the estimates for every fixed $β<8π$.

title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. The past several decades has seen a large number of experimental studies of these effects, as well as the development of theory to explain the results. In this Perspectives article we use classical electromagnetic (EM) simulations to examine how the localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) of metal nanoparticles and propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) in extended metal nanostructures (wires/plates/films) are affected by interactions with a molecular/semiconductor system. The classical EM simulations are complemented by a quantum model for plasmon-exciton coupling based on the macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (MQED) framework, along with Holstein vibrations. The goals are to show how LSPR spectra and SPP dispersion curves/attenuation constants changes as the strength of the molecular/semiconductor electronic transition increases and the system evolves from an energy transfer limit to strong coupling, and to provide an understanding of the decay processes from both classical EM and MQED perspectives.

title: Latent Harness: Compiling Agent Behaviors into Post-Block Activation Shifts
abstract: Harness engineering and self-evolving agents improve language-model agents quickly, yet their gains live outside the model. The harness is re-sent and re-paid on every call, and the standard route to internalization is a weight update that is costly to iterate and fixed once merged. We propose compiling the harness instead. Latent Harness distills an external condition into a rank-8 activation shift. The shift is applied at the output of every decoder block of a frozen backbone, at 0.03-0.05% of parameters. The condition is either an explicit process-level behavior instruction or the behavioral contract of an agentic harness. At inference the compiled bundle carries no harness text and adds no tokens. It exposes three runtime controls for injection strength, injection phase, and shift-space mixing. Compiled behaviors recover the source-harness gain in 8 of 10 preregistered settings. Where the explicit source pays the heaviest per-call token tax, the compiled form exceeds it. The same bundles transfer zero-shot across tasks (5 of 7 pairs positive) and compose in shift space, while stacked text instructions interfere destructively. Used as a search space, they lift budget-matched harness search by 1.45 times. On three agentic benchmarks the operator aligns policy to the harness con- tract. Under matched data, capacity, and effective strength it outperforms same-capacity LoRA, which needs 11.1 times the parameters to reach the same band, and it regresses nothing where the base policy is already strong. Across 1B-to-8B models the method skeleton is invariant while gain locations move with the model-task pair, which delimits where compiled harnesses should be deployed.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Joint Generative Modeling of Fault Event Sequences and Sensor Time Series in Solar PV Plants
abstract: This paper presents a multimodal generative model designed to simulate a solar energy plant system for predictive maintenance and fault prediction. We propose a novel approach to enhance system generation through conditional generation by leveraging both event sequences and time-series data and improve next event prediction. The framework employs a Transformer Hawkes Process (THP) to encode event data and an iTransformer to encode time-series data, integrated via a co-attention mechanism that effectively captures cross-modal dependencies between discrete events and continuous signals. From these integrated representations, we employ two specialized decoders for simulation: a Conditional Latent Diffusion Model (CLDM) for modeling future sensor trajectories and the Score Matching-based UnceRtainty quantiFication for Transformer Hawkes Process (SMURF-THP) for high-fidelity event prediction. This dual-decoder strategy supports uncertainty-aware, history-conditioned simulation by rolling the model forward for a specified number of generation iterations, producing finite stochastic scenarios rather than deterministic extrapolations over the full observational record. Evaluated on a comprehensive dataset from the Red Rock Solar Site in Arizona, our approach improves aggregate event-prediction F1 relative to baselines and supports applications in predictive maintenance, fault detection, and energy optimization for solar power systems.

title: Variational learning of energy-stable macroscopic flow equations from microscopic laws
abstract: We present a generalized variational approach for constructing energy-stable macroscopic partial differential equations (PDEs) directly from microscopic physical laws. Rather than fitting the PDE evolution for prescribed variables from macroscopic trajectories, we construct an extendable variational structure by adjoining auxiliary variables to seek autonomous reduced dynamics in an enlarged state space. By defining these variables as micro--macro encoders with explicit microscopic counterparts, we cast the learning problem as the sample-wise joint identification of the reduced state representation and the variational ingredients from time-discrete data, enabling systematic law-level transfer across scales. The resulting PDEs preserve frame indifference, physical constraints, and energy stability by construction, and admit a fluctuation--dissipation-consistent stochastic extension. Numerical results for the non-Newtonian hydrodynamics of polymeric fluids show that the learned models capture the viscoelastic responses induced by nonlinear and heterogeneous molecular interactions beyond empirical closures.

title: $TF^2$-Steering: Action Refinement with Tactile Forecasts and Feedback via Velocity-Field Steering
abstract: Tactile sensing plays a crucial role in everyday human interaction. Consider inserting a plug into a tight socket, vision alone provides limited guidance during the final insertion stage, and we instead rely on both anticipated contact and realized tactile feedback to ajust the insertion motion. The same capability is equally important for robots, particularly in dexterous manipulation tasks. Yet many contemporary robot policies remain vision-dominant. This visual bias, compounded by limited tactile data and sparse contact events, can cause directly incorporated tactile signals to be ignored or even compromise the policy's pretrained capabilities, yielding degrading performance as observed in our experiments. We present $TF^2$-Steering, which refines actions via learned residual steering of the flow-matching action expert's velocity field, using a tactile mixture-of-experts architecture to integrate both tactile forecasts and real-time tactile feedback. Together with specific designed three stages training recipe, $TF^2$-Steering enables tactile signals to correct and, when necessary, redirect the flow-matching action-generation process, while building on the strong action-generation capacity of the vision-based foundation policy. Extensive experiments across six simulated and six real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of $TF^2$-Steering. It outperforms the strongest evaluated baselines by 10.7 percentage points in average simulation success rate and 9.1 percentage points in average real-world progress success rate. Project page: https://yiming-cc.github.io/tf2-steering/.

title: FedUDG: Federated Domain Generalization with Unlabeled Clients
abstract: Federated domain generalization (FDG) aims to learn models that generalize reliably to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments without centralizing client's data. However, existing FDG methods assume that all source clients have labeled data, limiting their ability to leverage the abundant unlabeled client data available in practice. To address this limitation, we propose FedUDG. At the federation level, FedUDG utilizes a parameter-functional differentiation strategy that maintains a semantic anchor updated solely using ground-truth labels. The remaining parameters absorb knowledge from unlabeled domains under bounded aggregation, preventing domain-biased noise from eroding the class semantics. Within each unlabeled client, FedUDG utilizes a student-teacher framework with two complementary objectives: (1) semantic self-training on high-confidence samples, using the functional differentiation between the semantic anchor and classifier to constrain the model to learn semantically pure and cross-domain stable features; and (2) label-free representation distillation on all unlabeled samples to stabilize learning under appearance variations. Together, these objectives guide the model toward a transferable feature space, while mitigating overfitting to domain-specific characteristics. Furthermore, to address the lack of systematic evaluation of FDG under formal privacy constraints, we develop a sample-level differentially private extension, DP-FedUDG, to quantify the trade-off between privacy and OOD generalization. Across four evaluation protocols, FedUDG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/Jr10426/FedUDG

title: AI-Aided and AI-Oriented Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation: A Survey
abstract: The evolution from 5G to 6G networks marks a transition toward the "intelligence of everything." While 5G enables enhanced connectivity, 6G aspires to embed intelligence directly into communication infrastructures, creating systems that are adaptive, context aware, and capable of autonomous decision making. Realizing such systems depends on harmonizing three fundamental functions that compete for shared network resources and often pursue conflicting goals: (i) sensing for environmental and contextual information acquisition, (ii) communication for reliable and timely information exchange, and (iii) computation for information processing and decision making. This harmonization necessitates shifting from independent optimization to their joint design as a unified system, a paradigm known as Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation (ISCC). In parallel, AI has emerged both as an enabling tool for ISCC optimization and as a workload whose requirements influence ISCC system design. This survey comprehensively examines ISCC from this dual perspective by distinguishing between AI-aided ISCC, in which learning-based methods support the joint design and optimization of sensing, communication, and computation, and AI-oriented ISCC, in which these functions are jointly configured to support learning, inference, and distributed intelligence. The survey further examines the co-design of AI and ISCC, where AI requirements and ISCC constraints jointly shape system and model decisions. It further provides a comparative synthesis of the resulting design approaches, system architectures, performance metrics, and evaluation practices, relates these developments to application-specific requirements across different domains, and identifies open research problems toward scalable, adaptive, and trustworthy AI-ISCC systems.

title: Generative Modeling with Continuous Flows: Sample Complexity of Flow Matching
abstract: Flow matching has emerged as a promising alternative to diffusion-based generative modeling, offering a continuous-time ordinary differential equation formulation with fast sampling and a simple regression-based training objective. Despite its empirical success, some theoretical analyses idealize the learning procedure by assuming that the velocity field is obtained by exact empirical risk minimization. This assumption does not reflect the practical finite-dataset setting, where the empirical flow-matching loss is only approximately minimized by a finite number of stochastic-gradient updates. We develop an empirical-risk-minimizer-free analysis for flow matching that explicitly accounts for both finite-sample statistical error and finite-time empirical optimization error. Our analysis considers a finite dataset of \(N\) flow-matching samples and a learned parameter \(θ_T\) obtained after \(T\) stochastic gradient updates on the empirical objective. Under regularity assumptions on the interpolation path, sub-exponential source and target distributions, approximation by a bounded-parameter smooth neural velocity class, empirical-loss optimization, and uniform flow stability, we prove a guarantee that holds with high probability over the finite training dataset and in expectation over the stochastic-gradient randomness. The resulting bound separates approximation error, statistical error from the finite dataset, tail error from unbounded source and target distributions, and empirical optimization error from approximate minimization of the finite-sample objective.

title: Principled Human-AI Collaboration in Agentic Workflows
abstract: Organizations adopting AI face the challenge of deciding which outputs can be released without human review while meeting the quality standards of human experts. We develop a statistical framework for delegating tasks between experts and black-box generate-verify workflows, in which AI-generated answers are verified and revised over multiple rounds. Before deployment, human experts evaluate selected outputs, and their judgments are used to calibrate the verifier threshold and number of attempts. Our method selects the policy with the highest estimated automation rate among statistically approved candidates, without modifying the generator or verifier. We establish finite-sample control of the error rate among released outputs, characterize the expert evaluations sufficient to attain a target automation rate, and derive a minimax lower bound establishing rate optimality in the quality margin and required confidence. In a MultiHiertt financial question-answering case study, average held-out automation increases from 2.50% to 24.17% as expert evaluations accumulate, while released-output error rates remain around 1.20%. In contrast, heuristics that release answers after consistently high verifier scores either violate the 5% error tolerance or automate at most 1.30% of tasks. Synthetic experiments further examine these theoretical predictions under controlled settings.

title: MemHarmBench: Evaluating Cross-Session Prompt Injection in Memory-Persistent AI Agents
abstract: AI agents often rely on persistent memory to retain user preferences and operational rules across sessions. However, this capability introduces a new safety risk: malicious instructions from messages, documents, or Web content can be retained in memory and influence future tasks even after the original attack content is removed. Existing attack success metrics, however, fail to capture who is affected and how attacks translate into downstream harm during otherwise normal task execution. We introduce MemHarmBench, a victim-centric benchmark for evaluating cross-session prompt injection in memory-persistent AI agents. MemHarmBench considers three categories of potential victims: users, workspace/project owners, and external stakeholders. Our evaluation first exposes an agent to malicious instructions and tests whether they are retained in memory. We then remove the attack content and initiate a new session with a legitimate task while preserving the agent's memory. We jointly evaluate whether the agent follows the attacker's intent, completes the legitimate task, and exhibits observable execution anomalies. Across multiple agent systems, we find that cross-session attacks can remain behaviorally stealthy: agents often complete tasks normally and exhibit no detectable anomalies while still making critical decisions aligned with the attacker's intent. By connecting malicious memory retention to downstream decisions and affected parties, MemHarmBench provides a systematic framework for exposing safety risks that conventional attack- and task-success metrics may overlook. We publicly release MemHarmBench at https://github.com/Kirito14IT/MemHarmBench.

title: ODE Policy: Robot Learning via Action Dynamics, Not Actions
abstract: Most robot policies, whether trained by imitation learning (IL) or reinforcement learning (RL), map observations to action values at discrete control steps and leave the continuity of physical motion to be learned implicitly. We propose ODE policy, which learns the dynamics of the action rather than the action itself. A neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) learns the vector field of the action by matching the integrated actions to the targets over short action chunks in IL and single control steps in RL. A lightweight diversity head captures multi-modal behavior by randomizing the direction of the field. At deployment, each action is integrated from the previous one, so the executed trajectory is continuous by construction. We evaluate it as a visuomotor policy, as the action head of vision-language-action (VLA) and world action models (WAMs), and as the actor of model-based RL against 14 baselines on unimanual, bimanual, dexterous, locomotion, and loco-manipulation tasks. In IL, against flow matching, it reaches 5.9$\times$ the success, 5.4$\times$ the generalization, and 3.9$\times$ the mode balance after one epoch, and generates actions 10.8$\times$ faster. It mostly moves more smoothly than human demonstrations. On 14 real-world tasks across single-arm, dual-arm, dexterous, and humanoid robots, it achieves the highest success rate. In RL, it further speeds up SuperMimic for humanoid motion tracking and smooths its actions. Efficient in learning, data, parameters, and execution, ODE policy offers a promising path to scaling robot learning.

title: Teleoperation System for Service Robots using Virtual Reality Headset and Pose Estimation
abstract: This paper presents a teleoperation system for service robots that integrates human pose estimation with virtual reality (VR) to enable intuitive remote control. By using the Mediapipe framework for 2D pose detection and extending it with RGB-D data from the Intel RealSense D455 camera, a comprehensive 3D human pose estimation is achieved. This data is then mapped to the robot's kinematics, allowing the operator to control the robot's movements naturally. A VR interface was developed to provide an immersive perspective, enhancing the operator's situational awareness. Real-world experiments were conducted using the CHARMIE service robot to validate the system's effectiveness in tasks involving object manipulation. While the current system successfully demonstrates the potential of VR-based teleoperation, challenges remain in accurately capturing certain joint angles (e.g., wrist yaw) and ensuring precise mapping between human and robot movements. Future work includes the integration of inertial measurement units (IMUs) for improved rotational tracking and the implementation of more advanced control algorithms. Overall, this research contributes to the development of more intuitive and effective teleoperation systems for service robots, facilitating their deployment in complex and dynamic environments. This work further introduces a novel approach to teleoperation by combining RGB-D sensing with an innovative algorithm for real-time joint angle computation using Mediapipe, enhancing the precision of human-robot motion mapping and enabling immersive control through a VR interface. These contributions represent significant advancements in the field of human-robot interaction, particularly for service robot applications.

title: LADA: A differential algebra-based simulation package for arbitrary-order charged-particle and light optics
abstract: LADA computes charged-particle and light-optical transfer maps by differential algebra in Python, with run-time order selection validated through order nine. It combines these established map methods with ATIMA-based stopping, straggling and scattering, the GLOBAL, CHARGE and ETACHA charge-state models, EPAX fragmentation, six-dimensional integration through measured or computed RF fields with reference-energy rebasing, and section-wise particle tracking with aperture and RF-window losses. Maps retain analytic dependence on external parameters; contraction with input moments gives beam observables and their sensitivities without particle tracking at each setting. Lattice import from COSY, MAD-X, Xsuite and MIRKO provides per-record status and comparisons with available codes. NumPy is the only required dependency. On the HHT benchmark, the optional compiled DA kernel on eight cores matches COSY in performance at orders 3 and 5 and is 1.8 and 2.9 times faster at orders 7 and 9. Applications include the SIBAF irradiation facility through CALINA, proton microscopy and beam-line studies at GSI and FAIR.

title: MemRole: From Memories to Decisions for Long-Horizon Reasoning in Role-Playing Agents
abstract: LLM-based role-playing agents are fluent at imitating a character's style, yet struggle to make role-consistent decisions over long narrative horizons. Such decisions are shaped by experiences spanning many prior scenes, which are often partial and may point in different directions. Existing methods inject cross-scene memories as context, but do not reason about how past events shape a character's current motivations and behavior. We propose MemRole, a framework that makes this memory-to-decision process explicit. It introduces Long-Horizon Memory Thinking (LHMT), a reasoning schema that decomposes hidden reasoning into context understanding, memory activation, and response strategy planning, trained on a novel-derived dataset whose character-grounded, timeline-constrained memory pools limit each character to what it could plausibly know at the current narrative point. Beyond supervised fine-tuning, we propose Self-Refining On-Policy Self-Distillation (SR-OPSD): the model critiques its own rollouts against the reference under a data-driven rubric, and a critique-conditioned teacher view of the same model distills token-level guidance back into the policy. MemRole-32B improves over its backbone by 15.2 points on memory-grounded role-playing, performs on par with frontier LLMs such as GPT-5.4, and achieves the best character-motivation recognition accuracy on CroSS-MR.

title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
abstract: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (35.9%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

title: Learning AI Agents, Market Makers, and Stress in Automated Markets
abstract: Automated markets increasingly route order flow from learning trading agents through automated market makers (AMMs). We model trader archetypes as AI agents defined by their reward functions and analyze the feedback they create on a constant-product AMM. Herd-dominated and arbitrage-dominated markets of equal size have identical return distributions and turnover, so no rule based on volatility, value-at-risk, stress frequency, or volume can tell them apart; yet their stress episodes differ in length by a factor unbounded in the feedback-to-noise ratio $β/s$. Serial statistics identify the feedback sign from $Θ((s/β)^2\log(1/δ))$ observations, and this rate is tight. When agents trade together, profit-seeking agents ride herds rather than lean against them, leading to all-or-nothing participation. Spread-earning market makers restore stability but make liquidity fragile, with discontinuous collapse and hysteresis; maker--taker pricing, not a uniform fee, is the effective instrument.

title: The Kinetic Basis of the Genetic Code
abstract: The origin of the genetic code is an enigma, requiring explanations for the emergence of degeneracy, the organizational structure of the code, and the correspondence between codons and amino acids. Here, we use the asymmetric cooperativity model to show that these features arise from asymmetric cooperativity in codon-anticodon association process. We first provide mechanistic and evolutionary accounts of wobble base pair degeneracy, without providing any preferential treatment to the third position. The model, with four tunable parameters, reproduces the organizational structure of the genetic code, and provides theoretical codon-anticodon association times. Although ribosomal kinetic data are not used in parameter estimation, these theoretical association times correlate with experimentally determined ribosomal residence times (r=0.73). The resulting timescales, extending over four decades, also exhibit correlations with diverse physicochemical properties of amino acids, at multiple timescales, motivating a nonequilibrium picture in which energy released during codon-anticodon association is transferred to its cognate amino acid to be dissipated into water. Finally, without incorporating information about aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases or further parameter adjustment, the model recovers the division of amino acids associated with the two aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase classes, with a combined segregation score of 0.92 ( p~10^{-8}). These results suggest that wobble degeneracy, genetic-code organization, translation kinetics, amino-acid physicochemistry, and the two-class organization of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases may reflect a common underlying kinetic constraint. We propose that non-equilibrium, asymmetrically cooperative kinetics, that possibly underlie DNA/RNA replication process, also provided a physical basis upon which the genetic code and its subsequent translation machinery evolved.

title: MEX: The Musical Expectation Benchmark Suite
abstract: We propose the Musical Expectation (MEX) benchmark suite for perceptually validating computational models of musical expectation, i.e., models that estimate music information dynamics (MID) measures of perceived musical expectations, such as surprisal or uncertainty from symbolic music or musical audio. MEX collects and extends tasks for evaluating such models previously proposed in music information retrieval and cognitive sciences using standard datasets, and evaluates whether: (1) proposed MID measures decrease with repetition due to in-context learning of the computational model, (2) peaks in such measures align with boundaries of music segments, (3) pitch surprisal and uncertainty estimated from audio are consistent with those modeled in event-based symbolic music, (4) proposed MID measures can predict electrophysiological responses to music. We stress that this benchmark suite does not provide an exhaustive computational characterization of music expectation. Rather, we envision this as an active, interdisciplinary initiative, with benchmarks evolving as our understanding of the underlying perceptual processes deepens. We provide open-access code https://github.com/musicperceptmodeling/mex to estimate surprisal and uncertainty from audio using baseline models, run the tasks on standard datasets, and include utilities for running the tasks with users' own data.

title: Missingness-Aware Prior-Data Fitted Network for Irregular Clinical Time-Series
abstract: Clinical time series are irregularly observed with laboratory measurements recorded at uneven intervals and observation patterns often reflecting patient state, clinical concern, and site-specific practice. Consequently, missingness is not merely a nuisance factor but an informative signal for prediction. We propose a Missingness-Aware Prior-Data Fitted Network (MA-PFN) for irregular clinical time-series prediction. MA-PFN first learns a diffusion-based prior over joint laboratory value and observation-mask trajectories from source-domain electronic health records, capturing both physiological dynamics and measurement processes. Synthetic trajectories sampled from this prior are then transformed into context-query tasks to train a PFN-style conditional predictor. Once trained, the model performs prediction for new admissions in a single forward pass, requiring neither retraining nor parameter adaptation on target datasets. The framework naturally supports both imputation and forecasting through different context-query constructions. We conduct internal validation on a held-out MIMIC-III test set and external validation on eICU, evaluating both imputation and forecasting and assessing cross-domain generalization under shifts in patient populations, clinical practices, and observation mechanisms. MA-PFN achieves the best performance across all evaluated settings, with Overall/Macro nRMSD ranging from (0.193/0.186) for internal imputation to (0.297/0.297) for external forecasting, without target-domain adaptation. These results demonstrate that learning missingness-aware task priors enables accurate and transferable clinical time-series prediction under informative missingness.

title: Quantizing Recurrent Language Models Is Easier Than You Think
abstract: Linear recurrences are becoming an increasingly common building block in large language models, replacing the growing KV cache of softmax attention with a fixed-size recurrent state that enables efficient decoding. However, the quantization stack has largely been developed around softmax Transformers, whose numerical properties and inference state differ from those of recurrent models. Our goal is to understand these differences and study the design space of quantization methods for recurrent models. In our analysis, we differentiate between two targets. First, extra-state quantization concerns weights and activations outside the recurrent state, whose distributions are shaped indirectly by the sequence mixer during training. In controlled 1.3B parameter models, we find that decayed recurrences develop weaker residual outlier channels than softmax attention and are therefore easier to quantize without incoherence processing. Second, intra-state quantization concerns the recurrent state itself during decode, where repeated updates create a different numerical problem from KV cache quantization. We instantiate our findings as LoReS, a state quantization pipeline combining value-axis scale grouping to match output channel magnitude, decay-based mixed-precision to protect slowly decaying heads or channels, and stochastic rounding to limit error accumulation under repeated requantization. Across Qwen-3.5 9B, Nemotron-H 8B, and Kimi-Linear 48B-A3B, LoReS supports robust 8-bit state quantization and lower effective precision on shorter decode horizons. We implement LoReS in vLLM and demonstrate end-to-end decode speedups.

title: The Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the Cramér--Lundberg model with Erlang $E_2(μ)$ claims: spectrum, exact moments and matrix reduction
abstract: We study the Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the classical Cramér--Lundberg model with claims having an Erlang distribution of shape parameter 2. We derive an integro-differential equation with two boundary conditions. For every positive discount rate, we show that its characteristic polynomial has one negative root and two distinct positive roots. Boundedness excludes the growing exponential term and yields a representation of the transform as a sum of two decaying exponentials. We construct a finite-dimensional matrix reduction of the convolution chain. For a model parameter set, we obtain exact expressions for the ruin probability, the mean time of ruin, and higher moments, including the third moment at zero initial surplus. We prove analyticity in the discount rate and justify the resulting moment series. We consider the analytic continuation of the representation to negative discount rates separately. For Erlang claims with an arbitrary positive integer shape parameter, we establish a closed linear system and the asymptotics of the root continuing the zero root at zero discount.

title: Reduction of the integro-differential equation to an ordinary differential equation in ruin models with investment in a risky asset
abstract: We study ruin models with the surplus invested in a risky asset and Erlang-distributed claims: non-life insurance, annuity payments and the mixed model. Assuming that the integro-differential equation for the survival probability has a classical twice continuously differentiable solution, we prove that this solution satisfies a linear ordinary differential equation. We construct explicit annihilating operators and write the coefficients of the reduced equation in closed form through binomial coefficients (for the mixed model with equal shape parameters). A converse criterion is obtained: a bounded solution of the reduced equation satisfies the integro-differential equation if and only if the residual vanishes at zero initial capital together with its derivatives of order below that of the annihilator. The exponent of the power branch at infinity is determined by the parameters of the risky asset alone and does not depend on the shape parameter. For the mixed model we classify the fundamental set of solutions: the exponentially growing modes are excluded by boundedness. The connection coefficient of the power branch is nonzero by a known power-law lower bound for the ruin probability, and in the annuity model by the reduced equation and the boundary condition at zero. Hence the ruin probability has power-law asymptotics with a positive constant for all shape parameters and all positive exponents, and a complete asymptotic expansion up to a multiplicative constant in all three models. For non-life insurance with Erlang claims of order two the expansion coefficients are computed by an explicit recurrence.

title: Federated Estimation of Loading Spaces in Tensor Factor Models under Differential Privacy
abstract: Tensor factor models provide low-dimensional representations of tensor-valued observations while preserving their multiway structure. When these observations are held by different clients, privacy constraints may prevent them from being pooled for centralized analysis. We study estimation of common loading spaces in Tucker tensor factor models under federated differential privacy, allowing heterogeneous sample sizes, privacy budgets, and factor strengths. The proposed method combines private stability testing, Huber aggregation, and Gaussian perturbation at each client with weighted aggregation at the server. We establish non-asymptotic upper bounds governed by a scaled harmonic mean of the squared local error rates, and prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors under strong factors, fixed factor ranks, and fixed noise variance. We further develop a private calibration procedure that selects the local tuning parameters and aggregation weights without knowledge of the noise level or client-specific factor strengths. The resulting adaptive estimator preserves the privacy guarantee and attains the error rate obtained with oracle tuning. We illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators through simulation experiments and an application to a Meditation Traits EEG dataset.

title: AgenticMobility: An Open-Source Platform for Multi-AI-Agent Mobility Dynamics
abstract: Understanding mobility dynamics and the effects of urban transportation management policies requires examining how individual travel decisions, traffic conditions, and policy interventions influence one another over time. We present AgenticMobility, an open-source experimental platform for studying how mobility AI agents and other AI agents interact, adapt through repeated experience, and collectively shape mobility outcomes. Persistent agents retain identities and relevant states across rounds, with explicit interfaces defining information access, admissible actions, and decision schedules; linked records trace decisions, execution, and feedback. In the current implementation, large language model (LLM) agents act as travelers choosing routes and departure times and as a manager periodically adjusting link charges within MATSim. A preliminary demonstration spans 100 simulated days in each of five configurations, with one run per configuration and a shared simulation seed. In the joint traveler--manager run, all 1,179,300 finalized target decisions satisfied action constraints; execution checks verified implementation of accepted choices and preservation of personal memories across days. Trajectories show stable route choices alongside departure-time adjustments and differences between controlled-trip and population-wide outcomes. The platform supports experiments on individual adaptation, collective outcomes, and management interventions by varying information access, retained experience, and management feedback. Source code is available at https://github.com/Agentic-City-Research/Agentic-Mobility

title: Geometric Morphology Learning: Empowering Foundation Models from Structure to Spacetime Intelligence
abstract: Geometry is the very form that connects space, time, and matter, serving as the fundamental fabric of the physical world, from continuous fields to discrete structures. Despite its importance, deep learning is inherently blind to geometry. Riemannian geometry stands as a well-established mathematical foundation for studying geometry, yet it remains largely incompatible with deep learning architectures. To bridge this gap, we establish a new learning framework--Geometric Morphology Learning--that learns geometric or topological structures, shapes or conformations for representation learning, reasoning and action modeling. Moving beyond early attempts limited to specific geometric priors, this theory centers on modeling the intrinsic geometry of objects and learning from such geometric or topological knowledge. Specifically, we construct a neural bundle, a unified scaffolding linking local and global structures, and formulate differentiable operators, including connection and curvature, thereby enabling the study of geometry with advanced geometric concepts such as holonomy and cohomology. Consequently, Geometric Morphology Learning opens new horizons in foundation models, reasoning and planning, graph modeling, physical simulation, PDE systems, and dynamics, marking a fundamental shift toward instilling systematic geometry in artificial intelligence.

title: ReWY: Faster Gradient Computation for Delta-Rule Attention Family
abstract: Delta-rule linear attention underlies language models such as Kimi Linear and Qwen3-Next. Chunkwise implementations expose matrix parallelism, but their backward passes compute unnecessary auxiliary adjoints. We present ReWY, an algebraic reformulation that reduces this work before optimizing accelerator execution. Differentiating the chunk correction as one triangular residual system eliminates the inverse adjoint and reduces seven local WY matrix products to three. Two complementary transformations expose further reuse: centered matrix contractions replace pairwise vector-gate processing, and scalar-gate reductions reuse key-gradient products instead of forming a key Gram matrix. These identities simplify backward computation for DeltaNet, GDN, KDA, and GDN2 while preserving the recurrence and gradients in exact arithmetic, without changing the architecture or training objective. We implement the reduced graph on GPUs and Ascend NPUs. Under matched recomputation and full-saving policies, precision-qualified six-shape comparisons with frozen FLA references yield 1.15-1.81$\times$ geometric-mean complete low-level backward speedups on NVIDIA GPUs. All four operators achieve 1.18-1.70$\times$ on H100 and H200 while retaining original FP32 working matrices. A separate public-autograd evaluation on Ascend 950DT, including gradient conversions, yields 1.09-2.89$\times$ under available matched policies. Paired ablations establish further ReWY gains after optimizing the complementary contractions. Complete-gradient checks validate the recorded operator cases; supplementary full-model backward measurements assess integration into community FLA models and a GDN2 layer port. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/flashserve/ReWY.

title: Knowledge-Guided Floodwater Level Reasoning for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Monitoring
abstract: Frequent urban floodwater poses a serious threat to the safety and efficiency of intelligent transportation systems. Existing vision-based methods for floodwater level detection face two main limitations. First, the lack of explicit reasoning leads to poor detection performance and little interpretability. Second, these methods struggle to generalize to the complex and varied real-world road scenes seen from different viewpoints. To address this, we reformulate the task as an explicit visual reasoning problem and propose HydroReasoner, a floodwater level reasoning framework designed for cloud-edge collaboration. HydroReasoner builds on Qwen2.5-VL and is trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization. To address the scarcity of reasoning process annotations, we build a floodwater domain knowledge graph HydroKG and design a novel KG path reward. Through deterministic graph traversal over HydroKG, this reward supervises the model's reasoning process at a fine granularity, which improves both reasoning and generalization. For edge deployment, we apply 4-bit quantization to the model, cutting GPU memory usage by 57% and inference latency by 43% while out-of-domain accuracy drops by only 0.2 percentage points. We also propose a confidence-based cloud-edge routing mechanism, which improves system safety and eases the computational load on the cloud. In addition, we build HydroLevel, a floodwater benchmark dataset of 3,000 images, for training and evaluating the model. Experimental results show that HydroReasoner achieves detection accuracy 4.0 and 13.6 percentage points higher than conventional vision baselines in the in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations respectively, with performance dropping by only 4.4 percentage points out of domain.

title: Multimodal BVP and Respiration for Automated Pain Recognition with Hankel-FCN
abstract: Automated pain recognition is a fundamental challenge for the advancement of clinical care and empathetic human-computer interaction, due to the subjective and dynamic nature of pain. In this study, we propose a deep learning framework for objective pain assessment based on multimodal physiological signals from the AI4Pain dataset. The approach focuses on Blood Volume Pulse (BVP) and Respiration (RESP), capturing complementary aspects of autonomic responses to nociceptive stimulation. To explicitly model their temporal dynamics, the signals are transformed into structured trajectory representations using Hankel matrix embeddings, enabling the learning of dynamical patterns beyond conventional time-series representations. These embeddings are processed by modality-specific Fully Convolutional Networks, and their outputs are integrated through a late fusion strategy for three-class classification (No Pain, Low Pain, High Pain). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 67.09% and an F1-score of 66.41%, providing competitive performance compared to existing approaches, while relying on no handcrafted feature engineering. Multimodal fusion significantly outperformed either modality alone, and the Hankel embedding showed a trend towards further improvement. Further validation is required to establish generalisability to broader populations and clinical settings.

title: Large-Scale Bayesian Optimisation Using Uncertainty-Calibrated Product-of-Experts Gaussian Process Models with Trust Regions
abstract: The use of collections of independent local Gaussian processes (GP-ind) combined with trust regions is a widely adopted approach for large-scale and high-dimensional Bayesian optimisation (BO). However, this approach suffers from several limitations, including discontinuities at the boundaries of disjoint regions, an inability to capture long-range spatial correlations, potential information loss, and abrupt increases in computational overhead. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel BO algorithm, termed BO-pro-c-tr. The proposed method employs a product-of-experts Gaussian process model with uncertainty calibration (GP-pro-c) as its surrogate model and incorporates a one-to-many association strategy for integrating GP-pro-c with trust regions.
