title: Sustainable Multi-Zone Greenhouse Fertigation Through Reliability-Aware Sensing, Spatiotemporal Graph Learning, and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: With protected agriculture increasingly developing toward large-scale, multi-zone, and intelligent production, reducing water and fertilizer consumption, drainage losses, and energy waste while maintaining crop yield, product quality, and long-term economic profitability has become an important challenge for sustainable greenhouse production. To address sensor abnormalities, spatial heterogeneity among irrigation zones, competition for shared hydraulic resources, and the limited ability of conventional control strategies to jointly optimize resource efficiency and economic performance, a sensor-driven spatiotemporal graph multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, termed SensorGraph-FertiMARL, is proposed for state sensing, response prediction, and sustainable coordinated fertigation optimization in multi-zone greenhouses. Reliable zone-level states are first obtained through sensor-reliability gating, missing-state reconstruction, and multi-relational graph fusion incorporating spatial, hydraulic, and microclimatic relationships. An action-conditioned fertigation–yield–quality–profit digital twin is then constructed to jointly predict root-zone responses, resource consumption, marketable yield, product quality, and net profit associated with candidate control actions. Finally, graph-based multi-agent proximal policy optimization (Graph-MAPPO) with capacity, safety, and fairness constraints is employed to coordinate fertigation allocation among multiple zones under shared pump, main-pipeline, and nutrient-solution resource constraints. Evaluated through rigorous offline digital-twin simulation and replay testing calibrated against complete multi-stage historical dataset records from an eight-zone commercial greenhouse, experimental results show that the proposed method reduced water and fertilizer use to 75.8% and 78.3% (achieving water and fertilizer saving rates of 24.2% and 21.7%), respectively, relative to the uniform timer-based control baseline, while decreasing the drainage rate to 7.2%. The Grade-A product rate increased to 84.6%, net profit reached 138.9% of the baseline level (a +38.9% net-profit improvement), return on investment (ROI) reached 1.94, and the stress-violation rate was limited to 2.9%. For state sensing and digital-twin prediction, the sensor-state reconstruction mean absolute error (MAE) and coefficient of determination (R2) were 0.036 and 0.918, respectively; the water-content prediction MAE was 0.041, the electrical conductivity (EC) prediction root mean squared error (RMSE) was 0.119, and the drainage prediction mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 8.7%. In addition, the R2 for marketable-yield prediction reached 0.912, the macro-averaged F1 (Macro-F1) score for quality-grade prediction reached 0.851, the R2 for net-profit prediction reached 0.904, the mean prediction interval width (MPIW) was 0.142, and the prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) reached 0.931. These results demonstrate that SensorGraph-FertiMARL can simultaneously achieve water and fertilizer conservation, drainage reduction, operational-risk control, and economic improvement while maintaining marketable production and quality, thereby providing an effective intelligent optimization approach for resource-efficient, environmentally sustainable, and economically viable greenhouse production.

title: Spatiotemporal Evolution and Driving Factors of Coupling Coordination Between New-Type Urbanization and Digital Village Construction
abstract: Coordinating new-type urbanization and digital village construction supports urban–rural integration. Using 2012–2023 panel data for 30 Chinese provincial-level regions, this study constructs subsystem indices, calculates the coupling coordination degree (CCD) to summarize joint development, and assesses relative balance separately. The analysis combines kernel density estimation, Dagum Gini decomposition, traditional and spatial Markov chains, spatial autocorrelation tests, and a two-way fixed-effects spatial Durbin model. Both indices increased, and relative balance improved despite a widening absolute index gap. CCD rose as provincial disparities narrowed, but eastern leadership persisted alongside rapid western catch-up, steady central improvement, and slower northeastern progress. East–west and coastal–inland gradients persisted, with interregional disparities remaining dominant. CCD transitions were persistent and gradual, with conditional probabilities varying by initial levels and neighborhood conditions. Provincial CCD showed significant positive spatial dependence. Human capital and fiscal expenditure on science and technology had significant positive local and spatial indirect associations with CCD, while the positive association of fiscal support for agriculture was mainly local. Some estimated effects of openness, industrial structure upgrading, and agricultural machinery intensity were significantly negative. The findings support investment in human capital and technology, cross-regional collaboration, and region-specific policies.

title: Digital Infrastructure as a Systemic Buffer: Climate Risk, Agricultural Resilience, and the Full-Chain Mechanisms in China
abstract: Extreme climate disasters have become a major challenge to economic and social development worldwide. As a major agricultural country, China’s agricultural sector is particularly vulnerable to climate change. This study constructs an Agricultural Industrial Resilience (AIR) index from three dimensions—resistance, adaptation, and transformation—and uses panel data for 180 prefecture-level cities in China from 2006 to 2023 to examine the impact of climate risk on AIR and its underlying mechanisms. From the perspective of the agricultural value chain, we identify three key transmission channels—production efficiency, transport capacity, and market linkages—and further investigate the buffering role of digital infrastructure and regional heterogeneity. The results show that climate shocks significantly weaken AIR, and the mechanism tests provide empirical evidence consistent with the proposed production-efficiency, transport, and market-linkage channels, as reflected in agricultural total factor productivity (ATFP), transport infrastructure, and agricultural trade linkages. The moderated mediation analysis further shows that the negative indirect associations along the production-efficiency, transport-infrastructure, and agricultural-trade-linkage channels are significantly weaker at higher levels of digital infrastructure, providing further evidence of its buffering role. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the negative effect of climate shocks on AIR is more pronounced in non-major grain-producing regions. These findings suggest that building an intelligent and coordinated climate adaptation system covering the entire agricultural value chain can help strengthen the climate resilience of agricultural industrial systems and provide Chinese evidence and a theoretical basis for enhancing AIR under increasing global climate risks.

title: Early Paddy Yield Forecasting in Sri Lanka Using SARIMA and LSTM for Farmer and Collector Decision Support
abstract: Early paddy-yield information can support cultivation and procurement planning in Sri Lanka, where farmers and collectors make decisions before final harvest outcomes are known. This study developed and evaluated a web-based decision-support system (DSS) that integrates district-level paddy-yield forecasting with separate farmer and collector workflows. Historical district-seasonal records from 2004–2023 covered 21 retained districts and 797 observations. District-specific Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models were compared using an archived final-four-observation holdout. Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), averaged across districts, was 22.06% for SARIMA and 17.38% for LSTM, with LSTM recording lower MAPE in 12 of 21 districts; a paired district comparison reported *p* = 0.0333. However, chronology, scaling, and unequal forecast-information horizons limit this archived comparison, so the result is not interpreted as validated LSTM superiority. A problem-validation survey of 122 participants (103 farmers and 19 collectors) identified reported planning uncertainty and strong perceived need for earlier forecasts. The DSS was implemented using FastAPI and React/Vite with English and Sinhala presentation. A post-demonstration evaluation with 34 intended users produced a mean System Usability Scale score of 73.53. A shared planning-uncertainty item did not differ significantly from the independent baseline sample. The contribution is therefore an integrated and bounded forecasting-DSS prototype with preliminary stakeholder evidence and explicitly stated validation limitations.
journal: International Journal of AI and Advanced Computing

title: Pengembangan Media Kartu kata Bergambar Untuk Meningkatkan Keterampilan Membaca Permulaan Pada Siswa Kelas 1 SD Inpres Bertingkat Kelapa Lima 2 Kota Kupang
abstract: This research and development was motivated by a problem found at SD Inpres Bertingkat Kelapa Lima 2, Kupang City. This problem is characterized by students' suboptimal beginning reading skills, particularly in memorizing and recognizing letters of the alphabet, which hinders their learning in class. Therefore, media such as picture word cards are needed to assist students in learning beginning reading, to attract their attention and interest. This study aims to develop effective picture word cards to improve beginning reading skills in grade I students of SD Inpres Bertingkat Kelapa Lima 2, Kupang City. This study used the research and development method with the ADDIE model: Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation. The subjects were first-grade students at SD Inpres Bertingkat Kelapa Lima 2, Kupang City. The media development consisted of picture word cards, created based on the steps and tailored to students' learning needs. The quality of the picture word cards was assessed by expert validators, teacher responses, and student responses. The validation test results for the picture word cards by material experts and media experts categorized them as very valid, with validity scores of 95 and 90, respectively. The results of the teacher and student response tests for the picture word cards categorized them as very good (SB) with percentages of 87.5% and 83.3%, respectively. Based on the expert validation data, teacher responses, and student responses, it can be concluded that the picture word cards developed for beginning reading material are suitable for use as a medium in the learning process.
journal: Didaktik : Jurnal Ilmiah PGSD STKIP Subang

title: Communication Behavior and Communication Barriers Between Agricultural Extension Agents and Farmers: A Systematic Review
abstract: Effective communication between agricultural extension agents and farming communities is a fundamental driver of knowledge transfer, technology adoption, and overall agricultural development. Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) framework, this systematic review synthesizes literature across developing agrarian contexts to evaluate extension-farmer communication behaviors and multi-dimensional barriers. From an initial database search of 1,420 records, 56 eligible studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. The review traces the evolution of extension paradigms from linear, top-down approaches to two-way participatory models and digital/ICT advisory services. It categorizes the primary obstacles disrupting knowledge exchange into five distinct dimensions: language and literacy gaps, socio-cultural hierarchies, gender-based exclusions, structural institutional constraints, and digital infrastructure divides. The findings demonstrate that while vertical agent-to-farmer channels deliver technical innovations, horizontal peer-to-peer networks are essential for information validation and community-wide adoption. Strategic recommendations emphasize capacity building in facilitation soft skills, scaling up peer-led participatory approaches, developing local-language visual media, and establishing interactive digital-extension hybrid models.
journal: Journal of Economics, Finance And Management Studies

title: When Is POME a Residue? Definitional Boundaries, Carbon Accounting and Policy Integrity in Sustainable Aviation Fuel
abstract: This qualitative literature review examines the definitional controversy surrounding palm oil mill effluent (POME) and its recovered oil as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) feedstocks. Drawing on 52 cited peer-reviewed journal articles from 2020–2026 and official ICAO and certification documents, it distinguishes unavoidable wastewater, genuinely recovered residual lipids and deliberately diverted primary palm oil. The review interprets the CORSIA POME-HEFA default core lifecycle value of 18.1 g CO₂e/MJ, derived from two modelling estimates, without conflating its assigned indirect land-use change treatment with measured system-wide climate effects. Five thematic findings concern classification boundaries, model-dependent emissions, wastewater methane interactions, plausible recovered-oil supplies and an auditable chain of custody. An origin-and-function framework is proposed to preserve legitimate feedstock eligibility while preventing inappropriate relabelling, duplicate emissions claims and undocumented changes in oil flows. The discussion differentiates official fuel lifecycle accounting from supplementary assessment of methane management and displaced product markets. It recommends mill-level mass balances, independent verification, measured conversion inputs and an adaptive Indonesian policy roadmap. Definitional precision is necessary for regulatory credibility, but cannot substitute for reliable environmental performance or certified fuel production
journal: Journal of Business Research and Reports

title: Indonesia’s Palm Oil Trilemma: Reconciling Biodiesel Expansion, Export Competitiveness, and Supply Resilience under Climate and Governance Constraints
abstract: Indonesia’s palm oil sector is being asked to serve an expanding domestic energy market while sustaining food and oleochemical supply, export competitiveness, rural livelihoods, and ecological integrity. This interpretive qualitative literature review examines the resulting policy trilemma using peer-reviewed research published during 2020-2026 and the IPOSS fourth-quarter 2026 industry outlook as a contextual, explicitly prospective source. The analysis differentiates observed evidence from institutional forecasts, policy announcements, and conceptual scenarios. It synthesises eight interconnected themes: stock-flow consistency; biodiesel allocation and fiscal costs; climate-related production lags; smallholder yield gaps and replanting; commodity pricing and fiscal instruments; welfare distribution; deforestation-related market governance; and adaptive policy coordination. The synthesis indicates that additional domestic biodiesel demand can support energy substitution while raising the opportunity cost of exports and the exposure of levy-financed incentives to commodity price cycles. Weather risks, delayed biological yield responses, constrained smallholder finance, and traceability demands further limit simple supply-side solutions. We propose an integrated decision architecture combining equivalent-unit physical accounting, reserve and food-security safeguards, risk-sensitive biodiesel support, productivity-led expansion without deforestation, and inclusive market access. Five conditional scenarios clarify where policy complementarities are possible and where trade-offs remain unavoidable. The analysis does not claim new econometric estimates or validate IPOSS forecasts. Rather, it identifies measurable policy thresholds, evidence limitations, and a research agenda for jointly assessing energy security, trade value, public finances, farmer welfare, and ecological boundaries.
journal: Journal of Business Research and Reports

title: Respons Kalender Tanam Tanaman Pangan terhadap Variabilitas Iklim di Indonesia: Tinjauan Sistematis Literatur 2015–2025
abstract: Shifts in food crop planting calendars are an important concern in agricultural adaptation to climate variability in Indonesia. This study synthesizes evidence on planting calendar responses, associated climatic and agroclimatic factors, and reported adaptation strategies across regions and crops. Unlike studies focused on specific locations or approaches, this review compares delayed planting, changes in cropping patterns, adjustments to planting windows, and relatively stable planting schedules. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted using Google Scholar to identify publications from 2015 to 2025. Following predefined eligibility criteria guided by PRISMA 2020, 10 of 125 identified articles were analyzed through narrative synthesis and comparative analysis. The findings reveal heterogeneous planting calendar responses across Indonesia. El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), El Niño events, rainfall patterns, water availability, hydrological conditions, soil characteristics, and crop types are associated with these responses. Seasonal forecasts, crop simulation models, and planting calendar information systems offer opportunities to support adaptive planting decisions, although their effectiveness depends on local suitability and implementation by farmers. This review highlights the importance of integrated, adaptive, and location-specific planting calendars that consider climate information, water balance, agroecological conditions, and crop requirements.
journal: Journal of Agriculture and Animal Science

title: Strategi Pengembangan UMKM Berbasis Sistem Agribisnis Kopi dan Pisang Di Pekon Sri Menanti Kecamatan Air Hitam Kabupaten Lampung Barat
abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) based on leading agricultural commodities play an important role in creating added value and increasing community income. Pekon Sri Menanti, Air Hitam District, West Lampung Regency, has considerable potential for developing MSMEs within the coffee and banana agribusiness system, supported by the availability of raw materials. However, these enterprises continue to face several challenges, including traditional marketing practices, the absence of standardized production processes, and limited human resource capacity. This study aims to identify key internal and external strategic factors and formulate development strategies for MSMEs within the coffee and banana agribusiness system in Pekon Sri Menanti. A case study approach was employed, involving business owners, academics, and relevant stakeholders. Data were analyzed using the Internal Factor Evaluation (IFE), External Factor Evaluation (EFE), Internal-External (IE), Strengths-Weaknesses-Opportunities-Threats (SWOT), and Quantitative Strategic Planning Matrix (QSPM) methods. The results show that the main strength of these MSMEs is the availability of coffee and banana raw materials, while their main weakness is traditional marketing. The main opportunity is the use of information technology for marketing, while the main threat is inadequate infrastructure to support MSME development. The IE matrix places these enterprises in Cell IV (growth and build). Based on the QSPM analysis, the priority strategies are increasing sales through digital marketing (6.806), maintaining production stability through raw material management (6.516), improving product quality through product innovation and the implementation of production standards (6.423), and strengthening human resource capacity through training (6.289).
journal: Journal of Agriculture and Animal Science

title: Threat Modeling Intimate Partner Abuse in Agentic Systems
abstract: Agentic systems are AI-powered technologies capable of autonomous action within digital environments, such as sending emails or making reservations. They are deeply connected to external tools as well as users' data and resources, making them vulnerable to attacks which exploit their access and capabilities. In this work, we apply the technology-facilitated abuse threat model, in the context of intimate partner violence and surveillance, to these systems, revealing threats that require deliberate investigation and mitigation. We categorize attacks based on system ownership: (1) Abuser-as-owner attacks demonstrate how agentic systems make existing forms of technology-facilitated abuse far easier and more scalable. (2) Victim-survivor-as-owner attacks show how agentic systems create a new attack surface which abusers can exploit. In light of these risks, we outline research and development directions for effective mitigation strategies.

title: MESSPa: A Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad for Preserving the Sense of Agency in a Detachable Robotic Arm
abstract: Wearable robots such as supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) can augment human capability, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the operator's sense of embodiment, comprising the sense of agency (SoA) and the sense of ownership (SoO). When an SRL is detached from the body so that the operator can act in two places at once, both the sense of agency and task performance tend to degrade. This paper presents the Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad (MESSPa), a wearable interface that combines one-to-one motion transfer with spatially distributed pneumatic (balloon) haptic feedback on the shoulder, with the goal of preserving the sense of agency across attached and detached states. We describe the system design, the control mapping, and a controlled experiment using a $2\times2$ mixed design that crosses the control interface between groups (MESSPa, $N=13$, vs. keyboard control, $N=12$ from our previous study) and attachment (on-shoulder/detached) within participants, under single- and dual-task loads. Compared with keyboard control in the detached condition, MESSPa significantly reduced task completion time and significantly improved the sense of agency in the detached state, while narrowing the performance gap between the attached and detached conditions. The sense of ownership did not change significantly. These results indicate that combining motion transfer with positional haptic feedback is an effective way to recover agency when a robotic limb is operated remotely.

title: AStockArena: Beyond Returns, Can We Entrust Real Capital to the Decisions of Financial Agents?
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in dynamic financial trading, yet real-time trading benchmarks mainly evaluate agents by cumulative returns and risk-adjusted performance. Such outcome metrics cannot show whether trades are faithfully reported, supported by available evidence, and consistent with account states. We introduce AStockArena, a real-time decision-auditing benchmark for continuous trading in China's A-share market. Under shared market conditions and execution constraints, we evaluate 13 open- and closed-source models over 3,198 sequential decisions. AStockArena reconstructsthe actions actually posted to accounts by aligning reports, trade requests, execution responses, and account states, and audits them with eight checks spanning execution traceability (O), evidence sufficiency (RK), and financial meta-awareness (B), combining record verification with consensus expert annotation. Of 1,070 trading points, 72.99% exhibit at least one audit gap; model-level rates range from52.2% to 91.2%, with evidence gaps most prevalent. Historical trade-filtering replay further shows thatportfolio outcomes are sensitive to these flagged trades. Decision-process auditing thus offers a verifiable complement to return-based evaluation of financial agents.

title: Agentic Context Management for Multi-Turn Human-AI Conversations
abstract: LLMs degrade in multi-turn conversation partly because of context pollution: the model's own earlier outputs stay in context and anchor later turns, so an early misreading of the user's intent can persist after the user corrects it. Assistant omission (AO), dropping every assistant message, removes this pollution but fails when interaction is referential: later turns refer back to drafts, decisions, and tool-call results that exist only in assistant turns. We propose Agentic Conversation Context Curation (AC3), a training-free method in which a separate analyzer (1) consolidates the task specification from the user's messages alone, (2) audits the assistant's prior outputs against it, and (3) edits the context, either appending the analysis or discarding the assistant side and rebuilding the context from the specification. A second finding: pollution is contagious. An analyzer that sees the assistant's reasoning while extracting the specification can do worse than no intervention, and instructing it to ignore them did not close the gap, so we exclude assistant turns structurally. On Lost in Conversation (replaying difficulty-selected instances), where AO is an oracle by construction, AC3 closes 55-84% of the gap between full context and AO on three of four tasks and exceeds AO on the fourth, and an LLM that faithfully summarizes the history does not reproduce the gain even with more compute. On real WildChat conversations, a GPT-5-mini judge prefers AC3's next turn over both full context and AO in every configuration of our main table, though this preference depends on the judge; on CollabLLM results are mixed. In stateful tool use (tau2-bench), AO collapses to 0% on every model; AC3 does not collapse, though it falls slightly behind full context. Detector studies show that Reset removes injected pollution but is not span-selective: the gain comes from rebuilding the specification.

title: Governing Equations of Human Sleep Macro-Structure:Symbolic Discovery from 1,106 Nights
abstract: Human sleep is organized into a small number of cycles per night: deep sleep dominates early cycles, REM lengthens toward morning, and light sleep clusters at cycle boundaries. These regularities have long been described qualitatively but never distilled into closed-form laws from large-scale data. A total of 1,106 nights (Sleep-EDF 153 + SHHS 953) are segmented into REM-anchored cycles, and four cycle-indexed statistics follow simple closed-form equations: cycle length declines nearly linearly (R^2=0.996), REM duration follows an inverted U (R^2=0.873), deep-sleep (N3) run length decays exponentially (R^2=0.987) with a time constant of 2.94 cycles, consistent with the homeostatic Process S of the two-process model, and light-sleep (N1) run length follows a U shape (R^2=0.956), confirming a "long-short-long" pattern across the night. The laws are reproduced by per-night differentiable fitting (142/142 and 773/773 nights converge), by unconstrained symbolic regression (PySR), and by a 500-night generative synthesizer built from them. Their robustness is established against the two main methodological threats: bootstrap CIs computed by resampling whole nights (1,000 replications) exclude zero for every shape term, and a five-level scan of the REM-merge segmentation threshold preserves every qualitative form. These appear to be the first closed-form laws governing the macro-structure of sleep, distilled and tested across an age-mixed sample (healthy young adults and community-based older adults).

title: Enhancing Language Model Reasoning with Structured Multi-Level Modeling
abstract: Inference-time scaling enhances a model's reasoning by extending its chain-of-thought (CoT). However, existing approaches typically rely on a single policy trained with outcome-reward reinforcement learning (RL), which often suffers from long-horizon plan failures where the implicit plan drifts from valid strategies, especially for small LMs with limited capacity. To address this, we propose Multi-Level Reasoning (MLR), which reformulates long-CoT generation as a two-level stochastic process. A high-level planner generates structured step descriptors specifying both the reasoning mode and the semantic subgoal. The low-level executor then produces detailed reasoning conditioned on these descriptors, forming an alternating plan--execute loop. To maintain scalability, we adopt a minimal design where the base model serves as the low-level policy and a lightweight LoRA module implements the high-level policy. For training, we observe that outcome-reward RL provides sparse and delayed feedback for long trajectories (e.g., several thousand tokens), hindering credit assignment. We therefore introduce iterative Step-DPO, a process-level preference optimization scheme that leverages Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo (TSMC) to provide scalable stepwise supervision. This yields more effective training, improved stability, and higher accuracy. Extensive experiments on challenging math, science, and logical reasoning benchmarks show that, under the same reduced data budget (10% SFT and 5% preference relative to the DeepSeek-R1 distillation setup), MLR outperforms both SFT-based distillation and strong RL/preference-optimization baselines across multiple base models and tasks. Moreover, MLR exhibits slower performance degradation on long-horizon reasoning, demonstrating stronger robustness under extended CoT generation.

title: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems with Agentic AI
abstract: A central obstacle in realizing color center cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is inhomogeneity, or disorder, among individual emitters. As the number of emitters increases, so does the complexity of the experimental data, making it difficult to quantify the present physical mechanisms of disorder. Here we introduce an artificial intelligence-driven model discovery framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent, equipped with tools and a structured workflow, proposes candidate Hamiltonian and Lindbladian models, generates computational tools, and quantitatively evaluates competing physical hypotheses. We apply the workflow to three previously published experimental cavity-QED datasets collected from color centers in diamond and silicon carbide. Across the experiments, the agent successfully identifies physical models for the system and characterizes the disorder. In assessing reproducibility, we find that run-to-run variability is concentrated primarily in the research plan generation step, while the computational analysis itself is substantially more consistent. Our results suggest that structured LLM agent workflows can support model discovery from quantum optical experimental data while simultaneously allowing for human expert supervision and collaboration.

title: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
abstract: Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution. A regime-adaptive objective selects the tuning signal according to the information available from a time-limited run, while a log-based completion signal estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth recorded in ordinary solver logs, so that solved and unsolved runs share one time scale. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduces geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. In both regimes, LDST achieves a lower loss with 10 proposals than any of these baselines achieves with 50. Configurations that LDST tunes on a single instance also transfer better than baseline configurations to unseen instances of the same family.

title: XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale
abstract: Accelerating modern foundational models has pushed domain-specific compilers toward increasingly complex, multi-tiered optimization pipelines. However, this heavy optimization focus introduces delicate tradeoffs between peak execution performance and correctness. Subtle codegen defects can trigger numerical degradation and memory or buffer corruption, invalidating multi-million-dollar training runs and degrading live serving quality without raising obvious compiler errors. In this paper, we present a battle-tested methodology for verifying and triaging Google's XLA:TPU compiler at hyperscale. We leverage fuzzing techniques, combining synthetic program generation with real production traces, while orchestrating AI agent swarms to autonomously generate stress tests, reproduce failures, and draft fixes. To pinpoint root causes in full workloads, we pair this with a hierarchical differential pipeline that bisects large graphs down to individual failing operations inside fused kernels. Deployed in production, our framework has already driven the resolution of over 142 compiler bugs (with 103 additional findings under review), from which we distill pragmatic lessons learned.

title: Autonomous Analysis of Thermoelectric Materials Big Data by Multi-Agentic AI and Construction of a Knowledge Base and Specialized AI
abstract: Extracting knowledge from large databases of experimental materials data requires repeated analyses and reusable records of their choices and results. We developed Multi-Agentic AI (MAA), a multi-agent system in which AI agents with distinct roles analyze experimental thermoelectric data under predefined instructions and quality checks, saving analysis records traceable to their sources. In four experiments varying theme and cycle counts, we measured what accumulated in these records. In the largest experiment (100 analyses across 10 themes and 10 cycles), concept co-occurrences were concentrated within themes, vocabulary was shared across themes and some relation descriptions were first detected in later cycles. A specialized AI that searches this experiment's knowledge bases and reads their analysis records answered materials questions with cited sources. Retrospective checks, including tracing an answer generated with a preliminary corpus back to the source data, exposed errors: traceability makes errors findable but not absent.

title: Heirloom: Carrying a Phone's Personalization Across Base-Model Generations
abstract: On-device language models can learn a user's preferences through adapters trained on private data. However, a base-model upgrade may change the layers or vocabulary, leaving the personal adapter incompatible. Replacing it with a non-personal adapter loses much of the personalization, while retraining requires retaining the user's labeled history. We present Heirloom, a system that transfers a personal adapter to a new base model on the phone without retaining labels. Heirloom uses the old personal model as a teacher, collecting its predictions on stored unlabeled inputs, vendor-provided prompts, or prompts generated by the new base. It then unloads the old base and trains an adapter for the new model to match those predictions, keeping only one base model in memory at a time. We evaluate Heirloom across three generation upgrades from two model families, an architecture-preserving refresh, and three personalization tasks. On movie tagging, migration from stored inputs maintains pre-upgrade accuracy and differs from labeled retraining by at most 1.7 percentage points across the three upgrades. On a phone's neural processing unit (NPU), a fixed-length migration for the 4B upgrade takes 38 minutes and consumes 20% of the battery end to end, making the stored-input setting feasible during overnight charging.

title: Vision-based Sensing of Urban Environment using Hardware-Software co-design at Scale
abstract: Urban environmental monitoring is crucial for climate-adaptive cities, yet current approaches rely heavily on human inspection, overhead remote sensing, or limited terrestrial RGB imagery, thereby lacking comprehensive multispectral perspectives at street level. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces UrbanScapes, an adaptable and flexible hardware-software co-design platform for large-scale, vision-based sensing of urban environments. Built on a modular architecture, UrbanScapes seamlessly integrates multispectral imaging channels, including Red, Green, Blue (RGB), Near-Infrared, and Thermal, to capture multispectral street-level imagery. The system is designed for both opportunistic deployment on bicycles, vehicles, or pedestrians and targeted deployments on municipal fleets, ensuring high spatio-temporal scalability without requiring hardware redesigns. Crucially, the platform utilizes on-device deep learning models to automatically remove personally identifiable information (PII) at the edge, addressing privacy concerns inherent in street-level data collection. By combining this multispectral street-level imagery with overhead multispectral remote sensing imagery, UrbanScapes enables scalable calculation of physics-based environmental indices, providing a foundational tool for advanced citywide analysis.

title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
abstract: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The outputs from these boosted models are aggregated to generate a corrected, high-fidelity prediction. The proposed methodology is systematically validated through quantitative metrics and comparative analysis against the standard PINN baseline. The results demonstrate that the boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error, and improves generalization, offering a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.

title: STEER: Route-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Vision-language action (VLA) models excel for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet their tendency to over-invoke chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning mirrors a human cognitive pitfall: overthinking. Just as deliberate reasoning can slow or mislead human judgment in routine tasks, excessive CoT in VLA incurs unnecessary compute overhead and can paradoxically degrade planning performance. Recent research tackles this via adaptive reasoning, which dynamically modulates inference complexity by selectively triggering CoT for complex scenes while responding directly to routine ones. While prior adaptive methods rely on implicit adaptation, recent work shows that explicitly optimizing the route between CoT and direct responses yields superior performance, assuming scene-difficulty annotations which are labor-intensive, poorly scalable, and prone to error due to the subjectivity of judging driving complexity. We explore, for the first time, whether adaptive reasoning with explicit route optimization can be achieved without any scene-difficulty labeling. We introduce STEER, a generic over-reasoning mitigation strategy featuring two key components: (i) routing uncertainty-aware rollout, which calibrates sampling to align routing diversity with model uncertainty; and (ii) cross-route advantage credit assignment, which introduces a differential metric to reinforce optimal routing decisions based on environmental rewards rather than subjective labels. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v1/v2 demonstrate that STEER is competitive with state-of-the-art methods in both planning quality and the Pareto front of inference efficiency.

title: Learning hidden-state dynamics from unpaired snapshots with lift-project SDEs
abstract: Many systems are observed only through unpaired snapshots, with population samples available at each time point but no correspondence between samples at different times. These snapshots determine the one-time distributions but leave the temporal coupling unspecified, requiring a modeling prior to connect successive times. We propose the lift-project stochastic differential equation (SDE), an autonomous SDE on the observed coordinate and a few hidden coordinates, trained only to match the snapshots. Most existing methods, including time-dependent SDEs, Schrödinger bridges and optimal transport, evolve the observed coordinate alone. For a scalar observation, the classical comparison theorem implies that all such models have non-negative lagged covariance, so on data whose lagged covariance turns negative, their error has a computable floor. The lift-project SDE is not bound by this floor. On two representative partially observed systems, the Duffing and pendulum oscillators, at comparable fit to the snapshots, the proposed method reduces the lagged-covariance error by factors of 2.4 and 6.6 relative to the strongest baseline and is the only model below the error floor; one hidden coordinate is already enough for such improvement. Furthermore, if a second experiment changes only the initial state of the hidden coordinate, no single model that evolves the observed coordinate alone can fit both experiments, whereas a single lift-project SDE can.

title: The MASSIMAL Dataset: UAV Hyperspectral Images and Ground Truth Observations for Coastal Habitat Mapping in Norway
abstract: The MASSIMAL dataset was collected in an effort to develop new remote sensing methods for mapping shallow water coastal habitats, such as kelp forests, seagrass meadows and maerl beds. The main component of the dataset is a set of hyperspectral images collected using a unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Images were collected during 45 UAV flights performed at 4 main areas along the Norwegian coast, spanning across a wide latitude range, from 59 to 67 degrees north. The ground sampling distance of the hyperspectral images is 3.5 cm, and the spectral range is 400-1000 nm, sampled across 300 spectral bands. During acquisition, push-broom imagery was automatically split into images with a maximum along-track length of 2000 lines. Out of approximately 1000 hyperspectral images, 221 have been annotated, using segmentation masks and a hierarchical taxonomy. An open source image processing pipeline has been developed as part of the dataset preparation, enabling efficient generation of reflectance images and glint-corrected images based on published radiance images. The dataset also includes color images (RGB) and multispectral images collected using UAV, and georeferenced image mosaics constructed from these. Ground truth data supporting the remote sensing images include hours of underwater video, thousands of geotagged underwater images, and tens of kilometers of single-beam sonar data. The data provide a foundation for assessing habitat distribution, tracking changes, and evaluating ecosystem services, thus supporting evidence-based management in Norwegian coastal environments.

title: DADKC: Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation for Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification
abstract: Lifelong Person Re-identification (LReID) aims to match the same person using sequentially collected data. In practical long-term deployments, however, the model must handle both domain shifts across cameras and scenes, and irregular clothing changes of the same identity. This gives rise to the Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification (CH-LReID) task, which demands balancing cloth-relevant and cloth-irrelevant knowledge in streaming data. While existing LReID methods have explored replay-based or distillation-based anti-forgetting strategies, they typically fail to sufficiently model stage-aware domain distributions and cross-stage feature continuity under exemplar-free training. To address this problem, we propose a Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DADKC) framework. The core idea is to enhance the existing Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DKC) paradigm with adaptive distribution modeling. To this end, three lightweight modules are designed: (1) an Anchor Pool Adapter (APA) to retrieve learnable anchor cues for refining identity features; (2) a Phase Path Mixer (PPM) to perform stage-aware expert routing for integrating domain-specific distribution paths; and (3) a Stage Bridge Alignment (SBA) module to regularize the continuity of base, anchor, and path representations between adjacent stages. Extensive experiments on the CH-LReID and LReID benchmarks show that DADKC gains 4.1%/4.5% mAP/R1 on Order-1 and 3.6%/3.4% mAP/R1 on Order-2 over the DKC baseline, and lowers weighted forgetting from 2.4%/1.7% to 1.8%/1.4%, while storing neither historical images nor per-image features. The code is available at https://github.com/fire667/DADKC.

title: DramaVQA: Probing Detailed Understanding of Ultra-Long TV Dramas
abstract: Despite recent progress in long-form video understanding, current benchmarks mostly focus on short clips or hour-scale videos. This leaves a major gap in evaluating ultra-long video understanding, where videos often last tens of hours. To bridge this gap, we introduce DramaVQA, a large-scale benchmark built upon long-form TV dramas. Containing approximately 20K question-answering (QA) pairs, the scale of DramaVQA exceeds previous long-video datasets, such as Video-MME and LVBench, by an order of magnitude. Our benchmark has two main features that make it stand out from existing datasets. First, we establish a scalable, LLM-assisted annotation pipeline that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to generate complex questions, followed by strict human checking to ensure high data quality. Second, DramaVQA introduces a multi-level time structure; queries are designed across different video lengths, with the hardest questions requiring overall understanding across the entire drama. Extensive evaluations show that state-of-the-art MLLMs face major challenges when tested on these very long videos, highlighting the need for agentic AI algorithms capable of managing long-term memory. The project is available at https://github.com/xinyuehuo/DramaVQA

title: Embodied AI for Radio Mapping: From Solo to Swarm
abstract: Radio maps provide spatial knowledge of wireless environments to assess coverage, manage spectrum use, and support connectivity-aware mobility. Recent advances in embodied intelligence (EI) offer a promising approach to radio map reconstruction by enabling agents to perceive the environment and autonomously adjust their survey paths toward safe, reachable locations. However, a single agent remains constrained by limited endurance and onboard computing capacity, limiting measurement collection and reconstruction performance. Swarm cooperation can support more efficient radio mapping over larger areas by sharing observations and coordinating members' sampling. This article first explores the capabilities and applications of cooperative embodied agents. A cooperative radio map reconstruction framework is then presented, together with its key enabling techniques. Case study results illustrate how scene perception supports access to informative sampling locations and how air--ground cooperation improves reconstruction through complementary measurements and mobile support. The article concludes with open challenges and future research directions for reliable and efficient embodied cooperative radio mapping in complex environments.

title: From Static Models to Editable CAD: A Design-Intent-Aware Framework for Reverse Parametrization
abstract: Neutral CAD formats such as STEP typically preserve geometry but not feature histories or parameter dependencies. Thus, they are inherently limited for iterative design that requires modifications, a critical limitation for design optimization that relies on iterative processes. This study presents a design-intent-aware reverse-parametrization framework that converts history-free STEP parts into editable Grasshopper definitions and represents their assembly relations. Without task-specific training, the framework combines kernel-measured features, geometric relations, a compressed attributed adjacency graph, and multiview renderings. An LLM assigns dimensions independent, fixed, or dependent roles, confirms candidate joints, and interprets verification reports. Kernel- and rule-based modules perform measurement, parameter binding, geometry construction, and verification. Evaluation distinguishes default-shape preservation, design-intent reflection, and edit validity, with the latter examined through assembly-level editing examples involving checks for geometry regeneration, joint alignment, interference, and mechanism closure. As an example, five components of a mechanical mechanism were used, and across 25 runs, the mean global and analytic-feature-region intersection over unions (IoUs) were 0.984 and 0.983, respectively; all runs passed the combined shape-preservation criterion. In a separate request experiment, the requested dimension was selected as an independent variable in 19 of 20 runs. Product-level examples show coordinated changes in part geometry and assembly design while preserving assembly relations and avoiding inter-part interference. These results demonstrate editable reconstruction of history-free CAD models under the evaluated geometric and assembly constraints, indicating potential for subsequent design optimization.

title: Semi-classical analysis of noise squeezing in Kerr microresonators
abstract: Kerr microresonators are integrated nonlinear devices widely used to generate classical optical frequency combs and nonclassical states of light. In particular, they provide a promising platform for squeezed light sources, which are important elements of emerging quantum sensing, communication, and computing technologies. Designing such sources requires numerical tools that efficiently incorporate realistic device physics and noise processes. Here, we show that established semi-classical frameworks based on the Lugiato-Lefever equation and the Ikeda map, instrumental in the development of classical light sources, can also predict the quadrature-noise properties of squeezed light when vacuum fluctuations are properly included. We consider three canonical configurations producing two-mode quadrature squeezing, single-mode quadrature squeezing, and intensity difference squeezing. In each case, the semi-classical simulations produce quadrature variances and noise spectra in close agreement with the quantum theoretical predictions. These frameworks therefore provide practical tools for designing squeezed light sources, with the capability to incorporate additional noise mechanisms, nonlinear effects, and complex resonator arrangements. More fundamentally, our results show that key experimental signatures of squeezing can be modeled as phase-sensitive amplification of properly normalized vacuum fluctuations within stochastic semi-classical field equations. This observation helps distinguish squeezing properties accessible through semi-classical field evolution from those intrinsically requiring a full quantum description.

title: Streaming Virtual Metrology via Lightweight Adaptation under Temporal Distribution Shifts
abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. GRAPE integrates a stable global predictor based on interpretable representations with two lightweight streaming adapters that correct feature-level and environment-level shifts through online updates. Experiments on two real-world semiconductor manufacturing datasets, including chronologically held-out blind-test streams, show that GRAPE improves robustness and generalization under real temporal drift compared with both conventional batch-learning methods and existing online learning baselines.

title: AI Data Analysis: A New Approach - Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis
abstract: AI data analysis today is three fragmented worlds: LLMs understand semantics but cannot compute; BI aggregates precisely but is stateless; ML processes large-scale data on a stateful kernel but lacks semantics. This paper proposes a combination mechanism, named Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis, that fills a still-open gap - the multi-engine joint context: the data context is embedded into LLM conversational analysis, where the LLM serves only as the semantic, reasoning, and orchestration layer (not computation) and connects four engines through the 1M context window - Python and R ML kernels, SQL over relational databases, Cypher over graph databases - yielding two multiplications, "semantics and precise computation" and "relational and graph", under enterprise-grade governance. The novelty is a four-dimensional coordinate system: horizontal (engine kinds), vertical (state flow - the watershed), spatial (business generalization), temporal (iterative convergence); a deterministic grounding method (one-shot injection of schema.json + notes.md, M+S) carries the spatial and temporal dimensions. Empirically, all four dimensions are substantiated: horizontally, four engines are quantified - SQL, Cypher (96.5% on CypherBench movie), ML in Python and R (TabReD weather); vertically, state flows across engines and grounding is reused across kernels; spatially, SQL generalizes across three business databases - AdventureWorks 91.3%, financial 95.3%, formula_1 94.6% (average), about 20-23 points above single-shot SOTA 74.45%; temporally, accuracy converges monotonically as notes accumulate. The core invariant - the separation of semantics from computation plus a cross-data-domain persistent context - does not expire as LLMs and agents evolve or engine forms change.
