title: ODC: Orthogonal Drift Correction for Improved Text-to-Image Semantic Alignment at Inference
abstract: Text-to-image models have achieved remarkable success in generating high-quality images from textual descriptions. However, they often struggle with "semantic drift," where the generated output fails to precisely align with complex or nuanced text prompts. While recent approaches have attempted to address semantic errors regarding attribute binding or object presence, there remains a gap for a more holistic method that addresses these issues by directly refining the text embeddings of the initial user prompt. In this work, we introduce Orthogonal Drift Correction (ODC), an inference-time guidance method designed to mitigate semantic drift without requiring model retraining or additional user inputs. ODC guides image generation through a two-stage process. In the first stage, it identifies the semantic drift by evaluating the initially generated image against the user prompt in a shared vision-language embedding space. It then isolates the component of this drift vector that is orthogonal to the prompt's direction and translates it back into text via a vocabulary-based surrogate mechanism. In the second stage, it produces refined text conditioning for a second generation pass by feeding both the initial text embedding and the re-embedded drift representation into an adaptive rank-reduced concept removal module. Our experiments demonstrate that ODC consistently improves prompt-image alignment, increasing CLIP scores by up to 5.4% over the baseline on the COALBench-300 and PartiPrompts benchmarks. Furthermore, on the T2I-CompBench complex subset, ODC improves the average 3-in-1 score by 4.5% over the competing methods. As a plug-and-play module, ODC offers a practical and efficient method for improving the reliability of text-to-image models. Code is available at https://github.com/kasrakamali/ODC.

title: Identities for generalized Bernoulli numbers from a Lie model of the 2-disk
abstract: We define generalized Bernoulli numbers as appropriate coefficients of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) product formula, extending the classical sequence of rational numbers to a 2-dimensional setting. We give an identity involving these numbers and the classical Bernoulli numbers which is equivalent to the existence of a particular complete differential graded Lie algebra modelling a cell decomposition of the 2-disk and based on the Lawrence--Sullivan model of the interval. From this identity we derive explicit quadratic relations. The existence of Lie models for the symmetries of the interval and the disk is related to certain properties of the BCH product and to some notable features of the classical Bernoulli numbers: the two choices for $B_1$, the vanishing of $B_n$ for odd $n\geq 3$, and the equality $B_4=B_8$.

title: Can Agentic AI Undermine Its Own Assurance Loop? Closed-Loop Dependency Assurance for Cognitive Network Digital Twins
abstract: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Network Digital Twins (NDTs) are increasingly combined to form Cognitive Digital Twins (CDTs) that translate operational intents into network changes and support closed-loop management. However, a network change may achieve its intended objective while disrupting the monitoring or recovery mechanisms needed for subsequent decisions. For example, a service may be rerouted while its latency-monitoring traffic continues along the original path, producing measurements that no longer reflect the service's performance. We propose Closed-Loop Dependency Assurance (CLDA), an assurance mechanism that augments agentic AI-enabled NDTs with dependency-aware validation. In our framework, an agentic AI planner generates and refines network plans, while the NDT evaluates the projected network outcomes of these plans. CLDA extends this analysis using a Loop Dependency Graph (LDG) that connects service requirements to monitoring mechanisms, forwarding paths, failure domains, and recovery prerequisites. CLDA projects candidate actions onto these dependencies, checks intermediate states of multistep plans, and supports deterministic make-before-break repairs using temporary monitoring mechanisms. Unlike the Large Language Model (LLM)-based planner, CLDA uses explicit, deterministic rules for assurance decisions and repair. We evaluate CLDA through controlled reconfigurations, a 240-trial LLM-based planning campaign, and live network execution. A separate synthetic study examines deterministic assurance scalability across network models representing up to 1,024 routers.

title: What Is the Dynamic Capacitance of a Memristor?
abstract: Impedance spectroscopy of memristors, nanofluidic channels and halide perovskite devices often shows a low-frequency capacitance that is orders of magnitude larger than any plausible stored charge, or that becomes negative and appears together with an inductive loop. We distinguish two kinds of capacitance that enter the impedance in the same way: a storage capacitance, the derivative of a stored charge, and a dynamic capacitance, produced by the delayed response of a conduction current. Using the conductance-activated quasi-linear memristor (CALM) model, and a general memristor in which an internal state controls the conductance, we show that the dynamic capacitance is the time integral of the transient differential conductance after a small voltage step, measured from its final value. For a single relaxing state it is the product of a relaxing conductance and a relaxation time, with a negative sign. It vanishes at zero bias, and its sign is set by whether the stationary conductance increases or decreases with the magnitude of the voltage. Potentiation gives a negative capacitance and a chemical inductor, and depression gives a positive capacitance that is easily mistaken for stored charge. The analysis gives an explicit formulation of the time-domain criterion for negative capacitance of Jonscher and Ershov. In conical multipore nanofluidic membranes, the dynamic capacitance obtained from impedance and from voltage pulses shows the same sign change at zero bias and reaches values several hundred times larger than the membrane capacitance. The same picture accounts for the capacitive and inductive regimes of halide perovskite memristors.

title: Multi-Antenna Channel Prediction in 5G and Beyond using Data driven approach
abstract: As Wireless Communication evolves towards 5G and beyond, it satisfies Quality of Service (QoS) requirements of users by utilizing beam forming, adaptive transmission and multi antenna communication techniques. It is essential to have accurate channel information at Base station (BS) to provide satisfactory QoS to users. Traditional channel estimation approach involves transmitting pilots from User Equipments (UEs) and estimating the channel at BS, increases computational complexity as it is periodic process. It also increases communication complexity as number of antennas at BS increases which leads to increase in pilots. In this paper, we consider channel vector prediction using Machine learning approach at 7GHz. In this work, we generated data using ray tracing mechanism and used this generated data to train Machine learning models. We Considered XG Boost regression and Multilayer perceptron regression model.

title: Consumption and Investment with Multiple Job-Switching Opportunities
abstract: We study finite-horizon optimal switching with affine rewards in a consumption-investment model with finitely many occupational regimes. Directed shortest-path costs yield the exact natural borrowing limit. A dual transformation reduces the control problem to a one-dimensional system of variational inequalities with interconnected obstacles. Convexity and a distributional waiting inequality give local spatial $C^{1,1}$ regularity and smooth fit, including destination ties. These estimates establish strong duality and recover optimal consumption, investment, and switching strategies. A reflected backward stochastic differential equation representation yields a set-based integral formula without prescribed boundary geometry. Every connected component of the spatially regular locus is a maximal smooth graph over time. Exact examples exhibit disconnected contact sets, temporal boundaries under strict triangle costs, and a corner in an individual boundary component under additive route costs. A convergent time discretisation completes the analysis.

title: MarkovTS: Pretrained State-Transition Representations for Zero-Shot Time Series Generation
abstract: Across heterogeneous real-world domains, time-series generation supports simulation, model development, and data augmentation by generating sequences that preserve target-domain statistics and temporal dependencies when real observations are scarce or costly. However, existing methods predominantly address in-domain generation, limiting their reuse in unseen domains. We study reference-conditioned zero-shot time series generation: target domains are unseen during pretraining, generation uses a single target-domain reference sequence, and no model parameters are updated. MarkovTS characterizes sequence evolution through local morphologies and their ordered transitions at multiple temporal scales. Its pretrained encoder quantizes normalized time-series patches into multiscale morphological states with a state codebook, while a transition codebook encodes contextual transitions between adjacent intervals. These transferable state-transition representations condition a pretrained flow-matching model. At generation, the frozen model combines a reference-derived condition with independent Gaussian noise to produce stochastic samples that retain the reference's temporal organization. Across 12 unseen target datasets, MarkovTS outperforms strong baselines in most distributional comparisons and generates diverse, reference-consistent sequences. As downstream augmentation, its samples yield overall gains across forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection benchmarks and diverse model families. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/MarkovTS.

title: EPIC: Differentiable Energy-Force Consistent Uncertainty Quantification and Propagation for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now rival density functional theory in accuracy and are increasingly used to screen vast crystal databases, yet they can produce unreliable predictions for chemistries outside their training distribution without clear warning. Existing force-level evidential approaches do not inherently define a corresponding uncertainty model over the potential energy surface, limiting the consistent propagation of uncertainty to energy-derived observables. Here we introduce Energy-Propagated Intrinsic Confidence (EPIC), a general energy-centered evidential framework that derives forces as exact gradients of the predicted mean energy, ensuring conservative force fields while providing an analytical estimate of energy uncertainty. Coupled to a MACE backbone trained on the Materials Project trajectory dataset, EPIC propagates uncertainty diagnostics to equations of state, anisotropic structural uncertainty ellipsoids, and phonon dispersions through a Monte Carlo procedure. Applied to 10,966 candidate crystals, the fraction classified as robustly dynamically stable increases from 11\% in the highest-uncertainty quartile to 53\% in the lowest-uncertainty quartile. Furthermore, element-resolved analysis reveals a pronounced chemistry dependence in the relationship between epistemic uncertainty and predicted dynamical stability, highlighting potential limitations in the description of complex bonding environments. EPIC thus provides a physics-aware, chemistry-sensitive uncertainty diagnostic for high-throughput screening and autonomous materials discovery.

title: Heavy Quarkonium Physics: An Experimental Review at Tevatron, LHC, and e+e- Colliders
abstract: We review recent experimental advances in heavy quarkonium physics at the Tevatron, e+e- colliders (Belle, BaBar, Belle II, BESIII, and LEP), and the LHC (ALICE, ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb), including Run 2 and early Run 3 results. Differential cross sections and polarization measurements of charmonium (Jpsi, Psi(2S)) and bottomonium (Upsilon(nS)) test perturbative and non-perturbative QCD within the Non-Relativistic QCD (NRQCD) framework and probe symmetry relations among spin and orbital configurations. CDF and D0 established production baselines and exposed polarization tensions with early NRQCD predictions. Complementary e+e- measurements provide precise spectroscopy, branching fractions, radiative and hadronic transitions, and observations of exotic quarkonium-like states, constraining non-perturbative dynamics. LHC measurements extend production and polarization studies across broad kinematic ranges. Spectroscopic advances include fully-heavy tetraquark candidates, exotic structures in Jpsi Jpsi and Jpsi Psi(2S) reported by LHCb, and studies of toponium (ttbar) quasi-bound states. Sequential bottomonium suppression in PbPb collisions probes the quark-gluon plasma, while pPb measurements constrain cold nuclear matter effects. Multi-quarkonium production explores multi-parton interactions and exotic-hadron structure. Together, these results establish heavy quarkonium as a laboratory for QCD and a probe for physics beyond the Standard Model, while highlighting unresolved theoretical challenges. Future programs at the LHC, Belle II, and BESIII promise greater precision and new discoveries.

title: Why Koopman Structure Does Not Help Differentiable World Models for Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking
abstract: We test whether Koopman structure, linear dynamics in a lifted state space, helps when a humanoid whole-body tracking policy is trained by backpropagating through a differentiable world model, replacing the MLP world model of an otherwise unchanged pipeline for simulated Unitree G1 tracking. It does not: return is at best equal (0.823 versus 0.830), one-step error on identical data is 1.3 to 1.6 times the MLP's, and training is about 15% slower. Lifted rollouts diverge or fail to train a policy; of the schemes tested, re-lifting at every imagined step trains best. Re-lifting never uses the lifted linear dynamics and leaves a model affine in the action, with state-dependent offset and slope; an action-affine MLP also predicts worse, so the cost belongs to this class. At a fixed state, the curvature of the true dynamics in the action explains only part of it. Across states, the policy's actions span a curved region, so an affine model fits policy data only as the tangent at the policy's action, the operating point: on G1, the MLP's tangent there is as accurate as the MLP; at the mean action, 31 times worse. The offset must encode, from the state alone, where the policy acts, whereas an MLP reads the action. Supplying the policy's action removes most of the remaining gap on G1, Ant and Humanoid. The only online repair approaching the MLP feeds the action into the nonlinear lift, giving up the structure. The MLP world model thus remains the better choice here.

title: NovaFilter - A Rule-Based ETL Staging Framework for Fault-Tolerant Relational Databases
abstract: NovaFilter is a completely new approach to deriving structured relational data from heterogeneous input data in different data formats. It combines consistency checks, rule-based data transformation, and a human-in-the-loop example discussion. Using these three components, NovaFilter stores all transformation knowledge in an explicit rule base, which is continuously expanded through the example discussion with the user. The resulting data transformation process is deterministic, transparent, and reusable. As a result, the method can replace conventional ETL scripts and offers a completely new strategy for transforming data between different data models and schemas. Its main advantage is that users without programming skills (e.g. domain experts) can answer the example discussion and thus it is a building block for democratization of ETL script developement.

title: 4K Image Super-Resolution on Mobile NPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
abstract: Image super-resolution is widely used on mobile devices for upscaling various types of image data. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on neural processing units (NPUs) present in the majority of mobile and IoT chipsets. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can upsample images from Full HD to 4K resolution while running on popular mobile NPUs from Qualcomm and MediaTek. For this, the participants were provided with the DIV2K dataset and trained models to do an efficient 3X image upscaling. The competition had two tracks: in the first track, the models had to be fully quantized (INT8), and the runtime of all models was evaluated on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 NPU. In the second track, the participants were developing floating-point solutions that were evaluated on the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 NPU. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to reconstruct 4K images under 5 milliseconds while reaching a PSNR score of 30 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

title: E-UDE: A Scientific Machine Learning Model for Malware Propagation Dynamics
abstract: Understanding the malware propagation dynamics over the Internet is crucial for effectively controlling its spread. Existing mechanistic and data-driven models in the context of malware propagation dynamics, have some issues with either interpretability or predictive accuracy. This study presents an Enhanced Universal Differential Equation (E-UDE) framework that explicitly incorporates more detailed key factors that influence malware propagation. Evaluation on real-world malware propagation data shows that the E-UDE achieves the best overall performance, attaining an overall RMSE of 783.70 and MAE of 421.65. Compared with the Classical ODE and the UDE models, the proposed approach reduces RMSE by approximately 66 percent and 39 percent, respectively. Its robustness to predictive capability is further evaluated. In this experiment, the E-UDE achieves a Test RMSE of 634.6, a Test MAE of 419.3, and a Test Correlation of 0.964. The E-UDE maintains relatively stable prediction performance as the noise level increases, showing limited degradation compared with the baseline models. Furthermore, this E-UDE model enables us to perform several scenario analyses under different cybersecurity scenarios, providing a useful framework for better understanding the effective control factors. To study the wide applicability of the E-UDE framework, the model performance is assessed by two different datasets, namely, Code Red dataset and Witty Worm dataset.

title: Efficient Image Denoising on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
abstract: Image denoising is a fundamental problem in mobile photography. Despite a large number of solutions proposed for this task, the majority of them are trained on synthetically produced noisy images, and are additionally too computationally heavy for processing full-resolution images on mobile devices. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on constrained mobile hardware. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can denoise Full HD resolution photos while running on popular smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale dataset consisting of noisy-clean image pairs captured in the wild. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets with the Adreno and Mali GPUs, respectively. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to perform high-quality image denoising under 100 milliseconds on both platforms while reaching a PSNR score of over 37 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
abstract: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.

title: Multiparameter quantum metrology for general and adaptive strategies
abstract: We develop a conic-programming framework for multiparameter estimation of quantum processes under different classes of sensing strategies. Estimation precision depends on the choice of input probe state and measurement and, when a channel is used multiple times, on the arrangement of channel uses and intermediate controls. We specify different strategy classes through linear normalization constraints on generalized measurements, and formulate the local estimation problem using linear constraints and a linear objective function. We show that the separable-cone program gives the exact precision limit under the local estimation conditions considered here, while cone relaxations yield Cramér-Rao-type lower bounds. For $N$ uses of an identical quantum channel, we prove an exact $1/N$ scaling law for an RLD-based positive-cone lower bound, even for general process-matrix testers that allow indefinite causal order. Under the stated conditions on the channel and its parameter dependence, the minimum weighted mean-square error also scales as $1/N$. This extends an RLD-based restriction on Heisenberg scaling from adaptive strategies to this broader class. For fixed-order adaptive strategies, we show that each process-side conic bound equals the corresponding state-estimation bound optimized over sensor combs. We establish this equality by constructing a sensor comb from the process-side normalization operator. A noisy three-parameter field-sensing model illustrates the framework.

title: Adaptive Land Units from Earth Embeddings
abstract: Modeling land use starts with a choice of spatial units, typically a regular grid of pixels whose resolution is set by the spatial detail the process requires and, often more critically, by the computational budget. With Earth observation data more abundant than ever, we ask whether good land units can instead emerge from the data itself. To do that, we cluster AlphaEarth embeddings with a parallel Bayesian hierarchical clustering into adaptive land units, large where the land is uniform and small where it is highly heterogeneous. Using Denmark as a case study, we turn 402M land pixels into 1.27M newly defined units, about 320 times fewer, without any labels (i.e., unsupervised), making it possible to fit the whole country on a single consumer-grade GPU. Importantly, these units describe the land well, as a regular grid needs about 5 times as many cells to match them against land-use labels, and about 4 times as many against the declared crop of every field. Compared to clustering the satellite images themselves, the embeddings need half the units for the same purity. But more notably, they work as modeling units. Land-use maps learned on them are within a few points of accuracy of pixel models at a small fraction of the cost, and they make whole-country land-use estimates with reliable uncertainty possible in under a minute, where the same model on pixels does not even fit in device memory.

title: Understanding Work/Life Balance Through Mathematical Model
abstract: Work/life balance (WLB) remains a central yet elusive concept in social and organizational sciences, often described qualitatively without a unified quantitative framework. To address this gap, a novel compartmental mathematical model is proposed that formalizes WLB as a dynamic population-level phenomenon. The individuals are categorized into 4 compartments, namely, regularly employed, temporarily employed, imbalanced (infected), and balanced (recovered), representing balanced and imbalanced states. Role-based complaints govern the transitions between states, the conflict conversion rates of these complaints, and the recovery rate. The model, structured as a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations, is analyzed for the existence of the equilibrium and its stability. In the analysis, the stable disease-free equilibrium is found to exist, representing complete societal balance. The other endemic equilibrium is shown to be infeasible through simulations and thus requires certain parameter constraints, which represent a specific scenario that may occur in the population. However, it is found that the endemic equilibrium always remains unstable. The model's ability to quantify how micro-level stressors spread into macro-level imbalance is demonstrated by numerical simulations, which also validate the analytical results. This work establishes a rigorous mathematical foundation for WLB, enabling future empirical and mathematical calibrations.

title: World Models Need Not Be Right to Rank Policies Right: Relative Bounds and Audit Limits
abstract: Selecting a reinforcement-learning (RL) policy usually requires additional environment interaction, while learned world models offer cheap but potentially biased evaluations. This raises two distinct questions: can shared model errors preserve pairwise rankings despite poor absolute values, and do they make a small number of real audits more informative? We derive an exact pairwise simulation identity and a relative bound separating common-mode Bellman residuals from policy-specific error. The analysis motivates RAVEL (Relative Auditing of Value Errors in Learned models), a selective policy tournament whose eliminations use held-out real outcomes. We test 45 SAC, TD3, and PPO policies per task in DMC cheetah-run and walker-walk. At rollout horizon 500, model rankings remain strong (Kendall tau = 0.962 and 0.800), and same-run differential-error ratios are 0.674 and 0.106. Yet mean paired audit-error correlations are only 0.007 and 0.090, and pairing changes standard deviation by -2.5 percent and +1.9 percent. Simultaneous intervals attain 99.98 percent and 99.75 percent coverage, but certify only 13.2 percent and 0 percent of decisions at eight audits. RAVEL improves low-budget walker-walk regret, whereas real-only successive halving is better at the largest budget, rejecting the precommitted twofold efficiency target. Frozen-model optimization lowers real return without increasing predicted return on average. Thus ranking fidelity, useful audit covariance, and upward model exploitation are distinct properties, separated in part by closed-loop trajectory divergence.

title: GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling
abstract: Generative spoken language models (SLMs) offer a route to learning linguistic structure purely from speech, yet they lag far behind text-based models in both capability and data scaling efficiency. We identify two bottlenecks underlying this gap: the limited linguistic quality of existing speech units and the reliance on a single stream of discrete units to represent speech. Multiple codebooks are widely used to encode acoustic features but rarely to represent speech semantics. We present GSLM2, which learns and models complementary properties of speech at multiple levels of abstraction. Its encoder, SpidR 2.0, uses self-supervised learning with differentiable prediction heads to induce high-quality discrete units at multiple levels. A multi-stream SLM then jointly models these units using a shared temporal backbone, stream-specific predictors, and an autoregressive head that captures cross-stream dependencies. Across training data sizes and model scales, up to 6M hours and 6.5B parameters, GSLM2 consistently improves linguistic competence while scaling more efficiently with data. As a result, it substantially narrows the gap between spoken and text-based LMs; across read and conversational speech domains, we shrink the gap by about two orders of magnitude on sWuggy, sBLIMP, and tSC, while also outperforming competitive speech-text systems on all three tasks. We open-source the training code and model checkpoints at https://github.com/facebookresearch/gslm2.

title: The upper main sequence in h and chi Persei
abstract: Binary interactions play a crucial role in the evolution and eventual outcomes of massive stars. Rich young open clusters provide large coeval populations to constrain the effects of binary evolution. The Double Cluster, with a turn-off mass well above the threshold for core-collapse supernovae, is an excellent test bed for these processes. We used h and chi Persei, together with NGC 663, to constrain the evolutionary pathways of massive stars, particularly the role of binary interaction. We present spectroscopy of around 80 stars to obtain spectral types and derive stellar parameters. We combined this dataset with Gaia astrometry to evaluate their evolutionary status and possible evolutionary paths. We derived atmospheric parameters for almost 60 stars in the upper main sequence (B2V and earlier) and found broad agreement between two independent fully automated procedures. We identified the cluster turn-offs between B1 V and B1.5-2IV and differentiated this feature from the vicinity of theTAMS, where we found a population of B1-B1.5 giants, with a high fraction of Be stars. The bulk of the population in all of the massive clusters studied in the Perseus arm is consistent with single-star evolutionary models at a given age, but some B-type supergiants are much more luminous than any other cluster star. Their typical cluster kinematics and stellar parameters suggest a merger origin. Other lower-luminosity B-type supergiants seem consistent with the rest of the population. Kinematic analysis has indicated that most Be stars have not been dynamically perturbed by a supernova explosion. Those below the turn-off are likely to have been formed via case A mass transfer. The more massive Be stars above the turn-off do not display any other characteristic indicating a distinct evolutionary population (abridged)

title: Ranking the Parameters Shaping Grid Dynamics
abstract: Generator and transmission line parameters do not shape the time-domain behavior of a power system equally; a parameter that dominates one dynamic property can be almost invisible to another. This paper studies how the physical parameters of a detailed and general nonlinear differential algebraic equation (DAE) grid model shape the properties that decide whether system states such as frequencies, voltages, and angles can be inferred, observed, controlled, and kept stable. The rankings are conditional as they depend on where grid sensors and actuators sit, on the operating region and the disturbance, on the network topology, and on other settings that the operator chooses. The framework combines DAE trajectory sensitivities, variational Gramians, and stability margin sensitivities to measure how much each parameter reshapes the network dynamics. On three benchmark systems, the rankings show where dynamic leverage concentrates and where the control-theoretic metrics disagree, and they point to how parameter studies can guide calibration, sensor and actuator placement, and security assessment. The proposed methods herein are also scalable and can be tested on grids with tens of thousands of buses.

title: A model-based adaptive sampling framework for infectious disease surveillance
abstract: Longitudinal surveillance must choose each round's sampling design before the next observations arrive. Fixed sample-size rules treat each round as an isolated cross-sectional survey and ignore the evolving uncertainty in the epidemic process, which changes as transmission, vaccination, interventions, variants, and behavior change. We present a model-based adaptive sampling framework for choosing the next-round design. A state-space model represents the epidemic process and maps latent states to surveillance estimands. A statistical filter calibrates the model as observations arrive, propagating uncertainty in latent states, time-varying parameters, stochastic dynamics, and sampling noise. A Bayesian assurance criterion converts the one-step-ahead predictive distribution into the minimum-cost design likely to achieve a target posterior credible-interval width. We evaluated the framework in two simulations and in a retrospective case study of SARS-CoV-2 serosurveillance among Canadian blood donors in four regions, replaying the series with each week's specimens subsampled to the selected design. In simulations, the policy increased sampling effort during an anticipated high-variance period, and the share of intervals meeting the width target (0.970) agreed with validated assurance (0.974). After an unanticipated change in transmission rate, validated assurance stayed at 0.960 while the share meeting the target fell to 0.894 (95% Monte Carlo interval 0.869 to 0.919) in the transition window. Sampling effort rose while the filter relearned the transmission rate, then fell. In the case study, recommended sample sizes tracked the one-step predictive uncertainty and were largest during the Omicron wave, and the 90% filtering interval had width at most 0.10 in 94% of region-rounds with specimens. The modular framework extends to other pathogens, data streams, and surveillance objectives.

title: GraCo: A Unified Toolkit of Graph Coarsening Algorithms and Metrics
abstract: Graph coarsening aims to reduce a graph to a smaller one that preserves chosen properties of the original. It is increasingly used to scale graph learning to large graphs, as a non-differentiable step applied once before training. Many coarsening methods have been proposed in recent years, each with its own implementation, notation and evaluation. In this work, we introduce GraCo, a unified toolkit of graph coarsening methods. It relies on a single definition: a coarsening is fixed by a partition of the nodes and by the Laplacian the coarsened graph is consistent with. The coarsened graph, and the reduction and lifting matrices that map signals from the original graph to the coarsened one and back, follow from these two choices. We implement 17 methods from the literature and a random baseline, grouped into five families, with the same notation, inputs and outputs. We also build a collection of metrics from different papers, applicable to any coarsening. We check the implementations on a synthetic stochastic block model, then we report the runtime and peak memory of each method on Cora, PubMed, ogbn-arxiv and ogbn-products. GraCo is open-source and available at https://github.com/Antonin-J/graco.

title: Differentiable Iterative Learning Control for Black-Box Position-Commanded Manipulators
abstract: High-accuracy repetitive tracking is challenging for position-commanded manipulators whose low-level controllers are inaccessible, while constrained model-based iterative learning control (ILC) can require substantial manual parameter tuning. We present Differentiable Iterative Learning Control (Diff-ILC), an online bilevel framework that adapts the parameters of a constrained ILC update between physical robot executions. A closed-loop differential model is identified once from paired smooth perturbations and subsequently kept fixed. At each trial, a constrained quadratic program computes a feasible command correction, while a real-anchored next-trial prediction defines a task-level objective. Hypergradients are obtained by implicitly differentiating the locally active KKT system, enabling multiple computational parameter updates without additional robot executions. Experiments on a 6-DoF DOBOT CR3 across unseen planar and three-dimensional trajectories show substantially faster physical-trial convergence than fixed-parameter model-based ILC. Across the four primary trajectories, after only two trial-to-trial updates, Diff-ILC achieves 78.8% and 76.4% lower mean joint-vector and Cartesian RMSE, respectively, than fixed-parameter model-based ILC.

title: Learning about Markets from Models: Evidence from an AI Hiring Platform
abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used to not only inform, but make decisions. Sometimes platforms add value by pooling data across contexts to improve models' decision making---but when the optimal decision differs by context, pooling may not increase accuracy. We argue that a platform storing starkly distinct models across contexts nevertheless captures a model comparison externality. Together, these models reflect how decision makers respond differently to the same data in the current equilibrium. Policymakers can use this differentiation to prioritize interventions; firms can learn how they are already differentiated from competitors to focus future investments. Our evidence comes from an AI hiring platform used by large employers of low-skill workers. The platform uses a standardized psychometric assessment to create firm-specific models estimating each application's retention likelihood at that firm. Each firm's model is highly predictive for itself but no better than chance at other firms. We use these models to create a firm-application matrix: each firm scores each application, not only the ones it receives. An application's improved retention likelihood if submitted to a different firm is highly heterogeneous based on traits. Further, these gains are due to two distinct mechanisms. Finally, firms value traits differently even in this low skill market: they disagree about whether important traits improve or worsen retention at the margin. These insights are only possible when a platform can access both the full application pool and each firm-specific model. We explain the value of these insights to firms, policymakers, and platforms.

title: Mathematical Formulation and Comparative Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Maize Land Suitability Prediction
abstract: Addressing the food needs of a growing population is one of the major challenges of developing countries like Ethiopia. Various policies aimed at increasing food production have been enacted by governments and development partners. Although efforts in this regard have been made, there is still inadequate emphasis on increasing food production through the use of high technology practices. Precision agriculture using technology has been utilized to increase crop yield. Precision agriculture also relies on identifying land for a crop, which is a key factor that affects crop yield. Traditional methods of assessing land suitability for crop production are time-consuming, costly and unreliable. Against this background, the aim of this study was to assess the potential of machine learning (ML) in improving the speed and accuracy of assessing land suitability for maize, a staple crop in Ethiopia, as compared to traditional methods. The study is investigated in three areas (Burie, Shindi and Tilili) in the Amhara region. Data collection was done through the local agriculture offices and survey teams. The data were coded, scaled and balanced. Various feature extraction techniques, which included Univariate Feature Selection(UFS), Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross-Validation(RFECV) and Sequential Feature Selection(SFS), and various classifiers, which were K-nearest neighbor (KNN), gradient boosting (GB),random forest (RF) with mathematical formulations were employed. The best models were constructed through combining GBOOST and SFS and achieved an accuracy of 99.41% and 99.35% for both precision and recall. Our results showed that using machine learning is a reliable method of assessing land suitability for maize in Ethiopia. Keywords: Maize, Gradient boosting,Land suitability,Machine learning, Mathematical formulations

title: Toward Bounding Coding-Agent Autonomy in Software Maintenance: A Pilot Study of Boundary Contracts
abstract: As coding agents gain greater autonomy to modify software repositories, relevant context alone does not define their operational authority. An artifact may be relevant to a maintenance task while being inappropriate to edit; conversely, another artifact may be required even when it is not explicitly mentioned in the request. We explore Boundary Contracts, a machine-readable abstraction that makes task-specific artifact roles (editable, inspect-only, required, and protected) explicit before repository modification begins. We conduct a pilot study on 40 maintenance tasks from a real enterprise repository, comparing the same Codex-based coding agent with and without Boundary Contract information. The boundary-informed condition improves macro edit-selection F1 from 0.440 to 0.682, required-behavior coverage from 0.429 to 0.673, and the number of strictly acceptable patches from 9 of 40 to 18 of 40. To probe whether these gains are explained only by improved file localization, we additionally analyze 21 tasks in which both conditions modify at least one identical file. Differences remain in edit selectivity and patch outcomes, providing initial evidence that explicit artifact roles may influence maintenance behavior beyond localization alone. This pilot does not establish the general effectiveness of Boundary Contracts. Rather, it provides initial evidence for a broader research question: how should the operational boundaries of coding agents be generated, validated, revised, and ultimately enforced as repository-level maintenance becomes increasingly autonomous?

title: Forecasting the Ambient Solar Wind With a Physics-Informed Learned Inner Boundary: Part I-Differentiable Inverse Reconstruction From Solar Images
abstract: The solar-wind speed at the inner boundary of heliospheric models is not observed; near-Earth monitors record the wind only after nonlinear propagation. We pose the reconstruction of an effective boundary speed at $21.5\,R_\odot$ as an inverse problem and train a map from solar observations to that boundary by differentiating through a reduced heliospheric transport solver from 21.5$\,R_\odot$ to measurement locations near the L1 Lagrangian point. Screening 42 candidate features from SDO/AIA 193~Å images and SDO/HMI magnetograms identifies coronal-hole area, its proximity to the ecliptic and its darkness as the most informative; the reference model adds their recent history, the expansion factor of GONG-based potential-field models and the speed observed one rotation earlier. In five-fold chronological cross-validation over solar cycle 24, the reconstruction outperforms 27-day recurrence and a linear regression on the screened features at a fixed lead (ROC area for wind above 600~km~s$^{-1}$: 0.879 versus 0.802 and 0.850) with a predicted-to-observed standard-deviation ratio of 0.81, at the cost of a $+26$~km~s$^{-1}$ bias from its tail-weighted loss. A factorial comparison shows that the skill comes from training through a speed-dependent propagation: a fixed lag degrades the score by 8.6~km~s$^{-1}$, stream interaction adds little, and a linear map, or a model with one coefficient per physical quantity, matches the neural network. About 57\% of the variance of the hourly speed is not determined by these inputs, and the remaining error is common to all model classes: better reconstructions need more informative inputs rather than more flexible models. Forecasting and probabilistic prediction are addressed in Parts II and III.

title: Accuracy Is Not Risk: Why Medical AI Should Not Report Only Its Most Likely Label
abstract: Background. Many medical AI models are trained to reproduce a single reference label and hand the most likely label to the next step in a clinical workflow. A classifier can select that label correctly while providing an inadequate summary for estimating downstream risk. Methods. We use Jeffrey's rule of conditioning to specify when probabilities over intermediate states, such as diagnoses or imaging categories, can be carried forward to an outcome risk. We separate two errors of reporting only the most likely label, discarding the probability of the other states and applying the risk of patients who have the leading diagnosis to a patient who only probably has it. We also give conditions under which the label and the full distribution lead to the same decision, and we propose guardrails for device developers, regulatory reviewers, and health insurers. Results. In a hypothetical chest-pain differential, reporting only the benign leading diagnosis greatly understates the patient's risk of death or cardiac arrest, so a patient who warrants evaluation could be discharged or denied imaging. In a hypothetical BI-RADS example, the most likely category is "probably benign," yet the propagated malignancy risk exceeds the ceiling that defines that category. Conclusions. A predicted label is not an observed state, and a calibrated classifier is not automatically a valid outcome model. Clinical and insurance coverage decisions should rest on the patient's outcome risk, judged against a threshold justified by the consequences of acting and not acting. Developers should state what each model output means and check that every step between the model and the decision preserves the patient's risk.

title: Unsatz: Evaluating Scientific Discovery Without a Given Ansatz
abstract: Before a scientist fits any parameter, they must decide what the model contains: which quantities exist, which are hidden, how they interact, and how they are measured. Physicists call such a trial form an ansatz. Benchmarks for automated equation discovery mostly supply it, by fixing the variables, a library of candidate terms, or a law to be modified. We introduce Unsatz, a benchmark in which an LLM agent must construct the ansatz itself. Each task is a simulated system, generated from a private seed as a program in a small modeling language: ordinary, delay, or partial differential equations, discrete maps, static and causal models, or stochastic processes, possibly with hidden states, distorted sensors, and uninformative measurement channels. The agent buys experiments within a budget, writes candidate programs in the same language, obtains their coefficients from the benchmark's fitter, and is scored only on how its final program predicts experiments it never saw: conditions outside the range it could explore, interventions, and longer runs. Across 80 systems in 20 domains, nine language models solve between 21% and 60%. On 44 of these systems, classical equation-discovery methods almost never succeed, although the same data usually suffice once the true equations are given with unknown coefficients; the difficulty lies in finding the structure, not in estimating it. Because mechanisms recur across systems, we also give agents the program they discovered for a related system; it helped only when the new system shared the mechanism and the first investigation had succeeded. Stronger agents make fewer unscientific errors; beyond these, agents find which variables a system has but not how they act, and prefer revisions that lower the training error to revisions that predict better.

title: Programmable Robotic Process Automation Modelling of Software Process
Purchase Intention Formation for K-Beauty Cosmetics: The Mediating Role of Sensory Expectation and the Moderated Mediation of Cosmetic Involvement
abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of consumers’ perception of K-beauty cosmetics in the digital consumption environment on purchase intention and to examine the mediating effect of sensory expectation and the moderated mediation effect of cosmetic involvement. An online survey was conducted from April 1 to April 28, 2026, with 305 Korean women aged 20–49 years. The collected data were analyzed using SPSS 30.0 and Hayes’ PROCESS Macro. Exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, multiple regression analysis, mediation analysis (Model 4), moderation analysis (Model 1), and moderated mediation analysis (Model 7) were performed. The results indicated that quality perception, price perception, and brand image all had significant positive effects on purchase intention, with quality perception showing the strongest effect. Sensory expectation partially mediated the relationships between quality perception, price perception, and brand image and purchase intention, while cosmetic involvement significantly moderated the relationships between each of these perception dimensions and purchase intention. Furthermore, moderated mediation analysis revealed that only the indirect effect of price perception on purchase intention through sensory expectation significantly varied according to the level of cosmetic involvement, with the indirect effect decreasing as cosmetic involvement increased. No significant moderated mediation effects were found for quality perception or brand image. These findings demonstrate that sensory expectation and cosmetic involvement play important roles in consumers’ purchase decision-making process in the digital consumption environment. By examining the mediating and moderated mediation effects, this study provides a more comprehensive understanding of purchase intention toward K-beauty cosmetics. The findings also offer valuable practical implications for developing differentiated digital marketing strategies based on consumers’ sensory expectation and cosmetic involvement.
journal: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology

title: The Effect of Niche Perfume Selection Attributes on the Consume Happiness: The Moderating Effect of Generation through Multi-Group Analysis
abstract: Niche perfume has emerged as a mainstream segment of the perfume market, moving beyond mass-market offerings by reflecting Millennials and Generation Z’s strong preference for individuality and distinctive scent identities. This study aims to analyze the effects of niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. In addition, Millennials and Generation Z are proposed as a moderator affecting the niche perfume selection attributes on consumer happiness. An online survey targeted Korean women from Millennials and Generation Z who have experience using niche perfume. A total of 296 survey responses were analyzed using structural equation modeling with AMOS 26.0 and SPSS 25.0. The results revealed that four key selection attributes emerged from the analysis: trend orientation, brand awareness, premium price perception, and scent. In addition, scent, brand awareness, and premium price perception had significant effects on consumer happiness. Furthermore, the moderating effect of generation was confirmed through multi-group analysis. Specifically, Among Millennials, trend orientation, brand awareness, and premium price perception influenced consumer happiness, whereas scent was the most influential factor among Generation Z. By identifying these causal relationships, this study contributes to expanding the advancement of research on niche perfume and provides implications for developing differentiated strategies tailored to generational characteristics of the Millennials and Generation Z.
journal: Journal of the Korean Society of Cosmetology

title: Implementasi Model Hibrida RT-DETR dan Vision Transformer untuk Deteksi dan Klasifikasi Produk Retail Berdasarkan Citra Kemasan
abstract: Identifikasi produk retail pada kemasan merupakan salah satu penerapan computer vision yang dapat mendukung proses pengenalan produk secara otomatis. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengimplementasikan model hibrida Real-Time DEtection TRansformer (RT-DETR) dan Vision Transformer (ViT) untuk mendeteksi dan mengklasifikasikan produk retail berdasarkan citra kemasan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan eksperimental dengan dataset yang dikumpulkan secara langsung melalui dokumentasi citra kemasan produk retail. Dataset terdiri atas 1.202 citra dari 15 kelas produk, yang dibagi menjadi data pelatihan, validasi, dan pengujian dengan rasio 80:10:10. RT-DETR digunakan sebagai model deteksi untuk menentukan lokasi objek produk melalui bounding box, sedangkan ViT digunakan untuk mengklasifikasikan hasil cropping objek ke dalam kelas produk. Model RT-DETR-L dilatih selama 36 epoch dengan ukuran citra 640 × 640 piksel dan batch size 8, sedangkan ViT-Base Patch16-224 dilatih selama 6 epoch menggunakan citra berukuran 224 × 224 piksel. Evaluasi RT-DETR dilakukan menggunakan metrik mean Average Precision (mAP), precision, dan recall, sedangkan kinerja klasifikasi hibrida dievaluasi menggunakan accuracy, precision, recall, dan F1-score. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa RT-DETR mampu mendeteksi objek produk dengan nilai precision dan recall sekitar 0,90 serta mAP@50 sekitar 0,93–0,95. Pada tahap klasifikasi, ViT mencapai akurasi validasi sebesar 99,2% pada akhir pelatihan. Berdasarkan evaluasi rinci sistem hibrida, diperoleh nilai accuracy, precision, recall, dan F1-score masing-masing sebesar 100%. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi RT-DETR sebagai pendeteksi objek dan ViT sebagai pengklasifikasi mampu menjalankan proses deteksi dan klasifikasi produk retail pada dataset penelitian dengan kinerja yang sangat baik.
journal: Journal Artificial: Informatika dan Sistem Informasi

title: MARKET INFORMATION ACCESS AND WOMEN’S PARTICIPATION IN IRISH POTATO MARKETING: A STRUCTURED NARRATIVE REVIEW
abstract: Women contribute substantially to potato production and post-harvest handling, yet they often enter markets with less information, weaker bargaining positions, and fewer productive assets than men. This structured narrative review examines how access to price, demand, buyer, quality, logistics, and risk information shapes women's participation in Irish potato marketing. Literature published between 2000 and 2025 was identified from major academic databases, Google Scholar, and institutional repositories. Potato-specific studies were prioritized, while broader evidence from smallholder agriculture and digital extension was used only to explain mechanisms where direct evidence was limited. The evidence indicates that market information can improve sales timing, market selection, price negotiation, and coordination of storage and transport. However, information availability alone is insufficient. Benefits depend on women's control of communication devices, literacy, mobility, time, working capital, group membership, and the reliability and actionability of the information received. Mobile platforms can widen reach, but radio, extension agents, and farmer organizations remain important for women with limited connectivity. Direct evidence on marketing intention is sparse; most studies measure access, use, commercialization, or participation and rely on cross-sectional designs. Causal claims should therefore be made cautiously. The review proposes a capability-based pathway in which information contributes to market participation only when women can access, understand, trust, and act on it. Policies should prioritize blended communication channels, local-language and voice-based services, gender-responsive extension, collective marketing, verified buyer networks, and links to storage, transport, finance, and risk-management services.
journal: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities

title: Economic Development of Tourism Villages Sustainable Community-Based Tourism through Indonesia–Australia International Collaboration
abstract: Local economic development through the tourism sector is one strategy to improve community welfare. Sekotong Timur Village, West Lombok Regency, has various local economic potentials that can be developed through a Community-Based Tourism (CBT) approach. However, the community still has limited knowledge in identifying and developing these potentials. This community service activity aims to increase community understanding regarding the development of local economic potential through community-based tourism. The activity was carried out using a participatory method through observation, socialization, counseling, and interactive discussions. The results of the activity indicate that Sekotong Timur Village has natural and coastal potential, agricultural and fishery products, local culinary, crafts, and various community economic activities that can support tourism activities. The activity also increases community understanding regarding the relationship between tourism and the creation of added value, business opportunities, and increased income. CBT development needs to be supported through increasing community capacity, strengthening local businesses, marketing, utilizing digital media, and institutions to encourage sustainable local economic development

title: Agentic AI-Driven Data Engineering: A Framework for Self-Directed Enterprise Data Pipelines
abstract: Enterprise data pipelines have grown in scale and interdependency faster than the operational practices used to maintain them. Pipeline failures are still predominantly diagnosed and remediated by human engineers reading logs, tracing lineage, and applying tacit knowledge, which produces long mean-time-to-recovery and concentrates institutional knowledge in a small number of individuals. This paper proposes an agentic architecture in which large language model (LLM) agents, constrained by explicit tool interfaces and policy guardrails, perform continuous monitoring, root-cause triage, and bounded remediation of production data pipelines. The framework specifies five cooperating agent roles — Observer, Diagnostician, Remediator, Verifier, and Orchestrator — operating over a shared state store containing pipeline metadata, lineage graphs, data-quality expectations, and incident history. We define a capability-tiering model that maps each remediation action to one of four autonomy levels (observe, recommend, act-with-approval, act-autonomously), and we describe a human-in-the-loop governance layer providing approval routing, immutable action logging, and rollback. We further propose an evaluation protocol covering task success rate, mean-time-to-detection, mean-time-to-recovery, false-remediation rate, and escalation precision, together with a reference workload derived from common ingestion, transformation, and schema-evolution failure modes. The paper concludes by analysing failure modes specific to agentic operation — hallucinated root causes, unsafe tool invocation, reward-free drift, and accountability gaps — and argues that autonomy must be earned incrementally through measured reliability rather than granted by architectural default.
journal: International Journal of Frontline Research in Engineering and Technology

title: A Drift-Aware MLOps Pipeline for Retail Demand Forecasting and Inventory Replenishment: A Semi-Synthetic Proof of Concept
abstract: Retail demand forecasting can lose accuracy as demand patterns evolve, which motivates operational pipelines that monitor model errors and govern replacement decisions. This study describes a drift-aware machine learning operations (MLOps) framework integrating stock-keeping unit (SKU)-level Prophet forecasts, rolling mean absolute error (MAE) monitoring, a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE)-based candidate-model safety gate, and inventory replenishment calculations. It is a controlled semi-synthetic proof of concept based on 160,000 Kaggle retail transactions: unit quantities are synthesized from category heuristics, daily series are extended beyond the observed period with a historical-mean procedure, and four controlled drift windows are injected into selected SKUs. Preprocessing yields 52,632 daily records for 72 SKUs. In a leakage-free rolling-origin evaluation over July 3 to 31, 2025 (2,088 one-day-ahead SKU-day forecasts), Prophet achieves an aggregate MAE of 1.49 units/day and a MAPE of 11.65%, against 1.83 and 1.85 units/day for the naive and weekly seasonal-naive baselines and 1.47 units/day for a historical-mean baseline. The illustrative SKU APPL-001 has an MAE of 1.43 units/day and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.72 units/day. These measurements do not identify an effect of retraining. The rolling-MAE detector detected 21 of 48 SKU-window injections (median delay 6 days) and raised 436 alert-days outside the injection windows; the held-out MAPE safety gate accepted 139 of 231 candidate models (60.2%). The pipeline design is coherent, but the study does not establish causal retraining benefit, real-drift detection accuracy, operational scalability, or production effectiveness, which require unit-sales data with naturally occurring drift.
journal: Journal of Computers, Mechanical and Management

title: Digital Literacy and Institutional Support as Predictors of Library Database Use among Undergraduate Students in Two Nigerian Universities
abstract: University libraries invest heavily in electronic databases, but the return on that investment depends on whether students can use them and on the institutional conditions that make access possible. This study examined the extent of library database use among undergraduates in two Nigerian universities and tested whether digital literacy and institutional support predict that use. A descriptive survey was conducted at the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB) and Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife. A sample of 379 undergraduates, allocated proportionately (119 from FUNAAB and 260 from OAU), completed a structured online questionnaire using a four-point agreement scale. Mean scores showed moderate database use (M = 2.64) and favourable ratings of digital literacy (M = 3.00) and institutional support (M = 3.00). Digital literacy (β = .54, R² = .29) and institutional support (β = .71, R² = .51) each significantly predicted database use (both p < .001). Together they explained 55.8% of the variance, F(2, 376) = 237.62, p < .001, and institutional support was the stronger predictor (β = .59 versus β = .26). The findings suggest that building students’ digital skills will yield limited gains unless it is matched by dependable electricity, connectivity, remote access and responsive library support. Because the design is cross-sectional and self-reported, the results indicate association rather than causation, and the study does not measure academic performance or test moderation.
journal: Lead City International Journal of Library Information & Communication Sciences

title: Reliability and Calibration Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Aircraft Recognition in Remote-Sensing Imagery
abstract: Aircraft recognition in remote-sensing imagery is usually reported through detection or classification accuracy. Accuracy alone says nothing about how confident a model is when it is wrong, or how much of an apparent architectural advantage comes from the training budget rather than from the architecture. This study reports a reliability and calibration analysis on the MAR20 benchmark under a complete two-factor design. YOLOv8n and YOLOv8s were trained for aircraft detection, and MobileNetV3-Large, EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet50 were each trained under two training protocols across five fixed seeds, giving thirty classification runs. Classification is evaluated on ground-truth crops and therefore describes an oracle-crop setting rather than an end-to-end pipeline. The effect of the training protocol proved to depend on the architecture and to be of the same order as the differences between the architectures themselves: the longer schedule improved ResNet50 and MobileNetV3-Large on every seed, while EfficientNet-B0 was not separated from its own baseline. Once the protocol was held fixed, EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet50 both reached approximately 0.98 top-1 accuracy and could not be separated by any paired test at either the sample level or the seed level, although both separated from MobileNetV3-Large. Model ranking also depended on the calibration estimator, because the highest equal-width bin holds over 90 percent of the test crops: after temperature scaling, equal-width expected calibration error favored EfficientNet-B0 and equal-mass expected calibration error favored ResNet50. Temperature scaling left accuracy unchanged in all thirty runs while reducing wrong predictions issued above 0.95 confidence by between a quarter and a half. Code, configurations and per-run outputs are archived.

title: Single-cell foundation models transfer across deep evolutionary distances
abstract: Single-cell foundation models are trained mostly on human and other vertebrate cells, yet are proposed as general-purpose models. Whether they transfer far beyond their training species is unknown. We evaluated zero-shot embeddings from Geneformer, scGPT and UCE against PCA and scVI in developmental atlases of Dictyostelium discoideum and Caenorhabditis elegans , separated from humans by 1.2 billion and 600 million years. Without retraining, the models recovered developmental order and preserved organism-specific cell identities. UCE encodes genes by protein sequence and could use 97% of measured genes, whereas Geneformer and scGPT, after ortholog mapping, used under one-fifth. UCE performed most consistently, often exceeding species-native baselines. Restricted to ortholog-mappable genes, it still scored above vocabulary-based models on five of six annotation tasks, some narrowly. Foundation models can thus yield informative cell embeddings across more than a billion years of evolution, and protein-sequence gene representations make these embeddings more complete and often more accurate.
