title: SegFormer and SegFormer-UNet for anthropogenic geomorphic feature extraction from land surface parameters
abstract: Accurate, scalable mapping of anthropogenic geomorphic features from high spatial resolution terrain data remains challenging. While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) excel at characterizing local texture and patterns, their limited receptive fields may fail to capture broader spatial context. Transformer-based architectures, such as SegFormer, support stronger long-range dependency modelling, but their value for geomorphic mapping has not been systematically tested. We compare three architectures for pixel-level extraction of features from light detection and ranging (lidar)-derived land surface parameters (LSPs): (1) SegFormer, (2) SegUNet (a hybrid SegFormer-UNet model), and (3) a fully CNN-based UNet with a ResNet-34 encoder. Models are trained on 512×512 LSP chips for three tasks: agricultural terraces, historic mine benches, and valley fill faces. We evaluate random vs. ImageNet initialization and, when pretraining is used, frozen vs. unfrozen encoders. Training uses focal Tversky loss to address class imbalance; performance is assessed with F1-score, precision, recall, and overall accuracy, with robustness summarized via resampling of test chips. Results suggest that end-to-end training is the most consistent driver of gains across backbones and datasets, particularly for SegFormer. UNet-style architectures with CNN-based decoders generalize most reliably: SegUNet and the UNet typically achieve the best precision and recall balance and the smoothest optimization. Contrary to common practice, random initialization often matches or exceeds ImageNet pretraining for LSP inputs, suggesting a domain gap between natural-image features and lidar-based terrain representations. Across tasks, difficulty tracks object morphology: agricultural terraces are hardest, mine benches intermediate, and valley fill faces easiest. Practically, we recommend unfrozen encoders with a CNN-based decoder as a strong default, and we caution against assuming ImageNet pretraining will help when using LSP predictor variables. These findings provide clear guidance for selecting and optimizing deep learning models for anthropogenic geomorphic feature extraction from high spatial resolution digital terrain data.

title: Three-dimensional bioglass-nanoclay scaffold with localized controlled release of 4-octyl itaconate promotes bone regeneration in osteoporotic bone defects.
abstract: Osteoporotic bone defect repair is a complex physiological process occurring under pathological conditions, which primarily involves the inhibition of bone resorption and the promotion of bone formation. In recent years, composite scaffolds for localized drug delivery have been developed to enhance the healing of osteoporotic bone defects, emerging as a promising yet challenging area of research and clinical application. In the present study, we fabricated a composite scaffold (BG-XLS/ZIF8@4-OI) enabling the localized and controlled release of 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI), a cell-permeable itaconate derivative, for the treatment of osteoporotic bone defects. The scaffold exhibited an interconnected porous structure with pore sizes ranging from 100 to 500 μm, favorable mechanical strength, and sustained release of 4-OI. In vitro, MC3T3-E1 cells demonstrated strong adhesion and proliferation on the composite scaffold. Additional in vitro experiments confirmed that scaffold extracts were non-toxic to cells, effectively inhibited osteoclast formation, and promoted osteoblast proliferation and differentiation. In vivo, the BG-XLS/ZIF8@4-OI scaffold effectively promoted local bone regeneration within the defect region in a rat osteoporotic cranial defect model. In conclusion, these findings indicate that the BG-XLS/ZIF8@4-OI scaffold exhibited good biocompatibility and safety for osteoporotic cranial bone defect repair in rats, improved the local osteoporotic microenvironment, and promoted bone formation, holding immense potential to enhance osteoporotic bone defect repair.

title: Silk-hyaluronic acid bioinks recreate a dynamic chondrogenic niche for stem cell differentiation and matrix-driven maturation in bioprinted cartilage models.
abstract: Progress in cartilage engineering requires advanced tissue models capable of replicating the structural and cellular organisation of native tissue whilst supporting extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling and functional tissue maturation. In this study, methacrylated silk fibroin (SFMA) and hyaluronic acid (HAMA) were combined into a dual-component, photopolimerisable biomaterial ink designed to recreate the biochemical composition and mechanical dynamics of the native cartilage ECM in bioprinted constructs. HAMA incorporation produced a denser, structurally stable hydrogel system, supporting longterm stem cell viability and a rounded, chondrocyte-like cell morphology. SFMA-HAMA hydrogels consistently promoted higher expression of chondrogenic markers -SOX9, COL2A1, and ACAN -and suppressed COL1A2 compared to SFMA, and supported deposition of a hyaline-like matrix rich in sulphated glycosaminoglycans, collagen type II, and hyaluronic acid. Time-resolved mechanical analysis revealed progressive stiffening of cell-laden SFMA-HAMA constructs over 28 days, driven by matrix deposition and hydrogel network reorganisation, distinct from the intrinsic material stiffening observed in SFMA hydrogels. Bioprinted constructs maintained robust chondrogenic potential and construct shape fidelity following fabrication. This work demonstrates that SFMA-HAMA bioinks recreate a dynamic chondrogenic niche capable of directing stem cell chondrogenesis and supporting cell-mediated matrix remodelling and construct maturation -paving the way for more physiologically relevant bioprinted platforms for studying cartilage biology, disease modelling, and the development of innovative regenerative therapies.

title: Assessment of LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks requiring multi-step reasoning and code writing.
abstract: MOTIVATION Large Language Models (LLMs), AI agents and co-scientists promise to accelerate scientific discovery across fields ranging from chemistry to biology. Bioinformatics- the analysis of DNA, RNA and protein sequences plays a crucial role in biological research and is especially amenable to AI-driven automation given its computational nature. Here, we assess the bioinformatics capabilities of popular general-purpose LLMs on a set of tasks covering basic analytical questions that include code writing and multi-step reasoning in the domain. RESULTS Utilizing questions from Rosalind, a bioinformatics educational platform, we compare the performance of the LLMs on 104 questions relative to expert ground truth and 68,760 humans with varying levels of expertise. Among the frontier LLMs evaluated (GPT-5.2, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Llama-3-70B, Llama-4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6), GPT-5.2 exhibited top performance, providing correct answers for 80/104 (77%) questions followed by Claude Sonnet 4.6. LLM performance varied widely depending on the biological categories of questions. While the latest generation of frontier LLM models showed overall improvements in performance, their performance in specific categories of biological questions was lower than first generation models. Overall, LLMs performance mirrored that of humans with lower performance in tasks in which humans had low performance and vice versa. However, LLMs also failed in some instances where most humans were correct and, in a few cases, LLMs excelled where most humans failed. To the best of our knowledge, this presents the first assessment of general purpose LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks in distinct areas relative to both expert and non-expert ground truths. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION The complete analysis was implemented in Python; all code is available at https://github.com/SiwoResearch/lllm-bioinformatics. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: KDM3B regulates hair follicle stem cell differentiation by activating the mTOR-dependent translation program.
abstract: Hair follicle (HF) development and regeneration rely on the precise differentiation of hair follicle stem cells (HFSCs), a process governed by epigenetic regulation. While nutrient-sensing mTOR signaling is known to be pivotal, the upstream epigenetic triggers and the downstream events orchestrating this pathway remain poorly defined. The histone H3K9me2 demethylase KDM3B has recently emerged as a key player in stem cell fate decisions. By integrating recent high-throughput sequencing data and employing a conditional knockout mouse model, we demonstrated that KDM3B was essential for HFSC differentiation, as its loss led to severe defects in postnatal HF development and HFSC differentiation. Mechanistically, we identified the mTOR signaling pathway and its downstream protein translation machinery as the primary effectors of KDM3B. KDM3B activated mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling, which subsequently upregulated the TOP mRNA-binding protein LARP1 to drive ribosome biogenesis and global protein synthesis. Our work delineated a complete 'KDM3B-mTORC1-LARP1-ribosome' axis that functionally integrates epigenetic control with translational regulation to direct HFSC differentiation. These findings not only establish KDM3B as a novel key regulator in skin epithelia but also provide the first comprehensive mechanistic link from an epigenetic modifier through the mTOR pathway to the ribosomal translation program within the HF model.

title: Phenylboronic acid-induced defects in maize roots are independent of rhamnogalacturonan-II dimerization.
abstract: Soil boron deficiency is a global abiotic stress, negatively impacting on crop yield. In the dicot model species Arabidopsis thaliana, inhibition of root elongation is one of the earliest symptoms of boron deficiency. In the monocot model maize (Zea mays L.), boron deficiency-induced root defects are widely unexplored. In this study, we assessed boron deficiency-induced defects in the primary root system of maize and tested the suitability of phenylboronic acid (PBA) as boron deficiency mimic by performing phenotypic, histological, molecular, and biochemical analyses. Our analyses showed that boron deficiency and PBA resulted in similar defects in primary root elongation and lateral root density. The PBA-induced defects, however, were much stronger than those induced by boron deficiency, particularly regarding lateral root development. We provide evidence that the PBA-induced defects were caused by the boric acid moiety and show that both boron deficiency and PBA altered the levels of auxin and reactive oxygen species. Strikingly, PBA did not affect rhamnogalacturonan-II (RG-II) dimerization. Interference of boron-mediated RG-II crosslinking, however, was previously proposed to be the mode of action of PBA in planta. Our study shows that PBA is particularly suited for the molecular dissection of lateral root development in maize and suggests that PBA does not mimic known molecular boron deficiency responses.

title: Transcriptional coordination of the aromatic amino acid metabolic network in Petunia and beyond.
abstract: Plants produce vast arrays of specialized metabolites mediating ecological interactions, notably including phenylalanine-derived metabolites. Biosynthesizing these metabolites requires not only defined structural pathways, but also tight coordination between the shikimate pathway, aromatic amino acid production, and downstream specialized metabolism, such as benzenoid metabolism. Regulation occurs at multiple levels, including post-translational control of enzymes through mechanisms such as allostery, wherein binding of a regulatory metabolite alters catalytic activity. However, transcriptional regulation is also a flux control mechanism in these pathways and has increasingly been studied. Here, we summarize recent developments in this field. Petunia emerged as a key model for understanding how transcriptional networks regulate this metabolic system, complemented by discoveries in other species. Central to this regulation are MYB transcription factors, including PhODO1, PhEOBI, and PhEOBII, which coordinate the expression of genes involved in both precursor supply and volatile formation. These regulators operate within broad networks that integrate environmental signals, including light, circadian rhythms, temperature, and hormonal cues, through additional transcription factors. Developmental regulators, particularly MADS-box transcription factors, link floral organ identity with metabolism, ensuring scent production occurs within appropriate developmental stages and tissues. Beyond transcriptional and enzymatic regulation, accumulation and utilization are also influenced by post-synthetic processes, including glycosylation, intracellular sequestration, transport, storage, and export. Together, these elements form multilayered frameworks that coordinates primary and specialized metabolism, ultimately determining composition, accumulation, and utilization of specialized metabolites. Expanding this framework across plant species will be essential for understanding metabolic regulation and enabling targeted manipulation of aroma and stress-related traits in crops.

title: Weather-driven infection events as indicators of severe wheat stripe rust.
abstract: Plant pathologists, agronomists and crop consultants are often called on to help growers evaluate in-season disease risk and determine if management actions are needed to suppress disease development. Tools that help disease specialists and other practitioners better evaluate the influence of environment on disease development could help guide these recommendations. The objectives of this research were to identify weather conditions influencing the infection of wheat by stripe rust (Puccinia striiformis f.sp. tritici) in field environments, to develop models estimating the probability of infection based on environment, and to evaluate if the predicted infection events were an indicator that weather conditions were favorable for severe stripe rust development in commercial wheat fields. The influence of environment on infection was studied using a bioassay approach that involved exposing inoculated, susceptible wheat seedlings within a wheat field environment. Following the exposure, the plants were incubated with a diurnal temperature cycle of 12-20°C and stripe rust incidence and severity visually evaluated after 14 days. The bioassay was conducted 116 times over three wheat growing seasons. Infection was coded as a binary variable with ≥1% incidence considered an infection event and logistic regression used to model the probability of infection based on weather during the exposure period. Multiple predictive models of stripe rust infection in field environments were developed based on the bioassay results. Several of the identified models correctly classified days as favorable for infection with more than 80% accuracy. The infection models confirmed the importance of extended periods of high relative humidity and favorable temperature on the infection processes of P. striiformis f.sp. tritici and provided guidance on specific thresholds that were conducive for infection in field environments (e.g. > 8 h of RH ≥ 87% and a temperature between 5-25°C). The experimental approach also helped evaluate the influence of wind speed and rainfall events on the infection process that are difficult to accurately simulate in controlled environments. The resulting infection models were combined with simulations of wheat growth and used to estimate the risk of severe stripe rust developing at locations throughout Kansas (n=104). This analysis identified that the accumulation of infection events between jointing and flowering stages of growth were influential on the development of severe disease in research plots and commercial wheat fields. Models estimating the risk of severe disease correctly classified 79% of disease observations collected over 17 years. The timing of these predictions relative to crop growth and disease development could help disease specialists evaluate and communicate the risk of stripe rust in the future.

title: Squash bug host preference is associated with cucurbit yellow vine disease incidence across cucurbit species.
abstract: Cucurbit yellow vine disease (CYVD), caused by Serratia ureilytica and transmitted by the squash bug [Anasa tristis (De Geer), 1773], is a recurring threat to cucurbit production in the United States, yet information on vector host preference and its relationship to disease incidence remains limited. Understanding squash bug-host associations is critical for improving integrated pest management (IPM) strategies for CYVD. We evaluated squash bug abundance and CYVD incidence across six cucurbit species (Cucurbita maxima, C. pepo, C. moschata, Cucumis melo, C. sativus, and Citrullus lanatus) in field trials conducted in Geneva, NY, USA, from 2023 to 2025. Adult, nymph, and egg abundance were recorded weekly, and CYVD incidence and plant mortality were assessed throughout the season. Squash bug populations differed significantly among cucurbit species and years, with consistently higher abundance observed on Cucurbita spp. compared with Cucumis spp. and Citrullus sp. In addition, CYVD incidence and plant mortality were highest in Cucurbita spp. Interannual variation in squash bug abundance and disease incidence was associated with temperature and growing degree-day accumulation, with the highest disease pressure observed in 2024 following a mild winter. Linear regression analyses indicated that squash bug abundance was correlated with CYVD incidence across host species. These results demonstrate that, although other factors might play a role in CYVD incidence, host preference by squash bugs appears to strongly influence CYVD incidence in cucurbits. Insights from this study provide a foundation for improving predictive models and IPM strategies for CYVD and targeted scouting and potential trap cropping for squash bugs.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Generalized Linear Models for Predicting Stagonospora Nodorum Blotch in Winter Wheat. Part II: Validation, Yield Loss Quantification, and Fungicide Profitability.
abstract: Translating plant disease forecasts into profitable management decisions requires quantifying model prediction accuracy, yield response variability, and economic uncertainty. A Bayesian hierarchical framework employing Beta regression was recently used to develop models to predict severity of Stagonospora nodorum blotch in winter wheat. However, performance of these models (validation, yield loss quantification and stochastic fungicide profitability analysis) has not been conducted. Using 394 disease cases from 22 environments (2012-2014), the most complex weather-based model had the lowest root mean square error (RMSE = 11.7%) and near-nominal calibration predictive interval coverage probability (PICP = 100%), although systematic underestimation at high severity (mean error = -16.8% at high disease epidemic scenarios) was observed. Covariate shift analysis across 1,104 synthetic deployment environments identified divergence in some weather predictors. Population-level yield loss was modest (-13.6 kg ha⁻¹ per 1% severity increase) but with extreme environment-specific heterogeneity, indicating that disease severity alone is a poor predictor of yield impact in this pathosystem. A multi-trait Bayesian meta-analytic model jointly estimated disease suppression and yield response to a single fluxapyroxad + pyraclostrobin application at Feekes Growth Stage 8-10, which provided disease protection (46% efficacy) and a severity-independent benefit (+151.3 kg ha⁻¹). Economic simulations showed that breakeven severity shifted from ~5% at low application costs to ~15% at moderate costs under typical wheat prices . Return on investment was more uncertain under higher disease pressure and premium market conditions, where potential gains were also the largest. The integrated framework developed here provides a template for risk-informed decision support system.

title: Spontaneous neuropathic pain
abstract: Spontaneous pain is a highly prevalent and disabling consequence of neuropathic disorders, yet it remains mechanistically underdefined and therapeutically underserved. Historically, preclinical animal models and clinical trials have been overwhelmingly biased toward stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity, relegating spontaneous pain to a secondary manifestation. Emerging evidence now challenges this view. Converging data from pharmacology, neural recordings, and systems-level causal manipulations indicate that spontaneous and stimulus-evoked pain arise from substantially dissociable molecular, cellular, and circuit substrates. Injured-fiber–derived ectopic activity within specific sensory neuron subtypes serves as a dominant peripheral generator of spontaneous pain, whereas cellularly distinct, intact spared-fiber pathways mediate stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity. At spinal and supraspinal levels, spontaneous pain preferentially engages affective–salience networks during pain chronification and may ultimately become stabilized within higher-order circuitry—while remaining dynamically coupled to afferent input. This mechanistic delineation carries critical translational implications. Current diagnostic and treatment guidelines rarely differentiate symptom domains, and most therapies have been validated primarily using stimulus-evoked or overall pain intensity endpoints—potentially contributing to a mechanism–therapy mismatch and variable efficacy. We argue that spontaneous neuropathic pain should be defined as a separate symptom domain rather than considered as a spontaneous manifestation of evoked pain mechanisms. This recognition demands longitudinal, biomarker-informed phenotyping to capture its persistent and fluctuating nature, and thereby enable robust mechanistic dissection at peripheral, spinal, and cortical nodes. Reframing spontaneous neuropathic pain along these lines will provide a foundation for precision therapeutics that target defined cell types, specific molecular drivers, and maladaptive network states—enabling mechanism-based, symptom-aligned treatments.

title: Dynamic modelling and forecasting of interest rates: evidence from Scandinavian countries
abstract: Using unique data of three Scandinavian countries (Denmark, Norway and Sweden), the study examines the term structure of their interest rates and the performance of the Babbs and Nowman model in forecasting the rates covering their economic stability and financial crisis periods from 2000 to 2014. The continuous-time multi-factor model developed by Babb’s and Nowman (1999) is employed for the research alongside the state-space form (TSIR) of the model. The linear Kalman filter algorithm is further implemented to produce the estimates for both the observable and unobservable variables. The dataset used in the study enables a critical assessment of the in-sample and out-of-sample performance across three versions of the multi-factor Babbs and Nowman model. The research shows that the complexity of the three-factor model is necessary to better explain the yield curve dynamics in the case of Denmark and Norway, while for Sweden there is no clear benefit in adding a third factor. However, under the best predictive specification, the out-of-sample analysis produced different results for each country. The findings further exhibit that when considering the forecasting errors, the continuous-time models generate superior forecasts, a feature of great interest in pricing interest rate derivatives and hedging strategies. The study's empirical findings provide insights to investors, forecasters and central banks on the BN model attributes and its ability to explain the yield curve dynamics in times of economic stability and in financial crisis. The research presents new insights on the BN multi-factor model applications on forecasting interest rates and draws on unique data of three Scandinavian countries (Denmark, Norway and Sweden). The study also provides a full spectrum of the model with application to the financial crisis period and for the post-crisis era.

title: Sustainable development of BIM-enabled digital twin framework for monitoring indoor environmental quality: fuzzy analytic hierarchy process approach in educational buildings
abstract: Existing BIM-enabled digital twins visualize indoor environmental quality but don't rank spaces by environmental risk across occupancy states. This study creates an occupancy-aware fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (FAHP) decision layer, integrated with a low-cost BIM-enabled DT, to generate ranked classroom priorities for intervention in educational buildings. A four-layer DT architecture (data acquisition, transmission/storage, modeling/integration, analysis/visualization) was implemented using Arduino UNO R4 Wi-Fi microcontrollers and low-cost sensors (temperature, humidity, CO, NO2, PM2.5, CO2) across five classrooms in an educational building in Vellore, India, under both occupied and unoccupied conditions. Data were transmitted via ThingSpeak and visualized in a Revit/Dynamo BIM model. Three experts pairwise compared six IEQ parameters using Buckley's geometric-mean FAHP to derive crisp weights (consistency ratio = 0.087). Final classroom scores combined weighted, normalized occupied and unoccupied values (a = 0.5), with sensitivity analysis across a = 0.3–0.9, and a two-tier decision rule reconciled relative FAHP rankings with absolute exceedance of WHO/ASHRAE guidelines. PM2.5 (0.428) and CO2 (0.231) received the highest weights. Classrooms 2 (0.2895) and 3 (0.284) ranked highest (worst relative IEQ) and were consistently top priorities across most a values; all five classrooms exceeded WHO CO guidelines at some point. Linking real-time IoT data to the DT supports demand-controlled ventilation and timely interventions, reducing unnecessary energy use and pollutant exposure, supporting SDG 7 and SDG 13. The study introduces a novel occupancy-differentiated FAHP weighting scheme that links BIM-DT sensor data directly to actionable classroom prioritization, thereby addressing the gap between IEQ visualization and facility management decision-making.

title: Chaotic Artificial Protozoa Optimization-based Ensemble Deep Learning Model for Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Accurate crop yield prediction is the significant component while considering the modern precision agriculture due to the increasing demand for food production, climate variability and the necessity for efficient agricultural resource management. The traditional crop yield prediction model has issues with poor scalability, inability to handle large multidimensional datasets and reduced prediction performance for dynamic environmental conditions. In addition, existing prediction methods has challenges like noisy data, redundant feature selection, over-fitting and insufficient capability to capture complex nonlinear and temporal relationships from the data. To address the limitations, this research proposed the crop yield prediction model that integrates data normalization, feature selection and ensemble deep learning model. Initially, data acquired from the publicly available dataset and is preprocessed using Z-score normalization to standardize feature distributions. Then, the proposed Chaotic Artificial Protozoa Optimization (CAPO) algorithm is utilized for optimal feature selection. The optimized feature subset is utilized for crop yield prediction using the ensemble model designed with Support Vector Machine (SVM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Transformer model. Each model has the unique learning capabilities like nonlinear pattern recognition, spatial feature extraction, temporal sequence learning and long-range dependency modeling. Finally, the majority voting criteria is employed to combine the outputs of all models to generate the final prediction outcome.

title: MCapsNet: Modified CapsNet Architecture for Crop Disease Classification
abstract: Accurate crop disease recognition is essential for effective disease management and ensuring food security. Deep learning (DL) models have demonstrated strong potential for automated and accurate disease identification from crop images. However, DL-based methods typically require large-scale training datasets, which can limit their scalability and applicability in agricultural environments. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Modified Capsule Network Architecture (MCapsNet) for effective crop disease classification. The proposed MCapsNet framework consists of multiple processing stages. First, input images of apple crops are preprocessed using bilateral filtering to improve image quality while preserving important structural information. Subsequently, image augmentation techniques, including rotation, shifting, and zooming, are applied to increase dataset diversity and improve model generalization. The augmented images are then fed into the proposed MCapsNet for crop disease classification. Conventional CapsNet architectures may exhibit limitations when processing complex, high-resolution crop images containing multiple disease symptoms because of their relatively shallow architecture. To overcome these limitations, MCapsNet incorporates a modified hyperbolic sigmoid activation function-based Spatial Channel Attention (SCA) mechanism. This mechanism enables the network to selectively emphasize informative spatial regions and feature channels, thereby facilitating the extraction of discriminative features and richer hierarchical representations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MCapsNet achieves a classification accuracy of 95.3% using 90% of the dataset for training, outperforming the evaluated existing crop disease classification methods. These results demonstrate the potential of MCapsNet as an effective approach for automated crop disease classification in agricultural applications.

title: An Ensemble Learning Approach for Crop Yield Prediction in Smart Agriculture
abstract: Crop yield prediction plays a vital role in improving agricultural productivity and supporting informed decision-making for sustainable farming. Conventional forecasting approaches primarily rely on historical observations and manual estimation, which often fail to capture the complex relationships between environmental factors and crop productivity. This study presents a machine learning-based crop yield prediction framework using agricultural and weather-related attributes obtained from a publicly available dataset. Data preprocessing techniques were applied to improve data quality prior to model development. Ensemble learning algorithms, namely Random Forest and XGBoost, were employed to model the relationship between environmental parameters and crop yield. Model performance was evaluated using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the coefficient of determination $\left(\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}\right)$. Experimental results indicate that XGBoost achieved the best performance with an $\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$ score of 0.93 and an RMSE of 1.98, outperforming Random Forest $\left(\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}=\mathbf{0 . 8 9}, \mathbf{R M S E}=\mathbf{2 . 4 5}\right)$ and Linear Regression $\left(\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}=\mathbf{0 . 8 2}\right)$. The proposed framework can assist farmers and agricultural planners in crop planning, irrigation scheduling, and resource management through accurate yield prediction. Although the proposed system demonstrates promising performance, future work will focus on integrating real-time weather information, IoT-enabled sensing, and temporal forecasting techniques to improve prediction accuracy under dynamic environmental conditions.

title: Visual-Inertial RGB-D SLAM with Encoders for a Differential Wheeled Robot
abstract: Recent years have seen multiple impressive results in visual-inertial odometry (VIO) techniques, by which accurate state estimation can be achieved via the extended Kalman filter (EKF) or nonlinear optimization. However, these approaches are rarely open source, and they tend to fail in real experiments due to the temporary lack of feature points and fast motion. Therefore, in this study, we used encoders to overcome the temporary failure of purely vision-based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Here, we propose a generative measurement model for encoders and derive an expression for the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate and necessary Jacobians for optimization. We use our theory to present a novel tightly coupled visual-inertial encoder RGB-Depth (RGB-D) SLAM system. Tests on our system on an in-house dataset confirmed that our modeling effort led to accurate (with a root mean squared error (RMSE) of approximately 2-7 cm) and robust state estimation in real time. The source code and our dataset containing the encoder information have been published for verification.

title: Cube-Drone: A Hybrid Multi-Rotor Robotic Platform for 3D Mapping and Ultrasonic Inspection in Complex Structures
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a multi-rotor drone called Cube-Drone, a hybrid aerial–ground multirotor robot designed for inspection in confined and complex civil infrastructures such as bridges, culverts, and high-rise structures. The platform combines aerial access with surface operation to support an inspection-centric workflow: rapid 3D reconstruction to localize and select regions of interest, followed by repeatable close-range and contact-based measurements using an onboard linear actuator and ultrasonic thickness gauge. The robot carries a 3D LiDAR, camera, onboard computer, and inspection payload while remaining capable of both flight and ground traversal. For flight control, we implement a nonlinear model predictive controller (NMPC) deployed on a resource-constrained embedded processor (Teensy 4.1), enabling onboard optimization-based control without relying on commercial autopilot stacks. We further integrate a LiDAR–inertial mapping pipeline and evaluate its performance and robustness through simulations and real-world experiments, including inspection deployments on representative infrastructure environments. Experimental results demonstrate stable hybrid operation, accurate mapping for inspection planning, and successful acquisition of visual and structural inspection measurements.

title: 3D Gaussian Digital Twins for View-Robust 3D Visuomotor Policy Learning on Articulated Objects
abstract: Single-view 3D visuomotor policies based on point-cloud observations, such as 3D Diffusion Policy, often suffer from limited viewpoint generalization due to partial observability and occlusion. This is particularly challenging for articulated objects whose internal motion induces geometry changes. To address this problem, we propose an articulation-driven digital twin augmentation approach that couples reconstruction, online articulation-state estimation, and observation generation within a shared 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model. Offline, we reconstruct an articulation-aware 3DGS part model and parameterize the articulation. Online, we optimize joint states through differentiable rendering conditioned on the base pose, then transform pre-sampled part point clouds using the estimated configuration. Fusing the object point cloud with robot geometry enables real-time augmentation from partial to global observations using single-camera input during execution. Experiments on the complete pipeline in simulation and the real world demonstrate accurate articulation tracking and improved viewpoint generalization of 3D Diffusion Policy.

title: Edge-Enabled Collaborative Localization With Task-Oriented Communication for Multi-Agent Embodied AI in Smart Factories
abstract: Smart factories increasingly rely on embodied AI agents such as autonomous mobile robots and automated guided vehicles to perform real-time manufacturing, logistics, and inspection tasks. These systems require accurate and low-latency localization to enable safe navigation and coordinated multi-agent operations within dynamic industrial environments. However, conventional localization approaches often depend on centralized processing or raw multi-modal data transmission, which leads to excessive communication overhead, increased latency, and limited scalability in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks. This article presents an edge-enabled collaborative localization framework that integrates multi-agent sensing, task-oriented semantic communication, and edge-based collaborative fusion for smart factory environments. Instead of transmitting raw sensor streams, the proposed framework extracts task-relevant semantic features and transmits compact feature vectors to an edge server, significantly reducing bandwidth consumption while maintaining accurate localization. The edge layer performs collaborative pose fusion and global map refinement across multiple robots, enabling scalable and real-time localization under IIoT communication constraints. A case study-based evaluation demonstrates that the proposed approach improves localization accuracy, reduces communication latency, and enhances scalability compared with conventional cloud-centric and non-collaborative localization methods. The results highlight the potential of combining edge intelligence and semantic communication to support reliable multi-agent coordination in next-generation smart factory systems.

title: Generative AI for Green Energy: Task-Specific Inverse Design of Rectifying Metasurfaces for Embodied IIoT
abstract: The evolution of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) towards collaborative embodied intelligence is fundamentally constrained by energy autonomy, while traditional Rectifying Metasurface (RMS) design is too slow and isolated to support dynamic task coordination and safety in human-robot collaboration. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a generative Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven inverse design framework centered around directly synthesizing metasurface parameters based on on-demand energy targets, which redefines hardware customization as a cross-layer mapping task from network-level energy directives to physical-layer structures. By rapidly customizing efficient RMSs for embodied agents, the framework integrates a multimodal-guided latent diffusion model (LDM) with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning and Cartesian product data augmentation to achieve second-level generation, effectively addressing the few-shot design challenge. Such generation is implemented at the digital design stage rather than real-time physical reconfiguration of fabricated RMS hardware. Crucially, the RMS hardware digital twin proposed in this work is formally defined as a pre-fabrication digital design surrogate customized to task-specific energy harvesting demands without real-time physical synchronization with fabricated rectifying metasurfaces; it constructs such standardized hardware digital twins for multiple agents, enabling concurrent, on-demand structure generation that transcends isolated device optimization and aligns physical-layer energy provisioning with collective intelligence. Validated in a smart factory case, the proposed method significantly reduces design latency and shows potential for resilient operation under dynamic channel conditions, providing a novel solution for adaptive, green, and collaborative IIoT infrastructures.

title: Fabry-Pérot Cavity formed by Magnonic waveguide using holes and notches
abstract: In this paper, we have investigated a spin-wave-based Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity using two air holes and notches embedded in a magnonic waveguide. Through micromagnetic simulations, we have demonstrated the spin-wave profile, as well as the transmission and reflection spectra of the FP type magnonic waveguide, by varying the distance between the center of holes and notches. We have introduced an analysis of the reflection spectra in an FP type magnonic waveguide, which is essential and considerable for the performance of magnonic integrated circuits. We have also presented a theoretical model to describe the transmission and reflection characteristics of the FP-type magnonic waveguide. Furthermore, active tuning of the resonance peak of the FP type magnonic wavguide by varying the external magnetic field has been demonstrated. Our proposed structure and its study may contribute to the development of magnonic integrated circuits for low-power computing and data processing in next-generation spintronic technologies.

title: Senescent Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Drive Stem Cell Aging Through Dysregulated Chemokine Synthesis.
abstract: Aging is accompanied by a progressive decline in tissue regenerative capacity, driven by intrinsic stem cell dysfunction and age-associated deterioration of the surrounding stem cell niche. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are ubiquitous components of stem cell niches, where they integrate structural, metabolic, inflammatory, and paracrine cues to regulate stem cell quiescence, activation, and differentiation. With age, MSCs undergo functional decline and senescence, altering their secretory and signaling profiles. Across tissues, MSC senescence emerges as an intermediate amplifier of aging: molecular, metabolic, epigenetic, and inflammatory stressors promote the senescent state, which converts these upstream insults into chemokine imbalance, chronic inflammation, and progressive loss of stem cell support. Here, we synthesize classical and emerging literature to examine how age-associated changes in MSC chemokine synthesis contribute to stem cell aging, and we propose a synthesis-based model in which MSCs translate age-associated stressors into altered chemokine repertoires that disrupt stem cell-supportive signaling. We also discuss therapeutic strategies, including chemokine-directed therapies, senolytics, and MSC rejuvenation, that may restore regenerative capacity by normalizing MSC-derived signals. Together, the evidence identifies dysregulated chemokine synthesis as a conserved mechanism linking tissue-resident MSC aging to declining regenerative capacity.

title: A Cross-Sectional Study Exploring the Nature, Contributing Factors and Consequences of Violence Against Nurses in Emergency Departments.
abstract: AIM To explore the nature, contributing factors, and consequences of violence against emergency department nurses by patients and visitors in tertiary hospitals in a major city in China. DESIGN A cross-sectional descriptive study. METHODS Data were collected between December 2023 and February 2024 using a translated and adapted questionnaire examining the prevalence, forms, contributing factors, and consequences of violence. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory logistic regression. RESULTS A total of 336 emergency nurses were included, of whom 66.7% reported violence exposure within the past year. Visitor-perpetrated violence was reported more frequently than patient-perpetrated violence. Psychological violence was more common than physical violence and most frequently involved verbal abuse, disruptive speech, and blame. Illness-related impairment was prominent in patient-perpetrated physical violence, whereas alcohol impairment was frequently reported in visitor-perpetrated violence. Dissatisfaction with medical staff outside the emergency department and delayed or inadequate security responses were also commonly reported as contributing factors. Among the variables included in the exploratory regression model (n = 298), uncertainty or absence of workplace violence policies was the only factor significantly associated with reported lifetime violence exposure. Peer support was more commonly reported than managerial assistance following incidents, and visitor-perpetrated incidents generally received higher short-term impact ratings, including impacts on work motivation and personal and psychological well-being. CONCLUSION Violence against emergency department nurses was common, with visitors reported more frequently as perpetrators than patients. Patient- and visitor-perpetrated violence showed different patterns, particularly in the circumstances surrounding incidents and in short-term impact ratings. The findings support differentiated prevention and response strategies, together with clearer workplace violence policies, timely security responses, and structured post-incident organisational support. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE Emergency nursing education and organisational responses should distinguish between patient violence associated with illness-related impairment and visitor violence occurring in contexts such as alcohol impairment, dissatisfaction, or unmet expectations. De-escalation for patient-perpetrated violence should consider the patient's clinical condition, whereas visitor-related incidents may require expectation-focused communication, behavioural boundaries, and timely security involvement. Structured post-incident support should form part of the organisational response to both types of violence. REPORTING METHOD This study adhered to the STROBE reporting guidelines. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION There was no patient or public involvement in the design, conduct, or reporting of this study. IMPACT WHAT PROBLEM DID THE STUDY ADDRESS?: Violence against emergency nurses is a persistent global problem, yet limited evidence has examined patient- and visitor-perpetrated violence separately in Chinese emergency care settings. WHAT WERE THE MAIN FINDINGS?: Visitor-perpetrated violence was reported more frequently than patient-perpetrated violence and generally received higher short-term impact ratings. Illness-related impairment was prominent in patient-perpetrated physical violence, whereas alcohol impairment was frequently reported in visitor-perpetrated violence. Among the variables examined in the exploratory regression, uncertainty or absence of workplace violence policies was associated with reported lifetime violence exposure. WHERE AND ON WHOM WILL THE RESEARCH HAVE AN IMPACT?: The findings may inform nursing educators, hospital administrators, and policymakers developing differentiated prevention, visitor management, and organisational response strategies for emergency nurses.

title: Genome-Wide Splicing Landscapes Across Poplar Cultivars Reveal a GBF3-Mediated Post-Transcriptional Switch Modulating Monolignol Biosynthesis.
abstract: Black poplars (Populus deltoides, P. nigra, and their hybrids) represents economically and ecologically vital hardwood taxa characterised by rapid biomass accumulation, superior wood properties, and wide adaptability. However, the post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms orchestrating xylem development in these perennial trees remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically profiled transcriptome and alternative splicing (AS) dynamics in the developing xylem across five representative cultivars: P. euramericana 'Zhonglin46' (Pe1), P. euramericana 'Guariento' (Pe2), P. nigra 'N179' (Pn1), P. deltoides 'Danhong' (Pd1), and P. deltoides 'Nanyang' (Pd2). RNA-seq analysis of 20 independent xylem libraries revealed 9,981 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and 6,638 alternatively spliced genes across 10 pairwise comparisons. Functional enrichment indicated that transcriptional variations primarily coordinates cell wall biosynthesis and cytoskeleton organisation, whereas AS preferentially tunes nucleic acid binding and metabolic processes. Regulatory network modelling positioned key AS events upstream of core xylogenesis cascades. Crucially, we identified the G-box binding factor GBF3 as a master splicing-regulated hub during secondary vascular differentiation. An intron retention event in GBF3 yields a truncated isoform with aberrant subcellular localisation and abolished DNA-binding capacity, which impairs its transcriptional repression of key lignin biosynthetic genes (PAL2, CAD1, and CCoAOMT2). Collectively, these high-resolution transcriptional and post-transcriptional landscapes illuminate the regulatory architecture of wood formation and provide a valuable genomic resource for trait improvement in woody perennials.

title: PHYA and PHYC as Candidate Loci for Flowering Time and Developmental Plasticity in Wheat.
abstract: Plant architecture and developmental timing are influenced by light availability, especially in high-density cropping systems, where canopy shading modifies both light intensity and spectral quality. Despite their ecological and agronomical importance, the genetic basis of these responses in wheat remains poorly understood. Here, using a Recombinant Inbred Lines (RILs) population, we investigated phenological and morphological traits under sunlight and simulated canopy shade. We identified a major QTL on chromosome 5A with light-dependent allelic effects, indicating genotype-by-environment variation in developmental responses. This QTL corresponds to a structural rearrangement, consistent with an inversion in the wild emmer reference genome that suppresses recombination and maintains a haplotype block at a flowering locus including PHYTOCHROME C (PHYC-A) and VERNALIZATION-1 (VRN-A1). Analysis of a tetraploid wheat diversity panel further showed that natural variation at PHYC-A interacted with VRN-A1 to regulate heading time, with the effect of PHYC-A being substantially stronger in winter VRN-A1 backgrounds. This epistatic interaction likely reflects PHYC's role in modulating the circadian phase of photoperiod-pathway genes. Additionally, we found an early stop codon in the BB genome copy of PHYTOCHROME A (PHYA-B) on chromosome 4B associated with delayed heading, supported by TILLING-derived phytochrome mutants that reveal distinct and complementary roles for PHYA and PHYC in regulating flowering time, plant height, and leaf elongation under simulated canopy shade. Our findings highlight the potential contribution of phytochrome variation to wheat development under canopy-like light environment, thereby extending model insights to agronomically relevant conditions.

title: A Modified Single-Stacked Ensemble Regression Framework for Data-Driven Rice Yield Forecasting in Southeast Asia
abstract: Food insecurity in Southeast Asia has intensified in recent years, highlighting the urgent need for reliable and interpretable quantitative methods for agricultural yield forecasting under data-limited conditions. This study develops a modified single-stacked ensemble statistical framework that integrates Simple Linear Regression (SLR) and Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) to enhance predictive robustness and interpretability. The proposed framework is implemented within the Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining (CRISP-DM), ensuring systematic data preparation, algorithm construction, and validation across five Southeast Asian nations, utilizing 28 potential determinants. From a numerical statistics perspective, the ensemble configuration is designed to improve predictive stability and reduce variance while maintaining algorithm transparency under constrained sample conditions. Comparative evaluation against selected conventional Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms demonstrates that the proposed regression-based ensemble achieves competitive and, in several cases, superior forecasting performance in terms of accuracy, generalizability, and computational efficiency. The results further quantify the interconnected effects of geographical characteristics, climate variables, and macro-structural factors on rice yield dynamics. By providing a scalable and computationally efficient modeling approach, this framework offers a practical foundation for applied mathematical and statistical applications in data-driven agricultural decision-making. The findings also offer actionable insights to support evidence-based policymaking and related strategic investment, contributing indirectly to the advancement of regional food security and related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including SDG1 (No Poverty), SDG2 (Zero Hunger), SDG3 (Good Health and Well-being), and SDG8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

title: Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution
abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue–compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue–adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition–associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8 + T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.

title: Graph-based pangenome analysis uncovers structural and functional impacts of allopolyploidization events
abstract: The emergence of graph pangenomes has advanced the study of structural variants (SVs) across diverse species, yet the impact of complex ploidy on SV landscapes remains poorly explored. Brettanomyces bruxellensis , a yeast shaped by multiple allopolyploidization events, offers a compelling model due to its well-characterized genomic and phenotypic diversity. Here, we integrated subgenome-resolved assemblies with population-scale genomic and transcriptomic datasets to characterize SV distribution and functional impact at the species level. Leveraging a reference graph pangenome, we detected 5972 unique SVs across 1060 isolates. Allopolyploid genomes harbored significantly more SVs (320 on average) than diploids (116), reflecting hybridization’s extensive impact on genome architecture. Functional association analysis revealed that 27.5% of SVs locally influence gene expression. Furthermore, a subset of SVs originating from ancestral divergence between subgenomes (hybridization-associated SVs) formed hotspots of structural diversity and disproportionately affect gene expression, with larger effect sizes than other SVs. These findings underscore allopolyploidization as a driver of structural and functional genomic diversification, highlighting the value of graph-based approaches in dissecting complex genome evolution.

title: A nematic framework for sprouting angiogenesis
abstract: Sprouting angiogenesis is critical for embryogenesis, wound healing, and tumor growth. Here, we show that the liquid crystal framework, which has recently been leveraged to study various morphogenetic events, provides unique insight into angiogenic sprouting. In response to vascular endothelial growth factor, a potent proangiogenic factor, endothelial cells cultured on the surfaces of soft collagen hydrogels form elongated cell streams that coexist with more polygonal cell regions. Angiogenic sprouting initiates preferentially at cell stream tips, where nematic order gradients are most pronounced. We demonstrate that cell streams are associated with large traction forces that lead to three-dimensional deformations of the underlying hydrogel and that stream formation results from a delicate balance between microtubule polymerization and actomyosin contractility. Last, we show that active control of nematic order allows modulation of sprout formation, highlighting the key role of endothelial cell orientation gradients in angiogenic sprouting and paving the way for new therapeutic avenues.

title: Oxygen-dependent constraint of glycolysis through the mitochondrial electron transport chain
abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) are constitutively active in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) cells. Here, we investigated whether these cells could still respond to hypoxia independently of canonical HIF activation. We found that hypoxia provokes a NADH reductive stress that attenuates lactate release when the supply of extracellular pyruvate becomes limited, a response that was restored by the ectopic expression of the cytosolic and mitochondria-targeted NADH oxidase ( Lb NOX). Suppression of the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mtETC) alone is sufficient to attenuate glycolytic flux when extracellular pyruvate is limited, a situation consistent with metabolomic data from human ccRCCs. Furthermore, this response can be mimicked by pharmacological or genetic inhibition of mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) activity and restored by the mitochondrial-targeted alternative oxidase (AOX). Therefore, our data suggest that cells can respond to low oxygen tension through a mitochondrial-dependent elevation of NADH/NAD + , resulting in the suppression of glycolysis when pyruvate availability is compromised.

title: Robust pan-junctional reinforcement preserves the gut epithelial barrier under mechanical stress
abstract: Epithelia are specialized tissue barriers that safeguard the organism’s internal milieu from the external environment, a function critically dependent on intercellular junctions. In the colon, this barrier is repeatedly challenged by mechanical distension from feces, but it is unknown whether and how the colon adapts to this stress, which could otherwise compromise barrier integrity. Here, we show that feces-mediated mechanical distension triggers coordinated remodeling at cell and tissue scales, consistent with a mechanoadaptative response. This response includes recruitment of junctional proteins at all three types of adhesive cell-cell junctions (tight junctions, adherens junctions, and desmosomes). We identified protein-specific temporal profiles of junctional enrichment during distension, with ZO-1, E-cadherin, desmocollin 2, and plakoglobin exhibiting sustained junctional enrichment, whereas desmoplakin and keratin 8 showed progressive accumulation peaking at 15 min of distension. Distension was also accompanied by perijunctional recruitment and activation of nonmuscle myosin II (NMMII). Through genetic, pharmacological, and mechanical perturbations, we demonstrated that NMMII activation is required for epithelial mechanoadaptation. This process depends on extracellular calcium availability and mechanosensitive ion channel activity, supporting a role for calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling in NMMII-mediated junctional reinforcement. Loss of NMMII function impaired the junctional response to distension across all three junctional complexes, including desmosomes, resulting in disorganized junctions and barrier breach. Together, our findings uncover a robust physiological mechano-adaptive response of the adult colonic epithelium to an extrinsic mechanical stress, whereby coordinated reinforcement of all junctional complexes, requiring myosin II activity and calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling, preserves intestinal barrier integrity.

title: Chirality-selective second-harmonic response with Floquet engineering
abstract: Symmetry breaking profoundly influences the macroscopic physical properties of materials. For instance, inversion symmetry breaking in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides enables the emergence of chiral selection rules, featuring distinct optical chirality-selective electronic properties. Here, we demonstrate ultrafast, coherent manipulation of chirality-selective nonlinear optics in monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) through time-reversal symmetry breaking via Floquet engineering. By using sub-bandgap, circularly polarized ultrafast optical pulses, we introduce nondegenerate, chirality-selective optical Stark and Bloch-Siegert shifts. This approach effectively lifts the energy degeneracy, leading to pronounced chirality-selective second-harmonic generation. Furthermore, we reveal that the Floquet-engineered chirality-selective states can be finely tuned using optical parameters such as intensity and chirality. Our results show a method for manipulating the energy degree of freedom, paving the way for ultrafast nonlinear photonics.

title: RNA binding by ADARs prevents RNA interference from attacking self-produced dsRNA
abstract: The ability of an organism to distinguish between self and foreign double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is central to eliciting an immune response when needed while preventing autoimmunity. Using Caenorhabditis elegans , we investigated the interplay between two host pathways that regulate dsRNA expression and function, adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing by adenosine deaminases that act on RNA (ADARs), and RNA interference (RNAi). We found that the number of small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) targeting edited genes is significantly up-regulated in ADAR mutant animals. In addition, despite an almost complete depletion of primary siRNAs generated from editing sites in wild-type animals, secondary siRNAs are generated from edited transcripts, suggesting that ADARs antagonize only the first step of RNAi processing. We show that ADARs interfere with the efficacy of exogenous RNAi in vivo, likely to prevent trans-silencing, and provide evidence that ADR-2 binding to dsRNA is required for efficient RNAi suppression. This work sheds light on how RNA editing safeguards self-dsRNAs against immune recognition and by-product degradation.

title: Monsoon zonal seesaw: Development of the South Asian monsoon aridified North Africa in the Cenozoic
abstract: North Africa experienced a pronounced transition from humid to arid conditions during the early Cenozoic. Meanwhile, the South Asian monsoon underwent substantial intensification, largely driven by the uplift of the Himalayan-Tibetan Plateau. Here, we demonstrate that the two events, which greatly shaped the paleoenvironment and modern regional climate, are not independent responses to paleogeography changes; rather, the former is primarily driven by the latter through the monsoon-desert mechanism, in which South Asian monsoon diabatic heating produces large-scale subsidence and aridity over North Africa. Using multiple ensembles of paleoclimate simulations and a model for the atmospheric response to imposed diabatic heating, we show that the intensification and poleward shift of Asian monsoon rainfall each make comparable contributions to the aridification of North Africa. Our findings identify a persistent dynamical pathway linking the South Asian and North African monsoons and suggest that it played a major role in early Cenozoic North African aridification, while its climatic expression at other times depended on the relative strengths of competing forcings.

title: Enhanced room-temperature spin transport in a deuterated molecular single crystal
abstract: Achieving high-efficiency spin transport at room temperature remains a central challenge in spintronics. Molecular single crystals are ideal candidates for addressing this challenge because their highly ordered lattices and uniform transport pathways intrinsically suppress spin scattering and enable long spin lifetimes. However, integrating these intrinsic advantages into practical devices has remained challenging, primarily because molecular single crystals are extremely fragile during device fabrication. Here, we design a molecular single-crystal system with uniform spin-transport pathways and suppressed spin-relaxation channels, resulting in a substantially enhanced room-temperature spin lifetime, as confirmed by both theoretical analysis and experimental characterizations. By applying a damage-free crystal-handling method with an optimized electrode-transfer technique, we fabricate high-quality single-crystal spintronic devices and achieve a spin-transport efficiency of 15.17% at room temperature, nearly twice the previous benchmark (∼8%). This work establishes a generalizable strategy for designing long-spin-lifetime molecular spintronic materials and demonstrates the practical viability of molecular single crystals as a platform for efficient room-temperature spin transport.

title: Evidence of active whole-genome doubling (WGD) subclones in non-WGD tumors
abstract: Whole-genome doubling (WGD) occurs frequently in human cancer and influences tumor evolution, metastasis, and treatment response. Here, we integrate bulk, single-cell, and spatial data to dissect the subclonal dynamics of WGD. Single-cell data analysis shows that WGD cells are prevalent even in tumors that are classified as non-WGD (nWGD). WGD subclones actively acquire somatic copy number alterations as they expand, suggesting ongoing evolution. We developed and rigorously validated a gene expression–based method, WAGES, to map WGD cell clonal fraction in bulk tumors. Applying WAGES to nWGD tumors, we reveal genomic correlates including TP53 mutations and chromosomal instability that are consistent with the presence of WGD subclones. Clinically, WAGES scores are strongly correlated with tumor metastatic potential, response to treatments including chemotherapy and immunotherapy, and patient prognosis. These findings reveal widespread WGD subclones in nWGD tumors and demonstrate their substantial impact on cancer evolution and therapeutic outcomes.

title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction
abstract: Diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction is difficult to reverse due to long-term impairment of cavernosal microenvironment. Conventional oral or intracavernosal injection therapies suffer from poor targeting, uneven drug distribution, and potential complications. Here, we propose a soft, wireless electronic patch for treating erectile dysfunction (SWEED) in diabetes mellitus, which enables safe, noninvasive, and controllable modulation of penile microenvironment. With its “microelectrode–drug reservoir–nanopore” configuration, SWE intensifies local electrical field nanoscopically and achieves uniform transdermal drug delivery. Through the enhanced local delivery of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), SWEED demonstrates high efficiency in promoting the expression of vascular factors for endothelial repair and enhancing cavernosal blood perfusion. In both in vitro and in vivo settings, the platform achieves vascular regeneration and functional recovery comparable to clinical intracavernosal injection therapy. Moreover, it activates proerectile signaling pathways (EP2/PKA/CREB) and suppresses the TGF-β/Smad pathway, markedly alleviating cavernosal fibrosis. This work presents a paradigm for noninvasive diabetes mellitus–induced erectile dysfunction therapy.

title: Human hair–bearing skin organoids reveal cell type–specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1
abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair–bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type–specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor–α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α–responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α–expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair–bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host–HSV-1 interactions.

title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3
abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against “unseen” epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000 TCRs mapped to >1000 distinct epitopes restricted by >70 MHC class I/II alleles, we identify features that distinguish cognate triads from controls. The resulting model achieves median areas under the curve of 0.81 to 0.92 on validation triads unseen by AF3 or during feature selection. Our results reveal that generalized prediction of TCR specificity from sequence is possible, with the potential to greatly accelerate the decoding of immune responses.

title: Photosynthetic chimeric stem cells function as mitochondrial batteries
abstract: Therapies built on mitochondrial transfer hold promise for repairing dysfunctional, energy-deficient cells. Still, mesenchymal stem cells used as mitochondrial donors are limited by poor engraftment, risk of aberrant differentiation, and low transfer efficiency. Herein, we constructed photosynthesis-empowered cross-kingdom chimeric stem cells (PCSs; “mitochondrial battery”) by introducing plant-derived thylakoid-based artificial nuclei plus FGF21 -encoding messenger RNA (mRNA) into enucleated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Photosynthetic activity enhances mitochondrial transfer to restore metabolism in damaged cells and elevates anabolism to increase FGF21 production. Sustained FGF21 release promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and sustains long-term cellular energy homeostasis. Mouse and porcine wound healing models demonstrate that PCSs recharge cellular energy to accelerate wound repair. This light-activated cellular photosynthetic platform supports modular mRNA programmability, shows no engraftment or aberrant differentiation, and allows repeated administration for diverse therapeutic applications.

title: Intrinsic cellular persistent firing sustains hippocampal spatial representations during working memory
abstract: Neurons are the fundamental units of cognitive processing. The prevailing view holds that neurons are input-output units that fire action potentials only upon receiving sufficient synaptic input. Here, we demonstrate that this may not be the sole operational mode of neurons in vivo during cognitive tasks, by showing that hippocampal place cells actively maintain firing and preserve spatial information through molecularly defined intrinsic mechanisms. Using in vitro and in vivo recordings coupled with molecular manipulation in mice, we reveal that hippocampal persistent firing during spatial working memory is supported by individual neurons via TRPC4 ion channels. Despite the general belief that persistent activity maintains working memory content, we demonstrate that persistent firing instead maintains immediate spatial representations, potentially supporting the encoding of spatial information to guide behavior. These findings position individual neurons as active contributors to information retention, extending their traditional role as passive input-output units and potentially broadening our understanding of neural computation.

title: Tunneling spectroscopy of topological insulator Josephson junctions
abstract: In the seminal proposal by Fu and Kane, the superconducting proximity effect is used to realize topological superconductivity in the topological surface state (TSS) of a 3D topological insulator (TI). In a Josephson junction made on the TI surface, the spin-momentum locking of the TSS guarantees the existence of spin nondegenerate, perfectly transmitted Andreev modes. These modes lead to gap closing as a function of the superconducting phase difference φ. Here, we report the observation of highly transmissive Andreev modes in a TI Josephson junction, probed via tunnel contacts and φ controlled by a flux loop. Within our experimental resolution, they could indicate a gap closing and reopening. This phenomenon is observed for a wide range of chemical potentials, supporting its TSS origin. Under an applied magnetic field, highly transmissive modes are observed locally, matching theoretical predictions for Josephson vortices in the TSS. Our results support the fundamental role of spin-momentum locking in the Andreev physics in the TSS.

title: LAMP2A gene therapy mitigates Parkinson’s disease–related pathology in nonhuman primates
abstract: Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), regulated by its lysosomal receptor LAMP2A, is a key pathway for αSynuclein (αSyn) clearance and a direct target of αSyn-related neurotoxicity. Rodent studies show that LAMP2A enhancement reverses neurodegeneration, whereas its deficiency accelerates pathology. To test translational relevance, we examined whether increasing LAMP2A expression in nonhuman primates could mitigate α-synucleinopathy induced by injections of Parkinson’s disease patient-derived Lewy body (LB) extract. Increasing LAMP2A expression protected nigral dopaminergic neurons from LB-induced αSyn neurodegeneration, delayed the formation and release of pathology-related αSyn species, and evoked a beneficial effect on motor behavior and on cognitive functions of the primate model. Our findings provide preliminary preclinical evidence supporting CMA enhancement as a therapeutic strategy for αSynucleinopathies.

title: PDS5A and TOP2B cooperate for chromatin recruitment via CTCF
abstract: PDS5A, a cohesin regulatory subunit, and topoisomerase IIB (TOP2B), an enzyme resolving DNA topological problems, interact with CTCF and regulate transcription and genome organization. We ascertained that PDS5A and TOP2B are recruited to CTCF-bound chromatin cooperatively and that catalytically active TOP2B increases PDS5A occupancy genome wide. Notably, the amino-terminal 95 to 116 amino acids of CTCF interacts with PDS5A, giving rise to CTCF-PDS5A-TOP2B interaction in vitro and to PDS5A chromatin enrichment via active TOP2B in vivo. PDS5A-TOP2B function together in moderating the resultant gene expression and genome organization. Loss of CTCF (95 to 116 amino acids) led to dysregulated gene expression and mildly reduced chromatin loops. In gliomas, PDS5A and TOP2B expression levels vary, but correlate, contributing to distinctive gene expression patterns. Inducible PDS5A knockdown led to reduced TOP2B occupancy and altered gene expression. Furthermore, PDS5A mediated sensitivity to TOP2 cancer drugs in glioma cells. This functional interaction between PDS5A and TOP2B at CTCF boundaries expands upon the mechanisms affecting gene regulation through genome organization, with implications for glioma therapeutics.

title: The Fireside Database: Large-scale evidence from 25,419 psychedelic support interactions
abstract: Most psychedelic experiences occur outside clinical settings, yet as policy frameworks rapidly expand to accommodate nonclinical use, no systematic data exist on who seeks psychedelic support, under what circumstances, or what makes that support effective. We present the Fireside Database, a US-based dataset comprising 25,419 peer support interactions conducted by 220 trained volunteers at Fireside Project’s Psychedelic Support Line between April 2021 and February 2026. The released resource integrates structured interaction logs with volunteer-coded metadata and 2777 caller satisfaction surveys across five outcome dimensions. Psilocybin was the most commonly reported substance (59.9% of coded interactions), while cannabis produced the highest distress rate (47.2%). The nested data structure—with 50 supporters each completing ≥10 surveyed interactions—supports multilevel modeling of individual supporter effects on caller outcomes. This resource enables research in psychedelic epidemiology, evidence-based training design, and the investigation of what makes psychedelic psychological support effective.

title: Augmenting intercellular mitochondrial transfer for tissue repair and rejuvenation
abstract: Cells exhibit innate reparative communication, enabling the exchange of bioactive molecules and, in some cases, entire organelles. Harnessing this endogenous process of intercellular organelle transfer represents an emerging therapeutic paradigm for restoring cellular function in diseases driven by organelle dysfunction. Mitochondrial transfer has gained prominence for its ability to restore bioenergetic capacity, mitigate oxidative stress, and rescue metabolic function in cells with impaired mitochondrial activity. Given that genetic or acquired defects in mitochondrial function are associated with diverse pathologies, including neurodegeneration, cardiovascular diseases, metabolic disorders, skeletal muscle defects, immune dysregulation, and age-associated decline, mitochondrial transfer offers broad therapeutic potential. Mitochondrial transfer seeks to deliver functional mitochondria to injured cells to reestablish metabolic competence. However, insufficient organelle trafficking and limited control over transfer dynamics remain critical barriers to clinical translation. Recent biotechnological developments aimed at enhancing donor-recipient connectivity, increasing mitochondrial availability, and modulating transfer machinery have begun to address some of these key challenges. This review highlights recent advances in mitochondrial transfer bioengineering, emerging therapeutic applications, and key challenges that must be resolved to enable clinical deployment.
