title: Correction: Accountability in smart contracts and agentic AI: How to address the responsibility gap and retain meaningful human control?
Automated Parkinson’s disease identification from MRI images using InceptionV3 transfer learning and ensemble stacking
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurological disorder caused by a lack of dopamine. It affects the connections between the body and brain, damaging motor functions. The main symptoms are rigidity and tremors. According to WHO reports, 8.5 million individuals were affected by this disease in 2019. Some research estimates indicate that 25.2 million individuals will suffer from it by 2050. Most people affected by this disease are 60 years old, where PD is an aging disease. Disease detection is very difficult, as it has symptoms similar to those of old age (above 50 years). Therefore, early disease identification is essential for improving patient outcomes and ensuring appropriate treatment. Imaging tools and techniques play a vital role in the early identification of neurological diseases such as PD and AD. Advanced machine learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models have been useful for disease identification using imaging technologies in recent years. In this study, we analyzed and extracted features from PPMI PD MRI scans using the Inception V3 (IV3) Transfer Learner (TL) model and stacking-based (Ensemble Learner) classifiers. ML models such as SVM (RBF), MLP (50,50), MLP (70,70), and stacking are used IV3 PD MRI scan features and provide the performance results. A 5-fold cross-validation is a crucial implementation for dataset accuracy stability. The experimental results show that the stacking classifier achieved the best performance, with an AUC of 0.999, classification 98.4% -Accuracy (CA), 98.4%-F1-Score, and 98.7%-recall and 98.3%-Presession. The proposed model shows high accuracy and reliable prediction of PD from MRI images. The proposed model efficiently differentiates PD patients from healthy CN subjects. This was verified by comparing the confusion matrix and ROC curve. Future studies can employ larger multihospital MRI databases to increase the reliability and generalizability of the proposed system. The utilization of DL models along with multimodal clinical data can be suggested to increase the accuracy of predicting the early stages of PD.

title: A systematic review of sustainable pathways for balancing food production and environmental sustainability in Ethiopian agriculture
abstract: Between 2010 and 2026, Ethiopia faced the dual challenge of increasing agricultural production to meet growing food demand while safeguarding the natural resources that underpin long-term agricultural sustainability. Thus, the objectives of this review were to examine the interactions between food production and environmental sustainability in Ethiopian agriculture. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, evidence was synthesized from 130 peer-reviewed empirical studies and supporting grey literature identified through comprehensive searches of Scopus, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, and Google Scholar. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using an adapted Critical Appraisal Skills Programme checklist. The evidence indicates that agricultural expansion and conventional farming practices have contributed to widespread environmental degradation through soil erosion, nutrient depletion, deforestation, land degradation, and inefficient water use, threatening long-term agricultural productivity and ecosystem resilience. The review consistently identifies Climate-Smart Agriculture, agroforestry, sustainable intensification, and improved water management as the most effective pathways for enhancing agricultural productivity while improving soil health, water-use efficiency, biodiversity conservation, and climate resilience. However, their implementation remains constrained by socioeconomic limitations, weak institutional and extension support systems, insecure land tenure arrangements, knowledge gaps, population pressure, and climate-related risks. The review also identifies opportunities associated with supportive national policies, indigenous farming knowledge, climate financing mechanisms, and digital innovations. Nevertheless, the findings should be interpreted with caution because the review included only English-language studies conducted in Ethiopia and was limited by the methodological heterogeneity of the included studies. Thus, the review suggests that balancing food production and environmental sustainability in Ethiopia requires integrated and context-specific approaches that simultaneously address productivity needs and ecological sustainability.

title: Next-generation cotton improvement through integrated biosynthetic pathways, multi-omics, artificial intelligence and advanced breeding technologies
abstract: Cotton (Gossypium spp.) is a globally important fibre and oilseed crop whose productivity and quality are increasingly constrained by climate change, biotic stresses and the complex genetic architecture of key agronomic traits. Recent advances in genomics, high-throughput phenotyping and systems biology have transformed our understanding of cotton evolution, fibre development, stress adaptation and defence mechanisms. This review synthesizes current progress in cotton improvement through integrative approaches encompassing pan-genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and phenomics, with particular emphasis on fibre quality regulation, secondary metabolite-mediated insect resistance and abiotic stress tolerance. We highlight how polyploidy, structural variation, homoeolog expression bias and regulatory network rewiring underpin phenotypic diversity and environmental adaptability in cotton. Furthermore, we discuss the emerging roles of artificial intelligence and machine-learning models in genomic prediction, trait mapping and decision support for precision breeding. The review also examines translational innovations, including CRISPR-based genome editing, nano-enabled delivery systems and nano-formulated inputs for sustainable pest and nutrient management. By integrating multi-omics data with AI-driven analytics, we propose a next-generation framework for accelerating cotton breeding pipelines under changing agro-ecological conditions. Despite rapid progress in Genomics, Bioinformatics, and Plant Breeding, existing reviews lack a systems-level perspective that links data generation, predictive modeling, and targeted intervention. This review addresses this gap by conceptualizing these advances as components of an integrated, data-driven breeding pipeline. This review uniquely integrates multi-omics and AI-driven approaches into a unified framework for cotton improvement, highlighting existing gaps and future opportunities. By integrating genome editing, nano-enabled delivery systems, and predictive analytics, these approaches enhance selection accuracy, reduce generation intervals, and enable high-throughput screening, collectively improving breeding efficiency, reduces breeding cycles and field-level resilience.

title: Stress biology of Cannabis sativa regulating cannabinoid and terpene biosynthesis at physiological, molecular and metabolic levels
abstract: Cannabis sativa L. is a valuable crop in the medical and industrial fields that possesses several unique secondary metabolites, including cannabinoids and terpenes, that play a role in the therapeutic effects and quality of Cannabis. The number of cannabinoids and terpenes produced is affected by many environmental stressors, making Cannabis an excellent model for understanding how various stressors influence metabolic processes through hormonal regulation. This review combines all the current information available on the physiological, molecular and metabolic responses of Cannabis sativa to different stressors such as drought, salinity, high temperatures, low temperatures, nutrient deficiencies, light stress and pathogen pressure. The changes caused by environmental stresses on photosynthesis, water status and the use of hormones in the development of glandular trichomes and the flux of secondary metabolites are examined closely. Also, the molecular responses to these changes, with attention given to gene networks that respond to stress, transcription factors that mediate stress responses and the pathways that regulate different enzymes involved with the cannabinoid and terpene biosynthetic pathways, are examined. The review reveals the significance of the relationship between the metabolic processes associated with primary and secondary metabolites, as well as how an organism’s genetic expression can be affected by environmental elements. The comprehensive approach to incorporating these different levels of view expands the understanding of stress physiology of C. sativa and provides an overview of the major research areas that need to be expanded to improve C. sativa response to stressors and phytochemical optimization due to climate change. The novelty of this review lies in its integrated synthesis of physiological, hormonal, molecular and metabolic mechanisms linking environmental stress with cannabinoid and terpene biosynthesis in C. sativa, while identifying key gaps in stress intensity–metabolite relationships, terpene regulation, stressor interactions and high-altitude responses that require multi-omics investigation.

title: Improving multilayer soil moisture estimation using a tri-step framework coupling optimized physical and data-driven models
Eating Experiences and Behaviors after Metabolic Bariatric Surgery: A Multicenter, Longitudinal Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND Metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS) often results in substantial changes of patients' eating behavior through physiological and behavioral mechanisms. However, its effects on different dimensions of eating, including eating in the absence of hunger (EAH), the subjective experience of eating (eating hedonics), and eating-related practices, remain insufficiently understood. This study examined longitudinal changes in these domains following MBS. METHODS N=1058 patients (mean age 46.76, 68.20% female) undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy completed clinical interviews and questionnaires assessing EAH, eating hedonics, and eating-related practices pre-MBS, 6-, 12- and 24-months postoperatively. Item-level longitudinal changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. Standardized mean differences were calculated to estimate effect sizes. Longitudinal associations with percentage total weight loss (%TWL) were examined using adjusted linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS Descriptively, EAH decreased post-MBS, with the largest reductions for palatability-driven EAH. Eating hedonics showed very small to small changes, with increases in sensory enjoyment and decreases for negative affect during eating. Greater decreases in EAH were associated with 2.07 percentage-points higher %TWL, while changes in eating hedonics showed small, directionally mixed associations with %TWL. Compared to pre-MBS, some eating-related practices changed (e.g., increased chewing), whereas others (e.g., time spent on food preparation) remained largely unchanged. CONCLUSIONS Findings of reduced EAH, small but overall positive changes in eating hedonics and specific changes in eating-related practices contribute to a differentiated characterization of postoperative eating across multiple domains of eating. Longitudinal associations between EAH and weight loss highlight the importance of monitoring non-normative eating behaviors for optimizing postoperative outcomes.

title: DHA-H and HPA restore impaired neurogenic phenotypes and BDNF-TrkB signaling in Ts65Dn neurospheres and hippocampus.
abstract: Impaired neurogenesis is a hallmark of neurodevelopmental disorders, including Down syndrome, and contributes to long-lasting deficits in brain structure and function. Membrane lipid composition is emerging as a critical regulator of cell fate decisions in the developing and adult brain. Here we investigate the pro-neurogenic potential of the synthetic PUFA DHA-H (2-hydroxylated DHA) and its immediate metabolite HPA (Heneicosapentaenoic acid) in cellular and tissue models derived from the Ts65Dn mouse model of Down syndrome, using DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) as a reference pro-neurogenic ω-3 PUFA. In primary neurospheres, DHA-H and HPA increased the expression of neural stem and progenitor cell markers, including Sox2, Ki67, and Nestin, and stimulated proliferative activity, accompanied by a parallel upregulation of early neuronal differentiation markers such as Doublecortin and PSA-NCAM. Notably, both compounds promoted the recovery of these markers in Ts65Dn neurospheres, with HPA achieving restoration to wild-type levels for several markers, while DHA-H exerted beneficial effects that varied across the evaluated parameters. These improvements were associated with enhanced BDNF production and TrkB phosphorylation, highlighting the BDNF-TrkB signaling axis as a potential molecular mediator of their pro-neurogenic effects. In vivo, administration of DHA-H and HPA increased BDNF and phospho-TrkB protein levels, together with the number of proliferating cells and mature neurons in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus, suggesting enhanced activity of the adult neurogenic niche and potential neuroprotective effects. Together, our findings identify DHA-H and HPA as promising modulators of neural progenitor dynamics and neurogenesis in a trisomic context, revealing a lipid-dependent mechanism of neurodevelopmental plasticity and supporting their therapeutic potential for ameliorating impaired neurogenic programs in Down syndrome and related disorders.

title: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication.
abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.

title: HFPO‑TA induces developmental hepatotoxicity in hESC‑derived hepatocyte‑like cells by disrupting lipid homeostasis and mitochondrial function.
abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA), an alternative to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), can cross the placental barrier, raising concerns regarding fetal hepatic development; however, the mechanisms underlying its developmental hepatotoxicity remain poorly elucidated. Here, human embryonic stem cell-derived hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) were exposed to HFPO-TA at 3, 15, or 75μM for 28 days during hepatocytic differentiation. HFPO-TA accumulated intracellularly in a dose- and time-dependent manner and impaired hepatic function, evidenced by reduced albumin secretion and CYP activity and increased alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling revealed extensive disruption of lipid metabolism, including increased triglycerides, total cholesterol, and low-density lipoprotein levels, and decreased high-density lipoprotein levels. HFPO-TA activated PPAR signaling and altered genes and proteins associated with lipid synthesis and oxidation, with significant perturbations even at the environmentally relevant concentration of 3 μM. Oil Red O staining and altered PLIN1 and PLIN2 expression confirmed lipid droplet accumulation. HFPO-TA also disrupted mitochondrial function, altered respiratory chain activity, reduced ATP production and mitochondrial membrane potential, and up-regulated fission-fusion-related genes. Collectively, these findings indicate that HFPO-TA impairs hepatocyte differentiation through PPAR-mediated lipid remodeling and mitochondrial dysfunction, highlighting safety concerns for this PFOA alternative. Furthermore, HLCs are a valuable in vitro model for assessing the developmental toxicity of PFOA alternatives.

title: Peripheral nerve block injection pressure monitoring: A systematic review.
abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVE To determine whether injection pressure and pressure-time characteristics can discriminate potentially hazardous needle-tip locations during peripheral nerve injection. DESIGN Systematic review of experimental preclinical studies with narrative synthesis. SETTING Animal, ex vivo biological nerve, and human cadaver models of peripheral nerve injection. INTERVENTIONS Needle placement and injection at intraneural, intrafascicular, perineural, or extraneural locations. MEASUREMENTS CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 28, 2026 and updated on September 19, 2026. Studies reporting opening, peak, or plateau pressure or pressure-time characteristics in relation to anatomically defined needle-tip location were eligible. Human clinical studies and non-biological bench models were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using SYRCLE for animal studies and a domain-based framework for cadaveric studies. Because of substantial heterogeneity in experimental models, injection techniques, and pressure definitions, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate. MAIN RESULTS Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria: 12 animal or animal ex vivo studies and 16 human cadaver studies. Intraneural injection was generally associated with higher peak and plateau pressures than perineural injection, but substantial overlap occurred across needle locations. Importantly, low pressure did not reliably rule out intraneural injection, while elevated pressure was also observed during needle-nerve contact and fascial injection. Consequently, the commonly proposed 15-psi threshold showed inconsistent sensitivity across experimental settings. Lower thresholds, including 12 psi, appeared more sensitive in some models but have not been clinically validated. Beyond absolute pressure values, the rate of pressure rise and pressure-time curve morphology showed potential for differentiating needle-tip locations. CONCLUSIONS Injection pressure monitoring may provide a nonspecific warning of needle placement within or against a poorly compliant structure. However, preclinical evidence alone cannot establish whether it should be used routinely or whether it reduces nerve injury. No universal pressure threshold or clinically recommended injection rate can currently be defined.

title: Quantifying environment-dependent global antibiotic resistance gene risk patterns and mitigation scenarios using integrated machine learning and counterfactual scenario evaluation.
abstract: Environmental antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) pose major ecological and public health risks, yet environmentally conditioned risk patterns and mitigation potential remain poorly quantified. This study aimed to characterize global ARG risk patterns, identify associated environmental and agricultural factors, and evaluate potential mitigation scenarios using an integrated machine learning framework. Using 274,382 sample-ARG-environment records and 150 environmental and agricultural variables, quantile models characterized conditional risk index (RI) distributions and upper-tail risks, multi-model analysis assessed predictive variable importance, and DML estimated covariate-adjusted conditional associations. Heterogeneity was assessed across habitats, countries, and ARG categories, followed by directionally constrained counterfactual evaluation of multi-factor mitigation scenarios. Global ARG risk varied strongly with environmental conditions. In predictive importance analyses, winter temperature anomalies, manure nutrient loading, and pesticide application were important for upper-tail RI prediction. Separately, DML identified positive conditional associations of RI with insecticide application, cropland nutrient surplus, and manure loading, and negative associations with nutrient use efficiency. These associations varied across habitats, particularly soil, crop roots, freshwater, and biological waste environments. Under a predefined 50% predicted RI reduction target, nine-factor adjustment reduced mean standardized adjustment distance by 69.1% relative to single-factor adjustment, although outcomes varied among ARG categories. These model-based findings support global ARG risk characterization and management prioritization within the One Health framework, subject to empirical validation.

title: Salidroside engages HSPA5 and attenuates PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP signalling in ovariectomy-induced bone loss.
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE Rhodiolae Crenulatae Radix et Rhizoma (Hong-jing-tian) is a well-documented traditional Chinese medicinal herb. Its pharmacopoeial marker salidroside exerts osteoprotective effects in ovariectomized models, yet its molecular targets remain elusive. AIM OF THE STUDY To investigate salidroside-HSPA5 engagement, restoration of ER-stress-disrupted BiP-PERK association, and HSPA5 requirement for salidroside responses in stressed osteoblasts. MATERIALS AND METHODS Ovariectomised rats received salidroside (30 or 100 mg·kg-1·d-1) or alendronate, followed by bone, serum and protein analyses. Plasma proteomics identified HSPA5. Salidroside-HSPA5 interaction was validated by docking, SPR, CETSA, DARTS and ATPase assays. Tunicamycin-stressed MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts were used to assess cellular rescue, HSPA5-PERK interaction (co-immunoprecipitation) and UPR signalling. Hspa5 siRNA verified HSPA5-dependent mechanisms. RESULTS HSPA5 and eIF2α were core network nodes. Molecular docking predicted that salidroside binds to the HSPA5 ATPase domain (-8.53 kcal mol-1). Direct target engagement was supported by SPR (KD = 30.3 μM), CETSA (ΔTm = 2.61 °C) and DARTS assays, which showed concentration-dependent HSPA5 stabilization (90.0% residual HSPA5 at 1 mM salidroside vs. 38.3% for vehicle). Salidroside mildly suppressed recombinant HSPA5 ATPase activity (<30% inhibition at 1 mM). In ovariectomized rats, high-dose salidroside increased bone volume fraction from 9.8% to 36.4%, restored bone-formation markers and reduced ER-stress signalling. In tunicamycin-challenged osteoblasts, salidroside recovered viability, osteogenic differentiation and nuclear RUNX2. It attenuated three UPR branches and partially restored stress-disrupted HSPA5-PERK interaction (normalized co-precipitated HSPA5: 0.74 vs. 0.15, P = 0.001). Hspa5 knockdown abrogated the cytoprotective and osteogenic responses to salidroside. CONCLUSIONS Salidroside engages HSPA5 to restore stress-disrupted BiP-PERK complexes. It suppresses pathological PERK-driven UPR over-activation and rescues osteoblast function in osteoporosis models. Its osteoprotection is HSPA5-dependent.

title: A comparative computational analysis of guard cell and mesophyll cell metabolism across C3 and CAM photosynthesis.
abstract: Understanding the interlinked metabolism of guard cells (GCs) and mesophyll cells (MCs) and their roles in stomatal movement in C3 and Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM) is important for designing crop plants with improved water use efficiencies. Although previous studies reported specific metabolic, osmotic, and enzymatic patterns in isolated GC and MC of both C3 and CAM, and the role of different osmolytes in stomatal opening in combined GC-MC metabolism of C3, a detailed phase-wise comparison of osmolyte accumulation, metabolism, enzyme activities, and energetics between GC and MC within an integrated GC-MC model for both photosynthetic modes is still lacking. Here, we integrate osmolyte accumulation-dependent stomatal opening, gas exchange, and metabolism in the six-phase diel combined GC-MC metabolic model and simulate cellular metabolism using Flux Balance Analysis. Results capture the phase-specific contribution of diverse osmolytes, including K+, Cl-, NO3-, malate2-, citrate3-, glucose, fructose, sucrose, etc., on stomatal regulation in C3 and CAM. It further predicts phase-specific MC-to-GC carbon transfer and reproduces higher activities of C4-like enzymes, including PEPC, MDH, ME, PEPCK, etc., in C3 GC relative to MC. It also captures temporal enzymatic patterns in CAM GC and MC and reveals differential fluxes through reactions involved in the production and utilization of ATP and reducing equivalents across the diel cycle. Collectively, these findings provide a quantitative framework for understanding the coordinated metabolic, osmotic, and energetic regulation of GC and MC in C3 and CAM and identify metabolic processes that may require coordinated regulation for engineering CAM-associated traits into C3 crops.

Asymmetric Janus Patch Integrating Antifouling and Wet-Adhesive Functions for Infected Wound Repair.
abstract: The wet, dynamic, and bacteria-contaminated microenvironment of infected wounds creates conflicting demands for stable wound-facing adhesion and outward antifouling protection. To address these demands, we developed an asymmetric Janus hydrogel-film patch (JP-TA/Fe) with a coordination-stabilized bilayer interface. The patch consisted of a dense nonadhesive layer containing silk fibroin/tannic acid (SF/TA) and an adhesive hydrogel layer containing polyacrylic acid/recombinant collagen/tannic acid (PAA/rhCol/TA). TA-Fe3+ chelation was introduced at the bilayer interface through a facile process to strengthen interlayer bonding and maintain bilayer structural integrity during hydration and mechanical deformation. The outward-facing SF/TA layer provided mechanical support and an antifouling barrier, whereas the wound-facing hydrogel layer exhibited favorable fluid-uptake capacity and maintained stable tissue adhesion. Benefiting from this asymmetric design, the patch exhibited robust wet-tissue adhesion, pH-responsive TA release, asymmetric antifouling and adhesive properties, antibacterial activity, biofilm-disrupting performance, and efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging capacity. In a rat full-thickness skin incision model and a Staphylococcus aureus-infected full-thickness skin defect model, JP-TA/Fe promoted stable wound closure, reduced bacterial burden, and accelerated collagen remodeling and epidermal regeneration. This study presents a structurally stable Janus wound patch with spatially differentiated functions, providing a multifunctional material platform for infected wound repair.

title: Agentic, Autonomous Design Evolution of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Recent AI systems can autonomously execute scientific workflows and empirical software tasks. We investigate whether an autonomous agent can use evaluation feedback to iteratively develop a scientific model. To address this question, we developed AutoResearch-MLIP, a research protocol in which the agent follows predefined instructions to propose, implement, and evaluate MLIP designs, with outcomes carried forward to guide subsequent iterations. Starting from a simple pair-distance MLIP, each generation selects a parent model by balancing exploration and exploitation, while structured design records guide subsequent proposals. Across 40 generations, the agent explores MLIP designs spanning local message passing, radial representations, scalar-vector states, body-order terms, residual readouts, long-range-inspired terms, and periodic image-offset graph construction. The final G40 model is competitive with established MLIP baselines in post hoc benchmarks. These results show that, within predefined rules, an autonomous agent can use evaluation feedback to iteratively improve MLIP implementations.

title: Coregulation patterns in emotional sharing dynamics among adolescent friend dyads.
abstract: Adolescence is a critical period characterized by heightened emotional intensity and volatility during which peer friendships gradually replace family as the primary source of emotional support. Understanding patterns of emotional interaction between adolescent friends is crucial for promoting their socioemotional development. Guided by the temporal interpersonal emotion systems theory, the present study focused on emotional coregulation-reciprocal emotional linkage in which mutual damping enables dyads to reach dynamic equilibrium. We employed dyadic discussion tasks (negative problem discussion vs. pleasant topic discussion), combined with second-by-second facial expression coding to capture adolescents' emotional expressions. Emotional dynamics were modeled using the coupled oscillator model, and distinct patterns were identified through latent profile analysis. Associations between these patterns and individual traits as well as relational characteristics were also examined. In the negative context, two profiles emerged: "coregulation," marked by mutual emotional convergence and gradually stabilized over time, and "nonregulation," marked by persistent fluctuation without returning to equilibrium. Friendship duration was positively associated with the likelihood of entering the coregulation pattern, whereas perceived problem severity and affective empathy were negatively associated with this pattern. In the positive context, coregulation did not emerge as a typical pattern. Instead, dyads were differentiated by "in-phase" versus "out-of-phase" oscillation, which were not significantly associated with individual or relational factors. The results provide empirical evidence for understanding the emotional dynamics in adolescent close friendships and may help inform peer-oriented approaches aimed at supporting adolescents' socioemotional well-being. title: A qualitative exploratory study of pathways to moral repair and moral injury in U.S. veterans.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Potentially morally injurious events (PMIEs) are situations in which individuals perpetrate, fail to prevent, witness, or are directly impacted by actions that violate deeply held moral beliefs. Approximately half of U.S. veterans endorse PMIE exposure, and about 13% of those exposed meet criteria for probable moral injury, a syndrome of functionally impairing moral emotions, beliefs, and social behavior indexed to one's worst and most distressing PMIE. Little is known about why some individuals recover following PMIE exposure whereas others experience enduring impairment. METHOD This qualitative study examined psychological, social, and institutional processes that differentiate veterans with probable moral injury from PMIE-exposed noncases. In-depth interviews were conducted with 39 veterans (20 cases, 19 noncases) sampled from a nationally representative study. Applied thematic analysis was used to identify cross-cutting themes and compare trajectories across groups. RESULTS Cases and noncases described similar acute moral distress, but their reported experiences diverged over time. Six overarching themes emerged the following: (a) a widening experiential gap characterized by identity disruption, moral emotions, and functional impairment among cases; (b) early emotional and behavioral responses that shaped trajectories; (c) the central role of social ecology in maintaining or eroding belonging; (d) divergent moral emotion trajectories (i.e., shame, guilt, anger) among cases; (e) meaning-making and repair processes facilitated recovery; and (f) the influence of leadership and institutional betrayal in exacerbating impairment. CONCLUSIONS These findings offer empirical support for key components of the social-functional model of moral injury, while generating hypotheses that highlight potential targets for prevention, mitigation, and treatment. title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immune-related adverse events in a multi-phase validation study.
abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) affect up to 40% of patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet identification requires laborious, inconsistent manual chart review. Here we show that agentic artificial intelligence coupled with human verification could enhance efficiency, performance and consistency for irAE assessment. We developed and evaluated an agentic large language model system to extract the presence, temporality, severity grade, attribution and certainty of six irAE types from clinical notes. Retrospectively, the system achieved a macro-averaged F1 of 0.92 for current-event detection and 0.66 for multi-class severity grading; self-consistency improved F1 by 0.14. The best-performing configuration cost approximately US$0.02 per note. In prospective silent deployment over 3 months, the binary F1 was 0.72-0.79. In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff, agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 min (P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (odds ratio 1.45; 95% confidence interval 1.01-2.08; P = 0.045) and improved interannotator agreement (Krippendorff's α from 0.22-0.51 to 0.82-0.85).

title: ESMRank: learning-to-rank prediction of missense variant effects from deep mutational scanning data
abstract: Predicting the functional effects of missense variants is limited both by predictor performance and by the lack of principled strategies to integrate heterogeneous multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs), including deep mutational scanning, into transferable sequence-function models. Here, we show that redundancy among partially overlapping deep mutational scanning experiments, often treated as noise, yields a consensus landscape of mutational constraint. We introduce “variant soundness”, an overlap-aware rank-fusion score that uses cross-experiment consistency to derive an assay-agnostic ordering of mutational tolerance within proteins. Applied to ~1100 MAVEs spanning over two million missense variants, this approach reveals a mutational landscape enriched for structural stability constraints. Guided by this integrated signal, we develop ESMRank, a sequence-based learning-to-rank predictor combining ESM2 representations with physicochemical descriptors. Under strict protein-level partitioning, ESMRank outperforms widely used predictors across abundance-, folding-, and stability-related assays in ProteinGym and Domainome. Predicted deleterious variants are enriched for ClinVar pathogenicity and, in CFTR, correlate with folding efficiency, channel activity, and pharmacological responsiveness. Together, these results turn assay redundancy into a scalable resource for interpretable missense variant prediction.

title: Stem cell-delivery hydrogels with shear-thinning injectability promote bone healing in distraction osteogenesis.
abstract: Distraction osteogenesis (DO) is a widely used surgical procedure for limb lengthening, deformity correction, and management of segmental bone defects. However, delayed bone consolidation can lead to a long treatment time and poor healing quality, which remains an unsolved clinical problem. Herein, a bioactive injectable material (BIM) was developed to improve the clinical outcome of DO. A naturally-derived polymer (gelatin) composed of bioactive silicate-nanodisk (LAPONITE®) was crosslinked with natural-origin genipin. The BIM features sustainable linear release of pro-osteogenic components (Mg2+, Li+ and Si4+ ions) and linear biodegradability upon gradual tensile loading during the DO procedure. The BIM promoted the proliferation and osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in vitro, with RUNX2 and OCN mRNA expression upregulated by 112% and 160%, respectively, and VEGF expression increased by 357% (p < 0.01). In a rat DO model, single injection of the MSC-laden BIM during the distraction phase significantly augmented healing quality, with BV/TV increasing by 358% and BMD by 288% compared to the control group (p < 0.01). Mechanical testing revealed a 243% increase in maximum load (p < 0.01), and immunohistochemical staining confirmed enhanced blood vessel formation. The special design of this novel injectable material together with MSC transplantation provides a novel strategy to reconstruct a favorable microenvironment for bone regeneration, unachievable by the traditional methods (using growth factors like BMP-2 or VEGF with high cost and poor stability), which provides insight into the development of a promising translatable biomaterial-enhanced strategy for DO.

title: Stability-oriented variance forecasting for financial panels under market-state shifts
Beyond frameworks: The political economy of One Health integration in Africa
abstract: Background : Africa’s post-pandemic moment has produced an abundance of One Health frameworks but limited critical engagement regarding which integrative arrangements actually work, for whom, and at what scale. Continental frameworks articulate the case for cross-sectoral coordination, yet implementation remains fragmented, and the evidence base for specific policy levers is uneven. Methods : We conducted a purposive narrative review of peer-reviewed literature published between 2020 and 2025, complemented by policy documents from continental and regional bodies. Sources were selected to illustrate both integrative possibilities and documented failure modes of cross-sectoral implementation in Africa. Results : We synthesise evidence across four pathways – health systems, climate-smart agriculture, community-led conservation, and institutional coordination – with digital transformation, gender inclusion, and indigenous knowledge as cross-cutting enablers rather than parallel domains. For each pathway, we engage critically with both flagship successes and their documented limitations. These include evidence gaps in AI-enabled surveillance platforms, governance critiques of community conservation finance, persistent shortfalls in domestic health financing, and a coordination paradox in which continental frameworks have multiplied faster than implementation capacity. Conclusions : Across all four pathways, the binding constraints on One Health integration are political and fiscal rather than conceptual. We identify three policy levers most likely to translate integrative rhetoric into measurable outcomes: mandatory inter-ministerial reporting on shared indicators, legal recognition of community institutions, and ringfenced domestic financing. This synthesis is relevant to African policy makers, funders, and practitioners working at the intersection of public health, agriculture, conservation, and governance in a period when the external funding environment is shifting rapidly. By examining evidence from four interconnected pathways in parallel, we show that cooperation across the human, veterinary, plant, environmental, and social science sectors surfaces integrative failure modes, such as digital surveillance systems that improve detection without changing outcomes, or conservation finance that celebrates community leadership while eliding governance critiques, that single-sector analyses miss. This synthesis combines peer-reviewed evidence with policy documents, practitioner reports from African-led institutions, and critical scholarship on community governance. We argue that mandatory joint reporting, legal recognition of community institutions, and ringfenced domestic financing are the near-term reforms most likely to translate One Health integration from rhetoric into measurable outcomes.

title: AI-Driven Discovery and Delivery Systems for Anti-Parkinsonian Agents.
abstract: Parkinson's disease is the second most widely diagnosed neurodegenerative disorder in the world, affecting more than 10 million people, with current drug therapies for treatment providing limited symptomatic relief and no effect on stopping disease progression. The integration of AI and Pharmaceutical Sciences has led to a change in the approach to discovering and developing new anti-Parkinsonian drugs. This review presents a comprehensive overview of the many applications of Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Generative AI to the PD drug development process.We have critically examined AI-guided target identification, including disruption of α-synuclein (SNCA) fibrils, inhibition of Leucine Rich Repeat Kinase 2 (LRRK2), modulation of GBA1/Glucocerebrosidase and restoration of mitochondrial functions via PINK1/Parkin along with the application of Transformer-based models such as AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold to elucidate the structures of Pathological proteins and create the basis for conducting AI-accelerated Virtual Screening studies, yielding exciting lead compounds.Although tremendous advancements have been made, many obstacles need to be overcome, such as obtaining rare disease data, improving the interpretability of the data used in AI models, developing appropriate regulatory pathways, and bridging the gap between pre-clinical and clinical data.

title: Digital finance and agricultural entrepreneurship
An update on combinational chemo-immunotherapy for breast cancer using nanotechnology.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Breast cancer is still a considerable public health issue worldwide. However, earlier studies reported that chemotherapeutic drugs suppress the immune system. Therefore, a combination of chemotherapeutic agents with an immunomodulator might enhance antitumor immunity through immunogenic cell death, cross-priming, and the regulation of immune checkpoint molecules. AREA COVERED Nanotechnology-enabled drug delivery has received considerable attention in chemo-immunotherapy. A comprehensive literature review was performed using google scholar, Science Direct, the Clinical Research Database, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and DOAJ. The review discusses the combination of immunotherapy and nanotechnology including AI-based techniques used to identify suitable biomarkers and to enable selective drug delivery to breast cancer cells. EXPERT OPINION The combinational therapy containing chemotherapeutic agents and immunomodulators has shown promising results due to their synergistic effects. The application of artificial intelligence (AI) in nanomedicine has enabled the design of nanoparticles, predict their interactions with drugs, and personalize treatment based on patients' individual tumor profiles. This advancement has marked the advent of precision medicine in oncology, which focuses on tailoring therapies to each tumor's molecular and genetic profile. Despite these encouraging developments, several challenges remain in nanotechnology for cancer therapy, including mass production, biosafety, regulatory issues, and the successful translation of laboratory findings into clinical practice.

title: Cross-machine profile prediction and differentiable optimization by learning multi-tokamak databases
abstract: The development of high-performance plasma regimes is becoming increasingly important for tokamak operation and scenario design. Conventional operation-space exploration relies on computationally expensive iterative simulations and experimental trial and error. Although machine-learning methods have recently been applied to this problem, many optimization approaches treat the predictive model as a black box. They can therefore require a large number of model evaluations and must be retrained when the objective or operational constraints change. In this work, we develop a neural-network surrogate for multi-tokamak profile prediction using public databases. Device-dependent dimensional input and output variables are transformed into appropriate normalized quantities. These normalizations of input and output variables enable the prediction model to be applied to new devices such as ITER. The surrogate forms a fully differentiable mapping from engineering parameters to plasma profiles and derived performance metrics. Automatic differentiation provides the exact Jacobian of this mapping and enables gradient-based optimization without treating the model as a black box. Under identical objectives and bounds, the proposed method requires substantially fewer model evaluations than other machine-learning approaches. The proposed framework offers an efficient route from multi-machine data to interpretable plasma optimization and reactor scenario design.

title: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived spheroids and microtissues for biofabrication: advances in bioassembly and bioprinting strategies
abstract: Biofabrication integrates biological and engineering principles to generate functional tissues for regenerative medicine, drug screening, and disease modeling. Among the diverse cellular sources available, mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have emerged as a critical component due to their multipotency, immunomodulatory capacity, and scalability. This review focuses on MSC-derived spheroids and microtissues as building blocks for biofabrication, organizing recent advances in bioassembly and bioprinting strategies around the axis of undifferentiated versus pre-differentiated microtissues and how the timing of differentiation shapes construct functionality. Key technological innovations, including dynamic culture systems, scaffold-free assembly, and high-resolution bioprinting (e.g. droplet-based), have enabled enhanced control over microtissue maturation and structural fidelity. The role of the cellular microenvironment in determining MSC fate is examined, emphasizing how biochemical cues, mechanical properties, and oxygen gradients can be engineered during microtissue formation. Cellular heterogeneity is addressed as a path-dependent variable continuously reshaped by donor-specific factors (age, sex, health status) and process-imposed cues (isolation methods, expansion conditions, and mechanical stress) throughout the in vitro life cycle, and concrete mitigation strategies are discussed, including prospective cell sorting and a proposed functional potency panel (extracellular matrix deposition, fusion competence, and secretome profiling), alongside recent advancements in automated and machine learning-based biofabrication platforms. Vascularization and immunological integration are examined as central translation bottlenecks, covering endothelial co-culture, prevascularized spheroids, sacrificial bioprinting, and MSC-driven modulation of the host immune response. By integrating the fabrication route, heterogeneity as a manufacturing process variable, and translational/regulatory bottlenecks into a single framework, this review highlights recent advances, discusses current limitations, and outlines future directions for clinical translation of MSC-based biofabrication.

title: Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded in microbiome research, yet the way microbiome scientists are trained has not kept pace. Existing discussions frequently emphasize AI literacy and responsible tool use. We argue that literacy alone is insufficient in a field where data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, inappropriate model selection and unverified generative-AI outputs can produce convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. We propose an AI-competence framework comprising five connected capabilities: data and platform fluency, machine-learning competence, advanced model competence, large-language-model and agent competence, and biological closure. The final capability-the ability to connect computational predictions to independent data, mechanistic reasoning or experimental evidence-is essential for ensuring that predictive performance becomes meaningful biology. We further propose that competence should be demonstrated through reproducible scientific artifacts rather than course completion alone. Shared datasets, computational platforms and benchmark challenges could make such training broadly accessible while establishing common standards for evaluating AI competence in microbiome science.

title: TEMPEST - A modular Python-based thermophysical model for rough, irregularly-shaped airless bodies
abstract: Comparing observed and predicted surface temperatures on airless planetary bodies is crucial for interpreting their surface processes, constraining activity, and deriving their surface properties. We present a new tool in this endeavour: TEMPEST (Thermophysical Evolution Model for Planetary Environment Surface Temperatures). It is a modular, open-source Python model for diurnal thermal evolution on irregular bodies. TEMPEST can reproduce non-Lambertian multiple scattering using arbitrary Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Functions (BRDFs) and notably incorporates surface roughness on sub-facet scales through representative sphere-section geometry. The model includes an explicit time-stepping one-dimensional periodic conduction solver influenced by Spencer's thermal model Thermprojrs, and a semi-implicit Crank-Nicolson solver, and can be paired with other thermal solvers. Precomputed look-up tables enable fast application of scattering laws (Lambertian, Lommel-Seeliger, Hapke, or input empirical BRDF data), allowing the user to assess their effects in permanently shadowed regions or partially shadowed terrains. TEMPEST is parallelised, running on personal computers in minutes for thousands of facets and scaling to high-performance servers for models exceeding 100,000 facets. Validation was performed against Thermprojrs in one dimension, against Sorli's Binary Thermophysical Model in three dimensions, and with empirical thermal data from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, showing good agreement in each case. Application to the high-resolution shape-model of 25143 Itokawa shows the importance of self-shadowing and radiative mutual heating in controlling local temperatures. TEMPEST has already been used to analyse data from the Lucy Mission, Galileo, and ground-based observations, and is adaptable to upcoming datasets from targets of missions such as Comet Interceptor and Europa Clipper.

title: Credit expansion and countercyclical bank equity issuance: evidence from China
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between macroeconomic credit expansion and external equity financing within China's heterogeneous banking system. Specifically, it seeks to document the countercyclical pattern where credit booms systematically crowd out equity replenishment. Furthermore, the research aims to deconstruct the underlying transmission mechanisms, including liability-side liquidity constraints, mechanical risk accumulation and profitability dilution. Crucially, it explores how institutional backstops and frictions – such as state ownership, deposit insurance and cross-border market discipline – modulate this behavior. Ultimately, this research seeks to inform targeted macroprudential policy design in emerging markets. This study employs a dual analytical approach. First, we construct a dynamic two-sector banking model to theoretically ground the relationship between credit cycles and equity issuance. Second, we utilize an annual panel of China's A-share listed commercial banks from 2007 to 2023 for empirical validation. We apply two-way fixed-effect regressions to test the baseline countercyclicality. To rigorously address endogeneity, we implemented a Bartik shift-share instrumental variable, seemingly unrelated regression (SUR) and system GMM estimators. Furthermore, we conduct mediation analysis using a bias-corrected bootstrap approach and employ triple-difference (DDD) frameworks to evaluate institutional moderating channels. Furthermore, we document that institutional backstops, notably state ownership and implicit guarantees, actively amplify this countercyclicality by serving as substitutes for market-based recapitalization. Conversely, exposure to rigorous market discipline – evidenced by higher debt-financing costs, elevated credit risk and cross-border dual-listings – dampens these extreme procyclical swings. Notably, the formalization of deposit insurance stabilized funding and effectively neutralized this historical countercyclicality. Our results, robust across Bartik shift-share IV and SUR approaches, demonstrate that this reluctance to replenish capital extends to hybrid tier-1 instruments, providing a unified account of how institutional frictions reshape bank financing hierarchies in emerging markets. This study advances the literature through a multidimensional approach. First, we develop a dynamic framework illustrating how credit cycles and debt supply drive banks' financing trade-offs. Second, we empirically document countercyclical bank equity issuance and deconstruct its core transmission channels. Third, we reveal how institutional features – namely state ownership, deposit insurance and cross-border market discipline – modulate this procyclical retrenchment. By integrating theory and empirics, our study provides a foundation for moving beyond one-size-fits-all models and advocating for differentiated macroprudential policies and targeted recapitalization tools in emerging markets.

title: Impact of mobile money adoption on remittances and net farm income of oil palm farmers in Ghana
abstract: This study examines the factors affecting the adoption of mobile money, its effects on remittances received by oil palm farmers and the net income of smallholder oil palm farmers in the Prestea-Huni Valley Municipal District of Ghana. Using a multi-stage sampling technique, a total of 400 oil palm farmers in the study area were surveyed, and the data were analyzed using a Firth Penalized Logit model to determine the factors affecting the adoption of mobile money. In addition, an endogenous switching regression model was used to determine the effects of mobile money use on remittances received and the net income of oil palm farmers. The study finds that the probability of adopting the use of mobile money increases with the ownership of a mobile phone, access to the network, distance to the farm, educational level of the farmer and the experience of the farmer in oil palm production, but decreases with the age of the farmer. The average treatment effects of mobile money on remittances and net farm income are positive. The study also finds a large and statistically significant potential income gain for current non-users of about GH¢750 per year, which is largest among older non-adopters and robust to alternative specifications. This study provides policy implications for the use of digital finance in agriculture in Ghana. This study contributes to the existing body of knowledge on the use of digital finance in agriculture in Ghana and similar smallholder agricultural contexts.
journal: Journal of Agribusiness in Developing and Emerging Economies

title: The algorithmic mirror: AI disinhibition and anxiety-driven compensatory consumption
abstract: Consumers are increasingly exposed to AI influencers across digital marketing environments, yet little is known about how these virtual agents shape anxiety-driven purchasing behavior. This study aims to propose the AI disinhibition effect, a dual pathway model in which appearance anxiety drives consumption through a fear of missing out (FOMO)-mediated compensatory route common to all influencer types and a direct disinhibitory route unique to AI contexts where social evaluation is absent. Four experimental studies expose participants to human, realistic AI or animated AI influencers presenting products at varying risk levels. Conditional process analyses examine the mediating role of FOMO and the moderating roles of influencer type, visual realism and product risk. Appearance anxiety increases FOMO, which drives compensatory consumption across all influencer types. A direct anxiety to impulsive and compulsive buying pathways additionally emerges in AI contexts, where the absence of social evaluation reduces self-regulatory restraint. This disinhibitory effect is stronger for animated than realistic AI influencers and diminishes as product risk increases, disappearing entirely for high-risk categories where safety concerns restore deliberative processing. The studies rely on experimental stimuli and short-term behavioral intentions, suggesting opportunities for longitudinal and field-based extensions. AI influencers are most effective for low-risk, identity-expressive categories such as fashion and beauty and considerably less so in high-risk categories such as health or financial products, where consumers engage greater scrutiny. By identifying conditions under which AI influencer environments amplify anxiety-driven consumption while bypassing deliberative control, this research raises important concerns for consumer well-being and highlights the ethical responsibilities of firms deploying virtual agents in marketing practice. This research introduces the AI disinhibition effect and integrates it with compensatory consumption theory. It advances understanding of how influencer type, visual realism and product risk jointly shape anxiety-driven purchasing in AI-mediated marketing environments.

title: Cereal Biomass Valorization for Functional Food Ingredients: Fractionation and Circular Biorefinery Strategies.
abstract: Food processing must transition toward resource‐efficient systems that operate within planetary boundaries. Cereals, as climate‐resilient staples, offer strong potential to valorize nutrient‐rich fractions. Zero‐waste biorefinery concepts and green fractionation technologies, integrated with structure–function principles, enable the conversion of whole‐grain biomass into functional ingredients for food applications. This review systematically evaluates recent advances in fractionation and separation technologies, including nonthermal physical and biochemical approaches. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA)‐guided analysis of peer‐reviewed articles (2020–2025) was conducted to assess extraction strategies, functional performance, and sustainability‐related aspects. Mechanistic insights into recovered biopolymers are discussed to design process–functional relationships, with an emphasis on fractionation strategies such as synergistic recovery, fraction precision, and yield optimization relative to process complexity. The analysis shows that 46.75% of studies focused on common grains, whereas 53.25% utilized side streams (42.86% bran) for the recovery of proteins (32.47%), fibers (55.84%), lipids (10.39%), and phytochemicals (89.61%). Although hybrid techniques enhanced selectivity, multi‐fraction recovery, and the preservation of biopolymer functionality, linear pathways dominated (70.13%), particularly in ultrasound‐assisted methods (57.14%). Few studies investigated whole‐system biorefinery approaches (14.29%), sustainability assessments (<5%), or pilot‐scale validation (10.39%). Findings reveal critical opportunities for integrating life cycle assessment, techno‐economic analysis, and digital modeling to facilitate scale‐up and industrial translation. Furthermore, underutilized crops and industrial residues show promise for circular valorization. The review highlights the potential of sustainable biorefineries to reduce waste, enhance resource efficiency, and support circular‐driven food innovation.
journal: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

title: Global Change Is Reshaping Coral Communities and Threatening Reef Physical Functionality
abstract: Coral reefs are undergoing profound compositional changes driven by climate change, disease, and chronic human disturbance. Coral cover is the primary metric used to track reef condition, but it often fails to capture the contributions of different coral species to reef carbonate production, structural complexity, and associated biodiversity. Here, I review evidence showing that global change disproportionately removes competitively dominant and architecturally complex corals, driving non‐random changes and coral community homogenisation. These changes erode reef functionality, even when overall cover is maintained. Species‐specific contributions to calcification and structural complexity span orders of magnitude, such that targeted losses of framework‐building taxa collapse carbonate budgets and habitat architecture in ways not predictable from cover trends. These structural changes cascade through associated communities, undermining functional diversity and the ecosystem processes on which reef resilience depends. Critically, rebounds in coral cover frequently reflect the colonisation by fast‐growing opportunistic species, which yield slow or absent recovery of physical functionality, while reassembly and the re‐establishment of large, structurally complex colonies (and the physical functionality they provide) might lag by decades. Furthermore, as mass disturbance events occur at ever‐shorter intervals, recovery windows close before reef‐building potential and complexity can be fully restored. Monitoring, management, and restoration should therefore focus on trait‐ and species‐explicit assessments that prioritise protection and restoration of keystone reef‐builders, target sites with high functional potential, and reduce stressors at appropriate scales. Integrating functional metrics into policy and restoration planning is essential to safeguard reef geomorphic and ecological services under continued global change.
