title: Preserved B Cell Function in CD23-Cre Transgenic Mice Allows Reliable Flox-Only Controls in Mouse Models.
abstract: B cells are pivotal for adaptive immunity by mounting antigen-specific humoral protection. They form unique B cell-receptors, enabling them to differentiate into effector cells upon antigen activation. T-independent B cell activation results in rapid IgM production, whereas T-dependent activation initiates a germinal center reaction in which memory B cells and plasma cells that produce high-affinity antibodies are generated. However, dysregulated B cells lead to diseases like autoimmunity or immunodeficiency, highlighting the importance of understanding B cell mechanisms. As immune responses are complex, in vivo models are essential. Conditional knockout-mouse models using the Cre-loxP system allow cell-type-specific gene deletion and subsequent analysis of protein functions. Hereby, CD23-Cre transgenic mice are used to study mature B cell responses. Unfortunately, the CD23-Cre transgene was inserted randomly, and Cre-associated toxicity has been reported in other mouse strains. Therefore, off-target effects cannot be excluded, so most studies use Cre-only mice as controls. Unfortunately, breeding Cre-only mice and knockout littermates yields significant numbers of non-experimental genotypes and contradicts the 3R-rule for animal welfare. Here, we demonstrate that CD23-Cre-only mice show no signs of Cre-mediated toxicity and establish a reliable mature B cell compartment. T-independent activation of CD23-Cre-only B cells results in normal plasmablast differentiation and IgM production. Furthermore, CD23-Cre-only mice demonstrate robust vaccination-induced T-dependent germinal center responses and stable antigen-specific humoral immunity. Thus, the CD23-Cre transgene leaves the B cell compartment fully functional and enables the use of flox-only controls in immunological studies. This reduces the number of surplus animals generated and supports the 3Rs principle in animal experiments.

title: An AI agent-enabled smart home control system with ESP32
abstract: Smart home systems continue to suffer from limited cross-platform compatibility, insufficient personalization, and unreliable remote access, hindering the unified device management expected in modern living environments. This paper presents an AI agent-based home control system centered on the ESP32-S3 microcontroller. The system integrates environmental sensors, a voice interaction module, and actuators, and combines automatic speech recognition, a large language model for natural language understanding, and MQTT-based messaging to enable coordinated multi-terminal control. It supports three concurrent interaction modes—local voice commands, a mobile application, and third-party ecosystem integration—while providing environmental monitoring, conversational response, and remote management capabilities. A prototype implementation demonstrates low latency, reliable cloud-edge synchronization, and modular hardware extensibility. Owing to its low cost and flexible scalability, the system is suitable for residential, research, and educational deployments. These results indicate that integrating on-device AI inference with lightweight communication protocols offers a practical route toward interoperable and user-centric intelligent spaces.
journal: 3rd International Conference on Electronic Materials and Information Engineering (EMIE 2023)

title: Research on lightweight modeling and incremental synchronization mechanism of state-aware digital twins
abstract: In view of the problems of complex modeling, synchronization redundancy, and poor real-time performance inherent in distributed scenarios such as smart cities and smart agriculture, a lightweight modeling method for digital twins based on multi-source IoT sensors is proposed, along with a well-designed three-layer lightweight architecture of " sensor compression—proxy modeling—incremental synchronization ". Improved PCA is used to achieve efficient transmission of time-series data, a parameterized proxy model replaces conventional high-complexity geometric modeling, and an incremental synchronization mechanism based on state differences significantly reduces synchronization overhead. The experimental results convincingly show that the method reduces model storage size by 62.7% and data synchronization latency by 47%. Since it has a compression ratio of 3% and keeps the state restoration accuracy above 97%, therefore it can be very reliably deployed on low-computing-power edge platforms, making it ideal for real-time decision-making applications in urban operation monitoring and plant growth sensing.
journal: 3rd International Conference on Electronic Materials and Information Engineering (EMIE 2023)

title: A prediction model for higher education learning behaviors based on deep learning
abstract: With the rapid advancement of deep learning technology, research on intelligent models centered on learning behavior prediction has become a key direction in higher education informatization. Addressing the challenges of complex and highly temporal student behavior patterns in university online learning environments, this study proposes a deep learning model tailored for predicting learning behaviors in higher education. The model employs multi-layer neural network technology to perform deep data mining learning through data preprocessing, feature extraction, model construction, and optimization training, thereby achieving precise identification and dynamic prediction of learning behaviors. This paper utilizes data from a university online learning platform, encompassing information such as assignment submissions, resource access, and interactive participation. Experimental results demonstrate that this learning behavior prediction model achieves higher prediction accuracy (93%), recall rate (91%), and F1 score (92%) compared to LSTM, while reducing training time by nearly 30.7%. This validates the model's effectiveness in feature fusion and parameter optimization. As an intelligent learning analytics solution, deep learning-based learning behavior prediction models can serve as an effective technical approach for university learning support systems and personalized teaching decision-making.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Cross-border E-commerce customer preference prediction based on transfer learning
abstract: Convolutional neural networks and transfer learning techniques are leveraged in this study to address the complex challenge of customer preference prediction within cross-border e-commerce environments. Traditional recommendation systems often struggle with the high heterogeneity of multi-lingual, multi-domain user data and the significant domain shifts typical in global markets. In this paper, we propose a deep learning framework based on attention-based feature alignment and adversarial domain adaptation to overcome these limitations. By using this approach, the model is able to learn semantically robust and transferable feature representations, which effectively bridges the gap between different regional markets. The experiments use a large multilingual dataset from eBay and Amazon, which includes a rigorous preprocessing procedure including Z-score normalization, language coordination, and outlier removal. The results show marked improvements in prediction accuracy, recall, and F1-score over established baselines, especially under conditions of pronounced domain and language disparity. Ablation studies demonstrate the important role of attention mechanism and adversarial components in promoting knowledge transfer and domain invariance. This study shows that the scalability, robustness and interpretability of the recommendation model of cross-border e-commerce platform can be greatly improved by using attention-driven neural architecture and advanced domain adaptation strategy.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Deep graph neural network for hidden link prediction on heterogeneous temporal graphs
abstract: The flow data between enterprise entities usually has the characteristics of complex structure, hidden association and significant timing change. Traditional methods have limited ability to describe multi-hop propagation relationships and weak ties patterns, and it is difficult to complete the identification of deep hidden association. To solve this problem, this paper abstracts multi-source stream data as heterogeneous temporal graph, and constructs a unified representation of node attributes, relationship edge features and temporal information. On this basis, a deep neural network analysis framework is introduced, high-order topological features are extracted by graph neural network, the dynamic evolution of association relationships is described by combining temporal state modeling, and the collaborative learning ability of structural information and temporal information is enhanced by a joint loss mechanism. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves better performance in accuracy, recall rate, F1 value and other indicators, and has strong recognition ability for implicit relationships in complex networks. The model also shows good engineering adaptability in terms of stability and computational efficiency.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Deep learning-driven mining and prediction model for blended learning behavior in lifelong education
abstract: Lifelong education increasingly relies on blended learning environments that combine online and offline modalities, generating rich multi-dimensional behavioral data. Accurately mining and predicting learning behaviors is critical for personalised intervention and dropout prevention. This paper proposes a CNN-BiLSTM-Attention hybrid deep learning model for mining temporal patterns in blended learning behaviors and predicting student outcomes. Convolutional neural networks extract local behavioral features from interaction logs, bidirectional long short-term memory networks capture long-range temporal dependencies, and a self-attention mechanism identifies the most predictive time steps. Experiments on the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD) demonstrate that the proposed model achieves 91.2% accuracy and 0.897 macro-F1 score, outperforming traditional machine learning baselines and single-architecture deep learning models. An ablation study confirms that each component contributes meaningfully to overall performance. The results suggest that hybrid deep learning architectures can effectively support learning analytics in lifelong education settings.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Analysis and prediction of carbon market fluctuations based on multi-factor attention deep learning
abstract: To address the challenges of high volatility and complex multi-factor interactions in carbon market price forecasting, this paper proposes a novel deep learning framework based on multi-factor attention mechanisms for comprehensive fluctuation analysis and accurate prediction. The proposed approach integrates heterogeneous factors—including economic indicators, energy commodity prices, and macro-level policy signals—and employs a dynamic attention mechanism to adaptively adjust the influence weights of each factor over time. This enables the model to precisely capture the dominant market drivers and their temporal evolution. Extensive experiments on large-scale historical datasets from China’s regional carbon markets and the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms traditional statistical models and mainstream deep learning baselines in terms of root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R²). Furthermore, attention-based feature analysis reveals the dynamic importance of different drivers under varying market conditions, providing scientific support for market design, risk management, and algorithmic trading. This study not only enhances the interpretability and robustness of carbon price fluctuation analysis and prediction, but also lays a solid methodological and data-driven foundation for climate policy evaluation and carbon finance innovation.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for rock mass blastability
abstract: A hierarchical sensor network combined with deep learning is utilized to predict rock mass blastability in large-scale mining environments. Tri-axial vibration and acoustic emission sensors, synchronized via GPS, collect high-frequency signals during blasting events. To extract robust features from the data, signal pre-processing uses adaptive normalization and principal component analysis. Deep long short-term memory (LSTM) networks are used to model the inherent nonlinear temporal dependencies in the blasting process. A comprehensive dataset containing more than 200 productionscale blasts was validated, which was divided into strict training, validation and testing. According to the quantitative evaluation, the LSTM model is consistently superior to the traditional regression and shallow learning methods under various geological conditions. This indicates that the LSTM model reduces the mean absolute error and root mean square error. According to the operation statistics and spatial energy distribution analysis, the implementation of the system can improve the blasting energy distribution and significantly reduce the dangerous flyrock events. The real-time edge-based deployment ensures strong fault tolerance and low-latency inference under field conditions. These findings support the practicality of combining sensor networks and advanced deep learning techniques for dynamic, data-driven blasting assessment in mine engineering.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Real-time urban traffic flow prediction and congestion cause analysis based on multimodal open-source data and deep learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of urban traffic flow and timely identification of congestion causes are essential for intelligent transportation systems. However, existing approaches typically rely on single-modality traffic data and fail to incorporate contextual factors such as weather conditions, special events, and road network topology. This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates open-source traffic speed and volume data, road network topology, weather records, and event information for real-time traffic flow prediction and congestion cause analysis. The framework employs a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to capture spatial dependencies among road segments, a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to model temporal traffic patterns, and a cross-attention fusion module to integrate heterogeneous contextual features. A multi-task learning head jointly predicts traffic flow values, congestion levels, and congestion causes. Experiments on the PeMS-BAY and METR-LA benchmark datasets augmented with weather and event metadata demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 14.6 and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 20.8 on PeMS-BAY, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines including GCN-LSTM (MAE 17.8) and standalone TCN (MAE 19.2). The congestion cause classification achieves 87.3% accuracy across five categories.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Reinforcement learning-based energy-efficient scheduling and performance prediction for cloud data centers
abstract: The growing energy footprint of cloud data centers makes power-aware resource scheduling an urgent concern. Conventional heuristic schedulers often fall short when confronted with fluctuating demands and heterogeneous server configurations. This paper proposes PPO-EES, a Proximal Policy Optimization-based Energy-Efficient Scheduling framework that jointly optimizes virtual machine placement, resource allocation, and workload migration. The framework incorporates a state observation module that captures real-time CPU utilization, memory consumption, and energy metrics, and an actor-critic architecture that learns scheduling policies maximizing energy efficiency while satisfying service-level agreements (SLAs). We further introduce an LSTM-based performance predictor to forecast server utilization and proactively adjust scheduling decisions. Experiments on the Google Cluster Trace and Azure VM Trace datasets demonstrate that PPO-EES reduces energy consumption by 18.3% compared to threshold-based methods and achieves a prediction R-squared of 0.943, outperforming DQN and A2C baselines.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Deep learning-based dynamic prediction of optical fiber transmission loss
abstract: Accurate dynamic prediction of optical fiber transmission loss is fundamental to proactive optical performance monitoring, capacity planning and elastic wavelength provisioning in dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) networks. Conventional analytical models capture only steady-state attenuation and react poorly to non-stationary disturbances such as ambient temperature swings, mechanical stress and gradual ageing of in-line components. This paper proposes a hybrid deep neural architecture that couples a one-dimensional convolutional feature extractor, a bidirectional long short-term memory temporal encoder and a multi-head self-attention fusion module to forecast fiber loss multiple hours ahead from heterogeneous monitoring telemetry. We evaluate the model on a 168-hour DWDM-link telemetry corpus that integrates launch power, OSNR, wavelength, span length, ambient temperature and link age. On a 12-hour prediction horizon, the proposed model attains a mean absolute error of 0.0023 dB/km and a coefficient of determination of 0.987, outperforming ARIMA, support vector regression, LSTM, GRU and a vanilla Transformer by 30 percent or more in MAE. Ablation experiments confirm that the convolutional front end and the attention fusion module contribute complementary gains.
journal: International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning (OIDL 2026)

title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
abstract: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice
abstract: A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe 2 /WSe 2 bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

title: Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error
abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun’s arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters ( Puffinus puffinus ) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars’ early crust and mantle
abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet’s geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars’ surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18 O, before ejection into space by an impact.

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF 2
abstract: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF 2 showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF 2 . This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum
abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs
abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas , the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS . However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter ( SOPT ) and S locus glycine-rich protein ( SGRP ), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: When AI takes away the thrill of discovery
abstract: “Pure math is being devastated or revolutionized, depending on your point of view.” So said Cornell professor Steven Strogatz after the artificial intelligence (AI) company OpenAI announced in early September a potential solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize problems that represent the highest goals for mathematical proofs. OpenAI’s solution involved unleashing an army of AI agents at a cost of millions of dollars in computing power, and it also certainly drew on decades of human effort in mathematics before it. Then a few weeks later, OpenAI posted 722 manuscripts describing progress on 372 mathematical problem families, and Google DeepMind published (in Science ) solutions from their own AI math system. These events are potentially exciting for those who long to know the answers to these problems as soon as possible, but they have also sent the world of mathematics reeling, and pose an even bigger question for all fields: Can the satisfaction of understanding ever replace the thrill of discovery?

title: TalkFlow: Structured Latent Flow Matching for Speech Driven Holistic Motion Generation
abstract: Holistic co-speech motion generation aims to synthesize coordinated facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements from speech, which is challenging due to heterogeneous part-specific dynamics, long-range temporal coherence, and cross-part coordination. Directly modeling high-dimensional motion can be unstable, while overly compact or unstructured latent spaces may lose fine-grained motion details. We present \textbf{TalkFlow}, a structured latent flow framework for speech-driven holistic motion generation. TalkFlow learns a continuous three-stream latent representation for upper-body motion, lower-body motion, and facial expressions, preserving part-specific dynamics without forcing heterogeneous motion components into a single latent space. To maintain holistic coordination, lightweight cross-stream interactions are incorporated in both latent representation learning and flow-based generation. Conditioned on multi-level speech features, TalkFlow performs speech-conditioned latent flow matching, learning a continuous transport process from source latents to realistic motion latents. Experiments on the BEAT2 dataset demonstrate strong performance across facial expression accuracy, body gesture quality, and speech-motion synchronization. Qualitative comparisons and user studies further show that TalkFlow generates more natural, expressive, and speech-aligned holistic motion than state-of-the-art methods. The project page is available at https://xinmuwang.github.io/TalkFlow/.

title: InferD: A Honeypot Framework for AI Inference Infrastructure
abstract: Large language model serving stacks, commercial inference APIs, vector databases, and agent orchestration gateways are now ex- posed on the public internet and indexed by commodity scanners within hours of deployment. The threat characteristics of this sur- face are only beginning to be measured, and the honeypot frame- works that could measure it were designed for conventional net- work services rather than for AI infrastructure. In fact, emulating an AI service is a distinct deception problem: the observable behavior of the service, including model inventories, token formats, tool-call protocols, and authorization flows, must be reproduced faithfully, while the underlying computation, model inference and tool ex- ecution, must never occur. We present InferD, a low-interaction honeypot framework organized around a single principle we call deception without inference: every request an adversary can observe is answered from static response pools, and nothing an adversary submits is ever executed. InferD decomposes the emulation into four deception planes, transport, service protocol, vulnerability surface, and agentic session, adds a provenance plane that links a planted credential to evidence of downstream model-mediated processing.

title: Adaptive Artificial Intelligence Models for Enhancing Digital Inclusion and Sustainable Development in Underserved Communities
abstract: Technology is playing a vital role across various sectors like education, healthcare, agriculture, financial services, employment, governance, and social development. However, we still see significant digital inequalities, especially in underserved communities, particularly in rural and low-income areas. Here, challenges such as limited connectivity, high technology costs, lack of digital skills, language barriers, and inaccessible digital services hinder meaningful participation in the digital economy. This conceptual paper delves into how adaptive Artificial Intelligence (AI) models can boost digital inclusion and support sustainable development in these communities. It brings together insights from literature on artificial intelligence, digital inclusion, adaptive learning, responsible AI, and sustainable development. The paper introduces the Adaptive AI Digital Inclusion and Sustainable Development (AIDISD) framework, which is built around five key dimensions: accessibility, personalization, contextual adaptation, resource efficiency, and community empowerment. It explores potential applications in education, healthcare, agriculture, financial inclusion, employment, and public services. Additionally, the paper highlights challenges related to infrastructure, data scarcity, algorithmic bias, privacy, cybersecurity, affordability, digital literacy, and institutional capacity. The analysis emphasizes that adaptive AI should be viewed as part of a larger socio-technical strategy rather than just a standalone tech solution. For inclusive deployment, we need local participation, suitable infrastructure, responsible data governance, human oversight, and ongoing evaluation. Ultimately, the paper concludes that well-designed adaptive AI systems can foster more inclusive and sustainable digital ecosystems, provided they are affordable, locally relevant, accessible, transparent, and aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Machine Learning in the Differential Diagnosis of Bipolar and Borderline Personality Disorders: A Scoping Review.
abstract: BackgroundBipolar disorder (BD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) are associated with substantial morbidity and can be difficult to distinguish when symptoms are assessed cross-sectionally. This scoping review examines machine learning (ML) and related predictive approaches designed to differentiate the two conditions.MethodsWe searched Ovid MEDLINE, APA PsycInfo, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and selected computer science conference proceedings through July 2, 2026. Full-text peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers were eligible when they used a data-driven computational or statistical prediction approach to distinguish, classify, or characterize BD and BPD. Of 2,594 records identified, 2,523 unique records were screened, and 24 full texts were assessed. Screening followed the Population, Concept, Context framework, Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, and preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses extension for scoping reviews.ResultsNine reports met the inclusion criteria. Seven participant-based reports contributed an aggregate of 986 report-level participants, although two reports used overlapping cohorts; one conference paper used synthetic data, and one study analyzed 149,798 Reddit posts. Studies including clinical samples reported BD versus BPD discrimination AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) values of 0.67 to 0.91 and accuracies ranging from 61.7% to 90%. These estimates were not directly comparable and were derived from small, often imbalanced samples using heterogeneous internal validation. No model was externally validated in an independent clinical cohort.ConclusionThe evidence remains preliminary and does not support clinical deployment. Reported performance is constrained by small samples, class imbalance, uncertain ground-truth labels, spectrum bias, and reliance on pre-existing diagnoses. Prospective studies in consecutive at-risk cohorts, with transparent reporting and independent external validation, are required.

title: Collagen I-rich microenvironments influence cholangiocyte specification and tubulogenesis in stem cell-derived models of liver development.
abstract: Cholangiocyte dysfunction accounts for a substantial proportion of liver transplantations, yet progress towards regenerative therapies is limited by an incomplete understanding of the developmental cues that regulate human cholangiocyte specification and morphogenesis. Here, we established a defined culture system to investigate how collagen I influences hepatobiliary differentiation from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). Increased collagen I presentation was associated with a bias towards cholangiocyte specification, reduced hepatocyte identity and the formation of branched duct-like tubular structures. Similar effects were observed in primary human foetal hepatoblast organoids, indicating that collagen I-dependent lineage bias is conserved across independent model systems. Mechanistically, collagen I presentation was associated with activation of integrin α2β1- and YAP-associated signalling, while inhibition of collagen-integrin interactions impaired both cholangiocyte specification and tubulogenesis. Together, our findings support a role for collagen I-rich extracellular environments in human hepatobiliary differentiation and provide a defined experimental system for investigating extracellular matrix-dependent mechanisms of bile duct development in vitro.

title: Digital Transformation in Agri-Food Supply Chains for Adaptive Sustainable Growth among Latin American Firms: A Systematic Review, 2018–2025
abstract: Background Digital transformation is reshaping agri-food supply chains through technologies designed to improve efficiency, traceability, sustainability, and resilience. However, the evidence remains fragmented, and Latin America continues to be underrepresented. Methods A systematic review complemented by bibliometric analysis was conducted using Scopus and Web of Science in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The search identified 2,553 records; after filtering, duplicate removal, and eligibility assessment, 85 studies were included in the systematic synthesis. Data were analyzed using Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and Microsoft Excel. Results Scientific output increased steadily, particularly after 2021. Blockchain, the Internet of Things, big data, artificial intelligence, and precision agriculture were the most frequently studied technologies. The findings showed improvements in traceability, operational efficiency, resource management, resilience, and organizational capabilities. Nevertheless, persistent barriers included inadequate infrastructure, limited financing, poor interoperability, and gaps in digital skills. Latin America accounted for only a small share of the scientific literature. Conclusions Digital transformation can support the sustainable growth of agri-food firms when it is integrated with organizational capabilities, data governance, stakeholder collaboration, and inclusive technology policies. Further empirical evidence from Latin America is needed, together with models tailored to the characteristics of its firms and territories.

title: Stock-level volatility forecasting using machine learning: A comparative study of GARCH, Random Forest, LSTM, and GRU on US Equities
abstract: Forecasting stock price volatility at the individual stock level is a major challenge in managing financial risks; it has widespread implications for portfolio strategies, pricing derivatives, and assessing regulatory capital adequacy. Although there have been a number of studies using market indices (e.g., VIX and associated methods) to study forecasting stock market volatility, relatively few studies have applied and evaluated a number of different types of machine learning methods to individual stock data in terms of actual (realised) volatility forecasting. This study fills that gap by presenting a comprehensive analysis of the relationship between stock price volatility and various machine learning techniques on a sample of ten well-known US stocks (across three sectors: technology, finance, and energy) based on data from January 2018 to December 2024 (1,759 trading days). We apply five modelling approaches: a classical GARCH(1,1) econometric model, a classical GJR-GARCH(1,1,1) econometric model, a Random Forest regressor, a two-layer Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, and a two-layer Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) network. For each of the four modelling techniques, we use a rolling 5-day annualised actual (realised) volatility forecast as our final outcomes. Evaluation of the prediction results of each of these models was measured using RMSE, MAE, QLIKE loss, parametric Value-at-Risk (VaR) measures, Expected Shortfall (ES), and the Kupiec backtest. We also performed an analysis of the prevailing market regime through K-Means clustering, created an ablation study using variables as features in the models to assess the importance of those variables, and developed a computational efficiency benchmark for each model. In terms of predicted errors, Random Forest was proven to yield very low predicted error (mean RMSE = 0.0892) in comparison to deep learning methods, plus Random Forest was able to be trained approximately 7 times faster than deep learning methods. GRU was ranked second and outperformed LSTM on most of the metrics used in this evaluation. GARCH models remain a viable option for estimating risk measures and calibrating VaR, especially during period of stability in the financial markets.

title: The Role of Extension Workers and Farmers' Perceptions in Digitizing Rubber Marketing in Kuantan Singingi District, Indonesia
abstract: Due to Covid-19 restrictions on physical interaction, the marketing digitization system has grown rapidly and become popular on social media. Indonesia’s agricultural sector, which includes rubber as a mainstay commodity besides palm oil, has also been affected by this trend. Indonesia is the world’s leading rubber area, covering 3,826,191 ha, with Riau province alone accounting for 334,610 ha. Kuantan Singingi Regency has the largest rubber area in Riau, covering 29,617.32 ha, and the highest rubber prices in the district. This study aims to examine the role of extension workers in digitalizing rubber marketing and farmers’ perceptions of marketing digitalization. The survey was conducted in three sub-districts with the largest rubber plantation areas, and a sample of 80 people was taken by Proportional Random Sampling. The data were analyzed using the Likert Scale. The study found that extension workers play an important role in carrying out their duties and that farmers have a positive perception of digitalization in rubber marketing.

title: Application of the Concept of Best Efforts and Result Achievement for the Classification of Medical Obligations in the Sphere of Transplantation
abstract: The article examines the legal nature of organ and tissue transplantation relations in the Russian Federation through the prism of the French concept of dividing obligations into obligations to apply efforts (“obligation de moyens”) and achieving results (“obligation de resultat”), adopted by Russian law enforcement practice in distinguishing between contracts for work and service contracts. It is noted that organ and tissue transplantation is an obligation to apply efforts due to an objectively high therapeutic risk and is exhausted by the traditional design of the contract for the provision of paid services. Activities relating to the removal, storage, conservation and transportation of organs and tissues tend towards the model of commitment to achieve results, as a result of which they are a mixed contract with elements of contract and paid services. The proposed differentiated approach makes it possible to balance the limits of civil liability of medical organizations.

title: Fintech Integration in Microfinance: Opportunities and Risks for Small Businesses
abstract: The integration of financial technology (fintech) into microfinance has significantly transformed the delivery of financial services to underserved populations, particularly micro and small enterprises. This paper examines the role of fintech-enabled models of microfinance in promoting financial access, enterprise activity, and risk. The study follows a quantitative and analytical approach based on the secondary data of a microfinance platform based on fintech (Kiva) to explore the patterns of loan distributions, the characteristics of borrowers, and the engagement of the sector. The results show that the fintech integration promotes the financial inclusion by increasing access to credit, particularly among women and borrowers in developing areas. Loans are mainly concentrated in the sectors of agriculture, retail and service and this indicates a high concentration on the livelihood based and informal economic activities. Although digital platforms enhance outreach, efficiency, and global connectivity of capital, the findings also show that most loans are small, which restricts the possibility of a major business growth. Secondly, the paper lists some of the risks of fintech-enabled microfinance, such as inadequate credit assessment tools, possible difficulties with repayment, and dependence on digital infrastructure. These aspects draw up issues of sustainability and long-term effects. Overall, the study finds that the integration of fintech enhances microfinance by making it more accessible and inclusive, although the effects of its development are limited due to structural constraints. The results underscore the necessity of a balanced measure that involves integrating technological innovation with institutional resource and policy frameworks to make sustainable development of enterprises.
journal: Computer and Decision Making: An International Journal

title: PrivateAgent: Mobility-Aware AI Agents for Safe Private Networks
abstract: Private cellular networks increasingly support video analytics, connected workers, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and other industrial applications whose mobility and control deadlines vary widely. A single artificial-intelligence (AI) agent cannot safely manage all of these loops because perception, planning, networking, and governance operate at different time scales and execution locations. This paper presents PrivateAgent, a mobility-aware framework that classifies private-network applications as stationary, low-mobility, or high-mobility and maps their functions across device, site-edge, and cloud tiers. Hard real-time perception and actuation remain local; near-real-time planning and network optimization run at the edge; long-horizon learning runs in the cloud. Network-changing actions are represented as typed artifacts with explicit evidence, scope, authority, monitoring, and rollback requirements before execution. We detail representative use cases including perimeter video, machine vision, connected workers, forklifts, AMRs, and drones, and specify suitable agent families, latency targets, failure modes, and benchmark dimensions. We also instantiate the action-admission boundary with SafeFlow-Real50, a 50-scenario benchmark derived from four anonymized private-network traces. In a blind evaluation, the model selected the correct act/clarify/reject mode in 50/50 scenarios, an acceptable action in 45/50, and the preferred action in 43/50. The deterministic gateway detected all 400 injected corruptions versus 150 for schema-only validation. These results show that mobility should determine the real-time agent boundary, while independent validation should determine whether generated network actions may advance toward execution.

title: Predicting Seasonal Activity of Blunt-nosed Leafhoppers Using Degree-day Models in Cranberry
abstract: Accurate prediction of pest and crop phenology is essential for optimizing integrated pest management (IPM) in cranberry production systems. Degree-day models are widely used to forecast insect development and crop phenology; however, few have been developed for cranberry insect pests. We developed and validated degree-day–based models for the blunt-nosed leafhopper, Limotettix vaccinii (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae), in relation to cranberry bloom phenology in New Jersey, USA. Multiyear field data collected from commercial cranberry beds between 2022 and 2024 were used to develop and optimize the models, whereas independent datasets collected from 289 beds over a 5-year period (2021–25) were used for validation. Phenological progression of both pest and crop was modeled using logistic functions driven by growing degree-day (GDDpest and GDDcrop, respectively), with optimized base temperatures and biofix dates. The optimal L. vaccinii model used a base temperature of 10 °C and a biofix corresponding to floodwater drawdown [day of year (DOY) 112], whereas the cranberry bloom model converged on a base temperature of 4.44 °C and a DOY 94 biofix. Developmental trajectories showed consistent biological patterns, with nymphal activity preceding bloom and adult emergence overlapping the later stages of bloom. Model integration revealed that 10% bloom occurred, on average, at 716 GDDcrop (DOY 160), by which time ∼70% of nymphal development had already been completed. Based on these dynamics, the optimal insecticide application window was identified between 195 GDDpest (DOY 144; 25% nymphal progression) and peak nymph abundance at 266 GDDpest (DOY 153; 50% progression), maximizing nymph suppression while minimizing pollinator exposure. These results demonstrate that empirically optimized degree-day models can effectively synchronize L. vaccinii management with cranberry crop phenology. This framework provides a practical decision support tool for cranberry IPM and highlights the importance of regional calibration of phenology models to local climatic conditions and management practices.

title: Mathematical Modeling and Simulation of Eimeria spp. Transmission Dynamics Between Poultry Manure and Vegetable Crops in Integrated Farming Systems
Forecasting financial support for government institutions using artificial intelligence: The case study of museums
abstract: Subject. Forecasting the financial support of public institutions based on regional panel data of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Objectives. To develop and test a methodology for forecasting the financial support of museums using artificial intelligence methods. Methods. A panel dataset of 85 constituent entities of the Russian Federation for 2018–2024 was compiled. Machine learning methods were applied, including gradient boosting, regularized linear models, and their ensembles. Hyperparameter tuning was carried out using an artificial intelligence agent (AI agent) based on the Qwen3.5‑27B language model. Thirty‑two computational experiments were conducted. Forecast accuracy was assessed using the median absolute percentage error (MdAPE); rolling validation was applied over four test years (2021–2024). Results. The gradient boosting model achieves an MdAPE of 8.1% across regions, outperforming the best naive forecast by 1.9 percentage points and the previous‑year forecast by 4.6 percentage points. The average MdAPE under rolling validation was 12%. For 64% of the regions, the forecast error does not exceed 15%. Infrastructure‑related characteristics of institutions (28.6%) and personnel‑related characteristics (22%) demonstrate the highest predictive power. A systematic tendency to underestimate forecasts for large regions was identified; this is driven by discretionary budgetary decisions that cannot be predicted based on operational indicators. Conclusions and Relevance. Artificial intelligence methods demonstrate an advantage over traditional econometric approaches in the context of nonlinear relationships and interregional heterogeneity. The proposed methodology is applicable to forecasting financial indicators of public institutions in other sectors, provided that similar operational data at the regional level are available. The results can be used by public authorities in budget expenditure planning and in preliminary assessments of expected levels of financial support.

title: Accounting and control support for settlements with certain categories of employees: Issues and solutions
abstract: Subject. This article addresses theoretical and practical aspects of accounting for and internal control over settlements with personnel in agricultural organizations operating under seasonal production conditions. Objectives. Based on assessing the current state of accounting practice and designing innovative forms of internal reporting, as well as identifying the specific features of managing settlements with seasonal personnel, the article aims to develop scientifically grounded recommendations for improving the accounting and control framework for settlements with seasonal workers. Methods. For the study, we used the general scientific methods, statistical analysis, and digital modeling. Results. The article proposes and substantiates areas for improving the accounting and control framework for settlements with seasonal workers involving the implementation of an integrated digital profile of a seasonal worker and an operational register of seasonal operations, which enables real-time monitoring of performance against planned targets and supports timely managerial decision-making. Conclusions and Relevance. The digital transformation of accounting through the implementation of an employee's digital profile and an operational register of seasonal works incorporating predictive analytics ensures end-to-end traceability of labor input and the timely detection of deviations from planned targets. The proposed approach contributes to greater reliability of accounting data, more effective internal control and the mitigation of tax and labor risks. The proposed internal reporting forms and digital tools are designed for agricultural organizations characterized by pronounced production seasonality. Accounting and economic departments may apply these solutions to enhance the reliability of accounting for settlements with personnel, strengthen internal control and mitigate the risks of non-compliance with labor and tax legislation. The findings are also applicable to organizations in other industries.

title: Geoclimatic changes, industry structure and external energy dependence as factors of economic dynamics
abstract: Subject. The impact of geoclimatic shifts – temperature anomalies and extreme hydrometeorological events – on the economic development of national economies. Objectives. Construction and econometric verification of a panel model that makes it possible to assess the direction and impact of geoclimatic factors on the logarithm of per capita GDP for a sample of 54 countries for 2000–2024. Methods. The study is based on a synthesis of theoretical analysis of the climate-economic literature and an empirical assessment using panel data. Results. An increase in the average annual temperature by 1°C relative to the climatic norm of 1961–1990 reduces per capita GDP by an average of 1.8%, and each additional extreme event (drought, flood, storm) – by 2.6%. The share of agriculture in GDP and energy dependence significantly increase climate vulnerability, while increased grain yields and trade openness act as compensating mechanisms. The model explains 80.7% of the intra-country variation in per capita GDP. Conclusions. Taking into account the combined effects of temperature anomalies, extreme events, and structural characteristics of the economy allows for more accurate estimates of climate damage compared to traditional approaches that consider these factors in isolation. The high share of agriculture and energy dependence create a "structural trap" that increases vulnerability, while technological modernization of the agricultural sector and diversification of foreign trade can partially compensate for losses. The results obtained substantiate the need to integrate climate risks into macroeconomic forecasting and budget planning.

title: Digital maturity of agroecosystems in the global economy: Theoretical and methodological approach to assessment and forecasting
abstract: Subject. This article focuses on the digital ecosystems of the agro-industrial complex of different countries. Objectives. The study aims to develop a theoretical and methodological approach to assessing the maturity of digital agroecosystems in the global economy and to identify the conditions for the transition from fragmented digitalization to a sustainable digital agro-industrial ecosystem. Methods. For the study, we used methods of content analysis, comparative and institutional analyses, systematization of scientific literature and regulatory methods, expert grouping of indicators. Results. The article proposes a stage-based model of digital agroecosystem formation in different countries. It also substantiates the need for a comprehensive methodology to assess the depth of digital ecosystems, and identifies the main barriers to the transition from fragmented digitalization to an ecosystem. Conclusions. The choice of financial and credit mechanisms for small and medium-sized agricultural producers in global and Russian practice will depend on the level of digital agroecosystems maturity. The research results can support the development of agricultural digitalization roadmaps, digital ecosystem architecture design, and the analysis of digitalization projects by maturity level.

title: The role of digitalization in creating agro-industrial clusters: Regional aspects and economic efficiency
abstract: Subject. Economic efficiency of agriculture, development of digitalization processes in the economy at the regional level. Objectives. Assessment of the economic effects of implementing digital technologies in agricultural enterprises. Methods. Systematic, comparative analysis. Results. Digital platforms and modeling tools make it possible to optimize the process of creating agro-industrial clusters. By using digital tools, costs for fertilizers, fuel, and other components are reduced. However, the level of digital maturity in Russian agro-industrial companies is still low. Conclusions. An important task for Russia is creating a unified state policy aimed at actively developing the agro-industrial complex in the regions.

title: Conceptual aspects of strategic planning of a large metallurgical company
abstract: Subject. The conceptual foundations of strategic planning of large metallurgical companies and the possibilities of their practical application in modern conditions of industry development. Objectives. Development of conceptual provisions for strategic planning of large metallurgical companies based on the differentiation of the concepts of strategic planning and strategic management, the formation of an adaptive cyclical model for the preparation, implementation and adjustment of strategic decisions, as well as an assessment of its practical applicability. Methods. The research is based on systematic and comparative approaches, methods of analysis, synthesis and generalization, as well as a comparative analysis of industry statistics and corporate strategies of the largest metallurgical companies. Results. A conceptual model of strategic planning of a large metallurgical company has been developed based on the cyclical interaction of the stages of diagnosis, goal setting, implementation, adaptation and strategic monitoring. The proposed model provides continuous feedback and the ability to adjust strategic decisions based on changes in the external and internal environment. Conclusions. An analysis of the industry dynamics and strategies of the largest Russian metallurgical companies has confirmed the relevance of an adaptive approach to strategic planning and the need to integrate its key elements into a single system.

title: Digital Transformation of Agricultural Libraries for Supporting Smart Agriculture: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Digital transformation has created new opportunities for agricultural libraries to support smart agriculture through improved access to digital resources, information dissemination, and technology-enabled services. The present study examines the opportunities, challenges, and factors influencing digital transformation in agricultural libraries in Nagpur City. A quantitative and descriptive research design was adopted, and data were collected from 44 agricultural library professionals using purposive sampling through a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Cronbach’s Alpha, and multiple linear regression were applied. The factor analysis identified seven factors explaining 74.377% of the total variance, with reliability coefficients ranging from 0.856 to 0.919. Regression analysis showed that the identified factors did not significantly predict technology adoption (R² = 0.064; F(7,36) = 0.355; p = 0.922). Therefore, the null hypothesis was not rejected, indicating no statistically significant influence of the identified factors on technology adoption in the present sample. The findings highlight the need for stronger financial and institutional support, improved digital infrastructure, staff training, and user-oriented digital services to strengthen agricultural libraries for smart agriculture.

title: ТЕОРЕТИКО-МЕТОДОЛОГІЧНІ ЗАСАДИ УПРАВЛІННЯ ФІНАНСОВО-ЕКОНОМІЧНИМ ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННЯМ РОЗВИТКУ МАТЕРІАЛЬНО-ТЕХНІЧНОЇ БАЗИ АГРАРНИХ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ
abstract: The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of managing the financial and economic support for the development of the material and technical base of agricultural enterprises under current macroeconomic challenges, instability, and martial law. The strategic importance of the material and technical base for ensuring the efficiency of production and economic activities, the competitiveness of agricultural enterprises, and the sustainable development of rural areas is substantiated. The specific features of the formation and reproduction of the material and technical base are revealed, taking into account the seasonality of production, dependence on natural and climatic conditions, the territorial dispersion of resources, the need for maintenance services, and the impact of scientific and technological progress. The main sources of financial and economic support for its development are systematized, and the need for their diversification is substantiated. Conceptual principles for managing the development of the material and technical base are proposed, including innovative modernization, digitalization of production processes, resource conservation, development of processing capacities, optimization of logistics flows, improvement of maintenance services, and strengthening the role of the intellectual and human-resource component. Strategic, tactical, and operational objectives of managing the financial and economic support of the material and technical base of agricultural enterprises are identified. Criteria for the effectiveness of such management are substantiated, including the completeness of financial support, timeliness of decision-making, balance of funding sources, economic justification of expenditures, resource conservation, adaptability, transparency, and flexibility of the management system.
journal: Herald of Khmelnytskyi National University. Economic sciences

title: ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЯ УПРАВЛІННЯ ВИРОБНИЧИМИ ПРОЦЕСАМИ СІЛЬСЬКОГОСПОДАРСЬКИХ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ В УМОВАХ СУЧАСНИХ ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЙ
abstract: The article analyzes the relevance and essence of digitalizing production process management in agricultural enterprises, that is a topic of particular importance in the current business environment, especially taking into consideration martial law. It notes that the evolution and development of agricultural technologies necessitate managerial transformations, with digitalization serving as a key tool in this process. The article outlines the primary tools and capabilities associated with digitalizing the management of agricultural enterprises, citing examples such as cloud technologies, artificial intelligence, analytics platforms, the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain technology, precision farming systems, and digital accounting systems. Special attention is paid to blockchain technology, which is currently gaining traction and enhancing corporate transparency and efficiency by enabling process monitoring, data collection, execution of smart contracts, and fraud prevention. Blockchain technology plays a vital role in providing the information necessary for enterprise operations – a factor that is currently crucial for the effective management of modern agricultural businesses under the conditions of uncertainty and transformation. The study concludes that digitalizing production process management offers significant advantages to Ukrainian agricultural enterprises, bolstering their resilience and competitiveness. These benefits are realized through faster managerial decision-making supported by analytics tools and software, more efficient resource allocation in production, and the use of systems for monitoring and tracking logistics processes. All of this contributes to increased efficiency and labor productivity, improved product quality, responsiveness to changes in consumer demand and preferences, the mitigation of climate change, and the addressing of other threats. Thus, the digitalization of management processes in agricultural enterprises has a significant, positive, long-term impact on the operations of domestic agricultural businesses.

title: ІННОВАЦІЙНО-ТЕХНОЛОГІЧНА ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ АГРАРНИХ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ УКРАЇНИ: ВІД ВОЄННОЇ АДАПТАЦІЇ ДО ЦИФРОВІЗАЦІЇ ТА ТОЧНОГО ЗЕМЛЕРОБСТВА
abstract: The article presents a comprehensive theoretical and empirical diagnosis of the current state, dynamics, and structure of innovative activity among Ukrainian agricultural enterprises amidst geopolitical, macroeconomic, and war-induced shocks. It is evident that innovation adoption has shifted from a tool for maximizing profits to a fundamental prerequisite for operational survival and long-term business resilience. The study examines Ukraine's positions in global innovation benchmarks (European Innovation Scoreboard, Global Innovation Index). It analyzes the financial structure of R&D expenditures, revealing an over-reliance on internal firm funds against the backdrop of stagnant R&D intensity below 0.38% of GDP. The catastrophic damage to the sector's capital stock is estimated at over $12.1 billion in direct agricultural losses and the destruction of over 130,000 machinery units. The structural aging of the machinery fleet is detailed—with 42–67% of combine harvesters and tractors exceeding 12 years of age—leading to disproportionate repair costs and a 20–28% drop in seasonal operational output. The study categorizes digital technology adoption across four maturity levels (RTK satellite navigation, NDVI satellite monitoring, Variable Rate Technology (VRT), and Farm Management Information Systems (FMIS)). The economic returns of drone-based land auditing and resource optimization are quantified, highlighting the prevalence of "patchwork digitalization." Key operational bottlenecks include declining EBITDA, GPS suppression via Electronic Warfare (EW), field contamination from unexploded ordnance, and severe shortages of skilled human capital. Finally, institutional and economic policy recommendations are formulated: promoting the Precision Agriculture as a Service (PAaaS) model, reorienting the "5-7-9%" preferential credit scheme toward technological modernization, unifying digital registries via open APIs, and establishing public-private educational-innovation clusters.

title: ІНТЕГРАЦІЙНІ МЕХАНІЗМИ УПРАВЛІННЯ «ЗЕЛЕНОЮ» КОНКУРЕНТОСПРОМОЖНІСТЮ В СИСТЕМІ НАЦІОНАЛЬНОЇ ЕКОНОМІЧНОЇ ПОЛІТИКИ УКРАЇНИ
abstract: This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for developing and integrating mechanisms to manage "green" competitiveness amidst the transformation of Ukraine’s national economic policy. Given contemporary global challenges and the country’s European integration objectives, the article argues that traditional approaches to securing competitive advantages require a synergistic combination of fundamental instruments. The author proposes an architecture for how institutional, organizational-managerial, economic, and innovation-technological mechanisms interact, with an information-digital framework serving as an overarching "superstructure" to ensure transparency, monitoring, and adaptable management decisions. Ukraine's key strategic priorities for economic policy are systematized in the context of the transition toward a climate-neutral economy, circularity, and the "greening" of the agricultural sector. A hierarchical system of integration principles is proposed—ranging from the foundational alignment of goals to the achievement of an overall synergistic effect. Particular attention is paid to the need to align national regulatory norms with European standards, particularly the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). The text emphasizes the importance of decentralizing environmental initiatives and engaging regional stakeholders in implementing climate projects. The availability of critical raw materials, combined with a post-war reconstruction approach of "building back better," provides a strong foundation for integrating Ukrainian industry into European value chains. Furthermore, the success of environmental transformations depends directly on developing human capital, upskilling the workforce, and increasing investment in clean technologies (clean-tech). These factors provide a solid basis for the national economy's long-term competitiveness in the global market. The authors conclude that comprehensive implementation of the proposed concept will not only ensure effective economic growth but also guarantee a high level of environmental security and sustainable development for the nation in the future.
