Migrant Labor and Regional Economic Performance: Spatial Associations by Skill Level and Industrial Structure
abstract: This study investigates how skill-specific migrant labor is associated with regional economic performance, with a focus on industrial structure and spatial interdependence. Using a balanced panel of 16 metropolitan cities and provinces in Korea over the period 2012–2023, we estimate spatial panel models and adopt the Spatial Durbin Model as the main specification because the diagnostics indicate spatial dependence and the research question requires decomposition into direct, indirect, and total effects. The results indicate that a higher share of low-skilled migrant labor is positively associated with regional GRDP per capita, both within regions and through indirect spatial associations across neighboring regions. In contrast, the association for high-skilled migrant labor is more contingent on regional production structures. Although the baseline estimates suggest a negative average association, this relationship varies systematically by industrial composition. The association becomes more favorable in manufacturing-oriented regions, although this manufacturing-related pattern is less robust to the inclusion of additional native labor-market controls. In service-oriented regions, the within-region association is less favorable, but positive indirect associations make the overall spatial-system association more favorable. Taken together, the findings show that the economic role of migrant labor is shaped by both industrial heterogeneity and spatial interconnectedness. These findings imply that migrant labor policy should be spatially and industrially differentiated, with attention to skill-specific matching and cross-regional indirect spatial associations rather than uniform national allocation.

title: Nanoformulations of Asiatic Acid and Asiatic Acid-enriched Fraction of Centella asiatica Preserve Mitochondrial and Dopaminergic Integrity in Cellular and MPTP-induced Mouse Models of Parkinson’s Disease

Landscape connectivity and climatic drivers shaping Noctuidae communities in a Brazilian seasonally dryland fruit-producing region
abstract: Drylands are highly sensitive to climatic shifts, affecting insect population dynamics and multi-trophic interactions. This study evaluated Noctuidae diversity and temporal distribution in the São Francisco Valley, a semi-arid, irrigated, fruit-producing region in Northeast Brazil, in relation to local environmental factors. We conducted monitoring over two consecutive years using Pennsylvania light traps deployed across two agricultural landscapes integrated with native Caatinga dry forest: an experimental multi-crop station and a commercial table grape farm. We captured 12,407 Noctuidae moths; raw richness favored the grapevine site, but diversity did not differ, and per-individual richness favored the multi-crop site once sampling effort was considered. Four Noctuinae species dominated the assemblage (94.04% of total captures): Spodoptera frugiperda (Smith) (39.53%), Elaphria agrotina (Guenée) (36.89%), Spodoptera cosmioides (Walker) (9.21%), and Spodoptera albula (Walker) (8.40%). Immediate captures of S. frugiperda and S. albula rose with lower wind speed and higher precipitation; previous-month captures showed the same patterns for S. frugiperda and S. albula, but E. agrotina responded to temperature and S. cosmioides to site and precipitation instead. Circular statistics indicated a stark temporal segregation between S. frugiperda and S. cosmioides. These findings suggest Caatinga connectivity elevates vineyard abundance, whereas the multi-crop mosaic’s heterogeneity yields higher per-individual richness. Specialized crop management practices, such as continuous vineyard pruning, generate stable niches that favor detritivorous species like E. agrotina. Local multi-year calibrations are essential for accurate pest forecasting and integrated management across agricultural-forest interfaces in semi-arid zones.

title: SPEI-based drought forecasting using decomposition-coupled LSTM models: a case study of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea
Prioritizing Circular Supply Chain Strategies in Construction: A Hybrid Delphi–AHP–DEMATEL–TOPSIS Framework
abstract: The construction industry is a major contributor to economic development in the United Arab Emirates (UAE); however, it simultaneously places considerable pressure on natural resources, energy systems, and construction and demolition waste management infrastructure. Despite national sustainability initiatives such as the Circular Economy Policy 2031 and Net Zero 2050, the implementation of circular supply chain (CSC) practices within the UAE construction sector remains fragmented and operationally inconsistent. Existing studies provide limited empirically grounded and context-specific decision-support approaches capable of prioritizing circular strategies while accounting for multidimensional sustainability trade-offs and interdependencies among influencing factors. To address this gap, this study develops and validates an integrated multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework for evaluating and prioritizing CSC strategies in the UAE construction sector. The framework integrates Delphi, Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), and Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Delphi established expert consensus on evaluation dimensions, AHP quantified hierarchical importance, DEMATEL identified causal relationships among sustainability criteria, and TOPSIS prioritized alternative CSC strategies. Expanded robustness and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to evaluate ranking stability under multiple weighting and alternative-removal scenarios. The findings indicate that environmental criteria received the highest hierarchical importance, while DEMATEL identified environmental and technological dimensions as dominant causal drivers within the CSC system. At the strategy level, Modular Prefabrication and Off-site Manufacturing (A2) emerged as the most preferred strategy with the highest TOPSIS closeness coefficient (CC = 0.841649), followed by BIM/IoT-enabled Material Traceability (A4) (CC = 0.581554), Construction and Demolition (C&D) Waste Recycling (A1) (CC = 0.36718), Green Procurement and Local Sourcing (A3) (CC = 0.349074) and Reverse Logistics and Take-back Systems (A5) (CC = 0.213104). Expanded sensitivity and alternative-removal analyses further demonstrated that the prioritization of A2 and A4 remained stable across multiple perturbation scenarios, confirming the robustness of the proposed decision-making framework. The study also fulfills its theoretical contribution by empirically differentiating between importance and causality-based appraisals in circular supply chain decision-making and by showing the usefulness of thoroughly integrated hybrid MCDM models in sparse and scarce data situations. In practice, the findings can be inferred to actionable recommendations for construction companies, supply chain management, and policy makers to align high-leverage circular drivers with strategic investments. Altogether, the suggested framework will provide a clear, high-quality, and context-sensitive decision-support tool to speed up the circular supply chain change in the UAE construction industry and similar emerging economies.

title: Explainable multi-agent AI systems for intelligent software engineering and business automation
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) are revolutionizing software programming and enterprise business automation in the 4th industrial revolution era. Current multi-agent systems, however, are constrained in being able to collaborate, in understanding how to reach consensus, in their knowledge sharing and, in their ability, to adapt to changes and therefore are not suitable for certain industrial critical applications. To address the above challenges, this paper introduces a cognitive swarm-based multi-agent framework with collaborative reasoning, collective cognitive memory, explainable decision intelligence, digital twin simulation and autonomous governance, which are integrated into an explainable cognitive swarm control framework XCognitive SwarmNet. Proposed framework mathematically models agent collaboration, trust, explainability, Knowledge sharing and Optimization of the flow of business tasks to support the complete Software Development Lifecycle and Intelligent Business process Automation. By using the powerful and representative software engineering and business process datasets, some experimental assessments are performed and the proposed mechanism is compared to six state-of-the-art multi-agent approaches. The proposed framework completes the task with 98.1% accuracy, reduces resource consumption by 22.8% relative to the selected baseline/reference configuration, achieves 97.5% in explainability fidelity, optimizes the workflow by 95.9% and optimizes the efficiency of agent collaboration by 94.7% with a 27.4% reduction in execution time. Overall, the results indicate that XCognitive SwarmNet provides a promising framework for transparent, adaptive, and trustworthy AI-assisted software engineering and business automation, while further industrial validation is required before claims of deployment in safety-critical or operational Industry 4.0 environments can be established.

title: Monitoring enabled livestock decarbonization through MRV digital technologies and governance in sustainable production systems
abstract: Livestock production systems are vital to global food security, rural livelihoods, and agricultural economies, yet they remain a major source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly methane (CH₄), nitrous oxide (N₂O), and carbon dioxide (CO₂). Although significant progress has been made in developing mitigation strategies, measurement tools, and monitoring technologies, the widespread adoption of climate-smart approaches within sustainable production systems is constrained by persistent and interconnected barriers. This review critically synthesizes these constraints, emphasizing the role of monitoring and sensing technologies in enabling mitigation and sustainable livestock production, and categorizing constraints across four domains: technical, economic, data-management, and socio-political. Technical limitations include uncertainties in emission factors, sensor accuracy, and the integration of advanced tools into farm operations. Economic constraints arise from high upfront costs, limited financial incentives, and market inequities that disproportionately affect smallholder producers. Data-related constraints involve fragmented datasets, inadequate monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) frameworks, and poor interoperability across production scales. Policy and governance constraints reflect institutional fragmentation, regulatory misalignment, and inequitable policy structures that hinder alignment with sustainable production objectives. Recognizing these constraints as deeply interdependent, the review highlights key solution pathways, including advances in sensing and AI-driven technologies, improved emission metrics, strengthened MRV frameworks, policy reforms, and global collaboration mechanisms. By linking uncertainty reduction in emission quantification with MRV credibility, economic incentives, governance systems, and value-chain accountability, this review positions emission monitoring as foundational infrastructure for scalable and sustainable livestock decarbonization aligned with long-term climate-neutrality objectives.

title: Imidazole derivative-regulated Cu-MOF nanozyme sensor array integrating machine learning for flavonoids detection and soy milk traceability.
abstract: Flavonoids are important natural bioactive compounds with remarkable health benefits, requiring rapid and accurate detection for food nutrition assessment and quality control. However, it remains challenging to simultaneously discriminate multiple flavonoids in complex matrices. Taking inspiration from the tunable structures of MOF-based nanozymes and the ability of sensor arrays to simultaneously detect multiple substances, we herein propose an innovative four-channel colorimetric sensor array for flavonoid identification. Four copper-based MOF nanozymes (Cu-ImC2N, Cu-ImC2, Cu-ImCl2, Cu-ImPh) were synthesized with different imidazole derivatives as ligands, showing significant differences in their peroxidase-like activities. Exploiting their specific catalytic activity variations at pH 6.0 and 6.5, the two most active nanozymes (Cu-ImC2N and Cu-ImC2) were strategically selected to construct the array. Upon processing the array data with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), the array achieved 100% accurate discrimination and quantitative detection of seven flavonoids, with limits of detection (LODs) ranging from 0.039 to 0.982 μM. Furthermore, comparisons of concentration-independent models built with multiple machine learning algorithms showed that the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) method outperformed LDA, effectively reducing interference from concentration variations. The sensor array was successfully applied to the analysis of commercial soy milk, reliably differentiating products from different brands and bean sources (e.g., soybean and mung bean). This strategy surpasses traditional single-analyte methods and holds substantial practical potential for the rapid on-site detection of complex food systems.

title: HyGage: Solving the hysteresis puzzle with a new streamflow monitoring method
abstract: 11 The questionable reliability of discharges obtained using the traditional stage–discharge 12 method under gradually varied flow conditions continues to motivate the search for 13 improved monitoring approaches that support water resources management, streamflow 14 forecasting, and multipurpose scientific investigations related to the water cycle. This 15 paper introduces HyGage, a new physically based monitoring method grounded in the 16 governing equations of spatiotemporal, gradually varied, shallow open channel flow. The 17 methodology integrates measurement elements commonly employed in the index velocity 18 and slope area methods within a unified analytical framework, enabling real time discharge 19 estimation in both steady and gradually varied flows without relying on the semi empirical 20 techniques of the past. The performance of HyGage is evaluated by comparing its discharge 21 estimates with those obtained from established methods. Unlike conventional approaches, 22 HyGage is not built around any specific instrument; instead, it can flexibly incorporate 23 combinations of immersed, close range, and remote sensing measurements through 24 seamless integration. 25

Impact of S-metolachlor, atrazine and their metabolites on the morphological, structural and functional properties of the intestinal barrier.
abstract: S-metolachlor (MTC) and atrazine (ATZ) are herbicides commonly applied to corn and soybean crops. Their persistence in water and soil has led to frequent detection of these compounds and their metabolites in the environment, supporting the need to better understand their potential impact on organisms. Contaminated water and food represent important routes of human exposure to MTC and ATZ through ingestion, bringing these compounds into direct contact with intestinal epithelial cells. Such exposure may affect intestinal epithelial function and compromise barrier integrity. We used Caco-2 cells as an in vitro model to assess the effects of exposure to MTC, ATZ and their metabolites on the morphological, structural, and functional properties of the intestinal barrier. Despite the absence of functional or morphological effects following exposure to ATZ and its metabolites, ATZ fully crossed the epithelial barrier, indicating a potential route to systemic exposure and warranting further investigation of its effects beyond the intestinal compartment. After prolonged exposure, MTC induced an epithelial hypertrophic response characterized by increased cell and nuclear size and reduced proliferation, without overt disruption of intercellular junctions or barrier integrity. In contrast, its metabolites did not induce the hypertrophic phenotype observed with MTC but displayed distinct molecular effects, highlighting the need to consider both parent compounds and their metabolites in toxicological assessments. The biological significance of this hypertrophic response and the consequences of repeated or chronic exposure remain to be determined.

Transformation of aflatoxins by a thermostable and mediator-independent laccase from Thermincola ferriacetica.
abstract: Aflatoxin, a potent carcinogenic mycotoxin, commonly contaminates crops and poses a serious threat to global food and feed security. In recent years, enzymatic degradation of aflatoxins (AFs) has attracted considerable attention, with microbial laccases being the most extensively investigated. Here, we identified a thermostable laccase from Thermincola ferriacetica (Thfe-Lac) that is capable of transforming AFB1 in the absence of mediators. Under mediator-free condition, Thfe-Lac removed over 95% of 20 μg/mL AFB1 within 12 h. The optimal pH of Thfe-Lac against ABTS and AFB1 were pH 4.0 and pH 8.0, indicating distinct oxidation mechanisms for these two substrates. Thfe-Lac exhibited its optimal temperature at 70 °C and retained over 60% of residual activity after 2 h of incubation at 70-80 °C. The addition of the natural mediator acetosyringone (AS) further enhanced the AFB1-transforming ability of Thfe-Lac. In the presence of AS, Thfe-Lac was also able to transform other mycotoxins, including zearalenone (ZEN) and deoxynivalenol (DON). Moreover, several key residues within the substrate-binding pocket were identified through molecular docking. Further quantum mechanics calculations on residue-substrate interaction models revealed that dispersion interactions played an important role in AFs binding. Notably, elimination of unfavored π-π interaction and steric hindrance significantly improved the activity of the F232A mutant. Meanwhile, the enlarged substrate binding pocket facilitate AFB1 entry and promotes closer positioning toward the His500-Cys501-His502 motif. Finally, Thfe-Lac and its mutant F232A represent efficient mediator-free laccase for decontamination of AFB1 in food and feed systems.

title: Biosurfactants in the food chain: Perspectives and challenges.
abstract: Biosurfactants (BS) of microbial origin combine inherent surface activity with unique functional properties and natural status, enabling the development of innovative clean-label products and more sustainable processing strategies. This article synthesizes recent advances in the application of BS throughout the food chain, from farm to table with particular emphasis on studies reported during the last five years and validated in food-relevant models. The review highlights BS applications in crop protection, animal health, food processing and formulation, waste valorization, and nanotechnology, while critically discussing current limitations and emerging opportunities. The multifunctional nature of BS supports their use as antimicrobial agents, functional ingredients, sanitizers, postbiotics for animal health, and components of smart and active packaging systems. Furthermore, the valorization of food residues and agro-industrial waste streams as substrates for BS production contributes to circular bioeconomy approaches and more sustainable food systems. However, despite promising laboratory-scale results, the translation of BS applications into industrial practice remains constrained by limited validation in complex food systems, production and purification costs, safety assessment requirements, and regulatory challenges. Future research should prioritize application-oriented studies, safety and regulatory frameworks to facilitate the broader adoption of BS across the food chain.

title: From SCA cupping to Coffee Value Assessment: non-interchangeable scores, multidimensional sensory profiling and sensory-volatile links in Brazilian Federal District coffees.
abstract: The Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) replaced its former cupping protocol with the Coffee Value Assessment (CVA), which separates affective quality judgments from descriptive sensory characterization. Coffees from 14 producers in the Brazilian Federal District were evaluated in 2024 and 2025. Former SCA cupping was conducted by certified Q Graders, whereas CVA was applied by a coffee-experienced, semi-trained panel. SCA and CVA affective scores were not numerically interchangeable, and their final-score configurations were not significantly aligned. Assessor-blocked models detected producer differentiation under both protocol-panel conditions. SCA showed stronger adjusted differentiation and greater sensitivity to the markedly defective coffee in each harvest; removing these samples substantially reduced SCA effect sizes, while CVA effects changed little. Among non-defective coffees, SCA scores were comparatively compact. CVA affective ratings spanned a wider range but showed greater within-sample variability and did not produce stronger score-based differentiation. CVA descriptive intensities, structured check-all-that-apply (CATA) descriptors and free notes provided complementary sensory information and revealed harvest-specific patterns not captured by final scores alone. Fisher-selected volatile features added an exploratory chemical dimension, but whole-configuration sensory-volatile alignment was low to moderate and nonsignificant. Overall, former SCA cupping yielded a more compact and defect-sensitive score representation, while CVA contributed a broader multidimensional sensory record. Because different assessor panels applied the two frameworks, the observed contrasts reflect both protocol and panel composition.

title: PdO-T nanozyme-based three-channel colorimetric sensor array coupled with machine learning for accurate differentiation and quantitative detection of aflatoxins in U.S. pecan.
abstract: Aflatoxins (AFs) represent a class of highly toxic food contaminants, yet existing detection approaches still suffer from several critical limitations. Herein, three PdO nanoenzymes (denoted as PdO-160, PdO-200, and PdO-240) were synthesized by regulating the hydrothermal temperature. All three nanozymes display robust and stable peroxidase-like activity via the generation of •OH and 1O₂. By exploiting the distinct inhibitory effects of AFB1, AFB2, AFG1, and AFG2 toward these nanoenzymes, a three-channel colorimetric sensor array was rationally constructed. Combined with a random forest (RF) model, the proposed array enables accurate discrimination of all four AFs independent of concentration. Further quantitative prediction was conducted using RF regression and artificial neural network (ANN) models, and the RF regression delivers optimal fitting performance with the maximum determination coefficient R2 up to 0.971 for the four target analytes. In real-sample analysis, the array obtains favorable classification performance for mixed aflatoxins, with an accuracy of 95.65% for concentration-independent identification, and all R2 values above 0.956 in quantitative analysis. The nanoenzymes also exhibit excellent batch-to-batch reproducibility and long-term storage stability. This study offers a promising colorimetric sensing strategy for the screening of aflatoxins in food matrices.

title: Multi-label classification model of the five tastes based on molecular structure and natural language processing techniques
A data-driven approach to evaluating the use of the periodisation of skill training framework for classifying training in a team-sport context.
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the application of the PoST framework in a team sport context and compare two data-driven classification methods to objectively assess the skill training outcomes. Training drills were assessed for information complexity and game-representativeness using variables describing the training environment and athlete performance. Coach classifications of drills were analysed using repeated-measures MANOVAs, while k-means and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering objectively grouped drills based on information complexity, and compared with PoST stages. Coach classifications varied, with training intentions not always clearly distinguished, and similar game-representativeness observed across classifications, despite PoST emphasising this as a key differentiator. Both clustering methods identified three distinct training types, aligning with PoST's 'Complex Training', 'Team-based Training' and 'Performance Training' stages. However, the probabilistic overlap of the GMM better captured drills transitioning between stages. Neither method identified drills reflecting PoST's Coordination stage, suggesting misalignment between coach intent and the framework's definition. Coaches should consider both training complexity and representativeness to better align drills with game demands and desired outcomes. A modified framework designed for team-level skill development may support this, while objective classification methods may be used to enhance training design and evaluation.

title: Structures and therapeutic mechanisms in ZNF384-r B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
abstract: ZNF384 gene rearrangement (ZNF384-r) is one of the major genetic lesion in 4% B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) patients. However, the exact pathogenic mechanism leading to the leukemia outbreak remains elusive. Here, we determined the crystal structure of the ZNF384 zinc finger (ZF) domains 3-4 (2.0 Å). This helped to obtain the model ZNF384-DNA complex by AlphaFold 3, SAXS and X-ray crystallography. Site directed mutagenesis identified key residues Q68 in ZF3 and Q98 in ZF4 that were essential for transcriptional activity. Clinical characteristics of 10 new cases of ZNF384-r B-ALL were reported and integrated multi-omics profiling identified ID2 as a ZNF384-r-dependent target gene that was frequently associated with poor prognosis. Abnormal ID2 expression delineated a clinically adverse subgroup characterized by more severe differentiation arrest and immunosuppressive signature. Supportively, targeting ID2 in ZNF384-r cells induced mitochondrial apoptosis and effectively suppressed leukemia progression in patient derived xenograft (PDX) mice. Altogether, this study not only revealed the DNA engagement mechanism in oncogenic ZNF384-r fusion, but also highlighted ID2 as a promising therapeutic target in B-ALL.

FLORO: A multimodal geospatial foundation model for ecological remote sensing across sensors and scales
journal: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Foundation models offer a promising route to transferable remote sensing representations, but many current approaches depend on very large pretraining datasets and fixed sensor configurations, limiting their suitability for ecological and environmental applications, where observations often vary across platforms, spatial and spectral resolutions, and available modalities. We introduce FLORO, a multimodal geospatial foundation model designed to learn transferable representations from a small but highly diverse remote sensing corpus. FLORO is pretrained using masked autoencoding on a heterogeneous combination of Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, SkySAT imagery, elevation, and UAV-derived data. To accommodate sensor variability, FLORO incorporates availability-aware inputs that indicate which spectral bands and auxiliary modalities are present in each sample, enabling a unified input space across heterogeneous sensor configurations. We evaluated FLORO on the PANGAEA benchmark under a frozen-encoder protocol across scene classification, segmentation, and regression tasks. Despite being pretrained on a smaller corpus than competing foundation models, FLORO achieved strong and stable transfer across optical, optical-SAR, and optical-elevation benchmarks spanning medium-resolution satellite, airborne, and ultra-high-resolution UAV imagery. FLORO obtained the second-best average segmentation performance across six PANGAEA benchmarks, the third-best average rank across three scene-classification benchmarks, and excelled in regression tasks, while qualitative results showed improved preservation of spatial structure in flood, urban, biomass, and canopy-height prediction settings. Overall, these results position FLORO as a practical framework for ecological and environmental monitoring under heterogeneous sensing conditions.

title: Speech-based differentiation of unipolar and bipolar depression across scripted reading and interview questions.
abstract: BACKGROUND Differentiating bipolar depression (BPD) from unipolar depression (UPD) remains clinically challenging. We examined whether acoustic and linguistic speech features could support this distinction and whether their informativeness varied across scripted reading and interview questions. METHODS This study included 109 healthy controls (HCs), 52 patients with UPD, and 53 patients with BPD experiencing depressive episodes. Participants completed a scripted reading task and an interview-based speech task comprising 16 questions. Acoustic features were extracted from all audio recordings, and linguistic features were derived from interview transcripts. Group differences were examined using robust analysis of covariance with global false discovery rate correction. Two-level stacking models with fold-wise sex adjustment of acoustic features evaluated classification performance and importance of speech features and interview-based speech elicitation prompts. RESULTS Multiple acoustic and linguistic features showed significant group differences in interview responses, whereas no acoustic features differed significantly during scripted reading. The best-performing models achieved F1 scores of 0.6655 for three-class classification (HC, UPD and BPD) and 0.6430 for binary classification (UPD and BPD). Within interview-based speech, statistical and machine learning analyses identified Average Pause Duration, Phonation Ratio, and quantity-related expressions as particularly informative features. Two interview questions about (hypo-)manic experiences contributed most to differentiating BPD from UPD. CONCLUSIONS Acoustic and linguistic speech features may help differentiate BPD from UPD during depressive episodes, with their informativeness varying across speech tasks and interview questions. Our findings suggest that targeted interview-based speech assessment may have potential as a non-invasive adjunct to conventional clinical evaluation.

Integrating periphyton dynamics into an agroecosystem model for rice paddy N footprint evaluation.
abstract: Periphyton at the soil-water interface regulates nitrogen (N) cycling in rice paddies, yet its role in multi-pathway N losses is overlooked in agroecosystem models, leaving a critical gap in assessing the integrated environmental N footprint (NF) of rice systems. The core challenge lies in capturing the seasonal sink-source transition of periphyton under coupled environmental controls and upscaling its heterogeneous N accumulation to regional scales. Here we incorporated a process-based periphyton module into the rice version of the soil Water Heat Carbon Nitrogen Simulator (WHCNS_Rice) and upscaled site-scale observations to watershed-scale application via a soil organic carbon-based parameter transfer function (μ0 = 6.05 + 5.77 × SOC, r = 0.79). The improved model, constrained by temporal measurements, published N-loss data, and field surveys from 14 paddy sites, reproduced the seasonal sink-source shift (r = 0.95) and the spatial heterogeneity of periphyton biomass N (PBN; mean 13.9 kg N ha-1, CV = 30.1%) at watershed scale. Periphyton decreased NH3 volatilization by 17.8%, while increasing denitrification, N leaching, and runoff N losses by 28.6%, 2.7%, and 7.0%, respectively, with crop N uptake remained nearly unchanged (+0.4%). As the reduction in NH3 volatilization dominated the integrated response, the yield-scaled NF declined by 5%, from 9.3 to 8.8 kg N-eq t-1 on average. The NF reduction scaled positively with PBN (r = 0.55, p < 0.001), with each 1 kg N ha-1 increase in PBN corresponding to a 0.02 kg N-eq t-1 decrease in NF, indicating greater mitigation potential in areas with larger PBN. These findings demonstrate that representing periphyton is essential for unbiased regional N footprint assessment, particularly in paddy fields with higher periphyton N storage, and provide a modelling framework to support region-specific evaluations.

title: Knowledge and influence mechanism of leader–member exchange on hotel employees’ craftsmanship spirit:An empirical exploration based on SEM and fsQCA
abstract: In high-contact service industries, the craftsmanship spirit plays a pivotal role in driving the continuous improvement of service quality and the enrichment of customer experience. Its formation mechanism, however, requires meticulous investigation from the perspective of organisational behaviour. Grounded in the social exchange theory (SET), this study develops a chain-mediated model linking leader – member exchange (LMX), voice behaviour, organisational citizenship behaviour (OCB), and craftsmanship spirit, and further incorporates employee trust as a moderating variable to clarify the multiple pathways leading to the craftsmanship spirit. Data were collected through a questionnaire survey of 393 employees from 12 hotels, and the proposed model was empirically tested using structural equation modelling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). The results reveal that: (1) LMX serves as a core situational factor in stimulating employees ’ craftsmanship spirit; (2) voice behaviour and OCB constitute a chain-mediated pathway through which LMX influences craftsmanship spirit; (3) employee trust plays a significant and differentiated moderating role in the LMX – craftsmanship spirit relationship, with LMX exerting a stronger positive effect under high-trust conditions; (4) fsQCA identifies three equivalent configurations leading to high craftsmanship spirit: trust-based mutual support, empowerment-driven participation, and reciprocity – trust integration, highlighting the complementary roles of institutional resources and relational capital in different contexts. Theoretically, this study extends the application of LMX and SET to the hotel industry, enriching research on the processes and boundary conditions underlying craftsmanship spirit formation. Practically, it offers differentiated managerial strategies for enhancing the craftsmanship spirit by optimising superior – subordinate relationships, promoting employee voice, fostering OCB, and cultivating a high-trust organisational climate.

miR-342-3p as a Candidate Biomarker and Potential Regulator of Osteogenic Dysfunction in Experimental Radiation-Combined Bone Injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND Radiation-combined bone injury (RCBI) is commonly caused by nuclear incidents, yet its healing mechanisms are poorly understood and therapeutic options remain limited. This study explores the expression and regulatory role of miR-342-3p in experimental RCBI using human radiation-exposure and fracture cohorts, a murine RCBI model, and irradiated mouse bone marrow stromal cell (mBMSC) assays. METHODS Differentially expressed miRNAs linked to radiation exposure and fracture healing were identified from GEO datasets and cross-analyzed to prioritize candidates. Target genes were predicted by TargetScan 8.0 and validated by dual-luciferase assays. Plasma miR-342-3p was measured in glioma patients undergoing radiotherapy, long-bone fracture patients, and healthy volunteers. Murine RCBI and irradiated mBMSC models were established to characterize pathophysiology; the effect of a miR-342-3p inhibitor on osteogenic function was assessed in vitro. RESULTS Circulating miR-342-3p is context-dependently regulated: its change during early fracture healing was normalization-dependent (upregulated with the miR-16-based two-step normalization but reversed with spike-in-only normalization) and could not be reliably established, whereas it was downregulated post-radiotherapy. Dual-luciferase assays confirmed RUNX2 as a direct target. In murine RCBI, radiation and bone injury exerted interactive (radiation-dominant) effects on hematopoiesis and synergistic suppression of osteogenic protein expression; histological evaluation at day 7 revealed reduced collagen deposition and impaired early callus formation. Intracellular miR-342-3p was upregulated in irradiated mBMSCs, with exploratory correlation analysis (n=3 per group) suggesting altered association patterns between miR-342-3p and osteogenic gene expression under irradiation; these descriptive correlations do not establish a mechanistic switch. The miR-342-3p inhibitor reduced radiation-induced apoptosis and restored osteogenic differentiation in vitro. CONCLUSION This exploratory study demonstrates that circulating miR-342-3p is differentially regulated by radiation and fracture healing in separate human cohorts, although the fracture-associated direction was normalization-dependent and could not be reliably established, and its intracellular expression is associated with altered osteogenic gene regulation in irradiated mBMSCs. These findings identify miR-342-3p as a preliminary candidate biomarker and regulator of osteogenic dysfunction in experimental RCBI.

title: Selective recovery of molybdenum from spent iron-molybdate catalysts through NH4OH(NH4)2SO4 leaching and solvent extraction
abstract: An integrated hydrometallurgical process was developed for the selective recovery of molybdenum from spent iron-molybdate catalysts generated during formaldehyde production. Ammoniacal buffer leaching was statistically optimized using response surface methodology based on central composite design to evaluate the effects of NH 4 OH:(NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 molar ratio, total ammonia concentration, pulp density, temperature, and time on molybdenum dissolution. The developed quadratic model demonstrated strong predictive capability and identified the ammonia-ammonium ratio as the most influential parameter. The kinetic analysis revealed that leaching proceeds through a multi-step mechanism involving NH 3 -NH 4 + coupled solution equilibria, surface reactions, and interfacial transport. Under optimized conditions, 98.3% molybdenum leaching was experimentally achieved with only 2.1% iron co-dissolution in ammoniacal solution. The pregnant leach solution was directly treated by solvent extraction using protonated tri-n -octylamine modified with tributyl phosphate in kerosene. Selective extraction of 96% molybdenum was achieved at pH 5.4 without measurable iron co-extraction. Two-stage counter-current extraction enabled an overall extraction efficiency of 99.96%, demonstrating strong potential for continuous and scalable operation. Quantitative stripping with NaOH solution produced a molybdenum-rich solution (~103 g ⋅ L (cid:0) 1 Mo), from which high-purity sodium molybdate (Na 2 MoO 4 .2H 2 O) crystals were recovered by evaporative crystallization. The integrated process combines NH 4 OH – (NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 leaching, liquid-liquid separation, and crystallization techniques into an efficient hydrometallurgical route for recovering molybdenum from spent Fe – Mo catalysts and provides a promising strategy for the efficient utilization of secondary mo-lybdenum resources.

An Exploratory Study of Fusion of Intratumoral and Peritumoral Ultrasound Radiomics With Clinical Features for Distinguishing Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma From Hodgkin Lymphoma.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To develop a model integrating clinical features with intratumoral and peritumoral ultrasound radiomics features for distinguishing Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) from Hodgkin Lymphoma (HL). METHODS This study retrospectively analyzed data from 102 DLBCL patients (218 enlarged lymph nodes) and 37 HL patients (105 enlarged lymph nodes) at The First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University. The enlarged lymph nodes were randomly allocated to a training cohort (227 nodes) and a test cohort (96 nodes) in a 7:3 ratio. Radiomics models were constructed based on ultrasound images from both the primary tumor and the peritumoral regions (8/16/24-pixel extensions). For the optimally performing regions of interest, two fusion strategies, a feature-based and a decision-based model, were applied to build the fusion models. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, with the area under the curve (AUC) calculated to quantify discriminative ability. Clinical utility was assessed through decision curve analysis (DCA). Calibration curves were generated to evaluate the goodness-of-fit. The study strictly adhered to the TRIPOD-AI checklist. RESULTS In the test cohort, the radiomics model using a 16-pixel peritumoral extension demonstrated optimal performance with an AUC of 0.636. The decision-based fusion model (Radexpand16_Clinica_R) achieved the highest AUC (0.943) among all models evaluated. Additionally, the Radexpand16_Clinica_R model exhibited excellent sensitivity, specificity, and favorable clinical utility as shown by DCA. CONCLUSIONS Our exploratory analysis suggests that a decision-based fusion model shows potential in differentiating DLBCL from HL. Incorporating peritumoral regions improved the predictive capability of the radiomics models.

title: Patent landscape study on agentic AI systems and related technologies
Moving beyond overconfidence: A clinical roadmap for integrating uncertainty-aware AI models into medical workflows.
abstract: Conventional artificial intelligence (AI) models can remain overconfident when their predictions are unreliable, limiting clinical adoption. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) supplements predictions with information about confidence, but the literature is often mathematically dense and difficult to translate into action. In this clinically oriented review, we synthesize current evidence and offer a practical perspective on the deployment of uncertainty-aware AI. We describe how uncertainty arises, summarize four principal computational approaches, and examine applications across clinical tasks, model development, foundation models, large language models, and agentic workflows. Uncertainty estimates may identify outputs requiring review, but they do not independently establish safety; their value depends on validation against relevant errors and linkage to appropriate actions in the intended setting. We, therefore, propose an adaptable roadmap connecting local reliability evaluation and threshold selection with subgroup assessment, prospective clinical evaluation, ongoing monitoring, and governance.

title: Evaluating bias-adjusted climate data for extreme heat metrics in agricultural applications
abstract: Bias adjustment is standard preprocessing for climate model output used in crop-impact and damage-assessment work. Most validation studies still emphasize mean temperature, even though agricultural applications often depend on nonlinear heat metrics built from daily extremes. We evaluate how bias adjustment propagates into Extreme Degree Day (EDD) metrics, which crop-yield and damage functions use to summarize heat stress above specified temperature cutoffs. Using ERA5 reanalysis as reference, we compare EDD from raw and bias-adjusted CMIP6 models (GFDL-ESM4, MPI-ESM1-2-HR, and EC-Earth3) across European ADM1 regions for 1994–2014. We compute EDD at seven thresholds (0, 4, 8, 12, 28, 30, and 32 °C), aggregate it with harvested-area weights for seven crops under rainfed and irrigated management, and sum it over crop-specific phenological windows. Bias adjustment reduces mean absolute error at low and moderate thresholds (EDD ≤ $ \le $ less than or equals 12 °C) by 37–86 °C ⋅ $ \cdot $ dot days at EDD-0 and 29–64 °C ⋅ $ \cdot $ dot days at EDD-8. At extreme thresholds (EDD ≥ $ \ge $ greater than or equals 28 °C), Δ $ \Delta $ upper Delta Skill is small on average (1–4 °C ⋅ $ \cdot $ dot days at EDD-28), and bias adjustment increases error in about 40% of evaluated combinations. The split between helpful and unhelpful bias adjustment follows the EDD threshold more closely than model identity, which has implications for impact studies that treat bias-adjusted data as uniformly preferable.

title: Comparison between days of antibiotic spectrum coverage and days of therapy as risk factors for Clostridioides difficile infection: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE The relative contributions of antibiotic duration (days of therapy, DOT) and spectrum intensity (days of antibiotic spectrum coverage, DASC) to Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) risk remain unclear. This multicenter study aimed to identify independent risk factors for CDI, differentiate the impact of length of therapy (LOT) from combination therapy intensity (DOT/LOT ratio), and characterize continuous risk profiles to inform actionable antimicrobial stewardship. DESIGN Retrospective cohort study. SETTING The study was conducted at two Japanese tertiary hospitals from 2016 to 2024. PATIENTS AND METHODS Hospitalized patients undergoing CDI testing after receiving systemic antibiotics were classified into CDI and non-CDI groups. Independent risk factors were identified using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) models. Internal validity was evaluated using bootstrap resampling. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to achieve balance in baseline CDI risk factors. RESULTS Among 3,073 patients, 186 developed CDI. Prolonged DOT was independently associated with an increased risk of CDI; RCS analysis demonstrated progressive increase in CDI risk beyond the median DOT of 16 days. Bootstrap validation showed minimal optimism. In the PSM cohort (n = 186 pairs), prolonged DOT remained significantly associated with CDI, and lower DASC emerged as a significant risk factor, reflecting the disproportionate use of specific high-risk, narrow-spectrum antibiotics. Furthermore, supplementary models revealed that both prolonged LOT and higher DOT/LOT ratio were independent risk factors for CDI. CONCLUSIONS Prolonged DOT was a primary factor associated with CDI. Antimicrobial stewardship interventions could benefit from incorporating duration reduction measures alongside careful evaluation of individual antibiotic CDI risks.

title: Boosting soil health and profitability with cereal rye in Midwest crop-livestock systems under future warming
abstract: Maintaining agricultural productivity and soil health in the U.S. Midwest amid changing weather patterns is a critical challenge. Using a system-dynamics model previously calibrated and validated against 2002–2022 Iowa data, we conducted the first century-scale (2023–2122) evaluation of four agricultural production systems: conventional corn–soybean cropping with/without rye cover crops (CwCC, CwoCC), and integrated crop–livestock systems with/without grazed rye cover crops (ICLSwCC, ICLSwoCC), under intermediate and high-temperature trajectories. Under the high-temperature scenario, cropping-only systems and ICLSwoCC reach peak farm wealth in 60–70 years, then stagnate or decline, while environmental quality steadily deteriorates. In contrast, ICLSwCC sustains strong wealth accumulation and the highest environmental scores for the entire 100 years, driven by temperature-stimulated rye biomass that supports larger herds (~8.2 million cow-calf pairs versus ~925,000 currently) and enhanced manure nutrient cycling. System rankings remain consistent under the intermediate scenario, though absolute divergences are smaller. Labor–leisure trade-offs persist in both ICLS variants. These exploratory scenarios indicate that only ICLSwCC simultaneously maintains long-term profitability and soil health under substantial temperature increase, making it the most resilient strategy among those examined for the U.S. Corn Belt.

title: A TGF-β1-Binding and Stem Cell-Homing Peptide Hydrogel Loaded with BMSC-Exosomes Enhances the Endogenous Repair of Surgically Induced Osteochondral Defects.
abstract: To address the poor self-repair capacity of experimental osteochondral defects and the inefficacy of conventional hydrogels, this study developed a biodegradable peptide hydrogel, Exos@TRM. This study used an acute surgically created osteochondral defect model in rats, which does not fully reproduce experimental cartilage defects or chronic human cartilage degeneration. Based on the RADA16 framework, this hydrogel incorporates a TGF-β1-binding peptide and a stem cell-recruiting motif, and is loaded with exosomes derived from bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). In vitro experiments demonstrated that Exos@TRM effectively binds TGF-β1, promotes BMSC migration, and enables sustained exosome release for up to one week, thereby facilitating BMSC proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation. In a rat cartilage defect model, Exos@TRM reduced pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages, recruited endogenous TGF-β1 and BMSCs to the injury site, promoted chondrogenic differentiation at week 3, and achieved tissue regeneration resembling natural cartilage with functional mechanical properties by week 8. Mechanistic studies confirmed that the regenerative effects are TGF-β1-dependent, and comprehensive biosafety evaluation revealed no systemic toxicity. This study demonstrates that Exos@TRM achieves significant cartilage repair without exogenous cells or high-dose growth factors through synergistic immunomodulation, localized TGF-β1 recruitment, and stem cell homing, offering a clinically promising strategy for experimental cartilage defects.

title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers.
abstract: The N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification is one of the most prevalent tRNA modifications, mainly catalysed by the METTL1-WDR4 protein complex1-4. The m7G methyltransferase METTL1 has been linked to oncogenic transformation and the maintenance of several aggressive malignancies; however, the clinical implications of therapeutically targeting a tRNA-modifying enzyme have not been established. Here we present the development and characterization of STM9005, a highly selective and potent first-in-class tRNA methyltransferase inhibitor of METTL1. Treatment of numerous cancer cell models (including leukaemia, melanoma, pancreatic carcinoma, oesophageal cancer and small cell lung carcinoma) with STM9005 blocks cell growth, causes differentiation changes and dysregulates cell cycle progression. These cellular effects were accompanied by a selective decrease in m7G on a subset of tRNAs and a reduction in their expression levels, which impacted the translation of oncogenic mRNAs. We show that pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and significantly prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin. Collectively, our results provide a strong proof of concept that targeting of tRNA methylation is a promising avenue of anti-cancer therapy and illustrate that catalytic inhibition of METTL1 represents a therapeutic strategy against a number of aggressive malignancies.

title: Rail transit passenger flow prediction and headway optimization based on a deep learning hybrid model
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: An agentic framework for intelligent clinical laboratory medicine
abstract: Clinical laboratory medicine is fundamental to healthcare yet remains an underrecognized frontier for artificial intelligence. We propose LabARIA, a human-supervised multi-agent framework that coordinates laboratory data, quality management, workflow optimization, and operational intelligence. By integrating specialized agents under transparent governance, LabARIA enables proactive laboratory management while preserving human oversight. Laboratory medicine offers a promising environment for developing, evaluating, and translating trustworthy agentic AI into healthcare delivery.

title: Integrating Bayesian Filtering and Gaussian Process Modeling for Identification of Structural Systems under Misspecified Dynamics
abstract: Bayesian filtering methods are an interesting avenue for structural health monitoring because they enable joint estimation of dynamic states and model parameters from noisy dynamics data, yielding a physics-based model of the structural system in its current condition necessary for prognosis. However, filtering methods such as the unscented Kalman filter (UKF) require knowledge of the functional form of the dynamics of the system, including potential nonlinearities, and model discrepancies can yield divergence of the filter and parameter estimates. This work proposes a framework that integrates a Gaussian process within the UKF to represent the unmodeled or missing dynamics, mitigating the impact of inaccurate modeling on the estimation of the physical parameters that characterize the known portion of the dynamics. First, we show that under some conditions on the measurements, integrating a probabilistic model to account for the uncertain portion of the dynamics yield heteroskedasticity and correlation between the process and measurement noise terms in the system’s equations, requiring appropriate modifications of the UKF formulation. We then present a method to learn the Gaussian process (GP)-based model error in a online fashion, which requires (1) careful consideration of the heteroskedastic uncertainty in both the input and output training data, and (2) a downsampling technique to avoid increase in computational time over time. We illustrate the behavior of our proposed algorithm on numerical examples, considering imperfectly known damping restoring forces. Using these examples we illustrate potential nonidentifiability issues that arise when performing joint state–parameter–model error estimation, and discuss the importance of appropriate GP prior design in this setting.
journal: ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems, Part A: Civil Engineering

title: Dynamic Event Knowledge Graph–Based Fault Diagnosis for Multisensor Electromechanical Systems of Aviation Equipment and Its Application
abstract: Aviation equipment, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) rely on a suite of sensors to support their control and navigation functions. Yet, in challenging operational conditions, these sensors are prone to malfunction, posing risks of serious safety incidents and financial harm. Although neural network–based fault diagnosis techniques have gained traction in mechanical systems, they typically struggle to synthesize data from multiple sources and disregard the value of event-based system insights. The rise of large language models (LLMs) and multimodal foundation models is transforming risk assessment and predictive maintenance in engineering systems. These models excel at processing heterogeneous data including maintenance logs, equipment manuals, time-series sensor data, and visual reports, yet suffer from inherent cognitive uncertainty, model hallucinations, black-box opacity, and poor adaptability to dynamic working environments, which limit their use in safety-critical aviation systems. To address this, this work leverages an event knowledge graph (EKG) for UAV sensor fault diagnosis: the graph’s architecture inherently structures the array of distinct sensors. Concretely, causal logic derived from event progression boosts the graph nodes’ ability to extract meaningful features, and a relationship-focused attention mechanism (built on gated convolution) captures spatial–temporal patterns within sensor data. Additionally, this study incorporates a UAV dynamic model (rooted in an event-triggered framework) into EKG construction to improve diagnostic precision, interpretability, and safety margins. When tested on three custom-built data sets, the approach achieved diagnostic accuracies of 94.93%, 98.71%, and 92.97%, respectively. Relative to standard data-driven methods and pure LLM-based diagnostic schemes, the proposed technique also exhibits stronger feature extraction performance, fewer hallucination risks, full decision traceability, and delivers the top overall diagnostic accuracy.
journal: ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems, Part A: Civil Engineering

title: Quantifying Vernacular Window Geometry via CNNs for Simulation-Oriented Analysis: An Iranian Architecture Case Study
abstract: Environmental performance is a key concern in contemporary architectural design, as buildings significantly affect energy consumption and contribute to climate change. Iranian vernacular architecture, particularly traditional window types, incorporates passive design strategies associated with thermal comfort regulation and daylight modulation. Decoding these window typologies can reveal climate-responsive design principles rooted in environmental and cultural contexts, with continued relevance to current sustainability goals. However, the geometric and formal complexity of traditional Iranian window systems has limited the systematic analysis of these systems using conventional methods. Existing research has primarily relied on visual, descriptive, or syntactic approaches, with limited emphasis on extracting quantitative, simulation-oriented data. This study proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based visual framework for automated classification of traditional window typologies and extraction of architectural parameters from façade images. Fine-tuned CNNs are employed to identify window types and derive key geometric descriptors commonly used in environmental performance modeling, including window-to-wall ratio, frame depth, and perforation density. The extracted parameters are organized into structured, simulation-oriented data sets intended for downstream use in energy and daylight modeling workflows, including tools such as EnergyPlus and Radiance. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping is used to verify that the model focuses on morphologically meaningful features, while statistical analysis (Kruskal–Wallis, P < 0.001) confirms significant typological differentiation in the extracted parameters. While environmental simulations are not conducted in the present study, the resulting parameter sets are explicitly designed to be compatible with established simulation platforms, enabling downstream use in performance evaluation workflows. Although developed using traditional Iranian window typologies, the proposed framework provides a transferable methodology for linking visual data with simulation-oriented architectural parameterization.

title: Stiffness Distribution Updating Method for Box Girder Bridges Considering Nonuniform Cross-Section Stiffness
abstract: Under long-term coupled effects of various loads, the stiffness distribution within box girder bridge cross sections becomes nonuniform. Moreover, as thin-walled closed sections, box girders exhibit more complex stress–strain states compared to conventional members. Consequently, research focusing on stiffness degradation and its implications for the complex stress state of box girder bridges is essential. This paper proposes a method for updating the stiffness distribution of box girder cross sections that considers nonuniform cross-section stiffness. The Generalized Beam Theory (GBT) is employed to accurately analyze the stress–strain state of the box girder cross section. The recommended discretization approach and analysis procedure for the box girder cross section are presented. Based on the GBT analysis, a strain gauge layout scheme is designed to obtain more robust responses that effectively reflect local stiffness variations. The updating process for cross-section stiffness distribution consists of two steps: first, traditional model updating is performed to obtain the global cross-section stiffness; second, the internal stiffness distribution of the cross section is determined by updating multiple stiffness coefficients within it. The proposed method is validated through numerical examples and field tests on an actual bridge. Results demonstrate that the updated model achieves good agreement with measured strains, with the average error significantly reduced. The proposed updating strategy enables independent analysis of stiffness distribution variations within local beam segments, achieving multimatching between global and local structural responses at different locations. This approach provides a more accurate basis for stress analysis and load-bearing capacity assessment of box girder bridges under service conditions.

title: Intelligent Prediction of Rock Mass Classification Using TBM Multivariate Time Series and Multichannel Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: In tunnel boring machine (TBM) operations, a large volume of feedback data related to the excavation process is collected in real time, which directly reflects the interaction between the TBM and surrounding rock. The key challenge in ensuring efficient and safe tunneling is to accurately extract sensitive features from vast, fluctuating, and complex multidimensional time series data to understand the geological conditions ahead of the cutterhead. In this study, a novel intelligent recognition method for TBM rock mass classification is proposed, based on piecewise aggregate approximation (PAA) and a multichannel one-dimensional convolutional neural network (MC-1D-CNN). The method effectively maps the interaction between the TBM and surrounding rock to the associated rock classes information ahead of the cutterhead. Five tunneling parameters are selected as input features. First, the PAA technique is applied to transform the multidimensional, raw TBM time series data, which exhibit different scales, into fixed-length one-dimensional feature vectors. This process reduces dimensionality and fuses the data along spatial channels. Then, a MC-1D-CNN model is constructed, which takes the multichannel PAA sequence matrix as input for training. Through multilayer nonlinear mappings and dynamic optimization, the model automatically learns the features of univariate time series within each channel, further reducing the dimensionality and extracting high-order features more strongly correlated with the rock classes. Additionally, to enhance the feature extraction ability and generalization capability of the model, a MC-1D dilated CNN (MC-1D-DCNN) is developed by incorporating dilated convolutions. The method is validated using TBM monitoring data from the second section of the Yinchao project, demonstrating its capability to accurately classify the rock classes. Comparative analysis with several ensemble machine learning models based on key tunneling parameter time series statistical features shows that the proposed TBM surrounding rock level intelligent method PAA-MC-1D-CNN has better feature mining ability and higher recognition accuracy and robustness.
journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering

title: Noise-Invariant Agentic Human-Robot Interaction GenAI System Using a Dual-Encoder Contrastive ASR Architecture and VLMs for Robot Control and Navigation in Acoustically Challenging Jobsites
abstract: Speech-based human–robot interaction (HRI) offers a natural, hands-free interface for humans and robots to collaborate in construction environments. Construction settings—characterized by acoustically challenging environments with multiple nonstationary noises—pose serious challenges to effective voice-based HRI, highlighting the need for noise-robust HRI systems tailored for acoustically volatile construction settings. This paper proposes an HRI agentic artificial intelligence (AI) system—integrating a construction domain-specific, noise-robust automatic speech recognition (ASR) agent and a vision-language model (VLM)-based robotic control agent—to reliably transcribe speech in noisy environments and parse instructions for robot navigation in acoustically challenging construction jobsites. The ASR agent was developed based on a novel dual-encoder speech transcription deep learning architecture enhanced with a contrastive learning module for noise-invariant representation learning. The ASR agent is trained on a large speech data set augmented with real-world construction noise and synthesized undertones to reflect actual construction site conditions. On top of the developed ASR, the HRI agentic AI system also includes a closed-loop VLM as an application layer that semantically parses transcribed speech into robotic tasks, such as safety inspection, predefined waypoint navigation, and adaptive navigation. The proposed system was validated using different simulated and real-world experiments replicating various cluttered construction scenarios. The results showed that the ASR agent outperforms existing baseline models in noisy conditions and that the closed-loop VLM has a high task success rate across various testing scenarios using vision-only navigation. The primary contribution of this research is the construction-tailored, noise-robust deep learning–based ASR architecture and data set curation, with the VLM control stack demonstrating the feasibility of deploying the developed ASR system in end-to-end voice-based HRI for real-time autonomous robotic and navigation tasks within noisy construction sites.

title: ASSPSE-Net: A Novel Deep Network with Multifeature Fusion for Extracting a Building Contour from High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images
abstract: As urbanization accelerates, automatic building contour extraction from high-resolution images is crucial for urban planning and disaster assessment. Traditional methods struggle with complex backgrounds and occlusions. We propose a multifeature fusion deep network ASSPSE-Net. First, it improves based on the U-Net structure, using the residual network ResNet50 as an encoder to enhance the deep feature detail extraction ability of the model. Second, the squeeze-and-excitation networks (SE-Net) in the channel attention mechanism are added to make the model pay more attention to the detailed features of the building, and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) is added to the last layer of the encoder to improve the ability to recognize multiscale buildings. Finally, the loss function combining focal loss and Dice loss is used to balance the ratio of the target to the background to enhance the extraction of difficult sample information. Experiments on the Wuhan University (WHU), Massachusetts, and self-made Changsha Building Dataset show that the accuracy of ASSPSE-Net on the three datasets is 98.17%, 93.98%, and 90.84%, and the mean intersection over union (MIoU) is 93.36%, 79.30%, and 71.02%, respectively. Compared with other semantic segmentation methods, ASSPSE-Net can accurately extract building contours and local detail features in complex backgrounds and multiscale buildings.
journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering

title: Data-Driven Differentiated Analysis of Construction Accident Causes Using Hybrid Knowledge Graphs and Bayesian Networks
abstract: Construction accidents are characterized by a high level of risk and are typically caused by the combined effects of multiple interacting factors. However, systematic investigation into the causes of construction accidents is lacking in current research, and differentiated analysis of accident types has not been provided, which renders the formulation of targeted prevention strategies challenging. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multilevel analytical framework to explore the underlying causes of construction accidents. First, accident reports of various types were collected and analyzed to extract causal factors, and a construction site accident knowledge graph (CSAKG) was established to visualize their interrelationships. Second, the decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory method was applied to simplify the complex interrelationships among causal factors within the CSAKG and to identify the key influencing elements. These elements were subsequently incorporated into a four-layer hierarchical Bayesian network (BN) model, which was developed based on the human factors analysis and classification system framework. Finally, differentiated causal pathway analyses were performed using the BN model to identify the critical causal factors and clarify their interaction mechanisms. The results demonstrate significant variations in key causal factors and their interaction pathways across different accident types, each exhibiting distinct causative logics and evolutionary characteristics. The identified pathways were further validated through tolerance design, thereby confirming the robustness and reliability of the proposed model. Overall, the proposed analytical framework effectively addresses the shortcomings of traditional approaches, offering precise, multilevel, and practical decision-support for construction safety risk management.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Attentive Point Aggregation Network for Semantic Segmentation of Building Pipeline Point Clouds
abstract: Accurate detection and modeling of pipeline systems from point cloud data are critical challenges in creating Building Information Models (BIM) of as-built environments. This study aims to develop an automated approach for semantic segmentation of building pipeline systems. To achieve this objective, we present two main contributions to the body of knowledge: a practical workflow for generating and annotating synthetic point cloud datasets from BIM models, which significantly reduces manual labeling effort, and the Attentive Point Aggregation Network (APANet), a novel deep learning architecture specifically designed for pipeline segmentation tasks. The effectiveness and components of the proposed network were analyzed through comprehensive ablation studies. Based on the synthetic dataset, experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of APANet against baseline methods. Results demonstrated that APANet achieved performance with 92.62% overall accuracy and 85.10% mean Intersection over Union (IoU) when evaluated on real-world test datasets. Comparative evaluation against four baselines confirms that APANet achieves superior performance across all metrics on this domain-specific task. A supplementary evaluation on the Stanford Large-Scale Three-Dimensional (3D) Indoor Spaces (S3DIS) public benchmark further confirms the architectural generalizability of the proposed network. The ablation studies revealed that the feature aggregation module contributed most significantly to model performance, with a 12.86% improvement in mean IoU. The case studies further validated the effectiveness of the proposed approach in handling imbalanced point cloud distributions between cylindrical pipes and rectangular ducts. The cross-domain evaluation approach (training on synthetic data, testing on real data) and specialized network architecture presented in this study provide an efficient and task-specialized solution for point cloud recognition, segmentation, and modeling of different pipeline categories in building environments, which can significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of as-built BIM modeling processes.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: A BIM-Based Framework for Managing Variation Claims in Tunnel Projects
abstract: Tunnel construction projects are highly prone to variations (change orders) and claims due to inherent geotechnical uncertainties that often result in cost overruns and delays. Traditional project management skills relying on fragmented documentation are inadequate for managing the complex and prolonged variation claims. To fill this gap, this study proposes a building information modeling (BIM)-based framework that uses both contractual and construction data to estimate project data–based potential outcomes of variation claims. It integrates BIM three-dimensional (3D) modeling and four-dimensional (4D) visualization to analyze data, identify accurate scope, calculate changed quantities for cost adjustment, and estimate potential time extension under variations. The framework is validated through two case studies, demonstrating its capability to provide intermediate settlements that can facilitate human negotiators to decide the claims. The findings highlight the framework’s potential to enhance transparency, efficiency, and fairness in the dispute resolution process, extending BIM’s application beyond design coordination toward digitally supported claim management and settlement.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: “We Are a Family Out Here”: Team Belongingness as a Resource for the Wellbeing of Fly-In-Fly-Out Workers on a Remote Construction Site in Australia
abstract: The mining and construction industries are vital to Australia’s economy, but are also characterized by demanding fly-in-fly-out (FIFO) arrangements that present unique psychosocial hazards. Drawing on the job demands-resources framework and conservation of resources theory, this study explores how team belongingness is shaped and how it helps workers manage the unique demands of FIFO work. Using an arts-based qualitative approach, 53 Draw, Write, Reflect sessions were conducted with FIFO workers on a remote mine site under construction. Thematic analysis revealed that team belongingness acted as a salient social and emotional buffer, with participants describing their teams as their ‘family away from home.” Laughter, humor, and banter were central mechanisms for fostering a sense of team belongingness and making long shifts more manageable. Everyday acts of mutual support and care further strengthened camaraderie across roles and hierarchies. However, the study also found that experiencing a sense of belongingness was more challenging for some managers and operators who felt isolated due to job demands and site structures. The findings highlight the importance of recognizing team belongingness as a core wellbeing resource that enables FIFO workers to cope with the unique demands of their work and sustain long-term participation. This has important implications for policy initiatives and organizational strategies for fostering inclusive team cultures to support safety and wellbeing.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: ProcuTrust: A Trustworthy Procurement and Management System for Building Services by Enabling Blockchain Integration
abstract: Building services systems (BSSs) require complex procurement and management (P&M) requirements due to multiple stakeholder involvement, extensive documentation, and complex workflows. Blockchain technology (BT) has shown its potential in enhancing project performance through its decentralized structure, immutability, and smart contract functionality, enabling secure, transparent, and automated transactions. Despite growing interest in blockchain within construction, there remains a combined knowledge and empirical gap in the literature, particularly regarding the absence of a single source of truth system in the procurement and management of BSS. This study addresses the gap by developing, testing, and validating ProcuTrust, a blockchain-based system tailored for BSS. The system was developed using integrated blockchain platforms (BPs) Hyperledger Fabric and Hyperledger FireFly, following the design science research (DSR) methodology. Simulations and an expert forum were used to test and validate ProcuTrust. The system architecture, development process, and user interface of ProcuTrust are presented in the paper. The simulation testing and expert forum validation established that ProcuTrust is a trustworthy P&M system for BSS that meets industry requirements. The strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats (SWOT) analysis of ProcuTrust further analyzed the strengths and opportunities that will benefit the industry, as well as the weaknesses and threats in the system that could be mitigated in the future. ProcuTrust is a unified management system that governs the entire life cycle of the BSS, from procurement to end of life, achieving trust, transparency, and efficiency. The ProcuTrust development process also provides a replicable model and system development process for future blockchain technology-based built environment applications.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Tail-Dependent Price Escalation Risk in Road Projects: A Hybrid LSTM-Gumbel Copula Model for Probabilistic Contingency Estimation
abstract: Road and bridge projects are exposed to escalation in key construction inputs such as diesel, cement, structural steel, and construction steel, where common shocks can generate jointly adverse price movements and weaken fixed-percentage contingency practices. Prior construction cost-forecasting studies have largely emphasized single-series point accuracy and often rely on independence or linear dependence assumptions, leaving a gap in contingency sizing that explicitly accounts for multivariate co-movement in escalation shocks. This study proposes a hybrid framework that couples multivariate long short-term memory (LSTM) forecasting of monthly input-index log-returns with copula-based dependence modeling of strictly out-of-sample forecast innovations. The workflow follows a blocked walk-forward design, using separate validation and test blocks for dependence calibration and final evaluation, respectively. A Monte Carlo engine integrates the trend component and dependent residual shocks to generate joint escalation scenarios and produce decision-grade cost percentiles. Using official Peruvian monthly indices from 2013 to 2025, the empirical results show heterogeneous dependence across inputs, with the strongest positive rank association observed between structural steel and construction steel ( τ = 0.9394 ), while several other pairwise links are weak or negative. In this context, the Gumbel copula is used as a conservative upper-tail benchmark, yielding θ ˆ = 16.5000 and λ ˆ U = 0.9571 . For the analyzed material basket, the benchmark tail-dependent model yields contingency requirements of 1.72% at the 90% confidence level and 3.99% at the 95% level above 50th percentile ( P 50 ). The results show that dependence assumptions materially affect high-confidence cost thresholds and that contingency reserves are better treated as confidence-based governance choices than as fixed deterministic add-ons.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Simulating Contact and Friction within the Discrete Body Dynamics Formalism
abstract: Contact and friction significantly influence the dynamics of mechanical systems. This study presents an approach for modeling contact and friction forces within the discrete body dynamics (DBD) framework, which solves the equations of motion as ordinary differential equations by replacing kinematic constraints with compliant elements. This formulation preserves the main advantages of DBD, body-wise force evaluation, and efficient element-wise computations, thereby avoiding costly matrix decompositions.
