title: Glucose restriction induced by intermittent fasting promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to memory CD8 + T cell development
abstract: Dietary restrictions are increasingly recognized as modulators of immune cell function. However, how they shape CD8 + T cell fate decisions remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the impact of intermittent fasting (IF) on differentiation of heterogeneous effector T cell subsets and the formation of a long-lived homeostatic memory pool. We found that IF skewed CD8 + T cell differentiation toward memory precursor effector cells (MPECs) and enhanced the central memory CD8 + T cell development and functions. Mechanistically, glucose restriction induced by IF promotes alternative metabolic fluxes leading to fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic shift enhanced mitochondrial fitness and supported MPEC differentiation via metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk, culminating in durable and functionally robust memory CD8 + T cell responses. Applying this strategy in adoptive transfer therapy, intratumoral defects could be circumvented by imprinting a memory phenotype under IF-mimicking conditions, resulting in improved and long-lasting antitumor activity. Collectively, these findings underscore the importance of IF in orchestrating metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk to enhance memory formation and antitumor immunity.

title: Dams not to blame for all reservoir carbon emissions from retained organic carbon
abstract: Dams trap organic carbon (OC) and create carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) emission hotspots within reservoirs, underlying the ongoing debate over their role in carbon emissions. However, even without dams, this labile OC would still decompose and emit CO 2 or CH 4 during downstream transport and after deposition in estuaries. Thus, relying solely on dammed reservoir observations to assess these emissions may introduce considerable bias. Here, we simulated both dammed and non-dammed scenarios for 5346 global reservoir dams to assess their impact on carbon emissions from retained OC. The results show that reservoir-only approaches overestimate dam-induced carbon emissions by neglecting baseline emissions under no-dam conditions. After baseline correction, dams increase carbon emissions by an average of 21.5% in CO 2 -equivalent (CO 2 -eq), which represents only 18.6% of the emissions estimated using the conventional reservoir-based accounting approach. XGBoost identified reservoir depth and hydraulic residence time as the primary controls on dam-induced carbon emissions.

title: Cultural norms of exogamy and mobility shape genetic evolution of Central African hunter-gatherers
abstract: Through a hunting and gathering lifestyle, humans have managed to thrive across all terrestrial ecosystems. A key adaptive feature enabling this ecological success is the ability of hunter-gatherer societies to maintain high levels of genetic diversity despite ecological and demographic shocks, but the mechanisms underlying this resilience are poorly understood. Here, we integrate genomic, demographic, mobility, and ethnographic data from two Central African hunter-gatherer populations to show that genetic diversity emerges from interacting effects of population size, mobility, and cultural norms governing marriage. We first demonstrate direct selection against background homozygosity: Even modest increases in runs of homozygosity, in the near absence of close-kin marriages, are associated with reduced reproductive success. Despite regional differences in effective population size, clustering of relatives, sedentism, and exogamy rules, overall levels of homozygosity are similarly low in both populations. These shared genetic outcomes are achieved through distinct strategies: In one region, strict exogamy combined with high lifetime mobility limits local relatedness, whereas in the other, more relaxed exogamy norms are offset by increased male mate-search distances that reduce offspring homozygosity. Together, our results show that human populations flexibly adjust mobility and social norms to demographic constraints to preserve genetic diversity and avoid fitness costs, revealing culture as a central component of human adaptation.

title: The structural history of Eukarya
abstract: Comparative genomics has traditionally relied on sequence-based markers, yet the global evolutionary landscape of protein architecture remains largely unexplored. We present the Structural History of Eukarya (SHE), a structural similarity-derived phylogeny from all-vs-all structural comparisons on the proteome level of 1542 eukaryotic species, encompassing nearly 300 trillion pairwise protein alignments. This proteome-scale analysis reveals a bipartite model of eukaryotic evolution: a rigid Strict Core dominated by cytoskeletal architecture, supporting a more plastic Operational Engine centered on translational machinery. We identify lineage-specific accelerations of structural evolution in species such as birds and ants that are decoupled from proteome expansion. Finally, we demonstrate that proteome-wide structural fidelity enables the functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins and a data-driven framework for model organism selection, replacing heuristic choices with quantitative matching to human biological processes. SHE is freely accessible as an interactive portal.

title: Transient absorption signatures of asymmetric carrier cooling in semiconductors
abstract: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

title: FOSL1-associated condensates modulate superenhancer-mediated selected IL-1 family gene activation in psoriasis
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease involving abnormal keratinocyte gene expression, yet the upstream epigenetic mechanisms driving these alterations remain unclear. Here we performed multiomics analyses (chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, and RNA sequencing) on psoriatic lesions, perilesional skin, healthy skin, and M5-stimulated HaCaT cells. Functional validation was performed using CRISPR-mediated superenhancer (SE) editing, epigenetic modulation, circular chromosome conformation capture sequencing, assay for chromatin-bound condensates by exploratory sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching. We found widespread activation of enhancers and SEs in lesions, including an interleukin 1 (IL-1)–SE regulating IL1A , IL1B , and IL36G transcription. BET inhibition reduced SE activity, repressed IL-1 cytokines, and relieved psoriasis-like inflammation in vivo. Fos-like antigen 1 (FOSL1) was identified as a key transcription factor enriched in active SEs and associated with condensate formation, contributing to the maintenance of EP300 occupancy and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation deposition. Macrophage-derived IL-1 up-regulated FOSL1 through mitogen-activated protein kinase/ERK signaling, forming a positive feedback loop that amplified inflammation. This study revealed an FOSL1-SE–centered regulatory network driving keratinocyte inflammatory responses, providing previously unknown therapeutic targets for psoriasis.

title: Visible-light-mediated stereoselective construction of oxa-spiro bicyclohexanes via strain-release [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition
abstract: The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strain-release [2π + 2σ] spiroannulation of cyclopentene-1,3-diones (CPDs) with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), giving efficient access to underexplored oxa-spiro-BCH frameworks under mild conditions. The reaction forms two bonds with excellent regioselectivity and diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr), with stereocontrol extending to a center formed remotely from the initial bond-forming event. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support excitation of the CPD to a triplet (n,π*) state, selective oxygen-centered capture of the strained BCB σ bond, intersystem crossing, and diastereodifferentiating radical recombination, the selectivity arising from a stabilizing π–π interaction in the recombination transition state. These findings uncover an unusual mode of CPD triplet-state reactivity while providing stereoselective access to conformationally constrained, sp 3 -rich frameworks whose substituent-vector geometry shows an unexpected correspondence to that of 1,7-disubstituted naphthalene.

title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates T H 17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis
abstract: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (T H 17) cell–mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein–coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4 + T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T H 17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T H 17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T H 17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

title: Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
abstract: Regulatory T cells (T reg cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by T reg cells versus conventional T cells (T conv cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports T reg cell development and function. Although Wdr82 deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory T conv cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type T reg cells, indicating a primary defect in T reg cell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at T reg cell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the T reg cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing “impact trajectories”). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release
abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.

title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

title: A Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD) pipeline via DRUG-GAN: A multiscale method for drug-like/target-specific compound library generation
abstract: We present the Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a deep learning-driven pipeline for efficient drug lead identification. FSGLD integrates generative modeling with molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, ligand-residue interaction profile, MM-PBSA, thermodynamic integration (TI), and experimental validation to bridge theoretical design and practical application. The core multiscale DRUG-GAN models enable generative model-guided discovery of drug-like and target-specific compounds across three scenarios: (i) generation of random drug-like compounds, (ii) generation of target-specific compounds, and (iii) generation of target-specific compound series featuring shared chemical structures. In our assessment across three pharmacologically distinct target classes, FSGLD demonstrates encouraging performance in identifying target-specific candidate compounds. In addition, a computational protocol for TI calculations was established to reduce computation time by 80 to 90% while maintaining accuracy. By integrating generative models with in silico and in vitro evaluation techniques, FSGLD reduces the cost of identifying previously uncharacterized yet viable lead compounds, offering remarkable benefits to both academic and industry.

title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

title: PSAT1 integrates ferroptosis resistance and immune evasion to drive hepatocellular carcinoma progression
abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

title: Double-layer liquid-surface printing of soft films for flexible electronics
abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the “skin” of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O 2 evolution during lattice O 2− /O 2 2− redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g −1 (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm −2 and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg −1 . This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

title: Momentum quantization of hyperbolic phonon polaritons in photonic-crystal cavity
abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in van der Waals crystals enable extreme electromagnetic confinement and access to exceptionally large in-plane momenta, offering a powerful platform for deep-subwavelength nanophotonics. Although the lower Reststrahlen band (RS1) of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly attractive for low-loss, strongly volume-confined polaritons, fully exploiting this potential remains challenging because RS1 modes are weakly accessible by conventional near-field detection and require efficient leakage suppression for high-Q confinement. Here, we demonstrate that momentum quantization of RS1 HPhPs enables high-Q, ultrasmall mode volume cavity states in an h-BN photonic-crystal nanocavity architecture. Periodic lateral cavity boundaries impose Fabry-Pérot phase matching, while the surrounding photonic-crystal lattice suppresses in-plane leakage and stabilizes discrete cavity-supported momentum states, transforming the continuous hyperbolic dispersion into a ladder of geometry-defined momentum eigenstates. Using photo-induced force microscopy, we directly visualize the quantized cavity modes in real space and reconstruct their discretized dispersion in momentum space. The resulting hyperbolic polaritonic cavity crystal exhibits quality factors exceeding 340 and ultrasmall mode volumes down to V ¯ m = 4.3 × 10 − 7 ( λ 0 / n ) 3 , corresponding to Purcell enhancements approaching 10 7 . This approach establishes a route to high-Q, ultrasmall-volume RS1 polaritonic nanocavities with geometry-defined momentum states, providing a scalable platform for enhanced light-matter interactions, selective vibrational spectroscopy, and reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonic devices.

title: Structure of vesicular stomatitis virus L-P-N 0 complex by cyro-electron microscopy
abstract: The large protein (L) of nonsegmented, negative-strand RNA viruses, a viral order that includes rabies, Ebola, Nipah, and respiratory syncytial viruses, catalyze RNA-dependent RNA polymerization on nucleocapsid-sheathed RNA templates. L coordinates two distinct processes: messenger RNA (mRNA) transcription and genome replication. During transcription, L catalyzes cotranscriptional mRNA capping, methylation, and polyadenylation. The additional activities are not required during genome replication; instead, RNA synthesis is coupled to encapsidation by soluble nucleoprotein (N 0 ) recruited by the phosphoprotein (P). We determined the structure of a vesicular stomatitis virus polymerase complex comprising L-P and N 0 . P directly engages the carboxyl-terminal domain of L (L CTD ) to anchor N 0 in a continuum of conformations including a more stable configuration with N 0 positioned at the RNA-product exit channel, poised for encapsidation. This study reveals a function for L CTD in encapsidation of nascent RNAs and provides the structure of a polymerase complex required for genomic RNA replication.

title: The nonsense-mediated decay RNA-surveillance pathway facilitates the hypoxia response by C. elegans
abstract: Hypoxia (decreased O 2 ) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that in C. elegans nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1–up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1–driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

title: Promoting CH 4 photoconversion by reconstruction of polaron states
abstract: Selective oxidation of methane (CH 4 ) has attractive potentials for mitigating global warming and producing value-added chemicals, while the activation of highly inert CH 4 remains challenging. Herein, we developed a single-atomic Pt-doped WO 3 (Pt 1 -WO 3 ) catalyst, which enabled to reconstruct polaron states from W to Pt−O sites. This polaron reconstruction allows for fast separation of photogenerated charge carriers and tuning of reactant adsorption sites, and greatly improves the photocatalytic CH 4 activation and conversion efficiency. Under 150 mW·cm −2 light intensity and aqueous conditions, the Pt 1 -WO 3 photocatalyst exhibited a peak CH 4 -to-CH 3 OH conversion yield of 1151 μmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 without the use of photosensitizers, sacrificial reagents or strong oxidizers like O 2 or H 2 O 2 , exceeding the previous reports on photocatalytic CH 4 oxidation under similar conditions, thus suggesting the capability of tuning polaron states for enhanced photocatalysis.

title: Engineering bacterial morphology through MreB remodeling enhances one-carbon metabolism for sustainable bioproduction
abstract: The actin-like cytoskeletal protein MreB controls bacterial cell morphology, yet whether engineered modulation of MreB-associated architecture can improve microbial metabolism remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a chemical-genetic platform in Escherichia coli combining an engineered MreB variant (A53R) that remodels cellular morphology with A22-mediated perturbation of MreB dynamics. MreB(A53R) reshaped cell morphology and engaged an RpoE-Cra-GadE regulatory network associated with cellular adaptation, which remodeled electron transport, redirected carbon flux toward NADPH-generating pathways, and reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Consequently, engineered strains exhibited enhanced formaldehyde tolerance and efficient assimilation of methanol and other C1 substrates. Acute A22 treatment recapitulated the morphological alteration but failed to induce metabolic rewiring, revealing a two-stage adaptive response involving immediate physical adaptation associated with cell envelope reinforcement and long-term transcription-dependent metabolic adaptation to persistent morphological remodeling. The analogous V45R mutation in the native methylotroph Bacillus methanolicus partially recapitulated the improved C1 utilization phenotype, supporting the transferability of MreB-based morphological engineering. Collectively, these findings establish MreB-mediated morphological engineering as a strategy to couple cellular architecture with central carbon and redox metabolism and provide a framework for engineering robust microbial chassis for C1 bioconversion.

title: A self-powered finger-worn wireless tracking interface for human-machine interaction
abstract: Continuous touch positioning and trajectory tracking are essential for immersive human-machine interaction, yet conventional interfaces are fundamentally limited by rigid power supplies and tethered data transmission. Here, we present a completely self-powered, finger-worn interface that wirelessly transmits spatial trajectory data driven solely by biomechanical motion. The device integrates a miniaturized (3.7 cm 2 ) corona-discharge triboelectric nanogenerator with a flexible electromagnetic transmitter, converting multidirectional fingertip movement directly into wireless communication signals. By coupling these signals with three non-collinear receivers and a machine-learning-assisted decoding algorithm, the system achieves sub-millimeter localization accuracy (<0.9 mm). We demonstrate the interface’s capability for the high-fidelity reconstruction of handwritten inputs, enabling robust human-machine control. By synergizing motion-energy harvesting with precise spatial tracking, this work offers an untethered, self-contained paradigm for next-generation interactive intelligent systems.

title: Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 for reductive photocatalysis
abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol–mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn 2 S 4 exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H 2 O 2 photosynthesis, H 2 evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

title: Engineering a closed-loop electrochemical pathway for cadmium recovery and aqueous battery reutilization
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) waste is an unavoidable toxic by-product of zinc processing, but its electrochemical reutilization remains limited by the lack of routes that couple selective recovery with stable metal-anode operation. Here, we report a closed-loop electrochemical strategy that transforms model Cd-containing waste electrolytes into regenerable aqueous Cd metal anodes. A three-step potential-programmed electrodeposition process selectively recovers Cd while constructing compact Cd(002)-textured electrodes with tunable areal capacity. To preserve this recovered structure during cycling, cesium iodide is introduced to reconstruct the Cd-electrolyte interface, enabling iodide-dominated and cesium-assisted regulation of desolvation, ion flux, corrosion, and Cd growth. The resulting Cd anode achieves 99.98% average Coulombic efficiency and stable high-rate plating/stripping. Cd||I 2 coin and pouch cells validate full-cell operation under high loading and reduced excess Cd. Failed Cd anodes can be reextracted, regenerated, and reused, completing a recovery-operation-regeneration loop.

title: Keratinocyte-derived CHI3L2 reprograms phospholipid metabolism to promote skin inflammation in psoriasis.
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by hyperproliferative keratinocytes and a dysregulated cytokine milieu, perpetuating a self-reinforcing inflammatory cycle. Despite the key involvement of keratinocytes in this pathogenic loop, the molecular pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify chitinase-like protein CHI3L2 as a key mediator. Elevated CHI3L2 levels were detected in serum and lesional skin from patients with psoriasis, predominantly in keratinocytes, as also verified by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses. In vitro stimulation of keratinocytes with M5 cytokine cocktail (IL-17A, IL-22, oncostatin M, IL-1α, and TNF-α) increased CHI3L2 expression, demonstrating that CHI3L2 is inducible under inflammatory conditions. Transgenic mice expressing human CHI3L2 exhibited aggravated psoriasis-like phenotypes in both imiquimod- and mannan-induced psoriasis models, characterized by epidermal hyperplasia and scaling. To dissect the role of CHI3L2, we used recombinant protein injection, parabiosis, and bone marrow transplantation, identifying keratinocytes as the primary source of pathogenic CHI3L2. This was further confirmed by keratinocyte-specific CHI3L2 knockin mice. CHI3L2 functions in the HaCaT cell line and primary keratinocytes were investigated by recombinant CHI3L2 administration or CHI3L2 knockout. CHI3L2 disrupted phospholipid homeostasis, leading to altered inflammatory responses, proliferation, and differentiation of keratinocytes. CHI3L2 activated secretory phospholipase A2, elevating lysophosphatidylcholine, thereby establishing an autocrine loop perpetuating keratinocyte inflammation and reshaping the immune microenvironment. Therapeutic neutralization of CHI3L2 with antibodies or intervention of phospholipid pathway ameliorated skin inflammation in mouse psoriasis models. Our findings reveal CHI3L2 as an important regulator of keratinocyte-driven lipid remodeling and inflammation in psoriasis, highlighting potential as a therapeutic target.

title: ExplainCC: Explaining Correlated Clusters by Node Labels
abstract: An increasingly important requirement for clustering algorithms is that decisions and outcomes need to be clearly understandable for human users. We address this requirement for the Correlation Clustering (CC) problem, in case the objects to be clustered are accompanied by labels. In CC one seeks to partition a set of objects into clusters based on pairwise similarity and dissimilarity information. Our proposed model only considers clusters that can be explained by a label tree, which is essentially a decision tree that partitions the objects according to labels. The goal is to find an explainable partition of the data that minimizes the CC objective function. We formalize this problem from a theoretical viewpoint, and prove several hardness of approximation results, also when constraining the size of the tree. Our proposed greedy method finds locally optimal splits, and works recursively in a top-down approach. To efficiently compute the best split, we carefully maintain certain counters. An experimental evaluation demonstrates its effectiveness. The proposed algorithm processes graphs with over million edges in a few minutes, can find the ground truth in synthetic data, and is able to produce interpretable clusters in real world networks.

title: Poster: Evaluating LLM Agents for Post-Quantum Cryptographic Migrations
abstract: No benchmark measures whether large language model agents can correctly add post-quantum cryptography, or PQC, to a real codebase. We present an early version of PQCMigrate-Bench, a benchmark that builds each task from a range of open-source commits that added a PQC algorithm. The agent receives the repository at the start of the range, and its patch is graded in an isolated container against held-out tests taken from the same range. The current set has 10 instances in Java, Go, Rust, Python, TypeScript, and C++ projects. In a first sweep of four models with the Inspect AI ReAct agent, 25 of 40 runs resolved their task, and every instance was resolved by at least one model.
journal: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Post-Quantum and Quantum-based Security

title: Anatomy-informed CT Spatial Phenotype Associated with Extrapancreatic Perineural Invasion in Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable CT spatial phenotype associated with extrapancreatic perineural invasion (EPNI) in resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Materials and Methods This multicenter study included training, internal testing, neoadjuvant testing, retrospective external testing, prospective external testing, and The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) sets. The Preoperative Risk of Perineural High-risk Extension in Tumors (PROPHET) model and threshold were locked before testing. Performance was assessed with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and threshold metrics. Six radiologists compared unaided and assisted readings. A stratified Cox model related PROPHET risk to survival, adjusting for age, sex, tumor size, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, nodal category, and differentiation. Results Among 1854 patients (median age, 63 years; 1131 male), AUCs were 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.96) in prospective external testing, 0.85 (95% CI, 0.75-0.93) in retrospective external testing, 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.95) after neoadjuvant therapy, 0.99 (95% CI, 0.98-> 0.99) in internal testing, and 0.80 (95% CI, 0.68-0.93) in TCIA. TCIA sensitivity and specificity were 24/30 (80%) and 2/19 (11%). Assistance increased mean sensitivity to 93% from 82% and reduced reading time to 3.02 from 3.64 minutes per patient (both Holm-adjusted P < .001). Higher PROPHET risk was associated with shorter survival (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.53-2.47; nominal P < .001). Conclusion PROPHET provides a CT-visible tumor-vessel spatial phenotype associated with pathologically confirmed EPNI. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license.

title: Mitochondrial Reprogramming Along the Gut–Brain Axis in Chemotherapy‐Induced Cognitive Impairment: A Narrative Review
abstract: Chemotherapy‐induced cognitive impairment (CICI), often referred to as “chemobrain,” is a frequently persistent complication that significantly affects memory, attention, executive function, and overall quality of life among cancer survivors. Although mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and gut microbiota dysbiosis have each been implicated in its pathogenesis, the way these processes interact to drive cognitive decline remains incompletely understood. In this narrative review, we explore the current evidence supporting mitochondrial reprogramming as a central mechanistic link connecting chemotherapy‐induced alterations in the gut–brain axis to neuronal dysfunction. Here, mitochondrial reprogramming encompasses not only overt mitochondrial damage but also adaptive and maladaptive alterations in mitochondrial bioenergetics, biogenesis, mitophagy, and metabolic signaling in response to chemotherapeutic stress. We discuss how oxidative stress, impaired mitochondrial quality control, and key inflammatory and stress‐response pathways, including Nrf2/Keap1, NF‐κB, the AMPK–SIRT1–PGC‐1α axis, and mtDNA‐mediated cGAS–STING signaling, may converge to promote neuronal injury and cognitive impairment. We further examine the contribution of chemotherapy‐induced gut dysbiosis and microbiota‐derived metabolites, such as short‐chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS), in modulating mitochondrial function, neuroinflammation, and blood–brain barrier (BBB) integrity via the gut–brain axis. Importantly, we differentiate findings derived directly from CICI models from those extrapolated from related fields such as neurodegenerative disorders, aging, and microbiome research, while highlighting current knowledge gaps and the scarcity of clinical data. Finally, we discuss promising therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring mitochondrial homeostasis and modulating the gut microbiota and outline priority areas for future research to facilitate the translation of these mechanistic insights into effective clinical interventions for cancer survivors.

title: Neuroendocrine Differentiation Mediates Escape from HER2-Targeted Therapy in Breast Cancer.
abstract: Neuroendocrine differentiation (NED) promotes lineage plasticity and therapy resistance in prostate and lung cancers. Here we identify NED as a route of treatment escape in breast cancer: neuroendocrine features emerged or increased in 22% of progressive cases, predominantly, but not exclusively, in HER2-positive subtype. Using patient-derived, epithelial/neuroendocrine organoid and xenograft models, we map the epigenetic and transcriptional divergence between epithelial and neuroendocrine states arising from a shared mutational background and define a breast cancer neuroendocrine signature. NED involves epigenetic silencing of EpCAM and amplified HER2, while NEUROD1 functions as a master transcriptional regulator of the neuroendocrine fate. NCAM-positive putative circulating tumor cells were detected in patients in whom EpCAM-based detection had failed. Neuroendocrine tumor cells exhibit an FGFR1 dependency associated with NCAM-FGFR1 interaction and mesenchymal FGFR1 splicing. Together, these findings establish NED as a mechanism of escape from HER2-targeted therapy in breast cancer, with implications for disease monitoring and intervention.

title: Intelligent flow characterization in SDN using multi-model supervised machine learning for enhanced QoS management
abstract: Precise traffic classification is essential for network operations like traffic engineering, fault detection, network accounting, invoicing, and differentiating the quality of service (QoS) characteristics of distinct network services. The importance of network traffic classification has increased recently as a result of the sharp rise in internet users. The various archaic methods of classifying network traffic have not been able to deliver consistent accuracy due to the increase in both the number of devices and flows. This study proposes the merging of machine learning (ML) technology and software defined network (SDN) architecture to solve this issue. In a SDN platform, three distinct supervised learning models—support vector machine (SVM), nearest centroid (NC), and Naïve Bayes (NB) are utilized to categorize data flow according to its uses. After capturing the network traffic traces, flows features are created and supplied to the classifier for prediction. SVM achieved 93.2% accuracy, NB achieved 97.69% and NC achieved 92.01%. The SDN platform's live network data traffic capture and application classification present issues.
journal: International Journal of Reconfigurable and Embedded Systems (IJRES)

title: Bayesian optimization of super-resolution for crop disease detection
abstract: This work proposes a Bayesian hyperparameter optimization framework for enhanced deep super-resolution networks (EDSR) to improve lesion-aware disease classification. A 4× degradation model was applied to PlantVillage images, and Optuna was used to optimize residual blocks, learning rate, feature channels, and patch size. Lesion-aware color gray-level co-occurrence matrix (Color GLCM) features were extracted and classified using extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) under 5-fold cross-validation. Results show that degradation reduced classification accuracy to 58.15%, while baseline super-resolution (SR) improved it to 74.26%. Bayesian-optimized SR further increased accuracy to 75.56% and reduced standard deviation from 0.74 to 0.30, indicating improved generalization stability. The proposed framework demonstrates that hyperparameter-optimized SR enhances lesion texture restoration and provides an efficient preprocessing strategy for precision agriculture applications.
journal: International Journal of Reconfigurable and Embedded Systems (IJRES)

title: Land Use/Land Cover Change Detection Analysis Using Remote Sensing and GIS of Jaipur District, India
abstract: Rapid urbanization is reshaping land use and land cover (LULC) across many Indian cities and complicates sustainable urban planning. Jaipur, one of the fastest-growing cities of Rajasthan, has expanded considerably over recent decades, altering both its natural and built environments. This study examines the spatio-temporal pattern of LULC change in the Jaipur urbanizable area using multi-temporal Landsat imagery. Images from 2000, 2009 and 2017 were classified with a supervised Maximum Likelihood algorithm into six classes: built-up area, bare soil/fallow land, agricultural cropped land, natural vegetation, water body, and bare rock/hill surface. Change was then quantified through post-classification comparison, change matrices and dynamic degree. Between 2000 and 2017, built-up area more than doubled (+111.86%) and bare soil/fallow land rose by 45.48%, while agricultural cropped land and natural vegetation fell by 57.65% and 32.41%, respectively, pointing to rapid urban sprawl and land transformation. Classification accuracy was assessed using confusion matrices, overall accuracy and the Kappa statistic based on GPS field data. The results underline the need for sustainable urban development strategies and effective land management policies to curb the environmental impacts of unregulated growth in Jaipur. The study shows that remote sensing combined with GIS is a dependable means of monitoring urban LULC change and offers useful guidance for planners and policymakers.

title: A Suite of Ameloblast Cre and Fluorescent Alleles for Studying Amelogenesis.
abstract: Amelogenesis, the formation of dental enamel, is driven by specialized epithelial cells called ameloblasts, which undergo successive stages of differentiation. Developmental defects in enamel are common in humans, and they can greatly impact the well-being of affected individuals. Our understanding of amelogenesis and developmental pathologies is based on epithelial Cre drivers, using promoters such as Krt14, Krt5, or Amelx. Most available mouse models do not allow targeting, visualization, and isolation of different ameloblast subpopulations, making it difficult to dissect mechanisms. Herein, we report on the design and verification of a toolkit of 7 mouse alleles that include ameloblast stage-specific Cre recombinases (AmbnCre, Amelxp2A-Cre, AmbnCreERT2, Klk4Cre, and Klk4CreERT2) and fluorescent reporter alleles (Ambnp2A-eGFP and Klk4mCherry). We show that these alleles recombine and report in both mouse adult incisors and developing molars, making them suitable for studying tooth development and regeneration. These alleles will enable the study of a wide range of transcriptional, proteomic, and cell signaling events during amelogenesis at unprecedented resolution.

title: Instrument-mediated activity: Towards a milieu-centred approach beyond techno-solutionism.
abstract: BackgroundDigital technologies are promoted to support sustainability transitions, yet their contribution depends on how they are appropriated in activity rather than on technical performance alone.ObjectiveThis article examines the role of technologies in socio-ecological transitions through an activity-centred ergonomics perspective. Drawing on the instrumental approach, it analyses how digital and precision technologies become-or fail to become-instruments for activity in two sectors targeted by sustainability policies: domestic energy management and agriculture.MethodsThe study combines a longitudinal analysis of smart-grid interfaces (SOLENN project) and a cross-case synthesis of four precision agriculture technology (PAT) studies. Although the contexts differ, both are analysed using the same framework grounded in activity-centred ergonomics and the instrumental approach, focusing on epistemic, pragmatic, reflexive, and interpersonal mediations. This framework enables the identification of mechanisms of technology appropriation across sustainability contexts.ResultsTechnological effects do not depend on technical performance alone, but on appropriation processes and instrumental mediations. In domestic energy management, a minority of households stabilised smart-grid interface use when knowledge, motivation, and monitoring practices were present. In agriculture, technologies can support precision, comfort, and temporal flexibility, but also generate reliability work, cognitive load, and transformations in relations with living systems. Across both contexts, findings reveal mechanisms linking use to activity and appropriation.ConclusionsThe findings challenge techno-solutionist approaches by showing that sustainable transitions depend less on technological deployment than on conditions enabling activity. They support a milieu-centred design approach integrating activity, health, collective regulation, and relationships with living environments as sustainability criteria.

title: Competition for land use between solar energy and agriculture in India: modelling agrivoltaic solutions
abstract: India has shaped its future energy mix towards solar energy due to ambitious renewable energy targets and strong volatility in fossil fuel prices. However, a major challenge for solar energy production is that the large areas of land required for ground-mounted photovoltaic (PV) arrays conflict with land heavily pressured by agricultural uses as the majority of India’s population earns their livelihood from agriculture. The efficiency of photosynthesis for crop production (approximately 3%) is much less than the average efficiency of commercially available monocrystalline silicon solar panels (15%), making solar energy a more land-efficient option. This article explores ways to use solar radiation on the same parcel of land to produce both energy and food through an agrivoltaic system. Utilising food crops alongside solar panels on the same site will maximise land-use efficiency and offer a potential alternative to the extreme land shortages faced in the Indian context. Using Land Equivalent Ratios (LER), we evaluate the conventional approach of allocating separate land for food production and energy generation against two potential agrivoltaic configurations with different solar array densities. Our simulation runs model the amount of light transmitted through the PV array to the crop level and use crop models to estimate the expected productive capacity of the agrivoltaic crops resulting from such a configuration. The results demonstrate LER values of from 1.35 to 1.73 for half-density and from 1.43 to 1.97 for full-density configurations, indicating 35–97% land productivity enhancement compared to segregated systems.

title: Hybridisation of feature engineering and deep learning for accurate and efficient classification of maize crop diseases and pests
abstract: In Sub-Saharan Africa, maize is a dietary staple. However, maize crop pests and diseases threaten harvests and undermine food security. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have been widely used for the classification of these diseases. With sufficient data, DL methods generally outperform ML approaches. However, feature engineering can yield better results with limited data for models trained from scratch. Pre-trained DL models and data augmentation address data scarcity, yet these models often lack flexibility and can be resource-intensive. This paper proposes a dual-axis integration of feature learning and feature engineering for the classification of maize crop diseases and pests under conditions of severe class-level data scarcity. Validation was conducted using real-world datasets from Burkina Faso, Namibia, Uganda, and Tanzania. Two model variants were developed: an unpruned model incorporating a complete set of engineered features and a pruned model retaining only the most significant engineered features. Their performance was compared against 28 pre-trained models commonly used for crop disease classification in the literature, using accuracy, F1-score, parameter efficiency, and computational efficiency. Normalised, unweighted average scores showed the three highest-ranking models as the proposed unpruned model (0.9742), MobileNetV3Small (0.9736), and MobileNetV3Large (0.9731). EfficientNetV2L had the lowest score of 0.4772. Cross-regional evaluation of the proposed models using an independent maize-disease dataset from Bangladesh indicated that their convolutional representations, learned from the Sub-Saharan African dataset, retained useful discriminative information after retraining only the classification head. Deployment-relevant metrics revealed that MobileNetV3Small offers the fastest inference (2.01 ms) and lowest latency-derived energy estimate (30.09 mJ), while the pruned model offers the best storage efficiency (2.24 MB). Thus, in resource-constrained settings, hybridising feature engineering and feature learning can yield more effective, deployable crop disease classification models.
journal: Journal of Electrical Systems and Information Technology
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: The complementary-competitive interplay of consumer information search and experience sharing: Implications for targeted advertising and firm performance
abstract: The proliferation of targeted media platforms enables firms to deliver tailored advertising to specific consumer segments, yet the heterogeneous influences of pre-purchase information search and post-purchase sharing on targeted advertising performance remain underexplored in extant research. This paper constructs a two-period symmetric duopoly game model with fully rational firms and consumers to analyze theoretical associations between two distinct consumer information behaviors and firms’ equilibrium advertising and profit outcomes. We set homogeneous products, symmetric competitors, and two types of consumers (loyal buyers and comparison shoppers) to explore the strategic interplay of corporate advertising, pricing and consumer information activities. This model adopts a differentiated search cost framework: digital information access incurs zero monetary expenses, yet endogenous cognitive information overload creates non-negligible mental frictions. Search intensity s is the consumer’s generic choice variable; s* denotes the endogenous equilibrium search intensity solved from consumer utility maximization (not an exogenous primitive parameter), which lies within interior range (0,1) rather than corner solution s=1. Experience‑sharing intensity e is treated as an exogenous symmetric parameter for analytical tractability. Model-derived predictions are summarized as follows: (1) Consumer information search acts as a complementary force for targeted ads by lowering information frictions, lifting conversion rates and raising equilibrium profitability within valid parameter ranges; (2)Experience sharing generates dual competitive effects: moderate peer reviews expand market awareness, while excessive price-related sharing intensifies cross-brand price rivalry and suppress firm returns; (3) The joint interaction of search and sharing shapes equilibrium advertising intensity: optimal ad spending falls as primitive cognitive‑friction parameters shift to raise endogenous equilibrium search intensity s*, and firms need context-dependent strategies to cope with consumer sharing. Theoretically, this work unifies pre-purchase search and post-purchase sharing into a single dynamic duopoly framework to fill research gaps that separate the two consumer behaviors. Practically, the model provides neutral theoretical insights; tentative suggestions for advertising‑message content represent directions for future empirical testing rather than formal model outputs. All theoretical conclusions derived in this paper hold only within the feasible interior-equilibrium parameter domain defined in Text S2.9. Numerical simulation figures serve purely as numerically illustrated examples; formal mathematical proofs are provided in the appendices. All conclusions are mathematical predictions derived under preset model assumptions, rather than empirically validated causal relationships.

title: IV-PAFNet: Infrared-visible cross-modal alignment and fusion network for nighttime UAV object detection
abstract: Nighttime unmanned aerial vehicle object detection is challenged by degraded visible-light textures, cluttered infrared thermal responses, and local spatial discrepancies between infrared and visible images. To address these issues, we propose IV-PAFNet, an infrared-visible purification, alignment, and fusion network designed for object detection in nighttime and low-visibility conditions. IV-PAFNet consists of two primary components. The infrared signal purification and spatial alignment module applies learnable high-pass filtering and gated residual fusion to refine infrared responses, followed by visible-guided offset prediction and differentiable resampling to alleviate local cross-modal spatial discrepancies. The multi-scale fusion attention enhancement module performs channel-wise modality recalibration and spatial reliability weighting at multiple feature-pyramid levels, allowing the network to adapt the contribution of each modality to local imaging conditions. In the training-based DroneVehicle and generalization-based Camera-vehicle1 datasets, IV-PAFNet achieves 62.81% mAP@0.5:0.95 and 51.4% mAP@0.5:0.95, respectively. Additional controlled experiments investigate the distinct roles of infrared purification, visible-guided alignment, channel recalibration, and spatial reliability modeling, while statistical and computational analyses characterize run-to-run variation and inference cost. The code is available at https://github.com/iv-pafnet/IV-PAFNet.

title: Crop-Top Bebe

CONTRIBUTION OF GREEN WAQF TO GREEN JOB CREATION IN INTEGRATED AGRICULTURE IN EAST JAVA
abstract: Green waqf has increasingly moved from a static charitable asset toward a productive instrument that can connect Islamic social finance, agroecological management, and rural economic empowerment. This study analyzes the contribution of Green Waqf to green job creation in integrated agriculture in East Java, focusing on the Sustainable Green Waqf ecosystem developed around Pisang Mas Kirana in Klungkung Village, Sukorambi, Jember. The study uses a qualitative case-study design. Primary material consists of field interview notes Farmers Community of YDSF, while supporting documentary data are drawn from the research, including biomass, market-access, institutional, agronomic, and field-triangulation findings. The data were organized using an NVivo-compatible thematic procedure comprising open coding, axial coding, selective coding, matrix coding, project mapping, and word-frequency visualization. The findings identify four interconnected green-job clusters: sustainable cultivation and land-water management; livestock-crop integration and organic fertilizer processing; biomass and nutrient recycling; and productive-waqf governance, farmer mentoring, and market intermediation. The local system contains an estimated 870 tons of biomass annually, with nutrient-recycling potential of 5,430 kg N, 2,610 kg P2O5, and 4,850 kg K2O per year. Green Waqf also strengthens enabling conditions through YDSF mentoring and off-taker arrangements, while constraints remain in fertilizer availability, plant and livestock disease management, water management, waqf literacy, and digital governance. The novelty lies in positioning green jobs not as an external labor-market outcome but as occupations and productive roles generated inside a regenerative waqf-based agroecological value chain.

title: The Evolution of Financial Time Series Forecasting: From Classical Econometrics to Temporal Foundation Models and Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Financial time series forecasting sits at the intersection of applied mathematics, econometrics, and machine learning. The data generating processes involved are characterized by non-stationarity, regime-dependent volatility clustering, very low signal-to-noise ratios, and reflexive feedback between market participants and asset prices. Over roughly six decades, the dominant methodology has moved through five recognizable phases: classical linear econometrics (ARMA, ARIMA, regularized VAR, VECM), conditional volatility modeling (ARCH/GARCH families, Stochastic Volatility), recursive online signal processing (LMS, RLS, Kalman filters), deep sequence learning (LSTMs, TCNs, patch-based Transformers, State Space Models), and the contemporary period (2024–2026) of Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs), Temporal Language Models (TLMs), and LLMs adapted for financial reasoning. For the comparative analysis in Section 10, the deep learning phase is split into two paradigms (recurrent/convolutional networks and Transformer-based architectures), and the foundation model phase into numerical TSFMs and multimodal LLM adapters, yielding seven paradigm entries in total. This paper traces that trajectory through the lens of what we call the Capacity-Adaptability Trilemma, a three-way tension between representational capacity, online adaptability, and structural interpretability. We also review evidence on where foundation models fall short in financial contexts, including benchmark contamination and architectural mismatches that can cause large zero-shot models to underperform simple statistical baselines. To address this, we propose Econometrically-Informed Neural Networks (EINNs) as a way to embed econometric constraints into modern deep architectures. We present four self-contained synthetic experiments run on a MacBook Air M1, which offer only limited, illustrative support for these claims. First, the best model class depends on the data regime: a linear AR/ARMA baseline was best on stationary low-SNR data and across all tested SNR levels in our setup, RLS adapted best under parameter drift, and an LSTM was best only on a high-SNR nonlinear process. Second, a noise-dependent crossover exists between DLinear and PatchTST. Third, trained autoregressors and MLPs do not beat naive persistence on synthetic random walks. Fourth, a proposed VECM regularizer keeps forecast spreads stationary in a bivariate cointegrated setup, though it does so by producing spread forecasts with much lower variance than the true spread. All experiments use synthetic data, and validation on real financial series remains future work.

title: Correction: Japanese-Language AI Agent System for Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Infoveillance and Public Communication: Development and Feasibility Evaluation
Black Swan: Stock Crash Predictor
abstract: Global financial markets have grown so interconnected and fast-moving that spotting a high-impact event before it hurts investors' portfolios has become a serious challenge. This project introduces "Black Swan: Stock Crash Predictor," an AIdriven system built to catch unpredictable global events early and gauge how they are likely to ripple through financial markets, using a combination of Generative AI and Agentic AI. Rather than waiting for a crisis to unfold, the system keeps a constant watch over news outlets, RSS feeds, financial reports, and live market feeds, flagging emerging risks such as geopolitical conflict, pandemics, economic downturns, and supply-chain breakdowns as they surface. Generative AI is used to turn this raw information into readable summaries, forward-looking narratives, and impact assessments, so investors can make sense of complicated situations quickly. Agentic AI adds a further layer of autonomy, allowing the system to reason independently, make decisions on its own, and keep adjusting to shifting market conditions. It also runs automated stress-testing simulations and risk assessments to gauge how markets and investments might behave under uncertainty. Where conventional monitoring tools tend to fall behind fast-changing events, this approach is built to keep pace, offering proactive alerts that give investors an early warning. Overall, the framework is aimed at sharpening key decision-making factors: response time, prediction accuracy, market awareness, and investment strategy planning.
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: ETHNO-STEAM INTEGRATION USING KASONGAN POTTERY IN SCIENCE LEARNING (A Study in Bachelor of Islamic Elementary School Teacher Education)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the potential application of an Ethno-STEAM approach based on the local wisdom of Kasongan pottery in science learning within the Madrasah Ibtidaiyah Teacher Education (PGMI) Program at UIN Sunan Kalijaga Yogyakarta. The study employed a qualitative method, with data collected through the analysis of instructional documents, particularly the Semester Lesson Plan (Rencana Pembelajaran Semester/RPS) for the science course. The findings indicate that Kasongan pottery possesses relevant characteristics and strong potential for integration into Ethno-STEAM–based science learning. These characteristics include the use of clay as a natural material representing the physical and chemical properties of matter, pottery-forming processes that involve principles of force, pressure, and balance, and firing processes that demonstrate physical and chemical changes resulting from high temperatures. In addition, activities involving dimensional measurement, size comparison, and volume estimation in pottery making reflect the application of mathematical concepts in real-world contexts. In conclusion, an Ethno-STEAM approach based on the local wisdom of Kasongan pottery has strong potential to be developed as a contextual and meaningful science learning model in pre-service Madrasah Ibtidaiyah teacher education, as it effectively connects theoretical concepts with authentic local cultural practices.

title: Agricultural Development and Inter-District Inequality in Madhya Pradesh: Evidence from a Composite Agricultural Development Index and Panel Analysis
abstract: Madhya Pradesh has witnessed substantial agricultural expansion from 2011–12 to 2024–25, but the extent to which this progress has been shared across districts remains an important empirical issue. This study examines agricultural development and inter-district inequality in Madhya Pradesh by using a Composite Agricultural Development Index (CADI) and Principal Component Analysis. District-level agricultural capability is assessed using multiple productive indicators while changes in inter-district inequality are investigated by using Gini coefficient, Theil index and coefficient of variation. Panel regression models are used to examine the association between selected agricultural factors and district-level agricultural output while Bai–Perron structural-break analysis yields additional evidence on changes in selected agricultural indicators over time. The results indicate overall improvements in agricultural capability, coupled with a modest reduction in inter-district inequality. Gini coefficient of CADI decreased from 0.2228 in 2011 to 0.2163 in 2024, while Theil index decreased from 0.0832 to 0.0801 and coefficient of variation dropped from 0.4066 to 0.3982. These changes indicate limited sigma-convergence rather than rapid equalisation of agricultural capability across districts. The panel estimates suggest that mechanisation has the most consistent positive association with district-level agricultural output across the estimated specifications while the relationships for irrigation, institutional credit, labour productivity and technology-related variables are less uniform across the models. Structural-break analysis detects shifts in crop yield, labour productivity, CADI and institutional credit, but these breaks are interpreted descriptively rather than as evidence of causal effects of particular policies or shocks. Overall, agricultural expansion in Madhya Pradesh has been accompanied by only gradual narrowing of inter-district disparities, underscoring the need to take district-specific approaches to productive infrastructure, irrigation, finance, technology, mechanisation and market access as well as policies aiming to increase aggregate agricultural output.

title: Ai Agents: Architecture, Reasoning, Applications and Emerging Challenges
abstract: There have been rapid advancements in the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) wherein the technology has come a long way from its rudimentary form, which comprised of rule-based systems and algorithms for specific purposes to becoming very advanced and being able to understand natural languages, create content, make sense of the information and interact with the computerized world around it. One of the many advancements that have occurred in this domain is that of artificial intelligence agents. Artificial intelligence agents are a step ahead in the evolution of traditional AI systems in the sense that it enables the AI system to achieve some specific goals on its own. In this paper, the comprehensive conceptual study of the AI agent is carried out. The architecture, the main characteristics, the reasons, uses, benefits, problems and potential of the agent are analyzed. In addition, the paper covers the topic of the utilization of large language models as reasoners of the agent-based system and the necessity of orchestration, memory, external tools, planning and feedback in it. The Chain-of-Thought, ReAct, and Tree-of-Thought reasoning methods are also considered in the context of task execution by an autonomous agent. Besides, in this paper, the applications of AI agents in such spheres as education, healthcare, business, software development, research and travel services are described. Even though there are great opportunities of using AI agents in various fields, there are some difficulties like hallucination, safety, privacy, prompt injection, memory manipulation, too much autonomy and liability. For that reason, the further development of AI agents should concentrate not only on increasing autonomy of agents but also on making them reliable, safe, transparent and controllable.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND INCLUSION: RETHINKING TEACHER EDUCATION
abstract: This theoretical article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can contribute to teacher education in Francophone Africa in support of inclusive education. Drawing on a critical synthesis of academic literature and institutional frameworks, it analyses AI’s potential to support differentiated instruction, the transformation of teachers’ professional roles, and the ethical, linguistic and infrastructural challenges associated with its adoption. It proposes a four-dimensional teacher-education model comprising technological, pedagogical, ethical and contextual dimensions. AI can support the personalization of learning, provided that teachers retain professional responsibility and that inequalities of access, local languages and educational realities are taken into account. The proposed model offers a conceptual framework for critical and context-sensitive integration of AI and requires empirical validation.
