title: When Should AI Decide, Defer, and Deviate? Responsible Automation for Deceased Donor Kidney Allocation
abstract: We ask when an AI trained on historical decisions should be allowed to recommend decisions, defer to human experts, or in other cases, flag concerning patterns in data and deviate from past practice. This can be challenging because past decisions record what was done rather than what should have been done, and where data is sparse, a model's predictions may be too uncertain to act on. We provide a framework for addressing this problem using a case study in deceased-donor kidney allocation. Nearly 30% of kidneys recovered from deceased donors in the United States are never transplanted, largely because they are hard to place through the standard waitlist sequence. One can use AI to flag kidneys at risk of delayed or failed placement for out-of-sequence (OOS) allocation, but this comes at the cost of bypassing candidates higher on the waitlist. Thus, OOS allocation should only be used when the organ is demonstrably at high risk of discard on the standard sequence. Using Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network match-run data from 2016-2019 and 2023-2025 (excluding COVID-19-disrupted years), we build the Arbitrator framework, which combines various interpretable models and acts only when the uncertainty in their predictions cannot change the preferred action. Our Arbitrator resolves 93.5% of organ placement decisions using explicit medical criteria learned from data, and defers the remaining 6.5% to a human or a more complex model. We show that the Arbitrator correctly identifies 70.1% of historically discarded low-KDPI kidneys as OOS candidates, projecting that up to 43.9% of historically discarded kidneys could be flagged for expedited placement and potentially transplanted. We then exploit the interpretability of the Arbitrator to create an agentic audit comparing the learned rules to published clinical literature in order to flag decision-making patterns that are contentious.

title: Reinforcement Learning for the Game of Balatro: A Fast Simulator and Two-Policy Training Approach
abstract: Balatro, a 2024 roguelike deckbuilder, presents three difficulties that have historically derailed reinforcement learning methods: a 3,000-action state-dependent action space, horizons of several hundred decisions with sparse rewards, and pervasive stochasticity in both card draws and shop generation. Published RL results on the game remain scarce. We introduce an end-to-end pipeline comprising (i) a high-throughput Rust simulator that is automatically state-diffed against the live game client via BalatroBot, (ii) a condensed observation-action interface with dynamic per-step masking of legal moves, and (iii) a multi-agent PPO architecture that decomposes play into a tactical blind policy and a strategic shop policy that share the full game state but act in disjoint phases. Long-horizon credit assignment is partially addressed by per-agent reward routing with explicit cross-agent credit. On the main joint run, training metrics show a sharp phase transition in which the first-blind clear rate converges above 99% and mean episode return increases by roughly an order of magnitude, plateauing at a mean maximum ante of 3 out of 8; single-agent baselines under identical rewards oscillated between greedy and hoarding failure modes and did not stably clear the first blind. These results establish the two-policy decomposition as a strong reactive baseline for Balatro and localise the remaining gap to long-horizon strategic planning rather than tactical blind play.

title: Intelligent Agriculture for Plant Disease Management: A Critical Review of Operational Value, Field Reliability, Adoption Barriers, and Research Priorities
abstract: Plant disease management increasingly integrates artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT) sensing, remote and proximal sensing, disease forecasting, robotics, cloud–edge computing, and decision-support systems (DSS). This critical narrative review evaluated their operational value, reliability under production conditions, barriers to adoption, and priorities for improving field performance. An initial 99-record bibliography was screened, yielding 45 eligible sources; targeted searches of DOI/indexing services and publisher databases from 2010 to July 2026, while retaining earlier foundational studies, identified 35 additional DOI-verified sources, producing an 80-reference corpus. Evidence was appraised across five deployment-oriented domains: field representativeness, diagnostic ground truth, comparator quality, uncertainty and failure reporting, and operational outcomes. Intelligent tools provide three main benefits: earlier or more scalable detection, continuous and spatially explicit risk assessment, and targeted intervention. Field evidence is strongest for established disease-warning systems and selected precision-spraying applications, whereas image classifiers, foundation models, and autonomous robots remain more commonly validated in curated or crop-specific settings. Distribution shift is a major reliability concern, with commercial-field studies showing substantial performance losses under open-set conditions. Wider adoption is constrained by interoperability, cost, maintenance, connectivity, data governance, trust, liability, and unequal access. The most credible near-term pathway is supervised, context-sensitive autonomy. Future progress requires multi-farm and multi-season validation, explicit uncertainty reporting, FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) data architectures, economic evaluation, climate-adaptive hybrid models, and end-to-end comparisons with best conventional practice. Intelligent agriculture should therefore be developed as accountable plant-health infrastructure that keeps plant pathologists, advisers, and farmers in the decision loop.

title: CROSS-DISCIPLINARY ANALYSIS OF DIGITAL MARKETING FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS UNDER THE THREE-DIMENSIONAL FRAMEWORK OF INFORMATION CREDIBILITY, LEGAL COMPLIANCE, AND BRAND VALUE: A CASE STUDY OF YUNNAN SMALL-LOT COFFEE
abstract: The digital transformation of agricultural marketing has emerged as a critical pathway for rural revitalization and high-quality agricultural development in China. However, existing research often examines digital marketing strategies from a single disciplinary perspective, neglecting the intricate interplay among information credibility, legal compliance, and brand value. This paper proposes a three-dimensional analytical framework—Information Credibility, Legal Compliance, and Brand Value (ILCB)—that integrates insights from information science, regulatory law, and marketing management to examine digital marketing practices for agricultural products. Drawing on signaling theory, institutional theory, and brand equity theory, this study employs a qualitative case study approach to investigate Yunnan small-lot coffee, one of China’s most geographically indicated agricultural products with rapidly growing digital market presence. The analysis reveals that: (1) information transparency mechanisms, including traceability systems and content marketing, significantly enhance consumer trust and purchase intention; (2) legal compliance frameworks, particularly food safety regulations and geographical indication protection, serve as foundational institutional safeguards that reduce information asymmetry; and (3) regional brand value is co-constructed through the synergistic interaction of credible information delivery and regulatory adherence. The study contributes to the literature by offering an integrated cross-disciplinary framework that explains how digital marketing outcomes for agricultural products are shaped by the convergence of technological, legal, and market forces. Practical implications for policymakers, platform operators, and agricultural enterprises are discussed, emphasizing the need for coordinated governance that aligns information disclosure standards, regulatory enforcement, and brand development strategies.
journal: Global Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Extension Design for the Use of a Mobile Application for Oil Palm Harvest Recording in Laut Tador District, Batu Bara Regency
abstract: Harvest recording supports transparent oil palm production reporting for Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO) certification. However, smallholders in Laut Tador District, Batu Bara Regency, continue to rely on simple manual systems that may expose harvest data to loss. This study developed an agricultural extension design for a mobile harvest-recording application and assessed its acceptance, behavioural outcomes, and continued application use. A quantitative descriptive approach was employed, with data collected through interviews and questionnaires and analysed using extension planning procedures and Likert-scale scoring. Regional potential identification informed a design specifying objectives, target participants, content, methods, media, session volume, location, timing, and costs. The objectives followed SMART and ABCD principles, with a target achievement level of 60%. Overall acceptance of the extension design reached 86.1%. Evaluation results were 80.9% for knowledge, 78.86% for attitudes, 67% for skills, and 30.4% for continued application use. These findings indicate strong acceptance of the extension design alongside limited sustained use of the application. The study provides an extension design tailored to local conditions and highlights continued assistance as a priority for translating acceptance into routine digital harvest recording and strengthening the transparency of production reporting.

title: Assessing the Influence of Land Use Change Pattern and Soil Erosion on Sediment Delivery Ratio in the Upper Mahaweli River Catchment of Sri Lanka
abstract: The Mahaweli River takes in the largest volume of water amounting to one seventh of Sri Lanka’s total runoff and has a catchment area that covers 15 % of the land in the country. A number of multipurpose reservoirs have been stored in the Upper Mahaweli River Catchment (UMRC) mainly to generate hydropower, which contributes to about 40-50% of the total hydropower production in the country. This study investigates the impacts of land use change patterns and soil erosion on the sediment delivery ratio (SDR) within the UMRC in Sri Lanka. Utilizing Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing (RS) tools, the land use and land cover (LULC) changes were analyzed over a period from 2007 to 2023, focusing on soil erosion's contribution to sediment dynamics in the basin. By employing the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE) model, factors such as rainfall erosivity, soil erodibility, slope characteristics, crop cover, and land management practices were assessed to estimate soil loss and map erosion hotspots. The InVEST SDR model was then applied to quantify sediment transport and deposition patterns, helping to identify priority areas for soil conservation. Results revealed an average annual soil loss ranging from 0 to 95.015 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ in the catchment and a mean annual sediment export of 5.56 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. It shows mean sediment deposition rate as 2.4 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. Erosion severity was classified into five hazard classes, very low (0 - 5 t ha-1 yr-1), low (5 - 10 t ha-1 yr -1), moderate (10 - 20 t ha-1 yr-1), high (20 - 50 t ha-1 yr-1) and very high ( >50 t ha-1 yr -1). A critical 1.5% area was identified as a considerable soil erosion hazard area, necessitating urgent measures for erosion control. Findings indicate significant LULC changes, driven primarily by deforestation, agricultural expansion, and urbanization, which have intensified mean soil erosion rate from 2.39 t ha-1 yr-1to 11.22 t ha-1 yr-1, highest mean sediment export rate as 2.29 t ha-1 yr-1 and highest mean sediment deposition rate as 5.36 t ha-1 yr-1 in different watersheds. Importantly, the identified erosion hotspots and sediment export zones indicate a substantial risk of accelerated sedimentation in downstream reservoirs, potentially reducing storage capacity and affecting hydropower efficiency in the Upper Mahaweli system. These findings support targeted watershed management interventions to mitigate long-term sedimentation impacts.

title: Geospatial Quantification of Human–Elephant Conflict Hotspots in the Southern Western Ghats
abstract: Human–elephant conflict (HEC) in the Southern Western Ghats has significant socio-economic and ecological impacts, highlighting the need for an integrated mitigation approach. The present study leverages a geo-tagged database of 1,22,986 HEC incidents from 2019 to 2023 sourced from the e-Parihara web portal, Karnataka Forest Department (KFD), to analyse conflict patterns, damage types, and compensation trends across eight districts of Karnataka. Kodagu became the district with the highest number of cases and compensation, highlighting the need for targeted interventions. The study distinguishes between districts within the Western Ghats and those outside, such as Mandya and Ramanagara, to understand the geographical and ecological aspects of HEC dynamics. A significant increase in HEC cases and compensation was observed during the study period, with the number of cases rising from 8,184 in 2019 to 30,912 in 2023, while compensation payments increased from ₹53.7 million to ₹390.4 million over the same period. As a result, a total of ₹1,050.5 million was spent on compensation during the 2019–2023 period. The damage was categorised into six types: plantation damage, crop loss, property damage, human injury and death, livestock kills, and other damages. A total of 1,998 conflict-prone villages were identified and classified into five categories: Very High (26.1%), High (35.4%), New/Emerging Hotspots (9.4%), Sporadic Hotspots (19.2%), and Cold Spots (9.9%). This classification aids in prioritising mitigation efforts, particularly in high and emerging hotspots, to prevent further escalation. The study aligns with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) 2023 HEC mitigation guidelines, emphasising the implementation of early warning and rapid response systems. The village-level hotspot database serves as a strategic tool for conflict mitigation, supporting targeted habitat management and policy interventions to reduce human–wildlife conflict in the Southern Western Ghats.

title: IoT-Based Smart Farm Protection and AI Crop Disease Detection System
abstract: Crop damage caused by unwanted animals and the difficulty of identifying crop diseases at an early stage are two common problems faced by farmers. This paper proposes the IoT-Based Smart Farm Protection and AI Crop Disease Detection System, a low-cost smart agriculture system that addresses both problems through a single web platform. For farm protection, a copper wire arrangement installed around the farm boundary acts as the sensing element; when an animal touches it, an ESP32/Arduino-class microcontroller detects the contact and activates a buzzer, and the farmer can turn the buzzer OFF remotely through the website. For crop health monitoring, a camera captures an image of a crop leaf, and an AI/ML-based image classification model identifies the possible disease, which is displayed on the website. The proposed classifier is a lightweight convolutional neural network (MobileNetV2, transfer learning) to be trained on the public PlantVillage leaf image dataset. The web application provides homepage, admin and farmer modules, and a MySQL database stores user, farm and crop details, intrusion alerts, buzzer control records and disease detection results. The system is organized into six modules: homepage, admin login, farmer login, crop disease detection, farm protection and database design. This paper presents the proposed architecture, methodology and planned evaluation; the system is at the design stage, all modules are described as proposed, and no experimental results are claimed
journal: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology

title: Domestic Resource Mobilization & Fiscal Probity: Antidote for Bridging Liberia’s Fiscal Gap in the wake of the Dwindling of Donor Aid to Liberia
abstract: Liberia has long depended on foreign assistance or aid to complement its domestic resources to deliver on its evolving complex development priorities and needs. The decline in foreign aid poses major challenges which can be surmounted through effective domestic resource mobilization strategy and fiscal probity. This research paper aims to provide antidotes to strengthen Liberia’s ongoing domestic resource mobilization efforts and strategies to adequately bridge its fiscal gap arising from the plummeting of donor aid to Liberia. A mixed method of research designs was adopted for this study. The paper was developed from secondary data extracted from reports and studies on domestic resource mobilization, case studies, and primary data obtained through interviews with tax experts and practitioners from Liberia. The paper found that Tunisia, Seychelles, Morocco, South Africa and Senegal have sustainably mobilized domestic revenues through effective DRM strategies, including tax administration modernization and digitalization, economic diversification, broadening of tax base, transparency and fiscal governance, and effective tax audit programs. Liberia’s potential to accrue more domestic resources lies in exploring its mining sector, biodiversity and ecotourism, agricultural value chains, informal economic sector, tax administration modernization, and specialized tax compliance audit programs. These findings can support Liberia’s ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development and reduce dependence on foreign aid.
journal: Journal of Economic Development and Village Building

title: Image-Based Soil Nutrient Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
abstract: Recent advances in precision agriculture have enabled the use of machine learning and image processing for rapid soil nutrient assessment. This study presents a non-destructive approach for estimating soil nutrient content from digital soil images captured using a camera and analyzed through specialized software. A dataset of 1,500 soil images was processed using color correction, noise reduction, and feature extraction techniques to improve data quality. Five machine learning models, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and a Stacking Regressor, were evaluated for predicting nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based deep learning model was served as a benchmark. No single model was best for every nutrient and metric. For nitrogen, GBM achieved the lowest test MAE (0.1652), whereas the Stacking Regressor achieved the highest test R² (0.9886). For potassium, Random Forest achieved the lowest test MAE (0.0051), whereas XGBoost achieved the highest test R² (0.9999). For phosphorus, XGBoost achieved both the lowest test MAE (0.1558) and the highest test R² (0.9929). Thus, the best-performing model depends on the nutrient and evaluation metric. Further validation using independent field datasets is required to establish robustness under diverse environmental conditions.

title: Model Terpadu Pemberdayaan Desa Berbasis Green Economy melalui Hilirisasi Nilam dan Perlebahan di Desa Lambadeuk, Aceh Besar
abstract: Lambadeuk Village, Aceh Besar Regency, possesses patchouli and linot (stingless bee) honey potential that remains underutilized for economic value addition. Partner groups face challenges such as limited processing technology, absent SOPs, low capacity, weak business governance, and restricted market access. This community initiative aims to establish a green economy-based empowerment model through appropriate technology, capacity building, and product downstreaming. Carried out with the Benteng Makmur Farmer Group and KTH Lestari Alam, activities employed a participatory method spanning problem identification to evaluation. Benteng Makmur was facilitated with a stainless-steel steam distillation unit and patchouli processing SOPs, while KTH Lestari Alam received additional linot bee colonies and harvesting SOPs. The initiative improved community capacity, production self-reliance, and value-added opportunities. The added colonies are targeted to increase honey production by up to 50%, while the distillation unit underpins high-value patchouli oil development. Integrating appropriate technology, standardization, and green economy principles effectively supports sustainable village-level enterprises.

title: HOW DOES DIGITAL TWIN–BLOCKCHAIN INTEGRATION ENHANCE TRACEABILITY TRUST? A PHYSICAL–DIGITAL–TRUST TRIPLE MAPPING MODEL
abstract: Agricultural traceability increasingly combines digital twins with distributed ledgers, yet the two technologies are often treated as if co-deployment were enough to create trust. This paper challenges that assumption. It treats traceability trust as the result of three linked translations: physical events into a digital representation (representational fidelity), that representation into a tamper-evident record (evidential integrity), and the record into evidence that stakeholders can inspect and understand (verification confidence). Using affordance theory, signaling theory and the trust literature, the paper explains why these translations operate sequentially, why a weak translation can produce false assurance, and why consumers, firms and regulators attach different weights to the three qualities. Nine propositions and a focused research agenda follow from the argument. The contribution is a configurational account that connects traceability design to the judgments stakeholders make about provenance.

title: Digital Economy and Rural Industrial Integration in Ethnic Minority Areas of Sichuan: A Theoretical Analysis of Driving Mechanisms
abstract: Digital technologies can connect geographically dispersed rural producers with markets, but greater connectivity does not necessarily constitute industrial integration. Focusing on the ethnic minority areas of Sichuan, China, this paper examines how digitalization may transform separate activities in agriculture, processing, distribution, and services into coordinated economic relationships. Drawing on transaction cost economics and the literature on rural industrial integration, it develops a four-stage analytical framework: lowering information and transaction costs, improving cross-industry factor matching, coordinating agricultural value chains, and creating complementary value across industrial boundaries. The analysis distinguishes the potential benefits of digital technologies from the organizational conditions needed to realize them. It argues that infrastructure complementarities, production standards, contractual reliability, local capabilities, and benefit-sharing arrangements condition whether digital connections become durable industrial linkages. The framework offers a bounded theoretical interpretation of digital-driven rural industrial integration in mountainous ethnic minority areas and identifies questions for subsequent empirical research.
journal: International Journal of Social Sciences and Public Administration

title: DETERMINANTS FOR ADOPTION OF CLIMATE-SMART AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AMONG COMMERCIAL FARMERS IN BAUCHI STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: This study investigated the determinants for the adoption of Climate-Smart Agricultural (CSA) practices among commercial farmers in Bauchi State, Nigeria. The study was guided by two objectives, two research questions and two hypotheses. The population of the study consisted of eight hundred and fifty registered commercial farmers across Bauchi State's three agricultural zones. The sample size for the study was Two hundred and sixty-two commercial farmers from the twenty Local Government Areas of the State using multi – stage sampling technique. Data were collected through a structured four-point rating scale structured questionnaire which was developed and adopted. In order to find out the reliability of the instrument, a pilot test was conducted, from which a crombach alpha of 0.95 was obtained as the reliability coefficient. The data collected was analysed using mean and standard deviation and to answer the research questions and simple linear regression to test the null hypotheses at 0.05 level of significance. The findings revealed that weather information dissemination significantly influenced CSA adoption, with mobile applications serving as critical channel. Socio-economic factors demonstrated the strongest positive influence on adoption of climate-smart Agricultural practices among commercial farmers in Bauchi state, Nigeria. The study concluded that effective information dissemination and favorable socio-economic conditions, are essential for enhancing CSA adoption among commercial farmers in Bauchi State, Nigeria. Based on these findings, it was recommended that strengthening digital platforms for climate information dissemination, providing affordable credit and farmer-friendly subsidies, expanding extension services and institutional collaborations, and implementing demonstration farms will build farmers' confidence in risk-taking in the state.
journal: VUNOKLANG MULTIDISCIPLINARY JOURNAL OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY EDUCATION

title: Frequency-Domain Evaluation and Estimation of Semi-Markov Disease Natural History Models
abstract: Introduction: Natural history models must often be estimated from data that do not directly capture disease transitions. Semi-Markov processes let the risk of progression depend on the time spent in a health state, which Markov models need extra states to represent. Their limitation is computational: discretizing time introduces approximation error, and simulating individuals introduces Monte Carlo error and a non-differentiable calibration objective. Methods: We show that the model-implied prevalence, incidence and cause-specific mortality of a continuous-time semi-Markov model satisfy convolution equations that become a small linear system when Laplace-transformed. Solving it on a grid of complex frequencies and inverting with an accelerated Fourier series returns the targets without a time grid or Monte Carlo error, and yields exact first- and second-order derivatives for one additional linear solve each. These support Newton-type maximum likelihood estimation, gradient-informed Bayesian sampling, and local identifiability diagnostics. We apply our open-source implementation to a urinary bladder cancer model calibrated to SEER incidence and mortality by age and stage. Results: The method reproduced an independent implementation to within its accuracy (maximum relative difference 8x10-6) and evaluated all targets, their gradient, and their Hessian in 1.3, 2.5, and 9.1 milliseconds; a one-year-cycle cohort approximation deviated by up to 42% and a two-million-person microsimulation by up to 811%. Maximum likelihood and Bayesian estimates agreed, and second-order information showed that the aggregate targets constrain where individuals go from preclinical states far better than how long they stay. Early-stage incidence and mortality showed systematic misfit across age. Conclusions: The framework supplies existing calibration algorithms with fast, exact model evaluations and derivatives for models whose transition hazards depend on time in state rather than on age.

title: Closing the phenotyping gap: non-invasive electromagnetic induction enables high-throughput screening of crop root function in the field
Legal Pathways for Digital Empowerment of Rural Revitalization in Old Revolutionary Base Areas
abstract: Digital empowerment can provide important governance and legal support for rural revitalization in old revolutionary base areas. Yet wider network coverage or the launch of a digital platform should not, by itself, be treated as evidence that rule-of-law governance has been achieved. Many old revolutionary base areas are located in remote mountainous regions, where digital legal governance has developed slowly, infrastructure is not always fully used, and platforms can easily become little more than visible traces of administrative assessment. Whether digital empowerment is effective should instead be judged by more concrete questions: whether legal services respond to villagers’ needs, whether different groups can participate meaningfully, and whether disadvantaged residents have access to remedies. Three problems are especially prominent at present. The ownership and sharing of agricultural data remain unsettled; digital capacity in grassroots law enforcement and justice is still limited; and some groups, particularly older residents, do not receive sufficient information or protection of their data-related rights. This article therefore argues that technology should be placed within a legal framework rather than allowed to determine governance on its own. Data sharing should follow the Regulations on Government Data Sharing, information collection should comply with the Personal Information Protection Law, coordination and online case handling at the grassroots level should be improved, and participation and remedies for vulnerable groups should be made genuinely accessible. The Ma Xiwu judicial tradition may also be carried forward through forms such as online courts, but its continuation must be supported by institutions and procedures rather than by the mere existence of a platform.
journal: International Journal of Asian Social Science Research

title: A Lightweight Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Cyberattack Detection in Internet of Things Networks
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) networks introduces significant cybersecurity challenges because connected sensors, gateways, and embedded controllers operate with limited memory, processing capacity, and energy. Conventional intrusion detection solutions may impose computational costs that exceed the capabilities of these devices, while cloud-only analysis adds latency and creates privacy concerns. This narrative review develops a conceptual lightweight deep learning framework for real-time cyberattack detection at the IoT edge. The proposed architecture combines flow-based feature extraction, selective preprocessing, a compact one-dimensional convolutional network, calibrated risk scoring, and adaptive response at the gateway. It discusses feature selection, class imbalance, model compression, data drift, adversarial resilience, and deployment constraints. An illustrative design chart compares qualitative trade-offs between model classes; it does not represent measured experimental findings. The article outlines an evaluation protocol using reproducible train-test separation, device-aware latency measurement, and cross-dataset validation. The central conclusion is that practical reliability requires jointly optimizing detection quality, false-alarm burden, inference time, memory use, and operational maintainability rather than accuracy alone.

title: Evaluating Software Quality Through Automated Testing and Predictive Defect Detection Using Machine Learning
abstract: Software quality assurance increasingly depends on the ability to combine automated testing with data-driven estimates of defect risk. Conventional test suites reveal failures in executed scenarios but do not necessarily identify which untested changes are most likely to introduce faults. Machine learning models can prioritize code review and testing by learning associations between historical defect outcomes, code structure, change activity, and process characteristics. This narrative review synthesizes established research on software defect prediction and proposes a transparent evaluation framework integrating data preparation, temporal validation, calibrated prediction, risk-based test selection, and continuous monitoring. It distinguishes test effectiveness from model discrimination and emphasizes precision–recall analysis, operational cost, data leakage prevention, and human oversight. A conceptual graph illustrates how testing effort might be redistributed according to predicted risk; it does not represent measured experimental outcomes. The paper argues that machine learning should supplement rather than replace automated tests, and that deployment claims require prospective, project-specific evidence. Limitations include incomplete defect labels, shifting development practices, class imbalance, and uncertain cross-project transferability

title: Effectiveness of Minimum Support Price Policy for Oilseed Crops in Maharashtra, India
abstract: Minimum Support Price (MSP) is an agricultural price policy instrument intended to support farmers' price realisation and agricultural production. This study assessed the effectiveness of MSP for soybean, groundnut and sunflower in Maharashtra over 2014–15 to 2024–25. Using secondary data, compound annual growth rates and exponential trends were estimated for market arrivals and prices. Differences between market prices (MPs) and MSPs were examined, and multiple regression models were used to assess associations between production, MSP, MP and cultivated area. Soybean arrivals increased significantly by 7.76% annually, whereas groundnut arrivals declined by 4.75% and sunflower arrivals remained nearly unchanged, with growth of 0.03%. Market prices increased significantly for soybean (5.20%), groundnut (3.51%) and sunflower (5.72%) during the study period. Soybean market prices exceeded MSP in seven of the eleven years, compared with three years for groundnut. Sunflower market prices remained below MSP throughout the study period. Regression estimates indicated positive associations between MSP and production for soybean and groundnut at the 10% significance level, while the corresponding association was not statistically significant for sunflower. Cultivated area was positively associated with groundnut production at the 1% significance level and with sunflower production at the 10% level. Overall, the findings indicate crop-specific differences in observed price support and suggest the importance of effective procurement and market access for oilseed producers.

title: Growth and Instability in Blackgram Production in Karnataka and India: Trends in Area, Production and Productivity
abstract: Blackgram (Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper) is an important pulse crop in India, but its long-term production patterns differ between geographical regions. The present study analyses the growth and instability of area, production and productivity of blackgram (Vigna mungo) in India and Karnataka over a 25-year period from 1999–2000 to 2023–2024, using the compound annual growth rate (CAGR) and the Cuddy–Della Valle Index (CDVI). At the national level, blackgram showed positive trends in all three parameters. Area increased from 2.94 to 3.54 million hectares (CAGR 1.77%; CDVI 15.39%, medium instability). Production rose from 1.33 to 2.32 million tonnes (CAGR 3.59%; CDVI 19.07%), while productivity improved from 453 to 656 kg/ha (CAGR 1.79%; CDVI 11.08%, low instability). The pattern in Karnataka was contrasting. Area declined sharply from 131 thousand hectares in 1999–2000 to 48 thousand hectares in 2023–2024, a statistically significant negative CAGR of −3.53% (CDVI 17.20%). Productivity increased from 346 to 458 kg/ha (CAGR 3.61%, significant), whereas production showed no significant trend (CAGR 0.11%) and high instability (CDVI 40.62%). Linear, cubic and exponential trend models were compared to justify the use of the compound growth model. These findings indicate that national growth in blackgram has been supported by both area expansion and yield gains, whereas Karnataka faces a significant decline in area despite productivity gains and unstable production. Policy attention to area retention, irrigation access and the promotion of blackgram in pulse-based cropping systems is therefore warranted.

title: MGP_HNSC32: A H&E Morphology-Derived 32-Gene Prognostic Signature in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) exhibits substantial molecular and morphological heterogeneity, yet current morphology-based prognostic models often lack biological interpretability. We developed a transformer-based computational framework (CTransPath) to virtually predict gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images. Morphology-associated genes were identified from the TCGA-HNSC cohort, and a 32-gene morphology-guided prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) based on H&E-derived predicted gene expression was developed using Random Survival Forest and multivariable Cox regression modeling. In TCGA-HNSC, the MGP_HNSC32 risk score significantly stratified patients by progression-free interval (PFI; HR = 4.13, 95% CI: 2.84-6.02), overall survival (OS; HR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.78-3.29), and disease-specific survival (DSS; HR = 4.88, 95% CI: 2.95-8.06; all p < 0.001), and remained independently associated with prognosis after multivariable adjustment. High-risk tumors were enriched for cell cycle, E2F, MYC, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition pathways and displayed poorly differentiated histology with nuclear atypia and stromal desmoplasia. In contrast, low-risk tumors showed keratinizing morphology and immune-rich stroma, corresponding to differentiation- and metabolism-related transcriptional programs. In the independent HANCOCK cohort (n = 701), risk scores calculated entirely from H&E-derived predicted gene expression using the TCGA-derived coefficients and prespecified cutoff were associated with progression-free survival (HR = 1.40, 95% CI: 1.03-1.90, p = 0.034). However, the continuous risk score was not significantly associated with progression-free survival (HR = 1.001, 95% CI: 0.999-1.003, p = 0.328). MGP_HNSC32 links histomorphology to transcriptional programs and demonstrates preliminary prognostic associations using routine H&E images. The H&E-based gene-expression prediction component should be considered proof-of-concept, and further independent and prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Drought‐induced leaf senescence and regreening upon rewatering associated with chlorophyll metabolism in Kentucky bluegrass
abstract: Drought stress is a major factor limiting the quality and persistence of cool‐season turfgrass species by accelerating leaf senescence and reducing overall vigor. This study was conducted to examine physiological responses associated with drought‐induced leaf senescence and post‐drought regreening in Kentucky bluegrass ( Poa pratensis L.), with particular emphasis on chlorophyll metabolism. Plants of two cultivars, Baron and Bewitched, were grown under controlled environmental conditions and subjected to well‐watered control and drought stress treatments, with post‐drought rewatering. Physiological parameters such as turf quality, relative water content, chlorophyll fluorescence, and chlorophyll content were evaluated throughout drought and recovery. In addition, the activities of a chlorophyll degradation enzyme, pheophytinase (PPH), and a chlorophyll synthesis enzyme, porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), were measured in response to drought and rewatering to observe the effect of drought on chlorophyll metabolism and to determine which pathway plays a more important role. Drought stress caused leaf dehydration, chlorophyll loss, reduced photochemical efficiency, and lower turf quality in both cultivars, although these parameters recovered following rewatering. PPH activity increased significantly during prolonged drought stress, whereas PBGD activity did not change significantly under drought. During post‐drought recovery, PBGD activity increased, while PPH activity declined to non‐stress levels. The decline in chlorophyll during drought‐induced leaf senescence may be associated with enhanced chlorophyll degradation enzyme activity, whereas the regreening observed during rewatering is likely related to the resumption of chlorophyll synthesis. These findings provide insight into the physiological mechanisms controlling drought‐induced senescence and post‐stress recovery in turfgrass and may be useful for the development of drought‐tolerant cultivars.

title: Quantifying genetic and nongenetic improvement for grain yield in faba bean breeding
abstract: Faba Bean ( Vicia faba ) is a cool season legume crop, often grow as a rotation crop to improve sustainability of the farming systems. The Australian faba bean breeding program is publicly funded, with improving grain yield as a key breeding objective to increase grower profitability. In this study, we aimed to quantify the genetic and nongenetic improvement for grain yield using historical multi‐environment trial data collected from 2018 to 2024, comprising 1985 breeding lines evaluated in 158 field trials across 25 locations in southern Australia. Genetic gain estimates varied with the method used. Best linear unbiased estimates–based analyses showed negative gain with different breeding stages populations, whereas best linear unbiased prediction–based estimates indicated small but significant gains ranging from −1.6 to 7.8 kg/ha per cycle. With a subset data from 2020 to 2024 and pedigree information, genetic gain calculated via estimated breeding values–based method showed consistent positive gain across all populations, ranged from 7.6 to 15.3 kg/ha per cycle. Nongenetic trends estimated from check varieties (9 kg/ha/year) or using the single check PBA Samira (30 kg/ha/year) were positive but statistically insignificant. Environmental covariates analysis further suggested that water availability was the key driver of grain yield variation among breeding trials in faba bean. Despite the short timeframe, this study provided an evidence‐based evaluation of grain yield gain for the current breeding program and laid the foundation for future breeding program optimization.

title: Truncating leguminous fixation and post‐harvest scavenging: Two pathways for reducing nitrate leaching in potato rotations
abstract: Nitrate leaching from intensive potato production is a significant contributor to groundwater contamination and estuarine eutrophication in Atlantic Canada. This 5‐year study (2018–2023) evaluated two cover‐cropping strategies in a barley (Hordeum vulgare L.)–red clover (Trifolium pratense L.)–potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) rotation in Prince Edward Island: (1) mid‐season red clover termination followed by buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum Moench) seeding, and (2) winter rye (Secale cereale L.) established after potato harvest. Nitrate leaching was quantified using tile‐drain concentrations integrated with LEACHN‐modeled drainage. Introducing buckwheat reduced post‐potato nitrate leaching by 30.6% (p = 0.05) in 2019/20. The early termination of red clover truncated the biological N2 fixation period, fundamentally reducing the N pool available for mineralization and subsequent leaching. Conversely, winter rye acted through a traditional “Scavenging” pathway, reducing post‐harvest leaching by a pooled 37% (p = 0.02) through active N uptake (average 28 kg N ha−1). Neither strategy significantly impacted subsequent marketable potato yields. These results demonstrate that while winter rye is a robust scavenger of residual N, the early termination of leguminous forages to plant cover crops like buckwheat provides an effective “source‐control” intervention. Overall, both buckwheat and winter rye cover cropping strategies effectively mitigated nitrate leaching in this potato‐based rotation—through different mechanisms—and offered a practical framework for reducing the environmental footprint of potato production in humid, temperate regions.

title: UAV-based multispectral imaging and machine learning for characterizing herbicide injury and desiccant responses in field crops
abstract: Purpose Herbicides and desiccants are critical for weed control and harvest management; however, their efficacy varies across crop species, environments, and growing seasons. This study evaluated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral imaging combined with machine-learning (ML) as a non-destructive approach for quantifying herbicide injury and desiccation responses across Canadian Prairie agroecosystems. Methods Field trials were conducted from 2022 to 2024 at three sites in Alberta and Saskatchewanusing tame oat, oriental mustard, and lentil. Tame oat and oriental mustard were used as pseudo-weed models for wild oat and wild mustard, respectively. UAV multispectral imagery and concurrent ground-based visual ratings were collected from 0 to 21 days aftertreatment to characterize temporal crop responses. Six ML models were evaluated using UAV-derived vegetation indices. Results Ensemble models, including Gradient Boosting, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest, consistently demonstrated strong predictive performance, with site-specific coefficients of determination (R) of 66–90% in oat, 60–75% in mustard, and 43–96% in lentil. Multi-site models achieved R values of 65–83%; however, leave-one-site-out (LOSO) and leave-one-year-out (LOYO) validation for oat and mustard showed reduced predictive performance in independent environments, highlighting limitations in model transferability. Vegetation indices captured temporal herbicide injury and stress dynamics across crops, while area under the desiccation progress curve (AUDPC) analysis quantified lentil dry-down and differentiated desiccant performance. Pearson correlation analysis identified NDVI and NDGI indices strongly associated with visual injury ratings across crops and environments. NDVI showed the most consistent relationships in oat and mustard, whereas NDVI, NDGI, and VARI exhibited comparable relationships with lentil desiccation responses. Conclusion Overall, integrating UAV-based multispectral imaging, vegetation indices, ML, and AUDPC provides a scalable, objective, and non-destructive framework for evaluating herbicide injury and desiccant efficacy under variable field conditions.

Climate change impacts of recurring office fit-outs: a prospective life cycle assessment of circular economy-based improvements
abstract: Buildings with long service life are associated with recurring greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions arising from repeated activities such as refurbishments over time, which can significantly contribute to the cumulative climate change impact. In particular, multi-tenant office buildings, where fit-outs typically occur every 2–10 years, contribute approximately a quarter of GHG emissions over the building service life. This study applies prospective LCA (pLCA) to quantify the climate change impact over the service life of a tenanted office building and assesses the effect of circular economy (CE) strategies using time-differentiated analysis. In contrast to static life cycle assessment (LCA), this approach enables climate change impact assessment of future scenarios with changed processes to account for potential future emissions. An office fit-out case study in Aotearoa New Zealand was modelled using attributional LCA. The climate change impact was initially quantified using static LCA and hotspots were identified for applying CE strategies. Alternative CE strategies were then modelled using static LCA, related to maximising reuse, design for optimisation, and using low-impact materials. Then pLCA was conducted using the premise software to quantify the future climate change impact by analysing office fit-outs across four subsequent fit-out cycles at 10-year intervals, with and without implementation of CE strategies. In addition to the global future scenarios in premise, a national electricity decarbonisation pathway was included in the scenario modelling. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess the robustness to key assumptions in the evaluated CE strategies and use of alternative climate policy pathways. The static LCA results showed that office fit-outs in module B5 are dominated by GHG emissions arising from manufacture of materials and components. Implementing all the evaluated CE strategies can reduce the net climate change impact of a single office fit-out - modelled using static LCA - by 17%. However, when modelled using pLCA, the net climate change impact of the final office fit-out is reduced by 56% relative to the same office fit-out modelled using static LCA. The study shows that pLCA enables a more comprehensive evaluation of future GHG emissions associated with recurring fit-outs in office buildings, and the future mitigation potential of CE strategies that target current GHG emission hotspots. Through the incorporation of prospective background data, the results capture potential future technological, socio-economic, and climate policy developments that are not represented in static LCA.
journal: The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment

title: Digital cues for refillable packaging adoption: how sustainability framing and visible social endorsement shape consumer intentions
Lightweight transformer based WT-MobileViT framework for plant disease detection
abstract: The rapid spread of plant diseases significantly threatens global food security. Early and accurate detection of these diseases is crucial for effective disease management and crop protection. Manual identification of diseases requires expert knowledge in the field, and finding people with domain knowledge is challenging. In recent years, computer vision-based machine learning techniques have been proposed by researchers to overcome the challenge. In this paper, we have proposed a WT-MobileViT, a lightweight hybrid model that integrates frequency domain information with the MobileViT framework for the classification of plant diseases. The proposed method first performs a one-level Haar Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to decompose the input image into low-frequency and high-frequency sub-bands, preserving complementary structural and texture information, and concatenates with the original RGB image to construct a multi-frequency feature representation. In this article, we have created a tea leaf disease dataset with RGB images in field conditions. The proposed model was experimented on four datasets and achieved an accuracy rate of 99.44% in tea leaf images, 99.68% in the rice dataset, 99.17% in the bean dataset, and 99.21% in plantvillage dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed model outperforms several state-of-the-art deep learning models with fewer parameters.

title: Performance and moral trust in care robotics: ethical foundations for human–robot relationships
abstract: As global populations age and birth rates decline, many societies, especially in developed countries, face critical labor shortages in the caregiving sector. This demographic imbalance is straining existing care infrastructures and raising urgent questions about how to support an increasing number of elderly individuals who can no longer live independently. Socially interactive AI systems, particularly care robots, have emerged as a promising technological response. However, their successful integration into real-world care settings hinges on more than technical capability; it requires appropriately calibrated reliance on robotic performance and morally trustworthy sociotechnical care arrangements. This paper investigates the ethical and conceptual foundations of trust in human–robot interactions, with a focus on the caregiving context. Building on the distinction between performance trust and moral trust, we argue that its application to care robotics reveals an agency-trust mismatch: care robots are not moral agents, yet care contexts generate morally significant expectations concerning dignity, autonomy, privacy, non-deception, responsibility, and well-being. We therefore reconceptualize moral trust in care robotics as sociotechnical moral trust, directed not toward the robot alone but toward the broader care arrangement in which robotic behavior is designed, deployed, monitored, governed, and corrected by human and institutional actors. On this basis, we distinguish robot-level performance trust from system-level moral trustworthiness and derive ethical design and governance principles for trustworthy care-robotic systems.

title: Choosing, shedding, setting: three faces of AI responsibility
abstract: Although current AI systems are probably not autonomous agents in a robust traditional sense, we might nonetheless wonder: what capacities must they possess to justifiably be held morally responsible for their choices? This paper argues that the answer to this question depends on the kind of responsibility and choice in question. A system’s ability to choose between programmed goals and means to them may be necessary and (with other capacities) sufficient for the system to justifiably share moral responsibility with its designers, but not for any kind of stand-alone responsibility. By contrast, the ability to shed programmed goals in accordance with moral reasons may be sufficient for holding the system responsible for pursuing a programmed goal rather than not, but not for a contrastive choice between a programmed and a non-programmed goal. To be responsible for such choices, a system must be able to set goals in accordance with moral reasons. I propose operational tests for this capacity and argue that it does not require freedom in an incompatibilist sense; rather, it is analogous to the human capacity to pursue goals not conducive to our survival.

title: Recent advances in multimodal deep learning for breast cancer diagnosis using data fusion vision language models and foundation models
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the most prevalent cancers worldwide, underscoring the need for reliable diagnostic approaches that can support accurate and timely clinical assessment. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, have enabled the development of multimodal systems that integrate complementary data sources, including medical images, radiology reports, clinical information, and genomic data. Such approaches aim to exploit information that may not be fully captured by a single modality and have shown promising performance in breast cancer diagnosis and related prediction tasks. This review provides a comprehensive and critical overview of multimodal deep learning approaches for breast cancer diagnosis published between January 2021 and September 2026. It examines the principal data modalities used in multimodal systems, including mammography, ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging, histopathology, radiology reports, clinical information, and genomic data. The review also analyzes major multimodal fusion strategies and traces the evolution of the field from conventional machine-learning and radiomics-based approaches to deep learning architectures, vision-language models, and foundation models. Recent multimodal models are discussed according to the data modalities employed, model architectures, fusion strategies, clinical or diagnostic tasks, datasets, and reported performance. Particular attention is given to approaches integrating medical imaging with radiology reports and other textual information, including emerging vision-language and foundation-model-based methods for breast imaging. Publicly available datasets and multimodal resources used in breast cancer research are also summarized and compared. Despite recent progress, important challenges remain, including the limited availability of large-scale multimodal datasets, restricted access to paired image–report datasets, missing modalities, limited external validation, uncertainty estimation, explainability, fairness, generalizability, and barriers to clinical workflow integration. Current evidence is still predominantly retrospective and technical; therefore, reported improvements in model performance should not be interpreted as demonstrated clinical benefit without prospective validation. Future research should focus on robust multimodal foundation models, explainable and trustworthy artificial intelligence, federated and privacy-preserving learning, standardized external validation, and prospective clinical evaluation. Overall, this review provides an updated synthesis of methodological developments, multimodal data integration strategies, emerging vision-language and foundation models, and translational challenges in multimodal artificial intelligence for breast cancer diagnosis.

title: Keeping clinical evidence current as medical artificial intelligence systems change
abstract: Generative and agentic artificial intelligence systems may change faster than clinical evidence can be generated, reviewed, and implemented. Updates to the foundation model, prompt, retrieval layer, generation settings, tools, memory, interface, or workflow can alter behaviour without changing the product name visible to investigators or users. This Perspective synthesizes evidence on repeated-run instability, cross-version performance, human–AI interaction, agentic systems, and post-deployment monitoring. We propose VERSION-AI as a testable evidence-refresh framework that separates what changed from the clinical consequences of failure. C0–C8 describe the system or context change, whereas a distinct clinical-consequence tier reflects intended use, decision dependence, time sensitivity, and the likelihood and severity of harm from incorrect, omitted, or delayed actions. The combination determines whether evidence may remain current after audit, requires usability or repeated-run bridging, cross-version or local validation, shadow evaluation, continuous monitoring, rollback capability, or renewed prospective clinical assessment. Because VERSION-AI has not yet been prospectively validated, it is presented as a research and governance proposal rather than a regulatory instrument. Evidence transfer after a material system change should be demonstrated rather than assumed.

title: Configurations of competence-based curriculum implementation among secondary school teachers in Tanzania
abstract: Tanzania’s transition from a predominantly knowledge-oriented to a competence-based curriculum (CBC) reflects broader global efforts to develop learners’ capacity to apply knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values in meaningful contexts. Existing studies have documented variations in teachers’ interpretations of reform expectations, pedagogical translation of CBC principles, and perceptions of professional-contextual conditions influencing implementation. However, these dimensions have been examined separately, limiting understanding of how their combinations generate particular implementation patterns. Guided by Sense-Making Theory and the Concerns-Based Adoption Model, this study examined how these dimensions interacted to generate configurations of CBC implementation among secondary school teachers. An interpretive qualitative multiple-case study design was employed involving 10 secondary school teachers, each treated as an individual case, purposively selected to capture variation in teaching experience and school contexts across urban and rural settings. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews, document reviews, and classroom observations, and analysed through iterative thematic analysis and cross-case comparison. Findings revealed three recurring configurations of CBC enactment: Fidelity Alignment, where adopters’ strong alignment with competence-oriented interpretations translated coherently into CBC pedagogical practices; Strategic Adaptation, where adopters valued CBC principles but interpreted contextual constraints as requiring selective modification of pedagogical practices while preserving core CBC intentions; and Symbolic Adoption, where adopters’ perceptions of the feasibility and reliability of established instructional routines shaped selective incorporation of CBC elements alongside continued reliance on teacher-directed practices. The study concludes that CBC implementation is not a uniform process of policy realisation; rather, it is an interpretive, contextually negotiated process shaped by the interaction among cognitive, practical, and contextual dimensions. The findings highlight the importance of designing differentiated teacher professional development and implementation support that responds to diverse patterns of curriculum enactment.

title: A trait-based perspective on nitrogen limitation from leaves to crop canopies
abstract: Nitrogen limitation can strongly reduce crop productivity; however, changes in leaf-level photosynthetic performance do not always parallel reductions in growth and yield, highlighting the need to consider how nitrogen-dependent responses scale from individual leaves to whole canopies. Here, I develop a trait-based perspective for interpreting the coordination of leaf-level function, leaf-area deployment, canopy resource capture, and crop performance under nitrogen limitation. Rather than proposing an alternative to existing crop physiological or modeling frameworks, this Perspective uses functional traits as a cross-scale lens to examine conditions in which comparatively maintained leaf-level function may not translate into maintained canopy performance. A nitrogen-limited potato system is used as an empirically grounded illustrative case. Leaf-level observations show comparatively weak relationships between specific leaf area and area-based photosynthesis, whereas stronger associations emerge for mass-based photosynthesis and photosynthetic nitrogen-use efficiency. At the crop level, nitrogen nutrition status is associated with total and tuber biomass, while biomass accumulation is closely related to intercepted photosynthetically active radiation across crop development. Together, these observations support a condition termed leaf-canopy decoupling, in which leaf-level physiological function is maintained while leaf-area deployment and canopy resource capture are constrained. This interpretation does not imply that canopy limitation universally dominates crop responses to nitrogen, but it generates a testable cross-scale hypothesis whose magnitude and consequences may vary by developmental stage, environment, and crop source–sink strategy. By linking functional traits to canopy development and resource capture, this Perspective offers a complementary basis for investigating nitrogen responses across crop functional types and identifying trait and management combinations that may improve nitrogen-use efficiency.

title: Multi-index remote sensing assessment of drought dynamics and crop yield sensitivity in the Hadoti Region, Rajasthan
abstract: Drought is a stress that reduces the productivity of rainfed agriculture and is quantified using satellite vegetation indices. There is a lack of time-series district-level studies associating these indices with crop yields for the Hadoti region of Rajasthan. In this study, drought variability and its impact on crop yield was analysed for Baran, Bundi, Jhalawar and Kota districts for 1997–2022 using NDVI, NDWI and VCI calculated from annual, Kharif and Rabi composites of Landsat 5, 8 and 9 surface reflectance for cropland pixels. Rainfall was obtained from Indian Meteorological Department grids and crop yields of six crops from district statistics. Time-series trends were identified using the Mann-Kendall test corrected for autocorrelation, Sen’s slope and Benjamini-Hochberg correction, while the Pettitt test detected level shifts. Crop yield relationships were explored using Pearson correlation, regression, detrending and leave-one-year-out cross-validation. All four districts experienced extreme agricultural drought in 2010 (VCI 2.7 to 6.5). Jhalawar district had annual trends in all three indices, but none remained significant after rainfall correction. Rabi indices increased in all districts (p < 0.001), while Kharif indices showed no trend. From 2015 to 2022, severe or extreme drought affected 14.8% of the region in annual and 25.8% in Kharif composites. Yields of barley, wheat and rapeseed correlated positively with Rabi indices (r ≤ 0.74), while maize, rice and soybean showed weak negative correlations. These indices must be employed with the help of rainfall and Kharif composites for monitoring purposes and not for forecasting alone. Clinical Trial Registration: Not applicable (this study is not a clinical trial).

title: A Multicenter Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics Framework For Diagnosing Tuberculous Lymphadenitis And Stratifying Rifampicin Resistance Risk.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES To develop and validate an ultrasound-based habitat radiomics framework for the hierarchical differentiation of tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) from non-tuberculous lymphadenopathy, and to noninvasively predict rifampicin resistance risk using an independently collected cohort of patients with confirmed TBLN. MATERIALS AND METHODS In this multicenter retrospective study, 618 patients with superficial lymphadenopathy who underwent ultrasound examination between January 2022 and December 2025 at four tertiary hospitals were included. Among them, 530 patients with definitive diagnoses were used for diagnostic differentiation and were divided into a model-development (training) cohort and an external validation cohort, while 236 patients with confirmed tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) were included for rifampicin resistance risk assessment. Based on standardized B-mode ultrasound images, we developed a 2-stage ultrasound habitat radiomics framework that first differentiated tuberculous from non-tuberculous lymph nodes. Rifampicin resistance risk was assessed within the confirmed TBLN cohort using nested cross-validated out-of-fold predictions. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA), and model interpretability was assessed using SHAP-based methods. RESULTS For differentiating tuberculous from non-tuberculous lymph nodes, the habitat-based model demonstrated strong discriminative performance, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83 in the training cohort and maintaining consistent performance in the external test cohort. Using nested cross-validated out-of-fold predictions within the confirmed TBLN cohort, the habitat-based model achieved an AUC of 0.83 for predicting rifampicin resistance, outperforming conventional radiomics and demonstrating superior clinical net benefit. Spatial visualization revealed that high-risk habitats were localized to specific intralesional regions, underscoring the importance of spatial heterogeneity in both disease diagnosis and drug resistance assessment. CONCLUSION Ultrasound-based habitat radiomics provides an interpretable and clinically applicable framework for hierarchical diagnosis of tuberculous lymphadenitis and for rifampicin resistance risk assessment in an independent patient cohort, supporting precision imaging-guided management of tuberculosis.

title: Development and Multicenter Validation of a Hybrid Radiomics-Deep Learning Model for Risk Stratification of O-RADS 4 Adnexal Masses.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-driven hybrid model integrating ultrasound radiomics, deep learning (DL) signatures, and clinical predictors for differentiating benign from borderline/malignant Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System (O-RADS) 4 adnexal masses, and to evaluate its utility as a radiologist decision-support tool. MATERIALS AND METHODS This multicenter study retrospectively enrolled 653 patients from four centers (521 from Center A [training, n = 405; internal validation, n = 116]; 132 from Centers B-D [external validation]), and prospectively enrolled 126 patients from Center A. Pathological results served as the gold standard. Radiomics features were extracted to generate a Rad-score using machine learning classifiers. A transfer learning-based DL model using convolutional neural networks produced a DL-score. A hybrid model integrating Rad-score, DL-score, and clinical predictors was constructed. Diagnostic performance of models was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). In the prospective validation set, six radiologists interpreted cases with and without hybrid model assistance. Diagnostic differences were assessed using McNemar's χ² test, and inter-reader agreement by Cohen's kappa. RESULTS The hybrid model demonstrated good performance with AUCs of 0.88 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.82-0.93) and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.78-0.92) in the prospective and external validation sets. Model assistance significantly improved accuracy and specificity across all readers (p < 0.05), with inter-reader agreement improving from kappa 0.49 to 0.73. The model stratified lesions into low-risk (4a) and high-risk (4b) subcategories with consistently distinct malignancy rates across all datasets (4a: 4.5%-16.1%; 4b: 75.4%-97.1%). CONCLUSION The hybrid model demonstrated good performance for risk stratification of O-RADS 4 adnexal masses and improved radiologist performance across experience levels.

title: Blockchain and the transparency paradox: Fear of exposure, information asymmetry, and traceability resistance in Saudi manufacturing supply chains.
abstract: Blockchain can strengthen supply-chain transparency and traceability, but implementation does not necessarily imply full acceptance of the visibility it creates. This study examines how psychological transparency risk, economic transparency risk, and traceability resistance relate to blockchain traceability implementation in Saudi manufacturing firms. Drawing on Transparency Paradox Theory, Information Asymmetry Theory, and Technology Threat Avoidance Theory, the model distinguishes risk appraisals from organisational resistance behaviour. Three-wave survey data from 703 firms were analyzed using PLS-SEM, supported by confirmatory factor analysis, predictive assessment, unit-weighted comparison, and Gaussian Copula analysis. The model explained 67.3% of the variance in implementation and 66.7% in resistance. Contrary to expectations, psychological and economic transparency risks were positively associated with implementation and negatively associated with resistance. Traceability resistance was negatively associated with implementation and was the only direct relationship supported in the hypothesized direction. The indirect effects through resistance were positive, while relational trust and digital capability produced asymmetric moderating effects. The findings show that recognising exposure, control, and commercial vulnerability should not be equated with resistance. Firms may acknowledge these risks while continuing to implement blockchain, whereas delayed integration, restricted access, selective disclosure, and symbolic compliance remain important barriers. The study contributes by separating transparency-risk appraisal, resistance behaviour, and operational implementation, while offering practical guidance on differentiated access controls, disclosure governance, and monitoring of observable resistance.

title: A remote sensing-enhanced Digital Twin framework for multi-scale infrastructure monitoring
Spatio-temporal monitoring of agricultural drought in China based on downscaled soil moisture data
abstract: : Agricultural drought threatens China’s food and ecological security, and accurate spatio-13 temporal monitoring is key for disaster mitigation. Soil moisture is critical for drought assessment, 14 but the accuracy of existing remote sensing-based SM products in China remains to be improved. 15 This study develops a framework that synergistically integrates a spatiotemporally adaptive gap-16 filling algorithm with a machine learning-based downscaling approach, generating a seamless 0.05 ∘ 17 monthly SM dataset for China from 2003 to 2023. The methodology harnesses the complementary 18 strengths of random forest modeling and spatiotemporal reconstruction techniques to effectively 19 fuse multi-source satellite observations, achieving dual improvements in SM data accuracy and 20 spatial coverage. Using this dataset, the standardized soil moisture index was applied to characterize 21 the spatio-temporal evolution of agricultural drought. Results demonstrate that (1) The downscaled 22 SM dataset achieves significant improvements in both spatial resolution and accuracy, showing a 23 2.3–34.4% reduction in ubRMSE and 1.2–52.7% improvement in correlation coefficients compared 24 to benchmark datasets. (2) Drought characterization based on the downscaled SM dataset and SSI 25 accurately identified the extent of agricultural drought, showing a significant spatiotemporal 26 consistency with agricultural disaster area. (3) Agricultural drought intensified significantly across 27 China during the study period, characterized by northward migration of drought center and spatially 28 heterogeneous aridification patterns — decreasing severity from northwest to southeast while 29 increasing from northeast to southwest. High-frequency drought zones were predominantly 30 clustered in ecologically vulnerable regions, particularly the agro-pastoral ecotone of northern 31 China. (4) Distinct intra-annual drought dynamics emerged, with a southwest-to-northeast 32 expansion dominating from January to June, followed by bidirectional propagation from the Yellow 33 River-Huaihe River Basin (YRB-HRB) to northwestern and southeastern regions from June to 34 December. This study provides high-accuracy data support for agricultural drought monitoring and 35 offers scientific insights for developing regional differentiated drought mitigation strategies, which 36 are of great significance for ensuring national food security. 37

Posttraumatic growth in nursing home workers: differential associations of gratitude, meaning in life, and distress four years after the pandemic.
abstract: PURPOSE/AIMS To examine associations between posttraumatic growth, gratitude, meaning in life, and psychological distress among nursing home workers several years after the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS A cross-sectional study was conducted with 251 nursing home workers in Madrid, Spain, who had worked during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants completed the Posttraumatic Growth Inventory-Short Form, the Purpose in Life Test-10, the Gratitude Questionnaire-6, and the Patient Health Questionnaire-4. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression models were performed. RESULTS Posttraumatic growth was present across the sample several years after the pandemic, although spiritual change showed lower scores than other growth dimensions. Gratitude and meaning in life were both positively associated with posttraumatic growth at the bivariate level. In adjusted models, gratitude remained significantly associated with all posttraumatic growth dimensions, whereas meaning in life did not retain independent associations. Psychological distress was also positively associated with posttraumatic growth, indicating that growth-related appraisals and distress coexisted in this sample. No significant differences in posttraumatic growth were observed across professional roles. CONCLUSION/IMPLICATIONS This study contributes to the limited literature on nursing home workers by showing that posttraumatic growth remained present several years after the COVID-19 pandemic and was more closely associated with gratitude than with meaning in life in adjusted models. For research, the findings support a more differentiated view of positive post-adversity processes and their coexistence with distress. For geriatric nursing and long-term care, they underscore the value of considering not only emotional burden but also positive psychological appraisals when addressing staff well-being after major collective adversity.

title: Coupling ecosystem services and land-use disturbance to diagnose degradation and restoration in dryland watersheds.
abstract: Ecological degradation and restoration in arid and semi-arid watersheds are jointly shaped by water limitation, ecosystem-function change, and intensive land-use disturbance. However, existing assessments often treat functional status, process pressure, subsequent response, and spatial diagnosis separately. To address this gap, we developed an integrated degradation-restoration framework (IDRF) for the northern Inner Mongolia section of the Yellow River Basin using long-term land-use data and four InVEST-derived ecosystem services. IDRF links ecohydrological functional status (F), land-use process disturbance (D), disturbance-function response positions, and annual degradation-restoration screening. Because high modeled water yield does not necessarily correspond to high ecological functioning under water-limited conditions, ecologically constrained water yield (WY*) was introduced as a dryland-oriented functional adjustment. The results showed that: (1) F stably integrated multiple ecosystem services and captured watershed-scale functional gradients, providing a consistent basis for F-D response analysis. (2) D extended disturbance assessment from static land-cover attributes to process-based pressure by integrating baseline disturbance, neighborhood exposure, edge fragmentation, land-use transitions, and water/wetland support; neighborhood context was an important structural component. (3) The functional-improvement diagnostic position (τr) was lower than the composite degradation diagnostic position (τd), and this relative ordering remained stable under paired spatiotemporal resampling, indicating that improvement-related responses generally occurred at lower disturbance levels than degradation-related responses. (4) Background maintenance, stable conservation, and restoration limitation were the dominant annual screening classes, with long-term changes characterized mainly by localized transitions. During the study period, stable conservation increased from 18.20% to 21.51%, while restoration limitation remained at approximately 18%-19%. Spatial-block evaluation further supported the within-watershed discrimination of model-defined events. Overall, IDRF provides an annually updatable, watershed-scale diagnostic framework for arid and semi-arid regions where water limitation and land-use pressure interact strongly, offering a methodological basis for spatially differentiated management and targeted field verification.
