title: Integrated chemical profiling, transcriptomics and functional validation elucidate the multifunctional benefits of a triple-ferment filtrate complex for skin aging intervention.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Skin aging is driven by interconnected hallmarks including oxidative stress and chronic low-grade inflammation, cellular senescence, impaired epidermal function and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation. Fermentation-derived cosmetic ingredients have attracted increasing interest as multifunctional actives; however, their underlying mechanisms often remain poorly understood. This study aimed to systematically characterize the biological activities and mechanisms of a triple-ferment filtrate complex (TF Complex) derived from fermented rice, green tea and algae. METHODS An integrated approach combining chemical profiling, transcriptomic analysis and functional validation across multiple in vitro skin models was employed. Chemical constituents were characterized using UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS. Transcriptomic responses of human keratinocytes treated with TF Complex at different time points were evaluated by RNA sequencing. Functional activities were assessed in keratinocytes, fibroblasts and reconstructed human skin models relevant to skin aging. RESULTS Chemical profiling revealed a compositionally complex mixture containing diverse bioactive constituents. Transcriptomic analysis revealed a time-dependent response characterized by early activation of antioxidant defence pathways, followed by induction of epidermal differentiation related programmes. Functional studies showed that TF Complex promoted wound closure and attenuated UVB-induced inflammatory responses. Furthermore, selected representative constituents, turanose, caffeine and p-hydroxybenzaldehyde, enhanced antioxidant and keratinocyte differentiation-associated gene expression while down-regulating inflammation-related gene expression in skin cells. In H2O2-induced senescent fibroblasts, TF Complex reduced senescence-associated β-gal activity and p16/γH2AX levels while increasing SOD2 expression. In a reconstructed full-thickness inflammaging skin model, TF Complex restored epidermal thickness and filaggrin expression, preserved dermal-epidermal junction integrity and dermal ECM proteins and reduced the release of MMP-1, MMP-9 and IL-1α. CONCLUSIONS TF Complex exerts multifunctional activities relevant to skin aging intervention through coordinated regulation of oxidative stress responses, inflammation and epidermal homeostasis. These findings provide a comprehensive mechanistic framework supporting the development and application of fermentation-derived cosmetic actives for healthy skin aging.

title: The Evolution and Clinical Utility of Oral Epithelial Dysplasia Grading Systems: A Narrative Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND Histological grading of oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) is the gold standard for predicting malignant transformation in potentially malignant disorders. However, traditional grading systems suffer from subjectivity and poor diagnostic reproducibility, complicating patient management. This narrative review evaluates the clinical utility of current and emerging OED grading systems. METHODS We reviewed recent literature (2019-2026) comparing the traditional World Health Organization (WHO) classifications against binary grading, histopathological feature-specific models (two-point and six-point systems), diagnostic biomarkers, and clinical risk factors. RESULTS The WHO system frequently demonstrates poor-to-fair interobserver agreement. Conversely, binary and six-point grading systems provide superior reproducibility. While these models effectively stratify malignant transformation risk, their clinical utility is limited by tissue sampling errors, such as "skip areas." Furthermore, immunohistochemical biomarkers (Keratin 13 and 17) show promise as diagnostic adjuncts to assist in identifying high-risk variants like differentiated dysplasia. CONCLUSION While the WHO system remains the gold standard, its subjectivity complicates clinical decisions. Adopting objective binary and feature-specific models offers superior clinical utility for risk stratification. Clear numerical cutoffs alongside expanded morphological features and biomarkers may influence the accuracy of predicting malignant transformation, inform clinical decision-making regarding surgical versus conservative surveillance, and optimize patient management when integrated with clinicopathological findings.

title: CampusHAT: building-peer-context multiscale probabilistic forecasting and residual decomposition for campus smart-meter analytics
abstract: Campus smart-meter analytics must reconcile cumulative registers, resets, mixed sampling, missing observations, and metadata relations that are informative but not electrically additive. We present CampusHAT, a global model for forecasting the next 24 hourly meter-level energy intervals from 168 hours. It combines a Transformer branch, 1/6/24-hour dilated convolutions, meter/building/use-type embeddings, and a gated building-peer context. Quantile heads produce 0.1/0.5/0.9 forecasts; residuals support interval-normalized anomaly scoring and building-common versus meter-specific decomposition. Experiments use 1,094 meters assigned to 30 buildings over 21,071 hours from the HKUST campus dataset. On the 2024 test period, CampusHAT obtains 8.052 kWh MAE and 21.175%WAPE, improving both by 6.09% over Seasonal Naive and 12.13% over GRU, the strongest deep baseline by MAE and WAPE. The multi-scale branch reduces aggregate MAE by 1.83%, whereas the full context/peer-loss configuration does not yield a consistent point-accuracy gain. Compared with the joint no-context/no-peer-loss ablation, the full configuration raises empirical 80% interval coverage from 74.39% to 82.19% while widening the interval. On a fixed semi-synthetic anomaly realization shared across model seeds, an interval-normalized residual detector achieves 0.534 F1 and0.461AUPRC; these values do not capture injection-set uncertainty. Building-group residual decomposition reaches 0.698oracle-window conditional scope accuracy among detected row-level events but incurs substantially more false positives. Building-holdout performance is heterogeneous, the model is worse than Seasonal Naive at daily resolution, and cross-campus transfer is not evaluated. These results identify useful mechanisms and limits of building-peer-context forecasting.
journal: International Conference on Photonics, Smart Grid and Energy Technology

title: Receptive English proficiency across programs in engineering education
abstract: English proficiency is increasingly recognized as a prerequisite for disciplinary participation in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) higher education, yet large scale evidence on institutional variation among non-English-major engineering students remains limited in Vietnam. This study examined receptive English proficiency across three program types, mass, advanced, and international, using population-level placement data from 17,561 first-year engineering students over three consecutive cohorts (2022-2024). Listening and reading performance (10-990 total) was analyzed through a two-way general linear model (GLM) to assess main and interaction effects of program structure and academic year. Results indicated a consistent proficiency hierarchy (advancedinternationalmass), with program type explaining the largest proportion of variance (partial η²=0.21). Academic year demonstrated a medium effect (partial η²=0.09), reflecting a progressive decline in cohort readiness, while the interaction effect (partial η²=0.03) showed more pronounced decreases in the mass program. These findings suggest that English-medium environments partially buffer national level declines but cannot fully offset systemic weaknesses in receptive preparedness. Implications include differentiated instructional pathways, placement informed curriculum design, and targeted academic English support in Vietnamese-medium engineering programs. The study provides empirical evidence for equity-oriented English medium instruction (EMI) development and contributes data driven insights for policy and curriculum in STEM higher education.

title: Bridging teacher talk time and multiple intelligences for deep learning
abstract: This study investigates the systemic tension between the dominance of teacher talk time (TTT) and the urgent need for deep learning strategies tailored to students’ multiple intelligences (MI) within the context of teaching English to young learners (TEYL). Adopting a descriptive mixed-methods design with a concurrent triangulation strategy, this research was conducted across a representative developing region in Central Java, Indonesia, involving a stratified sample of 450 upper-primary students and 45 English teachers. Data were collected using the student learning profile inventory (SLPI), TTT observation trackers, and semi-structured interviews. The findings reveal a critical pedagogical dissonance: while 72% of students exhibit a clear dominance in bodily-kinesthetic and visual-spatial intelligences profiles that biologically necessitate active, multimodal engagement classroom interactions remain heavily monopolized by teachers, who occupy 75% of lesson duration with verbal instruction. This excessive TTT acts as a significant constraint to the implementation of differentiated instruction (DI), effectively trapping students in surface-level rote memorization and inhibiting the development of communicative competence. The study concludes that the successful implementation of student-centered curricula requires a fundamental deconstruction of the traditional “teacher-as-broadcaster” model. Reducing TTT is identified not merely as a classroom management technique, but as a prerequisite for creating the temporal and cognitive space necessary for MI-based differentiation and deep learning.

title: Remote Sensing, Surveys, and Stories: Lessons From a Mixed-Methods Retrospective Evaluation of a Digital Agriculture App in Nepal
abstract: Evaluation methods have recently expanded, with options ranging from remote sensing to qualitative and quantitative methods, but deciding which to use can be challenging. This paper explores three evaluation methodologies used to retrospectively evaluate an agricultural app in Nepal. This includes using remote sensing to measure vegetation health, a limited quantitative survey to explore app usage and GPS accuracy, and qualitative interviews to contextualize app usage. Remote sensing outcomes show no differences in outcomes for farmers who utilized the app more, while the quantitative survey highlights that app usage was limited and the GPS data should be approached with caution. Qualitative results indicate that while the app attracted interest from local farmers, continued support could have increased usage. While these methods are useful individually, only by laying them together can we evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of each one, while gaining a holistic view of the app rollout and training.

title: Representation and differentiation of audiology interventions within the international classification of health interventions.
abstract: BACKGROUND Standardised intervention coding supports service visibility, reimbursement, resource planning and health-system analytics. The International Classification of Health Interventions (ICHIs) provides a standardised framework for representing health interventions, but its ability to capture the breadth and clinical specificity of contemporary audiology practice requires evaluation. OBJECTIVE To evaluate the extent to which contemporary audiology interventions can be represented and differentiated within ICHI and identify limitations in coding granularity that may affect health information management, service reporting and reimbursement. METHOD An inventory of audiology interventions was derived from historical and current South African tariff schedules, scope-of-practice documents, university curricula and contemporary clinical practice. A total of 105 interventions spanning hearing and vestibular assessment, electrophysiology, device-related procedures, and counselling and rehabilitation were independently mapped to ICHI using a structured coding rubric aligned with the Target-Action-Means framework. Interrater agreement was calculated for a predefined subset. RESULTS All included interventions could be represented within ICHI. Most (92.3%) demonstrated direct one-to-one alignment with an ICHI stem code. The remainder required approximate ('best-fit'), postcoordination, or composite coding using multiple descriptors and/or extension codes. Clinically distinct interventions frequently converged under identical stems, particularly within rehabilitation, counselling, device management and tele-audiology. This convergence reduced coding granularity and differentiation of clinical intent, service complexity and resource utilisation. CONCLUSION ICHI provides broad structural coverage of contemporary audiology interventions; however, limited granularity constrains its utility for detailed health-system reporting, reimbursement modelling and service evaluation. Greater differentiation within rehabilitation- and technology-related categories is warranted to better represent contemporary audiology practice and support person-centred ear and hearing care within universal health coverage frameworks.Implications for health information management practice:High-level ICHI stems may obscure clinically meaningful variation in audiology services, reducing data precision for funding, workload measurement, service evaluation and national reporting. Implementation guidance and standardised composite coding protocols may improve specificity where existing stems are insufficient. Identified classification gaps may inform formal submissions to the World Health Organisation Family of International Classifications Network. Improved specificity could strengthen interoperability, secondary data analytics, reimbursement modelling, and evidence-based hearing-care planning.
journal: Health information management : journal of the Health Information Management Association of Australia

title: Non-electrophilic TRPA1 modulator MNP-021 protects neuronal and glial function from diabetes-associated glucotoxicity and neuroinflammation
abstract: Diabetes-associated neurodegeneration is amplified by methylglyoxal (MGO)-driven dicarbonyl stress linking hyperglycemia to neuronal insulin resistance and maladaptive neuroinflammation. We tested the neuroprotective activity of MNP-021, a non-electrophilic transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) modulator, in neurons and glial cells in vitro. SH-SY5Y neurons were pretreated with MNP-021 and challenged with MGO, then profiled by high-content imaging, RNA-seq, Seahorse Oxygen Consumption Rate (OCR) and Extracellular Acidification Rate (ECAR), glycolytic stress assays, and immunoblotting for AKT, ERK, and cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB). In an additional sustained glucotoxicity paradigm, differentiated SH-SY5Y cells were exposed to high glucose for 7 days and viability was assessed by LIVE/DEAD™ high-content imaging. HMC3 glial cells were treated with MNP-021, exposed to Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), Tumor Necrosis Factor-α (TNF-α) or Aβ(25–35), and tested for viability and inflammatory markers by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) and RT-qPCR. MGO increased nucleus-to-cytoplasm area ratio by 49% and dysregulated glucose handling, increasing 2-(N-(7-Nitrobenz-2-oxa-1,3-diazol-4-yl)Amino)-2-Deoxyglucose (2-NBDG) uptake by ~ 25%, with GLUT1/GLUT4 membrane redistribution; MNP-021 normalized morphology, glucose uptake, and transporter localization without cytotoxicity up to 10 µM. RNA-seq identified 754 MGO-deregulated genes, including ISR/metabolic nodes such as glucokinase (GCK), Sestrin-2 (SESN2), phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH), Phosphoserine Aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1), phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 2 (PCK2); MNP-021 buffered stress-induced transcription with limited baseline effects, modulated mitochondrial morphology and redox-associated fluorescence while preserving overall respiratory flux and blunting stress-evoked compensatory glycolysis. MNP-021 restored pro-survival signaling (pAKT/pERK and nuclear pCREB), including insulin responsiveness during MGO exposure. In a sustained high-glucose model, MNP-021 reduced the high-glucose-associated increase in cell death, extending its protective effects beyond the acute MGO paradigm. MNP-021 reduced Interleukine-6 (IL-6)/TNF-α release while increasing Interleukine-10 (IL-10) and Arginase 1 (ARG1) (~ 1.9-fold vs. LPS/TNF-α) in HMC3 glial cells, shifting them toward a pro-resolving IL-10/ARG1 program with reduced amyloid β-peptide 25–35 (Aβ(25–35))-evoked cytokine release and Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) remaining very low (≤ 10 pg/mL) and not significantly increased in this system. MNP-021 coordinates transcriptomic restraint, transporter-level glucose handling, mitochondrial resilience, and pro-survival/pro-resolving signaling in neuron–microglia cell models. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of MNP-021 in dicarbonyl-linked neuro-metabolic stress and provide pharmacological evidence consistent with a TRPA1-linked component of its activity. • A non-electrophilic TRPA1 modulator MNP-021 protects neurons from methylglyoxal stress. • MNP-021 normalizes glucose uptake and GLUT1/GLUT4 trafficking under stress. • It modulates mitochondrial morphology/redox-associated readouts and blunts stress-evoked glycolysis. • It restores AKT/ERK/CREB signaling and insulin responsiveness during glucotoxicity. • It modulates HMC3 inflammatory responses toward an IL-10/ARG1-associated profile.

title: Dual antigen-sampling sites support early mucosal antigen uptake in the porcine nasal cavity
abstract: Intranasal vaccination is a promising strategy for preventing respiratory infections. However, the anatomical and cellular pathways responsible for antigen sampling in the porcine nasal cavity remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified and characterized two spatially distinct antigen-sampling sites in the porcine nasal cavity: the anterior respiratory mucosa (RM) and the posterior nasopharynx-associated lymphoid tissue (NALT). Following intranasal administration of ovalbumin (OVA), a subset of OVA+ epithelial cells at both sites was labeled by Ulex europaeus agglutinin I (UEA-1) and NKM 16-2-4, indicating that these cells might exhibit an M-cell-like phenotype. In RM, OVA was initially localized to the epithelium and was subsequently detected in the lamina propria by 6 h and in CD11c+ cells (a population that might include dendritic cells) at 24 h. By contrast, OVA reached the underlying lymphoid follicles in NALT as early as 2 h. OVA+ cells were also detected in mandibular draining lymph nodes at 6 h. Moreover, an air–liquid interface co-culture model showed apical-to-basolateral OVA transport across differentiated nasal epithelial cultures and subsequent OVA acquisition by underlying differentiated bone marrow cells (dBMCs). Together, these findings identify anterior RM and posterior NALT as two antigen-sampling sites with distinct temporal dynamics and define early cellular events that might contribute to mucosal immune induction in pigs.

title: From label to table: Can co-labeling boost trust and value in PDO cheese?
abstract: The Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) plays a fundamental role in the territorial recognition and value of Grana Padano cheese. However, there are several factors that can influence consumer choices and consequently affect their willingness to pay for the product. Among these, ethical and sensory aspects can play a fundamental role that has yet to be thoroughly analyzed in the literature. This study has the overall objective of assessing the importance attributed by consumers to various attributes of Grana Padano cheese, including PDO certification, ethical aspects mediated by animal welfare claims, and sensory aspects, also considering the effect of consumers’ socio-demographic and psychometric characteristics. To achieve this objective, a conjoint experiment ranking was carried out using rank-ordered logistic regression as the estimation model, which made it possible to estimate the willingness to pay (WTP) for these attributes and in relation to various drivers. The study showed that PDO certification is the attribute of greatest interest to consumers, although ethical and sensory aspects can be positively integrated to ensure the success and differentiation of the product.

title: Engineering sulfate potassium nutrient pathways as a nature-based solution for productivity recovery and externality mitigation in degraded humid-tropical ultisol agroecosystems
abstract: Humid-tropical ultisols supporting smallholder horticulture in Southeast Asia are widely recognised as degraded agroecosystems whose biogeochemical functioning has been disrupted by accelerated cation leaching, sulfur depletion following reduced atmospheric S deposition, and decades of chloride-loaded fertilisation. From an ecological engineering perspective, restoring the productive capacity of these soils requires interventions that simultaneously address nutrient cycling, soil-microbiome connectivity, and avoidance of off-site externalities, rather than yield optimisation alone. This study evaluated potassium sulfate (K₂SO₄) as an ecologically engineered substitute for potassium chloride (KCl) in a degraded humid-tropical ultisol of Indralaya Selatan, Ogan Ilir, South Sumatra, Indonesia, using shallot ( Allium cepa var. aggregatum L.) as a sentinel crop. A randomised complete block design with four K₂SO₄ doses (0, 60, 90, 120 kg ha⁻¹) and three replications (n = 12) was implemented across an eight-week growing season. Fourteen plant-level state variables describing canopy, photosynthetic and harvest-organ traits were monitored and combined with site-level inputs to estimate avoided chloride load and net sulfate input to the agroecosystem. Multivariate ordination (PCA, 63.1% cumulative variance) positioned the 90 kg ha⁻¹ treatment in the high-functioning quadrant aligned with bulb dry weight, shoot dry weight, bulb volume and chlorophyll, while supraoptimal dosing (120 kg ha⁻¹) shifted system state back toward control, consistent with the self-organ - ising response expected of ecologically engineered nutrient pathways. Pearson connectivity analysis revealed a coherent yield-component cluster (bulb diameter–bulb dry weight, r =.909, p <.01) interpretable as a functional ecological module mediated by K⁺-driven turgor and S-dependent structural integrity. An OLS model (R² =.827) is proposed as a non-destructive ecological monitoring tool for in-field state assessment. Substitution of K₂SO₄ at 90 kg ha⁻¹ for an equivalent K-rate of KCl avoided an estimated ~32 kg Cl⁻ ha⁻¹ season⁻¹ entering the rooting zone and added ~16 kg S ha⁻¹ to the soil S pool, quantifying a tangible nature-based-solution benefit. The findings advance an ecologically engineered nutrient-pathway framework chloride-free, dual K–S supply, dose-bounded by ecosystem self-organisation, and coupled to non-destructive monitoring for the restoration of productive function in degraded humid-tropical ultisol agroecosystems.

title: The effect of biological fertilisation on the intensity of nitrogen-carbon cycling in crop rotations in the forest-steppe
abstract: The aim of the study was to determine the parameters of a novel integrated stoichiometric model of the interrelated nitrogen and carbon cycles under conditions involving the implementation of different types of crop rotations, alternative types of organic fertilisation and varying methods of mechanical soil cultivation in the agrocenoses of the forest-steppe of Ukraine. The research methodology was based on a combination of long-term field observations and an integrated stoichiometric framework for evaluating nitrogen, as well as carbon balances under different fertilisation systems and soil tillage practices. It was established that the type of organic fertiliser directly correlates with the level of CO₂ emis - sions resulting from mineralisation processes: when manure is applied, the range of emissions is usually 25–85 tonnes, whereas the use of by-products increases this level to 80–160 tonnes. In the first scenario, a more intensive nitrogen removal relative to its input was observed, whereas in the second, a progressive increase in total stocks was recorded. An increase in CO₂ emissions in such cases is accompanied by an improvement in the soil carbon balance and an in - crease in the overall yield of the system. An assessment of the impact of black soil tillage methods showed that with non-inversion tillage technology - regardless of the type of crop rotation or fertiliser – a positive trend in soil carbon balance is observed, whereas with ploughing, the nature of the increase in organic matter deficit has a non-linear (para - bolic) form. Ploughing is characterised by a wider range of CO₂ emissions, indicating more active mineralisation. The results of the study confirmed the high efficiency of using shredded crop by-products in combination with appropriate nitrogen compensation via mineral fertilisers. The practical significance of the results lies in substantiating the effec - tiveness of using crop by-products and non-inversion tillage to stabilise nitrogen-carbon cycling, restore the fertility of chernozems and increase the productivity of agrocenoses in the forest-steppe of Ukraine.

title: Analysis of the global and local effects of urban green space vegetation types on early-summer near-surface O3 concentrations based on street view imagery – A case study of hangzhou
abstract: With the expansion of urban development, air pollution has become increasingly severe. In recent years, ozone (O3) pollution has emerged as a major threat to air quality in China. Existing studies have rarely explored the impact of vegetation types on O3 from a micro-scale perspective. Taking Hangzhou, a city with severe O3 pollution, as an example, street-view images from eight districts were first collected. A DeepLabV3+ semantic segmentation model trained on the ADE20K dataset was employed to accurately classify trees, shrubs, and grasses in the images. Meteorological and urban structural factors were incorporated, and Bayesian-optimized Optimization-based Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), and Geographically Weighted Random Forest (GWRF) models were applied to analyze the independent effects of the three vegetation-type factors on O3 concentration and their synergistic interactions from both global and local scales. The results indicate: (1) Xiaoshan District and the core urban areas such as Xihu District and are severely polluted, with an overall decreasing trend in O3 concentration (the area with O3 concentration in the range of 120.01–160.00 μg/m3 decreased from 2,100 km2 to 0 km2). (2) Meteorological factors dominate O3 variation, while the contributions of vegetation-type factors are relatively low. Nevertheless, vegetation-type factors still exhibit stable and differentiated contributions to O3 concentration. At the global scale, tree area proportion (TAP) shows either positive or negative effects on O3 concentration at high levels (average contribution = 0.002), shrub area proportion (SAP) has a positive influence, and grass area proportion (GAP) demonstrates a negative influence (average contribution = 0.006 for both). (3) At the local scale, the extremely high-importance areas of TAP shifted from northern Xihu District and Gongshu District in 2014 to southern Xihu District and Binjiang District in 2017. SAP exhibited relatively high and extremely high importance in southern Xihu District and western Xiaoshan District. The relatively high and extremely high importance areas of GAP were distributed in core urban zones such as eastern Xihu District, southern Gongshu District, Binjiang District, and Shangcheng District. The extent of extremely high-importance areas for all vegetation-type factors showed a decreasing trend. (4) High-importance areas of building density (BD) and industrial impervious surface percentage (ISP) spatially overlapped with those of vegetation-type factors, concentrating in core urban areas and the industrial zone of Xiaoshan, whereas meteorological factors played an independent role mainly in the peripheral areas of the city. This study aims to provide a scientific basis for precise O3 pollution control and optimal configuration of urban green spaces.

title: Plastic mulching consistently improves brinjal performance, but drip irrigation benefits are soil dependent: A two-location field study
abstract: Brinjal (Solanum melongena L.) requires considerable soil moisture throughout its life cycle, therefore, its cultivation in water constraint area is difficult. Though different soil moisture conservation technologies and lower water use irrigation systems have been developed for crop cultivation, their successful deployment largely depends on the locality, especially on soil characteristics. This study evaluated the effects of irrigation regimes, mulching practices, and their combination on growth, stress physiology and irrigation water use efficiency (IWUE) of brinjal across two field locations with contrasting soil conditions. Location 1 had coarser soil, lower nutrient and organic matter content profiles and lower water-holding capacity than location 2. The experiment comprised three irrigation levels [rainfed (I0), conventional furrow irrigation (IC), and drip irrigation (ID)] and three mulching treatments [no mulch (M0), straw mulch (MS), and plastic mulch (MP)] with three replications at both locations. Irrigation and mulching both significantly influenced growth, stress indicators, fruit yield, and IWUE, though the effects of the treatment on these parameters varied between locations. At Location 1, drip irrigation (ID) produced a fruit yield of 8.90 ± 5.68 t ha−1, with considerable variability among replicates, and did not differ significantly (p = 0.88) from conventional furrow irrigation (IC) or the rainfed treatment (I0). In contrast, at location 2, drip irrigation outperformed (21.88 ± 9.44 t ha−1) other treatments, being 117% and 32% higher than I0 and IC, respectively. Plastic mulching (MP) improved growth, reduced drought stress and increased yield compared to MS and M0 at both locations. The highest yield at location 1 (23.18 ± 6.62 t ha−1) occurred under IC × MP, while the highest yield at location 2 (32.93 ± 1.62 t ha−1) was achieved under ID × MP. IWUE peaked at 38.84 kg ha−1 mm−1 (IC × MP) in location 1 and 65.87 kg ha−1 mm−1 (ID × MP) in location 2. A linear mixed model estimated that plastic mulch increased yield by ~10.63 t ha−1 (95% CI: 6.58–14.68 t ha−1, p < 0.001) over no mulch, and IC × MP produced a synergistic yield gain of 11.03 t ha−1 (95% CI: 5.3–16.76 t ha−1, p = 0.003) over the control. Overall, plastic mulching consistently enhanced brinjal performance, while the benefit of drip irrigation was soil-dependent and was most evident in the higher water-retention field.

title: Oxidative stress-driven cellular heterogeneity in Knee Osteoarthritis: scRNA-seq pinpoints SPP1 and CYBA for diagnostic development
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration, synovial inflammation, and subchondral bone remodeling. Oxidative stress plays a critical role in KOA pathogenesis. This study aimed to identify oxidative stress–related hub genes by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with machine learning to uncover potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for KOA. ScRNA-seq data from KOA cartilage tissues were obtained from the GEO database to characterize cellular heterogeneity and identify disease-associated chondrocyte subsets. CellChat was used to analyze intercellular communication, and Monocle2 was applied to reconstruct cell differentiation trajectories. Oxidative stress activity at the single-cell level was evaluated using AUCell, while high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) was performed to identify oxidative stress–related gene modules. Candidate genes were screened using Venn analysis and further refined by LASSO regression, SVM-RFE, and XGBoost combined with SHAP analysis. Diagnostic performance was assessed, and biological relevance was explored through immune infiltration and pathway analyses. Experimental validation was conducted using qRT-PCR and western blot assays in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. InfC and ProFC were detected specifically in OA cartilage and exhibited high oxidative stress activity. InfC was enriched in inflammatory and immune-related pathways, whereas ProFC was associated with cell cycle regulation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Integrated hdWGCNA and machine-learning analyses consistently identified CYBA and SPP1 as candidate genes. The two-gene model achieved bootstrap-corrected AUCs of 0.937 and 0.825 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. qRT-PCR and western blot analyses further showed increased CYBA and SPP1 expression in H2O2-treated chondrocytes. Conclusion InfC and ProFC may represent OA-associated chondrocyte states characterized by enhanced oxidative stress, while CYBA and SPP1 may serve as candidate diagnostic biomarkers. Given the small cohort sizes and preliminary in vitro validation, these findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts and functional studies.

title: From public digital discourse to sustained engagement: Digital cultural translation of the Twenty-Four Solar Terms
abstract: Digital media can increase the visibility of living heritage without securing understanding or sustained engagement. We examined how public digital discourse about the Twenty-Four Solar Terms can be translated into an interpretive stimulus and how users evaluate it. We collected 3,433 publicly visible online text units and retained 1,101 after cleaning and anonymisation. The retained corpus informed collaborative thematic reading; 1,089 texts met the token threshold for keyword extraction and auxiliary topic-model inspection. Thematic analysis identified six cultural theme categories. They covered seasonal diet and bodily care; temporal order and heritage knowledge; and natural phenology and seasonal perception. They also covered folk customs and ritual life; aesthetic imagery and digital creative expression; and agricultural production and everyday practice. These categories informed a five-page storyboard through theme-design mapping and expert-assisted review. Survey data from 350 valid respondents were analysed with covariance-based structural equation modelling (CB-SEM) and supplementary fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). Information clarity, visual aesthetics, perceived explorability and perceived authenticity were positively associated with perceived cultural value. Perceived explorability had the largest standardised path estimate for cultural value, and perceived authenticity was also associated with cultural identity. Perceived cultural value and cultural identity were associated with sustained cultural engagement intention. Configurational analysis identified four sufficient configurations for high engagement and four for low engagement. The two solution sets were asymmetric rather than mirror images. These findings link perceived interpretive qualities, cultural value and cultural identity with sustained cultural engagement intention.

title: ANALYSIS OF GEOMETRIC ACCURACY OF GAOFEN-7 SATELLITE SCENES
abstract: The aim of this article was to investigate the quality and accuracy of images taken from the first Chinese civilian VHRS Gaofen-7 satellite. Visual evaluation of the images was carried out, in particular, to assess the remote sensing capabilities of objects with sizes comparable to the field size at the sampling distance (GSD). The main part of the experiment was geometric analysis, in which the distribution of errors in the positions of the measurement points relative to the aerial orthophoto was examined, divided by their distance from the sensor, including the imaging angle for forward and backward imaging. Distance measurement errors were also checked by measuring the differences in the length of individual objects in relation to their orientation and the image angle of view. The result was the determination of the average geometric accuracy at approximately this level. 10 m. The measurement accuracy of linear objects was close to the spatial resolution of the imagery, within the limits of the measurement error. The experiments proved that Gaofen-7 satellite scenes have measurement potential that approaches the sensor's spatial resolution, making them useful for the applications for which this system was designed.
journal: Archives of Photogrammetry, Cartography and Remote Sensing

title: High-Availability Architecture Patterns for Enterprise Network Management Platforms
abstract: The activities of telemetry-based network operations require continuous collection of increasingly precise measurements. Making operations effective requires creation of a complete and trackable route between telemetry creation and source semantics and analysis, decision-making, remediation, and verification of results. The architecture described in this paper serves this need by integrating a source-aware collection, transport reliability, canonical normalisation, multi-tier processing, evidence-based findings, and remediation that is governed by policies. Topology-aware correlation and event-time processing can provide the context by which it is possible to distinguish between real and delayed, duplicated, or unrelated observations. Well-defined data-quality indicators: Clear data-quality indicators and metrics are necessary to lessen the confidence of analytics with missing or incomplete telemetry rather than being based on the interpretation of an indication of an operational state. Further separation of fast, operational, and planning analytics enables various control loops to run based on their latency, computation, and risk sensitivity. Adaptive telemetry is another approach for balancing observability and resource efficiency. In situations where additional evidence is justified, a wide coverage is achieved by baseline collection, and the diagnostic and forensic modes are selective to narrow the data to a finer degree. Adaptive collection lacks the possibility of fairness limitations and guided transitions that would provide false feedback or take control over available resources. This is further divided between automated action and the results of analysis regarding the architecture. Evidence-based discoveries sum up paralleled observing and policy regulation verification to approve, trust, fulfils a deadline, blast radius, rollback claim, and file validation requirement before remediation. The approach complies with automation and warns against operating responsibility. In general, the idea of telemetry is most beneficial when gathering is geared toward clear operational choices as opposed to the dashboard or unlimited building of data. Future areas of work can delve deeper into the architecture by learning-based anomaly detection, more advanced models of confidence, auto-optimization of the policy, and standard evaluation of remediation results in a wide variety of network environments.
journal: International Journal of Advanced Engineering Science and Information Technology

title: Optimization of Spray Drying Parameters for Producing Red Pitahaya Powder Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: Research background. Red pitahaya (Hylocereus polyrhizus) is an exotic tropical fruit rich in antioxidants and betalains, but it is characterised by a relatively short shelf life. An effective and safe means of processing this fruit is the production of dehydrated products that can be readily reconstituted. Therefore, this study aimed to optimise the spray drying parameters for producing red pitahaya powder with suitable physicochemical and reconstitution properties. Experimental approach. Response surface methodology based on a central composite design was applied to evaluate the effects of inlet air temperature, feed flow rate and maltodextrin mass per volume ratio. The experimental data were modelled using a second-order polynomial equation to describe and predict the assessed responses: yield, moisture, water activity, hygroscopicity, flowability, cohesion and solubility. In the optimised sample, betalains, total phenols and antioxidant capacity were quantified as complementary quality indicators. Particle size and morphology were analysed using scanning electron microscopy. Results and conclusions. The quadratic models adequately described the main physicochemical responses, including yield, moisture content, water activity, flowability, cohesion and solubility. The selected processing conditions resulted in a powder with suitable physicochemical characteristics and reconstitution properties, including appropriate powder recovery, moisture content, water activity, flowability and solubility. The powder also showed measurable levels of betalains, phenolic compounds and antioxidant capacity. Microscopic observations revealed irregular particles with smooth surfaces and no visible cracks or fractures. Novelty and scientific contribution. The results demonstrate that inlet air temperature, feed flow rate and maltodextrin mass per volume ratio influenced the physicochemical and reconstitution properties of red pitahaya powder. The scientific contribution of this work lies in defining suitable processing conditions for a juice matrix rich in low-molecular-mass sugars and natural pigments, where powder recovery, moisture control, water activity, flowability and solubility must be balanced. These findings provide specific information for the production of red pitahaya powder with suitable technological properties and support its potential use as an ingredient in food formulations.

title: Bankruptcy Risk Analysis and Estimation of Healthy and Distressed Stocks Using Extended Black-Scholes Model
abstract: The classical Black-Scholes model assumes that stock prices follow a Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM) process, in which stock prices remain strictly positive throughout time. However, this assumption restricts the model’s capability to represent firms experiencing financial distress, where stock prices may gradually approach zero as bankruptcy risk increases. This study employs the Extended Black-Scholes Model (EBSM), which introduces a stoppingtime mechanism that enables stock prices to reach the bankruptcy boundary, to analyze and compare bankruptcy risk characteristics between financially healthy and distressed stocks. Historical adjusted closing price data from Microsoft Corporation (MSFT.US) and Bed Bath Beyond Inc. (BBBY.US) were utilized, with model parameters estimated using quadratic variation and Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) methods. The estimation results revealed different stochastic characteristics between the two stocks, where MSFT.US generated a positive drift parameter of 0.216682, whereas BBBY.US generated a negative drift parameter of −0.248385 along with higher volatility. The bankruptcy risk analysis demonstrated that MSFT.US produced infinite Expected Bankruptcy Time (EBT) and Conditional Expected Bankruptcy Time (CEBT) values, while BBBY.US yielded a finite EBT of 5.113633 years, with CEBT values updated according to the observed stock price conditions. These results suggest that the EBSM framework can effectively differentiate bankruptcy risk characteristics by combining stochastic stock price dynamics with time-to-bankruptcy measures.
journal: CAUCHY: Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi

title: Assessing the Role of AI Agents in DNA Methylation Analysis and Biomarker Discovery
abstract: DNA methylation biomarker development spans data discovery, assay-specific processing, marker selection, model development, and independent validation. Agentic systems could help coordinate these stages, but current studies use the term agent for systems with markedly different levels of autonomy and domain-specific evidence. We conducted a structured evidence synthesis, screening 2,801 unique records and organizing relevant systems along three dimensions: workflow autonomy (M0–M4), direct methylation-task evidence, and evidence maturity (E0–E5).Current systems cover complementary parts of the workflow. MethylCurate supports public methylation-data curation; AutoBA and BioMaster execute methylation-analysis pipelines; CpG Atlas provides a self-correcting query interface; and EpiBench, BixBench, and BixBench3 provide direct benchmark evidence for bounded methylation tasks. Across these studies, evidence is strongest for data access, workflow execution, and task-level evaluation. Among systems with task-level evidence reviewed here, we did not identify one that spans dataset discovery, marker selection, classifier development, independent validation, and sample-level uncertainty reporting within a single validated workflow.We therefore propose a matched evaluation framework comparing fixed workflows, rule-based routers, and general or domain-specific agents under shared data, tools, compute, and retry budgets. The framework separates execution reliability, scientific validity, replication, uncertainty, and resource use. Current evidence supports agentic components for methylation analysis, while end-to-end autonomous biomarker discovery remains an open evaluation problem.

title: Certified Tool Execution Framework for MCP-Based AI Agents: Provably Secure Defense Against Tool Poisoning and Credential Theft
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has emerged as the de facto standard for enabling Large Language Model (LLM) agents to interact with external tools, APIs, and databases. While MCP significantly extends agent capabilities, it introduces critical security vulnerabilities: tool poisoning attacks can inject malicious behavior into seemingly benign tools, and prompt injection can trick agents into leaking credentials or performing unauthorized actions. Current defense mechanisms—including prompt filtering, guardrails, and adversarial training—are heuristic and bypassable, with reported evasion rates reaching 100% against state-of-the-art systems.We present the Certified Tool Execution Framework (CTEF), the first provably secure defense against tool poisoning in MCP-based AI agents. CTEF employs a three-layer architecture: (1) capability-based access control (CAP-MCP) that enforces cryptographically unforgeable permissions, (2) formal pre/post-condition verification using Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solvers, and (3) sandboxed execution with syscall-level monitoring. We prove that CTEF achieves (ε, δ)-certified security, where ε < 2-128 represents the probability of accepting a poisoned tool and δ bounds the capability forgery risk.Through comprehensive evaluation on the MCP-Security benchmark comprising 50 benign and 30 poisoned tools across 6 attack categories, CTEF achieves 96.7% true positive rate and 3.2% false positive rate in poisoned tool detection—a 47% improvement over the next-best baseline. We establish theoretical sample complexity bounds showing that detecting a poisoned tool with violation probability, p requires Ω(1/p log 1/δ) samples. The framework incurs 2.3--8.7x execution overhead compared to unprotected MCP, acceptable for security-critical applications. CTEF enables safe deployment of autonomous AI agents in domains where tool integrity is paramount: healthcare decision support, financial trading, infrastructure management, and legal document processing. Our open-source implementation and benchmark are available on [anonymized for review].

title: Human-Centric HRC for Agriculture]{Design and Validation of a Human-Centric Human--Robot Collaboration System for Agriculture Using an AI-Driven Digital Twin
abstract: UK agriculture is facing an acute labour shortage, particularly on small farms where unpredictable and unstructured environments make automation difficult. Although robotic systems offer promising solutions, fully autonomous approaches remain costly and complex to implement. Human--Robot Collaboration provides a more practical alternative by combining human judgement with robotic assistance. This study investigates how digital twin-based simulation platforms can be designed to effectively model and optimise collaboration between humans and robots in complex agricultural settings. It also examines the performance trade-offs in vision and gesture-based collaboration systems, focusing on the balance between speed, accuracy and robustness, and explores the safety challenges related to recognising human intent and ensuring safe adaptive behaviour.To address these issues, a digital twin framework was constructed using the NVIDIA Omniverse platform, enabling the simulation of collaborative agricultural scenarios. The virtual testbed includes dynamic farm layouts, human models, and mobile robots equipped with RGB and LiDAR sensors to interpret gestures and actions with AI and a Vision-Language Model. Experimental results show high human detection accuracy (intersection over union up to 97%) and reliable robot responses to human guidance. This research presents the first virtual environment in agriculture that integrates human factors and intelligent robotic reasoning. The proposed framework provides a scalable, low-risk approach for developing, testing and optimising collaborative robotic systems, supporting wider adoption of intelligent automation in the farming sector.

title: Governing AI Coding Agents: An Empirical Analysis of Repository Artifacts
abstract: Purpose: Software projects are increasingly using repository-level governance artifacts, such as \texttt{CLAUDE.md} and \texttt{AGENTS.md}, to communicate project-specific guidance to AI coding agents. Although these artifacts have become an important mechanism for governing AI coding agents, little is known about the governance practices and liabilities they encode, or whether their observable characteristics are consistent with organizational governance capability. Method: To examine these questions, we conducted an exploratory sequential mixed-methods study of 555 AI agent governance artifacts collected from public GitHub repositories. Using Socio-Technical Grounded Theory for Data Analysis (STGT4DA), we developed taxonomies of governance practices and governance liabilities, which were converted into a structured codebook for LLM-based classification. The codebook was evaluated against manually coded reference labels and applied to the corpus to examine whether these artifacts exhibit observable characteristics theoretically associated with organizational governance capability. Results: The findings reveal that these artifacts primarily emphasize knowledge transfer, process guidance, and coding standards, whereas explicit oversight mechanisms, such as human approval gates, remain comparatively limited. The analysis also identifies recurring governance liabilities, most commonly vague instructions (36%) and fragmentation debt (35%). We found no systematic association between the governance observed in the artifacts and the repository maturity indicators examined in this study, nor did governance vary systematically across the application domains examined as broad proxies for potential operational consequences. The artifacts also showed limited evidence of characteristics associated with institutionalized governance, particularly regarding accountability mechanisms, coherence between governance content and governance quality, and project-specific adaptation. Conclusion: This study provides an empirical investigation of repository-level AI agent governance from an organizational capability perspective. By examining governance artifacts according to the governance functions they perform rather than solely the information they contain, the study develops taxonomies of governance practices and liabilities and an evaluated LLM-based classification approach for systematically characterizing AI agent governance in research and practice.
