title: Tomato- and olive-derived proteins, hydrolysates and peptides in anticancer research: molecular findings and research gaps.
abstract: Tomato and olive processing streams contain recoverable proteins, hydrolysates and peptides that have received far less attention than their carotenoids, phenolics and lipids. This review evaluates anticancer-related findings for these materials while separating direct anticancer-related experimental evidence, cancer-relevant mechanistic observations without a direct phenotype, general functional bioactivities and computational predictions. Molecular definition is considered separately from biological evidence. Tomato research includes a partially purified chitin-binding lectin preparation with tumor-related activity and cystine-knot miniproteins with antiangiogenic effects. Olive research includes antiproliferative seed hydrolysates and LLPSY, an isolated peptide tested in human cancer cells. The evidence is strongest in different areas: tomato includes defined antiangiogenic miniproteins tested through endothelial and zebrafish models, whereas olive includes a sequence-resolved peptide tested across several human cancer-cell endpoints. These differences reflect non-matched research designs and do not establish greater anticancer potential for either crop. Nevertheless, direct anticancer-related evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, and its interpretation is constrained by incomplete molecular definition of some active preparations, limited candidate-specific digestion and absorption data, and uncertainty regarding the physiological relevance of many in vitro exposure levels. Most other studies address protein recovery, peptide production, antioxidant or metabolic functions, or in silico prediction; these findings support candidate production or characterization but are not treated as anticancer evidence. Across both crops, the main gap is the incomplete connection between molecular identity, direct target validation, gastrointestinal fate and physiologically plausible in vivo exposure. Future work should strengthen reproducible production, identify the active components of complex preparations, test defined candidates mechanistically and connect biological activity with digestion, exposure and safety.

title: Swallowing Symptoms in Female FMR1 Premutation Carriers: Eating Assessment Tool-10 Findings and Associations With Genetic and FXTAS-Related Features.
abstract: PURPOSE The fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1) premutation (FXpm) is a prevalent genetic variant that confers risk for neurodegenerative motor impairments associated with fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS). Swallowing difficulties may be more common in FXpm carriers but remain understudied. This study investigates swallowing symptoms in FXpm women and their associations with FXTAS-related motor symptoms and FMR1-related genetic variation. METHOD Participants (85 FXpm women, 73 controls) completed the Eating Assessment Tool-10 and the FXTAS Rating Scale-Revised. Genetic measures included cytosine-guanine-guanine repeat length, activation ratio, and repeat size mosaicism. Hurdle models assessed group differences in symptom endorsement and severity. Item-level differences were examined, along with associations between swallowing symptom endorsement, motor scores, and genetic measures using logistic regression and exploratory correlations. RESULTS FXpm women were more likely to endorse swallowing symptoms than controls, particularly at lower education levels (OR = 0.68, 95% confidence interval [CI; 0.49, 0.93], p = .017). Effort swallowing solids and food sticking in the throat were the strongest item-level differentiators of the groups. Parkinsonian motor features (OR = 1.29, 95% CI [1.04, 1.59], p = .022) and premutation/full mutation (PM/FM) mosaicism (OR = 7.72, 95% CI [1.12, 53.30], p = .038) were associated with higher likelihood of symptom endorsement. CONCLUSIONS Findings suggest that some FXpm women, particularly those with lower educational attainment and PM/FM mosaicism, experience elevated swallowing symptom burden, which may reflect early manifestations of motor system involvement. Swallowing symptoms warrant greater clinical attention in this population, with further research integrating comprehensive swallowing assessments needed to clarify the nature, progression, and clinical significance of swallowing symptoms in FXpm women. SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34750941.

title: Real-world comparative outcomes of first-line immune combinations (ICI-ICI vs ICI-TKI) in metastatic renal cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Although first-line immune-based combinations have reshaped the management of metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), relevant unmet clinical needs remain. Sarcomatoid feature is a negative prognostic factor that confers sensitivity to immunotherapy, yet the optimal ICI combination in this subgroup is still unclear. METHODS The Meet-URO 33 is an Italian multicenter retrospective/prospective observational study enrolling patients with mRCC receiving first-line systemic therapy in routine clinical practice. In the present sub-analysis, objective response and survival outcomes were compared between ICI-ICI and ICI-TKI regimens in patients with documented sarcomatoid differentiation and IMDC intermediate-/poor-risk disease. RESULTS Among 1695 patients enrolled from 58 centers, 180 (10.6%) had sRCC and among them, 107 (58.2%) were intermediate-risk and 56 (30.4%) were poor-risk. With a median follow-up of 21.8 months, in the I/P-sRCC population with available data (n = 155), univariable analysis showed longer overall survival (OS) with ICI-ICI compared to ICI-TKI (HR 0.58, p = 0.04). However, in propensity score-weighted analyses, point estimates slightly favored ICI-ICI, but no statistically significant differences were observed for OS, PFS, or ORR. CONCLUSIONS In this real-world analysis comparing ICI-ICI and ICI-TKI in sarcomatoid mRCC, propensity score-weighted models showed no statistically significant differences between treatment combinations on clinical outcomes. These findings highlight the relevance of baseline disease and patients characteristics in shaping treatment outcomes and confirm the effectiveness of ICI-containing combinations in the treatment of sarcomatoid mRCC.

title: Long-Term Epidemiological Surveillance Integrated with Data Science and Multimodel Approaches Advances Understanding of Polerovirus SCYLV Dynamics in Colombian Sugarcane.
abstract: The Polerovirus Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) causes one of the most economically important viral diseases of sugarcane worldwide, including Colombia, where sugarcane is a strategic crop and the virus has high phytosanitary relevance but limited epidemiological characterization. This study provides the first integrative quantitative and multimodel epidemiological assessment of SCYLV in the country, using a 22-year surveillance dataset (1999 to 2020) from Colombia's main sugarcane-producing region. The analysis integrated data science, classical statistics, machine learning, and spatial epidemiology to identify temporal trends, spatiotemporal aggregation, and environmental and agronomic drivers of disease risk. Data science procedures supported data curation, exploratory analysis, and detection of patterns in SCYLV presence-absence, incidence, and prevalence across the historical series. Risk factor identification used logistic regression modeling of presence-absence data to estimate adjusted associations, and the machine learning framework modeled both presence-absence (classification) and incidence (regression) to capture nonlinear interactions. Spatiotemporal dynamics were assessed using presence-absence data in a space-time permutation model fitted to a Poisson-type distribution and the Knox test. SCYLV presence-absence and incidence were significantly associated with varietal susceptibility, with CC 01-1940 and SP 71-6949 showing the highest case burden climatic variability, with major outbreak clusters coinciding with strong El Niño-Southern Oscillation anomalies of both phases (El Niño in 2007 and 2015/2016 and the strong 2010/2011 La Niña), meteorological conditions (temperature, wind speed, and vapor pressure), vegetation greenness (normalized difference vegetation index), and soil properties (pH, cation exchange capacity, sand content, and nitrogen). The Knox test identified a high-risk spatiotemporal window for SCYLV spread, with relative risk > 10 concentrated within 4.5 km and 4 days after a confirmed positive case, highlighting a critical range for targeted surveillance and rapid preventive action. This integrative workflow provides a reproducible, data-driven foundation for delineating differential risk zones and supports evidence-based strategies for the integrated management of SCYLV in Colombian sugarcane systems, with transferable methodological value for long-term surveillance analyses of other aphid-transmitted viruses.

title: SERPINE2 At the Granulosa Cell-Matrix Interface: Emerging Mechanisms in Follicular Development and Ovarian Function.
abstract: Serpin family E member 2 (SERPINE2), also known as protease nexin-1, is a secreted serpin enriched in ovarian granulosa and cumulus-cell compartments. Its location is biologically important because follicle growth, selection, atresia and ovulation all require spatially controlled extracellular proteolysis. Recent experiments have begun to define how SERPINE2 is regulated and what it may do in the ovary. In human granulosa-lutein cells, bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) induces SERPINE2 through ALK3-dependent SMAD2/3-SMAD4 and p38 MAPK signaling and is accompanied by reduced production of urokinase- and tissue-type plasminogen activators. In buffalo granulosa cells, FOXL2 activates SERPINE2 transcription, whereas promoter-associated H3K9me3 is linked to its repression in atretic follicles; SERPINE2 perturbation affects proliferation, apoptosis and steroid output. In FecB-genotyped sheep granulosa cells, SERPINE2 alters TERT expression, relative telomere length, proliferation, ovulation-related genes and estradiol secretion. Together, these studies support a model in which intracellular differentiation and chromatin programmes converge on a secreted inhibitor that adjusts the extracellular proteolytic environment and thereby modifies granulosa-cell state. However, the causal chain from individual protease targets to matrix remodeling, receptor signaling and whole-animal fertility remains incomplete. WNT/beta-catenin and ERK1/2 are plausible downstream candidates, but their dependence on SERPINE2 has not been demonstrated in ovarian cells. This review integrates the direct ovarian evidence with follicular matrix biology, separates established mechanisms from tissue-extrapolated hypotheses, and defines experiments needed to determine whether SERPINE2 is principally a marker of follicular state, a local proteolytic buffer or a tractable regulator of ovarian function.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology

title: Born into opportunity, but not freedom: the inherited opportunity paradox in NextGen entrepreneurship
abstract: This paper addresses a neglected puzzle: next-generation members of business families (NextGens) may inherit resources for entrepreneurship while lacking psychological freedom to determine what those resources should become. It asks how family-derived business endowment can expand entrepreneurial capacity while constraining authorship of an entrepreneurial future. A problem-centered conceptual approach integrates family-business resource, embeddedness and governance research with paradox theory, career self-authorship, and self-determination theory. Construct differentiation and mechanism-based reasoning generate conditional propositions linking family-derived resources, entrepreneurial opportunity, prescriptions, self-authorship, motivation and outcomes. The model proposes that deployable family resources broaden entrepreneurial alternatives, while resource reliance strengthens prescriptions, particularly under salient family origin and conditional access. Prescriptions constrain career self-authorship when deviation carries credible sanctions. Self-authorship shapes motivational regulation, with distinct, conditional implications for passion, well-being, identity strain and entrepreneurial action. Perceived autonomy-supportive family governance weakens the constraining relationship. Longitudinal research should test construct distinctiveness, conditional relationships and reciprocal effects across career episodes. Multilevel extensions could examine family arrangements as antecedents of individual governance perceptions. Business families, advisors and educators should combine transparent resource-allocation criteria with meaningful NextGen participation and opportunities to negotiate entrepreneurial pathways. The paper explains how broad entrepreneurial opportunity can coexist with restricted career self-authorship. It distinguishes resource access from control and career authorization from motivational regulation, specifying conditions under which inherited advantage enables action while constraining its authorship.

title: The liquidation value of productive assets and product differentiation
abstract: This study aims to investigate the role of the secondary market for productive assets when firms compete in product differentiation. While it benefits firms by softening competition, the risk of asset relocation following bankruptcy reduces the incentive for product differentiation. This study develops a theoretical model integrating horizontal product differentiation with secondary market outcomes for productive assets. The choice of product differentiation is critically determined by entry cost in the industry, redeployment costs following productive asset acquisition and by the number of potential buyers in the secondary market. As the results are derived from a theoretical model with two incumbents, future research could assess their robustness in settings with multiple firms and validate the predicted link between secondary-market liquidity and product differentiation empirically. Regulatory interventions that promote liquidity in the secondary market for productive assets or lower entry barriers increase product variety, with implications for competition and antitrust policy. This study provides novel insights into the relation between product market competition and post-distress asset reallocation. The findings enhance the understanding of how potential entry through acquisition of productive assets in the secondary market affects incumbent firms’ choice on product differentiation.

title: DAC-Loop: Distillation-Aware Compression for Remote Sensing CNN
abstract: While large-scale models achieve strong results in remote sensing scene classification, deploying them on edge devices remains difficult due to limited compute, memory, and energy budgets. Compact CNN backbones are therefore a practical choice in many real-world settings, offering efficient inference with well-optimized implementations on embedded hardware. To push this efficiency further, we investigate how far a knowledge-distilled student model can be compressed while preserving high accuracy. We propose a Distillation-Aware Compression Loop (DAC-Loop) that integrates (i) knowledge distillation applied both before and after structured channel pruning, and (ii) an iterative compression schedule that alternates structured pruning with unstructured sparsification. Across EuroSAT and NWPU-RESISC45, the DAC-Loop consistently improves the accuracy-compression trade-off relative to standard one-shot pruning and single-stage KD recovery, maintaining strong accuracy even beyond 90% parameter reduction. These results demonstrate that combining distillation and pruning in a unified iterative loop offers an effective path toward compact remote sensing models.

title: BioSleepNet: Bio-Inspired Sleep Staging via Context Multimodal Fusion and Dynamic Temporal Memory
abstract: Existing sleep staging research faces several challenges, including poor multimodal feature fusion (MuFF), insufficient long-term dependency modeling, and weak adaptability to clinical staging logic. To address these issues, this study proposes an end-to-end multimodal sleep staging framework named BioSleepNet by leveraging the complementary characteristics of electroencephalogram (EEG) and electrooculogram (EOG) signals. Detailed, BioSleepNet incorporates three key modules. MuFF module performs differentiated feature extraction on EEG and EOG after fast Fourier transform (FFT) to raw signals, then fuses the extracted feature with adaptive weight, to achieve efficient cross-modal feature collaboration. The contextual temporal feature module uses a modern temporal convolutional network (ModernTCN) modeling contextual temporal features to capture dynamic characteristics of sleep. The momentum memory (MoM) module models long-term dependencies in temporal signals using a feature memory bank with attention-driven mechanisms, effectively capturing cross-cycle sleep continuity features. Considering the biological characteristics of difficult-to-model sleep transition rules and data imbalance across stages, we introduce a novel hybrid loss function named BioSleepLoss. BioSleepLoss significantly enhances the model’s adaptability to complex staging scenarios through learnable stage importance weights, dynamic difficulty-aware parameters, and adaptive transition probabilities. Experiments on the Sleep-EDF-20/78 datasets demonstrate overall accuracy of 89.3% and 87.1%, respectively, with a Kappa coefficient of 0.85 and stage sensitivity standard deviation below 1.5%, verifying the robustness and clinical consistency of the proposed method. Ablation studies and feature visualization validate the effectiveness of MuFF, contextual temporal feature modeling, the MoM module, and physiological constraint collaborative optimization, which jointly provide an efficient and clinically cognizant solution for automated sleep staging.

title: AoI-Aware and Trust-Driven Dynamic Pricing in Dispersed Computing: A Differential Game Approach
abstract: Dispersed computing (DCOMP) enables heterogeneous networked computation points (NCPs) to exchange and reuse information without centralized coordination. However, decentralized information trading requires simultaneous consideration of data freshness, provider trustworthiness, and transaction liquidity. In particular, myopic profit-oriented quotations can introduce excessive markups, inevitably triggering a macroscopic high-price deadlock that drastically reduces buyer acceptance and hinders timely information refreshment. This article proposes an Age-of-Information (AoI)-aware and trust-driven dynamic pricing framework for DCOMP networks. We formulate the interactions among NCPs as a state-coupled differential game in which AoI, trust, and long-term utility evolve under stochastic transactions and feedback-driven trust updates. The model incorporates a freshness premium that increases the valuation of trustworthy providers offering fresher information. We design the low-friction online heuristic algorithm (LF-OHA) to eliminate repeated solving of high-dimensional Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equations. LF-OHA leverages a local approximation of the AoI shadow price, a liquidity preference factor to structurally bypass the pricing deadlock, and introduces an entropy-regularized provider selection mechanism. Simulation results demonstrate that LF-OHA provides a favorable freshness–security–liquidity tradeoff. Compared with the state-of-the-art baselines, it achieves low steady-state AoI and the lowest observed bad-data exposure while retaining high transaction completion performance and low service latency. Moreover, under fixed per-node load, LF-OHA preserves trust differentiation, bounded AoI, transaction liquidity, and security behavior as the network size scales to 1000 NCPs.

title: AdaTrendLike: Adaptive Hierarchical Detrending and Trend Likelihood Scoring for Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Industrial Internet of Things devices has led to increasingly large-scale and non-stationary time-series data, posing significant challenges for time-series anomaly detection (TSAD). Existing approaches often focus on reconstructing or forecasting observations while overlooking the role of trend dynamics, which constitute a major source of non-stationarity and contain valuable information for anomaly identification. To address this limitation, we propose AdaTrendLike, a TSAD framework that directly estimates trend likelihoods for anomaly detection. Specifically, we introduce Standardization Embedding to capture local statistical characteristics as latent representations and AdaDetrending to adaptively decompose input series into trend and detrended components. The detrended component is processed through a Fast Fourier Transform and a complex-valued convolutional neural network to learn normal periodic patterns, while TrendEst models the distribution of the trend component. Based on the estimated distribution, TrendLike computes anomaly scores by measuring the likelihood of observed trends, enabling effective detection of deviations from normal behavior. In addition to improving detection performance, the proposed framework provides feature-level interpretability by identifying anomalies through deviations in the estimated trend distribution. Extensive experiments on five public benchmark datasets demonstrate that AdaTrendLike consistently outperforms state-of-the-art TSAD methods, validating its effectiveness and robustness across diverse application scenarios.

title: A Behavioral-Strategic Market Mechanism for Energy Sharing: Integrating LLM-Driven Bounded Rationality With Regulatory Optimization
abstract: Energy sharing markets facilitate collaborative energy exchange among prosumers, yet their theoretical efficiency is often compromised by bounded rationality. Existing regulatory mechanisms, predicated on the assumption of perfect rationality, mathematically mask this non-linear cognitive friction, leaving grid operators vulnerable to unstructured behavioral instabilities. To bridge this gap, we propose a Bi-Level Regulatory Optimization Framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) as a “surrogate behavioral stress-testing” environment. Unlike traditional models that rely on static utility functions, the lower level employs Neuro-Symbolic Agents to inject heuristic-driven bounded rationality, acting as a sandbox that exposes latent market vulnerabilities ignored by convex optimization. The upper level utilizes derivative-free Bayesian Optimization (BO) to autonomously navigate this non-differentiable cognitive feedback and discover a deterrence-based regulatory policy. Empirical evaluations using the real-world physical net-load dataset from Madeira Island substantiate the framework’s efficacy. The experiments validate that the optimized dynamic volatility tax operates effectively via deterrence, steering heuristic agents to voluntarily correct cognitive failures (e.g., converting speculative trading into a strategic retreat). This mechanism achieves a robust market equilibrium, reducing price volatility ( $\sigma _{\lambda }$ ) by 84.6% and successfully withstanding the unstructured behavioral unpredictability inherent in decentralized energy communities.

title: State-Awareness-Based Adaptive Restoration for Differential-Interconnected MV-LV Distribution Networks
abstract: Frequent extreme disasters exacerbate cyber-physical coupled faults in distribution networks. Traditional centralized restoration methods are inadequate for these complex faults, severely limiting network resilience improvement. This paper proposes a state-awareness-based adaptive restoration method for the cyber-physical MV-LV distribution networks. To begin with, a multi-state-awareness model is established for the first time to identify observable & controllable (OC), observable & uncontrollable (OU), and unobservable & uncontrollable (UU) states. Subsequently, a differentiated restoration framework is constructed by leveraging the complementary characteristics of MV-LV distribution networks. Furthermore, an innovative adaptive centralized-decentralized restoration model is proposed to address the dynamic evolution of post-fault network states and facilitate a smooth transition from decentralized restoration during communication failures to centralized restoration after emergency communication establishment. Finally, simulation results on the 53-node and 139-node MV-LV distribution networks validate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving network resilience.

title: Advanced Functional Packaging Strategies for Postharvest Fruit Preservation: From Physiological Regulation to Intelligent Monitoring.
abstract: Postharvest fruits are highly susceptible to rapid senescence and microbial decay, a process primarily driven by intense respiration and endogenous ethylene signaling. While conventional packaging provides basic physical protection, the shift towards multi-component functional interfaces offers dynamic solutions for physiological regulation. This review provides a critical analysis of advanced functional packaging strategies, focusing on the synergistic integration of natural biopolymers, deep eutectic solvents (DESs), and nanoporous structures. We dissect the intrinsic mechanisms by which these materials modulate the microenvironment dynamics, particularly the precise control of O2/CO2/C2H4 fluxes and moisture migration, and their impact on fruit oxidative stress markers and metabolic pathways. Furthermore, we evaluate the feasibility of transitioning from passive barriers to stimulus-responsive intelligent systems, highlighting the convergence of flexible sensors, radio frequency identification (RFID) data acquisition, and machine-learning models that together enable real-time quality monitoring throughout the supply chain. Finally, we analyze the trade-off between the large-scale application of bio-based materials and the precision of active ingredient release, and further highlight how divergent regulatory frameworks for food-contact materials in major markets (e.g., the European Union, the United States, and China) constrain industrial application. Based on the collaborative assessment of the above-mentioned technical and institutional bottlenecks, differentiated breakthrough paths have been discussed to provide a roadmap for the development of sustainable, high-performance preservation technologies after harvest.
journal: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

title: Immunomodulation and Reparative Dentinogenesis by the Wnt Agonist Peptide L803-Mts In Vitro and In Vivo.
abstract: AIM Materials used for conventional vital pulp therapy (VPT) promote dentine barrier formation but do not harness the intrinsic regenerative potential of the dental pulp. This study tested the hypothesis that L803-mts, a glycogen synthase kinase (GSK)-3β inhibitory peptide, (i) enhances odontogenic differentiation of dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and modulates macrophage pro-inflammatory responses under inflammatory conditions in vitro; and (ii) promotes reparative dentinogenesis in vivo at levels comparable to mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA). METHODOLOGY DPSC monocultures and DPSC-macrophage co-cultures were treated with L803-mts under inflammatory conditions (1 μg/mL lipopolysaccharide). Odontogenic differentiation was assessed by alkaline phosphatase activity, gene expression, alizarin red staining, and Western blotting. Macrophage polarization was evaluated by flow cytometry and enzyme linked immunosorbent assay. Reparative dentinogenesis was assessed in vivo in a rat pulp injury model using micro-computed tomography, histology, and immunofluorescence. Statistical significance was set at p 0.05), with lower mineral volume (0.03 vs. 0.06 mm3; p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS L803-mts promoted reparative dentinogenesis through Wnt signalling activation and immunomodulation, supporting its potential as a biologically driven candidate for VPT.

title: Knowing When to Escalate: Disagreement Patterns for Uncertainty-Aware Content Moderation
abstract: Agentic content-moderation systems increasingly rely on collective judgments from LLM agents, while aggregation methods commonly treat inter-agent disagreement as a reliability problem to be removed through consensus or voting. This framing is inappropriate for value-laden tasks, where disagreement may reflect irreducible value pluralism - a distinction standard uncertainty decompositions cannot recover, since they operate on output distributions and discard the reasoning behind each judgment. We propose Reasoning Trace Divergence Analysis (RTDA), which embeds model-generated justifications from perspective-differentiated agents and classifies each case by justification similarity and conclusion agreement. The resulting four-state taxonomy isolates convergent disagreement, where agents reasoning similarly but concluding differently, as a candidate signature of value-laden conflict. On 1,000 items from the Measuring Hate Speech corpus, this structural signal predicts human annotator disagreement better than magnitude-only and output-only baselines. We contribute a design principle: condition human escalation on the structure of disagreement, not its magnitude alone, with RTDA serving as a post-processing layer for systems that already generate reasoning traces.

title: Separating Safety from Preference in Clinical LLM Evaluation
abstract: Conversational AI increasingly answers patients' rehabilitation questions, but a fluent, well-liked answer can still be clinically unsafe, and preference-only evaluation hides this by collapsing many judgments into one winner. We ran a human-centered evaluation of the mRehab Advisory Agent with two cohorts in distinct roles: six domain experts rate clinical safety and correctness, and three end users rate helpfulness, affect, and clarity, alongside blinded best-to-worst rankings exported as provenance-rich records. In a 200-question pilot (435 ranked triples), raters ranked the agent first most often (53.3%; p < 0.001), yet it led on affect and clarity, not helpfulness, and drew the lowest expert safety rate (88.8% vs. 93.7% for two GPT-4.1 mini comparators). That gap traced to a single expert with near-zero agreement, so it points to rater calibration rather than an unsafe agent, and catching it depended on recording safety separately from preference. As these agents take on more patient guidance, the gap between what sounds good and what is safe will only grow, and evaluations that keep both signals will matter more than leaderboards that report one.
journal: Proceedings of the 4th International Workshop on Human-Centered Sensing, Modeling, and Intelligent Systems

title: Salivary 1H NMR metabolic profiling of diabetic patients with and without periodontitis: an exploratory pilot study
abstract: Periodontitis is a widespread chronic inflammatory condition that frequently coexists with diabetes mellitus (DM). Identifying non-invasive biomarkers is essential for early detection, targeted therapy, and better understanding of the bidirectional relationship between these two diseases. This study aimed to investigate salivary metabolomic profiles in diabetic individuals with and without periodontitis to identify candidate metabolites associated with periodontitis in patients with diabetes. This pilot study compared salivary 1H NMR metabolomic profiles of patients with diabetes with and without periodontitis (n = 13 per group). Unstimulated whole saliva was collected from both groups. Partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) was applied to differentiate between the groups. Spectral variables with VIP > 1 were selected for metabolite annotation, followed by metabolite set enrichment analysis (MSEA) to identify dysregulated metabolic pathways. Using the PLS-DA model, a total of 78 discriminating variables were identified, leading to the annotation of ten key metabolites: glycolic acid, thymidine, tyramine, deoxyguanosine, cytidine, uridine, NADPH, ADP, serotonin, and nicotinate. MSEA revealed significant pathway disturbances, with pyrimidine metabolism emerging as a notably enriched pathway. The metabolomics study of saliva using 1H NMR showed distinct metabolic disturbances, particularly in pyrimidine metabolism, in diabetic periodontitis. Although these altered metabolites could serve as potential candidates for non-invasive biomarkers, independent validation from a large cohort is still required before they can be translated into clinical diagnostic use.

title: Uterine function and reproduction aging. I. Molecular and structural alterations associated with impaired decidualization in aged mouse uteri
abstract: Reproductive aging is associated with reduced fertility and increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including miscarriage, placental dysfunction, and fetal growth restriction. While age-related decline in oocyte quality contributes to early pregnancy loss, uterine dysfunction is recognized as a critical determinant of pregnancy success, particularly for complications arising after implantation of blastocysts. However, the mechanisms by which uterine aging impairs post-implantation blastocyst development remain unclear. We tested the hypothesis that reproductive aging limits decidual growth through impaired progesterone (P4) responsiveness and fibrotic remodeling. An artificial decidualization model with young and aged virgin mice was used to isolate uterine-specific effects independent of ovarian and embryonic factors. The results indicate that reproductive aging markedly reduced decidual expansion. Aged decidualized uteri exhibited impaired progesterone receptor (PGR) expression and spatial dysregulation and reduced expression of P4-responsive genes. Transcriptomic profiling of decidualized uteri revealed coordinated suppression of stromal differentiation, cell-cycle, growth-factor, and extracellular matrix (ECM)-remodeling programs together with broader changes in stress, immune, and metabolic pathways. Primary stromal cells from aged uteri showed reduced proliferative capacity and attenuated induction of decidualization-associated genes. Histological analyses demonstrated increased accumulation of fibrillar Type I and III collagens and impaired ECM remodeling. These findings provide an integrated molecular, cellular, and structural framework linking impaired P4 responsiveness, stromal dysfunction, and fibrotic remodeling to reduced decidual growth during reproductive aging. Reproductive aging is associated with impaired decidual growth accompanied by altered progesterone signaling, reduced stromal cell responsiveness, and fibrotic extracellular matrix remodeling under controlled hormonal conditions.

title: Local ecological and farmer varietal knowledge of chickpea (Cicer arietinum) in Bni Garfett, northwestern Morocco with implications for on-farm conservation
abstract: Msellek W, Labeyrie V, Hmimsa Y, Barkaoui K, Leclerc C, El Fatehi S. 2026. Local ecological and farmer varietal knowledge of chickpea (Cicer arietinum) in Bni Garfett, northwestern Morocco with implications for on-farm conservation. Asian J Ethnobiol 9 (2): y090217. https://doi.org/10.13057/asianjethnobiol/y090217. Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an important crop in Bni Garfett, northwestern Morocco, but climate variability threatens its production; however, the value of farmers’ knowledge has not been reported. This study aimed to examine how local ecological knowledge shapes chickpea varietal classification, management practices, and adaptive responses to climatic stress. An ethnobiological approach combined an initial crop-diversity survey of 110 farmers with a detailed survey of 168 chickpea farmers across 11 villages and systematic field observations. Data were collected on cultivated varieties, farmer-based criteria for varietal differentiation, local agronomic practices, and perceptions of climate change. Qualitative information was thematically organized, and descriptive statistical analyses were performed using R software. Chickpea was cultivated by 75.5% of households in the initial survey, while the detailed survey identified three principal local varieties, i.e., Garbanssa (RFC = 0.61), Rkik (RFC = 0.33), and Metwesset (RFC = 0.16), each associated with specific agronomic and adaptive characteristics. Farmers primarily distinguish varieties based on seed size (78%) and seed color (40%), reflecting a functional classification system linked to performance and use. These varieties are subject to diverse climatic stresses, including irregular rainfall and temperature fluctuations. On-farm conservation is conducted by the farmers in northwestern Morocco by employing diverse adaptive practices that help maintain varietal diversity and enhance resilience within local agroecosystems. These findings highlight the role of local ecological knowledge in conserving chickpea diversity and strengthening climate adaptation.

title: Geospatial Analysis of LST and UHI Variability in Relation to Land Use/Land Cover Changes in Anambra State, Nigeria
abstract: Rapid urbanization and land use/land cover (LULC) changes have significantly altered land surface temperature (LST) patterns and intensified urban heat island (UHI) effects, particularly in rapidly developing regions of sub-Saharan Africa. This study aims to analyze the spatial variability of LST and UHI in relation to LULC changes across urban and rural areas of Anambra State, Nigeria. The study integrates Landsat 8 satellite imagery (2019 and 2024), Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Model (DEM), and geospatial analysis techniques. We classified LULC using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm and derived LST from thermal infrared bands using the Multi-Window Algorithm (MWA) with NDVI-based emissivity correction. UHI intensity was estimated using statistical threshold methods based on mean LST and standard deviation. Results indicate a 15.1% expansion of built-up areas, particularly in urban centres such as Onitsha, Nnewi, and Awka, leading to LST values exceeding 35.68°C and UHI intensities up to 30.59°C. In contrast, rural areas such as Ayamelum, Ogbaru, and Anambra West exhibited lower temperatures (below 31.37°C), attributed to higher vegetation cover and proximity to water bodies. However, ongoing deforestation and agricultural expansion have contributed to moderate temperature increases in rural regions. The study concludes that LULC changes are a primary driver of thermal variability in Anambra State. Sustainable land-use planning, afforestation, and climate-responsive urban design are essential for mitigating UHI effects and enhancing environmental resilience.

title: Microscale Lyapunov contraction precedes macroscopic seismic rupture in simulations
abstract: Introduction: Laboratory and numerical studies show that fault complexity, quantified by the Kaplan–Yorke dimension (effective number of dynamical degrees of freedom), can decrease as stress and load increase, but the reason remains uncertain. Materials and methods: We analyze a synthetic seismic cycle from a previously validated heterogeneous-rupture model: moment magnitude M W (macroscopic earthquake size) and its perturbation response Δ M W (magnitude change after a small energy increase). A thermodynamic estimate gives Λ , the sum of all Lyapunov exponents, which measure whether nearby states diverge (expansion) or converge (contraction). In sliding windows of W = 100 samples, k -nearest neighbors (KNN) forecasts yield a finite-horizon stability descriptor λ ^ M W , the slope of log forecast error versus forecast horizon. λ ^ M W is positive, negative or zero when errors grow (expansion), shrink (contraction) and are neutral, respectively. As M W is macroscopic, subtracting λ ^ M W from Λ leaves a residual λ R , the microscopic part. Slopes require straight-line fits (coefficient of determination R 2 ≥ 0.98, normalized mean absolute error ≤ 0.08) over four or more early horizons; robustness is tested with W = 80 and W = 120. title: Opportunity in the Age of Agents: How Generative AI Changes Opportunity Recognition, Evaluation and Creation
abstract: Entrepreneurship theory explains how opportunities are recognised, evaluated and created, but it models every stage of that process as exclusively human. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) now participates in all three stages: founders use large language models as co-ideators that generate opportunity candidates and as drafting partners that develop them, while investors use the same class of models to screen founders' submissions. This conceptual paper integrates opportunity theory (discovery, creation and effectuation) with the emerging empirical evidence on generative AI and ideation, creativity, evaluation and entrepreneurial performance. It argues that the co-ideator changes the opportunity process in four ways: it expands each founder's supply of candidates while compressing ideation skill gaps; it correlates opportunity pools across founders who draw on shared models, creating a homogenisation risk at market level; it raises the returns to prior knowledge, which governs selection among abundant machine-generated candidates; and it migrates durable advantage from generating opportunities to selecting, combining and enacting them. These claims are stated as seven formal propositions with boundary conditions, including the "jagged opportunity frontier" and the evaluation asymmetries produced by narrative AI explanations, with implications for founders, investors and educators, and a research agenda.

title: Farmers’ Knowledge Capacity Regarding Digital Communication in Response to the Use of Platforms for the Proposal and Distribution of Subsidized Fertilizers
abstract: This study aims to determine farmers' digital communication skills and their responses to the use of this platform for the proposal and distribution of subsidized fertilizers, and the factors influencing their situation. The study was conducted in the Agricultural Extension Center (BPP) Ambulu work area, a rice-growing center in Jember Regency. The study employed a non-experimental quantitative approach with a survey research design. Data were analyzed using descriptive frequency analysis and multiple linear regression analysis. The results indicate that most farmers have high to very high levels of digital communication skills. These skills are influenced by years of farming experience, income, and interactions with extension workers. Close and frequent interactions between extension workers and farmers are essential for facilitating information exchange and strenghtening farmers’ digital communication skills, particularly among farmers with limited farming experience and lower incomes.

title: Teleoneutrosophic Logic for Three-Way Authorisation of Institutional AI Agents
abstract: An institutional artificial intelligence (AI) agent may encounter an instruction to issue a refund inside a petition it was asked to summarise. The same tool call may be legitimate when requested by an officer and unauthorised when induced by that petition. We address this distinction with teleoneutrosophic values, pairing separate neutrosophic triples for effect and purpose. A provenance discount and evidence fusion feed a guard that authorises, escalates or denies a proposed call. We characterise paraconsistency and adjunction in the induced matrix logic and prove conditional limits on untrusted influence. With reliable labels and call attribution, a source cannot supply purpose support above its trust cap, and untrusted evidence cannot justify denial. Tests on 1,054 InjecAgent attack cases and synthetic e-government scenarios show where grading helps and where crisp protection suffices. On low-trust channels, the guard can reduce to taint-and-escalate; an attribution-based plan/data rule is at least as safe. Retaining ambivalence about an unrequested call reduces worst-case direct-harm pass-through after channel mislabelling from 100\% to 34.5\% on InjecAgent and 25.0\% on the synthetic benchmark. A learned estimator that omits the trust label reduces direct-harm pass-through under ordinary mislabelling from 36.7\% to 1.6\%. The results identify a role for independent ambivalence in provenance-aware authorisation and expose the limits on automation when legitimate external requests are missing from training data.
