We propose QS-IE, a knowledge extraction method constrained by quantity and operation scope. Its unit of extraction is a complete quantitative fact. Given a shared set of numeric candidates and a single base model, QS-IE selects complete candidates from several prompting strategies, verifies them against the source text, and applies scope constraints, so that every extracted quantity stays linked to its source evidence. We built a corpus of 4006 texts on tomato cultivation. Two researchers with agronomy backgrounds jointly annotated and reviewed 1000 of them; the other 3006 were annotated with large language model assistance and then reviewed by hand. The corpus was split into 3206 development texts and 800 independent test texts. On the 1152 reference facts of the test set, QS-IE reached a precision of 84.02%, a recall of 86.72%, and a micro-averaged F1 of 85.35%, which is 3.91 percentage points higher than the strongest baseline, a multi-strategy in-context learning ensemble. Removing the operation scope constraints lowered test F1 by 8.24 percentage points. In a sampled human audit of the test set, 82.00% of the outputs for texts containing target facts were judged usable, and all six engineering checks on storage and evidence traceability were passed. The results indicate that explicit association constraints make quantitative facts extracted from tomato cultivation texts more complete and easier to review, which supports the structured, traceable storage of experiential knowledge that experts express in non-standardized text.

title: Interpreting Short Tandem Repeat Variations with Plant Genomic Foundation Models in Olive
abstract: Short tandem repeats (STRs) are highly mutable, multiallelic variants with distinctive mutation dynamics and have been associated with phenotypic variation across diverse species. However, genome-wide STR variation remains poorly characterized in olive, and the large number of naturally occurring alleles creates a challenge for variant interpretation. Genomic language models offer a potential way to assess how STR length changes alter learned sequence representations, but their responses to natural multiallelic STR series have not been systematically evaluated. Here, we identified 117,119 polymorphic STRs across 212 Iranian and Mediterranean olive accessions. STRs recovered the major SNP-defined ancestry axes while resolving additional geographically structured subcomponents. We then quantified STR-induced embedding perturbation using three plant genomic language models: AgroNT, PlantCAD2, and GPN. Across all three models, embedding distance generally increased with repeat-length difference from the reference allele, and 7,417 loci were embedding-sensitive in all three models. These signals were robust to fixed-length input construction and exceeded those of matched nonrepetitive indels at most tested loci. Integration with oil-composition associations prioritized four exploratory loci supported by all three models. Overall, we provide a genome-wide olive STR resource and show that plant genomic language models capture reproducible responses to natural STR length variation. Combining cross-model embedding evidence with phenotype association provides a potential framework for prioritizing candidate STRs for further investigation.

title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models
abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

title: Using Diffusion Similarity Networks to Identify, Track, and Predict Movement Disorders
Economic Empowerment of Women Through the Processing of Household Waste into Marketable Products
abstract: Household waste is usually framed as an environmental burden, yet a growing body of community-based initiatives treats it as a raw material through which women can earn income and gain voice. This article examines how the processing of household and domestic waste into marketable products contributes to women's economic empowerment, and what conditions separate short-lived training projects from durable livelihoods. Using a systematic literature review, records were retrieved from the Consensus academic database, deduplicated, and screened against inclusion criteria covering publication between 2021 and 2026, an active DOI, a focus on women, and an explicit link between waste processing and economic value. Twenty studies met the criteria and were synthesised thematically, supported by five recent conceptual and empirical sources. The review identifies five value pathways: organic and biological conversion, plastic and packaging upcycling, textile and agricultural residue crafts, mixed household recyclables, and collective collection services. Across these pathways, empowerment advances through four mechanisms: skill acquisition, product diversification, market and digital access, and collective organisation. However, most evidence comes from short community-service programmes that report outputs rather than measured income or agency. The article proposes a Household Waste-to-Value Empowerment framework and argues that market linkage and collective institutions, not technical training alone, determine whether waste becomes a sustained source of women's economic power
journal: Archipel: Journal of Indonesian Interdisciplinary Studies

title: Predictive Ability of Psychological Alienation in Futsal Players
abstract: The present study sought to uncover the extent of psychological alienation and sporting ambition among futsal athletes, while also determining the relationship between these two variables and constructing a predictive model through a regression equation to forecast sporting ambition based on the facets of psychological alienation. The investigator employed a descriptive methodology incorporating both relational and predictive techniques to align with the research aims. The study population comprised futsal club athletes during the sports season, and the foundational sample was randomly chosen from 56 individuals. The investigator employed two validated psychological scales (honesty and consistency) to gather data: the first scale measured psychological alienation with 20 items across two dimensions, while the second assessed sports ambition level with 36 items across four domains. The statistical analyses were conducted utilising the Social Sciences Statistical Package (SPSS v27), employing: arithmetic means, standard deviations, t-tests for two independent samples and one sample, Pearson correlation coefficient, and Stepwise Multiple Regression analysis. The findings additionally indicated a statistically significant negative association between the two variables. The regression analysis yielded the development of a statistically significant prediction model, wherein the facets of psychological alienation accounted for 65.9% of the total variance in mathematical ambition (R^2 = 0.659). The aspect of handicap and the erosion of mathematical comprehension had the most significant adverse effect on forecasting aspiration, succeeded by the factors of isolation and psychological irregularity. Given the findings, a linear predictive model was developed to assess ambition levels concerning alienation, and the researcher advocated for the implementation of psychological sports counselling and the utilization of the predictive model by technical organizations as a preventative diagnostic instrument to safeguard players' motivational frameworks.

title: Ai Agents in Game Development Using an Engine or Specialized Libraries
Artificial Intelligence Applications in Fruit Production, Harvesting and Postharvest Quality: A Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a tool for improving decision-making across fruit production and postharvest management. However, evidence regarding its applications, reported performance, and practical limitations remains distributed across different fruit crops, sensing technologies, and computational approaches. This review systematically examines the applications of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, robotics, the Internet of Things (IoT), and remote sensing in fruit science. Relevant publications were identified through searches of [databases used] covering the period from [start year] to [end year], using predefined search terms and eligibility criteria. Of the [number] records identified, [number] studies were included in the final synthesis. The selected literature was categorised into precision orchard management, pest and disease detection, fruit detection and yield estimation, robotic harvesting, non-destructive quality assessment, and postharvest handling. The synthesis compares the reported performance of AI models, their application across fruit crops, the sensing technologies employed, and the principal limitations affecting field implementation. Particular attention is given to quantitative outcomes reported for detection accuracy, prediction performance, harvesting efficiency, resource use, and fruit quality assessment. The review also evaluates challenges associated with dataset availability, model generalization, computational requirements, sensor integration, and deployment under variable orchard conditions. Emerging approaches, including edge AI, multimodal data fusion, explainable AI, and autonomous orchard systems, are discussed in relation to the limitations identified in existing studies. By connecting reported experimental outcomes with implementation constraints, this review identifies evidence-based research priorities for developing reliable and scalable AI applications in fruit production and postharvest management.
journal: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology

title: Rice and Wheat Straw for Biofuel and Bioenergy Production: Implementation Evidence, Environmental Sustainability, and Scale-Up Gaps in Selected Countries
abstract: Aim: To evaluate rice- and wheat-residue biofuel pathways through documented implementation cases in India, China, Italy, Denmark, the United States, and Canada, with emphasis on evidence maturity, environmental trade-offs, and scale-up constraints. Approach: A structured comparative narrative review integrated peer-reviewed conversion and life-cycle studies with dated government, laboratory, and facility records. Each numerical observation was classified as measured operation, anticipated process performance, nameplate capacity, historical use, or modelled outcome. Mixed-feedstock attribution and variation in life-cycle assessment boundaries were considered explicitly. Findings: The Panipat plant in India was announced with a design basis of approximately 200,000 tonnes of rice straw and 30 million litres of ethanol per year; the associated 300,000 tonnes of CO₂-equivalent annual avoidance remains a government projection. In Qingpu, China, documented 2020 co-digestion of 2,125 tonnes of dry rice straw and 142 tonnes of fresh manure yielded 442,015 m³ biogas and 662,475 kWh electricity. The historical Tianguan demonstration had a reported capacity, rather than verified annual output, of 3,000 tonnes ethanol per year. Industrial lignocellulosic processing capacity was documented at Crescentino, Italy, whereas Denmark reported an expected ethanol yield exceeding 198 litres per dry tonne of wheat straw in earlier demonstration work. American and Canadian examples show why commissioning, government-fleet use, and later commercial continuity must be evaluated separately. Conclusions: Rice and wheat residues can support renewable fuels and integrated biorefineries, but crop-residue production is not equivalent to a sustainably harvestable supply. Climate and economic outcomes depend on the management baseline, soil-carbon and nutrient requirements, feedstock logistics, process inputs, coproduct treatment, and verifiable operating continuity. The six cases illustrate heterogeneous pathways rather than national or global adoption rates.
journal: Journal of Geography, Environment and Earth Science International

title: Finite Element-Based Stress Analysis of the Main Frame of a Battery-Operated Lathyrus Harvester
abstract: Lathyrus (Lathyrus sativus L.) is a climate-resilient pulse grown mainly as a relay crop in rice fallows, but it is still harvested by hand, a slow, labour-intensive and physically demanding process. A battery-operated lathyrus harvester was therefore developed, and this study evaluated the structural safety of its main frame, the principal load-bearing component, using finite element analysis (FEA). A three-dimensional model of the frame was analysed in ANSYS Workbench 2024 R1 under static loads representing field operation, namely the weight of the battery, motor and transmission, the cutting resistance of lathyrus stems and the inertial force of the reciprocating knife. Structural steel properties were assigned, and support reactions, equivalent elastic strain, directional deformation and von Mises stress were evaluated. The maximum von Mises stress was 223.92 MPa, confined to a critical joint region and below the 250 MPa yield strength of the material, giving a minimum factor of safety of 1.12. The maximum equivalent elastic strain was 0.0011939 m/m and was limited to local stress-concentration zones, while most of the frame showed negligible strain. The frame deflected like a cantilever, with a maximum upward displacement of 11.995 mm at the free end and a maximum downward displacement of 8.913 mm near the restrained region. The frame is therefore safe against yielding under static field loads, but the narrow safety margin and the free-end deflection show that local reinforcement is needed to resist dynamic loads and keep the cutter bar aligned. The study demonstrates that FEA is an effective, low-cost tool for designing lightweight battery-operated harvesters for small farms.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Growth, Trend and Decomposition Analysis of Garlic in Rajasthan State, India (2005–06 to 2024–25)
abstract: This study examines changes in garlic cultivation in Rajasthan from 2005–06 to 2024–25, with emphasis on cultivated area, production, productivity and the factors contributing to production growth. Secondary time-series data were analysed using absolute and relative changes, coefficients of variation, linear growth rates and a decomposition model that separates area, yield and interaction effects. The analysis covers 20 agricultural years and focuses on the aggregate indicators reported for Rajasthan rather than district-level variation. The reported area increased from 22,392 to 69,471, representing a relative increase of approximately 210%. Production rose from 113,980 to 423,012, equivalent to approximately 271% growth. Reported productivity increased from 5.09 to 6.08, an increase of approximately 19.45%. Variation was greatest for production (60.53%), followed by area (50.50%) and productivity (14.58%). The estimated linear growth rates were 1.57% for area, 2.63% for production and 2.52% for productivity, with the manuscript reporting statistical significance at the 5% level for all three indicators. Decomposition attributed 77.54% of the total production change to area expansion, 15.22% to the interaction between area and yield, and 7.24% to the yield effect. These findings indicate that cultivated-area expansion accounted for most of the increase in garlic production, although improvements in productivity also contributed. The results suggest that measures aimed at improving crop yield warrant attention alongside continued assessment of production trends in Rajasthan.
journal: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

title: Probiotic Extracellular Vesicles Enable Oral Alendronate Therapy for Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis.
abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) involves impaired bone remodeling, intestinal dysbiosis, and immune imbalance, which together limit the long-term benefit of conventional oral bisphosphonate therapy. Here, we report LpEVs@ALN, a probiotic extracellular vesicle-based oral nanoplatform constructed by loading alendronate (ALN) into Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-derived extracellular vesicles. LpEVs@ALN maintains vesicle integrity and epithelial compatibility, improves ALN retention under acidic exposure, and enables sustained ALN release at intestinal pH conditions. In dexamethasone-suppressed BMSCs, LpEVs@ALN enhances osteogenic differentiation, as evidenced by increased ALP activity and matrix mineralization. In zebrafish GIOP models, LpEVs@ALN improves cranial mineralization, new bone formation, scale regeneration, and locomotor/shoaling performance; accompanied by reduced inflammatory tone, improved ALP/RANKL-associated bone turnover readouts, and rebalanced oxidative-stress indices. Microbiome profiling shows recovery of richness/diversity and reduced Proteobacteria dominance, while scale RNA-seq reveals broad reversal of glucocorticoid-driven dysregulation toward pro-osteogenic and anti-inflammatory programs. Integrated correlation analysis further linked microbial remodeling with systemic and skeletal responses, suggesting involvement of the gut-immune-bone axis. Collectively, LpEVs@ALN alleviates GIOP by combining ALN-mediated bone protection with probiotic extracellular vesicle-associated regulation of intestinal and systemic homeostasis, highlighting its potential as an oral therapeutic strategy for GIOP.

title: In Situ Reconstructed Pt-CeO2 Nanozymes With Rich Interfacial Oxygen Vacancies for Kinetic Fingerprint-Based Clinical Thiol Discrimination.
abstract: Deciphering structurally similar thiol analogues is vital for disease diagnosis, yet conventional one-to-one sensing strategies are intrinsically bottlenecked by signal cross-interference. Herein, we report an in situ reconstructed interfacial oxygen vacancies engineering strategy to prepare vacancy-rich Pt-CeO2 nanozymes for intelligent thiol differentiation. By combining incipient wetness impregnation with subsequent H2 reduction, isolated Pt single atoms were transformed into uniformly dispersed Pt clusters on CeO2 nanorods, simultaneously inducing abundant oxygen vacancies and dynamically coupled Pt-CeO2 interfaces. The optimized nanozyme exhibited significantly enhanced peroxidase-like catalytic activity over its single-atom state or directly deposited cluster counterparts. Crucially, the boosted catalytic kinetics significantly amplified the subtle response discrepancies among different thiols, yielding highly resolved time-dependent fingerprints. By integrating these distinct kinetic profiles with multivariate statistical analysis and predictive machine learning models, accurate differentiation of thiol species, complex multicomponent mixtures and clinical serum samples was achieved. This work not only provides insights into reconstruction-induced interfacial defect engineering but also establishes an effective framework for intelligent kinetic sensing in early disease screening.

title: Lithium-Doped Hydroxyapatite Nanowires Rejuvenate Senescent Macrophages Via the Lysosome-Dependent Ferroptosis Axis to Promote Aged Bone Regeneration.
abstract: Senescent bone repair remains a formidable clinical challenge without an entirely satisfactory strategy. Emerging evidence has identified macrophage senescence as a critical determinant of impaired bone healing in the aged skeleton, and precisely reversing macrophage senescence has therefore emerged as a highly promising therapeutic approach. In this study, guided by multi-omics features of senescent macrophages, we develop lithium-doped hydroxyapatite nanowires (Li-nHAP) and demonstrate that Li-nHAP effectively alleviates macrophage senescence and subsequently enhances the osteogenic differentiation of aged bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Mechanistically, we identify the lysosome-dependent ferroptosis axis as a previously unrecognized target mediating the anti-senescent effects of Li-nHAP in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Specifically, Li-nHAP re-establishes lysosomal homeostasis, including restoring acidity, preserving membrane integrity, maintaining iron storage, and enhancing hydrolytic activity, thereby suppressing ferroptosis and ultimately reversing macrophage senescence. In vivo studies further validate that Li-nHAP significantly alleviates macrophage ferroptosis and senescence, reduces local iron accumulation, and accelerates bone regeneration in an aged mandibular defect model. Collectively, these findings establish Li-nHAP as a novel osteo-immunomodulatory biomaterial that offers a promising strategy for the repair of age-related bone defects.

title: Generative artificial intelligence in medical oncology: A clinically focused narrative review of large language, vision-language, and agentic artificial intelligence systems.
abstract: Rapid advances in cancer genetics and genomics, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and therapeutics have substantially increased the complexity of clinical oncology. Integrating large and diverse data streams into timely, patient-specific decisions provides a compelling rationale for incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into cancer care. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) encompasses several classes of models capable of generating new content. This clinically focused review concentrates on GenAI applications based primarily on large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), as well as emerging agentic systems that use these models to perform coordinated, multistep tasks. LLMs demonstrate substantial medical knowledge, strong performance on oncology-related assessments, and emerging capabilities in clinical reasoning. Guideline- and retrieval-augmented systems can improve concordance with expert recommendations and interpretation of complex treatment algorithms. LLMs and VLMs have been applied to documentation, patient communication, information extraction and summarization, clinical decision support, and multimodal data synthesis. However, performance varies substantially across tasks and clinical domains, with important limitations including incomplete or outdated information, training-data bias, automation bias, and confabulation. Agentic AI represents an emerging extension of these technologies in which LLMs or VLMs are incorporated into systems capable of multistep planning, external information retrieval, specialized tool use, and iterative evaluation and refinement. Early oncology applications include evidence synthesis, multimodal clinical decision support, radiology, pathology, surgery, and individualized treatment planning. With rigorous validation, transparent implementation, continual updating, and appropriate expert oversight, GenAI may augment oncologists' judgment, improve patient understanding and experience, streamline cancer care delivery, and advance personalized oncology.

title: A Projection‐Based ARIMA Framework for Nonlinear Dynamics in Macroeconomic and Financial Time Series: Closed‐Form Estimation and Fast Rolling Forecasting
abstract: We develop Galerkin–ARIMA, a projection‐based forecasting framework that expands observation‐ and innovation‐lag states with finite basis functions while nesting classical multiplicative SARIMA as a restricted linear specification. The model is estimated using preliminary residual proxies followed by a joint least‐squares or ridge regression, which supports efficient rolling refitting. For the fixed‐dimensional unpenalized estimator, we establish asymptotic normality while accounting explicitly for generated regressors. Across 10 US macroeconomic and financial series, Galerkin–ARIMA has competitive one‐step‐ahead forecast accuracy, with nonlinear gains varying across series and the linear specification providing the most stable performance. In pre‐specified runtime experiments on Real GDP, the S&P 500, and the Unemployment Rate, Ridge Galerkin–ARIMA is substantially faster than likelihood/state‐space SARIMA under fixed, initially tuned, and repeatedly retuned rolling specifications. The results suggest that the main value of the framework is flexible lag‐state modeling and computationally efficient forecasting. Nonlinear enrichment does not produce uniform accuracy gains.

title: Effects of Scallop Mantle Toxin on the Male Mouse Reproductive System.
abstract: The mantle of Yesso scallops contains a novel 18-/29-kDa protein toxin. Previous studies have confirmed that this toxin induces subacute toxicity without a clear dose-effect relationship. However, its effects on the male reproductive system remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the toxic effects of scallop mantle toxin (SMT) on the reproductive organs of male mice. Male Kunming mice were fed diets supplemented with 2% scallop mantle for 5 consecutive weeks, with the dosage determined based on previous studies from our research group. Instead of using purified toxin extracts, this study directly adopted raw scallop mantle tissue as the toxin source. Mouse growth status was monitored, with analyses performed on testicular and epididymal histology, sperm morphology, sperm DNA integrity, sperm nucleoprotein maturation, and the expression of spermatogenesis-related genes. The results showed that SMT induces significant reproductive toxicity in male mice by impairing spermatogenesis, as evidenced by structural disruption of seminiferous tubules, reduced spermatogenic cell layers, decreased counts of mature elongated spermatozoa, elevated sperm malformation and DNA damage, and disrupted histone-to-protamine transition. Furthermore, SMT significantly downregulated the expression of TSSK6, a postmeiotic differentiation marker, indicating that SMT primarily targets the late stages of spermatogenesis. Taken together, SMT damages the structural integrity of male reproductive organs and compromises sperm quantity and quality in mice, and may interfere with postmeiotic sperm formation and maturation. These findings provide an important theoretical basis for establishing scallop mantle-related reproductive toxicity models and evaluating shellfish food safety risks.

title: Porcupine Detection and Mitigation in Kashmir Valley Orchards Using Edge Computing
abstract: Roughly 20% to 28% of the GDP of the Kashmiri agricultural sector are based on high‐value crops, such as apples, walnuts, saffron, and apricots. These face significant economic challenges due to crop damage caused by the Indian crested porcupine (Hystrix indica). This research aims to study and develop an effective real‐time management solution for wildlife intrusion in orchards, overcoming the limitations of traditional deterrence methods. Methods : We propose a multilayered edge‐IoT architecture that combines motion, acoustic, and visual sensing with edge‐based machine learning and automated wildlife monitoring. The system leverages lightweight YOLOv8n models running on edge devices, secure communication frameworks, and intelligent monitoring with a user‐facing application for alerts and analytics. A comprehensive wildlife detection dataset was developed by integrating multiple public datasets and converting segmentation annotations into object‐detection bounding boxes. The final dataset contains 1758 images with 2249 annotated instances across three classes: porcupine, hedgehog, and others. Object detection is performed using YOLOv8n on resource‐constrained edge devices for efficient real‐time inference. Experimental results show that YOLOv8n achieves 93.9% mAP@0.5 and 86.4% mAP@0.5:0.95 with 84.0% precision and 89.9% recall on the test dataset. The porcupine class specifically achieves 99.5% mAP@0.5 and 95.4% mAP@0.5:0.95, demonstrating highly reliable porcupine detection performance. The lightweight YOLOv8n architecture achieves approximately 4.9 ms inference time per image on the validation host, and 81 ms per frame on a Jetson Nano edge node, enabling efficient edge deployment for real‐time orchard monitoring. All reported figures are obtained from real image data combined with simulated multi‐sensor confidence modeling; no result derives from a deployed orchard installation, and the scope of validation is stated explicitly. Furthermore, the proposed framework establishes a foundation for future privacy‐preserving and Agentic AI‐enabled intelligent wildlife monitoring systems capable of adaptive decision‐making, autonomous monitoring, and collaborative edge intelligence under dynamic environmental conditions

title: A predictive approach to genome design for multi-trait improvement and environmental adaptability via machine learning
Exploratory donor-aware analysis of developmental transcriptomic trajectories in 15q13.3-deletion cortical organoids
Automated classification of non-functional requirements twenty years later: why this isn’t a solved problem
abstract: This paper revisits “Automated Classification of Non-Functional Requirements”, published in the Requirements Engineering Journal in 2007, and reflects on how the underlying problem has evolved over two decades. The original work addressed the central challenge in requirements engineering that quality concerns are difficult to identify because they are distributed across heterogeneous artifacts and only partially documented. It introduced one of the earliest machine-learning approaches for NFR classification and produced the NFR PROMISE dataset, which became a widely used benchmark in this area. To understand the paper’s long-term impact, we conducted a citation review of 55 papers and replicated representative NFR classification approaches spanning two decades. The results show substantial advances in automated classification, culminating in modern LLM and agent-based techniques that outperform earlier approaches on PROMISE. However, improved accuracy has not solved the underlying problem. Contemporary AI-assisted development increasingly blurs the boundaries between Requirements Engineering, architectural design, and implementation. Quality concerns continue to emerge throughout development, but now appear as conversational fragments, implementation discussions, and architectural tradeoffs rather than explicit requirements statements. We argue that the next generation of requirements engineering tools must move beyond classifying documents toward identifying, surfacing, and preserving architecturally significant quality concerns as they emerge throughout development. We then outline a research agenda centered on detecting emerging and missing quality concerns, selective intervention, living documentation of quality decisions, and evaluation beyond classification accuracy. Finally we take a retrospective look at two decades of sharing and reusing the dataset, including the importance of dataset lineage, experimental comparability, and benchmark evolution.

title: Sustainable career in the age of artificial intelligence: an agent-based simulation from a complex adaptive systems perspective
Data-driven segmentation of solar filaments based on ground-based instrument data
abstract: The dynamic behavior of solar prominences and filaments is a precursor to coronal mass ejections (CMEs), which can disrupt Earth's magnetosphere and affect satellite communications. Systematic ground-based solar observations, conducted with high temporal resolution, are instrumental in monitoring these structures. Analysis of the morphological changes and destabilization processes of filaments and prominences captured in datasets can help identify early warning signs of potential eruptions. This capability is vital for developing reliable space weather forecasting systems, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of solar disturbances on Earth's technological infrastructure. Previously, we introduced hybrid algorithmic-data driven method which performance was shown on a set of Solar Dynamic Observatory (SDO) Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) instrument data performing segmentation of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and shock waves. In this work, we extend certain aspects of this approach to image segmentation of solar features -- filaments and prominences using H-alpha Kanzelhohe Observatory data. We describe a leakage-aware, sparse multi-year sampling strategy. We present image segmentation models pre-trained on synoptic and normalized image data, followed by a discussion of how model performance depends on training-set engineering, data preprocessing techniques, and the choice of loss metrics. We perform a limited study, both analytically and numerically, of the effect of external, fixed normalization versus native input for compact U-Net-based segmentation of solar H-alpha filaments, also contributing to ongoing research on normalization in deep networks in general and compact models in particular.

title: Integrating response surface methodology and Gaussian process regression for explainable quality modelling in packaging manufacturing
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Genome wide identification and in silico mRNA expression profiling of the WRKY transcription factor gene family in Salvia hispanica
abstract: This study presents the first comprehensive in silico genome-wide identification, characterization, and mRNA expression profiling of the WRKY transcription factor (TF) gene family in Salvia hispanica L. (chia), a nutritious crop of the family Lamiaceae. A total of 35 CsWRKY genes were identified from the chia reference genome and classified into 7 phylogenetic groups (I, IIa–IIe, III) based on WRKY domain number and zinc-finger motif type. Mean protein length, molecular weight and isoelectric point were 332.8 aa, 37,499 Da and 7.62, respectively, and protein length was almost perfectly correlated with molecular weight (r = 0.9995). Subcellular-localization prediction indicated predominantly nuclear and cytoplasmic distribution. Gene-structure analysis revealed 2–7 exons, and MEME identified 15 conserved motifs including the invariant WRKYGQK heptapeptide. Segmental duplication predominated and has evolved under purifying selection. Promoter analysis detected 20 cis-acting regulatory element classes, and a maximum-likelihood phylogeny grouped CsWRKYs with orthologs from Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, Glycine max, Medicago truncatula and Physcomitrella patens. In silico expression profiling used only verified, publicly available S. hispanica RNA-Seq datasets and was therefore restricted to tissue-specific and developmental patterns; because no abiotic-stress RNA-Seq dataset is currently available for chia, no stress-responsive expression analysis was performed. Homology models were built and docked with in silico predictions identifying CsWRKY3 as the strongest binder. These in silico predictions provide a preliminary genomic framework that requires future experimental validation and may guide the study of WRKY-mediated processes in chia.

title: The future of salicylic acid in agriculture lies in precision priming
abstract: As the world is moving towards enforcing strict regulations against pesticides, plant hormones triggering natural defenses represent a foundation of sustainable agriculture. Among them, Salicylic acid (SA) is a major phytohormone for governing systemic acquired resistance (SAR), a broad-spectrum immune response, against hemibiotrophic and biotrophic pathogens. Although it has huge potential as a sustainable alternative to synthetic pesticides, its field efficacy lags, with inconsistent disease control, phytotoxicity, and significant yield loss. This review gathers emerging evidence to explain the inconsistency of SA-mediated disease control under field conditions and proposes priming-based frameworks to improve reliability in crop protection systems. It focuses on two underexplored areas. First, the metabolic and hormonal basis of the growth-defense trade-off. Second, the climate-induced signaling failure, where elevated temperatures disrupt the SA transcriptional machinery. Simultaneously, the review explores emerging innovative strategies, such as nano-formulations for controlled release, synthetic analogues with enhanced stability, and the paradigm shift from direct induction to molecular priming to solve the existing problems. By integrating findings from the model and crop species, we infer that the future of SA in agriculture does not lie in direct, high-dose application in the field. Instead, it lies in the development of intelligent, climate-resilient priming systems that work in alignment with plant biology.

title: Comparison and application of remote sensing evapotranspiration retrieval models for the Inner Mongolian grassland region
A data-driven intelligent framework for silver carp (Hypophthalmichthys molitrix) surimi gel properties prediction and quality improvement.
abstract: This study developed a data-driven framework linking silver carp surimi gelling properties prediction with process optimization using raw-material characteristics and controllable processing parameters. A dataset of 1571 processing records spanning regions, seasons, fish-size grades, and key processing conditions was established. Target-specific stacked ensemble models predicted gel strength, breaking strain, and whiteness, with test set R2 values of 0.95, 0.82, and 0.93, respectively. SHAP analysis identified salt-soluble protein content and surimi moisture content as the most influential predictors of gel strength; region and season were most influential for breaking strain, whereas whiteness was more closely associated with season and the moisture-protein balance. The models were coupled with desirability-based optimization to generate raw-material-specific processing recommendations. Independent validation using six newly collected raw-material lots representing three regions and two seasons showed that the optimized schemes increased mean gel strength by approximately 25-107% relative to the conventional empirical process, with no significant differences detected in breaking strain; whiteness responses varied with raw-material and seasonal conditions. Overall, these results show that incorporating raw-material properties into interpretable multi-target prediction can support batch-specific process recommendations, and the desirable quality control.

title: Monitoring of protein secondary structure during surimi thermal processing using hyperspectral imaging: comparison of spectral, image-texture, and data-fusion strategies.
How food structure and processing govern metabolizable energy: a critical review of the food-matrix determinants of energy availability and the limits of the Atwater accounting.
abstract: Food energy is usually reported using Atwater factors: composition-based coefficients that treat metabolizable energy as a function of macronutrient mass rather than food structure. Yet a growing food-science literature shows that metabolizable energy can diverge materially from Atwater predictions according to the integrity of the food matrix and the processing applied to it. This review brings energy-accounting and food-structure science into direct contact. It defines where the Atwater system remains useful and where its structural blind spot becomes consequential; clarifies the frequent conflation of digestibility, bioaccessibility, bioavailability and metabolizable energy, and distinguishes physical resistance from chemical inhibition of digestive enzymes while treating the two as coupled rather than independent. It then maps major processing operations to their structural and energetic consequences, and compares methods used to quantify metabolizable energy and nutrient release, including human balance studies, ileostomy and intubation studies, standardised in vitro digestion, dynamic models and in silico approaches. Tree nuts provide the strongest empirical case. Measured metabolizable energy ranges from about 5% below the Atwater value for pistachios to more than 30% below for whole almonds, a divergence that is explained by matrix integrity and lipid encapsulation. Four energetic consequences of matrix disruption are considered: net metabolizable energy, rate of energy release, thermic effect of feeding and colonic salvage. The review concludes that energy values based on composition alone are insufficient for foods whose structure strongly constrains digestion, and that food-composition data, labelling, feeding research and reformulation would benefit from structure-aware measures of delivered energy.

title: Starch-derived oligosaccharides as prebiotics in innovative functional foods.
abstract: Driven by the escalating demand for innovative functional foods, starch-derived oligosaccharides (SDOs), particularly low-degree-of-polymerization fractions, have emerged as prominent functional carbohydrates, with selected SDO fractions exhibiting prebiotic properties. Their digestive behavior and gut microbial utilization depend strongly on degree of polymerization, glycosidic linkage, and molecular structure. Findings from in vitro and cell-based studies, animal models, and selected human intervention trials further indicate structure-dependent microbial and physiological responses. Herein, the structural characteristics, underlying prebiotic mechanisms, and traditional biocatalytic synthesis strategies of diverse SDOs are systematically summarized and discussed. Currently, enzymatic transglycosylation dominates the industrial production of SDOs; however, this process is fundamentally bottlenecked by the inherent hydrolytic propensity and poor regioselectivity of wild-type glycosidases or transglycosidases, leading to heterogeneous product profiles and limited thermodynamic yields. To overcome these natural biocatalytic constraints, customizing robust enzymes via artificial intelligence (AI) and computational structural redesign has become an important research direction. By integrating deep learning algorithms with structure-based de novo design and multidimensional kinetic prediction, the architecture of native catalytic clefts can be rationally remodeled. Such computational strategies facilitate favorable orientation of carbohydrate acceptor substrates and enhance transglycosylation selectivity toward targeted SDOs promoting innovative functional food applications.

title: Physics-based modelling within the process-structure-properties framework for fatigue life prediction of materials fabricated by pulsed laser powder bed fusion
Postoperative radiotherapy for early oral squamous cell carcinoma with a single ipsilateral lymph node metastasis - a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIMS Managing early oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) with a solitary ipsilateral lymph node metastasis (pN1) and no additional adverse features remains controversial, with conflicting international guidelines. Our study examined the effect of postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) compared with surgery only (SO) on several survival outcomes in a clinical cohort. METHODS Patients diagnosed with a primary pT1-2 OSCC and a single ipsilateral lymph node metastasis (pN1) without an extranodal extension were retrospectively identified. Factors associated with receiving PORT were assessed using logistic regression. Adjusted Cox regression models were used to examine the association between PORT and overall survival (OS) and regional recurrence-free survival (R-RFS) in the whole cohort and in different subgroups. RESULTS In total, 85 patients were included in our study, of whom 43 received PORT. Three factors were predictors of receiving PORT in our cohort, namely: poor differentiation, high-risk margins, and bilateral neck dissection. Overall survival and probability of regional recurrence after 60 months were comparable between groups: 63% and 30% in the SO group and 65% and 25% in the PORT group, respectively. After adjusting for established confounders, PORT was not associated with improved OS HR (PORT vs SO = 0.94; 95% CI 0.46-1.92; p = 0.9) nor with improved regional recurrence-free survival (PORT vs SO = 0.81; 95% CI 0.30-2.17; p = 0.7. Subgroup analyses revealed potential benefit from PORT in patients with pT2 tumors, age under 70 years, and inadequate neck dissection (lymph node yield < 18 nodes). CONCLUSION While registry-based studies often lack granular data on comorbidities and specific recurrence types, our results suggest that the marginal gains of PORT may not justify its high morbidity, including significant long-term impacts on quality of life. Observation seems to be a safe alternative to routine irradiation in carefully selected pT1-2 pN1 OSCC cases, provided surgical neck management is adequate.
journal: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery

title: Redox-responsive nanoparticles prevent post-ablation hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence by dual regulation of dendritic cells and tumor cells.
abstract: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is a locoregional therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the long-term efficacy for RFA is severely compromised by recurrence driven by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). In this study, we identify mature regulatory dendritic cells (mregDCs) as a key immune-regulatory population closely associated with this immune evasion. Following insufficient RFA (iRFA), sublethal thermal injury induces excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and hypoxia, which synergistically promote mregDC differentiation and upregulate PD-L1, leading to profound CD8+ T cell exhaustion. To address these challenges, we developed a redox-responsive nanoplatform for co-delivery of an ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine (NAC) and siPD-L1. This nanoplatform effectively mitigates hypoxia and oxidative stress within the TME while reprogramming mregDCs toward an immunostimulatory phenotype via PD-L1 silencing. In both subcutaneous and orthotopic iRFA-HCC models, treatment with NPs(siPD-L1/NAC) potently activates CD8+ T cells, suppresses tumor growth, and exhibits a favorable safety profile. Our findings uncover an mregDC-mediated immune evasion mechanism underlying post-ablation recurrence and present a promising dual-regulation strategy for remodeling the post-ablation TME to potentiate durable anti-tumor immunity.
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society

title: Zfpm1 regulates endothelial-mesenchymal transition and endocardial cell differentiation.
abstract: The endocardium is the endothelial component of the heart that forms valves. Endocardial (EC) cells undergo endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT) which distinguishes them from endothelial (ET) cells, despite sharing markers and a mesodermal origin. Nfatc1, uniquely labels EC cells but is not sufficient for EC cell specification, since knockouts form valves, albeit underdeveloped, therefore the regulators that specify EC fate remain incompletely defined. Using an in vivo Nfatc1 reporter system, we show that EC and ET cells are transcriptionally distinct and identify the transcription factor Zfpm1 (Fog1), as a potential regulator of EC cell specification. In an in vitro embryonic stem cell differentiation model, Zfpm1 knockdown results in an impaired EC cell differentiation, with reduced endothelial-mesenchymal transition and altered contractility and beating phenotype, consistent with reduced differentiation of EC cells affecting the crosstalk with myocardial cells. These findings are consistent with data linking mutations in the human ZFPM1 gene with non-syndromic tetralogy of Fallot. This and the broad expression pattern across all regions of the cardiac outflow tract support a role for Zfpm1 in mammalian EC cell differentiation and endothelial-mesenchymal transition. This study extends the in vivo evidence of its relevance to cardiac development and provides new insights into the transcriptional control of EC lineages.

title: Relationship of weather and plant microclimate parameters to rhizoctonia aerial blight development in soybean
abstract: Rhizoctonia aerial blight (RAB), caused by Rhizoctonia solani Kühn, is a major constraint to soybean production. This study evaluated weather and plant microclimate effects on RAB development using a split-plot design (two genotypes as main-plot, five sowing dates as sub-plot) over two kharif seasons (May-October, 2022–2023) at Jorhat, Assam, in India. Minimum temperature and evaporation showed the strongest negative correlations with disease severity ( r = − 0.86 to − 0.87, p < 0.01); soil moisture was positively correlated ( r = 0.68–0.91, p < 0.01). Disease severity, AUDPC, infection rate, weather, and microclimatic parameters were monitored weekly. Disease severity increased progressively with crop age ( p < 0.001) and was higher under early sowing. The highest severity occurred in JS 335 sown on 17 May (35.61% PDI; AUDPC 237.90), while the lowest occurred in KDS 753 sown on 1 and 16 July (16.34% and 14.73% PDI; AUDPC 102.92 and 105.16; p < 0.001). Treatment-specific stepwise regression equations explained 73.3–92.7% of the observed severity variability (adjusted R² = 0.706–0.900), but they were fitted and evaluated using the same two-season, single-location dataset and therefore represent exploratory fitted relationships rather than independently validated forecasting models. Lower disease severity in late-sown treatments is interpreted as reflecting a shorter epidemic window and altered weather exposure across phenological stages rather than an independent causal effect of sowing date. This study would support in the development of forecast models to assess soybean RAB risk in the hot and humid areas.

title: IoT and UAV Integration for Wheat Disease Monitoring: A Review of Multimodal Sensing and Analytical Frameworks With Perspectives on Cereal Crop Stress
abstract: Cereal productivity is increasingly threatened by both biotic stresses, such as fungal diseases including yellow rust and Fusarium head blight (FHB), and abiotic stress factors which cause substantial yield and quality losses worldwide. Conventional monitoring remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and spatially constrained, motivating automated, and scalable disease surveillance. Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms provide high-resolution, field-scale canopy observations for detection and severity mapping, while Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks deliver continuous microclimate measurements that are critical for forecasting disease risk. Importantly, integrating these modalities supports not only detection but also interpretation of plant–pathogen–environment interactions by linking microclimatic drivers to physiological stress responses in wheat. In contrast to prior reviews that focus on individual sensing modalities, this study synthesizes UAV imaging, IoT-based environmental monitoring, and physiologically grounded interpretation into a unified perspective. We compare sensing technologies, datasets, and analytical pipelines, and identify key gaps in interoperability, data fusion, and communication efficiency. To address these limitations, we propose a three-tier IoT–UAV conceptual framework that couples short-range IoT sensor clustering with long-range, delay-tolerant UAV data collection and edge/cloud analytics. This architecture enables scalable, energy-aware monitoring and serves as a reference model for biologically informed, data-driven early warning systems that connect environmental risk signals with observable disease expression. In addition, the reviewed approaches provide perspectives for extending wheat-focused disease monitoring frameworks to broader cereal crop stress analysis, including the integration of abiotic stress factors and their impact on crop resilience.

title: Trustworthy Collaborative Agents for Industrial IoT: A Multimodal Mixed Reality Framework for Human-Centric Precision Assembly
abstract: In the evolving industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), the complexity of assembly tasks requires intelligent agents capable of augmenting human capabilities through real-time perception and decision-making. However, deploying such agents on edge devices faces challenges in spatial alignment accuracy and computational efficiency, which compromise their trustworthiness in high-risk environments. To address these issues, this article proposes a human-centric collaborative agent (HC-CoAgent), a lightweight mixed reality (MR) framework tailored for precision circuit assembly. Unlike traditional static systems, HC-CoAgent functions as a “cognitive peer”—an AI partner that dynamically shares the operator’s cognitive load by fusing visual object recognition, gesture tracking, and gaze input. Crucially, to bridge the “reality gap,” we introduce a novel human-in-the-loop (HITL) spatial alignment mechanism utilizing a threshold-controlled 3-D pointing strategy. The theoretical rigor of this mechanism is validated via a support vector machine (SVM) analysis, which defines the precise trustworthiness boundaries for safe interaction. Furthermore, visual attention analysis reveals that the agent functions as a cognitive anchor, significantly reducing visual entropy and aligning novice gaze patterns with expert baselines. Experimental results from industrial wiring scenarios demonstrate that HC-CoAgent improves task efficiency by 33% and reduces error rates significantly compared to both traditional paper-based methods and uncalibrated MR baselines. The system also exhibits low cognitive load and high usability, validating its potential as an effective and efficient edge AI agent for empowering the IIoT workforce.

title: A Content-Adaptive JPEG-Based Encryption Framework for Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Remote sensing images (RSIs) are characterized by high data redundancy and strong sensitivity, posing significant challenges for secure transmission in bandwidth- and storage-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) environments. Existing RSI encryption schemes primarily emphasize security, while often overlooking compression efficiency, leading to substantial bit expansion and limited practicality in real-world IoT applications. To balance image privacy against storage capacity, we propose a JPEG-compatible RSI encryption algorithm based on content-adaptive criteria, which integrates reversible data hiding (RDH) to guarantee data integrity during transmission. Based on the structural characteristics of RSI, a block-separation strategy of varying block sizes employing content-adaptive criteria is introduced to replace the equal-size block separation in the block decomposition stage of JPEG compression. Following the quantization stage, the DC differences of variably sized blocks are encrypted according to their statistical characteristics, thereby significantly reducing bitstream expansion (BE) while enhancing computational efficiency. Moreover, to degrade the encryption overhead and reinforce the security of RSIs, we introduce both local and global confusion algorithms. The local algorithm employs circular distortion to encrypt blocks, while the global algorithm utilizes cross-disturbance to secure run/size (RS) pairs. Furthermore, an improved RDH algorithm based on histogram shifting (HS) tailored for RSI encryption is given to balance embedding capacity with bit increment. Extensive experimental evaluations and detailed security analyses reveal that the proposed algorithm decreases the bit expansion rate by 22.84%–56.83% compared with state-of-the-art schemes while maintaining strong resistance to statistical and structural attacks.

title: Reliable Hyperspectral Image Classification via Deviation-Guided Domain Adaptation
abstract: With the increasing deployment of hyperspectral sensors on IoT-enabled remote sensing platforms, massive hyperspectral image (HSI) data are continuously acquired from multiple sensors under varying imaging conditions and across different geographic regions. However, continuously acquired data may exhibit distribution shifts and contain unknown categories, which can result in ineffective knowledge transfer or even negative transfer. To this end, we propose a deviation-guided domain adaptation framework (DGDA) for reliable open-set HSI classification. Specifically, a Mamba-enhanced spectral–spatial encoder first learns transferable representations by jointly modeling local spatial patterns and long-range spectral dependencies, providing a reliable feature space for target-structure discovery. On this basis, dynamic virtual-unknown prototypes (DVUPs) are constructed from unmatched target clusters to explicitly characterize target-private structures. Finally, a deviation-guided selective alignment and unknown routing (DG-SAUR) mechanism uses source-known and virtual-unknown structures to align reliable known-like samples and route high-deviation samples toward the unknown space, thereby achieving shared-class transfer and unknown-sample rejection. Experiments on four cross-scene and cross-sensor adaptation tasks show that DGDA achieves the best HOS on all tasks and outperforms the strongest competing methods by an average of 11.6 percentage points. These results demonstrate its potential to reliably interpret unlabeled imagery from multiple IoT remote sensing platforms while preventing source-unseen observations from contaminating downstream monitoring and decision-making.

title: Hybrid Stackelberg Game and Diffusion-Based Auction for Two-Tier Agentic AI Task Offloading in Internet of Agents
abstract: The Internet of Agents (IoA) not only provides a foundational architecture for collaborative reasoning among artificial intelligence (AI) agents but also brings new challenges to task offloading. Unlike traditional task offloading, agentic AI tasks involve sustained multistep reasoning, planning, and context maintenance, thereby imposing coupled pressure on memory occupancy, inference latency, and energy consumption. To address these issues, we propose a two-tier agentic AI task offloading framework within the IoA scenarios. In the first tier, resource-requester agents (RRAs), e.g., autonomous vehicles (AVs), offload inference-intensive tasks to nearby resource providers. Such resource providers can be mobile resource agents (MRAs), e.g., neighboring vehicles, and infrastructure resource agents (IRAs), e.g., roadside units (RSUs). In the second tier, overloaded IRAs further procure supplementary inference resources from aerial resource agents (ARAs), e.g., uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs), to handle overflow workloads caused by limited residual video RAM (VRAM) and key-value (KV)-cache accumulation. We formulate the first-tier pricing and offloading interaction as a Stackelberg game, where MRAs/IRAs act as leaders and RRAs act as followers. Moreover, we model the second-tier IRA-ARA resource trading as a double Dutch auction (DDA). To solve the proposed hierarchical model, we develop an iterative best-response algorithm for the first-tier Stackelberg game and a diffusion-based deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm for the second-tier DDA process. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework can improve agentic task-offloading efficiency, auction reward, and social welfare while reducing information-exchange cost.

title: Toward IoT-Enabled UAV Swarms for Air-Quality Monitoring: A Comprehensive Survey on Technologies, Methods, and Optimization Strategies
abstract: Air-quality monitoring has become a significant global concern because poor air quality adversely affects human health and the environment. Recent advances in uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs), when integrated into Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures, offer a flexible and scalable solution for acquiring high-resolution air-quality data, especially in under-monitored or hard-to-access regions. UAVs can complement land-based monitoring by collecting measurements in remote, dangerous, or difficult-to-access locations. Because air-quality monitoring is conducted in uncertain and complex physical environments, UAV systems increasingly require swarm-based, autonomous, and intelligent capabilities. However, several technical challenges must be addressed for large-scale UAV-enabled air-quality monitoring, including reliable wireless communication, scalable multi-UAV networking, distributed control, and safe system operation. This survey discusses the enabling technologies of UAV-based IoT systems, including communication, networking, computation, trajectory planning, cooperation, and coordination, together with relevant optimization strategies. It then analyzes key operational and management considerations, including movement, connectivity, energy, safety, security, and privacy protection. Finally, it summarizes existing air-quality datasets, their roles in UAV-based sensing, and the challenges of UAV-based data collection. The survey concludes by identifying open challenges and discussing future research directions for advancing air-quality monitoring.

title: Internet of Agents (IoA): Sensing, Communication, Decision-Making, and Execution
abstract: Advances in sensing, communication, and reasoning are driving deeper integration of AI into IoT systems. However, progress remains siloed across two communities: agent research centers on task decomposition, semantic planning, and coordination, whereas IoT research prioritizes sensing, communication, and edge computing. Bridging these perspectives and integrating semantic reasoning with system foundations remains a key challenge. Therefore, we present the Internet of Agents (IoAs), a framework that reorganizes existing AI agent research from a systems perspective, following the classical IoT paradigm of sensing, communication, decision-making, and execution. IoA reconceptualizes system nodes as agents rather than traditional IoT endpoints. For sensing, IoA broadens awareness to include reasoning depth, knowledge gaps, and external tool capabilities. In communication, IoA adopts a three-layer architecture (environment, interaction, and semantic), designed to align with the five-layer Internet protocol stack. In decision-making and execution, IoA frames the shift from rule-based control to semantic planning and from reactive execution to proactive execution. We further identify open challenges and future research directions across the four modules of IoA.

title: Uncovering Delay Paths and Hidden Latency in Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: End-to-end latency is a key requirement for intelligent transportation systems (ITSs), particularly for safety-critical applications such as vulnerable road user (VRU) protection, cooperative perception, and remote driving. Existing studies typically evaluate latency from a communication perspective, implicitly assuming that network transmission dominates the end-to-end delay. However, measurements collected from operational ITS deployments reveal a different picture. In this letter, we introduce a structured framework for experimentally decomposing end-to-end latency into its main functional contributions across sensing, processing, communication, and visualization stages. The framework is validated through measurement campaigns conducted in the Modena Automotive Smart Area (MASA), a real-world ITS living lab supporting heterogeneous vehicular services. Experimental results consistently show that sensing and processing frequently dominate the overall latency budget, while communication contributes only a small fraction of the end-to-end delay. These findings highlight the importance of adopting holistic latency evaluation methodologies when designing latency-sensitive ITS applications.

title: GNSS Anomaly Detection in Urban Canyons: A Comprehensive Survey of Multimodal Visibility Inference
abstract: Reliable GNSS positioning in dense urban environments depends on assessing satellite visibility and identifying measurements degraded by non-line-of-sight (NLOS) reception and multipath. This survey organizes reception-state inference into three complementary evidence families: receiver-side signals, 3D maps and environmental models, and auxiliary sensors. Receiver-side approaches span antenna/electromagnetic, tracking/baseband, and observable-domain evidence, interpreted through rule-based, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods. Map-based approaches are examined by reviewing environmental representations and methods such as geometric screening, shadow matching, 3D ray tracing, and neural implicit visibility prediction. IMU, camera, and LiDAR measurements provide complementary kinematic, visual, and geometric evidence for online screening. Across these families, we compare accuracy, interpretability, hardware and calibration requirements, map dependence, computational cost, and suitability for real-time deployment. We identify open challenges in dataset quality and labeling, domain generalization, map freshness, and resource-efficient implementation. The resulting synthesis connects signal processing, environmental modeling, and sensor fusion to guide the design of robust urban GNSS measurement-screening systems.

title: MIDA: Multi-Interest Decoding with Adaptive Aggregation for Session-based Recommendation
abstract: Session-based recommendation (SBR) infers user interest from limited interaction sequences, yet current models show a consistent performance drop when longer histories are available. This degradation is associated with decoder designs that overemphasize recent items while underutilizing distant, yet semantically relevant, interactions, leading to poor modeling of long-range dependencies and multi-interest behaviors. To address this challenge, we introduce MIDA (Multi-Interest Decoding with Adaptive Aggregation for Session-based Recommendation), a lightweight and encoder-agnostic framework that provides a reformulation of the decoding stage. The central design principle is a two-space decoupling: clustering operates on raw item embeddings so that semantic groupings are not distorted by encoder-learned relational biases; encoder outputs are reserved for aggregation, where sequential context remains intact. Concretely, MIDA (i) employs differentiable multi-interest clustering on raw embeddings, preserving semantic structure that encoder representations would otherwise obscure, and (ii) fuses stability and plasticity branches through a gate conditioned on average cluster size, so that the inferred clustering structure directly governs aggregation behavior through a structural coupling across the two stages. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that MIDA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with meaningful accuracy improvements while remaining computationally practical.

title: A Data-Driven Probabilistic Harmonic Current Forecasting for Aggregated Harmonic Sources
abstract: With the increasing deployment of non-linear power electronic devices in distribution networks, the issue of excessive harmonics has become increasingly prominent. Accurate analysis and forecasting of harmonic currents are essential to better understand and mitigate harmonic-related problems. Common harmonic sources in power grids include various types of loads and renewable energy generation equipment, such as wind and photovoltaic systems. Accordingly, this paper focuses on forecasting harmonic currents for different types of aggregated harmonic sources. Considering the strong randomness, high time-variability, and coupling characteristics of harmonic currents, a data-driven probabilistic harmonic current forecasting method is proposed. First, the raw data are decomposed into deterministic and stochastic components. Next, a radial basis function autoregressive exponential model is employed to perform point forecasting of the deterministic component, accommodating multiple input factors and simultaneous multi-harmonic outputs while preserving model partial interpretability. Subsequently, the proposed multi-Gaussian fitting method and an improved Markov chain Monte Carlo approach are used for probabilistic forecasting of the stochastic component. Finally, the deterministic and stochastic component predictions are combined to yield the final probabilistic harmonic current forecast. Using actual harmonic measurement data, comparative analyses with multiple intelligent models are conducted to validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed forecasting method. Furthermore, the harmonic current predictions are applied to forward probabilistic harmonic power flows, and corresponding forward and new probabilistic harmonic mitigation measures are proposed, demonstrating practical engineering applicability.

title: Learning-Free Laplacian Kernel Modeling for Joint Imputation of Multi-Energy Load Data in Integrated Energy Systems
abstract: The reliability of data-driven applications in integrated energy systems (IESs), such as multi-energy load prediction, relies on the availability of complete and high-quality load data. However, real-world multi-energy load data can suffer from missing records, and accurate recovery remains challenging due to heterogeneous missing patterns and strong yet nontrivial coupling among different energy loads. To address this issue, this paper proposes an efficient learning-free Laplacian kernel framework for joint multi-energy load imputation, in which missing entries are directly treated as decision variables and the complete load matrix is reconstructed through a unified convex optimization formulation without requiring any training data. The proposed framework captures both the intra-load structure and cross-load coupling of multi-energy load data. This is achieved by combining a circulant Laplacian kernel-based temporal regularizer and a circulant tensor nuclear norm for local continuity and global periodicity, respectively, together with a correlation-based signed Laplacian regularizer for inter-load coupling relationship modeling. To efficiently solve the resulting optimization problem, an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is derived, where the dominant updates are implemented in the frequency domain via the fast Fourier transform (FFT) by exploiting the underlying circulant structures. This enables fast and scalable imputation of long-horizon and high-resolution load data with low computational overhead. Numerical experiments on real-world multi-energy load datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework not only consistently outperforms state-of-the-art imputation baselines under different missing patterns but also yields superior performance in downstream load forecasting tasks. The source code is available at: https://github.com/zhaopengfei12345/data-imputation

title: The Effect of Technology-Based Reading Comprehension Instruction for Students With or at Risk for Reading Difficulties: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Effective instruction is shaped by four interrelated components: instructional Quality, Appropriate levels of instruction, Incentives to motivate students, and sufficient Time for practice and feedback (QAIT). As many schools have adopted educational technology to provide reading instruction, this review examined the extent to which instructional technologies targeting reading comprehension align with Slavin's effective instruction framework, evaluated their overall effects, and identified which components differentiate intervention effectiveness. We identified 25 articles (26 studies) published from 2000 to 2025 examining technology-based reading comprehension interventions. Only nine studies included all four QAIT components. Using a random-effects correlated and hierarchical effects model, we estimated both main and moderation effects. The overall effect of technology-based programs on reading comprehension was small-to-medium (Hedges' g = 0.13, 95% CI [0.03, 0.23]) according to contemporary perspectives on effect size magnitude in education intervention research. Meta-regression analyses revealed that interventions incorporating extrinsic incentives (e.g., points and badges) were associated with smaller effect sizes. No significant moderation effects were observed for the other QAIT components or for the presence of all four components simultaneously. Implications for educational practice and directions for future research are discussed.

title: Robotization of vegetable production in Russia: current state, problems and prospects
abstract: Relevance . Vegetable production is one of the strategically important sectors of the Russian agro-industrial complex, ensuring the country's food security and supplying the population with vegetable products. Under conditions of labor shortages, rising production costs, and the need to improve production efficiency, robotization has become one of the priority areas of technological modernization in the industry. Methods . The article analyzes the current state of robotization in vegetable production in Russia and leading countries worldwide, examines the main challenges associated with the implementation of agricultural robots, performs a comparative analysis of automation levels, and identifies promising directions for further development. Particular attention is paid to the transformation of agricultural technologies to meet the requirements of robotic systems, import substitution, and practical experience in implementing robotic solutions in domestic vegetable production. Results . The study revealed that the main limiting factors are the high cost of equipment, a shortage of qualified personnel, an insufficient level of digitalization, and dependence on imported components. It is demonstrated that the successful implementation of agricultural robots requires the adaptation of vegetable cultivation technologies and the development of robot-friendly agricultural practices.

title: A Knowledge-Driven Cybersecurity Incident Response Framework Integrating Institutional Knowledge Management: Evidence from a Kenyan Agricultural Research Organization
abstract: Digital transformation has improved the efficiency of research institutions while increasing their exposure to complex cybersecurity incidents. Existing cybersecurity incident response frameworks provide comprehensive technical and governance guidance, but give limited attention to integrating institutional knowledge management throughout the incident response lifecycle. This study developed and validated a Knowledge-Driven Cybersecurity Incident Response Framework for a geographically distributed Kenyan Agricultural Research Organization. A pragmatic mixed-methods design guided by Design Science Research combined questionnaires, interviews, document review, expert evaluation, and scenario-based assessment. 52 questionnaires were distributed, and 40 were returned (76.9%). Institutional knowledge management was strongly associated with incident response effectiveness (r = 0.830, p < 0.001). The regression model was significant (F (3, 36) = 41.175, p < 0.001) and explained 77.4% of the variance in incident response effectiveness (R² = 0.774; adjusted R² = 0.756). The mean values of the framework were found to be relevant, usable, and applicable within the study context, as evidenced by expert- and scenario-based validation exceeding the acceptance threshold. This study adds a knowledge-driven incident response framework to the existing framework, integrates institutional knowledge management throughout the incident response lifecycle, and presents evidence of the proposed framework's applicability and relevance in the study context.
