title: Morphology guided hybrid deep learning for species identification of root knot nematodes
abstract: Root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.) are a major global constraint on crop productivity. The second-stage juvenile (J2) is the infective stage of nematode that actively seeks out and infects plant roots; thus, accurate identification at this stage is important for effective nematode management and control. However, current identification practices remain challenging and is time-consuming, due to their reliance on expert-dependent microscopic examinations. This challenge creates significant barriers to scalability and rapid decision-making. To address this, we propose a morphology guided hybrid deep learning framework for identifying Meloidogyne graminicola and M. incognita at the J2 stage. The proposed framework integrates biologically relevant shape descriptors with deep visual representations to improve species discrimination. Standardized morphological features are fused with convolutional embeddings via a modified MobileNetV2 classifier head, to enable joint and discriminative representation learning. The proposed approach was evaluated against morphology-based machine learning models and end-to-end deep learning baselines. The results demonstrate that the proposed morphology guided deep learning improves classification performance and interpretability. It provides a lightweight and biologically informed solution for automated identification of J2 root-knot nematode species.

title: Artificial intelligence methods for morphological analysis and diagnosis of bacterial and fungal leaf diseases
abstract: Bacterial and fungal leaf diseases frequently produce overlapping visual symptoms, complicating automated diagnosis and limiting the transferability of models across crops and field conditions. This review systematically evaluates artificial intelligence methods for the morphology-based detection and differentiation of these diseases. Following a PRISMA-based selection process, 95 records published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, of which 59 eligible studies were included. The survey covers the morphological characteristics that distinguish bacterial and fungal diseases, traditional image processing and machine learning approaches, deep learning and generative AI techniques, and publicly available datasets. It also critically compares the performance, advantages, and limitations of existing diagnostic approaches. The findings indicate that deep learning dominates the literature, particularly in fungal disease detection, whereas research on bacterial diseases and generative AI applications remains comparatively limited. Although convolutional and transfer-learning models generally demonstrated strong classification performance, comparisons across studies were constrained by differences in datasets, evaluation protocols, and performance metrics. The principal barriers to practical adoption include morphological overlap between infections, class imbalance, and scarcity of expert-annotated images of bacterial and early-stage diseases, reliance on controlled-background datasets, limited external validation, model complexity, and insufficient interpretability. Future research should prioritize pathogen-balanced multicrop field datasets, standardized reporting and cross-dataset evaluation, multimodal fusion of RGB images with spectral and environmental data, domain adaptation, validated generative augmentation, explainable models, and lightweight edge deployment. By connecting lesion morphology with methodological and dataset evidence, this review provides a structured roadmap for developing robust, interpretable, and field-ready plant disease diagnosis systems.

title: A closed loop multimodal auditing framework for enhancing artificial intelligence reliability in medical emergency response
abstract: Ensuring the reliability of AI-powered information retrieval systems is critical in high-stakes domains such as first aid. Traditional audit methodologies are often static, manual, and unimodal, failing to address the dynamic, time-sensitive, and multimodal requirements of these applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce RADAR-FirstAid (Reliability-Aware Dynamic Auditing Framework), a closed-loop auditing pipeline — not a competing information system — for real-time, multimodal, and edge-aware auditing. Its key components include a Dynamic Query Simulator for generating criticality-weighted scenarios, a Multimodal Audit & Fusion Agent for verifying cross-modal consistency, a Differentiable Reliability Evaluator that employs LLM-based judges for automated assessment, and an Edge-Optimization Scheduler for efficient deployment. Applying the framework to a curated dataset of 1, 508 first-aid queries, we conduct a large-scale audit of Google’s AI Overviews (AIO) and Featured Snippets (FS), operated purely as black-box Systems under Audit. The audit reveals substantial reliability gaps: automated consistency scores of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\Phi _{cons}=0.68$$\end{document} (FS) and 0.72 (AIO), safety/relevance scores of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\Phi _{safe}=0.71$$\end{document} (FS) and 0.76 (AIO), and pronounced weaknesses on safety-critical “Binary” and “How-to” queries and on negative-sentiment queries where cautious tone matters most. Manual annotation on a 200-query subset validates the automated evaluation (Spearman \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\rho = 0.74$$\end{document}–0.87). Ablation studies confirm the essential role of each pipeline module, and geographical variance is minimal (SD \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$<0.03$$\end{document}). RADAR-FirstAid offers a scalable, automated, and reproducible audit instrument for AI-powered search systems in safety-critical domains.

title: Enhanced cotton leaf disease classification Through ConvNeXt and Random Walk Grey Wolf Optimization
abstract: India has the highest number of cotton-cultivated land globally, thus placing it among the biggest producers of cotton in the world. Despite the huge cotton production, cotton leaf diseases still remain one of the most significant causes of yield losses in the crop. Accurate and early diagnosis is one of the first steps towards finding the solutions to mitigate the effects of the disease. In this research paper, we present the ConvNeXt deep learning framework used along with Random Walk Grey Wolf Optimizer (RWGWO) to diagnose and classify various diseases in cotton leaf. In its performance, ConvNeXt shows better accuracy when compared to the traditional CNN, Self-Organizing Map Artificial Neural Networks (SOMANN), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and other hybrid models with classification accuracy of 98.39%. Among others, our model successfully diagnoses and classifies the diseases of bacterial blight and aphid infestation, powdery mildew, armyworm, target spot, and healthy cotton leaves. All this is possible through a carefully chosen data set with proper data augmentation. The results of this research indicate that there is a high potential in using deep learning technology to improve agribusiness and textile fibers supply chain through early detection and management of the diseases outbreaks, which reduces the waste of pesticides associated with the late disease diagnosis. On the other hand, it should be noted that the use of ConvNeXt has limitations since larger models of this framework (ConvNeXt-Large and ConvNeXt-XL) have high computational complexity and energy consumption. The future work will include using field data sets and implementation of multi-modal learning, which will take into consideration various environmental factors.

title: AI driven oral cancer diagnosis from clinical imaging and computational pathology to precision therapeutics
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a computational approach for analysing the complex and heterogeneous data generated across oral cancer diagnosis and management. This narrative review provides an integrated overview of AI applications from early oral lesion detection, computational pathology, prognostic assessment, and precision therapeutics. It describes how machine learning and deep learning process clinical photographs, digitized histopathological images, whole-slide images, radiological examinations, and molecular or clinical data to generate task-specific outputs. The review covers AI-assisted identification of suspicious oral lesions, histopathological detection of oral epithelial dysplasia and oral squamous cell carcinoma, assessment of tumor differentiation, characterization of disease progression, and prediction of treatment response for therapeutic stratification. Particular attention is given to the relationship between the input data, computational task, and clinically relevant output rather than to model architecture alone. Although several studies report high diagnostic performance, much of the current evidence remains based on retrospective datasets and internal validation, while external, multicentre, and prospective evaluations are comparatively limited. Major challenges include dataset quality and representativeness, domain shift, annotation variability, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows. Future progress will require patient-level evaluation, multicentre validation, multimodal integration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and prospective assessment of clinical utility. This review outlines the evolving role of AI as a potential decision-support framework across the oral cancer care pathway.

title: Spatial distribution and severity of soil acidity across land uses in Gozamen District, Upper Blue Nile Basin, Ethiopia
abstract: Ethiopia is facing a soil pH problem that has not yet been accurately measured due to limited research on this issue. This study attempts to quantify the range of acid soils and develop land use-specific soil acidity characteristics in the selected kebeles of Gozamen District of northwestern Ethiopia through field soil survey, GIS, and digital soil mapping. Soil samples were taken using stratified random sampling over six kebeles of the Gozamen District. Soil pH was analyzed based on the standard procedure of FAO (2020) and GLOSOLAN (2019). Atmospheric images of Sentinel-2 Level-2 A were analyzed for vegetation cover via Random Forest (RF) Machine Learning Models, producing land-use/land-cover map with an overall accuracy of 92% and a Kappa Coefficient of 0.88. Spatial variability of soil pH was found to range from a minimum of 4.11 to a maximum of 6.58 throughout the selected kebeles of Gozamen District. Approximately 43% of the Gozamen District (selected kebeles) is very strongly acidic, and 39% is strongly acidic, with only 16% exhibiting moderate to slightly acidic pH, making them potentially useful for agricultural production. Agricultural and grazing lands were identified as having the greatest level of acidification, while forest ecosystems retained comparatively higher levels of soil pH, demonstrating the positive impact of natural vegetation in preserving healthy soils. This combination of field soil sampling, Sentinel-2 imaging, RF classification, and geostatistical interpolation offers an effective and economical method to develop accurate high-resolution mapping for soils that will ultimately lead to site-specific liming, precision soil fertility management, and planning for land restoration as part of Ethiopia’s agricultural transformation and sustainability initiatives.

title: Mapping and synthesis of evidence on soil fertility management, fertilizer use efficiency, and greenhouse gas outcomes
abstract: Soil fertility management influences fertilizer use efficiency (FUE), crop productivity, and greenhouse gas (GHG) outcomes, yet these dimensions are often reported separately. This study mapped and synthesized evidence linking soil fertility management with FUE and GHG outcomes using a structured analytical framework. Specifically, the study (i) assessed the distribution of soil fertility and nutrient management practices, (ii) explored reported FUE responses, (iii) evaluated GHG outcomes, and (iv) examined integration across soil, efficiency, and emission dimensions. A PRISMA-ScR-informed evidence mapping approach was applied to 40 open-access studies comprising field experiments, long-term trials, surveys, modelling studies, reviews, and meta-analyses. Evidence was extracted using a structured matrix and synthesized using a weighted Evidence Index (EI) and Integrated Evidence Score (IES). Integrated soil fertility management accounted for 12 studies, organic amendments for 10, enhanced-efficiency fertilizers and inhibitors for 9, and precision or optimized nutrient management for 9. Reported NUE values ranged from 25% to 70%, with increases of 10–40% for enhanced-efficiency fertilizers, 15–35% for organic amendments and biochar approaches, and 10–25% for precision or optimized nutrient management. Reported N₂O reductions ranged from 10% to 50% across management categories. NUE, N₂O, and soil organic carbon were reported in 70%, 65%, and 50% of studies, respectively. Category-level EI ranged from 1.79 to 2.17, whereas IES ranged from 1.89 to 2.42, reflecting differences between methodological weighting and dimensional coverage. The synthesis provides a structured basis for harmonizing soil fertility, nutrient efficiency, productivity, and GHG indicators in future evidence synthesis and agricultural management research.

title: EBM-Nav: energy-based model for zero-shot visual navigation via implicit scene representation
abstract: Zero-shot visual navigation enables agents to generalize to unseen environments without task-specific training and is core to service robotics, warehouse logistics, and autonomous exploration. Existing approaches are observed to fail to achieve genuine zero-shot generalization: explicit-map methods rely on accurate reconstruction and are sensitive to sensor noise; supervised policies memorize training-scene patterns and degrade under illumination, furniture, and layout shifts; implicit representations offer continuous, differentiable encoding but remain confined to passive reconstruction and lack effective coupling with active decisions. To address this, EBM-Nav is proposed as a zero-shot navigation framework built on an energy-based model. Specifically, a periodic-activation implicit scene encoder is employed to map discrete RGB-D observations into a continuous, differentiable representation supporting arbitrary-resolution spatial queries. An energy function over the observation–action–goal triple is designed to reformulate navigation as gradient descent on an energy landscape. A frozen multimodal large language model is integrated to decompose long-horizon instructions into subgoals and generate candidate directions. A contrastive-divergence learning mechanism is developed with short-step Langevin dynamics to efficiently construct negative samples for training the energy function. Systematic experiments are conducted on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE continuous vision-and-language navigation benchmarks, and it is shown that EBM-Nav significantly outperforms state-of-the-art zero-shot methods in success rate, path efficiency, and navigation accuracy, while providing an interpretable energy-confidence mechanism for decisions. These results verify the energy-landscape zero-shot navigation paradigm, offer a general learning paradigm for embodied intelligence, and extend energy-based models from static perception to sequential decision-making, with methodological implications for service robots and autonomous exploration.

title: When does competitive intensity improve service quality? The moderating role of differentiation strategy
abstract: Competitive intensity is widely assumed to push firms toward higher service quality, yet the strategic conditions under which this pressure actually translates into quality gains remain poorly understood. Drawing on contingency theory, this study examines whether a firm’s differentiation strategy moderates the relationship between competitive intensity and service quality, and specifically tests whether strong differentiation substitutes for, rather than amplifies, the quality-enhancing effect of competition. The study uses survey data from 204 non-manufacturing business units operating in the United Kingdom, drawn from a broader research project on costing systems (data collected September–December 2018). The present analysis addresses a distinct research question and an interaction-form contingency model that was not examined in the original study. Competitive intensity, differentiation strategy and service quality were measured with multi-item, previously validated survey scales. Hierarchical moderated ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was used, with continuous predictors mean-centered before the interaction term was formed; heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors were applied as a robustness check, and simple-slope and Johnson–Neyman analyses were used to probe the interaction. Competitive intensity and differentiation strategy were each positively associated with service quality. Contrary to a simple reinforcement account but consistent with a substitution logic, differentiation strategy significantly and negatively moderated the competitive intensity–service quality relationship (b = − 0.094, p = .013; HC3 p = .015). The positive effect of competitive intensity on service quality was strongest among low differentiators and weakened, without fully disappearing across the observed range, among firms with the strongest differentiation commitments. The study contributes to contingency-based strategy research by reframing competitive intensity and differentiation strategy as interacting rather than independent antecedents of service quality, and by providing empirical evidence, from a UK non-manufacturing sample, of a substitution pattern between external competitive pressure and internal strategic commitment as drivers of service quality. Because the design is cross-sectional and based on a single respondent per business unit, the findings should be interpreted as associational rather than causal. Practical implications for managers balancing strategic positioning and competitive response are discussed.

Chronic thoracic aortitis versus primary medial degeneration in ascending aorta: a digital morphometric analysis of aortic layers remodelling.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Chronic aortitis (CA) represents a diverse group of inflammatory conditions often diagnosed incidentally in ascending aorta biopsies. While the 2015 and 2016 Consensus Statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta provide standardised histological classifications, data quantifying structural remodelling within individual aortic layers remain limited. Furthermore, distinguishing CA from primary non-inflammatory medial degeneration (MD) can be challenging, particularly when inflammation is sparse or burnt out, and secondary degenerative changes predominate. We aimed to compare morphological changes in CA and MD aneurysms and apply digital image analysis to quantify aortic wall layers. METHODS Retrospective histological analysis was performed on 63 ascending aortic specimens: CA (n=21), MD (n=21), and autopsy controls (n=21). Digitised elastic-stained sections were analysed using QuPath software to measure the thickness and cross-sectional area of the intima (I), media (M), and adventitia (A). Overall MD scores (i.e., summaries of each MD grade component) were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis based on binary logistic regression models. RESULTS CA demonstrated a profound architectural shift, characterised by medial thinning alongside marked intimal and adventitial expansion, resulting in significantly lower M/(I+A) thickness and area ratios compared with MD and controls (p <0.001). CA specimens also exhibited the most severe secondary degenerative changes, with significantly higher overall MD scores (median: 15 vs. 8; p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis revealed diagnostic utility of both the M/(I+A) thickness ratio (AUC = 0.964) and the M/(I+A) area ratio (AUC = 0.955) for identifying CA. A multivariable model combining the overall MD score with the M/(I+A) thickness ratio achieved an AUC of 0.971 (accuracy 88.1%), whereas combining it with the M/(I+A) area ratio yielded an AUC of 0.968 (accuracy 90.5%). CONCLUSION Digital morphometric analysis provides a reproducible and feasible method for quantifying structural remodelling in chronic aortitis. Changes in the proportions of the aortic layers, specifically intimal and adventitial expansion combined with medial thinning and severe secondary medial degeneration, can facilitate accurate differentiation of aortic wall pathologies, particularly in cases with sparse inflammation.

title: Columbianadin promotes osteoblast differentiation by modulating the SIRT1/β-catenin pathway in periodontitis and orthodontic tooth movement-induced rats.
abstract: Periodontitis (PD), a common inflammatory disorder causing irreversible periodontal degradation, is linked to systemic issues. Orthodontic tooth movement (OTM) in the context of PD worsens bone loss, which severely compromises orthodontic treatment stability and increases the risk of treatment failure. This study aims to thoroughly investigate the protective effects of Columbianadin (CBN) against PD/OTM-induced alveolar bone injury and dissect its underlying molecular mechanisms. To induce osteogenic differentiation, MC3T3-E1 cells were maintained in a specialized osteogenic induction medium supplemented with ascorbic acid and β-glycerophosphate. In vitro experiments using MC3T3-E1 cells revealed that CBN treatment substantially fostered osteoblastic differentiation, as reflected by elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity and robust matrix mineralization. Mechanistically, CBN enhanced SIRT1-mediated β-catenin deacetylation, whereas EX527-driven SIRT1 inhibition reduced β-catenin activity in differentiated cells. A rat OTM model within the framework of PD was established to document alveolar bone loss. We found that CBN exerted a protective effect on alveolar bone mass in PD/OTM rats, as it not only promoted alveolar bone formation but also inhibited bone resorption. CBN treatment also suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion in the alveolar bone of PD/OTM rats. Network pharmacology analysis identified potential target genes involved in CBN-mediated osteogenic differentiation. In summary, CBN protects against PD/OTM-induced alveolar bone damage in a SIRT1/β-catenin-dependent manner, suggesting CBN as a promising candidate for treating periodontal and OTM-related bone disorders.

Anti-adipogenic effects of flavonoids and stilbenoids on adipocyte differentiation, lipid accumulation and adipogenic markers in a 3T3-L1 cell line.
abstract: Obesity is a major global health challenge characterized by excessive expansion of adipose tissue mass, driven in part by dysregulated adipogenic differentiation. Targeting adipogenesis has therefore emerged as a promising strategy to limit adipose tissue expansion and associated metabolic disorders. Naturally occurring polyphenols, particularly flavonoids and stilbenoids, exhibit anti-adipogenic properties through multiple mechanisms; however, the molecular determinants underlying their activity remain insufficiently defined. In this study, the anti-adipogenic potential of a panel of 16 structurally related flavonoids and 2 stilbenoids was evaluated using the 3T3-L1 pre-adipocyte differentiation model. Experimental conditions were carefully optimized to ensure biological robustness, including cell passage number, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) concentration, and differentiation timing. Following cytotoxicity screening, adipogenic differentiation was assessed by Oil Red O staining and enzymatic quantification of intracellular triacylglycerides. Compounds showing significant inhibitory effects were further characterized by Western blot analysis of key adipogenic and lipid-handling proteins (C/EBPβ, PPARγ, FABP4, and ATGL), with transcriptional regulation evaluated by RT-qPCR for selected compounds. The results indicate that the tested compounds predominantly interfered with late stages of adipogenic differentiation, as C/EBPβ expression was largely preserved. Among the compounds evaluated, C10 (a synthetic 3-decyl-3',4',5,7-tetrahydroxyflavone) and piceatannol (C18) emerged as the most effective inhibitors of lipid accumulation. C10 markedly suppressed PPARγ isoforms, FABP4, and ATGL in a concentration-dependent manner, whereas piceatannol (C18) primarily reduced lipid accumulation through sustained FABP4 suppression with minimal effects on PPARγ. Overall, these findings highlight C10 and piceatannol (C18) as promising modulators of adipogenic differentiation and emphasize the importance of structure-activity relationships in shaping anti-adipogenic efficacy.

Integrated chemical profiling for honey authentication and origin discrimination.
abstract: This study presents an integrative analytical approach for honey authentication by combining physico-chemical parameters, stable carbon isotope ratios, and detailed profiles of sugars and organic acids to differentiate honeys according to floral origin. The high-performance anion-exchange chromatography with pulsed amperometric detection (HPAEC-PAD) method for sugar analysis was optimized and validated for the simultaneous separation of 9 saccharides within a 35-minute run time. Additionally, nine organic acids were quantified using an optimized ion chromatography method with conductometric detection (IC-CD). Multivariate analyses (principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA)) revealed that minor saccharides (trehalose, raffinose, maltose, erlose, isomaltose), dominant sugars (fructose and glucose) and their ratios, organic acids (citric, malic, succinic, maleic, and isocitric), as well as key physico-chemical parameters (electrical conductivity, free acidity) are critical discriminative markers of botanical origin. Within the pre-screened dataset, the optimized PLS-DA models successfully classified Robinia pseudoacacia and Honeydew honeys with zero misclassification errors (class error = 0.00; R2pred > 0.86; RMSEP ≤0.14). Although differentiating closely related floral groups and utilizing multiple analytical platforms can be resource-intensive, this innovative, derivatization-free approach demonstrates strong discriminatory potential. Ultimately, integrating targeted chemical profiling provides a robust proof-of-concept framework for botanical authentication, offering a reliable tool to prevent mislabeling and adulteration of honey.

title: The Unfinished Story of Megakaryopoiesis.
abstract: Since their nineteenth-century discovery, megakaryocytes (MKs) and the platelets they produce have remained among the least understood lineages in hematology. Understanding megakaryopoiesis and thrombopoiesis is essential for deciphering hematological disorders and developing platelet biomanufacturing and cell-based therapies. We revisit MK and platelet biogenesis, from MK emergence from hematopoietic stem cells to platelet release through proplatelet formation and cytoplasmic fragmentation. The growing complexity of differentiation pathways challenges the classical hierarchical view of hematopoiesis. Many concepts established in mice remain insufficiently validated in humans, motivating 3D bioengineered models for disease study that may rewrite key chapters in human platelet biology.

title: Circulating immune cells phenotypes discriminate bipolar disorder from major depressive disorder during a depressive episode: A machine learning elastic-net approach.
abstract: MDD and BD are characterized by differences in peripheral immune markers, in frequencies of T helper, T cytotoxic, Natural Killer (NK) and T regulatory cells that may contribute to the development of mood disorders. However, few studies have used immune cells populations to discriminate MDD from BD with inconsistent findings. We applied an elastic-net machine learning pipeline predictive model using 5-fold nested cross-validation based on a wide panel of immune cell populations to discriminate between MDD and BD. The sample included 124 MDD and 89 BD hospitalised for depressive episode, and 40 healthy controls (HC). The predictive model achieved an accuracy of 78%, with 76% sensitivity, 80% specificity. The model performed significantly better than chance (p < 0.001). BD diagnosis was associated with higher frequencies of cells populations producing proinflammatory cytokines (i.e. CD4+IFN-γ, CD4+IL-17, CD4+TNF-α, CD8+TNF-α, NK cells/TNF-α), and regulatory cells (FOXP3), whereas MDD diagnosis was associated with elevated frequencies of early activating memory cells both T helper and cytotoxic (i.e. CD4+CM/CD69+, CD4+EM/CD69+, CD8+CM/CD69+), and cytotoxic effector cells producing apoptotic proteins (CD8+EM/Perf+GrzB+, NK cells/Perf+GrzB+). Excluding patients in lithium only early activated and cytotoxic cells differentiated the two diagnoses. Limitations include possible residual instrument-related effects and cryopreservation effects, lack of generalization to other phases of the illness, lack of external validation. Our data confirm that MDD and BD show different immune signatures and suggest a more pronounced alteration of immune cell populations in MDD especially in cytotoxic CD8+ cells. Future studies should address these differences to develop more effective therapies for mood disorders.

title: MOSAIC-Age: Initial binding states and shared ageing trajectories establish a method-compatible predictive baseline for soil metal ageing.
abstract: Sequential-extraction and longitudinal studies document soil metal ageing, but differences in protocols, matrices and exposure histories limit cross-study assessment. MOSAIC-Age maps exact analytical protocols to method-compatible domains, equally weights independent experimental programs, and reconstructs shared reference trajectories anchored to the earliest measured state. Evidence spans 70 model-development and 23 registered holdout papers. P1 core training comprises six programs and 86 compositional states. Whole-program validation of 64 post-anchor states yielded RMSE 1.072 and 79.0% directional agreement. Two independent holdout programs yielded RMSE 0.654; ten external endpoints in a Cd/As research-family stratum yielded RMSE 0.275. In an agricultural-wastewater wetland experiment, predictions across 32 non-baseline states correlated with observations (r = 0.837), with RMSE 0.439 and 84.4% directional agreement. Treatment ordering was retained across eight 60 d endpoints (Spearman ρ = 0.738). Prediction intervals were assessed by coverage, width and proper scoring. Incorporating measured 60 d states improved 120 d forecasts over initial-anchor forecasts; persistence comparisons attributed improvement primarily to intermediate observations. The anchored baseline provides a shared temporal reference for state comparisons, while exposure and process observations identify local departures. MOSAIC-Age converts dispersed fractionation evidence into a computable, updatable baseline for relative mobility/activity screening and targeted monitoring, with uncertainty and applicability feedback.

Inhibiting MD2 activates AMPK-dependent PPARγ/NOX4 signaling to attenuate mitochondrial oxidative stress and relieve pulmonary hypertension.
abstract: AIMS Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a severe vascular disorder, is closely associated with chronic inflammatory states and oxidative stress. Myeloid differentiation protein 2 (MD2), a key co-receptor of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), is well established in mediating various inflammation-driven pathologies. However, its role in pulmonary hypertension and its potential involvement in oxidative stress regulation remain unclear. METHODS AND RESULTS MD2 expression was upregulated in both PH patients and murine PH models. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of MD2 improved hemodynamic parameters, attenuated pulmonary vascular remodeling, and reduced right ventricular hypertrophy. MD2 inhibition significantly reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that suppression of the membrane protein MD2 activated intracellular AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, leading to enhanced peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) activity. PPARγ, in turn, suppressed nuclear transcription of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), resulting in a marked reduction in mitochondrial oxidative stress. CONCLUSION This study indicates that MD2 may act as an upstream regulator of mitochondrial oxidative stress in PH. Inhibition of MD2 attenuates pulmonary hypertension through activation of the AMPK/PPARγ axis, which suppresses NOX4 mediated mitochondrial oxidative stress. Targeting MD2 may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for PH.

title: Patch Management or Public Law? A Critical Comment on the Five Eyes Guidance for the Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services
abstract: On 1 May 2026, six Five Eyes cybersecurity agencies jointly issued Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services, the first coordinated Anglophone statement on the governance of LLM-based autonomous agents. This Comment argues that, although the Guidance offers competent cybersecurity risk management within its stated remit, its institutional weight invites a broader governance reading that the document cannot bear, and that five structural limitations then come into view. First, the cybersecurity doctrines on which it relies are necessary but insufficient for agentic systems, whose delegated authority, underspecified goals, and long-horizon autonomy strain the assumptions of conventional controls. Second, it privatises systemic risk by imposing duties on deployers without specifying public-law obligations, redress, or liability across the agentic value chain. Third, it prescribes human oversight without specifying the conditions of effective control, so that responsibility risks being assigned to reviewers who lack the information, authority, or time to exercise it. Fourth, it reduces accountability to auditability, confusing a technical property with a legal relation between duty-holders and affected parties. Fifth, the security-defined mandates of its six authoring agencies, and the intelligence-oversight structures within which most of them sit, raise questions of institutional voice, while its Five Eyes-only authorship raises a risk of divergence from the AI frameworks now emerging in the European Union, the Republic of Korea and Japan. The Comment concludes by outlining the elements of an enforceable, rights-protective, cross-jurisdictional legal regime that should supplement, rather than be displaced by, the technical controls the Guidance recommends.

title: Estimation Of The Mass And The Spin Of The Neutron Star 4U 1728-34 Using Triples Of X-Ray Quasi-Periodic Oscillations
abstract: X-ray quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) were reported for 19 different observations of the atoll source 4U 1728- 34. Three of them reveal triplets of QPOs: a lower and a upper kHz QPOs and a low-frequency QPO. Even though they are discernible only after averaging we assume them to be simultaneous. We apply a separate model (formula) for each of the three frequencies of the observed QPOs and compose a system which contains three algebraic equations for the three unknown parameters - the mass and the specific angular momentum of the central neutron star, and the radius of the orbit of orgin of the given triplet of QPOs, which allows us to find the numerical values of the later. Error propagation formulas are applied for the obtaining of interval estimates of the parameters of the star. This is done through implicit function differentiation. The calculations are repeated with several different models for the kHz QPOs.

title: Deep learning multimodal fusion model based on ultrasound images and clinical-ultrasound texts for differentiating benign and malignant renal tumors.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To develop a deep learning multimodal fusion model based on ultrasound (US) images and clinical-US texts to differentiate benign and malignant renal tumors. METHODS The retrospective dataset from January 2012 to February 2023 in a tertiary hospital was used for model development and randomly allocated to training and validation sets. An independent prospective test set was obtained from March 2023 to October 2024. We developed Model-G using grayscale US (GUS) images, Model-GC using GUS and color Doppler flow imaging images, Model-T using clinical-US texts, and Model-UT using US images and clinical-US texts. ResNet50 was used for image feature extraction, BERT for text encoding, and ViT for multimodal classification. RESULTS In total, 1008 patients (740 in training set, 186 validation set, and 82 prospective test set) with a single renal tumor were included. In the validation set, Model-UT achieved the highest diagnostic performance in comparison to Model-G, Model-GC, and Model-T with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.86-0.93) (all p-values < 0.05). In the prospective test set, Model-UT yielded an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.97), outperforming high-level, mid-level, and low-level radiologists (all p-values < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS The multimodal fusion model presents promising potential in differentiating benign and malignant renal tumors. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE Deep learning model integrating US images with clinical-US texts improved benign-versus-malignant renal tumor differentiation. Decision-curve, controlled ablation, and SHAP analyses support its potential use as a clinical decision-support tool.

title: Phytohormonal networks and thermomemory in plant heat stress tolerance: From mechanistic integration to precision engineering.
abstract: Rising global temperatures pose a major threat to crop productivity, requiring mechanistically informed, scalable strategies to enhance heat stress (HS) tolerance. Phytohormones are central regulators of plant HS responses; however, tolerance instead emerges from dynamic, context-dependent network behavior. This review provides a mechanism-oriented synthesis of how major phytohormones coordinate HS adaptation. Specifically, we (i) reframe phytohormone action through core regulatory modules, including redox control, carbon-energy allocation, reproductive stability, and growth-defense trade-offs; (ii) resolve phytohormonal crosstalk into functional interaction networks that determine stress outcomes; (iii) define the molecular basis of heat priming and thermomemory; and (iv) evaluate translational strategies, including genetic engineering, precision breeding, and advanced delivery systems, together with their limitations under field conditions. We propose a unifying conceptual model in which HS tolerance is an emergent property of hierarchical phytohormonal networks operating across fast signaling, transcriptional memory, and metabolic buffering layers. This framework shifts the focus from single-pathway manipulation toward precision "hormonomics" and network-level engineering, providing a systems-level platform for developing climate-proof crops in a future, hotter climate.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of carbonic anhydrase IX-targeted PET/CT for detection of clear cell renal cell carcinoma in patients with renal masses: a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies.
abstract: OBJECTIVE The preoperative differentiation of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) from other renal masses remains challenging. Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a highly specific target for noninvasive ccRCC imaging. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CAIX-targeted PET/computed tomography (CT) for differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC renal masses. METHODS A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Registers (up to 30 September 2025) was supplemented by a bibliographic review. Studies evaluating CAIX-PET/CT against histopathologically were included. Of 528 records, five studies (n = 544 patients) were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were synthesized using a univariate fixed-effects model; predictive values, likelihood ratios, and diagnostic odds ratio were also calculated. RESULTS For the detection of histopathologically confirmed ccRCC (vs. non-ccRCC renal masses), the pooled sensitivity was 85.5% [95% confidence interval (CI): 81.6-88.7] and specificity of 86.5 (95% CI: 80.4-90.9). The hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic model yielded an area under the curve of 0.894. Exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a potential difference in diagnostic performance between the tracer subtypes. CONCLUSION This review provides low-certainty evidence that CAIX-targeted PET/CT is a highly accurate, noninvasive tool for differentiating ccRCC from non-ccRCC renal masses in presurgical populations. Clinically, its high positive predictive value (94.6%) strongly 'rules in' disease, while its modest negative predictive value (~69%) limits its ability to 'rule out' malignancy. Further studies are warranted to validate these findings in broader clinical cohorts and for small-molecule agents.

title: Sustaining firm competitiveness under multipolar fragmentation: a high-performance organization response architecture
abstract: This study aims to examine how firms can sustain competitiveness in a multipolar economy characterized by geoeconomic fragmentation, politicized markets, differentiated regional rules and increasing uncertainty. It focuses on the internal management practices through which firms translate external fragmentation into organizational coherence, resilience, legitimacy and renewal. This study develops an integrative conceptual synthesis. It first draws on the multipolar economy and strategy literatures to identify firm-level competitiveness pressures. It then uses published high-performance organization (HPO) case studies to derive practice bundles that support adaptation under fragmented external conditions. The study seeks analytical rather than statistical generalization. The synthesis identifies four firm-level competitiveness pressures: uncertainty and complexity, operating-model and value-chain redesign, nonmarket and legitimacy pressure, and talent, learning and coordination pressure. From the HPO literature, six HPO practice bundles are proposed as a response architecture: execution backbone, capability carriers, legitimacy and resilience platform, ecosystem sensing and stakeholder orchestration, adaptive operating model and innovation-for-adaptation. This study connects multipolar-economy research with HPO research and shows how internal management routines can operate as firm-level carriers of competitiveness under differentiated location conditions.
journal: Competitiveness Review: An International Business Journal

title: AI-driven forecasting and portfolio optimization under ESG and uncertainty regimes: evidence from global equity indices
abstract: This study investigates how advanced machine learning (ML) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models can enhance forecasting accuracy and portfolio decision-making under environmental, social, and governance (ESG)-driven and uncertainty-sensitive market conditions. The objective is to compare the predictive efficiency of state-of-the-art ML architectures with policy-based portfolio strategies to uncover the role of sustainability indicators in shaping market dynamics. We analyze daily data for major ESG and conventional market indices across the USA, Europe, and China, integrating the Standard Statistics Company and Poor's Publishing Company (S&P) Green Bond Index, Geopolitical Risk (GPR), the US Financial Stress Index (FSI), Physical Risk Index (PRI), and Transition Risk Index (TRI). The forecasting stage combines a 20-day long short-term memory (LSTM) temporal representation with Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) under a strict 70/15/15 chronological train-validation-test design and train-only scaling. The portfolio stage compares Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) in a weekly self-financing environment with long-only weights, a 40% position cap, and proportional transaction costs. Random-Walk/Ridge/LSTM forecasting benchmarks and Equal-Weight/Minimum-Variance portfolio benchmarks are included, together with multi-seed and transaction-cost robustness checks. Local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) is retained for local model interpretation. Forecasting performance is market-dependent rather than governed by a universally dominant learner. Validation selects LSTM-LightGBM for the China and US ESG indices, LSTM-XGBoost for Europe ESG, and LSTM-CatBoost for the three conventional indices. Multi-seed robustness yields positive average root mean square error (RMSE) gains over the Random Walk in five of six markets, with the strongest stability in China and statistically significant main-seed improvement for US ESG. In portfolio allocation, TD3 on the conventional opportunity set provides the strongest ex-post DRL performance (11.10% annualized return; Sharpe ratio 0.776), while SAC is the strongest ESG DRL strategy. Equal Weight remains a demanding benchmark, particularly for ESG portfolios, and the DDPG policies selected ex ante on validation remain profitable across three seeds and under transaction-cost scenarios up to 25 basis points (bps). The study extends the emerging literature by integrating explainable hybrid forecasting and continuous-action DRL within a leakage-controlled, benchmark-oriented framework. Its contribution lies in combining ESG-sensitive uncertainty variables, chronological validation, realistic self-financing portfolio constraints, explicit transaction-cost analysis, and reproducibility checks rather than assuming universal AI or ESG superiority.

title: Fault Diagnosis for Optical Transmission Systems Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanism Using DSP Power Monitoring
abstract: This paper proposes a fiber fault diagnosis method based on multi-scale feature fusion and an attention-enhanced neural network utilizing digital signal processing (DSP) power monitoring data, with potential applicability to online monitoring in optical transmission systems. The proposed approach employs a parallel convolutional architecture to extract multi-scale features, while an attention mechanism is introduced to emphasize critical features. Furthermore, a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) network is utilized to capture the temporal characteristics of the signal sequence, enabling accurate fault identification in optical transmission systems. Experimental validation was conducted using five typical types of optical fiber faults collected from a 400-Gb/s wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) operational network environment. The results show that the proposed method achieves an average window-level recognition accuracy of 99.15%, outperforming convolutional neural networks (CNN), CNN-BiGRU, and Transformer models by 5.38, 7.65, and 12.72 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method improves fault identification capabilities in optical communication networks, showing potential as a practical solution for intelligent fault diagnosis based on DSP monitoring data.

title: Automated Fetal Magnetocardiography Reconstruction Using a Biophysical Forward Model
abstract: Objective: Fetal magnetocardiography (fMCG) enables early detection of cardiac disease by non-invasively measuring fetal electrophysiological activity. However, current signal estimation methods for fMCG require complex, labor-intensive human processing because they rely on blind source separation or template-based projection techniques. Methods: We propose an automated signal reconstruction approach that recovers fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG measurements without manual annotation. Our approach leverages the relationship between measurements and cardiac signals via a biophysically grounded forward model that represents cardiac sources as time-varying magnetic dipoles. This enables reconstruction of physiologically interpretable three-dimensional vectorcardiographic signals along with their spatial position. Results: Validation on synthetic data with known ground truth confirms accurate recovery of cardiac source parameters. On real fMCG recordings, the reconstruction shows strong agreement with established reference methods. Conclusion: The proposed forward-model approach automatically reconstructs fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG recordings and produces signals in an interpretable vectorcardiographic source domain. Significance: Automated, interpretable fMCG reconstruction could make fetal cardiac assessment more reliable and support potential translation into prenatal care.

title: DPSeg: Differentiated Perception Medical Image Segmentation via Context-Aware Compensation and Stratified Uncertainty Attention.
abstract: In medical image segmentation, accurate recognition of regions hindered by blurry boundaries, low contrast, and complex backgrounds is crucial. These issues lead to significant differences in segmentation difficulty within a single image. However, existing methods typically adopt a uniform modeling strategy across the entire feature map, overlooking the mismatch between segmentation difficulty and attention intensity. Consequently, they fail to adequately focus on key regions, diluting the representations of challenging regions. To address these challenges, we propose DPSeg, a differentiated perception medical image segmentation framework via context-aware compensation and stratified uncertainty attention. Specifically, DPSeg comprises three key components. The Context-Aware Compensation (CAC) module refines encoder features by integrating key region-aware prompts and contextual information, compensating for encoding-induced distortions and enabling differentiated perception, thereby providing higher-quality representations for decoding. Additionally, the Stratified Uncertainty Transformer (SUTrans) module explicitly modulates the attention intensity of different regions based on their segmentation uncertainty, thereby possessing differentiated perception ability while effectively suppressing redundant feature interactions. Moreover, we propose a Foreground-Uncertainty Adaptive Weighted Loss (FUAWL) to enable differentiated supervision across decoding stages, applying stronger guidance to uncertain regions in shallow decoding and emphasizing foreground regions in deep decoding to improve boundary delineation and mitigate foreground-background imbalance. Extensive experiments on four challenging datasets demonstrate that DPSeg achieves competitive segmentation performance.
journal: IEEE transactions on image processing : a publication of the IEEE Signal Processing Society

title: A Transferable Targeted Adversarial Attack Method Based on Feature Interpretation and Dynamic Optimization.
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely applied in critical fields but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Among them, transferable targeted adversarial attacks in black-box scenarios are particularly dangerous, as they can mislead models into predicting specified target labels. Existing methods improve targeted transferability through optimization refinement, input diversity, source-model enhancement, or feature-space perturbation. However, they generally do not exploit interpretation information from a white-box source model (WSM) as iterative feedback to refine global perturbations toward discriminative local regions. Thus, redundant and source-model-specific components may remain in less informative regions, limiting cross-model transferability. To address these limitations, we propose a transferable targeted adversarial attack method based on feature interpretation and dynamic optimization (TAFID). TAFID introduces an interpretation-feedback optimization mechanism within an iterative transfer-based targeted attack framework. It uses global-local feature alignment to maximize the target-label output and the cosine similarity between global and cropped local features, promoting stable target-oriented intermediate representations. Subsequently, it applies a dynamically updated perturbation mask to reweight the global perturbation according to the changing focus area of the WSM. Experimental results demonstrate that when attacking DNNs, third-party deep learning systems and defense methods, TAFID improves the average targeted attack success rate (TASR) on black-box target models (BTMs) by 48.6%, 30.6%, 30.7%, 42.8%, 48.3%, and 36.4% compared with reverse adversarial perturbation (RAP), object-based diverse input (ODI), sharpness-aware self-distillation and weight scaling (SASD-WS), clean feature mixup (CFM), SupHigh+ft and feature tuning mixup (FTM), respectively. Moreover, the generated adversarial examples maintain reasonable similarity to the original examples, indicating a favorable balance between attack effectiveness and example authenticity. Our code is available at https://github.com/zyt2020/TAFID.
journal: IEEE transactions on neural networks and learning systems

title: Enhancing wild pollinator diversity in Mediterranean central Chilean crops: The role of natural habitats and proximity to the orchard edges
abstract: Pollinator diversity is declining worldwide, mainly due to agricultural habitat loss, threatening wild plant reproduction and crop pollination. Although natural habitat supports pollination services in agricultural landscapes, the amount needed remains unclear. We assessed how the percentage of natural habitat (NH) and distance from the orchard edge (DFE) influence pollinator richness and abundance in sweet cherry and apple orchards in Mediterranean central Chile. Twenty‐seven orchards of each crop were sampled over 2 years, classified by NH within a 1‐km buffer ( 70%). Pan traps surveyed pollinators at three distances from the orchard edge to the crop interior (0, 70 and 140 m). Both crops were modelled jointly, as crop identity did not affect pollinator richness, abundance, or honey bee abundance. Wild pollinator richness and abundance were higher with more surrounding natural habitat and decreased with distance from the edge. This decline was steeper in orchards with less natural habitat, buffering the edge effect. Honey bee abundance was unaffected by NH or DFE, and both wild pollinator and honey bee metrics were lower in the second year. Species composition differed significantly among NH categories, crops and years, although crop‐ and year‐related differences were each driven by only a small subset of taxa. Most species contributing to compositional differences among NH categories increased in abundance with NH, and none were more abundant in orchards with less than 35% NH. Our results suggest that landscapes with at least 35% of NH may better maintain wild pollinator diversity, although this value should not be interpreted as a biological threshold.

title: Integrating developmental traits, morphometrics and machine learning for sex classification of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae).
abstract: Aedes aegypti (Linnaeus, 1762), the primary vector for dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever, requires precise sex separation for the effective application of the sterile insect technique. This study integrates developmental biology, morphometric analysis and machine learning to differentiate sexes in Ae. aegypti pupae and adults. We evaluated developmental parameters across six generations of the Old Balara strain. Morphometric data from pupae and adults, including pupal cephalothorax dimensions, pupal length, pupal weight, adult wing length and adult thorax length, were collected to assess their correlations. Pupal morphometrics (cephalothorax dimensions and pupal length and weight) were used to train nine ML models for pupal sex classification. Males pupated significantly earlier (5.61 ± 0.10 days) than females (6.40 ± 0.16 days). In the absence of mating, females lived longer (22.63 ± 0.42 days) than males (20.13 ± 0.34 days). After mating, longevity declined, with females showing a 10.34% reduction (2.34 days) and males a 32.94% reduction (6.63 days). Across all morphometric parameters (cephalothorax length, width and perimeter in mm; cephalothorax area in mm2; pupal length in mm; pupal weight in mg; adult wing length in mm; thorax length in mm), females were significantly larger than males. Pupal cephalothorax perimeter and area strongly correlated with adult thorax and wing lengths (R2 up to 0.88), indicating their predictive value for adult size. Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines and Naïve Bayes achieved 100% accuracy in pupal sex classification on the test set. Integrating morphometric analysis with machine learning significantly enhances sex sorting precision for the sterile insect technique, improving mosquito control efficiency by ensuring only males are released. Future research should explore incorporating image-based data and advanced machine learning techniques to further refine these methods across diverse mosquito populations.

title: Field generation of triparental sugar beet plants through polyspermy-induced three-parent breeding.
abstract: Polyspermy, the fertilization of an egg by two sperm cells, can generate viable triparental offspring in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. To explore the potential for three-parent breeding in a crop species, male-sterile sugar beet plants were grown alongside genetically distinct pollen donors carrying dominant, traceable selection markers. Progeny carrying genetic signatures from two fathers were identified and subjected to further genetic analysis. The combined detection of paternal markers from two pollen donors and an additional chromosome set confirms the triparental origin of these plants, demonstrating the potential for three-parent breeding in sugar beet under field conditions.

title: CO2 emission and microbial community dynamics in soybean farmland under different organic material returning.
abstract: Fertilization not only influences crop productivity but also plays a pivotal role in regulating soil CO2 emissions within agricultural ecosystems. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms governing soil CO2 emissions under different fertilization regimes in the Northeast China Black Soil Region. Field experiments were conducted using four treatments: mineral fertilizer (NPK), and NPK combined with biochar (NPK + BC), organic fertilizer (NPK + OF) or straw (NPK + SF). A comprehensive assessment was performed, including measurements of soil CO2 flux, physicochemical properties, microbial community composition, plant physiological traits and crop yield. The results showed that, compared with the CK, soybean yields significantly increased by 10.00%, 8.15% and 3.70% under NPK + BC, NPK + OF and NPK + SF, respectively. Regarding mature stage soil properties, NPK + BC, NPK + OF and NPK + SF significantly elevated soil organic matter (SOM) by 16.30%, 23.86% and 1.39%, meanwhile available phosphorus (AP) by 19.76%, 24.00% and 6.78%, respectively. CO2 flux was reduced by 24.66% in NPK + BC but increased by 41.34% in NPK + OF. Furthermore, fertilization significantly altered microbial diversity; the ACE index increased by 7.82% under NPK + BC in the mature stage. Specifically, Proteobacteria abundance rose by 41.30% under NPK + OF, while Basidiomycota-associated with carbon sequestration-increased by 163.88% under NPK + BC. Structural equation modelling indicated that variation in soil CO2 flux was associated with SOM and microbial metabolic responses. DNDC model projections suggest that adopting biochar-based fertilization could reduce CO2 emissions in Heilongjiang Province by approximately 586,465 tons annually. These findings provide quantitative evidence for developing low-carbon, yield-enhancing fertilization strategies in sustainable soybean production.

title: Biophysically constrained learning from healthy neural priors improves motor decoding in pathological cortical networks
abstract: High-performance brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) rely on stable neural representations, yet brain functional impairments inherently disrupt canonical encoding, creating a fundamental decoding paradox. Conventional data-driven approaches struggle to bridge this gap because of pathological data scarcity and heterogeneity. Here, we propose to leverage healthy neural priors and introduce Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a paradigm embedding biophysical constraints into healthy neural recordings to guide neural decoding. In a gesture classification task using high-density electrocorticography from patients with gliomas infiltrating the motor cortex, PACT improved the accuracy by more than 10%, effectively restoring the distorted semantic geometry of motor commands and realigning them with healthy canonical representations (correlation increase: r = 0.66 to r = 0.94). Mechanistically, PACT induced an emergent “inverse weighting” strategy: The model autonomously suppresses high-power pathological noise while reanchoring spatial attention to functional compensatory regions. This study provides a proof of concept for improving decoding in compromised networks by harnessing healthy neural dynamics, laying the theoretical foundation for future BCI deployments in clinical populations.

title: An in situ forming immunomodulatory hydrogel reinvigorates exhausted CD8 + T cells via preserving their mitochondrial fitness
abstract: CD8 + T cell exhaustion driven by mitochondrial dysfunction remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report an in situ forming d -α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS)–based hydrogel [multifunctional thermosensitive composite gel (MTC Gel)] that reinvigorates exhausted CD8 + T cells by preserving mitochondrial fitness through a two-pronged strategy. After intratumoral injection, MTC Gel rapidly undergoes gelation at physiological temperature and dissociates to generate a high local concentration of TPGS, which targets cancer cell mitochondria to trigger prodeath mitophagy. This process induces robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) and blocks tunneling nanotube–mediated mitochondrial hijacking. Meanwhile, NLG919-loaded hybrid nanoparticles released from MTC Gel synergistically restore mitochondrial biogenesis in CD8 + T cells suppressed by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. Across multiple murine tumor models, MTC Gel reprograms T cell immunity by reducing CD8 + T cells exhaustion while enhancing effector and cytotoxic functions, thereby eliciting potent tumoricidal activity. These findings highlight this rationally designed hydrogel system as a clinically translatable platform for next-generation ICD-based cancer immunotherapies.

title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment
abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor–mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate–induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

title: CASTOR1 functional inactivation drives KRAS -mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression
abstract: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS -driven non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRAS G12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRAS G12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS -driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

title: Learning by moving: Physical motion accelerates category learning
abstract: Categorization is crucial for survival, helping animals forage, navigate, and avoid predators—all tasks involving movement. Yet, dominant theories of category learning treat it as a purely cognitive or perceptual process. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating that physical movement can enhance category learning—but selectively. Using immersive virtual reality, we found that performing large actions, such as swinging a lightsaber, substantially improved learning of categories requiring integration of multiple cues (e.g., distinguishing aggressive from noncancerous lesions), while having minimal impact on categories involving independent evaluation of features (e.g., sorting by color and shape). This selective enhancement reveals a previously unrecognized motor contribution to categorization and may explain why prior studies missed it, opening avenues for optimizing training in critical categorization tasks.

title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs
abstract: Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 “FADDosome” complexes, restrained by cFLIP L . Accordingly, deletion of CASP-8 robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor–driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor–initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor–driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

title: Polycomb factor PHF19 affects AML initiation, patient prognosis, and survival
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19 KO ) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19’s role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19 KO hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature—PHFScore—which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19’s key role in AML biology and prognosis.

title: Lineage-specific and gestational age–dependent DNA methylation programming orchestrates human placental development
abstract: The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base–resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age–dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated that DNMT1 was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation
abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the Escherichia coli –containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest E. coli signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

title: SCML2 inhibits PrimPol-mediated DNA replication repriming and regulates replication gap-associated cancer cell vulnerability
abstract: PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser 267 , which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser 267 hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.
