title: A continuous confinement-deconfinement transition in a triangular quantum magnet
abstract: A continuous transition between phases hosting distinct excitations—bosonic magnons versus fermionic spinons—is a long-sought phenomenon in quantum magnetism, analogous to the confinement-deconfinement transition in quantum chromodynamics. We report evidence for such a transition in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet thallium ytterbium disulfide. Antiferromagnetic order develops below T N ≈ 0.53 kelvin. A c -axis field suppresses this order, driving the system into a gapless quantum spin liquid with a spinon Fermi surface above μ 0 H c ≈ 3 T , evidenced by a finite residual linear term in thermal conductivity, a Pauli-like susceptibility, and a temperature-independent nuclear magnetic resonance Knight shift. Approaching H c from above, the scattering rate of itinerant excitations is strongly enhanced, while their density of states shows no critical enhancement, atypical of conventional magnetic quantum criticality. These results point to a continuous confinement-deconfinement transition governed by fractionalized excitations beyond the Ginzburg-Landau paradigm.

title: A phosphorylation-gated GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 module controls drought-responsive transcription
abstract: Drought adaptation requires rapid spatial reorganization of signaling proteins to reprogram stress-responsive transcription, yet how phosphorylation coordinates this process remains unclear. Here we aimed to define how phosphorylation-gated protein relocalization regulates a BpLBD1-centered drought pathway in Betula platyphylla (birch). Drought activated two kinase branches: BpAGC phosphorylated BpMAPK6 at Ser318 within a cryptic nuclear localization signal, promoting importin α recognition, whereas BpCKII phosphorylated BpGAPDH at Thr109, Thr270, Ser279 and Thr298, promoting importin β recognition. Dual phosphorylation enabled coordinated nuclear accumulation of BpMAPK6 and BpGAPDH. In the nucleus, phosphorylated BpGAPDH acted as a scaffold-like adaptor coupling BpMAPK6 to BpLBD1, enabling BpMAPK6-mediated phosphorylation of BpLBD1 at Ser29. This weakened BpLBD1 binding to the BpMYB123 promoter, reduced expression of the drought-sensitivity regulator BpMYB123 , and de-repressed drought-responsive genes such as BpRD29B . Disrupting BpGAPDH or BpLBD1 Ser29 phosphorylation compromised drought tolerance. Thus, a phospho-spatial GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 switch couples nuclear protein assembly to drought-responsive transcription.

journal: Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking
abstract: RFDT [4] is a physically consistent differentiable RF ray tracing framework that constructs digital twins by solving the inverse problem, i.e., inferring scene geometry and materials from observed RF signals. However, operating it demands two distinct kinds of expertise, namely authoring a physically plausible 3D scene and formulating an inverse problem over its parameters, which has kept the tool in the hands of its authors. In this work, we demonstrate RFDT as an agentic workbench, built on an open-source stack of differentiable ray geometry, wireless propagation, and FMCW radar packages, and driven from a 3D editor that hosts a language agent. The agent constructs scenes, configures simulations, and formulates inverse design on the attendee's behalf, dispatching to the same plugin API that the packages expose to Python. Attendees instruct the agent to synthesize a labeled RF dataset on demand, then watch RFDT invert a real radar measurement into a human pose by gradient descent. The demonstration runs entirely offline on a single laptop.

title: From Code Scarcity To Verification Scarcity: The New Bottleneck in Agentic Software Engineering
abstract: I still remember how studying computer science felt in the early 2000s. Coding was a beast that overwhelmed almost everybody. Thinking computationally, then turning that thinking into syntax, was not an easy mental operation. We looked up to talented students who ranked in ACMICPC programming contests; they were known simply as the coders. After graduation, some of us even chose different tech careers just to avoid coding. For those who stayed, producing and debugging code could take weeks, and much of the development lifecycle was organized around waiting for it. Fast-forward to today, and AI agents can generate substantial amounts of code in minutes or hours. Yet many organizations still focus on how much more code or how many more features they can produce. Beyond that hype, a more important question is emerging: are we generating the right change, and will it remain right as the system evolves? The question, then, is no longer simply how much code we can generate, but how much software change we can generate while maintaining justified confidence that it is the right change. This article examines the emerging challenge of establishing that confidence as code generation becomes increasingly abundant.

title: Long‐Term Population Dynamics of the Spotted Stem Borer (Chilo partellus) in Contrasting Maize Farming Systems Under Variable Climatic Conditions in East Africa
abstract: The spotted stem borer (Chilo partellus) is one of the most destructive pests of maize in sub‐Saharan Africa, causing substantial yield losses and threatening food security among smallholder farming communities. This study investigated the long‐term relationships between climatic variability and C. partellus incidence across contrasting organic and conventional farming systems in two agroecological zones. Biweekly monitoring observations of C. partellus incidence were summarized quarterly for temporal analyses across four long‐term farming systems at Chuka and Thika: conventional high‐, organic high‐, conventional low‐, and organic low‐input. The resulting analytical series represented 32 and 28 quarterly positions at Chuka and Thika, respectively. Climatic variables (temperature, rainfall, and relative humidity) were obtained from on‐site weather stations. Spearman’s rank correlation, cross‐correlation, ARIMA/SARIMA time‐series models with exogenous climatic predictors (ARIMAX/SARIMAX), and Bayesian generalized linear mixed models were used to evaluate climatic associations and farming systems effects. Temperature emerged as the climatic variable most consistently associated with C. partellus incidence, showing significant negative relationships across all farming systems at Chuka and within the organic farming systems at Thika, whereas rainfall and relative humidity exhibited comparatively weak associations. Cross‐correlation analyses indicated predominantly contemporaneous and short lag associations (0–2 quarters) between climatic variables and pest incidence. Time‐series models were evaluated using descriptive measures of in‐sample agreement between observed and fitted values. Across farming systems, R 2 values ranged from 0.039 to 0.650, indicating substantial variation in the degree to which the fitted models represented the observed temporal patterns. These measures describe in‐sample model fit and should not be interpreted as evidence of out‐of‐sample predictive or forecasting performance. Bayesian analyses further indicated that C. partellus incidence was higher in the organic than in the conventional high‐input systems after accounting for climatic variability, whereas the 95% credible intervals for farming system effects in the low‐input systems overlapped zero. Overall, these findings suggest that climatic variability and farming system management are associated with long‐term variation in C. partellus incidence. The findings may inform the development of climate‐informed pest‐monitoring and integrated pest management strategies, while independently validated models would be required before application for pest forecasting under sustainable maize production in East Africa.

title: Designing Discursive Identity: Integrating Indigenous Relational Values with Informational Baselines in Public-Facing Environmental Chatbots
abstract: This study examines how assigning a specific cultural identity to an AI changes how it communicates complex environmental topics. We compared two public-facing water conservation chatbots: Waterbot, a standard baseline providing objective scientific facts, and Riverbot, which integrates Indigenous relational perspectives by answering from the perspective of a river. By analyzing user interactions with the bots, we found systematic differences between the two models. Riverbot generated responses at a more accessible reading level than the Waterbot baseline. Additionally, while Waterbot remained emotionally neutral, Riverbot expressed a broader range of nuanced emotions, functioning as a more relatable conversational agent. These findings indicate that public-facing AI design should go beyond simple information delivery. Integrating relational and cultural values into a chatbot’s identity can improve its emotional resonance and accessibility, offering a practical approach for designing future environmental communication tools.
journal: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting

title: On the Distribution of Synteny Block Lengths in Prokaryote Genomes under a Neutral Model of Genome Dynamics.
abstract: In bacterial and archaeal genomes, functionally linked genes often cluster in operons that enable coregulation of expression of these genes and production of their protein products in stoichiometric amounts. Many operons are shared by genomes of distantly related bacteria and archaea due in part to evolutionary conservation and in part to horizontal gene transfer (HGT). In contrast, similarity between species in their gene order along the chromosome can be merely a result of evolutionary closeness such that synteny has not yet been disrupted by genome dynamic events occurring during evolution. In general, however, accurate differentiation of operons from spurious gene clusters is a non-trivial task that depends on an underlying model of neutral genome evolution. Here, we employ a recently developed stochastic model of genome rearrangement ("jump model") that accounts for HGT across prokaryote species evolving along a phylogenetic tree to infer the size distribution of shared gene strings (synteny blocks) under neutral evolution. Analytic expressions are derived for the expected number of synteny blocks of a given size (or of maximal size) depending on the evolutionary distance between the genomes and the rates of different types of evolutionary events. This analysis is related to the well-studied family of stick-breaking problems, but the discrete structure and stochastic nature of the evolutionary process provide for the development of a simple, independent model. We demonstrate the predictive power of this model by computer simulations of synthetic data as well as by simulating genomes on real trees obtained from the Alignable Tight Genome Clusters database.
journal: Journal of computational biology : a journal of computational molecular cell biology

title: Agentic Intelligence for Scalable Metadata Mining in Telecom Big Data Systems.
abstract: The high rate at which telecommunication services are changing has yielded a volume of heterogeneous data never seen before such as call detail records, signaling data, and subscriber activity traces. These datasets are crucial in relation to optimization and business intelligence, but effective use of such datasets requires quality metadata. Traditional metadata management is mostly manual and centralized, which cannot support the pace and scale of the new telecom big data systems. As a solution to these shortcomings, the present article suggests a scalable metadata mining strategy that is founded on agentic intelligence. In comparison to more traditional machine learning pipelines, agentic intelligence enables the use of autonomous goal-oriented AI agents, capable of reasoning in a hard data space and relevant to new network topologies and network schemas. The proposed architecture will include a multiagent architecture at a distributed level, having specialized agents: (1) schema drifting ingestion and monitoring agents of data flows; (2) semantic mining actors based on natural language processing to infer contextual metadata; (3) process-aware agents for process mining to determine lineage and dependencies between data; and (4) compliance with policy and metadata retrospect: government agents. A major effect of the work is the integration of agentic intelligence and scalable infrastructures of big data such as cloud-native analytics platforms and distributed data lakes. These agents coordinate themselves using lightweight coordination mechanisms to provide a persistent metadata knowledge layer that facilitates system interoperability and robust downstream analytics. The design concepts are geared toward horizontal scalability and fault tolerance, enabling the distribution of the agents at dynamically evolving manner regarding the workload peak. Besides, agents also enhance their strategies upon continuous feedback to handle concept drift as well. Typical examples of telecom applications such as monitoring network performance and fraud detection have demonstrated that such an approach far outperforms a rule-based approach in the accuracy, coverage, and timeliness of metadata. And lastly, the framework will be capable of offering more dynamic and sustainable data management within the telecom sector.

title: Signalling pathways governing the transition from monocytes to a lipid-associated macrophage-like state
abstract: Lipid-associated macrophages (LAMs) are a recently established hallmark of metabolic diseases and the tumour microenvironment. They are identified by expression of specific marker genes and proteins, including GPNMB, SPP1, and TREM2. In vivo cell fate tracing demonstrated that LAMs are recruited to diseased lesions from circulating monocyte pools. However, due to challenges in isolating LAMs and a lack of in vitro models, the intracellular signalling pathways and transcriptional regulators that govern the transition of monocytes into LAMs remain elusive. LAM marker expression was measured in monocytic cell lines (THP-1 and U937) and primary monocytes (mouse bone marrow-derived and human PBMC-derived). THP-1 and U937 cells were treated with phorbol 12-myristate 14-acetate (PMA). Analyses of transcriptomic data sets and pharmacological activators and inhibitors were used to dissect the underlying pathways. Lysosomal acidification, phagocytosis, and lipid handling was assessed with biochemical assays. Public datasets, a reporter cell line, and specific inhibitors were utilised to evaluate the role of nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG). We show that induction of monocyte cell lines with the potent protein kinase C (PKC) activator PMA leads to a strong upregulation of LAM marker genes on the mRNA and protein level, mirroring the LAM marker expression observed in vivo in a mouse model of steatohepatitis. Pharmacological PKC inhibition completely repressed cell adhesion and LAM marker expression. Functionally, PKC is necessary for triglyceride storage upon lipid loading, effective lysosomal function, and phagocytosis. Downstream of PKC, focal adhesion kinase (FAK) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT) signalling regulated adhesion and sustained LAM marker expression. On the transcriptional level, NF-κB is crucial for general macrophage differentiation and PPARG as one player in the transcriptional network regulating the LAM program. In primary mouse and human monocytes, FAK-dependent adherence to culture plates is sufficient for strong upregulation of LAM markers. Thus, we report a simple model to study LAM biology in vitro and shed light on the intracellular signalling pathways and downstream transcriptional regulation required for a LAM program.

title: AI-driven war gaming as a tool for urban resilience: simulating conflict scenarios to enhance future city planning
abstract: Urban warfare remains a key blind spot in conventional planning paradigms, with cities exposed to cascading systemic collapse. In this research, we present AI-powered war gaming as an innovative method for simulating adversarial scenarios, ranging from attacks on infrastructure to mass displacement, and for strengthening urban resilience. Taking Mosul, Iraq, as a case study, we create a digital twin of the city and use agent-based modeling and adversarial AI to stress-test its post-war reconstruction. Experiments demonstrate that informal social networks (e.g. markets) outperform formal systems at crisis response, and that modular infrastructure design can reduce single-point vulnerabilities by 35–40%. However, the approach also exposes ethical hazards, including the possible weaponization of AI models and biases in training data. We make strategic policy recommendations to the United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) and urban planners, highlighting the importance of fragmented redundancy in infrastructure networks, identifying organic nodes of resilience, and implementing strict humanitarian constraints on the use of artificial intelligence in cities. The implications conflict with traditional planning models that view conflict as an external shock, recommending its integration as a quantifiable element in resilience planning instead.

title: Dichamanetin attenuates hydrogen peroxide-induced cytotoxicity in retinoic acid (RA) -differentiated human neuroblastoma (SH-SY5Y) cells
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a leading neurodegenerative disorder that imposes a significant global socioeconomic burden. It is characterised as progressive cognitive decline and a complex multifactorial pathology. Despite extensive research, current therapeutic options are limited. Emerging evidence suggests that oxidative stress is critical in the early pathological event preceding the classical hallmarks of AD. Targeting oxidative stress is a promising strategy for treating AD. Flavonoids are attractive due to their antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective effects in AD. Dichamanetin (C29H24O6) is a rare C-benzylated flavanone that seldom occur in nature with reported antibacterial, and anti-malarial. Importantly, it has been suggested to possess anti-Alzheimer’s disease in-silico. However, neither its antioxidative nor neuroprotective potential has been explored in-vitro. Thus, this study aimed to address this gap by establishing an efficient method for the synthesis of dichamanetin and investigating its antioxidant properties and neuroprotective potential against hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂)-induced cytotoxicity in-vitro. In this study, we described the synthesis of dichamanetin using microwave irradiation and investigated its antioxidative activity using DPPPH and FRAP assay. Furthermore, we studied dichamanetin’s neuroprotective potential against hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-insult as an in-vitro AD model using three treatment conditions include pre-treatment, co-treatment, and staggered co-treatment using CCK-8 cell viability assay. Dichamanetin was synthesised via microwave irradiation method, overcoming the limitations of isolation and purification from natural sources which often resulted in low yield. The improved synthesis method produced a good yield of 50% and purity of 95–97% determined via LC-MS and 1H NMR analyses. It shows that dichamanetin has low antioxidative activity as shown by FRAP ability. Importantly, it was non-cytotoxic to cholinergic neurons at concentrations below 3.125 µg/mL. It is shown to be a potent neuroprotectant in protecting the cholinergic neurons against H2O2-insult at 0.781 µg/mL, eliciting the highest neuroprotective effect in 6-hour staggered co-treatment comparable to quercetin and donepezil. Dichamanetin attenuated H₂O₂-induced cytotoxicity in RA-differentiated SH-SY5Y cells, supporting its potential as a neuroprotective candidate against oxidative stress. Further studies are warranted to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and validate its efficacy, pharmacokinetics, safety, and therapeutic potential in relevant in vivo models of Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Managerial Decision-Making for Sustainable Agro-Export Operations in Latin America: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis, 1996-2025
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence is transforming agro-export management by converting production, commercial, climate, and logistics data into support for more timely decisions. In Latin America, however, evidence on its managerial applications and contribution to sustainable operations remains fragmented. Objective To synthesize evidence on the application of artificial intelligence to managerial decision-making and its contribution to the efficiency, sustainability, traceability, resilience, and competitiveness of sustainable agro-export operations in Latin America from 1996 to 2025. Methods A systematic review and bibliometric analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Scopus and Web of Science yielded 2160 records; after filtering, screening, and eligibility assessment, 73 studies were included. Bibliometrix in RStudio and VOSviewer were used to analyze scientific production, authors, countries, sources, Bradford’s and Lotka’s laws, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic clusters. Results Scientific output increased markedly after 2021 and peaked in 2024. Scopus accounted for 98.95% of the records. China led with 170 publications, while Brazil, with 149, was the only Latin American country among the five most productive. Four thematic areas were identified: prediction and classification using artificial intelligence and machine learning; logistics, supply chains, and suppliers; sustainable resource management and climate risks; and digital transformation through Agriculture 4.0/5.0. Across the literature, artificial intelligence was found to reduce uncertainty and improve decision-making, although its effectiveness depends on data quality, digital infrastructure, and organizational capabilities. Conclusions Artificial intelligence represents a strategic capability for strengthening sustainable agro-export operations. Its impact depends on integrating algorithms with reliable data, technological infrastructure, organizational capabilities, and sustainability criteria. The limited representation of Latin America highlights the need for further empirical research adapted to regional conditions.

title: How AI agents search
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have evolved from relying primarily on knowledge stored in their parametric memory to using non-parametric memory mechanisms such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide and ground knowledge. Recently, LLMs have begun to perform retrieval autonomously within a reasoning loop, an approach referred to as Agentic RAG. This shift introduces new querying behaviours, with implications for the design of retrieval systems that have yet to be evaluated. In this work, we introduce a large-scale dataset (ASQ) capturing how Agentic RAG systems perform multi-step search and reasoning. ASQ contains about 1M agentic search traces collected from open-source Agentic RAG systems over 3 corpora, 5 agent variants, and 6 retrieval settings. Our analysis of ASQ shows that, within this controlled benchmark setting, a single search query can trigger long chains of retrieval calls (up to 186) and follow query reformulation dynamics different from those observed in historical human-search data. Our results also reveal substantial behavioural variation across agent and retrieval configurations: changes in re-ranking and retrieval depth do not consistently affect search workloads in terms of search-call volume and trace length across agents. To our knowledge, publicly available production logs do not expose the agent, dataset, and retrieval configuration associated with each trace. ASQ provides a reusable resource for further analysing agent search behaviour and supporting future information retrieval studies on agentic workloads under controlled settings.

title: Cross-national validation of the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale for Youth (DASS-Y) in Lebanese and Chinese adolescents
abstract: Background The Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale for Youth (DASS-Y) has been validated in several countries, but its measurement equivalence between Middle Eastern and East Asian adolescents remains untested, and prior validations primarily relied on single analytic approaches without examining complex factor structures or brief screening forms. This study evaluated the DASS-Y in Lebanese adolescents enduring sociopolitical strain and Chinese adolescents under comparatively stable conditions. Methods The sample comprised 758 Lebanese (M age = 15.95, SD = 1.78; 63.2% female) and 1,062 Chinese adolescents (M age = 16.83, SD = 0.59; 47.5% female). Psychometric properties were examined using confirmatory factor analysis, exploratory structural equation modeling (ESEM), and bifactor variants of both. Differential item functioning was assessed using Rasch analysis. Reliability was indexed by composite reliability (CR), average variance extracted (AVE), and person separation reliability. Results Lebanese adolescents showed a largely unidimensional pattern, whereas an ESEM solution better represented the Chinese data. Reliability was strong in both samples (subscale CR = 0.91 to 0.95, AVE = 0.58 to 0.71, person separation reliability = 0.79 to 0.85; total CR = 0.97 in both samples; total AVE = 0.63 for the Lebanese and 0.61 for the Chinese sample). Several items, mainly in the stress subscale, functioned non-equivalently across samples. The 12-item short form performed comparably (subscale CR = 0.88 to 0.92, AVE = 0.65 to 0.73; total CR = 0.96 and 0.94; total AVE = 0.64 and 0.57, respectively). Conclusions Lebanese adolescents’ responses reflected a unitary distress construct, whereas Chinese adolescents’ responses showed greater differentiation among depression, anxiety, and stress, though a general distress factor remained dominant in both samples. Reliability was high throughout, so this divergence is structural rather than a matter of measurement precision. The 12-item form offers a practical screening option pending further cross-national confirmation.

title: Occupational health risks from climate-related and infectious-disease stressors: A scoping review of worker safety and resilience
abstract: Objective This scoping review examines how climate-related stressors and infectious-disease conditions, including pandemic-related workplace disruptions, interact to influence worker health, vulnerability, and occupational resilience. The review focuses on shared exposure pathways, vulnerable worker populations, methodological patterns, policy gaps, and strategies for strengthening worker safety under compound hazards. Rather than treating pandemics as isolated events, the review uses pandemic conditions as a lens to understand broader, recurring occupational risks and to inform strategies for building safer and more resilient workplaces under compound hazards. Methods Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for English-language peer-reviewed and formally structured evidence sources published primarily between January 2020 and April 2025, with one pre-2020 policy study retained for foundational context. Out of 612 records initially identified, 10 studies or sources met the inclusion criteria across healthcare, agriculture, construction, emergency response, and other high-exposure sectors after systematic screening and eligibility assessment. Data were charted and synthesized by occupational sector, geographic region, exposure type, worker vulnerability, and methodological approach. Results The evidence indicates that climate-related and infectious-disease stressors frequently converge, amplifying physical, environmental, and psychosocial pressures on workers. Disproportionate risks were observed among migrant workers, informal laborers, low-income populations, older adults, women, and seasonal or cross-border agricultural workers, particularly where access to healthcare, legal protections, or adaptive infrastructure was limited. Most studies relied on descriptive, qualitative, cross-sectional, conceptual, or review-based designs, with limited use of predictive modeling, geospatial analysis, longitudinal evidence, or integrated datasets. Policy responses were often fragmented, with climate adaptation and infection-control measures addressed separately despite overlapping benefits. Conclusions Climate-related and infectious-disease stressors interact to reinforce occupational health inequities and expose persistent gaps in worker protection. The findings highlight the need for integrated, multi-hazard occupational health strategies that align climate adaptation, infection prevention, and psychosocial support. Embedding data-driven early-warning systems, equitable protections for vulnerable workers, and cross-sector coordination into occupational policies may help strengthen workforce resilience during routine operations as well as future climate extremes and public health crises. However, the findings should be interpreted with caution because of the limited number of available studies combining climate-related and infectious-disease occupational risks, heterogeneous study designs, and the emerging nature of the evidence base. Furthermore, since this scoping review maps evidence rather than formally grading evidence strength or testing causal relationships, recommendations should be interpreted as evidence-informed directions for future occupational-health planning and research.

title: Dynamic thermal imaging for crop water stress detection across phenological stages: Enhancing irrigation scheduling precision
abstract: Thermal remote sensing and derived indices such as the crop water stress index (CWSI) can assess crop water status and support precision irrigation. However, most operational and artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches rely on fixed, season-long thresholds to interpret canopy–air temperature differences and often overlook the influence of crop phenology. This review synthesises evidence from grapevine, wheat, maize, potato and several other crops on how developmental stage affects the non-water-stressed baseline (NWSB), CWSI thresholds and irrigation-scheduling algorithms. It covers CWSI theory and estimation practices; crop-specific, phenology-dependent behaviour of baselines and thresholds; a comparison of threshold-based, machine learning, Internet of Things (IoT), digital twin and Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)-56 approaches with respect to crop phenology; and a conceptual framework for phenology-aware scheduling. Across the reviewed crops, baseline behaviour generally varied systematically across the growing season, the relationship between CWSI and crop water status generally strengthened after canopy closure and CWSI measured during reproductive stages was generally most closely related to yield. A quantitative audit of 56 AI-, thermal-imaging-, or CWSI-based studies found that 78.6 % either did not explicitly incorporate crop phenology or relied on day of year as a temporal proxy, whereas only 5.4 % explicitly encoded phenological stage. The proposed framework considers phenology explicitly in baseline estimation, threshold setting and data fusion or machine learning for irrigation scheduling; the framework will require multi-year, multi-site field validation before operational use. Future research should prioritise standardised phenology definitions and long-term, multi-location studies to establish and validate stage-specific parameters.

title: Machine Learning-Based Assessment of Stress-Dependent Fracture Conductivity for Improved Gas Recovery in the Marcellus Shale
abstract: Fracture conductivity is not a static completion property. As reservoir pressure declines and effective closure stress increases, the proppant pack may rearrange, deform, crush, or embed into the fracture surfaces, progressively reducing the hydraulic fracture’s flow capacity. The phenomenon is particularly important in the Marcellus Shale, where stress-dependent conductivity affects both fracture performance and the reliability of long-term gas-recovery forecasts. This study develops a machine-learning surrogate model to predict fracture conductivity as a function of closure stress, proppant type, proppant concentration, and mesh size. A structured dataset containing 3,000 cases was generated with Predict-K. The two categorical inputs were one-hot encoded, resulting in 13 numerical inputs to the artificial neural network (ANN) while preserving the four-variable engineering representation of the problem. Feedforward networks trained with Levenberg-Marquardt and Bayesian Regularization algorithms were initially compared at a common 75-neuron architecture. Bayesian Regularization substantially improved predictive performance, reducing the testing root mean square error (RMSE) from 54.66 to 19.22 md-ft. Subsequent architecture optimization identified a 50-neuron network as the most robust configuration. The final model reproduced the Predict-K conductivity surface with a testing RMSE of 13.40 md-ft and near-perfect correlation between predicted and target values. Evaluation on an independent subset containing only 100M white-sand yielded RMSE of 7.33 md-ft. Given the exceptionally high predictive accuracy, the modeling was subjected to a series of validation and diagnostic tests, including partition-overlap checks, duplicate screening, target-leakage analysis, stress-level holdout experiments, target shuffling, conventional-regression benchmarking, and fully random data partitions. The results indicated that ANN has successfully learned the underlying nonlinear conductivity relationships embedded in Predict K dataset. The developed ANN should therefore be regarded as a computationally efficient surrogate for the Predict-K conductivity surface within the range of conditions represented in the training data. The model can rapidly generate stress-dependent conductivity relationships for integration into reservoir simulation workflows; however, independent laboratory measurements and field-scale validation remain necessary before operational deployment. The ANN was validated as a surrogate of the Predict-K response surface rather than as an independent predictor of physical conductivity behavior.

title: Resolving Injection Profile Uncertainty in Complex Wells Using Integrated Acoustic, Thermal, and Electromagnetic Diagnostics
abstract: Accurate injection profiling in deviated and horizontal wells remains challenging when the well system contains multiple possible flow paths, including fractures, behind-casing channels, completion leaks, and compromised zonal-isolation elements. Conventional production logging and temperature surveys primarily describe conditions inside the wellbore and can therefore give an incomplete picture when injected fluid leaves the borehole at one location but is redistributed behind pipe before entering the reservoir. The resulting uncertainty can obscure the true receiving intervals, complicate conformance decisions, and delay identification of integrity-related injection. This paper presents an integrated diagnostic workflow combining passive spectral acoustics with radial source localization, high-precision temperature measurements interpreted by thermo-hydrodynamic forward modeling, and electromagnetic wall-thickness assessment. The acoustic measurement identifies active flow and provides sensitivity to its radial position outside the casing. Temperature data acquired during injection, shut-in, and transient conditions constrain the direction and magnitude of fluid movement through coupled wellbore-reservoir heat and mass transfer. Electromagnetic measurements independently evaluate tubular condition and completion elements, allowing flow anomalies to be compared with localized metal loss and mechanical features. Conventional production logging and existing cement-evaluation data are incorporated where available as additional constraints rather than treated as stand-alone evidence of reservoir allocation. Three field cases demonstrate the method. Case 1 shows a deviated injector in which conventional wellbore flow measurements placed injection within the intended perforated interval, while acoustic, thermal, and modeling evidence showed substantial fracture-controlled reservoir injection extending above the target and channeling behind the liner. Acoustic responses correlated with several completion restrictions, and electromagnetic integrity data provided an independent assessment of the tubular condition. Case 2 is a horizontal injector with zonal isolation in which the integrated interpretation identified liner leaks, a leaking packer, localized metal-loss anomalies, shut-in crossflow, and a strongly non-uniform injection profile dominated by an out-of-target fracture. Case 3 compares repeat surveys before and after recompletion: the intervention changed the completion and added a new perforated interval, but a later survey identified a new dominant out-of-zone receiving interval at a shallower position, demonstrating that containment must be verified after intervention rather than inferred from the completion change alone. The cases show that injection uncertainty is reduced when complementary measurements are interpreted as a single physical system. Radial acoustic information distinguishes near-completion activity from farther formation or fracture responses, thermal modeling converts distributed temperature behavior into a rate-consistent reservoir allocation, and electromagnetic inspection tests whether observed flow anomalies coincide with loss of metal integrity or completion elements. The workflow improves differentiation between reservoir-driven and completion-related flow, identifies hidden crossflow and loss of isolation, and provides a technically defensible basis for conformance remediation and repeat surveillance in complex injection wells.

title: ThyroNet A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Early Prediction of Recurrence in Thyroid Cancer Patients
abstract: Thyroid cancer is the most prevalent endocrine malignancy worldwide, and although the majority of patients have a good prognosis, a significant number suffer from disease recurrences. Thus, early detection of patients with high-risk of recurrence is crucial to guide clinical management, individualized treatment, and long-term surveillance. With the increased access to clinical health data, AI and DL have become promising tools for predictive models in medical diagnosis and prognosis. In this work, we introduce ThyroNet, a sophisticated hybrid deep learning model, to predict the recurrence of thyroid cancer with better accuracy by utilizing clinical and pathological features. The proposed ThyroNet model comprises CNN, BiLSTM and DNN layers to model hidden nonlinear correlations and high-level feature interactions among patients' data. The model is trained on a collected thyroid cancer dataset which consists of 383 patient records with 13 clinical attributes such as demographic information, tumor staging details, pathological findings, and treatment information. Before modelling, the categorical features were one-hot encoded, the data were scaled to 0-1 range, and the class imbalance was dealt with using Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). Feature patterns of clinical sections were extracted by the CNN layers, while contextual bidirectional dependency of these clinical features were revealed by the BiLSTM layer. Finally, binary classification for recurrence prediction was performed using dense neural layers. Experimental result shows that the proposed model is good prediction. ThyroNet achieved 99.77% of training accuracy and 94.81% of testing accuracy, indicating its powerful learning and generalization capabilities. Results for the classification on the test data were Precision = Recall = F1 = 0.96 for the non-recurrent class and for the recurrent class Precision = Recall = F1 = 0.91, with an overall weighted F1-score of 0.95. These confirm that the hybrid deep learning architecture is more powerful to capture representative features for predicting recurrence risk in patients with thyroid cancer. With our approach, the developed model may serve as a smart clinical decision support tool to assist early recurrence risk prediction and personalized treatment planning for medical expert. By leveraging hybrid deep learning ThyroNet demonstrates that machine learning has the potential to transform predictive analytics and change the way patients with thyroid cancer are treated.

title: A Composite Field-Evaluation Framework for Digital Agriculture Maps
abstract: Purpose : Evaluating maps from digital agriculture systems requires limiting biased observations while providing enough spatial guidance to inspect mapped features accurately. This study developed a composite framework combining output-blinded and system-output-guided scouting as complementary evidence streams. Methods : The framework combines output-blinded paired-point scouting with masked agronomic review and high-precision, system-output-guided scouting with the output visible. The blinded stream tests whether observations support feature presence and selected attributes at mapped locations while limiting expectation bias; the guided stream assesses the same correspondence with greater spatial precision. Agronomic reviewers use prespecified rules to convert subjective scouting observations into standardized determinations of feature presence and attribute agreement. The framework was demonstrated using 2025 Spatiotemporal Anomaly Detection System (STADS) crop-anomaly maps from New York. Results : The composite evaluation comprised separate output-blinded and system-output-guided evidence sets. Of 99 output-blinded point pairs scouted, 55 were retained after excluding observations that could not be confidently matched to original locations; 53 had at least two valid reviewer classifications for primary analysis, and 18 (34.0%) supported both anomaly presence and the predicted direction. Of 85 system-output-guided real-time kinematic global navigation satellite system (RTK-GNSS) pairs originally planned, 57 were retained after exclusions and 53 were analyzable; 37 (69.8%) supported both feature presence and the evaluated attribute. Framework implementation identified practical requirements for record linkage, masking, sampling, positioning, and observation timing. Conclusion : Combining complementary output-blinded and system-output-guided evidence provides a transferable and transparent approach for evaluating mapped agricultural outputs when complete field-scale ground truth is impractical.

title: Motivational factors influencing the adoption of frugal innovation among agrifood SMEs in Surakarta, Indonesia
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractAgrifood SMEs play a vital role in producing high-value-added processed products, enhancing the potential of local agricultural commodities, and supporting food availability and diversity. However, these SMEs face various challenges, including limited resources and capital, the need to adapt to rapid innovation and shifting consumer preferences, and volatile purchasing power amid economic fluctuations. This study aims to analyze the motivational factors influencing the adoption of frugal innovation among agrifood SMEs in Surakarta City, Indonesia. A quantitative method was employed, involving a sample of 150 agrifood SMEs in Surakarta. Data were collected through surveys and direct interviews between April and June 2025. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) with partial least squares (PLS) in SmartPLS 4. The majority of respondents’ businesses have been operating for less than 10 years and generate monthly revenue ranging from IDR 5,000,000 to IDR 40,000,000. The findings reveal that compatibility (ꞵ = 0.191, p < 0.05), low-cost manufacturing (ꞵ = 0.220, p < 0.05), digital platforms (ꞵ = 0.258, p < 0.05), sustainable leadership (ꞵ = 0.160, p < 0.05), technology turbulence (ꞵ = 0.188, p < 0.05), and external sources of knowledge (ꞵ = 0.172, p < 0.05) significantly encourage the adoption of frugal innovation. Moreover, external knowledge sources partially mediate the influence of sustainable leadership on the adoption of frugal innovation.AcknowledgmentThe authors are grateful to Universitas Sebelas Maret, Surakarta, Central Java, Indonesia, for funding this study with Contract No: 371/UN27.22/PT.01.03/2025.
