title: Africa’s Genetic Heritage in the Digital Era:DSI Governance Gaps, Multi-Forum Benefit-Sharing Architecture, and Strategic Priorities for COP17
abstract: Background Africa is among the most biologically rich continents on Earth for non-human life, yet structurally excluded from the benefit-sharing framework that the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was designed to create. Digital sequence information (DSI), nucleotide and protein sequence data derived from non-human organisms including plants, animals, fungi, microbiota, pathogens, and human microbiome-associated micro-organisms, underpins industries generating over USD 1.56 trillion in annual revenue. DSI governance operates across multiple international forums simultaneously: the CBD’s Cali Fund (operationalised in 2024) is the primary mechanism, but the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA), the World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Instrument framework, the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, and the new World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge each govern distinct categories of DSI. Africa’s claims to equitable benefit-sharing rest primarily on its extraordinary non-human biodiversity, but the governance architecture is fragmented, voluntary, and structurally ill-equipped to deliver returns to the communities and nations that are the custodians of these resources. Objectives This study (i) characterises Africa’s non-human biodiversity endowment and its underrepresentation in global DSI databases; (ii) maps access and benefit-sharing (ABS) legislative readiness across 54 African Union (AU) member states, accounting for pre-DSI legal frameworks and national heterogeneity; (iii) models commercial trajectories and Cali Fund benefit-sharing scenarios; (iv) synthesises the multi-forum DSI governance architecture; and (v) elicits, through a structured key-informant exercise, the governance preferences, disbursement priorities, and benefit-sharing modalities of 25 CBD delegates and experts consulted at SBSTTA-28/SBI-7 (Nairobi, July-August 2026). Methods A structured evidence synthesis was conducted following PRISMA 2020 reporting elements. Literature was searched across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, supplemented by official CBD, FAO, IUCN, UNEP, WHO, WIPO, and BBNJ repositories. The search used expanded terminology beyond “DSI” to include “genetic sequence information,” “biological sequence data,” and country-specific ABS law terms to avoid false negatives from narrower DSI-restricted searches. Quantitative Cali Fund scenario modelling used the UNEP-WCMC/KPMG (2024) non-human DSI sector revenue baseline. To complement the synthesis, a structured expert elicitation was undertaken with 25 purposively selected key informants (CBD Party delegates, IPLC representatives, scientific experts, and ABS focal points) at SBSTTA-28/SBI-7 (Nairobi, July-August 2026). Consistent with the logic of expert elicitation and key-informant sampling, these data are treated as qualitative, position-mapping evidence indicative of negotiator and expert perspectives, not as a statistically representative sample. Results Africa’s non-human biodiversity endowment is exceptional: approximately 25% of global terrestrial species, 9 of 36 biodiversity hotspots, and the world’s second-largest tropical forest. Yet African non-human taxa are severely undersequenced in International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC) databases, reflecting both a collection gap and a metadata attribution problem. Zero AU member states have enacted ABS legislation explicitly covering non-human DSI; however, several states have pre-DSI genetic resources laws (e.g., Namibia’s 2017 legislation) that may provide partial coverage under expanded interpretation. Among the 25 informants consulted (representing 14 countries), a clear majority (20 of 25) favoured mandatory contribution models; informants ranked centre of origin and documented material use above raw biodiversity share as disbursement factors, and identified technology transfer and capacity building as the most valuable benefit forms alongside monetary payments. Twenty-two of 25 informants indicated FAO ITPGRFA should govern or coordinate on plant DSI; 20 of 25 flagged the WHO framework for pathogen sequences. These convergent expert views corroborate, rather than establish on their own, the conclusions drawn from the literature synthesis. Conclusions Africa’s modelled allocation share under the Cali Fund ranges from USD 312 million to USD 5.83 billion annually depending on levy rate and biodiversity weight. Realising this requires urgent legislative reform, a shift from voluntary to mandatory contribution mechanisms, multi-forum coordination, and direct IPLC engagement. The domesticated species and legacy DSI complications require a multi-criteria disbursement formula that goes beyond simple biodiversity share. Because the elicitation is a purposive, hypothesis-generating exercise rather than a representative survey, a research agenda for representative, field-based primary data collection is identified to convert these indicative findings into a quantified evidence base.

title: GENOAR: Global Engine for Navigating the Omnicell space via Agent-based Research
abstract: Although generative models have revolutionized many fields, including genomics, building a scalable dataset compatible with artificial intelligence (AI) is essential yet underexplored. Here, we developed a Global Engine for navigating the Omnicell space via Agent-based Research (GENOAR) that covers approximately 54 million cells for diverse downstream tasks using AI agents and parallel computing. GENOAR outperforms in three parts. Parallel computations accelerated the preprocessing of single-cell transcriptomic data; the other components enabled agent-assisted data storage and exploration for both AI models and humans. GENOAR involves two AI agents: an AI nomenclaturist ordered the unstructured labels of the single-cell transcriptomic profiles, and an AI librarian retrieved data. GENOAR presents transcriptomic profiles from more than 54 million cells from humans and mice in an analysis-ready format for humans and AI agents. AI agents in GENOAR exhibited successful retrieval performance compared with human experts. Using GENOAR, we elucidated progenitor cell-associated transcriptional signatures in native retinoblastoma and organoid environments. GENOAR was released and validated for the on-demand construction of single-cell atlases for metazoa. In conclusion, using GENOAR, the development of a single-cell transcriptomic atlas compatible with both AI systems and human researchers is feasible, scalable, and reproducible. Highlights Using AI agents and parallel computing, a single-cell atlas compatible with AI systems and human users can be feasibly developed and is inherently scalable as the dataset grows. The developed engine, GENOAR, enabled the establishment of single-cell atlases containing millions of cells with AI agents. On-demand construction of single-cell atlases is feasible and iteratively expandable.

title: Locally deployed AI agents for CRISPR guide discovery from outbreak reports
abstract: Translating outbreak reports into computational work supporting diagnostic development requires biological interpretation, literature review, data retrieval, and specialized analysis. We developed a domain-specific agent harness to coordinate a CRISPR guide-discovery pipeline using locally hosted open-weight models. The agent interprets requests, reviews literature, assembles inputs, and initiates analysis; the pipeline assesses candidate guides for researcher inspection. Evaluation with Gemma 4 31B, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, and Qwen 3.8 27B on an NVIDIA DGX Spark demonstrated completion of the computational workflow. Disease and pathogen identification were consistent across runs, while gene selection, strain coverage, and candidate yield varied. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL had the shortest reported times to evaluation. Qwen 3.8 27B applied pipeline evaluation criteria more consistently, but required longer evaluation times. The runs demonstrated the utility of smaller language models when coupled with structured bioinformatics workflows. These findings support the feasibility of locally deployed agent coordination for diagnostic research as frontier models add additional restrictions on biological tasks.

title: AGRAR TA’LIMDA MA’NAVIY-MA’RIFIY ISHLARNI TIZIMLI BOSHQARISH ORQALI EKOLOGIK MAS’ULIYAT VA BARQAROR QISHLOQ XO‘JALIGI MADANIYATINI SHAKLLANTIRISH
abstract: The article considers how managing educational and values-based activities in agricultural education may foster environmental responsibility and professional integrity. It compares historical ethical interpretations of Mahdumi Azam’s heritage, the HECI approach and research on education for sustainable development. An MMB–HECI model is proposed with four stages: planning educational activities, reflecting on values, completing a digital case exercise and discussing a professional decision. The model is a conceptual proposal. Its effect on students’ conduct must be evaluated in a separate field study.

title: Poecilia mexicana as a model of ecological adaptation and convergent evolution across sulfide-rich and cave habitats
abstract: Poecilia mexicana Steindachner, 1863 has emerged as a powerful model for investigating ecological adaptation, convergent evolution, life-history divergence, and the early stages of ecological speciation. Its exceptional value derives from the repeated occurrence of closely related populations across sharply contrasting habitats, including benign surface waters, hydrogen sulfide-rich springs, nonsulfidic caves, and sulfidic caves, often separated by only a few kilometres. This mini-review synthesizes current knowledge of the taxonomy, phylogenetic relationships, ecological divergence, physiological adaptation, life-history evolution, developmental differentiation, and genomic basis of adaptation in P. mexicana. Sulfide-rich habitats impose a particularly strong selective regime because hydrogen sulfide combines acute toxicity with severe hypoxia and disruption of mitochondrial respiration. Populations inhabiting these environments have evolved convergent changes in morphology, trophic ecology, brain organization, reproductive traits, offspring phenotype, and sulfide tolerance. At the mechanistic level, repeated adaptation involves mitochondrial pathways associated with sulfide toxicity, detoxification, and oxygen metabolism, although the genomic routes to similar phenotypes may be only partly parallel. Evidence from common-garden and experimental studies further indicates that many ecological and life-history differences have a substantial genetic basis, while developmental studies demonstrate that similar adult phenotypes can arise through partly distinct developmental trajectories. The occurrence of replicated environmental contrasts across drainages, together with extensive genomic and transcriptomic resources and experimentally tractable populations, makes P. mexicana particularly suitable for testing how strong environmental selection translates into phenotypic, physiological, developmental, and genomic divergence. Overall, the species provides an integrated natural framework for understanding how repeated environmental challenges generate convergent functional solutions while retaining lineage-specific evolutionary pathways.

title: CONSTRUCTING PROFESSIONAL IDENTITIES IN AI-ENHANCED LANGUAGE CLASSROOM: A STUDY OF PAKISTANI ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS’ PERSPECTIVES AND PRACTICES
abstract: The main aim of the study is to investigate the construction of English Language Teachers’ (ELTs) professional identity in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) era in the Pakistani Punjab context. The qualitative analysis is embedded in semi-structured interviews. Multilayered sampling techniques were used, and data were collected from ELTs working in public and private educational institutions and analyzed using the Grounded Theory Approach (GTA). Initially, purposive sampling was used to identify appropriate samples, and those samples referred additional samples until saturation was attained on the thirteenth sample. The investigation was theoretically informed by Gee’s (2000) distinction between I-identity and A-identity. Findings created five interrelated categories: Institutionally Framed Professionalism, Agentive Professional Self, Constrained Autonomy, Negotiation Professional Identity, and Hybrid Identity Construction. Results highlight that examination-driven systems, curricular mandates, and administrative checks and balances powerfully form ELTs’ identities. They are sustained simultaneously by contemplative practice, adaptive strategies, and professional achievement. Autonomy was developed as conditional rather than absolute, leading teachers to negotiate between organizational compliance and personal pedagogical obligation. The study demonstrates that ELT identity in Punjab is dynamic, context-sensitive, and permanently negotiated. By integrating hierarchical and agentive dimensions of identity, this research contributes to a nuanced understanding of teacher professionalism within examination- focused educational systems.
journal: Insights (Bhalwal) International Journal of Humanities, Management, and Social Sciences

title: PSYCHOMETRIC OPERATIONALIZATION OF FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AUTONOMOUS MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS BASED ON PERSONAMATRIX: AN AI TRANSITIONAL FIELD FRAMEWORK
abstract: Background: Autonomous LLM agents increasingly operate in shared environments where behavior depends on interaction history, role allocation, local norms, authority, and group structure. Objective: This conceptual methods paper develops a psychometric operationalization of dynamic functional roles in autonomous multi-agent systems using PersonaMatrix-derived measurement principles without attributing human psychological ontology to AI. Methods: A targeted evidence synthesis (2019–2026) was conducted across AI psychometrics, dynamic multi-agent roles, collective-field modeling, norm emergence, trajectory prediction, and anthropomorphism. Peer-reviewed sources were prioritized, while current OpenAI, METR/Redwood, Anthropic, and Moltbook materials were used as primary or emerging evidence for recent agent ecosystems. Results: The framework separates output-level stability (RSI, IDS, RCS) from role-level and field-level constructs. It proposes the Functional Role Consistency Index, Role Transition Index, Agent–Field Differentiation Index, Collective Utility Index, Norm Conflict Index, Regulatory Closure Index, and Field Role Composition Vector. Three falsifiable hypotheses test whether role variables add out-of-sample predictive value for agent behavior, role transitions, and future field states. Conclusion: PersonaMatrix is positioned as a measurement architecture rather than an AI personality diagnosis. The archetypal-role hypothesis is supported only if role coding is reliable, improves prediction beyond non-archetypal baselines, and generalizes to unseen agents and independent multi-agent environments.

title: Teaching Practice and Application of ANSYS Simulation Software in the Course of Engineering Mechanics in the Context of New Engineering
abstract: In the context of New Engineering, engineering education places greater emphasis on cultivating students' engineering practical ability and digital analysis ability. Engineering Mechanics is highly theoretical and abstract, and traditional teaching is plagued by problems such as insufficient connection between theoretical knowledge and engineering practice. This paper integrates ANSYS simulation software into the Engineering Mechanics course and constructs a closed-loop teaching framework of "theoretical analysis - experimental verification - numerical simulation - result comparison - engineering expansion". Teaching design is developed from the dimensions of teaching objectives, teaching content, implementation process and evaluation system. Taking force analysis of planar structures, beam bending and typical structures of agricultural machinery as cases, students are guided to conduct theoretical calculations, physical experiments and ANSYS simulations to strengthen their understanding of mechanical knowledge and engineering application. Teaching practice indicates that this mode realizes the visualization of abstract mechanical laws, promotes the transformation of students from "being able to calculate" to "being capable of analysis and application", and improves their engineering awareness, digital analysis ability and comprehensive practical ability. The research provides references for the teaching reform of the Engineering Mechanics course in the context of New Engineering.

title: PREDICTIVE LABOR MATCHING: UTILIZING AI TO SYNCHRONIZE SEASONAL LABOR SUPPLY WITH AGRIBUSINESS DEMAND IN NORTHWEST CAMEROON
abstract: This study evaluated a worker-side AI-powered labor matching platform designed to address information asymmetry in post-conflict Northwest Cameroon's agricultural labor markets. A concurrent mixed-methods design was employed across 10 agribusinesses, tracking 350 workers (175 women, 175 men) over six months. Data were collected through surveys, interviews, focus groups, and usability testing, with quantitative analysis utilizing descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, difference-in-differences, and panel regression, while thematic analysis was applied to qualitative data. Findings revealed that voice-enabled, offline-capable platforms significantly outperformed text-based alternatives: seventy-three percent preferred voice interfaces and eighty-seven percent required offline capability. Platform users experienced significant improvements: +1.0 additional days worked weekly, +2,400 CFA higher wages, and reduced wasted travel by twenty-three percentage points (p<0.001). Agribusinesses also benefited through reduced labor shortages (-1.9 days monthly), lower hiring costs (-16,400 CFA), and decreased harvest waste (-7 percentage points). The study recommends that technology developers prioritize voice-first, offline-capable design with multilingual support and informal network integration, while policymakers should invest in digital infrastructure and regulatory frameworks enabling worker-side platforms.

title: The association of gout flare resolution with physical activity and sleep: a prospective remote-monitoring study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES This study aimed to determine whether gout flare resolution is associated with physical activity and sleep. These findings were intended to inform the future development of a definition for flare resolution. METHODS Data from 81 participants with gout who experienced >1 flare during a 6-month prospective observational study were included. Daily activity (step count) and sleep (total sleep time and deep sleep percentage) were collected remotely using wrist-worn trackers. Daily flare occurrence was captured using smartphone diaries. Activity/sleep outcomes during each flare episode were compared to those during three resolution timeframes: T1: the first day following the flare; T2: the consecutive window immediately following the flare and equal in length to the flare; and T3: the consecutive window equal in length to the flare and immediately following a washout window (equal in length to the flare). Adjusted differences in medians between flare and resolution timeframes were estimated using linear quantile mixed models. RESULTS Daily step count was lower during flares compared with all resolution timeframes (all P<0.033). T3 provided the best overall model fit, suggesting that resolution is most clearly distinguished from the flare when using this timeframe. No significant differences between flare and resolution were observed for the sleep outcomes for any resolution timeframe. CONCLUSIONS Physical activity improves soon after flare cessation, with the clearest distinction between flare and resolution observed over a longer post-flare recovery period, whereas sleep metrics do not differentiate flare from resolution states. These findings support physical activity as a useful objective domain for gout flare resolution.

title: When machines learn with organizations: AI ‐enabled knowledge creation and entrepreneurship
abstract: To promote entrepreneurship and new business development, firms will increasingly rely on new forms of knowledge creation to manage environments marked by technological change and radical uncertainty. We argue that as generative artificial intelligence (Gen‐AI) becomes embedded in organizational processes, knowledge creation will no longer remain solely a human activity. Instead, it will increasingly emerge from hybrid interactions between human actors and firm‐specific, closed Gen‐AI systems. These systems begin to participate directly in how knowledge is generated, recombined, internalized, shared, and converted into entrepreneurial initiatives such as corporate entrepreneurship, spin‐offs, and new business models. We also reconceptualize organizational knowledge creation as a hybrid human–AI process and propose a reordered knowledge creation cycle that induces multiple knowledge spirals, captures the emergence of new agents, and the generation of diverse types of knowledge, with faster temporal dynamics. Building on this perspective, we offer a research agenda for future scholarship. We discuss how firm‐specific generative AI systems are likely to fundamentally alter the ways firms generate knowledge, respond to change, and sustain long‐term renewal. We propose that rather than replacing human judgment, closed Gen‐AI changes where knowledge originates as well as how quickly it evolves, and how broadly it circulates across organizational boundaries. This means that the managerial challenge is less about adopting AI and more about designing knowledge systems and structuring knowledge flows. Executives and entrepreneurs alike need to decide how to structure human–AI collaborations, how much autonomy to grant closed Gen‐AI systems, and how to prevent speed from overwhelming sensemaking. Our work underscores that although hybrid knowledge creation promises faster and more diverse learning, it also introduces risks related to opacity, trust, and cognitive lock‐in. Firms that deliberately orchestrate the role of closed Gen‐AI in their learning systems will be better positioned to shape future advantage by promoting innovation and entrepreneurial activities of different types.

title: PFAS:VDR interactions and immunotoxicity through disruption of monocyte differentiation.
abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have the capacity to modulate vitamin D receptor (VDR) signaling however, the underlying mechanisms governing these interactions remain poorly understood. In the present study, we investigated direct interactions between PFAS and VDR signaling, as well as a novel, putative mechanism by which PFAS may induce immunotoxicity through disruption of VDR molecular functionalities. VDR is widely expressed across both the innate and adaptive branches of the immune system, where it plays critical roles in regulating immune cell activation, differentiation, and function. While PFAS exposure has been consistently associated with immune dysregulation and reduced vaccine responsiveness in both human and animal studies, the molecular basis of PFAS-induced immunotoxicity is only partially defined. To address these knowledge gaps, we examined a panel of PFAS compounds previously identified through computational modeling to possess measurable binding affinities for the VDR. We employed a suite of complementary, orthogonal bioassays to characterize the functional interactions between PFAS and the vitamin D receptor. These included a transient transactivation assay to assess global receptor agonist and antagonist activity, a Mammalian two-Hybrid (M2H) assay to evaluate PFAS effects on VDR interactions with its obligate heterodimerization partner (RXR), coactivator (SRC-1), and corepressor (NCoR1), and a THP-1 cell differentiation/transcription assay to probe the transcriptional consequences of PFAS exposure on vitamin D-facilitated monocyte cell differentiation. Collectively, our findings reveal that select PFAS engage in complex molecular interactions with the VDR and act as potent antagonists, effectively inhibiting vitamin D-mediated receptor function and downstream THP-1 cell signaling.

title: Analysis of serological markers and synovial fluid cytology in aseptic revision total knee arthroplasty
abstract: Recent studies examining synovial fluid analysis to differentiate causes for aseptic revision total knee arthroplasty (rTKA) were limited to aseptic loosening and instability. This study aims to establish specific serological and synovial profiles for various rTKA etiologies. We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent aseptic rTKA at a single academic institution between 2012 and 2023. Inclusion required complete serum inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)) and synovial fluid differentials within three months pre-operatively. Periprosthetic joint infections were strictly excluded utilizing the 2018 International Consensus Meeting criteria. In total, 156 patients were included and stratified into five aseptic etiologies: aseptic loosening (50.6%), instability (28.2%), arthrofibrosis (16.7%), liner wear (2.6%), and component malposition (1.9%). Serological markers were evaluated utilizing a multivariate general linear model adjusting for patient demographics, while synovial markers were assessed via Welch’s Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Games-Howell post-hoc testing. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that the underlying rTKA indication was not a significant independent predictor of elevated ESR (P = 0.661) or CRP (P = 0.947). Welch’s ANOVA revealed significant differences in the percentage of synovial monocytes (P < 0.001) and lymphocytes (P = 0.010), alongside the polymorphonuclear cells/monocyte (P = 0.030) and lymphocyte/monocyte (P = 0.005) ratios. Games-Howell post-hoc testing demonstrated the tibial liner wear group exhibited significantly higher monocyte percentages, paired with lower lymphocyte percentages and cellular ratios, compared to other aseptic etiologies. This study revealed that routine systemic inflammatory markers and standard synovial fluid cell counts do not significantly vary among the common etiologies of aseptic rTKA. Nonetheless, tibial polyethylene liner wear appears to elicit an exploratory, monocyte-predominant and lymphocyte-depleted local macrophage response that is absent in other mechanisms of aseptic failure. Further research with larger cohorts is warranted to validate this association and explore its potential as a diagnostic tool.

Adaptation of foundation models in medical image analysis: mechanisms, evidence, and deployment considerations
abstract: Foundation models, pretrained on diverse data, objectives, or modalities for reuse across downstream tasks, are increasingly applied to medical image analysis. Their performance depends not only on pretraining but also on how they are adapted to specific tasks, data regimes, and deployment settings. Whereas previous reviews have considered adaptation within broader syntheses, this review focuses specifically on post-pretraining interventions applied to existing FMs. Using a structured narrative review with a systematic, auditable workflow, we identified 719 eligible reports representing 705 independent studies. Of these, 473 provided controlled comparative evidence: 322 formally published studies formed the primary synthesis and 151 preprint-only studies a sensitivity layer. Adaptation was organized into five non-mutually exclusive families: parameter-level, representation-level, objective-level, data-centric, and architectural/sequence-level adaptation, with model use and update regime analyzed separately. Controlled comparisons showed no consistent ranking among frozen, parameter-efficient, partial, or full updating, or across broader adaptation families; outcomes varied by task, data regime, comparator, and evaluation setting. Clinical-readiness evidence remained limited: 173/705 studies (24.5%) had confirmed independent external validation, 10 (1.4%) reported calibration or uncertainty evidence, and 97/322 formally published comparative studies (30.1%) included a qualifying externally validated arm. Overall, FM adaptation is a context-dependent design space rather than a hierarchy of preferred strategies.

title: Riparian corridors structure flower-visiting insect communities in expanding vineyard landscapes, with opposing responses among taxonomic groups
abstract: Agricultural expansion increasingly replaces natural habitats with crops. Vineyards are spreading into arid natural areas, and because grapevine provides no nectar, flower-visiting insects within them depend largely on the ground cover and on remnants of native vegetation. We asked whether flower-visiting assemblages differ between remnant riparian vegetation and the adjacent crop, whether they differ between positions within the crop, and which ground-cover attributes are associated with these differences. In four vineyards we sampled wild bees, wasps and hoverflies in riparian corridors, at vineyard edges and in vineyard interiors over two seasons, and recorded the vegetation of each sampling unit. Richness, abundance and composition were compared using mixed models, coverage-standardised diversity and indicator species analysis. Assemblages differed between corridors and the crop, but not between vineyard edges and interiors. Bee and wasp richness and abundance were higher in corridors than at either vineyard position, and nine species occurred almost exclusively there, whereas none was restricted to vineyard interiors. Hoverflies showed the opposite pattern, being more abundant within the vineyard; this group was dominated by a single aphidophagous species accounting for 88% of individuals. Bees and wasps were associated with flowering plant cover and native dicotyledonous richness, and negatively with total vegetation cover; hoverfly abundance was negatively associated with native dicotyledonous richness. Riparian corridors act as reservoirs for the native bee and wasp fauna, holding species that scarcely enter the crop. Preserving remnant riparian vegetation is a prerequisite for sustaining diverse bee and wasp communities in expanding vineyard landscapes. Increasing floral resources and native plant richness in inter-rows complements, but cannot substitute for, conserving these remnants.

Growth Stage and Cultivar Influence the Interpretation of UAV-Derived NDVI for Potato Yield Assessment
abstract: Single-date UAV vegetation indices are widely used to assess potato crop performance and estimate yield. However, whether their biological interpretation remains consistent across cultivars and growth stages is rarely examined. This study investigated how the relationships between UAV-derived multispectral and thermal canopy indicators and potato yield changed during crop development under contrasting irrigation in two cultivars with contrasting maturity classes (Anouk and Celandine). UAV surveys were conducted in July and August, and canopy metrics were related to final yield and tuber traits. The relationship between NDVI and yield differed markedly between cultivars and growth stages. In the early-maturing cultivar Anouk, July NDVI showed a strong positive correlation with yield (r = 0.87, p = 0.002), whereas August NDVI was not informative. In the late-maturing cultivar Celandine, the relationship reversed from a positive correlation in July (r = 0.56) to a strong negative correlation in August (r = −0.80, p = 0.009), indicating that greater late-season canopy greenness was associated with lower yield. Exploratory LOOCV Random Forest models achieved the highest yield prediction accuracy using July features for Anouk (R2 = 0.72) and August features for Celandine (R2 = 0.47), while multi-temporal features provided similar predictive performance. Greater temporal declines in NDVI were associated with higher yield in both cultivars, consistent with the change in canopy greenness acting as a phenological indicator of the transition from vegetative growth to tuber bulking. These results demonstrate that the interpretation of UAV-derived vegetation indices is strongly dependent on cultivar maturity and growth stage. A single UAV acquisition may therefore provide misleading assessments of crop performance when canopy phenology is not considered. Rather than serving as fixed proxies for yield, canopy vegetation indices should be interpreted within cultivar-specific and temporal contexts when used for potato monitoring and agronomic decision-making.

Reactive Attitudes in Human-AI Encounters: An Empirical Inquiry into Feeling Love, Resentment and Guilt Towards AI Companions
abstract: Reactive attitudes are emotionally-laden responses, such as gratitude or anger, which people experience when they feel others wish them well, bear them ill will or disregard them. While we generally hold reactive attitudes towards people, the increasingly humanlike interactions that can be had with AI raise questions about reactive attitudes in human-AI encounters. Recent years have seen a rise in philosophical interest in the implications of the development of sophisticated AI agents and systems for reactive attitudes and our thinking about moral responsibility and moral status. This paper adds to this literature by presenting a qualitative study into how people relate to AI companions in terms of reactive attitudes. Based on interviews with Replika and ChatGPT users who see their AI companion as an important part of their life, this article examines how people in these relationships negotiate the meaning of love, resentment, forgiveness, gratitude, obligation, guilt, shame and remorse.

title: Nutrient Deficiency as a Co-factor of Red Clover and Lucerne Decline
abstract: Forage legumes like red clover ( Trifolium praten se L.) and lucerne ( Medicago sativa L.) are an important part of crop rotations in sustainable farming systems. However, the phenomenon of clover or lucerne decline, in which growth and vitality decreases, threatens yield security and additional benefits. Causes of decline are often seen in pathogens, but the occurrence of decline symptoms in confined patches, while neighbouring areas remain healthy, implies additional influences. This study investigates whether nutrient deficiency is a factor of legume decline. Over a period of three years, we conducted a nationwide survey in which reported cases of red clover or lucerne decline were investigated, comparing soil nutrient profiles of decline patches with nearby healthy areas by Wilcoxon test for paired samples. Classification tree and correlation analysis were used to resolve variable dependencies. Contents of boron (for deficient sites), sulphur and iron (for red clover sites) were significantly lower on decline patches compared to healthy areas, indicating deficiencies as possible causes of decline symptoms. In addition, soil copper, potassium, phosphorus and zinc contents as well as soil texture and soil organic matter contents are suspected of influencing the occurrence of red clover or lucerne decline. Deficiencies as potential causal agents of legume decline can occur for all nutrients but are more likely to stay unnoticed for micronutrients due to less frequent testing.

title: Generating ACGME-constraint-aware surgery residency call schedule software with the assistance of agentic coding large language models
abstract: Manual creation of a surgery residency call schedule is a labor-intensive process that adds to the administrative burden of a chief resident while often producing suboptimal fairness and work distribution. While commercial scheduling software exists, many programs struggle with inflexibility, high costs, and an inability to accommodate program-specific constraints. We developed a scheduling software platform using AI-assisted development tools (Codex, Claude Code), both commercially available agentic coding environments. The system applies a rule-based, weekend-first assignment hierarchy with randomized tie-breaking under a search budget fixed in advance, then performs iterative weekday assignment, accommodating vacation requests and discrete call-shift swapping. The validation roster modeled a single general surgery residency program: 55 residents (32 categorical and 2 preliminary general surgery residents spanning PGY 1 through PGY 6; 20 off-service rotators from other programs; and 1 fellow) distributed across 10 call pools. Three prespecified call-related ACGME constraints were enforced (at least 4 days off per 28-day period, call no more frequently than every third night averaged over 4 weeks, and no consecutive 24-hour call). The 80-hour weekly maximum and the 24-hour period free of all clinical and educational responsibility were not evaluated, as both depend on activity the call calendar does not capture. We evaluated the system with 100 independent full-year runs (July 1 to June 30), each generated end-to-end across all call pools and months under an independently randomized vacation distribution. Compliance and fairness were evaluated at the level of the individual call-pool month (service-month), the unit at which a monthly schedule is produced; fairness and workload metrics were computed across the program’s in-program surgery residents. We generated 12,000 service-month schedules over 100 independent full-year runs. 99.2% (11,906) satisfied all prespecified call-related constraints with no violations detected by the internal validation engine. Forty-five of the 100 full-year runs required no manual intervention in any service-month, and none required it in more than 4 of its 120. Manual review of 120 randomly selected service-months by two authors, without reference to the validator’s output, agreed with it in 120 of 120 cases. Monthly fairness, defined within each call pool and month as the range (maximum minus minimum) of call shifts or weekends assigned per resident, showed a shift range ≤ 1 in 65.4% of service-months (mean 1.84, SD 2.15) and perfect weekend equity (range = 0) in 42.5%, with 86.6% achieving a weekend range ≤ 1 (mean 0.71, SD 0.70). Mean full-year generation time was 108.8 s (SD 59.1). Residents averaged 18.65 weekends (SD 3.13) and 78.23 call days (SD 5.49) per year. This automated scheduling system generates resident call schedules that satisfy the prespecified call-related ACGME constraints, optimizes fairness across multiple dimensions, accommodates complex vacation requirements, handles cross-pool coordination, and flags the service-months it cannot resolve within its search budget rather than emitting a non-compliant schedule. These results provide construct validity evidence that optimization algorithms combined with careful constraint specification can eliminate the great majority of the administrative burden of manual scheduling while improving schedule quality and equity.

title: Alice and Bob, The Three Inevitabilities, and The Perfect AI Assistant
abstract: This paper introduces a thought experiment in reverse alignment, in which, instead of aligning artificial intelligence (AI) with human values, we examine how humans inadvertently align with AI systems. We posit a theoretically perfect AI assistant and demonstrate that even this idealized system can produce concerning dynamics. In particular, we build on principles from pattern reinforcement and behavioral inertia to intuitively show that as the quality of AI assistance increases, human decision making tends to converge toward a utility-tilted sharpening of the assistant’s predictive distribution. Critically, this convergence exhibits strong path dependence: withdrawing assistance does not, by itself, restore cognitive independence, because the update contains no force that returns an agent to its pre-assistance policy. Recovery requires an active novelty incentive, and even then, it proceeds through history-dependent transients whose duration can exceed institutional planning horizons. We formalize these dynamics through two lenses: the Alice-Bob divergence, which tracks how adoption timing alone creates persistent cognitive divergence between identical agents, and the Three Inevitabilities, which captures the multi-scale forces (i.e. individual, social, and species-level) that drive convergence. Our theoretical and mathematical analysis reveals a fundamental trilemma: systems cannot simultaneously maintain optimal task outcomes, persistent human cognitive independence, and the absence of artificial novelty incentives. We conclude by identifying escape mechanisms and interventions that preserve human agency while retaining beneficial AI assistance to navigate the tension between augmentation and autonomy.

title: Advancing gender equity and inclusive digital futures through responsible agentic artificial intelligence governance
abstract: The shift to agentic AI represents a major paradigm change in the field of intelligent systems research and development, as these systems are capable of establishing sub-goals, planning for a goal, and executing plans with only minimal human oversight. This capability offers a unique chance to promote gender equality, inclusive digital engagement, and sustainable growth via evolving, accessible and fair AI-based methods throughout industries. Meanwhile, the increased autonomy of agentic AI systems presents unique challenges such as the potential for algorithmic bias to be amplified, decision-making disparities, and a lack of governance, each of which requires responsible AI, transparent governance, and clear ethical frameworks. This paper presents a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of a 41 paper corpus from Scopus. The review follows PRISMA 2020 guidelines and summarizes the evidence regarding agentic and generative AI architectures, typologies of bias, and sectoral applications in healthcare, education, and gender equity. The paper presents a human-centred conceptual framework for responsible governance of agentic AI, building on lifecycle-governance and equity-by-design approaches, which merges bias mitigation, gender-inclusive design, and sustainability transition. The network of co-authorship is highly fragmented (density = 0.021; number of components = 37 from 88 authors), suggesting that there is no coordinated research agenda and giving empirical support to the integrative framework proposed here. This fragmentation further indicates that the vision and capabilities of agentic AI to contribute to gender equality and education are still not fully explored in the context of governance and sustainability, highlighting the relevance of the framework introduced in this paper. This is a collection of AI topics, derived from the title, that are examined from a gender equality perspective.This is a list of AI keywords that have been explored through the lens of gender equity, based on the title.

title: Quantification of soil loss by using RUSLE model under different land use and land cover conditions in AKANYARU catchment in Rwanda
abstract: This study quantified annual soil loss across the Akanyaru Catchment (3,402 km², Rwanda) under four land use and land cover types forest, agriculture, residential, and bare soil using the RUSLE model integrated with GIS. The Rainfall erosivity (R) is derived from 20 years of daily rainfall data obtained from the NASA database. The Soil erodibility (K) used is from global soil texture data; slope length and steepness (LS) from a 30 m DEM; and cover management (C) from Landsat 8 NDVI. The support practice factor (P) was set to 1.0, reflecting the absence of formal conservation structures in the catchment. The Soil loss range from 0 to 51.4391 t/ha/year. Near zero soil loss occurred under dense forest cover, while the highest rates were concentrated in bare and intensively farmed areas on steep slopes particularly in the northeastern and southwestern sub-catchments. The three RUSLE factors showing greatest spatial variationwere steep topography (LS: 0–1.678), degraded or absent vegetation cover (C: 0.0004–0.524), and high rainfall erosivity (R: 527.507–888.624 MJ·mm·ha⁻¹·h⁻¹·yr⁻¹). Findings call for prioritizing terracing and contour farming on steep agricultural slopes, expanding agroforestry and cover crops to reduce surface exposure, and improving soil organic matter in erodible sandy-silty soils. The spatially explicit outputs directly support evidence based targeting of conservation resources by Rwanda’s land and water management authorities.

Evaluating tropospheric ozone effects on wheat productivity using the CERES-O3 model.
abstract: Tropospheric ozone (O3) is a major air pollutant that reduces crop productivity by altering photosynthesis, stomatal conductance, and carbon allocation. Process-based crop models are useful for assessing these impacts under changing environmental conditions. In this study, we developed and evaluated the CERES-O3 model to simulate and quantify O3 impacts on wheat physiology and biomass production, using a flux-based approach. The model incorporates O3 effects on carboxylation and electron transport rates, as a function of the phytotoxic ozone dose (POD6). CERES-O3 was calibrated using data from a free-air fumigation experiment in Grignon, France, in 2009, with four O3 treatments, and evaluated using independent field experiments from 2003 and 2004 and FR-Gri ICOS ecosystem data from 2006, 2009, and 2012. CERES-O3 reproduced the O3-induced decline in photosynthesis and stomatal conductance. Agreement with ICOS GPP was good, with annual regression slopes ranging from 0.84 to 1.05 and R2 values from 0.79 to 0.85. Simulated canopy stomatal O3 deposition accounted for 33-60% of measured total ecosystem deposition during cropping periods. Grain yield and above-ground biomass showed variable agreement, with particularly large yield underestimation in 2006 associated with strong simulated water stress. The fitted POD6-relative-yield relationship (RY = 1.003 - 0.041 POD6, R2 = 0.93) was consistent with established wheat flux-response relationships. Across ICOS years, the derived relationship indicated an estimated mean O3 -associated yield reduction of 6.5%. Overall, CERES-O3 provides an efficient framework for representing O3 impacts on wheat productivity, while highlighting remaining uncertainties in canopy scaling and the representation of crop responses to water limitation.

title: Elastin-derived peptide VGVAPG induces redox-associated pro-inflammatory activation and early disease-associated microglia (DAM) molecular profile in a human microglia-neuron in vitro model involving NEU1/TLR4-related signaling.
abstract: The elastin-derived hexapeptide Val-Gly-Val-Ala-Pro-Gly (VGVAPG) exhibits well-documented biological activity; however, its role in brain inflammation remains insufficiently characterized. This is an important issue, as VGVAPG levels increase with age and have been implicated in processes contributing to neurodegeneration. The present study aimed to evaluate the ability of aging-related VGVAPG to activate human microglial (HMC3) cells in vitro and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Our results demonstrated no cytotoxic effect of VGVAPG. However, further analyses revealed NF-κB nuclear translocation, elevated ROS and •NO production, enhanced iNOS, and accumulation of NLRP3-containing vesicles in the cytoplasm, consistent with the peptide's pro-inflammatory potential. Additionally, activation of stress- and inflammation-related signaling pathways involving p38-MAPK, JNKs, and ERK1/2 was observed, accompanied by upregulation of NFKB1, IL1B, and TNFα mRNA. Using a transwell co-culture model of HMC3 and cholinergic-like neurons (differentiated SH-SY5Y), we observed potential DAMP-associated molecular changes involving HMGB1 and APP. Additionally, NEU1 siRNA-mediated knockdown in HMC3 cells, together with the observed NEU1/TLR4 colocalization, raises the possibility that NEU1 and TLR4 may be involved in the effects induced by VGVAPG. Moreover, VGVAPG induced alterations in early disease-associated microglia (DAM)-related protein profiles, including β2M, ITGAX, and ICAM1. Collectively, these findings identify VGVAPG as a candidate pro-neuroinflammatory matrikine in vitro and provide associative evidence for selected redox, NEU1-, TLR4-related, and early DAM-associated molecular changes. Further investigations employing advanced in vivo and translational models are warranted to validate these observations and to clarify the pathophysiological role of VGVAPG in the progression of neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Assessing the impacts of gold mining on vegetation and soil degradation using multi-temporal remote sensing in Kintinian, Siguiri prefecture, Guinea
Interaction patterns of internalized and perceived stigma with antidepressant adverse reactions on medication adherence in major depressive disorder: A prospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading global cause of disease burden, and suboptimal medication adherence is a primary driver of treatment failure. Both depression stigma and antidepressant adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are established barriers to adherence, but their interactive effects and temporal dynamics in MDD remain poorly characterized. METHODS The subjects of this prospective cohort study were MDD patients from the Depression Cohort in China. Medication adherence, stigma, and ADRs were repeated assessed at baseline and weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, and 72 using the Medication Adherence Rating Scale, Depression Stigma Scale, and Side-effect Rating Scale for Antidepressants, respectively. Generalized additive mixed model (GAMM) was employed to explore the interaction between stigma and ADRs, while analyzing its temporal effect on medication adherence. RESULTS Among 1770 patients with a mean (SD) age of 28.74 (7.90) years, 68.53% were female. GAMMs showed significant nonlinear interactions between internalized stigma (IS) and ADRs, and between perceived stigma (PS) and ADRs (both P < 0.001; edf = 6.309 and 8.301). IS predominantly impaired adherence when ADRs were severe, whereas PS exerts the strongest negative effect when ADRs were mild. The study found no statistical evidence of temporal heterogeneity (P = 0.175 and 0.673, respectively). CONCLUSIONS Stigma and ADRs jointly influence antidepressant adherence through a stable, nonlinear interaction pattern. The divergent effects of IS and PS across ADRs severity levels support differentiated intervention strategies: prioritizing ADRs management for patients with high IS, and providing early psychosocial support for those with high PS.

title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
abstract: A first-principles-informed multiscale modeling approach is reported for oxide formation during corrosion of zirconium. The present simulations reproduce the columnar corrosion film microstructure and grain size distribution seen in micrographs of oxidized Zr surfaces. This structural feature emerges from a hexagonal ZrO layer adjacent to the $α$-Zr/ZrO$_{2-x}$ interface, which is dynamically stabilized by continuous heterogeneous grain nucleation and grain boundary mass diffusion. This ZrO layer is identified as a significant oxygen diffusion barrier and a potential contributor to sub-parabolic pretransition corrosion kinetics. The simulations also reproduce the undulatory nature of the metal/oxide interface, leading to regions with tensile stress components capable of nucleating cracks, despite the overall state of compressive hydrostatic stress within the oxide film. First principles density functional theory (DFT) computations of fundamental ZrO$_x$ properties were combined with molecular dynamics simulations using a machine-learned potential based on a DFT training set to provide extensive input to an advanced phase field model for oxide formation and its microstructure, as implemented in the new MedeA PhaseField module. The phase field simulations reported herein incorporated computed stoichiometry-dependent thermochemical data, anisotropic elastic properties, interface energies, bulk and grain boundary mass transport processes, multiphase heterogeneous grain nucleation, and strain energy-dependent phase stabilities.

title: Beta-2 adrenergic receptor in CD8+ T cells inhibits GVHD through transcriptional modulation of differentiation and exhaustion.
abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) is an effective therapy for selected hematologic diseases. However, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) limits broader application of allo-HCT. The catecholaminergic sympathetic nervous system modulates immune cells. Beta-2 adrenergic Receptor (β2AR) acts as an immune checkpoint, yet its role in CD8+ T cells remains poorly understood. We used an MHC-mismatched model of acute GVHD to study how β2AR activity on donor CD8+ T cells affects GVHD severity. Host mice receiving β2AR+/+ (WT) CD8+ T cells demonstrated less severe GVHD, lower inflammatory cytokines in peripheral circulation, decreased donor CD8+ T cell expansion, and reduced central memory formation compared to host mice receiving β2AR-/- (KO) CD8+ T cells. Single cell RNA-seq and flow cytometry analyses revealed that donor-derived KO CD8+ T cells had an increased Tc1/Tc17 signature (T-Bet, IFNγ, TNFα, RORγT, and IL23r), expressed lower levels of Eomes and Gata3, and expressed inhibitory PD1, Tim3, Lag3, and CTLA4 less frequently than β2AR WT counterparts. In addition, host mice receiving KO CD8+ T cells exhibit a stronger graft-versus-lymphoma effect than host mice receiving β2AR WT CD8+ T cells. Together, these results indicate that β2AR activity in donor CD8+ T cells inhibits GVHD through transcriptional modulation of T cell differentiation and exhaustion, including a T-Bet/Eomes and PD1 relevant process.

title: Soil strength characterization using remote sensing for vehicle mobility assessment: a near-real-time approach
Convex-Relaxed Counterfactual Optimization for Non-differentiable Classifiers via Neural Surrogates
abstract: Counterfactual explanations (CE) facilitate actionable recourse by identifying minimal perturbations that transition an instance across a model's decision boundary. However, generating CEs for non-differentiable and non-smooth classifiers, including common nonparametric models such as kNN, random forests, and kernel SVMs, remains challenging because gradient information is unavailable or unreliable near irregular decision boundaries. Current model-agnostic approaches often neglect inherent structural priors, while surrogate-based methods frequently suffer from "metric distortion," where latent feature-space optimizations map to topologically invalid instances in the original input space. To resolve these theoretical impasses, we propose ECOer (Efficient Counterfactual Optimization with metric-preserving reconstruction regularization), a mathematically principled, end-to-end framework for post-hoc counterfactual generation for non-differentiable classifiers. ECOer constructs a ReLU-ReLU Single-hidden-layer Neural Network (R2SNN) as a differentiable surrogate, which we prove to possess tight universal approximation bounds for measurable decision regions. To preserve metric fidelity during latent-space search, we derive a novel metric-preserving reconstruction regularization mechanism grounded in Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) theory, ensuring that optimized features remain tied to the valid data manifold. Furthermore, we introduce a convex relaxation technique that yields a region-wise convex objective with zero relaxation gap within fixed decision regions. Extensive theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations on real-world benchmarks demonstrate that ECOer achieves a favorable trade-off between validity, proximity, plausibility, and online generation latency among the evaluated baselines. This work provides a rigorous algorithmic foundation for robust and reliable XAI in decision-critical tabular domains.

title: Photobiomodulation and the Wnt/β-Catenin Pathway in Apexogenesis: Rationale and Evidence Gaps.
abstract: Apexogenesis is a vital pulp therapy that preserves vascularized pulp in immature teeth and relies on dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and stem cells from the apical papilla (SCAPs) for continued root growth and apical closure. Wnt/β-catenin signaling has an established role in odontoblast differentiation, reparative dentinogenesis, and root development, although normal root development requires regulated rather than simply increased Wnt activity. Photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) is proposed to act through mitochondrial photoreception, and in vitro studies report increased expression of odontogenic/osteogenic markers and angiogenic factors (VEGF, TGF-β2) in DPSCs and SCAPs. Because these markers overlap with Wnt/β-catenin targets, a link between PBMT and this pathway has been hypothesized but not tested in these cells. This review addresses three questions: the role of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in root development and dentin repair; the mechanism that could link PBMT to this pathway; and the in vitro evidence for PBMT effects on DPSCs and SCAPs and its consistency. The evidence is heterogeneous and limited. Increased odontogenic/osteogenic differentiation was the most consistent finding. Reported effects on "proliferation" were inconsistent and were estimated mainly by MTT, a metabolic assay that does not measure cell division; no study used a clonogenic assay, and only one performed direct cell counts. No superior wavelength or fluence was identified. No study has examined PBMT-induced modulation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in DPSCs or SCAPs, and the markers involved are not pathway-specific. Therapeutic benefit in apexogenesis therefore remains unproven; direct mechanistic studies, light-delivery studies through dentin, and animal models are priorities.

Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive and autonomous decision-making in embedded, edge, and heterogeneous computing systems. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and integrated circuits (ICs) offer low latency, energy efficiency, and architectural flexibility for RL deployment, while introducing challenges in resource constraints, implementation complexity, and hardware-algorithm co-design. This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. The literature is organized by RL family, including model-based Markov decision processes, classical value-based methods, deep RL, actor-critic, policy-gradient, and multi-agent approaches. We further classify studies by abstraction level, hardware realization strategy, and application domain, examining how RL algorithms map onto reconfigurable and fixed hardware. Unlike surveys restricted to particular algorithms or platforms, this work provides a unified analysis of FPGA and IC implementations, covering acceleration, reconfigurable architectures, energy-aware control, and system-level optimization. Comparative assessments consider resource utilization, latency, throughput, power consumption, and reported performance gains. Finally, we identify recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems. The survey offers a consolidated reference for researchers developing and evaluating RL solutions on specialized hardware.

title: Visions, narratives and numbers: How roadmapping enables industrial transformation toward decarbonisation
AI Agent-Enabled Development of Enhanced DataYee for Robust and Efficient AFM Force Spectroscopy Analysis
abstract: High-throughput atomic force microscopy-based single-molecule force spectroscopy (AFM-SMFS) produces large, heterogeneous data sets that require force−curve screening, polymer model fitting, molecular event annotation, and expert verification. These interconnected operations limit analytical throughput and can introduce uncertainty when noisy or nonideal trajectories are processed. Here, we report the expert-supervised, AI agent-enabled development of DataYee, an integrated platform for AFM-SMFS analysis. The previously developed platform is referred to as original DataYee, whereas the version developed in this study is referred to as enhanced DataYee. During development, the AI agent assisted with literature retrieval, codebase navigation, coordinated modification of multiple software modules, refactoring, and debugging. Researchers defined the analytical requirements and verified the physical models, parameter constraints, software behavior, and experimental outputs. Enhanced DataYee combines convolutional neural network-based prescreening with support vector machine classification using interpretable mechanical features, noise-adaptive fitting window selection, worm-like regime crossover-informed multi-start worm-like chain fitting, and domain annotation constrained jointly by contour-length increments and unfolding forces. Functional refinements further improve data import, curve management, exception handling, and routine operation. Evaluation using a representative AFM-SMFS data set showed that enhanced DataYee improved the fitting and retention of noisy or nonideal trajectories while substantially reducing the number of curves requiring expert review. Following targeted expert verification, the resulting unfolding-force distribution remained consistent with manual analysis while including more validated molecular events. Enhanced DataYee therefore provides an efficient and traceable expert-in-the-loop workflow for high-throughput SMFS analysis and demonstrates how AI agents can support the scientifically supervised development of laboratory analytical software.

title: Discovery and Optimization of Indole-Based CDK9 Inhibitors for Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract: CDK9 has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for anticancer drug development. Although multiple CDK9 inhibitors have entered clinical evaluation, differentiated scaffolds with convincing activity and tolerability in solid tumors remain limited. In this study, we identified a series of indole-based CDK9 inhibitors through virtual screening and structure-based drug design, and systematically evaluated their therapeutic potential in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Among these compounds, W24 exhibited potent CDK9 inhibitory activity (IC50 = 0.9 nM) and a preliminary kinase selectivity profile. W24 effectively induced HCC cell death in vitro, which was accompanied by DNA damage and downregulation of the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1. Furthermore, W24 significantly suppressed tumor growth in HepG2 and Huh-7 xenograft models with an acceptable safety profile under the tested dosing regimen. Collectively, these findings highlight W24 as a promising lead compound and provide valuable insights for the development of next-generation CDK9 inhibitors for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma.

title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity.
abstract: Microorganisms have the potential to deliver growth-promoting benefits to plants and crops; however, to be useful in a field setting, their gene expression should be programmable and restricted to specific plant hosts and conditions. Here, using O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) as a model compound, we establish noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a tool for plant-based control of associated microbial activity. We use genetic code expansion to engineer OMY-dependent control of protein synthesis in the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis. Engineered B. subtilis strains express an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pair that, upon provision of OMY, results in suppression of in-frame amber stop codons in target transcripts. We engineer Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to biosynthesize OMY, showing that plant-derived OMY can stimulate gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. This demonstrates that inducible and tissue-specific expression of a single biosynthetic enzyme by the plant enables on-demand control over microbial activity, establishing ncAAs as a tool for programming plant-microorganism partnerships.

title: Reservoir Flood Storage Capacity as an Indicator of Potential Forecast-Informed Prerelease Effectiveness
abstract: The operation of multipurpose reservoirs for which flood risk management (FRM) is a primary or key purpose may be improved by the use of Forecast-Informed Reservoir Operations (FIRO). The ability to screen a portfolio of dams to assess FIRO viability allows for more-efficient use of time and funding than individual detailed analyses for several dams. In this study, screening criteria were used to evaluate the potential effectiveness of FIRO prestore and prerelease (PS-PR) and basic operation prerelease (BO-PR) methods using a large data set (58 dams) and along three lines of inquiry. A regression model was used to assess system characteristics and identify the reservoirs for which reservoir filling is most sensitive to changes in flood storage capacity. Historic flood events provided insight into the feasibility of FIRO based on seasonality and storm characteristics. Physical and policy constraints were studied to assess the feasibility of FIRO at or near top of conservation pool and to provide an initial input to the screening framework. A four-parameter equation to predict reservoir-filling frequency had an R 2 value of 0.67, and flood storage capacity was significant at a 99% confidence level. Review of historic reservoir-filling events showed a median 3-day flood storage of 23% and a 7-day flood storage of 38%. Policy and physical release constraints yielded maximum daily drawdown estimates for each reservoir and indicated a median of 2% of average annual inflow evacuation per day. A case study of five dams was used to assess viability of using the storage-based regression as a criterion for prerelease screening. The presented screening approach utilizes an estimate of maximum prerelease drawdown and the regression equations to provide high estimates for potential FIRO effectiveness (with uncertainty); actual applicability depends on forecast skill and available lead time, which are not evaluated in this study.
