title: pxGPT: A schema-constrained multimodal LLM framework for plant phenotyping.
abstract: Deep learning can scale image-based plant phenotyping but typically targets predefined traits, whereas manual phenotypic description is more flexible but difficult to scale. We present Phenotype eXplorer Generative Plant Traits (pxGPT), a Python framework that converts multi-view plant images into structured phenotype records. The workflow combines free-text description, dataset-specific schema generation with human review, and schema-constrained information extraction. We evaluated the extraction stage on three Brassica datasets using 78,973 annotations from ten annotators who had no access to pxGPT predictions. For 38-45 qualitative traits per dataset, pxGPT-human agreement ranged from 0.572 to 0.712, compared with 0.620 to 0.739 agreement among human annotators. All 32,736 required trait fields were present; 93 values were empty, and no qualitative descriptor violations were recorded. For selected morphological structures, pooled false-positive rates were 0.5-8.0%, while sensitivity varied across structure types in one mature-plant dataset (37.5-100%). The curated schemas were applied unchanged with two commercial models and one locally hosted open-weight model, with differences in mean accuracy of 0.03 or less. In the evaluated Brassica datasets, these results support schema-guided extraction of visible plant traits without separate model training for each trait. Human-guided schema development offers a path to extend pxGPT to other crops and imaging conditions, with accuracy requiring validation in each new setting. AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION The software is available at https://github.com/YaoChengLab/pxgpt and an archival version of the source code is available on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22931745). Curated schemas used in this study, annotation guides, phenotype records and human annotations are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907554. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: Agentic artificial intelligence for code status extraction from clinical notes: a cross-model comparison of single agent, reflective agent, and multiagent extractor-reviewer system.
abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate whether increasing agentic architectural complexity via self-reflection or multiagent design improves clinical code status extraction (Do Not Resuscitate [DNR], Do Not Intubate [DNI], Comfort Measures Only [CMO]) across open-source large language models (LLMs) of varying capabilities. MATERIALS AND METHODS We conducted a controlled cross-model comparison evaluating 3 architectures: (1) single extractor agent, (2) single agent with self-reflection, and (3) sequential multiagent extractor-reviewer system. Four open-source LLMs (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, GPT-OSS-20B, MedGemma-27B-IT, Qwen3.5-27B) were evaluated on 1000 Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV-Note discharge summaries. Ground truth labels were established through a physician-AI dual review with adjudication (Cohen's κ = 0.98-0.99). Models were evaluated on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen's κ, token consumption, and processing latency. McNemar's test was used for paired comparisons. RESULTS For capable larger models (GPT-OSS-20B, MedGemma-27B-IT, Qwen3.5-27B), single-agent architectures achieved comparable or superior performance for explicit code status (DNR, DNI) relative to complex systems, whereas multiagent review doubled token consumption and latency without accuracy gains. Reflective self-review significantly impaired MedGemma-27B-IT on DNI extraction (P = .047). For the smaller DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B, multiagent review provided statistically significant corrective benefits for DNR (P = .017) and CMO (P < .001), demonstrating a capability-threshold effect, though performance remained below clinically acceptable levels. DISCUSSION Architectural complexity does not enhance extraction performance for capable LLMs, and reflective self-review may cause conservative overcorrection. Multiagent verification value is inversely related to model capability. CONCLUSION Single-agent LLMs provide optimal accuracy and efficiency for explicit clinical extraction in capable models. Agentic complexity must be matched to both task characteristics and model capability rather than adopted by default.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

title: CHH demethylation of the BcMAM1 promoter contributes to cold tolerance in autotetraploid wucai (Brassica campestris L.).
abstract: Polyploidization has long been recognized as a driving force in plant adaptation to adverse environments. Chilling injury poses a major challenge to global crop production, and the regulatory hierarchies that govern cold adaptation in polyploid crops are unexplored. Here, we show that tetraploid wucai (Brassica campestris L.) displays greater cold tolerance than its diploid counterpart. Under prolonged cold stress, tetraploid plants displayed enhanced glucosinolate-associated transcriptional and metabolic responses, which may contribute to their improved stress adaptation. At the epigenetic level, diploid and tetraploid wucai showed distinct DNA methylation responses to short-term cold, with diploid plants tending toward greater CHH hypermethylation in promoter regions. This ploidy-specific increase in methylation correlates with transcriptional repression of multiple stress-responsive loci in diploids. Notably, expression of the glucosinolate biosynthesis gene METHYLTHIOALKYLMALATE SYNTHASE1 (BcMAM1) diverged between ploidies after cold treatment, inversely correlating with opposing CHH methylation (H = A, C, or T) trends in its promoter. Pharmacological demethylation using 5-azacytidine upregulated BcMAM1 and improved cold tolerance. Through a combination of functional assays and promoter-binding analyses, we identify the upstream transcription factor C-REPEAT BINDING FACTOR4 (BcCBF4), which binds to differentially methylated regions within the BcMAM1 promoter in a methylation-sensitive manner, supporting an association between the epigenetic state and transcriptional output. Together, our findings support a mechanistic model for the distinct cold response observed in the autotetraploid wucai line, involving coordinated changes in transcriptional activation and DNA methylation dynamics. The epigenetic and transcriptional targets identified in this study may inform breeding strategies for cold-resilient crops.

title: From risk to resilience: how insurance-linked agricultural credit policy and digital inclusion unlock smallholder farmers' access to credit
abstract: This study examines how crop insurance mitigates financial risk in accessing formal agricultural credit and how digital inclusion policies reduce transaction costs associated with borrowing. Using farm-level survey data, the analysis investigates both credit participation and the amount of institutional credit accessed, distinguishing demand-side and supply-side constraints. Heckman's two-stage selection model is employed to account for potential sample selection and heterogeneity among borrowers. The findings indicate that crop insurance plays a significant role in improving creditworthiness and willingness to engage with formal lending institutions. Insured farmers are also likely to obtain higher loan amounts compared to non-insured counterparts, reflecting reduced default risk perception by lenders. In parallel, digital inclusion measured through access to smartphones and banking services significantly lowers transaction costs related to credit application, documentation and loan disbursement. These findings suggest that both insurance mechanisms and digital tools enhance farmers' creditworthiness and lender confidence, thereby improving access to and uptake of formal credit. The study underscores the complementary role of risk mitigation and cost-reduction policies in strengthening agricultural credit. Crop insurance primarily addresses the financial risk, while digital inclusion improves procedural efficiency and access. The study highlights the importance of integrating crop insurance coverage with digital financial infrastructure to promote inclusive and resilient agricultural finance. The study is based on cross-sectional data from a specific geographic context, which may limit generalizability. Future research could explore longitudinal impacts or replicate the study in different agro-economic settings to validate the findings. This research provides empirical evidence on the synergistic role of crop insurance and digital inclusion in improving access to agricultural finance. It contributes to the growing discourse on integrated financial services for smallholders and offers important intervention policy insights for enhancing rural credit delivery systems.

title: IZeroDNAS: innovative differentiable NAS using zero-cost metrics and SuperNet initialization
abstract: This paper improves the stability and hardware-efficiency of zero-cost differentiable neural architecture search (NAS) for object detection, addressing two weaknesses of prior work: zero-cost rankings sensitive to SuperNet initialization and neglected edge-device deployment constraints. The authors propose IZeroDNAS, which integrates the NASWOT zero-cost metric into differentiable NAS. The authors introduce a SuperNet warm-up initialization, plus a depthwise-accelerated variant, to stabilize the rankings and a hardware-aware loss combining latency-aware and depth-aware terms built from a device look-up table. The authors evaluate on the ScaledYOLOv4 and YOLOv7 search spaces using Pascal VOC and COCO and deploy on Qualcomm RB5, Jetson TX2 and Jetson AGX Orin. Warm-up initialization reduces the mean average precision variance across random seeds from 5.687 to 0.0025 while raising accuracy. IZeroDNAS discovers shallower, wider models that are smaller and faster than manually designed detectors and the baseline ZeroDNAS, completing a search in under 5 h on a single RTX 2080, three times faster than comparable methods. The warm-up’s stabilizing effect is shown empirically rather than proven theoretically and a strictly fair comparison with proprietary methods such as YOLO-NAS is infeasible due to their undisclosed search spaces. Future work targets broader zero-cost proxies and more accurate device-performance predictors. IZeroDNAS is the first method to jointly tackle ranking instability and hardware-awareness in zero-cost differentiable NAS for object detection. Its warm-up and depthwise-accelerated variant offer a simple, modular, resource-efficient way to stabilize zero-cost metrics in large-scale SuperNets, benefiting practitioners deploying detectors on edge devices.
journal: APSIPA Transactions on Signal and Information Processing

title: Editorial: The superintelligence continuum: agentic AI, superintelligence, existential risk and the push for responsible AI
Integrating production systems, innovation culture and employee performance in the pharmaceutical industry
abstract: This study analyzed the effect of lean operation practices, continuous improvement orientation and total quality management on innovation culture within organizational culture, and how these factors influence employees' job satisfaction, organizational commitment and perceived work performance. Employing a cross-sectional survey design with 250 valid responses from employees in the Korean pharmaceutical industry, we used a 7-point Likert scale to measure eight constructs and tested hypotheses through structural equation modeling using SPSS 18.0 and AMOS 18.0, including comprehensive reliability and validity assessments through confirmatory factor analysis. Lean operational practices were not significantly related to organizational culture variables, whereas continuous improvement and total quality management were significantly related to collaborative organizational culture and innovation culture. Only innovation culture showed significant results in relation to the dependent variables of job satisfaction, organizational commitment and perceived work performance. This can be seen as occurring because, in the regulatory environment of the pharmaceutical industry, collaboration is already mandated for regulatory compliance and thus functions as a hygiene factor, whereas innovation culture functions as a differentiating factor that compensates for the autonomy restricted by regulation. This study is the first to empirically analyze the integrated relationship between production management systems, organizational culture and employee performance in the pharmaceutical industry. Although existing studies have explored individual variable relationships or dynamics in general manufacturing industries, we propose a convergent perspective on production and human resource management that considers the characteristics of the pharmaceutical industry.
journal: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management

title: Internationalization in turbulent times: revealing tensions and paradoxes in a comparative case study of Nordic-Baltic higher education institutions
abstract: This paper examines the tensions and paradoxes faced by Nordic-Baltic universities of applied sciences (UAS) in the context of internationalization, particularly within tourism management programs. By analysing case studies from Germany, Sweden and Lithuania, the research highlights the conflicting expectations UAS encounter as they balance regional development mandates with internationalization imperatives. The study reveals persistent paradoxes – such as the “cooperation-competition” dynamic and the struggle between vocational education and research ambitions – exacerbated by EU-driven policies like the Bologna Process and Lisbon Agenda. These findings underscore the need for nuanced strategies that reconcile local relevance with global competitiveness, while addressing resource constraints and stakeholder pressures. The paper contributes to critical debates on HE internationalization, advocating for adaptive frameworks that acknowledge the unique challenges of non-elite institutions. This study employs a qualitative, comparative case study approach to investigate the tensions and paradoxes arising from internationalization in Nordic-Baltic UAS. By analysing three UAS institutions in Germany, Sweden and Lithuania, the methodology integrates historical and contemporary data from policy documents, legislative sources and academic literature, supplemented by firsthand observations and stakeholder reflections. This multi-layered approach ensures reliability and credibility, while acknowledging the inherent limitations of case study generalizability. The analysis is structured around the dimensions of spatial orientation and academic identity, drawing on the paradox theory to interpret the conflicting expectations and operational challenges faced by UAS in a poly-crisis environment. The study reveals that Nordic-Baltic UAS face persistent tensions between their regional mandates and internationalization ambitions. Case studies from Germany, Sweden and Lithuania highlight paradoxes such as the “cooperation-competition” dynamic, the clash between vocational education and research expectations and the struggle to integrate international students into locally anchored programs. These challenges are exacerbated by EU policies like the Bologna Process, which prioritize competitiveness while undermining cohesion. The findings underscore the resource constraints, stakeholder conflicts and systemic barriers UAS encounter, emphasizing the need for adaptive strategies that balance local relevance with global engagement in an increasingly turbulent higher education landscape. This study's limitations stem from its qualitative case study design, which, while offering depth, restricts generalizability to broader higher education contexts. The focus on three Nordic-Baltic UAS may not capture the full diversity of internationalization challenges across Europe. Data reliance on policy documents, stakeholder reflections and institutional reports introduces potential bias, and the dynamic nature of EU policies may render some findings time-sensitive. Additionally, the absence of quantitative metrics limits the ability to measure the scale and impact of identified tensions and paradoxes. The paper's findings offer critical insights for policymakers and UAS leaders navigating internationalization. Institutions must develop adaptive strategies to reconcile regional mandates with global ambitions, such as targeted support for international students and faculty, and streamlined administrative processes for EU-funded projects. Strengthening partnerships with local industries and investing in applied research capacities can enhance both regional relevance and international competitiveness. Addressing resource constraints and stakeholder conflicts requires innovative governance and funding models, ensuring UAS can sustainably balance vocational education with evolving academic and international expectations. In particular, this includes differentiated research expectations that recognise the applied orientation of UAS rather than imposing metrics designed for research universities. The study exposes how internationalization in higher education amplifies social tensions within Nordic-Baltic UAS, particularly between local communities and global aspirations. The influx of international students and faculty staff enriches cultural diversity but risks marginalizing regional stakeholders, exacerbating disparities in access, integration and resource allocation. Rising nationalism and anti-immigration sentiments further complicate efforts to foster inclusivity and cohesion. These dynamics challenge UAS to act as bridges – promoting social mobility and intercultural dialogue while mitigating inequalities. The findings underscore the need for policies that align internationalization with social equity, ensuring that global engagement does not come at the expense of local belonging and collective well-being. This paper advances the discourse on higher education internationalization by focusing on the understudied context of Nordic-Baltic UAS, which occupy a distinct niche between vocational training and academic research. Unlike prior studies centered on elite or research-intensive institutions, this research uncovers the unique tensions and paradoxes UAS face – such as the dual pressures of regional embeddedness and global competitiveness – through a comparative, qualitative lens. By integrating paradox theory with empirical case studies, the paper offers a novel framework for understanding how poly-crisis environments and EU policies like the Bologna Process reshape institutional identities and operational realities, contributing fresh insights to both theory and practice in international higher education.
journal: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education

title: Learning-oriented climates and sales capability development in B2B markets: how coworker support mediates the path from climate to salesperson competence
abstract: This study aims to examine how learning-oriented organizational climates and perceived support structures relate to salesperson development in complex business-to-business (B2B) sales contexts, distinguishing between satisfaction with development and perceived competence. Survey data were collected from USA-based sales professionals. The study used confirmatory factor analysis and partial least squares structural equation modeling to test relationships among learning-oriented climate cues, perceived training, supervisory and coworker support, and two developmental outcomes. Internal work constraints were tested as a moderator of the coworker support–competence relationship. Learning-oriented climates were positively associated with perceived support and with satisfaction with development; tolerance for mistakes was also positively associated with perceived competence, whereas openness to new ideas was not. Coworker support was the support source most consistently and significantly related to perceived competence in the full sample. In the context-specific B2B analysis, coworker support emerged as the only significant predictor of perceived competence. All three support sources were positively related to satisfaction with development, whereas perceived competence was driven specifically by coworker support. Internal work constraints significantly moderated the coworker support–competence relationship, but opposite to a substitution account: coworker support mattered more when constraints were low. The findings demonstrate that salesperson development is shaped by an integrated system of climate cues and social support rather than sharply differentiated pathways. Coworker-based learning emerges as a particularly salient component of competence formation in complex selling environments. Managers should view capability development as embedded in social learning systems supported by learning-oriented climates and multiple support sources, rather than relying solely on formal development structures. This study offers a theoretically grounded account of how learning-oriented climates and multisource social support jointly shape evaluative and capability-based development in B2B sales contexts, while highlighting the particular salience of coworker-based learning for competence formation in complex B2B selling.

title: The impact of ESG ratings on corporate investment efficiency in a geopolitical context
abstract: This paper examines the impact of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) ratings on corporate investment efficiency amid rising geopolitical uncertainty, while uncovering the underlying transmission mechanisms and heterogeneous effects across firm types, thereby enriching the literature on ESG governance and corporate investment decision-making. This study employs a multidimensional fixed-effects model for the baseline estimation. It further conducts heterogeneity tests based on firm lifecycle, technological attributes, and pollution levels, and examines the transmission channels, including financing constraints, green innovation, management costs, and managerial myopia. Higher ESG ratings significantly reduce inefficient investments and enhance corporate investment efficiency. The positive effects are particularly pronounced in growth-stage, non-high-tech, and non-heavily polluting firms, while they are weaker in high-tech and declining firms. ESG ratings improve investment efficiency by alleviating financing constraints, promoting green innovation, reducing management costs, and mitigating managerial myopia. This study links ESG ratings with corporate investment efficiency amid geopolitical uncertainty, thereby enriching the literature on the micro-level economic consequences of ESG practices and corporate investment decisions. It provides empirical evidence for firms to adopt differentiated ESG strategies to enhance investment efficiency and offers implications for policymakers in designing refined ESG governance frameworks in the context of global geopolitical and sustainable development competition.

title: From exhibition to education: operationalizing VR for scholarship in research, teaching and learning
abstract: This case study demonstrates one way that an academic library can transition immersive technologies from novelty installations to core pedagogical infrastructure. It argues that for virtual reality (VR) to persist as a sustainable library service, it must function as an active platform for teaching, research and learning, rather than a passive website or collection of available, but underutilized, hardware (e.g. HMDs). We describe the development of an immersive “showcase” environment built around a library-based 3D scanning service representing Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable (FAIR)-aligned 3D production workflows (Cook, 2024), and the subsequent design-based/action-research pilot of the environment in select academic contexts. The paper details selection criteria for 3D capture, integration with repositories such as Sketchfab and the design of a web-based immersive VR space (the “Immersive Showcase”) that can be used as a customizable classroom, exhibit hall or event space. Two principal curricular cases – French language learning and a hybrid lecture–exhibition space – illustrate how this VR environment, incorporating multimedia and interactive collaboration features, supports constructivist, object-centered pedagogy and facilitates engagement with collective sense-making (Mills et al., 2020). User feedback from beta testing and pilot teaching engagements informs iterative design decisions, providing a way forward for these innovative curricular integrations and always-on virtual teaching and learning environments. Embedding high-fidelity 3D surrogates in accessible immersive spaces can support “field-like” engagement with primary source materials, multi-perspective analysis and appears to facilitate hybrid teaching models. Clear workflows, role differentiation (e.g. learner/presenter) and targeted interface adjustments (e.g. navigation aids, session controls) proved critical to instructor uptake and student usability. Iterative refinement highlights the importance of aligning technical affordances with instructional goals. As a single-institution case describing a service-oriented pilot, findings are context-specific; future work should include systematic assessment of learning outcomes and comparative studies across educational contexts and platforms. The case provides concrete guidance on staffing, infrastructure, access modalities and partnership models for libraries seeking to embed VR and 3D content into teaching and research. We posit that the success of programs of this nature requires a shift away from viewing VR as a “fieldtrip” destination, instead seeing it as a steady partner in the scholarly lifecycle – a shift which requires platform-agnostic asset management and iterative design based on pedagogically informed user data. Rather than treating VR as an experimental add-on, this paper operationalizes it as integrated library infrastructure that links digitization, preservation and metaverse-style delivery with a responsive pedagogical approach to activity design. This paper offers a replicable model for a service-oriented pilot showing how academic libraries can align VR, 3D data and instructional design to support scalable immersive learning.

title: S$^3$E-Det: A Strict Spatial-Spectral Equivariant Detector for Multispectral Object Detection
abstract: Multispectral object detection requires detectors to exploit material-dependent spectral responses while maintaining consistent localization under geometric variations. Existing MOD detectors learn discriminative spectral representations, yet lack a unified mechanism that preserves spectral order, adapts spectral-context fusion across pyramid levels, and regulates geometric responses under rotation. To address these limitations, we propose S$^3$E-Det, a strict spatial-spectral equivariant detector that couples ordered spectral modeling with transformation-consistent prediction. Spectral Order-aware Sampling Calibration (SOSC) imposes local order constraints on input-derived spectral features through first-order variation, while Common-Differential Equivariant Fusion (CDEF) adapts spectral-context aggregation across pyramid levels. A compact Geometric Alignment Head (GAH) reconciles invariant and equivariant output properties within a unified prediction stage. Across MODA, HOD3K, and DroneVehicle, S$^3$E-Det combines high detection accuracy with a compact parameter footprint and reduced rotation-induced variation. Code is available at https://github.com/Riiluo/S3E-Det.

title: SGLDet: Spectral-aware Global-Local Dynamic Modeling for Multispectral Aerial Object Detection
abstract: Multispectral aerial object detection aims to exploit spectral-spatial cues to address object detection challenges in complex aerial scenes. Existing methods mainly focus on spectral-spatial decoupling and object-aware spectral-spatial fusion to improve spectral utilization. However, two critical issues remain underexplored: 1) severe foreground-background imbalance caused by large scene coverage hinders reliable object recognition; 2) aerial objects exhibit substantial local variations in scale, orientation, and structure, which hinder accurate localization. To address these issues, we propose SGLDet, a spectral-aware global-local dynamic modeling framework for multispectral aerial object detection, which is motivated by the observation that object semantics are jointly determined by global spectral consistency and scene context, while precise localization requires dynamic feature modulation conditioned on the input spectral and spatial properties. To realize these properties, SGLDet consists of three coordinated components: a Spectral-driven Global Dynamic Modeling module that aggregates spectrally related features across the scene via similarity-guided sparse matching; a Multi-scale Global Context Integration module that constructs a compact scene memory for scene-guided contextual reasoning; and a Spectral-aware Input-dependent Calibration Aggregation module that performs expert-kernel aggregation with scene-guided spectral-spatial calibration to enable adaptive local feature modulation. Extensive experiments on MODA, HOD3K, and DroneVehicle demonstrate that SGLDet achieves superior performance with competitive computational cost. Code is available at https://github.com/Riiluo/SGLDet.

title: Generative AI as a team moderator in CSCL : Facilitating students' multidimensional engagement through adaptive scaffolding for socially shared regulation of learning
abstract: Socially shared regulation of learning (SSRL) is essential for successful collaboration, yet effectively scaffolding it remains challenging because regulatory needs are dynamic and context‐dependent. While generative AI (GenAI) offers potential for adaptive support, current applications in collaborative learning largely position it as a content‐oriented tutor for knowledge explanation or idea generation, leaving its role as a process‐oriented team moderator for scaffolding SSRL processes underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a 16‐week quasi‐experiment with 64 undergraduates in China, comparing adaptive SSRL scaffolding delivered by a GenAI agent in the adaptive‐SSRL condition with static scaffolding via structured digital worksheets in the static‐SSRL condition. Survey data and group discussion transcripts were analysed using statistical methods and epistemic network analysis. Results indicated several differences in students' multidimensional engagement between the two conditions: (1) Behaviourally, the adaptive‐SSRL group showed significantly higher participation equality, although participation intensity did not differ significantly between groups. (2) Cognitively, the adaptive‐SSRL group demonstrated deeper cognitive engagement, reflected in more advanced cognitive presence phases and more integrative, solution‐oriented discourse patterns. (3) Emotionally, the adaptive‐SSRL group reported significantly higher overall emotional engagement, particularly feeling more relaxed during collaboration and more connected with peers. These findings extend human–AI collaboration research by showing that GenAI can function as an SSRL‐informed team moderator rather than a content‐oriented tutor. They also offer design implications for GenAI‐enabled adaptive SSRL scaffolding and human–AI role division in CSCL. What is already known about this topic Socially shared regulation of learning (SSRL) is critical for successful collaboration and is closely associated with the quality of student engagement. While static scaffolds (eg, worksheets) provide a basic regulatory structure, they fail to adapt to the dynamic and emergent needs of collaborating teams. Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly used for personalised content support, yet its potential as a process‐oriented team moderator remains underexplored. What this paper adds This study introduced SSRLAgent, a GenAI agent grounded in SSRL theory and established principles of collective metacognitive support, to provide adaptive and interactive regulatory scaffolding. In a 16‐week quasi‐experiment, we compared GenAI‐enabled adaptive SSRL scaffolding (SSRLAgent) with static scaffolding (structured digital worksheets) in CSCL. Adaptive‐SSRL scaffolding was associated with higher‐quality engagement: greater participation equality, deeper cognitive engagement and higher overall emotional engagement. Implications for practice and/or policy The study underscores the necessity of shifting SSRL scaffolding from static, ‘one‐size‐fits‐all’ support to adaptive GenAI interventions to improve collaborative engagement. The findings provide design guidance for developing SSRL agents that are embedded in the shared interaction space and responsive to groups' moment‐to‐moment regulatory needs. The study suggests a productive human–AI division of labour: GenAI agents can support process coordination and regulatory prompting, while teachers and peers remain essential for relationally complex forms of support that collaborative learning requires.

title: Stratum Corneum Biomarkers for Differentiating Irritant and Allergic Contact Dermatitis.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES Occupational hand dermatitis (HD) comprises irritant and allergic contact dermatitis (ICD and ACD), which share clinical features, often overlap, and may coexist with atopic dermatitis (AD), complicating diagnosis. The objective of this study is to explore whether stratum corneum (SC) biomarkers discriminate ICD from ACD. PATIENTS We recruited 126 patients from the Occupational Dermato-allergology Clinics of the Amsterdam UMC. METHODS SC samples were collected from lesional HD skin and patch test reactions to nickel, chromium, methylisothiazolinone, sodium lauryl sulfate (irritant), and control sites. Thirty-three biomarkers were analyzed. Random forest and penalized regression models were trained on the patch test dataset and validated in HD; an additional model was trained and validated in HD. Exploratory analyses evaluated discrimination among individual allergens and between AD, ICD and ACD. RESULTS The patch test model showed good discrimination between ICD and ACD (mean AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.82-0.87), driven primarily by skin barrier-related biomarkers. In HD, performance declined (mean AUC 0.51, 95% CI 0.26-0.76); sensitivity for ACD was 88%. Model trained and validated within HD achieved mean AUC of 0.60 (95% CI 0.57-0.64). Discrimination between individual allergens yielded mean AUC of 0.75 (95% CI 0.72-0.77). CONCLUSION SC biomarkers discriminated ICD from ACD good in acute patch test, but showed limited discrimination in HD, reflecting differences between acute and chronic inflammation.

title: Anthropogenic Effects on Elementomes Across Organisms, Ecosystems, and the Biosphere
abstract: The elemental composition of organisms and ecosystems, termed the “elementome,” fundamentally determines biological function and ecosystem processes. These elemental profiles, historically relatively stable over geological timescales, have been profoundly altered by human activity, especially since the Industrial Revolution, giving rise to a novel “human elementome.” The number and amounts of elements used biologically and nonbiologically by humans, We synthesized multidisciplinary evidence demonstrating this critical shift, characterized by pervasive imbalances in the ratios of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus driven by extensive anthropogenic inputs, together with the unprecedented mobilization of a wide spectrum of elements, from critical raw materials and fossil fuels to novel technological elements such as rare‐earth metals. This shift in the human elementome is therefore at the root of many of the environmental changes observed today, as it profoundly alters the cycling, distribution, and availability of chemical elements across ecosystems. These elemental perturbations have not acted in isolation but have interacted synergistically with physiological stresses induced by elevated concentrations of CO 2 , warming, and drought, generating complex emergent effects on life. Our findings highlight a rapid transformation of the fundamental elemental makeup of the biosphere driven by humans, with cascading ecological consequences for ecosystem function and species composition globally. This elemental perspective offers a robust framework for understanding and predicting ecosystem responses in the Anthropocene, informing strategies for conserving biodiversity and managing ecosystems.

title: Research on automatic crack recognition of self-locking masonry wall based on convolutional neural network
abstract: To address low efficiency and pixel-level difficulties in manual crack detection for interlocking block masonry walls, this study developed an automatic identification method based on a Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) with VGG19 as the backbone, replacing fully connected layers with deconvolutional layers for end-to-end semantic segmentation. Images were collected, augmented via cropping, color jittering, Gaussian noise, and rotation, and annotated at pixel level. The model achieved maximum precision of 76% and recall of 75.9% on the validation set. Although global pixel accuracy reached 98.8% and 98.3% on training and validation sets, this metric is misleading for imbalanced segmentation (crack pixels <5%), so precision and recall serve as primary references. Results show FCN can preliminarily identify cracks, though precision remains limited. Future work will adopt IoU and Dice metrics. This research offers a feasible technical path for intelligent block masonry crack detection.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Machine Learning, and Image Processing (AMLIP 2026)

title: Smart inversion of constitutive parameters and deformation forecasting via gradient-free optimization coupled with finite element analysis
abstract: Forecasting the settlement of earth fills remains a fundamental obstacle in computational geotechnics, as inferring constitutive coefficients from scarce field measurements defines an ill-conditioned inverse task. This paper introduces a computationally intelligent framework that merges Biot’s consolidation model discretized through finite elements with a non-derivative complex optimization routine implemented within the BCF simulation environment. Two stress-dependent nonlinear descriptions—the Duncan-Chang E-ν and Duncan-Chang E-B relationships—are simultaneously utilized to depict the mechanical response of deep compacted subgrade fills. To counter the dimensionality explosion typical of highdimensional parameter domains, a systematic sensitivity assessment is first executed using perturbation-based numerical experiments to rate the influence of every constitutive constant on the predicted subsidence. The most sensitive quantities are selected as decision variables for the subsequent inversion, while parameters of minor effect are assigned fixed values derived from empirical correlations, thereby drastically condensing the inverse problem dimension and reinforcing the uniqueness of the recovered solution. The complex search algorithm, a direct strategy free of any gradient requirement, is tightly integrated with the finite element forward solver, enabling the objective function—which captures the misfit between simulated and observed settlement histories—to be assessed without analytical derivatives or surrogate constructs. The entire simulation-optimization workflow is authenticated against foundation settlement monitoring records obtained at two instrumented sections of the Hengzao Expressway. Comparative evaluation confirms that the back-calculated material constants empower the finite element model to faithfully reproduce the temporal evolution of observed settlements and to yield substantially refined predictions of both residual post-construction movement and final long-term deformation. Additionally, the E-B constitutive variant, which expresses volumetric behavior through a stress-dependent bulk modulus, consistently surpasses the E-ν variant in predictive fidelity, revealing a superior capacity to represent the consolidation mechanics of high embankments on yielding subsoils. By combining physics-based numerical replication with data-centric inversion, this study furnishes a robust decision-support engine for predictive asset maintenance and construction phasing in civil infrastructure practice.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Machine Learning, and Image Processing (AMLIP 2026)

title: A lightweight method for weed detection based on deep learning
abstract: Agricultural production is severely affected by weeds, which compete with crops for resources and result in reduced yields. Laser weeding robots with deep learning technology can avoid the environmental pollution problems caused by chemical weeding, however, computing resources constraints make it challenging to concurrently achieve high accuracy and realtime efficiency. Therefore, a lightweight YOLOv8n-based model LWYOLO is proposed for embedded laser weeding robots. Algorithmic improvements: depth-separable convolution-based C2f_EMBC module integrated with BiFPN enhances multi-scale feature handling; optimized detection head achieve light-weighting. Experiments show LWYOLO has 1/4 parameters of YOLOv8n, 74.4% lower complexity, with Precision (93.0%) and mAP50 (96.6%) improved by 3 and 4 percentage points, supporting weeding robot engineering.
journal: International Conference on Algorithms, Machine Learning, and Image Processing (AMLIP 2026)

title: Anabaena, a multicellular model for cyanobacterial cell biology and biotechnology
abstract: Heterocyst-forming cyanobacteria (order Nostocales) are a monophyletic group of organisms that grow as filaments usually made of dozens to hundreds of cells (termed vegetative cells) that can perform oxygenic photosynthesis. Under combined nitrogen deficiency, some cells in the filament differentiate into N2-fixing heterocysts, which do not produce oxygen and, indeed, keep a microoxic environment appropriate for the expression and functioning of the N2-fixing enzyme, nitrogenase. Thus, in the diazotrophic filament, oxygenic photosynthesis and N2 fixation are segregated into two different cell types, vegetative cells and heterocysts, which require intercellular molecular exchange to feed each other with fixed nitrogen and reduced carbon, respectively. The current understanding of heterocyst biology, including regulation of heterocyst differentiation, which also involves intercellular signaling, is the result of studying mainly a few strains of the genus Anabaena. Here, we review the classical studies that established Anabaena as a model for the Nostocales and clarified the basics of N2 fixation in these organisms. Then, we show how molecular genetics came into the scene and how it was complemented by genomic analysis. This, together with the introduction of modern cell biology approaches, led to a renewed understanding of cellular differentiation and unraveled a system for intercellular communication that is unique in the biological world. In turn, the new accumulated knowledge on Anabaena physiology and genetics makes these organisms an excellent system for the development of new synthetic biology tools that will be crucial for their use in biotechnology.

title: MIMOS-Tools: An Integrated Toolchain for Model-Based Design of Embedded Systems
abstract: Despite decades of progress in model-based methods and tools for embedded real-time systems, there is still no integrated environment that supports the entire development lifecycle. This paper presents MIMOS-Tools, a comprehensive toolchain spanning the key phases of development, including modeling, simulation, formal verification, real-time scheduling, schedulability and end-to-end latency analysis, and code generation for heterogeneous multicore platforms. All phases are grounded in a single, coherent, and deterministic model of computation, the MIMOS model, for which we present a formal operational semantics and establish both functional and timing determinism. This semantic foundation ensures that properties verified at the model level are preserved throughout the development process and in the generated implementation. A distinguishing feature of MIMOS-Tools is its support for not only deterministic but also modular, compositional design. Unlike synchronous design environments such as SCADE and Simulink, which rely on a global base clock and offline static scheduling, MIMOS-Tools supports time-triggered asynchronous communication together with flexible real-time scheduling of computation. This removes the tight global coupling of the synchronous paradigm: components can be added, modified, or updated without recomputing a system-wide schedule, enabling scalable and incremental design and dynamic updates throughout the system lifecycle. However, MIMOS-Tools also supports Simulink models when the deadlines of tasks are set to zero to emulate the zero-time semantics of synchronous design. The toolchain is available at uu-mimos.github.io.

title: RSPO2 synergizes with BMP2 to enhance Wnt-dependent bone healing.
abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP2) is used clinically to promote bone regeneration, but dose-limiting side effects restrict its clinical utility. Canonical Wnt signaling is essential for bone formation, and R-spondin-2 (RSPO2) is a secreted Wnt agonist highly expressed by osteoprogenitors. We found that BMP2 strongly induced RSPO2 during early human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSC) osteoblast differentiation. Recombinant RSPO2 synergized with BMP2 in both hMSCs and MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts, whereas RSPO2 silencing impaired BMP2-driven osteogenic responses. In a murine critical-size calvarial defect model, co-delivery of RSPO2 and a suboptimal dose of BMP2 yielded significantly more new bone than BMP2 alone, while RSPO2 alone was ineffective. Enhanced canonical Wnt activation with BMP2-RSPO2 co-treatment was shown with an in vivo Wnt reporter mouse. Bulk RNA sequencing of MC3T3-E1 cells revealed that BMP2-RSPO2 co-treatment differentially activated osteogenesis-related genes and pathways compared to BMP2 alone. The guanine exchange factor (GEF), Prex1, was selectively upregulated by BMP2-RSPO2 co-treatment, and was required for RSPO2-mediated enhancement of BMP2-induced osteoblastogenesis. These findings identify RSPO2 as an enhancer of BMP2-driven osteogenesis, amplifying Wnt activation and involving PREX1-dependent signaling. RSPO2 or PREX1 activation may represent a co-therapy that could enhance BMP2 efficacy while mitigating the adverse effects of high-dose BMP2.

title: Endothelial-pericyte interactions activate insulin signaling and its implications for blood-brain barrier dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: This study aimed to investigate how pericyte degeneration contributes to BBB disruption in Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on the roles of insulin signaling and the imbalance between matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) and endogenous tissue inhibitors of MMPs (TIMPs) We employed an in vitro BBB model constructed by co-culturing brain-specific microvascular endothelial-like cells (iBMECs) differentiated from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and primary human brain vasculature pericytes (hBVPs). Protein expression under solo- versus co-culture conditions was assessed by western blots. MMP enzymatic activity in the culture media was measured by fluorometric assay. Exosomes were isolated from conditioned media and brain derived neurotrophic growth factor (BDNF) concentrations were determined using ELISA assays. TIMP1 and collagen-IV expressions were significantly increased in co-cultured BBB endothelial cells and pericytes compared to solo-cultures. However, a greater effect was observed in cells co-cultured for 2 days than 7 days. Elevated TIMP1 in co-culture media significantly inhibited MMP activity. The AKT and ERK pathways were activated in both cell types after 7 days of co-culture, and the ERK signaling mediated TIMP1 upregulation in endothelial cells. BDNF was significantly enriched in exosomes isolated from co-culture media on the abluminal side compared to the solo-cultures. Reduced accumulation of toxic amyloid-beta 42 was observed in pericytes co-cultured with endothelial cells, concurrent with reduced expression of low density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1). These findings provide mechanistic insights into BBB disruption due to pericyte degeneration and highlight the important role of BBB insulin resistance in causing cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD.
journal: Fluids and Barriers of the CNS

title: Combined saccades and turning parameters for early identification of PIGD-subtype Parkinson’s disease
abstract: Early identification of the postural instability and gait difficulty (PIGD)-subtype PD remains challenging. Because PD patients often have concurrent impairments in eye movements and gait, we assessed whether integrating these two modalities could improve early identification of PIGD-PD. We enrolled 46 PIGD-PD patients and 22 healthy controls (HC) and collected eye-movement and gait parameters using video nystagmography (VNG) and wearable gait analysis devices. We established an integrated model for early identification of PIGD-PD using multivariate stepwise logistic regression. Compared with HC, PIGD-PD patients at Hoehn-Yahr stages 1–2 and 3–4 showed significantly lower saccadic accuracy in all directions, and longer saccadic latency only in the upward direction. Similarly, both PD subgroups exhibited longer turning duration and lower turning velocity. In the Hoeh-Yahr stage 1–2 PD subgroup, the areas under the curve (AUCs) for mean horizontal saccadic accuracy (cut-off = 91%, AUC = 0.819, P < 0.001) and turning velocity (cut-off = 177°/s, AUC = 0.888, P < 0.001) were both greater than 0.7. The combined use of these two indicators effectively differentiated symptomatic early-stage PD patients from HC (P < 0.001), with a sensitivity of 76%, a specificity of 100%, and an AUC of 0.939. The combination of horizontal saccadic accuracy and turning velocity has high value for identifying patients with early-stage (Hoehn-Yahr stage 1–2) PIGD-PD. Trial registration: This study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR1900022655, date: April 20, 2019).

title: Parental screentime limits and child computer and information literacy and computational thinking: a multilevel analysis of 2023 ICILS data
abstract: Adolescents’ digital skill development is shaped not only by school environments but also by parental regulation of technology use. While Parental Mediation Theory distinguishes between restrictive and enabling strategies, empirical research has rarely differentiated between forms of restrictive mediation, particularly the distinction between strict (no exceptions) and flexible (homework-permitted) screen-time limits. Moreover, existing studies often rely on self-reports for gauging student achievement, lack comprehensive controls, or overlook how the flexibility of rules may matter. This study examines how different forms of parental screen-time limits are associated with Grade 8 students’ computer and information literacy (CIL) and computational thinking (CT), and whether these associations vary by socioeconomic status. We analyze data from the International Computer and Information Literacy Study (ICILS) 2023 using three-level linear models (students nested within schools within countries). The analytic samples include 96,455 students (CIL; 4,609 schools; 29 countries) and 60,223 students (CT; 2,722 schools; 19 countries). Outcomes are CIL and CT plausible values. Key predictors distinguish strict and flexible parental screen-time limits (reference: no limits). Models adjust for gender, socioeconomic status (SES), immigration status, computer experience, ICT self-efficacy, and internet access, with covariates group-mean centered. Cross-level interactions test whether SES moderates associations between parental rules and outcomes. Within schools, strict screen-time limits are negatively associated with both outcomes (CIL: B = -14.94, p < .001; CT: B = -17.31, p < .001), whereas flexible limits are positively associated with performance, particularly for CT (CIL: B = 2.17, p < .001; CT: B = 8.34, p < .001). Similarly, at the between-school level, strict screen-time limits are negatively associated with both outcomes (CIL: B = -48.12, p < .001; CT: B = -47.22, p < .001), whereas flexible limits are positively associated with performance, particularly for CT (CIL: B = 9.74, p < .05; CT: B = 33.67, p < .001). Interaction models indicate no statistically significant moderation by SES for CIL. For CT, however, the positive interaction between flexible parental limits and SES (B = 3.82, p < .01) suggests that the association between flexible regulation and CT is stronger among higher-SES students, consistent with cumulative advantage. Not all restrictive parental strategies operate equivalently. While strict limitations appear to constrain opportunities for digital skill development, flexible rules that permit educational use are associated with higher performance, particularly among socioeconomically advantaged students for computational thinking. These findings extend Parental Mediation Theory by demonstrating that the structure and flexibility of rules—rather than restriction per se—are central to understanding digital skill acquisition. The results highlight the importance of context-sensitive parental guidance and suggest that policies should support parents in adopting balanced, education-oriented approaches to screen-time regulation.

title: An interstitial fluid-like NICHE-chip for neural stem cell niche modeling and nanoscale neurotrophic delivery
abstract: Neural stem cells (NSCs) reside in anatomically confined niches, where three-dimensional (3D) geometry and interstitial fluid (ISF) flow collectively regulate NSC behavior. However, in vitro platforms that simultaneously recapitulate size-controlled 3D architecture, ISF-like dynamics, and nanoscale therapeutic delivery remain limited. Here, we present a 3D printing-based platform with multi-sized microwells, termed the Neural-Inspired Culture for a Hydrodynamic Environment (NICHE)-chip, which incorporates an osmosis-driven flow system to generate ISF-like flow. The NICHE-chip enabled stable formation of uniform human neural stem cell (hNSC) neurospheres across defined microwell sizes. Under ISF-like flow, hNSC neurospheres showed enhanced viability, reduced apoptosis, and increased self-renewal and differentiation marker expression, particularly in 100 μm microwells. ISF-like flow also promoted laminin-rich extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition and cell–cell interactions, suggesting niche-like remodeling of the 3D microenvironment. In the ISF-integrated 100 μm neurosphere model, amyloid-β (Aβ) was introduced to establish an Alzheimer’s disease (AD)-like neurotoxicity model, which was then used to evaluate nanoparticle-mediated neurotrophic factor delivery using brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles. BDNF-loaded PLGA nanoparticles (BDNF-NPs) enabled sustained BDNF delivery, attenuated Aβ-induced neuronal marker loss, and counter-regulated a subset of Aβ-induced transcriptional alterations associated with neuroprotection. Overall, the NICHE-chip provides an ISF-integrated 3D neurosphere culture platform for NSC niche modeling, AD-like neurotoxicity assessment, and nanoscale neurotrophic factor delivery.

title: CYP1B1 is a potential target of kaempferol in renal fibrosis: a multi‑omics and single‑cell transcriptomics study
abstract: Renal fibrosis (RF) is a progressive and irreversible pathological process for which effective treatments are limited. This study explores the molecular targets and mechanisms through which kaempferol (Kae) ameliorates RF, with particular emphasis on cytochrome P450 1B1 (CYP1B1). Using a combination of transcriptomic profiling, weighted gene co‑expression network analysis (WGCNA), multi‑algorithm machine learning [least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), support vector machine‑recursive feature elimination (SVM‑RFE), and Random Forest], and single‑cell transcriptomics, we identified the core targets of Kae intervention in RF. shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis evaluated gene contributions to the predictive model, while cell‑type identification by estimating relative subsets of RNA transcripts (CIBERSORT) estimated the immune microenvironment. The cell type-specific distribution of core targets was further characterized through single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and the scTenifoldKnk (a machine learning-based virtual gene knockout tool) algorithm simulated the effects of CYP1B1 loss-of-function on fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Finally, molecular docking was performed to predict the binding conformations of kaempferol with the proteins encoded by the six prioritized genes. Six core genes (VCAM1, NFKBIA, SFN, CCL5, CYP1B1, and AXL) were identified from 25 Kae-RF-related genes, with CYP1B1 as an upstream regulatory hub. Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased plasma cells and eosinophils, alongside decreased M0/M1 macrophages and activated NK cells. Single-cell analysis localized CYP1B1 to smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, with significant upregulation during late-stage fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation. Virtual knockdown of CYP1B1 upregulated 46 genes associated with fibrosis-related biological processes, including cell adhesion, G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling, ion transport, and cytoskeletal remodeling. The six-gene diagnostic model achieved area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.889 (training) and 0.759 (external validation). Molecular docking showed favorable Kae–CYP1B1 binding (− 6.5 kcal/mol). CYP1B1 may serve as a potential functional target of Kae in RF, likely through modulation of fibroblast activation and ECM remodeling. These findings are hypothesis‑generating and provide a computational basis for future experimental validation of CYP1B1‑targeted strategies in RF.

title: A gut microbiota–metabolite–host gene score for subtyping and predicting the treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: integrative analysis with in silico knockout validation
abstract: The pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves a complex interplay between immune dysregulation and metabolic disturbance, with the gut microbiota and its metabolites playing pivotal roles. However, integrated biomarkers based on the “gut microbiota–metabolite–host gene” regulatory axis that can quantify its impact on RA stratification and therapeutic response are lacking. We integrated multiple RA transcriptomic datasets to screen for host genes explicitly associated with the gut microbiota and metabolites using the gutMGene database. A gut microbiota–metabolite–host score (GMS) was constructed via principal component analysis (PCA). Immune infiltration patterns were evaluated using CIBERSORT. Furthermore, scRNA-seq was employed to map the cellular origins of key genes, and in silico knockout analysis using scTenifoldKnk was performed to simulate the functional ablation of core host genes within this regulatory axis. Additionally, molecular docking was conducted to validate the binding affinities between the key host proteins and the optimal small molecule. We identified seven microbiota–metabolite–host hub genes (FOS, JUN, IDO1, PEMT, EGFR, ABCC4, and FADS3) and constructed the GMS. The GMS stratified patients with RA into two distinct functional subtypes: an adaptive immune activation subtype and an inflammatory–metabolic composite subtype. Notably, the GMS demonstrated superior performance in predicting responses to anti-TNF and rituximab therapies. The scRNA-seq analysis revealed high expression of FOS and JUN in T cells and NK cells. In silico knockout analysis further revealed the central transcription factors FOS and JUN as key executors of this axis, as their ablation significantly affected osteoclast differentiation and the enrichment of TNF/MAPK inflammatory pathways. These computational findings support the core mechanism by which gut microbiota–metabolite signalling drives RA joint pathology via FOS/JUN. Molecular docking results confirmed strong binding interactions between the identified active molecules and their respective target proteins. This study establishes a GMS based on the gut microbiota–metabolite–host gene regulatory axis as a robust tool for molecular subtyping and predicting biological therapy responses in patients with RA. Crucially, through integrated computational modelling, including in silico knockout and molecular docking validation, we identified FOS/JUN as critical executor genes linking the gut microenvironment to RA bone destruction, providing novel targets for therapeutic strategies aimed at the gut–joint axis.

title: Beyond functionality: prioritizing adaptive lower garment requirements for lower limb disabilities using a refined Kano model with demographic interaction analyses
abstract: This study investigates the multidimensional lower garment requirements of users with lower limb disabilities, extending beyond basic functionality to examine how physical constraints and user evaluations are reflected in adaptive clothing preferences. Specifically, this study aims to identify and prioritize adaptive design attributes and explore whether age, gender, and disability type are associated with variations in clothing preference evaluations. Utilizing a refined Kano model integrated with Better-Worse coefficients and sensitivity analysis, this quantitative research evaluated 30 adaptive design attributes based on structured survey data from 214 respondents. Exploratory two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was conducted to examine potential demographic interaction patterns associated with clothing preference evaluations. The results reveal that physiological comfort and accessible donning mechanics constitute baseline priorities at the overall-sample level, while exploratory interaction analyses suggest variations in preference evaluations across demographic subgroups. Exploratory analyses indicated four interaction patterns involving evaluations of specific garment attributes, including personalized design, Velcro fasteners, close-fitting silhouettes, and abrasion resistance. Ultimately, the findings indicate that adaptive lower garment requirements combine overall attribute-level priorities with subgroup-specific variations across age, gender, and disability type. This study provides a quantitative basis for differentiated prioritization of adaptive clothing design attributes while highlighting the potential value of accounting for demographic heterogeneity in design decision-making.

title: Toward AI-Augmented Applied Systems: Emerging AI and LLM Directions Across Trajectory Prediction, Cybersecurity, and Engineering Automation
abstract: This paper reviews fifteen recent publications (2015-2026) spanning trajectory prediction, cybersecurity and trust management, classical machine learning and algorithmic optimisation, and engineering automation, and asks a forward-looking question: where is artificial intelligence — particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), foundation models, and agentic AI systems — positioned to extend each of these research directions next? For each of four thematic clusters we first summarise the current method documented in the reviewed sources, then discuss a concrete, currently-emerging AI direction grounded in recent (2025-2026) literature: LLM- and foundation-model-based trajectory reasoning for Cluster A; agentic, LLM-driven security-operations copilots for Cluster B, including a reported 6.5x improvement in malicious-alert identification over human analysts in one production deployment; learned and graph-neural-network-based approaches to the classical optimisation and graph-isomorphism problems in Cluster C; and natural-language-to-workflow agentic automation for the low-code and embedded-systems work in Cluster D. Throughout, we explicitly separate what the reviewed papers themselves established from this review's own forward-looking analysis, and close with a discussion of the reliability, interpretability, and adversarial-robustness risks that accompany each proposed direction.
journal: International Journal of Computer and Organization Trends

title: Agent AI Zarządzający Siecią Open RAN Zorientowana na Użytkownika
abstract: Jednym z najważniejszych wyzwań związanych z implementacją sieci Open RAN o architekturze zorientowanej na użytkownika jest odpowiednie formowanie tzw. klastrów obsługujących. Problem ten może być efektywnie rozwiązany za pomocą zaproponowanego Agenta AI bazującego na modelu językowym. Wyniki symulacji pokazały, że zaproponowane rozwiązanie pozwala na ponad 2-krotne zwiększenie mediany rozkładu przepływności użytkowników względem standardowej architektury zorientowanej na sieć.

title: ПРІОРИТИЗАЦІЯ РЕМОНТУ ТЕПЛОВОЇ ІЗОЛЯЦІЇ ЕНЕРГЕТИЧНОГО ОБЛАДНАННЯ ТЕЦ НА ОСНОВІ ОЦІНКИ ТЕПЛОВТРАТ
abstract: Aim. Substantiation and development of a mathematical apparatus for prioritizing repairs of thermal insulation coatings of power equipment of thermal power plants in conditions of strict limitation of financial resources of the enterprise. Methodology. The study is based on the use of quantitative infrared thermography methods for remote measurement of temperature fields and local heat losses on protective metal casings. Contact thermometry is used to calibrate thermal imaging equipment and determine the real degree of blackness of surfaces. Mathematical modeling of convective-radiative heat transfer was implemented using classical criterion equations of heat transfer. Statistical processing of experimental data was carried out using the least squares method and assessment of the adequacy of the developed models. Results. Experimental data on actual temperature fields and heat losses on steam pipes of sharp steam, turbine cylinders and heat exchangers of thermal power plants were obtained. Local excesses of the design standard indicators of heat loss from one point sixty-three hundredths to five point seventy- five hundredths were recorded. An integral index of the technical condition of thermal insulation was constructed, which combines temperature deviations from the safe limit, specific energy losses and the degree of physical demolition of the structure into a single scale from zero to one. Defects were categorized by the degree of urgency for repairs with the allocation of critical areas, where the index exceeds zero by seventy-five hundredths. Scientific novelty. For the first time, an integral criterion for assessing the condition of industrial thermal insulation was proposed and mathematically described, which comprehensively takes into account thermographic parameters, energy losses and the visual and physical condition of the protective coating. A system of differentiated weight coefficients for different temperature groups of equipment was substantiated, which allows taking into account the destruction of exergy in high-temperature circuits. A mathematical algorithm for automatic ranking of repair work was developed. Practical significance. The implementation of the proposed methodology allows generating companies to rationally distribute a limited repair budget by first eliminating the most critical defects with a quick payback period. This ensures a reduction in fuel consumption, a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions into the atmosphere, and an increase in the overall efficiency of thermal power plants without the need for a complete renewal of the insulation ball of all equipment.

title: Constructing Cosmological Meaning in Q.S. Al-Anbiyā’ [21]: 30
abstract: Studies of Q.S. Al-Anbiyā’ [21]: 30 have largely focused on correspondences between the Qur’anic concepts of ratq (joining or closure) and fatq (opening or separation) and modern cosmological theories, especially the Big Bang, while the linguistic and cognitive processes through which cosmological meaning is constructed remain less examined. This study analyzes the construction of cosmological meaning in Q.S. Al-Anbiyā’ [21]: 30 by integrating al-Jurjānī’s contextual semantics with Lakoff and Johnson’s Conceptual Metaphor Theory. Using qualitative library research, the study employs a two-stage integrative procedure. First, naẓm analysis identifies the syntactic and semantic relations that constrain the ratq–fatq construction. Second, Johnson’s Conceptual Metaphor Theory maps only those textually licensed relations into source–target conceptual structures, after which the cognitive interpretation is checked against the Arabic linguistic structure. The findings show that the ratq–fatq relation forms a transformational semantic pattern from unity to differentiation. This pattern is conceptualized through three interconnected metaphors: The cosmos is a unified entity, creation is separation, and divine creation is cosmic transformation. The study proposes a Semantic-Cognitive Integrative Model in which naẓm provides textual constraints for conceptual mapping, while Johnson’s Conceptual Metaphor Theory explains how those relations are cognitively represented. Accordingly, the relationship between the verse and Big Bang cosmology is understood as limited conceptual correspondence rather than empirical scientific validation. The model offers a controlled interdisciplinary framework for analyzing Qur’anic cosmological meaning.

title: From Engineered Features to Foundation Models: A Decade of Teaching Machines to See, Told Through One Research Path
abstract: Many of the questions computer vision asked in 2017 are still being asked today. Can a machine understand a scene the way a person does? Can it find a tumor in a tissue sample? Can it tell who someone is from the way they move or read? The core questions are familiar, but the way we answer them has changed almost completely, and in the process some of the questions have grown. This paper tells that story through one line of research that started in the era of hand-built features and early deep networks and continues into the era of foundation models and AI agents. We walk through what we built then, what we build now, and what changed in between. We describe six shifts in plain terms: where a model's knowledge comes from, how much labeled data it needs, how it handles context, how it combines different kinds of signals, how it is adapted to a new task, and what it finally produces. We close with the questions that did not go away, and that matter more now than before.

title: Disparities in Digital Information Access in Indian Agriculture
abstract: Agricultural success hinges on the timely access to and application of precise information, which is critical for informed decision-making and sustainable outcomes. Traditional extension systems often struggle to meet the diverse and dynamic information needs of India’s vast farming population. While digital technologies are increasingly recognized as transformative tools for agricultural extension, systematic state-level evidence on the enabling digital infrastructure remains limited, particularly from a supply-side perspective. This study addresses this gap by developing a novel Digital Extension Service Preparedness Index (DESPI), a composite state-level index that captures the supply-side readiness of digital infrastructure for agricultural extension in India. The index is constructed by integrating multiple secondary datasets spanning household digital asset ownership, network connectivity, and electricity access from diverse national and industry sources that have not previously been combined for this purpose. Using Principal Component Analysis, these indicators are aggregated into a multidimensional measure of digital preparedness. The analysis reveals substantial inter-state disparities, with network access emerging as the most uneven and constraining dimension of digital infrastructure. By explicitly focusing on infrastructure availability and access rather than actual usage or outcomes, the study provides a foundational assessment of the structural conditions necessary for scaling digital extension services. The findings highlight the uneven geography of digital infrastructure and offer indicative insights into the conditions that may influence the reach of digital agricultural extension. The study provides an evidence base to inform more context-specific and targeted policy considerations for strengthening digital infrastructure, while recognizing that infrastructure alone is insufficient to ensure effective adoption or outcomes.

title: The Locality Gap: Bell-Inequality Audits for Covert Coordination Between Ostensibly Isolated AI Agents
abstract: Einstein’s “spooky action at a distance” names a correlation that no local mechanism can produce. This article turns that observation into an audit instrument for artificial intelligence. Two AI agents that share training data, weights or random seeds but cannot communicate are local systems in Bell’s sense, so their behaviour in a Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt (CHSH) game is bounded by S ≤ 2 whatever their architecture; a significant excess identifies a covert channel without modelling the agents. The instrument is tested in three computational experiments with known ground truth. First, 135 trained pairs of neural agents (three widths, three latent dimensions, two objectives) never exceed the bound (maximum S = 2.0000), including pairs trained to imitate the correlations of an entangled singlet. Second, opening a one-bit channel with probability p moves the learned CHSH value onto the theoretical optimum 2 + 2 p (mean absolute deviation 0.0016 across 220 runs); any leak below p ≈ 0.414 produces values indistinguishable in S from quantum entanglement. Third, as a finite-sample test the audit keeps its nominal size against honest but strongly correlated agents (rejection 4.4% and 4.3%), whereas a conventional dependence test flags the same agents in 100.0% of audits; detecting a 5% leak with 80% power needs about 7,375 rounds and a 1% leak about 185,120. The decisive weakness lies with the auditor: with predictable settings (a low-order bit of a linear congruential generator, a fixed rotation or a reused seed), agents with zero communication reach S ≈ 4 and trigger false alarms in 100% of audits, while cryptographic and freshly seeded generators restore the nominal error rate. The bridge to algorithmic collusion and multi-agent AI governance is stated as a formal analogy and a hypothesis for field testing, not as a finding about deployed systems. title: Realized annual price dispersion, trading activity, and contemporaneous price returns on the Amman Stock Exchange
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines how realized annual price dispersion and trading activity co-moved with 2025 price returns in the cross-section of Amman Stock Exchange (ASE) equities. The official yearly sector bulletin contains 160 valid securities; transparent activity and data-validity filters yield a 142-stock baseline sample. Cross-sectional OLS models use HC3 standard errors and are complemented by broad-sector controls, outlier-resistant estimation, alternative range scaling, sample sensitivity, signed range decomposition, and a manual corporate-action audit of extreme observations. The annual high-low range is strongly positively associated with same-year price return: its baseline coefficient is 0.883 (HC3 SE = 0.075). Scaling the range by average price leaves the coefficient positive but reduces R2 from .729 to .307. Decomposing the previous-close-scaled range produces an upside coefficient of 0.806 (SE = 0.071) and a downside coefficient of –0.630 (0.187), with equality strongly rejected (Wald χ2 = 72.61, p < .001). The extreme-observation audit identifies official 2025 capital reductions for PHNX, OFTC, NAQL, and DAFI. Excluding these four securities leaves the unsigned range coefficient positive at 0.850 (0.082; N = 138); the signed coefficients remain 0.792 (0.062) and –0.653 (0.186), respectively. Because return and range are constructed from the same annual price path, these results document robust contemporaneous directional co-movement rather than an ex-ante risk premium, causal liquidity effect, or forecasting relation.AcknowledgmentsThe author thanks the Amman Stock Exchange for making public yearly trading bulletins available. Any remaining errors are the responsibility of the author.

title: From Regulatory Vacuum to Socially Shaped Governance: A Responsibility-Gap Model of Facial Recognition
abstract: Facial recognition has transformed unchanging physical characteristics into instruments of economic and governmental power, but regulation has not kept pace with deployment; thus, enterprises are resorting to superficial ethical behavior. We believe that strategic underinvestment is an inevitable consequence of structural regulatory lag, not a moral failure by individuals, and dispersed social actors can help to address this problem. A delayed stock-flow system is employed to construct an ethical signalling game and a polycentric detection framework with correlated nodes for the construction of a formal responsibility-gap model. We apply theory-guided process tracing to the first facial recognition lawsuit in China (2019-2021) and, in conjunction with a five-regime fuzzy-set comparison, use a reproducible open dataset. We have built a socially constructed path of governance, and litigation, media dissemination, judicial decisions and legislative codification are all non-Western regulatory systems. The first is to extend the scope of ethics-washing to include the omission of under-investment, and the second is to differentiate between an institutional responsibility gap and a traditional epistemic gap.

title: Evidence-oriented managerial decision-making for digital transformation of business processes in agricultural enterprises
