The perceived impact of extreme weather events on care for people with HIV or tuberculosis and HIV in Zimbabwe: a survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study and formative evaluation.
abstract: BACKGROUND The growing threat to health systems posed by extreme weather events (EWEs) disproportionately affects people living with HIV and tuberculosis disease in high-burden, low-resource settings. In Zimbabwe, for example, the 2023-24 El Niño-induced drought intensified food insecurity and reduced access to clinics and medication for such vulnerable populations. We aimed to conduct a formative evaluation to assess the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery and identify potential climate-adaptive health-service strategies. METHODS In this survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study with a formative evaluation supplemented by qualitative data, we surveyed people living with HIV from Sept 19 to Dec 19, 2024, across 321 clinics in Zimbabwe to describe their perceived impact of EWEs on their health. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. The inclusion criteria were being diagnosed with HIV, being older than 18 years, and receiving HIV care at Organization for Public Health Interventions and Development (OPHID) clinics during the study period. Individuals who were not receiving HIV care at an OPHID clinic or who were younger than 18 years were excluded. A client satisfaction survey was used to collect data from in-person surveys. The survey included questions related to the general effects of EWEs, such as drought, extreme heat, and flooding; how EWEs had affected HIV or tuberculosis care; and what, if any, services were currently available or should be made available to mitigate climate impacts on health. We also conducted six focus group discussions (FGDs; five to eight participants per group) between March 12 and May 12, 2024, across the Bulilima, Mangwe, and Matobo districts. We used a convenience sampling approach to select patients who had visited the health facility for medical check-ups, medication resupply, or viral load testing, as recorded in clinical registers and verified by clinical staff. Eligible participants for the FGDs were adults (≥18 years) with HIV, or with current or previous tuberculosis treatment, receiving care at the study facility during the recruitment period; those under 18 years or not receiving care at the facility were excluded. Participants' sex was self-reported at enrolment. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, whereas FGD data were analysed using a modified framework approach. The main outcomes were the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery outcomes, as reported by affected communities, and community-prioritised mitigation strategies to feasibly address climate-sensitive determinants and barriers to care. FINDINGS Among 1804 eligible participants approached across 15 districts, all completed the survey and were included in the analysis. Most survey participants (1363 [75·6%] of 1804 participants) reported noticing changes in climate over the past 5 years; of these 1363 participants, 900 (66·0%) were female and 1024 (75·1%) participants reported disruptions to their HIV care during the time they noticed changes in climate. Survey respondents reported that climate-related disruptions were associated with increased food insecurity (reported by 877 [85·6%] of 1024 participants) and water shortage (667 [65·1%] of 1024 participants). Qualitative analysis confirmed that the barriers to HIV and tuberculosis care from EWEs included widespread food insecurity, crop failures, and livestock deaths, with consequent effects on income leading to challenges in paying for food and transportation to clinics. Participants highlighted the need for expanded services that facilitate social and economic wellbeing, including nutrition support, water access, transportation, and income-generating activities, and decentralised models of health-care delivery. INTERPRETATION Extreme heat and drought affect food and water security and have financial implications, creating challenges for patients to access care in Zimbabwe. Our findings underscore the urgent need for integrated, climate-adaptive strategies to maintain HIV and tuberculosis care in such climate-vulnerable regions. FUNDING Nina Ireland Program in Lung Health.

title: 660 nm LED preconditioning programs mitochondrial signaling in BMSCs for functional tracheal cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Stem-cell-based cartilage regeneration is limited not only by cell delivery, but also by the difficulty of establishing a stable and functionally competent regenerative cell state before implantation. Here, we report a photonic mitochondrial programming strategy in which 660 nm light-emitting diode (LED) irradiation preconditions bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) to enhance functional tracheal cartilage regeneration. BMSCs were seeded onto egg white-derived ring-shaped porous scaffolds and exposed to defined 660 nm LED irradiation before implantation. Among the tested irradiation conditions, 15 J/cm2 optimally promoted BMSC proliferation, chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic and matrix-degrading phenotypes. Mechanistically, 660 nm LED irradiation enhanced cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production and respiratory function, accompanied by moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling. This mitochondrial bioenergetic-redox response activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR/GSK3β-SOX9 axis, thereby promoting type II collagen, aggrecan and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix formation. Pharmacological inhibition of ROS signaling, mitochondrial activity, PI3K or mTOR attenuated the LED-induced chondrogenic program. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage ring defect model, 15 J/cm2-preconditioned BMSC-scaffold constructs improved cartilage-like tissue formation, airway epithelial repair, lumen patency and mechanical support after 30 days of observation. These findings support 660 nm LED irradiation as a controllable mitochondrial preconditioning strategy for stem-cell-based functional cartilage regeneration.

title: A CNN-based mapping approach for aeolian dunes in Arctic Sweden
Considering counterfactual prediction models in sleep research: A demonstration of incident stroke prediction in an observational cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Data-driven risk prediction algorithms are increasingly common. However, studies suggesting that a single set of variables are most "important" within a given risk prediction model ignore the reality that other equally useful models containing entirely different features may exist. We aim to use a novel approach (Model Path Selection) to demonstrate that, for any given health outcome, there are likely many comparable counterfactual models including different sets of variables. We focus on incident stroke as a scientifically meaningful outcome to motivate this demonstration. METHODS Model Path Selection uses an iterative model-building procedure to illustrate a set of counterfactual prediction models ("paths"). We applied Model Path Selection to Sleep Heart Health Study data (N = 4,512 adults) to predict 5-year incident stroke, considering 30 features comprising demographics, self-reported and measured medical risk factors, polysomnography, and self-reported sleep. Area Under the Curve was estimated for each resulting path based on 10-fold cross-validation. RESULTS Model Path Selection identified 61 unique counterfactual models. 13 of these achieved Area Under the Curves between 0.81 and 0.82. Area Under the Curves of the remaining models ranged from 0.53 to 0.68 (median 0.61). All 13 top models included age plus various combinations of other features (polysomnography indices, body mass index, and/or the Short Form 36 mental and physical component scores). CONCLUSIONS Model Path Selection can illuminate counterfactual prediction models, differentiate features that may be uniquely predictive from those that can be swapped out with other features, enhance reproducibility, inform the design of clinically practical predictive tools, and suggest sleep-related risk factors to be targeted for health promotion.

title: Firm-level effects of AI attention on wages and productivity: A global comparative study
Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Combined With Regional Division for Differentiating Benign and Metastatic Lymph Nodes.
abstract: OBJECTIVE Ultrasound Localization Microscopy (ULM) enables high-resolution visualization of lymph node microvasculature. However, most previous studies rely on whole-node analysis, which may overlook spatial heterogeneity and be affected by confounding factors. This prospective single-center study aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of ULM combined with regional analysis for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes. METHODS A total of 104 lymph nodes from patients with sonographically suspicious lymph nodes were included. All lymph nodes underwent ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy, which served as the reference standard for classification (benign or metastatic). Each lymph node was divided into central, peripheral, and global regions, and ULM quantitative parameters were extracted. Regional ratio features were calculated. Feature selection was performed using univariate analysis, LASSO regression, and backward stepwise logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using 10-fold stratified cross-validation, 2000 bootstrap resamples, decision curve analysis (DCA), and clinical impact curve (CIC). RESULTS Three diagnostic models were constructed: a conventional ultrasound (US) model, a ULM model, and a combined US-ULM model. The combined model demonstrated the best discriminative performance with an AUC of 0.866 (95% CI: 0.7875-0.9320), followed by the ULM model (AUC = 0.833, 95% CI: 0.7464-0.9108) and the US model (AUC = 0.730, 95% CI: 0.6219-0.8285). In multivariable analysis, SD.Density_C_P (OR =0.0578, p = 0.012), FD_C_P (OR = 0.8847 per 0.01 increase, p = 0.003), and peripheral vascular pattern (OR = 10.9501, p < 0.001) were identified as significant predictors of lymph node metastasis. At optimal cut-off values, the combined model achieved a sensitivity of 0.733 and specificity of 0.915. CONCLUSION The proposed region-based ULM model combined with conventional ultrasound provides an improved quantitative approach for differentiating benign and metastatic lymph nodes in patients with sonographically suspicious lymphadenopathy.

title: Contrasting Impacts on Plant Endogenous Metabolic Pathways from Trace Organic Contaminants Relevant to Recycled Water
abstract: Plant uptake and metabolism of contaminants from recycled water raise concerns regarding exposure through crops but may also cause plant endogenous metabolic network perturbation. In this work, we investigated impacts on endogenous metabolic pathways of Brassicaceae model plant Arabidopsis thaliana following hydroponic exposure for 48 h to anticorrosive benzotriazole (BT) or antimicrobial benzoisothiazolinone (BIT) at 200 μg/L and 2 mg/L, trace organic contaminants relevant to recycled water. We observed ∼99.9% uptake of both compounds and 13–25% lower plant biomass in exposed plants compared to no-exposure control plants. Despite the similar uptake and effect on biomass, plant metabolomics revealed that BT exposure significantly impacted the tryptophan metabolism through downregulation of indole metabolites and upregulation of kynurenic acid, indicating altered tryptophan utilization. Conversely, BIT exposure impacted antioxidant defense and oxidative stress signaling pathways through downregulation of flavonoids and upregulation of jasmonic acid. Even within shared impacted pathways such as phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, BT exposure shifted the main pathway toward benzoic acid derivatives, whereas BIT exposure shifted the pathway toward antioxidant defense-related compounds (e.g., flavonoids, sinapic acid). These findings demonstrate that structurally similar contaminants can cause distinct pathway-level metabolic shifts, highlighting the importance of evaluating biological impacts of specific trace organic contaminant uptake in crops relevant to recycled water irrigation.

title: Spatial Charge Separation in Porphyrin Metal-Organic Frameworks Enables Bifunctional Sites for Overall Water Splitting.
abstract: Solar-driven overall water splitting provides a route for converting solar energy into chemical fuels, but its realization in porphyrin-based metal-organic frameworks (PMOFs) is limited by the difficulty of coupling reduction and oxidation chemistry within a single framework. Herein, first-principles calculations reveal a spatial separation of the frontier electronic states in two-dimensional M-Cu PMOFs (M = transition metal): the conduction-band edge is predominantly associated with the Cu2(COO)4 paddle-wheel node, whereas the valence-band edge is mainly localized on the porphyrin linker. Combined with site-resolved reaction thermodynamics, this electronic partitioning predicts spatially distinct regions for the hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction. Systematic screening of 27 M-Cu PMOFs identifies Rh-Cu PMOF as the only candidate satisfying the adopted thermodynamic criteria for both half-reactions, with an idealized upper-bound solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 15.31% under the adopted spectral model. Sure independence screening and sparsifying operator (SISSO) analysis further identifies total magnetic moment, electronegativity, group number, and d-electron count as physically interpretable descriptors of property variations within this M-Cu PMOF series. These results highlight cooperative linker-node electronic regulation as a computational design principle for porphyrin-based frameworks with spatially differentiated redox functions.

title: Oncogenic mutations in non-small cell lung cancer: from molecular mechanisms to clinical practice
abstract: Targeted therapy has revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients harboring oncogenic alterations, and next-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) significantly increase blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, leading to improved disease control and survival benefits. However, several issues remain to be addressed, including the selection of more appropriate and individualized agents, the emergence of TKI resistance, and the challenging management of central nervous system (CNS) progression. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the efficacy and safety of TKIs and targeted specific antibodies in advanced or metastatic patients with common or rare mutations, providing guidance in selecting the optimal agent. We further explore the mechanisms underlying drug resistance and regimens aimed at overcoming resistance. In nonmetastatic resectable or unresectable NSCLC, we discuss the therapeutic potential of targeted agents and current issues requiring further research. In addition, we distinguish current and potential therapeutic strategies for patients with baseline brain metastasis (BM) and those without baseline BM who subsequently develop brain progression, leading to more effective and personalized treatment. Finally, we provide perspectives on challenges and future directions in the identification and treatment of oncogenic alterations, particularly in the context of co-mutations and the heterogeneous nature of metastases, and emphasize the clinical importance of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted genetic testing and biomarker development.

title: Dysregulated thymus-ovary axis promotes virtual memory T cell polarization to aggravate PMOS pathology.
Molecular predictors of minimal residual disease in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with quadruplet therapy.
abstract: Quadruplet therapy, combining anti-CD38 antibodies, immunomodulatory drugs, proteasome inhibitors and dexamethasone, is now the standard induction treatment for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM). However, treatment response is heterogeneous and molecular predictors are needed to guide early therapeutic decisions. We performed integrated genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of 423 tumor samples from patients with NDMM from the MIDAS cohort to characterize molecular heterogeneity and its association with measurable residual disease (MRD) after quadruplet induction with isatuximab, carfilzomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Isa-KRd). Postinduction MRD-negativity rates varied significantly across gene expression subtypes, with HP1/HP3 and MS groups showing superior responses compared to the MF and CD2 subtypes. B cell differentiation was associated with MRD positivity, while proliferation and MYC programs were associated with MRD negativity. These MRD-associated transcriptomic features were independently validated in the CASSIOPEIA cohort. Whole-genome sequencing revealed both known (APOBEC mutagenesis, chromothripsis) and new genomic instability phenotypes validated in the MMRF cohort. New driver alterations were identified with independent validation across three external cohorts with multiple myeloma (MMRF, MANHATTAN and CASSIOPEIA; 1,451 cases). Genomic instability features and driver genes such as CCND1 and MYC correlated with differential MRD outcomes. DNA methylation profiling identified nine MRD-linked subgroups distinguished by the extent of hypomethylation in quiescent chromatin and cis/trans signatures of driver translocations. A multimodal random forest model integrating genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic features predicted MRD status after induction, with an area under the curve of 0.77, outperforming clinical and genomic models, while providing comparable discrimination and improved calibration relative to the transcriptomic and epigenomic models. These findings define a multiomic classification of NDMM linked to Isa-KRd response. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04934475 .

title: Trace-IN625 a source aware literature derived dataset of tensile properties and microstructure for additively manufactured IN625
abstract: Additively manufactured IN625 superalloy has been widely studied, but evidence linking processing history, microstructure and tensile response remains dispersed across publications. We present Trace-IN625, a source-traceable, literature-derived dataset assembled from 305 papers. The dataset contains 482 specimen or source condition records, 149 tensile property records from 72 publications, 2206 microstructure and figure evidence records and 280 figure crops with source attribution. The tensile layer includes 120 IN625 records and 29 records for IN625-containing composite, graded or joined materials. Stable identifiers and page, figure, table and panel-level locators connect processing conditions, reported properties and published characterization evidence. Technical validation integrated AI assisted cross checking and manual review with verification of process condition classifications and measurement definitions, as well as relational consistency and file integrity checks. The image layer represents published figures and descriptors rather than instrument-native characterization data. Trace-IN625 supports source-aware property retrieval, condition-specific literature comparisons and inspection of published microstructural evidence.

title: Comparative drying kinetics and quality analysis of dried tomatoes through improving air distribution in a bin-type solar dryer versus conventional systems
abstract: Tomato is considered among widely consumed horticulture crops which provide essential nutrients and antioxidants to the human body. Being perishable crop, tomatoes require to dry for preservation. Solar drying provides a facility to dry the perishable crops efficiently and at low cost. These dryers are categorized for their efficiency and drying mechanism. In this study a Bin type solar dryer (BSD) with improved air distribution system was compared in terms of quality of dried product, moisture removal rate, thermal efficiency and techno-economic analysis with tray type solar dryer (TSD) and conventional type solar dryer (CSD). Three air velocities V 1 (1.5 ms −1 ), V 2 (2.5 ms −1 ), V 3 ((3.5 ms −1 ), and three different slice thickness S 1 (3 mm), S 2 (5 mm) and S 3 (7 mm) were selected for evaluation. Page model, Henderson and Pabi model, Modified Henderson and Pabi model, Midili-Kucuk model, Logarithm model and Approximate Diffusion Model were selected to study the kinetics of drying process in three drying systems. The moisture content of tomato slices was reduced from 89.63 to 9.95%. The results revealed with higher drying rate tomato slices dried in BSD had higher color changes than TSD and CSD. BSD exhibited better drying performance than TSD and CSD. Slice thickness directly affected the drying performance as with increase of slice thickness, drying rate was reduced. At optimum velocity (V 2 ), BSD took 10–12 h, TSD took 14–16, and CSD took 16–18 h to dry the tomato slices depending upon thickness. BSD, TSD and CSD had 19.17, 16.83 and 15.42% thermal efficiency respectively which support the improvement in design for better drying results. The specific energy consumption was 1.86, 2.12 and 2.31 kWh/kg water for BSD, TSD and CSD respectively. With four model parameters, Midili-Kucuk model had better fit with experimental data than other models with R 2 of 0.9998, χ 2 of 0.0002 and RMSE of 0.0048. The techno-economic analysis proves the economic feasibility of BSD with higher drying capacity and lower drying time with payback period of 1.10 years. BSD offers a sustainable and economically viable solution for small-scale farmers. Future integration of AI and thermal storage could further enhance drying efficiency, reducing postharvest losses and improving food security.

title: Bioactive ELP-coated scaffolds enhance cell-material interactions and support osteogenic differentiation.
abstract: Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) scaffolds are widely utilized in tissue engineering for their biodegradability and mechanical robustness; however, their inherent hydrophobicity and bioinert nature often result in poor initial cell attachment, a critical bottleneck for stable tissue integration. In this study, we developed a modular dual-layer surface functionalization strategy that combines a poly-L-lysine (PLL) electrostatic priming layer with a recombinant elastin-like polypeptide featuring RGD and YIGSR motifs (RY-ELP). The sequential PLL/RY-ELP coating significantly enhanced surface wettability without compromising the scaffold's interconnected porous architecture. This bioactive interface supported robust early adhesion and survival of both HEK293 cells (as a model for weak adherence) and human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). Mechanistically, this enhanced interaction was accompanied by the rapid activation of focal adhesion-related signaling pathways, including FAK, paxillin, and ERK, alongside the upregulated expression of integrin β1 and vinculin. Beyond initial survival, the PLL/RY-ELP coating effectively promoted the osteogenic differentiation of hDPSCs, as evidenced by increased osteogenic marker expression (RUNX2, COL1A1, ALPL, SP7, and BGLAP) and superior matrix mineralization. These findings demonstrate that combining electrostatic priming with sequence-defined bioactive motifs offers a versatile and effective approach to overcome the biological limitations of PLGA scaffolds for regenerative medicine.

title: Scattering-based detection of fungal spores on a photonic integrated platform: an ASCA-assisted proof-of-concept study
abstract: Airborne fungal pathogens, such as Penicillium expansum, pose a severe threat to post-harvest crop preservation and food safety, demanding rapid and reliable detection methods. This study presents a photonic integrated sensing platform, based on Ge-Se-Te RIB optical waveguides, as a proof-of-concept for the discrimination of fungal spores under controlled laboratory conditions in the short-wave infrared (SWIR) range. To evaluate the performance of the sensor over a comprehensive 45-day experimental campaign, Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations were combined with advanced chemometric analysis. FEM modeling confirmed the evanescent field interaction with micrometer-sized spores on the waveguide surface. To extract the subtle biological signal resulting from high-density spore deposition from dominant system drifts and environmental noise, ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis (ASCA) was applied to the multidimensional spectral data. ASCA successfully isolated the specific variance related to spore deposition, even though it accounted for only 0.2% of the global variance. These results highlight the potential of combining chalcogenide waveguide technologies with ASCA-driven analytics for scattering-based, label-free bio-sensing applications, paving the way toward future quantitative and species-selective developments in the mid-wave infrared (MWIR).

title: yancc: A GPU-accelerated, differentiable solver for neoclassical transport in tokamaks and stellarators
abstract: We present yancc, a new GPU-accelerated solver for the drift kineticequation that computes neoclassical transport fluxes, flows, and currents intokamaks and stellarators. The drift kinetic equation is challenging to solvenumerically due to strong advection-dominance, recirculating flows, internalboundary layers, severe anisotropy, and high dimensionality. Fast and accuratesolutions to the drift kinetic equation are required for high fidelity optimization,profile prediction, and analysis of experiments with uncertainty quantification.yancc solves both the full four-dimensional drift kinetic equation (retainingspeed-dependent collisions, energy scattering, and full interspeciescoupling), and the reduced monoenergetic form. The discretization combines aMaxwell polynomial collocation grid in speed with finite differences in pitch angleand the flux surface coordinates, using a modified upwind stencil designed toimprove diagonal dominance for multigrid efficiency. The resulting linearsystem is solved with a multigrid-preconditioned Krylov method. Built in JAX,yancc is fully differentiable, enabling gradient-based optimization andadjoint sensitivity analysis. Benchmarks against MONKES and SFINCS showagreement within 1\% across a range of collisionalities, geometries, andmulti-species configurations. yancc achieves roughly an order of magnitudespeedup over SFINCS on a per-scan basis while using an order of magnitude lessmemory, with runtime remaining nearly flat across the full range ofcollisionality.

Corrigendum: Scaffold-free bioprinted osteogenic and chondrogenic systems to model osteochondral physiology (2019 Biomed. Mater. 14 065010.
abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinted culture platforms mimic the native microenvironment of tissues more accurately than two-dimensional cell cultures or animal models. Scaffold-free bioprinting eliminates many complications associated with traditional scaffold-dependent printing as well as provides better cell-to-cell interactions and long-term functionality. In this study, constructs were produced from bone marrow derived mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) using a scaffold-free bioprinter. These constructs were cultured in either osteogenic, chondrogenic, a 50:50 mixture of osteogenic and chondrogenic ('osteo-chondro), or BM-MSC growth medium. Osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiation capacity was determined over an 8-week culture period using histological and immunohistochemical staining and RT-qPCR (Phase I). After 6 weeks in culture, individual osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiated constructs were adhered to create a bone-cartilage interaction model. Adhered differentiated constructs were cultured for an additional 8 weeks in either chondrogenic or osteo-chondro medium to evaluate sustainability of lineage specification and transdifferentiation potential (Phase II). Constructs cultured in their respective osteogenic and/or chondrogenic medium differentiated directly into bone (model of intramembranous ossification) or cartilage. Positive histological and immunohistochemical staining for bone or cartilage identification was shown after 4 and 8 weeks in culture. Expression of osteogenesis and chondrogenesis associated genes increased between weeks 2 and 6. Adhered individual osteogenic and chondrogenic differentiated constructs sustained their differentiated phenotype when cultured in chondrogenic medium. However, adhered individual chondrogenic differentiated constructs cultured in osteo-chondro medium were converted to bone (model of metaplastic transformation). These bioprinted models of bone-cartilage interaction, intramembranous ossification, and metaplastic transformation of cartilage into bone offer a useful and promising approach for bone and cartilage tissue engineering research. Specifically, these models can be potentially used as functional tissue systems for studying osteochondral defect repair, drug discovery and response, and many other potential applications. .

title: DNA-BFN: Bayesian Flow Networks for Generative Modeling of Regulatory DNA Sequences.
abstract: MOTIVATION Designing regulatory DNA sequences is challenging due to their discrete nucleotide alphabet and complex higher-order dependencies underlying regulatory function. Many existing generative models, particularly diffusion-based approaches, learn by injecting stochastic noise into sequences and training denoising processes, which can distort discrete sequence structure and weaken biological constraints. RESULTS Here, we introduce DNA Bayesian Flow Networks (DNA-BFN), a generative framework that models regulatory DNA sequences through iterative Bayesian updates of per-position nucleotide distributions. By directly modeling per-position categorical beliefs, DNA-BFN realizes a diffusion-like generative process without explicitly perturbing discrete nucleotide sequences, enabling fully differentiable training while preserving discrete sequence structure. Across eight regulatory sequence datasets spanning diverse species, scales, and sequence lengths, DNA-BFN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, faithfully preserves sequence feature statistics and regulatory patterns, enables few-shot sequence design, and achieves faster sampling efficiency. These results show that framing sequence generation as progressive uncertainty reduction in probability space provides an effective and generalizable approach for nucleotide sequence design. AVAILABILITY The software and its source code are publicly available at https://github.com/WangLabTHU/DNA-BFN. The dataset, source code and model weights are available in the Zenodo repository: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20177972. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

title: Niclosamide Suppresses Osteoclastogenesis and Bone Resorption: Involvement of STAT3 Signaling
abstract: Niclosamide, known for its anticancer and anti-inflammatory effects via modulation of NF-κB and STAT3 signaling, has now been shown to suppress osteoclast differentiation and function through STAT3 inhibition. In vitro experiments demonstrated that niclosamide downregulates STAT3 activation, leading to reduced expression of genes involved in osteoclast differentiation, acid secretion, chemotaxis, and pyroptosis, thereby impairing multiple osteoclast biological behaviors. In vivo, niclosamide treatment attenuated bone loss in an ovariectomy-induced mouse model of osteoporosis by inhibiting osteoclast activity. The STAT3 activator colivelin partially reversed these niclosamide-induced effects on bone metabolism. Collectively, niclosamide inhibits both osteoclast formation and the bone-resorptive function of mature osteoclasts via suppression of the STAT3 pathway, suggesting a novel therapeutic approach for osteoporosis.

title: Strange attractors: purpose, synchronicity, flow, and the neurodynamics of meaning
abstract: This paper proposes a neurodynamic framework for meaningful experience, grounded in the recursive alignment of brain dynamics across time. We argue that the meaningful experiences known as “purpose”, “synchronicity”, and “flow” are not distinct phenomena, but temporal expressions of the same underlying process: metastable coherence in the brain’s attractor landscape. Synchronicity marks transient realignments across representational levels; flow reflects the low-entropy navigation of emergent structures; and purpose encodes long-term integration into causal agency of a self-model. Drawing on active inference, dynamical systems theory, and recent work on predictive processing and memory consolidation, we formalize these states as trajectories through phase-space—differentiated by temporal depth, stability, and precision-weighting. We offer empirical predictions for each regime, linking neural signatures such as sharp-wave ripples, P300b activity, and network coherence to experiential markers of meaning. We also propose a developmental interpretation informed by Robert Kegan’s subject–object theory, framing purpose as an evolving attractor shaped through recursive narrative and identity updating. This model suggests that meaning is not only symbolic or semantic, but dynamic, embodied, and experimentally testable: a measurable function of the brain’s capacity to coordinate across nested timescales.

title: MRI-Based Machine Learning to Differentiate True Progression from Pseudoprogression in Glioblastoma: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Differentiating true progression (TP) from pseudoprogression (PsP) after chemoradiation for glioblastoma remains clinically difficult. We evaluated externally validated diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based machine learning models and appraised study quality and transparency. METHODS PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library were searched through October 1, 2025 (PROSPERO registration CRD420251144894). Eligible adult glioblastoma studies used MRI-based machine learning to distinguish TP from PsP against histopathology and/or clinicoradiologic follow-up. The primary meta-analysis included external test cohorts with extractable 2 × 2 data; internal and combined internal and external test analyses were secondary. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized with bivariate random-effects models. RESULTS Thirty-one studies including 2,344 patients undergoing imaging assessment were included. Seven external test cohorts, including 219 patient observations, entered the primary meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63-0.88), specificity was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.63-0.84), and summary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.81 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.69-0.91). Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Risk of bias was frequently high or unclear, and reporting transparency was heterogeneous. CONCLUSIONS MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation.

title: Trade Liberalization under Climate Pressure: A Recursive Dynamic CGE Analysis of Ethiopia
abstract: This paper assesses whether regional trade integration under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) can mitigate the economic and distributional impacts of climate-induced agricultural productivity losses in Ethiopia. A recursive dynamic Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) model is applied, incorporating crop-specific yield projections under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 climate scenarios alongside tariff reductions and trade facilitation reforms. Results show that AfCFTA generates modest but sustained gains: real GDP increases by 0.21–0.55 per cent by 2035, with gains of over 5 per cent relative to the initial level over the 2021–2035 projection period, while private consumption rises by 0.42–0.75 per cent and imports expand by 1.80 per cent. Sectoral outcomes indicate a climate-constrained structural transformation, with manufacturing and services expanding while the agriculture sector contracts, as the sector hardest hit by climate change. Trade liberalization accelerates labor reallocation toward less climate-sensitive sectors, boosting employment among unskilled and semi-skilled workers and progressively affecting welfare, with the poorest rural households experiencing the largest gains in consumption. Despite these benefits, AfCFTA only partially offsets climate impacts. Our findings highlight that trade integration can support resilience, food security, and structural change when complemented by targeted climate adaptation and industrial policies.

title: Navigating intentions: exploring the cognitive and environmental drivers of productive and destructive entrepreneurial intentions
abstract: This study aims to understand how entrepreneurial effort is allocated by differentiating between productive and destructive pathways. It examines how cognitive drivers (attitudes, subjective norms and perceived behavioral control) and environmental valuations (trust-based networks and status incentives) interact to steer entrepreneurship students toward value-creating or value-destructive entrepreneurial intentions in an emerging economy marked by institutional complexity. Building on an integrated framework that synthesizes the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) with institutional and social capital theories, we developed and tested a dual-pathway structural model. We collected data from 783 entrepreneurship students across nine Iranian universities. We used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling to test two separate models for productive and destructive entrepreneurial intentions. Core TPB relationships were supported for both pathways, but critical asymmetries emerged. Closeness valuation significantly strengthened attitudes toward productive entrepreneurship but did not influence the destructive pathway. Social valuation played a dual role: promoting productive intentions by strengthening perceived control and norms, while also inhibiting destructive intentions. Formal testing of comparative hypotheses revealed that attitude and subjective norms were significantly stronger drivers of destructive intention, while perceived behavioral control was more influential for productive intention. The study unpacks entrepreneurial intention into distinct ethical pathways, introducing a dual-pathway model specifying how identical environmental factors produce opposing effects depending on a venture's ethical valence. It provides rare empirical evidence from Iran's understudied entrepreneurial ecosystem and demonstrates how institutional voids shape intention pathways. The findings offer actionable guidance for educators and policymakers designing entrepreneurship education interventions that cultivate productive entrepreneurship while mitigating destructive practices in emerging economies.

title: Corporate ethical and responsible AI (CERAi) and AI trustworthiness: a lifecycle perspective and empirical insights
abstract: This study develops and empirically validates a Corporate Ethical and Responsible AI (CERAi) lifecycle framework. The framework comprises three interdependent stages: design and development, testing and training, and deployment and usage. The study aims to move the research beyond abstract principles and policy analyses toward empirically grounded, lifecycle-integrated artificial intelligence AI governance theory. It positions ethical AI and responsible AI governance as the two constitutive components of the CERAi construct, and AI trustworthiness as a conceptually and empirically distinct downstream outcome anchored in stage-specific organizational governance mechanisms. The CERAi framework is scoped broadly to encompass governance of both conventional/traditional machine learning models and autonomous AI agents operating within organizational settings. We administered a large-scale survey to 500 attendees at a national AI conference in the United States in early 2026, yielding 143 useable responses from AI professionals across healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, retail and energy sectors. We developed and validated multi-item scales for each CERAi lifecycle stage using established ethical AI and AI governance frameworks. Structural equation modeling was employed to assess the measurement model and to test both direct path hypotheses and mediation hypotheses. Both CERAIi design and development and CERAi deployment and usage have significant positive direct effects on AI trustworthiness, whereas CERAi testing and training do not. Our results also indicate a significant serial mediation pathway in which CERAi deployment and usage enhance AI trustworthiness through testing and training, followed by design and development. Conversely, testing and training alone do not mediate the relationship between deployment and usage and AI trustworthiness, indicating that design-stage ethics serve as an intervening (mediating) mechanism through which governance activity enacted at later lifecycle stages is associated with perceived AI trustworthiness. This is consistent with testing and training's association with trustworthiness operating indirectly, mediated by the ethical architecture established during the design and development stage. Findings of this study demonstrate that AI trustworthiness reflects differentiated perceived salience across AI lifecycle stages, whereby stakeholders appear to weight visible, deployment-stage governance more heavily than upstream design and testing stage governance in forming trustworthiness judgments, rather than reflecting a definitive validation that governance effects accumulate uniformly across all stages in isolation. This study makes a distinctive contribution by providing empirical evidence for a governance-sequencing mechanism, whereby design-stage ethics function as a mediating pathway shaping the effectiveness of governance activity at later lifecycle stages. To the best of our knowledge, such a mediated, stage-sequential mechanism has not previously been demonstrated using primary data within a comprehensive, three-stage CERAi lifecycle framework linking organizational ethical and responsible governance practices to AI trustworthiness outcomes.

title: Beyond usefulness: cognitive and emotional correlates of AI use intentions among HR professionals
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming human resource management (HRM), yet the cognitive and psychological factors associated with human resource (HR) professionals’ intentions to use AI remain incompletely understood. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and appraisal perspectives, this study examines the relative associations of Cognitive Evaluation, AI-Use Anxiety, AI-Related Job Insecurity, organizational AI use across HR functions, and AI Knowledge with behavioral intention to use AI. It also explores whether AI Knowledge moderates these relationships. Survey data were collected from 285 HR professionals. Confirmatory factor analyses assessed the measurement structure of the study constructs, followed by hierarchical moderated regression analyses examining their unique associations with behavioral intention and the exploratory moderating role of AI Knowledge. Cognitive Evaluation, reflecting perceived usefulness and ease of use, showed the strongest unique association with behavioral intention to use AI. AI-Use Anxiety demonstrated a smaller negative association, whereas AI-Related Job Insecurity, AI Use Across HR Functions, and AI Knowledge did not explain significant unique variance once the competing predictors were considered simultaneously. The comprehensive model explained 66.8% of the variance in behavioral intention. The exploratory interaction analyses provided no clear evidence that AI Knowledge systematically moderated the relationships examined. Organizations implementing AI in HR should address both employees’ evaluations of the technology and apprehension surrounding its use. Implementation strategies should demonstrate the practical usefulness and usability of AI through role-specific examples, hands-on training, and opportunities to experiment with AI tools in realistic HR contexts. Organizations should also recognize AI-use anxiety as a distinct potential barrier by providing accessible support, low-risk opportunities for familiarization, and clear communication throughout implementation. These strategies may help create conditions that support employees’ willingness to use AI. This study extends research on AI use intentions by examining cognitive, emotional, knowledge-related, and organizational-exposure factors simultaneously rather than in isolation. The findings show that HR professionals’ intentions to use AI are most strongly associated with evaluations of its usefulness and usability, while AI-use anxiety represents a smaller but distinct negative correlate. By distinguishing AI-use anxiety from AI-related job insecurity and individual AI knowledge from organizational AI exposure, the study provides a more differentiated account of the factors associated with HR professionals’ intentions to use AI.

title: The dynamics of knowledge transfer and retention in entrepreneurial education: a conceptual exploration of enabling technologies
abstract: This conceptual paper aims to examine Entrepreneurial Education (EE) in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) through a Knowledge Management (KM) lens. It explains how enabling technology affordances, when aligned with the characteristics of entrepreneurial knowledge, shape Knowledge Transfer (KT) and Knowledge Retention (KR) under conditions of cognitive bias. It clarifies how KM processes support durable entrepreneurial capability development. The study adopts a theory-driven conceptual methodology. Drawing on KM process theory and conceptual theory-building guidance, the paper develops a mechanism-based framework through six stages: problematisation, theoretical anchoring, construct selection, mechanism mapping, model integration and proposition development. The framework positions KT and KR as the analytical core, enabling technologies as differentiated KM affordances, and cognitive bias as an embedded condition that can distort knowledge interpretation, transfer, retention and reuse. The framework proposes that enabling technologies can strengthen KT and KR when their affordances align with the knowledge’s tacitness, codifiability and contextual dependence, and are supported by interaction, reflection, curation and governance routines. Immersive/simulation, AI/analytics and collaborative/process technologies support KT/KR mechanisms. Cognitive bias can weaken or distort knowledge transfer, retention and reuse, whereas bias-aware routines and cohort-to-cohort feedback can improve knowledge fidelity, programme memory and entrepreneurial capability development. The paper advances a KM-centred reframing of EE by positioning KT and KR as the focal mechanisms linking enabling technologies to durable entrepreneurial capability development. It differentiates technologies by their KM affordances and integrates cognitive bias, boundary conditions and programme-level feedback within a single conceptual architecture, offering testable propositions and design principles for technology-enabled EE.

title: Machine Learning-Based Screening for Osteonecrosis of the Jaw in Panoramic Radiographs.
abstract: BACKGROUND Osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ) is a serious condition associated mainly with antiresorptive therapy and maxillofacial radiotherapy. As detection of its radiographic findings may facilitate patient referral, this study aimed to develop convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for ONJ screening in panoramic radiographs (OPGs). METHODS A dataset of 888 ONJ-positive OPGs and 888 ONJ-negative controls was assembled and annotated using bounding boxes. The dataset was split at patient level 70-10-20 for training, validation, and testing. Multiple CNNs (ResNet18, ResNet34, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0) were trained on cropped image regions and evaluated using standard performance metrics. Performance on full OPGs (without cropping) was tested, and subgroup analysis was performed. Regions contributing to model predictions were visualised using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). RESULTS EfficientNet-B0 performed best, with per-crop accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score of 92.24%, 89.80%, 94.69%, 94.42% and 82.05%, respectively. At 0.9 probability threshold, per-image accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score equalled 76.65%. Grad-CAM highlighted clinically relevant regions; however, differentiation from other changes in bone density was suboptimal. CONCLUSIONS Despite promising results at crop level, model performance in full OPG analysis is currently insufficient for clinical application. Further optimisation of localisation strategies and external validation are needed for reliable clinical application.

title: Carbon Accumulation in Tropical Dry Forests and Savannas Despite Widespread Land‐Cover Change, Revealed by Radar Remote Sensing
abstract: Accurate mapping of woody biomass and its temporal change is critical for understanding the global carbon balance, informing restoration and supporting evidence‐based policy on climate mitigation and livelihoods. The vegetation of the dry tropics, comprised largely of dry forests and savannas, holds substantial woody carbon stocks, but both stocks and change over time remain uncertain. Where Earth Observation (EO) data have been used to estimate change over time, different products give conflicting results on the direction, magnitude and location of change. We present pan‐dry‐tropical maps of aboveground carbon density (AGCD) and AGCD change at 100 m resolution for the years 2015–2024, developed using ALOS ScanSAR satellite radar observations calibrated with in situ measurements ( n = 237). These maps suggest an aboveground woody carbon pool (AGC) in the dry tropics of 25.3 2.0 PgC, ~13.0% of global AGC. Net AGC has increased by 0.43 0.07 PgC yr −1 , ~20.0% of the global net land sink. The overall net increase (0.43 PgC yr −1 ) is comprised of gross losses from deforestation and degradation (0.27 0.05 PgC yr −1 ) and gains due to densification and extensification of 0.59 0.1 PgC yr −1 , with the balance accounted for by small changes (change < 20% of AGCD; 0.11 PgC yr −1 ). Losses are equally split between degradation and deforestation, while gains are divided roughly 2:1 between the densification of woody ecosystems and expansion into previously grass‐dominated areas. These new maps, created with a dry‐tropics‐specific EO method, highlight the importance of tropical dry forests and savannas in the global carbon cycle. The prominent role of degradation‐related losses suggests that climate change mitigation will need to focus much more on reducing losses from overharvesting than at present. The widespread increases in carbon density and the increase in tree biomass into open systems present major challenges for biodiversity conservation, restoration and livelihoods.

title: Thermal Generalism Shapes Tolerance to Extreme Heatwaves in Estuarine Fishes
abstract: Climate change is widely expected to push many taxa beyond their biological limits, yet some populations persist in environments that routinely experience climatic extremes. This raises a fundamental question: does their thermal tolerance reflect species‐level thermal generalism (an evolved capacity to maintain performance across a broad thermal range) or population‐specific acclimation to local conditions (phenotypic plasticity)? Distinguishing between these alternatives is key for predicting whether tolerance to climatic extremes will generalise across species distributions or remain restricted to heat‐tolerant populations. To test these competing hypotheses, we quantified physiological performance (at cellular and organismal levels) in three economically important estuarine fish ( Acanthopagrus australis , Sillago ciliata and Rhabdosargus sarba ) collected from 20 sites across 15 estuaries along a ~1000‐km latitudinal gradient spanning their core and poleward range edges. Sites differed in thermal variability, including some that intermittently exceeded the severest end‐of‐century climate projections. We then experimentally exposed two of the fish species from low and high thermal variability sites to moderate (+2°C, 14 days) or extreme (+4°C, 7 days) simulated marine heatwave events, assessing 12 physiological and behavioural proxies. All three species collected in situ maintained comparable physiological performance across sites of contrasting thermal variability. Both experimental species, each collected from a single high‐ and low‐variability site, tolerated heatwave conditions regardless of thermal history or heatwave intensity, supporting species‐level thermal generalism rather than population‐specific acclimation. In the absence of heatwave conditions, S. ciliata from high‐variability sites also showed steeper allometric scaling and faster growth at 26 versus 24°C experimental control temperatures, suggesting this species may benefit from the warmer baseline temperatures projected under gradual climate change. Combined, our findings support thermal generalism as the primary driver of tolerance in estuarine fishes to climatic extremes, with important implications for the fisheries they support under climate change.

title: Peptide Signalling as a Control Layer for Signal Prioritisation in Plant Stress Networks.
abstract: Plants in the field rarely encounter single stresses, and simultaneous stresses impose conflicting physiological demands that cannot be satisfied at once. Responses to such combinations are frequently non-additive and cannot be predicted from single-stress responses, a result that crosstalk models struggle to accommodate because they describe which pathways interact without specifying which prevails. This review proposes that peptide signalling functions as a control layer governing signal prioritisation. Under this hypothesis, secreted peptides act above the shared modules of cytosolic calcium, reactive oxygen species, and mitogen-activated protein kinase cascades, and determine which competing input is permitted to dominate their behaviour. Evidence for this proposal spans several peptide families. CEP, CLE and RALF signalling illustrate systemic demand signalling, developmental stabilisation, and receptor complex reorganisation respectively, and the same logic extends to PEP, IDA and PSK signalling across immune, developmental, and drought contexts. Combined drought and nitrogen limitation, resolved through ABA and CEP, provides a worked case in which a global signal sets operating boundaries within which a local signal refines the response, supported by evidence now extending from Arabidopsis into cereals. We derive falsifiable predictions tested against hormone-pathway negative controls and graded drought intensities rather than single treatments, which allows loss of prioritisation to be distinguished from general signalling fragility. We also identify a trade-off constraining crop application, since enhancing peptide-mediated nutrient foraging may reduce drought resilience. Substantial gaps remain in detecting peptide signals directly and in ranking peptide families under field conditions. Reframing plant signalling as a decision system rather than an input-output relay offers a testable foundation for improving stress resilience and nutrient use efficiency in crop breeding.

title: PREDICTIVE MODELING OF RICE GERMINATION SENSITIVITY TO SALINITY USING LITERATURE-DERIVED DATA
abstract: Soil salinity remained a major constraint on crop establishment, and rice (Oryza sativa L.) was recognized as particularly sensitive during germination. The present study aimed to quantify the concentration-dependent response of rice germination to NaCl stress using a literature-derived dataset and regression-based modeling. Published data on rice germination under different NaCl concentrations were compiled from peer-reviewed studies identified through Google Scholar. Germination percentage was used as the primary response variable, and linear regression as well as polynomial regression models of degree 2 and degree 3 were implemented in Python using the scikit-learn library. The compiled dataset showed uneven representation across salinity treatments, with concentrations of 75, 125, and 150 mM being reported more requently than several low and intermediate–high levels. Overall, germination declined with increasing NaCl concentration, although moderate-range variability was observed in the aggregated data. Regression analysis showed that all models captured the general negative trend, while their predictive behavior differed according to the evaluation metric. The second-degree polynomial model produced lower mean absolute error, whereas linear-type models showed stronger performance for error variance-related metrics in the current dataset. The study demonstrated that regression-based approaches were useful for integrating fragmented salinity experiments and for approximating the germination response of rice across tested and intermediate NaCl levels.

title: Modeling yield and carbon emissions in a wheat-maize rotation system on saline-alkaline soils using the DNDC model
abstract: This study investigated a winter wheat-summer maize rotation system on moderately saline-alkali farmland in Huanghua City, Hebei Province, China (0-20 cm soil layer: total salt content 2.1-3.5 g kg-1, pH 8.6-9.2). Through three years of empirical field data, we parameterized and validated the DNDC model to quantify the effects of alternative management strategies on crop yield and greenhouse gas (N2O, and CO2) dynamics in saline-alkali soils. The DNDC model demonstrated excellent performance in simulating crop yield and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across four management scenarios with high R2 (⪆ 0.80, P ⪅ 0.01) and low NRMSE ( ⪅ 5%). The optimized strategy (S3), combining controlled-release fertilizer, organic fertilizer, and CDSI (controlled drainage and sub-irrigation) technology, achieved the highest yields: 1207 kg C ha-1 for winter wheat and 740 kg C ha-1 for summer maize, representing 54.5% and 65.9% increases over the baseline (BAU), respectively. Our findings show that integrated management (e.g., using controlled- release fertilizer, organic amendments, and drip irrigation) can simultaneously enhance productivity and reduce emissions in saline-alkali wheat-maize systems.
journal: Seventh International Conference on Green Energy, Environment, and Sustainable Development (GEESD 2026)

title: Teaching Novice Computing and Programming in the Agentic AI Era
abstract: AI programming agents have profoundly disrupted computing education. Rather than treating this as a threat, we argue that it is an opportunity to refocus early curricula. We introduce the “flaky compiler” metaphor to frame what AI programming enables and what it demands of its users. We argue that introductory computing courses can and must become early software-engineering courses, with the objective of teaching students to take responsibility for the work they produce with AI. This induces the need for—indeed, demands—research into how to rethink teaching program specification. Introductory computing courses must, and can, become early software-engineering courses, and the metaphor of the “flaky compiler” offers guidance in how to structure learning.

title: Delegating Ourselves Away: Preserve Human Voice and Choice in Next-Generation Digital Systems
abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping the framing of equity and inclusion in information systems research. The editorial opens with an urgent call for a conversation about inclusion and equity in the age of agentic AI, given concerns that humans are increasingly removed from knowledge work in human-AI interactions. It then reflects on the digital systems research presented at HICSS over the past 60 years and explains how a new permanent research track has been established to focus on equitable and inclusive digital systems in society and institutions. The editorial outlines what agentic AI is changing, the equity and inclusion risks that follow, and the urgent research agenda this track is uniquely positioned to lead. It ends with a summary of the five papers published in this special issue, which advance our knowledge of equitable and inclusive digital systems from diverse perspectives, and calls for scholars and scientists in the research communities to pay attention to the profound socio-technical paradigm shift driven by the transition from traditional AI to generative AI and to agentic AI.
journal: ACM SIGMIS Database: the DATABASE for Advances in Information Systems

title: Amortized Neural Filtering for Calibrated Posteriors in Statistical Arbitrage
abstract: Statistical arbitrage trades on an estimate of the state of a residual spread, and conventional practice discards the uncertainty of that estimate. We keep the uncertainty and use it in the trading decision. A Neural Filter Estimator (NFE) is trained on simulated paths of a mean-reverting process whose innovation law is selected by testing candidates against real residuals; once trained, it returns the posterior over the latent state of every spread in a cross-section in one forward pass. Three results follow. On simulated paths with known truth, every practical estimator, ours included, falls in one narrow band of accuracy well below an estimator given full information, so the posterior gains no accuracy over a point estimate; its contribution is a correct account of its own uncertainty. On Korean equities, net of costs, the conventional point estimate forecasts about a thousand basis points per holding period more than it realizes, and the amortized methods cut that gap by a factor of roughly two to eight. Sizing positions from the posterior on the same learned factors as the end-to-end Attention Factor Model matches the Sharpe ratio of those factors under the base rule within the period's noise, at no more risk.

title: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Emergent Market Impact in Generative Limit Order Book Models
abstract: Realistic market impact is essential for generative limit order book (LOB) models to serve as world models for trading agents. If a simulator misprices this mechanism, agents learn policies that are optimal in the simulator but wrong in the real market. Existing metrics assess generated streams purely through distributional comparison with historical data, leaving counterfactual response to an agent's own orders largely unexplored. Here, we show that market impact emerges naturally in neural LOB generators trained solely for next-token prediction. We inject execution-style metaorders into the generated message flow of five autoregressive models across five NASDAQ stocks and measure the response using estimators from the empirical impact literature, validated on baselines whose physics is known in advance. Our benchmark evaluates any message-level generator in three phases: free generation (reading order-flow persistence against price diffusivity); metaorder injection (yielding the impact law's exponent and amplitude); and a post-execution window (measuring relaxation). In addition, comparing each visible injection to a blind, simulator-only control isolates the model's learned response from standard book mechanics. For every model on every stock, we measure how the impact responds as a function of cumulative metaorder participation. Interestingly, we observe emergent impact in generative models of market data, with exponents in the range of 0.63 to 1.21, slightly above the traditional 0.5 of the square-root law of impact. In the family of models tested, we are so far unable to observe impact decay during relaxation. We tentatively attribute this to the still-short context windows of the models. We release the benchmark as open source to validate future generative models for market data.

title: Application of ALADIN model outputs for solid precipitation forecasting and detection
abstract: Meteorological services face a major challenge in providing reliable snowfall forecasts and detecting solid precipitation, as precise data is needed for weather warnings, damage assessments, hydrological modeling, and many other tasks. This study evaluates the skill of the ALADIN numerical weather prediction model in solid precipitation forecasting at 126 stations of the Czech Hydrometeorological Institute (CHMI) between August 2019 and July 2025. Model performance was assessed against quality-controlled human present weather observations using common verification metrics, including the Probability of Detection (POD), False Alarm Ratio (FAR), Critical Success Index (CSI), and Heidke Skill Score (HSS). Further, the ALADIN_SN weighted index of solid precipitation occurrence was assimilated from ALADIN snow forecasts in hourly intervals using two sets of empirical lead-time-dependent weights. During the snow season, ALADIN_SN showed a mean POD of 0.68, FAR of 0.48, and HSS of 0.53, with an overall accuracy exceeding 83% at all stations. Air temperature is the most important variable affecting the model performance, with better results at temperatures below approximately +2°C. The skill of ALADIN_SN also improved with increasing solid precipitation intensity and duration. Case studies demonstrated that ALADIN_SN successfully captured large-scale snowfall events associated with synoptic systems but struggled with localized or short-lived precipitation and phase transitions at temperatures above freezing, and it often overestimated the spatial extent of solid precipitation zones. Overall, the ALADIN_SN parameter provides a spatially consistent, computationally efficient, and operationally feasible method for identifying solid precipitation occurrence, suitable for supplementing networks of automated measurement systems and human weather observers.
