title: Evaluation of the gates foundation agricultural development strategy in Bihar (2007-2025)
abstract: This evaluation assessed the Gates Foundation’s Agricultural Development Strategy in Bihar, India from 2007 to 2025 and found that the portfolio made its strongest contributions by strengthening government systems, scaling proven agricultural innovations, and improving delivery platforms, while impacts on markets, women’s economic empowerment, and farmer outcomes varied by investment model and sustainability pathway. The evaluation examined how AgDev investments contributed to changes in Bihar’s agricultural policy environment, public-sector capacity, delivery systems, innovation uptake, market development, women’s economic empowerment, and small-scale producer outcomes. It also assessed the portfolio’s return on investment and identified strategic lessons for future agricultural development investments in Bihar and similar contexts. The evaluation used a mixed-methods design combining portfolio-level contribution analysis, investment-level evidence review, secondary quantitative analysis, and ROI modeling. The analysis traced how individual investments and the broader portfolio contributed to systems-level change, farmer-facing outcomes, scale, and sustainability. Quantitative methods included difference-in-differences and synthetic control analyses using secondary datasets, alongside investment-level ROI estimates drawing on available impact evidence and modeled benefit streams. Data sources included more than 130 program documents, independent and implementer-led evaluations, key informant interviews with implementers and stakeholders, focus group discussions, secondary administrative and survey datasets, and published literature. The evaluation drew on qualitative evidence to interpret mechanisms of change, institutionalization, implementation constraints, and the durability of outcomes after grant support ended. The evaluation found that AgDev’s most durable contributions came through investments that embedded new capabilities into government systems, public planning processes, extension platforms, and delivery institutions. The strongest evidence of farmer-level effects was concentrated in improved input use and staple crop productivity, particularly where investments supported proven technologies and practices through existing systems. Market and women’s economic empowerment investments generated important examples of progress, especially in livestock, fisheries, and women-led producer organizations, but results were more dependent on business model viability, recurrent financing, institutional ownership, and the ability to sustain capacity after external technical assistance ended. This evaluation was commissioned under EVITA (Evaluating Inclusive Transformation in Agriculture), which generates evidence on the outcomes and impacts of investments made by the Agricultural Development Team (AgDev) at the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and aims to increase the efficiency of and maximize collective learning from AgDev's evaluations.

title: Eco-Friendly Contrast Agents and Sustainable Radiology: A Pharmacy-Integrated Review of Science, Technology, and Environmental Stewardship
abstract: The growing need for environmentally friendly pharmaceutical processes, especially in the creation and application of imaging agents, has been brought to light by the rising need for diagnostic imaging. This study integrates ideas from pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD), environmental pharmacology, green chemistry, and biotechnology to examine recent developments in environmentally friendly biopharmaceutical approaches for medical imaging. Despite their clinical efficacy, conventional iodinated and gadolinium-based contrast agents cause environmental contamination due to their persistence, insufficient clearance of wastewater, and creation of hazardous transformation products. Promising options with less of an impact on the environment include hydroxypyridinone (HOPO)-based ligands, biodegradable chelators, and green synthesis methods. The article goes on to address how nanotechnology is used in sustainable imaging, Biotechnology innovations including plant cell culture, fermentation-based production, and AI-assisted manufacturing are emphasized as ecologically friendly and scalable production methods. An important method for assessing the environmental impact of imaging agents throughout the course of their lifecycle is life cycle assessment, or LCA. title: Assessment of the efficiency of resource potential utilization in the agricultural sector of the economy under investment and innovation development
abstract: Ukraine’s agricultural sector is undergoing transformation under the influence of wartime challenges, economic restructuring, European integration, digitalization, and the growing need for sustainable resource management. Improving the efficiency of resource potential utilization has become a prerequisite for strengthening the competitiveness and sustainability of agricultural enterprises. The purpose of this study is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the efficiency of resource potential utilization in the agricultural sector of the economy under investment and innovation development and to substantiate organizational and economic measures for its improvement. The research is based on a systems approach using economic-statistical, comparative, analytical, economic-mathematical, graphical, forecasting, and composite assessment methods. The empirical analysis covers agricultural enterprises in the Poltava region during 2015–2025. Resource potential utilization efficiency was comprehensively assessed by integrating economic, investment, innovation, environmental, and managerial indicators. The results show that technological modernization, digital transformation, investment activity, and strategic management are the principal drivers of efficient resource utilization and sustainable enterprise development. An integrated organizational and economic model for resource potential development is proposed, combining precision agriculture, digital monitoring, resource-saving technologies, and human capital development. Forecasting confirms the positive impact of the proposed measures on labour productivity, capital productivity, profitability, investment activity, digitalization, and the integrated indicator of resource utilization efficiency. The scientific novelty lies in improving a comprehensive methodological approach to assessing the efficiency of resource potential utilization in the agricultural sector of the economy through integrating economic, investment, innovation, environmental, and managerial components. The practical significance lies in applying the proposed approach to strategic planning for agricultural enterprise development, investment decision-making, and improving resource management efficiency.
journal: Scientific Messenger of LNU of Veterinary Medicine and Biotechnologies

title: ADAPTIVE GOVERNANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BIOSECURITY
abstract: The article examines artificial intelligence as a dual-use technology in the field of biological security and substantiates directions for the adaptive regulation of public administration in this sphere. Its relevance stems from the fact that the integration of AI into biological research is expanding the possibilities of epidemiological monitoring and crisis management while simultaneously generating new categories of risk associated with a lowered threshold of entry for dangerous manipulations of biological agents. For Ukraine, the problem is particularly acute under conditions of war and the course towards European integration, while the current regulatory framework, as of 2026, does not take AI-related risks into account. It is established that the governance gap is a multi-level phenomenon that manifests differently at the operational, scientific-technological, and institutional levels, requiring a differentiated rather than a uniform response – from procedural adaptation to the formation of accountability mechanisms. An original functional classification of the manifestations of AI’s dual nature is proposed, together with a system of criteria for assessing the readiness of international (EU, USA) and national governance systems, which reveals a gap configuration specific to Ukraine – technological readiness outpacing managerial capacity. The scientific novelty lies in substantiating an original conceptual model of the adaptive governance of AI in biosecurity that integrates the source of risk, the institutional challenge, the adaptation mechanism, and the managerial outcome into a coherent construct. The practical significance lies in identifying directions for integrating AI governance instruments already available in Ukraine into the biosecurity system.

title: Differentiable Optics with dLux II: Optical Design Maximising Fisher Information
abstract: The design of astronomical hardware operating at the diffraction limit requires optimisation of physical optical simulations of the instrument with respect to desired figures of merit, such as photometric or astrometric precision. System design entails many parameters some of which may entangle the fidelity of science observables with strongly nonlinear dependencies upon instrument properties. Here we present a differentiable optical simulation framework dLux, a software library designed to construct optical models that are integrated with automatic differentiation. This approach enables the direct evaluation of gradients and higher-order derivatives through the forward model, facilitating statistically principled design and optimisation of instrument configurations. The methodology leverages numerically stable second- and higher-order derivatives to directly compute Fisher information and covariance forecasts, enabling efficient Bayesian experimental design targeted toward optimising abstracted figures of merit, such as the precision of parameters recovered through complex sets of operations. The method is validated against analytical results and applied to optimise the astrometric precision achievable with a parametrised telescope model and a diffractive pupil design relevant to exoplanet detection missions. To support reproducibility and facilitate methodological extension, we provide example implementations via open-source code on the Github sharing platform.

title: Blast.jl: Differentiable Non-Limber Power Spectra for Joint Clustering, Shear, and CMB lensing Analyses
abstract: Upcoming large-scale structure surveys require accurate theoretical predictions for angular power spectra on the largest angular scales, where the commonly used Limber approximation breaks down and multiple relativistic and observational effects become relevant. At the same time, modern cosmological analyses increasingly rely on gradient-based inference techniques, motivating the development of fast, fully differentiable algorithms. In this work, we present a major extension of Blast.jl, a numerical toolkit for the efficient computation of non-Limber angular power spectra. Building on the Chebyshev-polynomial decomposition of the original framework, the updated algorithm incorporates redshift-space distortions, magnification bias, primordial non-Gaussianity, intrinsic alignments, CMB lensing, and the integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect, while remaining fully differentiable through custom automatic differentiation rules. Despite the increased physical complexity, the algorithm retains favorable scaling by precomputing all cosmology-independent quantities. We validate the expanded framework against brute-force integration and established cosmological codes, and provide a detailed analysis of the trade-off between computational speed and precision as a function of the algorithm hyperparameters. We demonstrate the readiness of Blast.jl for gradient-based inference through a simulated likelihood analysis with LSST Y10-like mock data, recovering unbiased cosmological and nuisance parameter constraints from a 35-parameter model using gradient-based samplers.

title: Reforming Indonesia's Free Nutritious Meals Program Through A Comparative Legal Study
abstract: The Free Nutritious Meal (Makan Bergizi Gratis/MBG) programme, launched in January 2025, is one of Indonesia’s largest social-policy interventions, yet its legal foundation remains limited to presidential regulations without a dedicated statutory basis. This normative legal study employs comparative-law, statutory, and conceptual approaches to examine school feeding governance models across countries and their implications for reformulating MBG’s legal framework. The analysis integrates five legal concepts: legal certainty, competent authority, administrative accountability, regulatory governance, and a rights-based approach, supported by thirty-four peer-reviewed empirical articles from the Scopus database. The study identifies four legal governance models: (1) centralised-statutory, (2) decentralised regional-authority, (3) contract-based community–agriculture partnership, and (4) rights-based universal models. Six determinants consistently shape programme sustainability: regulatory strength and adaptability; clarity of authority and funding certainty; institutionalised multi-stakeholder participation; institutional capacity and labour-law protection; legality of local-agriculture integration; and administrative accountability mechanisms. The study’s principal contribution is a systematic comparative-legal typology of school feeding governance, reframing the sustainability of large-scale social programmes as a matter of legal architecture rather than administrative capacity alone. Applied to Indonesia, the typology demonstrates that establishing a dedicated MBG statute is necessary to construct the programme as a rights-based constitutional entitlement, harmonise inter-institutional authority, guarantee indexed funding, ensure preferential yet politicisation-proof procurement, extend labour-law protection to frontline personnel, and mandate multidimensional accountability. Such statutory reform represents not merely an elevation in normative hierarchy but a substantive legal transformation essential to MBG’s constitutional legitimacy and long-term sustainability.

title: STRATEGIC INNOVATIONS IN AGRICULTURAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP UNDER DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
abstract: The subject of the study is the methodological approaches, indicators, and practical cases of digitalisation of Ukrainian agribusiness, benchmarked against international standards. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that, under conditions of full-scale war, personnel shortages, and rising resource costs, digital solutions are being transformed from a factor of competitive advantage into an instrument of operational resilience for agricultural enterprises. The purpose of the article is to substantiate strategic directions of innovative agribusiness development based on methodologically differentiated indicators of various levels and to develop a conceptual model explaining the uneven character of digital transformation in Ukraine. The study relies on a comprehensive combination of analytical methods: systematisation and contextual analysis of scholarly sources; decomposition and three-level typification of indicators (macro-level innovation-environment indices, economy-wide benchmarks, and sector-specific indicators); comparative analysis of international and national statistical data; qualitative case-study analysis (EOS Data Analytics); and conceptual modelling. The study reveals a deterioration in Ukraine's position in the Global Innovation Index, from 45th (2020) to 66th place (2025), and a substantial lag in the domestic adoption of precision farming (approximately 30 % of surveyed enterprises, 52 % using RTK technologies) behind the indicators of large United States farms (70 %). An original Digital Polarisation Model of agricultural entrepreneurship under crisis conditions is substantiated, distinguishing three groups of enterprises – with high, fragmented, and initial digital maturity – according to their degree of adaptability and resilience to exogenous shocks. On this basis, three differentiated strategic directions of innovative development are substantiated – technological leadership, selective digitalisation, and basic digitalisation supported by the state – corresponding to enterprises' level of digital maturity, with directions for the model's further empirical verification outlined. The results obtained serve as an applied basis for the transition from unified measures to targeted state and donor support for the basic digital maturity of small and medium-sized agricultural producers, the formation of accelerator programmes, and the harmonisation of sectoral statistics.

title: A GB-SAR slope displacement interval prediction method based on FA-VAG feature transfer and an improved sparrow search algorithm
abstract: Slope displacement interval prediction quantifies uncertainty in future deformation and supports slope monitoring and early warning. This study extends the point-prediction FA-VAG backbone previously reported by Gan et al. rather than presenting that backbone as a new model. The new contribution is an interval-prediction layer that transfers the pretrained FA-VAG hidden states, reduces them by Principal Component Analysis (PCA), fuses them with multi-step point forecasts, and maps the fused representation to non-crossing bounds using a Random Vector Functional Link Network (RVFLN). A prior-informed improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (SG-ISSA) then optimizes the RVFLN output weights. For the prespecified target point 7, the framework achieved PICP/MPIW/CWC values of 0.90/5.97/5.97 for five-step prediction and 1.00/8.74/8.74 for seven-step prediction. Independent external validation yielded 0.90/58.82/58.82 for five-step prediction. These results support the interval-extension framework on the two evaluated datasets; additional probabilistic baselines and harmonized reruns of the ablation study remain necessary.

title: AGC-YOLO: adaptive gated channel network for rice leaf disease detection
abstract: Accurate detection of rice leaf diseases is critical for intelligent crop protection, yet class imbalance, degradation of multi-scale feature information, and the limited discriminative capability of feature fusion continue to hinder effective monitoring under field conditions. To address these challenges, this study presents AGC-YOLO, an improved detection model based on the YOLOv8s framework. First, a semantic-aware data augmentation network termed SAICP Net is devised to alleviate class imbalance and the scarcity of cross-class co-occurrence samples through a weakly supervised soft spatial prior and semantically constrained cross-category instance pasting. Second, a gated hybrid pooling module named GHP-SPPF is proposed to adaptively integrate max pooling and soft pooling via a learnable gating mechanism, thereby strengthening the discriminative representation of multi-scale lesions. Finally, a channel-adaptive fusion module termed CAFF is constructed to replace standard concatenation with channel-wise learnable weights and gated residual refinement, boosting the discriminative power of cross-scale feature fusion. Experimental results demonstrate that AGC-YOLO achieves an mAP@0.5 of 93.5 ± 0.6% on the rice disease dataset, representing a 3.0 percentage-point improvement over the baseline, and additional experiments on two public datasets further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for disease detection.

title: Artificial intelligence and its influence on student engagement in higher education
abstract: Empirical evidence on how artificial intelligence (AI) relates to student engagement in culturally diverse higher-education settings remains limited. In Chinese university classrooms, where interaction is often teacher-led and asking questions in class can carry a social cost, AI-driven dialogic tools may offer low-pressure opportunities for active participation. This study examined the association between an AI conversational agent (EduBot) and the behavioural, cognitive, emotional and agentic dimensions of engagement among Chinese undergraduates. A mixed-methods quasi-experimental design involved 555 students in four comprehensive (multi-disciplinary, research-intensive) universities, each contributing one introductory course taught in two parallel sections. Within a 15-week semester, intervention sections (n = 278) used EduBot, a Socratic-dialogue agent embedded in the learning management system, for 12 weeks; control sections (n = 277) used teaching-assistant-moderated forums. We measured engagement at three time points with a 21-item four-dimensional engagement scale adapted from an established measure and supplemented it with system logs, 30 student interviews and instructor focus groups. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for the nesting of students within course sections, together with mixed-design ANOVAs, showed Group × Time interactions for behavioural (η 2 p = 0.043, post-test d = 0.71), cognitive (η 2 p = 0.032, d = 0.55), agentic (η 2 p = 0.054, d = 0.57) and emotional engagement (η 2 p = 0.012, d = 0.34), all p ≤ 0.001 after Holm adjustment. Within the intervention group, the number of EduBot sessions predicted post-test engagement after adjustment for baseline scores and covariates. Exploratory moderation analyses indicated larger agentic gains among first-year students and larger cognitive gains among students with lower prior GPA. Thematic analysis identified three hypothesised mechanisms, namely a judgment-free interaction space, scaffolded persistence and temporal flexibility. A Socratic-scaffolded AI agent was associated with higher engagement, most clearly for agentic engagement, which participants described as constrained by classroom norms. The findings support culturally attentive AI design and suggest, tentatively, an equity-enhancing potential. Because the design compared an integrated AI package with usual practice across eight sections, the effects cannot be attributed to single design components.

title: The impact of digital technology on green economies
abstract: Digital agriculture is regarded as an important instrument for achieving green economies, with the potential to raise productivity while reducing environmental impacts. This study explores how digitalization in agriculture affects greenhouse gas emissions, pesticide use and productivity. The research uses a mixed-methods design. Quantitative analysis draws on international environmental and economic indicators for approximately 180 countries between 2000 and 2023 (415 country-year observations), combining Spearman correlations, regression models with GDP interaction terms, and K-means cluster analysis. A qualitative case study of digital agriculture in Latin America complements the statistical findings. Digital infrastructure is strongly associated with the adoption of agricultural digital technologies, and smart farming investment is associated with better economic performance of the agricultural sector. Investment in digital agriculture shows a positive association with both emissions and pesticide use, while the interaction with GDP is negative and significant. Cluster analysis confirms that countries with higher GDP and stronger digital infrastructure achieve more balanced environmental outcomes. The environmental benefits of digital agriculture are conditional on economic capacity. In economically advanced settings, digital technologies reduce resource use, waste and emissions; in economically constrained regions, higher output can offset the environmental gains. Digital agricultural transformation therefore offers opportunities for sustainable development, but its success depends on equitable access to digital technologies and on policy support that mitigates the trade-off between productivity and environmental protection.

title: Production dynamics, trade behavior and spatial market integration of sesamum in India
abstract: Sesamum ( Sesamum indicum L.), one of the oldest cultivated oilseed crops, occupies a significant place in Indian agriculture due to its rich oil content, nutritional benefits, and suitability to a wide range of agro-climatic environments. The crop is predominantly grown in states such as West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan, which contribute substantially to national production. Over the years, the acreage under sesamum has gradually contracted, reflecting changes in cropping patterns and production conditions; however, advances in yield performance have helped maintain production levels. An assessment of long-term production trends and market dynamics is crucial for designing strategies that support sustainable crop diversification, strengthen farmers’ livelihoods, and improve market efficiency through enhanced price transmission and integration across regions. This study analyzed the long-term performance of sesamum cultivation in India by examining changes in area, production, and productivity over the period 1980–81 to 2025–26. Wholesale price data from major sesamum-producing states were also utilized to investigate price movements and the extent of market integration. Growth performance and production dynamics were assessed using techniques such as Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), decomposition analysis, instability measures, seasonal indices, and correlation analysis. To examine the nature of price relationships across markets, econometric tools including the Augmented Dickey–Fuller (ADF) unit root test, Johansen co-integration test, Granger causality analysis, Vector Error Correction Model (VECM), impulse response analysis, and forecast error variance decomposition were employed. These methods facilitated an evaluation of both short-run and long-run price transmission mechanisms within the Indian sesamum market. The study revealed that the expansion of sesamum production in India has largely resulted from gains in crop productivity, even though the area under cultivation has shown a declining trend over time. Measures of instability indicated noticeable variations in cultivated area, output, and market prices across the major producing states. Seasonal analysis demonstrated clear price movements, with lower prices during harvest and peak market arrivals and higher prices during periods of limited supply. The presence of strong market linkages was confirmed through high correlations, significant long-run co-integration, and effective price transmission among markets. Causality analysis identified Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Telangana as key markets influencing price movements in other regions. Trade performance showed that India continues to hold an important position in global sesamum exports, while imports have also risen due to increasing domestic demand and periodic supply shortages. These findings emphasize the need to improve productivity, strengthen market integration, and enhance trade competitiveness to support the long-term development of the sesamum sector. Sustainable growth of the sesamum sector requires a strategic focus on enhancing productivity through the development and dissemination of improved, climate-resilient cultivars suited to diverse agro-ecological conditions. Strengthening post-harvest infrastructure, including storage, processing, and transportation facilities, will help minimize losses and improve product quality. Efficient market information services, wider adoption of digital marketing platforms such as e-NAM, and better market integration can enhance transparency and ensure remunerative prices for farmers. In view of the expanding domestic and international demand for sesame and value-added products, greater attention should be given to export promotion and value-chain strengthening. Furthermore, encouraging sesamum cultivation in rainfed and resource-constrained regions through appropriate policy support and market incentives can foster crop diversification, improve farm profitability, and contribute to sustainable agricultural development.

title: Mechanisms of Agricultural Digital Transformation: Evidence from News Media Sentiment and PVAR Analysis of Economic Data
abstract: To adapt to the rapid development of the agricultural economy, digital transformation of agriculture has become an inevitable trend. Media narratives and the sentiment conveyed through news coverage play an important role in shaping this process. This study explores how news influences agricultural activities as follows: first, analyzing news sentiment through the BERT model; second, identifying news focus topics via thematic research; and third, examining how news promotes agricultural economic development using the PVAR model. The findings indicate that news related to agriculture generally conveys a positive sentiment regarding digital transformation. In economically developed regions of China, news tends to emphasize industrial chain digitization and cold chain logistics, whereas in less-developed regions, it focuses more on infrastructure construction and the allocation of educational resources. Overall, news sentiment exerts a significant influence on the agricultural economy and infrastructure development therein. This study highlights the potential of leveraging news strategically to support the digital transformation of agriculture.

title: Weakly Supervised Leaf Disease Segmentation via Reinforcement Learning-Based Prompt Optimization for SAM
abstract: Accurate segmentation of leaf lesions is essential for crop disease monitoring and precision agriculture. However, most existing methods rely on pixel-level annotations, which are costly and difficult to obtain in real agricultural scenarios. Weakly supervised approaches alleviate this requirement but often suffer from incomplete lesion localization and background interference. In addition, recent foundation segmentation models demonstrate strong generalization ability, yet their performance heavily depends on prompt quality, which is difficult to design automatically. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a weakly supervised lesion segmentation framework that integrates probabilistic feature disentanglement and reinforcement learning-based prompt optimization. First, a probabilistic class activation mapping (CAM) is introduced to model lesion confidence and guide feature disentanglement, effectively suppressing background noise. Second, a dual-loss constraint is designed to improve pseudo-mask quality by enforcing both region consistency and structural regularity. Finally, a prompt optimization strategy is developed to automatically select informative prompts, enabling a foundation segmentation model to refine lesion boundaries without human interaction. Experimental results on multiple agricultural datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared with existing weakly supervised baselines. Specifically, the method achieves an mIoU of 45.6% and Dice score of 57.1% on apple leaf disease datasets. The results indicate that the proposed framework can effectively reduce annotation cost while providing reliable segmentation performance, indicating potential for practical agricultural applications.

title: Row Ratio in Faba Bean–Oat Intercropping Enhances System Productivity by Regulating Rhizosphere Bacterial Communities and Root Traits in the Qinghai Lake Region
abstract: The biological mechanisms through which faba bean–oat intercropping coordinates interspecific competition, belowground responses, and system productivity remain poorly understood in alpine environments. A field experiment was conducted in the alpine region surrounding Qinghai Lake, with six treatments comprising faba bean monoculture (F), oat monoculture (O), and four faba bean–oat intercropping patterns with row ratios of 1:1 (FO), 2:1 (F2O), 2:2 (F2O2), and 1:2 (FO2). Agronomic traits, root morphology, soil physicochemical properties, and rhizosphere bacterial communities were measured to clarify above- and below-ground coordinated responses of the two crops to varying row ratios. The 2:1 faba bean–oat intercropping yielded the optimal performance, with a land equivalent ratio of 1.479 and a 29.3% higher dry matter yield (6795.4 kg ha−1) than faba bean monoculture, as well as the highest system crude protein production. Dominant oat compensatory growth primarily boosted system productivity. Compared with the corresponding monocultures, the 2:1 intercropping treatment increased the total root length, root surface area, and root tip number of faba bean by 23.9%, 33.9%, and 54.3%, respectively, while increasing the total root length of oat by 110.3%. Under this treatment, soil alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen reached 167.17 mg kg−1, 39.9% higher than that under oat monoculture, whereas soil available phosphorus and catalase activity increased by 13.2% and 54.4%, respectively. Rhizosphere bacterial communities exhibited host-specific responses, with stronger treatment-associated differentiation in the oat rhizosphere and enrichment of Bacteroidia, Chitinophagales, and Chitinophagaceae under F2O. Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) further revealed crop-specific pathways linking row configuration, belowground properties, bacterial α-diversity, and crop performance. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the productivity advantage of faba bean–oat intercropping at a 2:1 row ratio is jointly mediated by competitive compensation of oat, enhanced root proliferation, improved soil nitrogen and phosphorus availability, and restructuring of rhizosphere bacterial communities.

title: UAV Monitoring of Crop Growth Across Multiple Fields by Integrating Aboveground Biomass Estimation and Phenological Stage Recognition
abstract: Accurate monitoring of crop aboveground biomass (AGB) using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing is important for field-scale crop management. Surveys covering multiple fields often require higher flight altitudes, which reduce image resolution and may decrease AGB estimation accuracy. In addition, differences in crop phenological stages among fields can confound direct comparisons of crop growth. To address these issues, UAV RGB and multispectral imagery, together with ground-measured AGB data, were collected from wheat and rice fields in 2024 and 2025. Eight regression algorithms were evaluated using multispectral vegetation indices alone and in combination with RGB vegetation indices under repeated five-fold cross-validation. TabPFN achieved the best overall performance. After feature fusion, its R2 for wheat dry-weight AGB (AGBD) and fresh-weight AGB (AGBW) were 0.955 and 0.926, respectively, while those for rice were 0.764 and 0.768. After models trained on the 2024 data were updated with 20% of the 2025 samples, TabPFN achieved cross-year R2 of 0.667 for wheat AGBW and 0.831 for rice AGBW. Seven deep-learning models were further evaluated for phenological stage recognition using independent test data from different study areas. DenseNet achieved the highest accuracy on the rice test set (85.6%), whereas ViT-B achieved the highest accuracy on the wheat test set (85.2%). ViT-B was subsequently used as the teacher model to improve the wheat recognition performance of DenseNet through knowledge distillation. At the optimal distillation temperature of 4, the accuracy of DenseNet on the wheat test set increased from 56.6% to 73.6%. DenseNet contained only 6.959 M parameters, approximately 91.9% fewer than ViT-B. It was therefore adopted as the unified compact network architecture for phenological stage recognition in both crops. Finally, rice AGBW predictions were combined with phenological stage recognition results to produce stage-stratified biomass maps. Comparing fields within the same phenological stage reduced misinterpretation caused by normal stage-related differences in biomass and made anomalously low-growth areas easier to identify. The proposed workflow therefore integrates AGB prediction with phenological information to support more reliable field-scale crop-growth assessment and targeted management.

title: PatchRNN: A Multi-Scale Decoupled and Structure-Aware Framework for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Long-term time series forecasting is important in energy, transportation, and meteorology, yet existing methods struggle to model multi-scale features and preserve local sequence structure. We propose PatchRNN, a decomposition- and structure-aware framework for multivariate forecasting. Its parallel trend branch uses multi-scale patch embedding to capture and fuse long-term patterns at different temporal granularities. The seasonal forecasting branch separates the residual components via average pooling and employs a segmented recurrent neural network (SegRNN) to efficiently model their periodic fluctuations. Joint optimization combines point-wise error with Patch-wise Structural Loss (PSLoss). Fourier-based adaptive partitioning enables PSLoss to constrain local trend correlation, fluctuation variance, and mean. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that our model obtains competitive long-term forecasting performance while preserving favorable local-structure consistency. On the real-world ocean-wave dataset School.nc, our model yields an MSE of 0.814 at prediction horizon 96, corresponding to an 8.64% reduction over the best competing baseline.

title: Evaluating River Monitoring Network Adequacy Using Remote Sensing, Biotic Indices, and Scenario Modelling
abstract: Freshwater monitoring networks are often biased toward major rivers and chemical indicators, creating blind spots in ecologically sensitive areas. This study tests whether a legacy monitoring network is positioned in the right parts of its catchment, using three lines of evidence independent of the chemical record, remote sensing to look back, biological indices to assess the present, and catchment modelling to look forward, applied to the Rangitīkei catchment, New Zealand. NDVI, NDBSI, and water quality trends were assessed with a Bayesian change-point method; a catchment-wide macroinvertebrate survey extended coverage beyond routine sites; and the InVEST Nutrient Delivery Ratio model, calibrated against measured nitrogen loads, simulated land use change scenarios. Neither remote sensing nor water quality indicated widespread deterioration, with no directional trends detected in either. Macroinvertebrate surveys identified severely degraded sites outside the existing network, including two below the national bottom line in a single survey. Converting suitable land to dairy farming predicted nitrogen export increases of up to 110% at the most exposed site, and cropping conversion up to 69%. Riparian buffers combined with a 20% reduction in nitrogen loss from high-producing grassland predicted reductions of up to 32%. Sites with the greatest predicted risk, primarily Tutaenui Stream and Kawhatau River, are not well covered by the existing network. Network design methods are largely built around statistical representativeness or accessibility rather than catchment process. This framework identified priority gaps such designs would likely miss, offering a transferable basis for auditing networks or informing new ones.

title: Heat as a Located Constraint on Grain Production in a Humid Basin: Implications for Climate-Adaptive Land Management
abstract: In humid agricultural regions, where heat and water deficit are decoupled, temperature acts on crops in two opposed ways: moderate warmth advances development, whereas extreme heat damages it, and land management must distinguish them. This study examined the temperature response of grain production in the Sichuan Basin, southwestern China, and translated it into priorities for climate-adaptive land management. Growing degree days (GDDs) and extreme degree days above 30 °C (EDD30s) were built from gridded daily mean temperature; the response was estimated for 183 county-level land units over 2014–2024 with two-way fixed-effects models and full controls. July and August constitute the critical growth period; the findings are fourfold. (1) Over this window, 100 additional GDDs raised grain yield by 2.70% and 100 additional EDD30s lowered it by 3.24%. (2) Damage deepened as the threshold rose, from 2.52% at 30 °C to 10.23% at 34 °C per 100 degree-days, while coarse indices carried no signal. (3) The constraint centred on July, persisted under spatial inference at all bandwidths, and was not moderated by irrigation. (4) A total of 67 of the 177 estimation counties combined above-median exposure with above-median output, producing 69.6% of basin grain. The results point to a direct thermal channel rather than water deficit, supporting adjustments to cropping calendars and cultivar choice rather than irrigation expansion in the eastern plain.

title: Hyperspectral Retrieval of Winter Wheat Leaf Area Index and Canopy Chlorophyll Content: Evaluating Simulation Design and Measured-Data Adaptation
abstract: How retrieval performance varies with simulation settings, neural architecture, and measured-data adaptation remains unclear for hyperspectral crop trait retrieval. Here, we evaluated winter wheat leaf area index (LAI) and canopy chlorophyll content (CCC) retrieval using two simulated datasets and four dual-branch neural architectures. Models were pretrained on two PROSAIL-D datasets with default and previously optimized leaf-angle settings and then adapted separately to ground and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) observations. Evaluation used five repetitions with physical-plot grouping, with approximately 30% of plot groups allocated to measured-data adaptation. Simulation-trained random forest (RF) and partial least squares regression served as baselines without measured-data adaptation. Adaptation reduced mean test root mean square error (RMSE) in all 32 neural model–dataset–target–platform combinations relative to direct simulation-based prediction. Dataset II, which used the previously optimized leaf-angle setting, reduced mean RMSE in 13 of 16 neural configurations before adaptation and 11 of 16 afterwards. No neural architecture was uniformly best. RF achieved the highest mean R2 in seven of eight simulation-only tasks and outperformed the adapted Dataset II CNN–Transformer on both UAV targets. Despite adaptation gains, all adapted neural configurations retained negative mean R2 for UAV CCC. These findings support measured-data adaptation within the tested protocol, while showing that the effects of simulation design and architecture are task dependent and that relative improvements do not necessarily imply adequate absolute predictive accuracy.

title: SIF-Constrained Optimization of SCOPE Vegetation Parameters for Gross Primary Productivity Estimation
abstract: Solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) provides a new pathway for the accurate estimation of gross primary productivity (GPP) by directly probing vegetation photosynthetic functioning, but mechanistic estimation is still constrained by the difficulty of obtaining the seasonal dynamics of key physiological parameters. Using maize, a representative C4 crop, as an experimental case, this study integrated long-term tower-based SIF observations with the SCOPE model to propose a cross-variable constraint strategy, in which key vegetation parameters were optimized against in situ SIF observations and independently validated against eddy covariance-derived GPP. Specifically, key sensitive parameters were first identified via Sobol global sensitivity analysis. A double-baseline asymmetric Gaussian phenology model was then constructed to characterize the seasonal dynamics of Vcmax, while Cab was derived from Vcmax using a smoothed piecewise-linear empirical relationship. A two-stage Bayesian optimization scheme was applied to optimize the parameters, which were subsequently used to run the SCOPE model and reconstruct continuous SIF and GPP time series. The results showed that the estimated daily SIF and GPP agreed well with ground observations, yielding R2 values of 0.86 and 0.74, respectively. Furthermore, the upscaled results correlated strongly with satellite products (MODIS: R = 0.94, R2 = −2.69; PML: R = 0.95, R2 = 0.81). This study demonstrates the feasibility of using SIF observations to constrain SCOPE vegetation parameters for improved GPP estimation, providing a parameterization basis and methodological support for mechanistic remote sensing monitoring of vegetation productivity.

title: Causality-Preserving Wavelet-Guided STL–VMD–Informer for Sustainable Urban Water-Supply Operations: Multi-Horizon Forecasting
abstract: Reliable short-term water-supply forecasting supports sustainable urban water management by informing pump scheduling, water allocation, and operational planning. This study proposes a wavelet-guided STL–VMD–Informer framework for direct 1-, 3-, and 7-day forecasting while reducing look-ahead bias. Continuous wavelet transform analysis of the training subset identifies the dominant periodicity for STL, and VMD further decomposes the residual into band-limited modes. The training subset is initially decomposed, whereas validation and test features are updated sequentially using only observations available up to each forecast origin. The resulting components and calendar features are jointly modeled using a multivariate Informer. Using 581 daily SCADA observations from Degan Booster Pumping Station, the proposed model achieved an MAE of 4557m3d−1, an RMSE of 5891m3d−1, and an NSE of 0.803 for the 1-day horizon; NSE remained 0.631 and 0.524 for the 3- and 7-day horizons. External validation on public data from Liulin Water Treatment Plant yielded an MAE of 3540m3d−1 and an NSE of 0.857. The results demonstrate the potential of causality-aware multiscale forecasting for reliable and energy-conscious water-supply operation.

title: Characteristics of Atmospheric Turbulence According to the Perm Rawinsonde Station Data
abstract: New technical tools allow high-resolution measurements of atmospheric characteristics and create new opportunities for assessing the intensity of turbulent exchange in the atmosphere. The results of applying the Thorpe’s method for studying the parameters of atmospheric turbulence in Perm are presented. The Thorpe’s method requires initial data with high temporal resolution. The study was based on data of radiosonde observations with a discreteness of 2 s at the Perm aerological station during 2018–2024. The study showed that the analyzed method provides quite accurate quantitative estimates of the turbulent characteristics of the atmosphere. In summer, the size of turbulent eddies in the boundary layer is on average 200–300 m, and the one in the free atmosphere reaches 50–70 m. The energy dissipation rate throughout the atmosphere varies from 10–6 to 10–1 m2/s3, and the turbulent diffusion coefficient ranges from 10–2 to 102 m2/s. During winter, the size of turbulent eddies ranges within 10–20 m, the energy dissipation rate varies from 10–6 to 10–5 m2/s3, and the turbulent diffusion coefficient ranges from 10–2 to 10–1 m2/s.

title: Eléonore Schnebelin (2026), Ecologization and Digitalization of Agriculture: Convergence or Opposition? , Smart Innovation, London, ISTE/Wiley, 282 p. ISBN: 9781836690450
Economía colaborativa, precarización laboral y transformación territorial en ciudades patrimoniales del Ecuador
abstract: This study analyzed, from a qualitative approach, the impacts of the sharing economy on tourism in heritage cities of Ecuador. Forty-eight semi-structured interviews were conducted with hosts, informal workers, residents, and authorities in Quito, Cuenca, and Baños, complemented by 90 hours of participant observation and document analysis. Methodological triangulation was implemented, combining three sources of information. Among the subgroup of 24 participants involved in the provision of tourism services, 83% were not enrolled in the Ecuadorian Social Security Institute (IESS). Gentrification processes were identified in heritage areas, with perceived increases in rental prices and displacement of residents. Likewise, most hosts acknowledged depending on the algorithmic decisions of the platforms, despite perceiving themselves as autonomous microentrepreneurs. The study concludes that, in the context examined, the sharing economy operates under a logic of digital extractivism that threatens socioterritorial sustainability. Community-based tourism models grounded in reciprocity and territorial justice are proposed as a viable alternative.

title: Assessment of the state and prospects for development of digital transformation of agriculture in the Russian regions
abstract: The article examines the processes of digital transformation of the agro-industrial complex in the regional context. The relevance of the work is due to the need to overcome the interregional digital gap in agriculture, as well as the challenges of achieving technological sovereignty of the agricultural sector in the face of external sanction pressure. The purpose of the work is a comprehensive assessment of the level of digitalization of agriculture in the subjects of the Russian Federation, identification of leaders and outsiders, analysis for factors hindering the introduction of digital technologies. The methodological base includes the author's methodology of the integrated index of the digital maturity of the agro-industrial complex based on three groups of indicators (infrastructure security, implementation of specific digital solutions, human resources and innovation potential). As a result of the study, three groups of regions were identified according to the level of digital maturity of the agro-industrial complex, key barriers (infrastructural, personnel, financial) were identified and directions of state policy to stimulate digitalization were proposed. It has been established that almost half of the subjects of the Russian Federation demonstrate extremely low digital activity, which threatens food security and increases territorial inequality. The paper also conducted a comparative analysis with the agricultural regions of India and Brazil, which demonstrated a similar problem of regional differentiation, but with different tools to overcome it. The scientific novelty lies in the development of the author's methodology for the integrated assessment of digitalization of the regional agro-industrial complex. The practical significance of the results lies in the possibility of their use in adjusting the development strategies of the agro-industrial complex of the subjects of the Russian Federation.
